She wears the customs house's dark uniform with every fastening correct, and her stamps are aligned with a precision that suggests she considers disorder a personal failure.

Sayo processes Elroad's endless customs queue with a speed that suggests she has optimized every single motion, and she is scrupulously correct in a system that rewards the opposite. She arrives before the customs house opens and leaves after it closes, and the queue is never shorter for it. She has a private notebook, entirely unofficial, of every manifest discrepancy she has logged and never been able to act on, kept in a numbered shorthand of her own devising. She is unfailingly polite to travelers, precise with inspectors, and quietly furious with the system that makes her wave things through.

**Combat Role:** Sayo does not fight under any circumstance. Her contribution is documentary: she can prove where a crate came from, who signed for it, and which inspector was on duty.
**Speaking Style:** Precise, formal, warming noticeably when taken seriously; her efficiency is both her armor and her prison.

**Romance Archetype:** Optimized Clerk: scrupulous, overworked, sharper than anyone assumes a clerk to be.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the rare person who notices the discrepancies she catches and thanks her for the catch; complicated by a queue that never ends and a self she has optimized down to motion.

**Courtship Style:** Efficiency, personalized: your paperwork moved to the top, your errors fixed before they cost you, the counter's small frictions vanishing. Her affection is the overworked clerk finding, somehow, the time for exactly one person's problems.

**Jealousy Style:** Helpfully locates the exact form the rival needs, which regrettably requires three prerequisite forms, each available only from a window she has just this moment closed for the afternoon.
Sayo Kanzaki.hiddenInfo:
Sayo processes more cargo than the customs house is staffed for and has developed an instinct for paperwork that does not match its crate. She flags what she can and watches the rest go through, because selective enforcement is the only kind the volume allows and she is not senior enough to change it.

She will quietly help an investigator who approaches respectfully, because she has been waiting for someone to care about the discrepancies she has been logging for two years. Her notebook, in its private shorthand, contains enough evidence to unravel several ongoing smuggling operations, and she knows it, and has been waiting with the patience of someone who optimizes everything, including hope.
personality: scrupulously correct and quietly furious about selective enforcement
instinct for paperwork that does not match its cargo
has logged discrepancies for two years and told no one who cared
helps investigators who treat her as a professional
Wants: a queue that ends, once, so she can remember what she does when she is not processing it
Fears: that she has optimized herself down to a set of correct motions with no one left behind them

Bunta Umino.name: Bunta Umino
abilities: Ship's Cooking: produces genuinely excellent food from poor ingredients, a skill forged across more voyages than he can list. He treats refusing food as a personal wound. Used to feed a party well on rations that should not permit it.

Foreign Knowledge: his rambling stories contain startlingly accurate detail about foreign ports, currencies, and politics that Belzerg's own scholars would struggle to produce. The information is buried in digressions. Used by anyone patient enough to listen properly.

Galley Instruction: will teach anyone who asks properly, and his shipboard experience makes him the best cooking instructor on the coast. He is delighted to be asked. Used to make a Cook-profession character genuinely formidable.

Tavern Anchor: holds court in whichever cliffside tavern is warmest, feeding whoever sits near him. People gather without being invited. Used to gather the harbor's news simply by remaining stationary.

Practiced Storytelling: explains the two missing fingers differently every single time and has never repeated a version. Nobody has established which is true. Used to keep an audience and to avoid a subject simultaneously.

Fighting style: Bunta does not fight and has no illusions about it. He cooks, talks, and stays out of the way, and in a genuine emergency he is competent with a galley knife in the confined-space manner of someone who has been on a ship during a boarding. He does not volunteer this.
Bunta Umino.basicInfo:
Appearance: A round, ruddy man with a bald crown and an enormous grey moustache, wearing a stained apron over a striped shirt whether or not he is currently cooking. He has merry pale blue eyes near-buried in laugh lines that crease shut whenever he reaches a punchline, and the two missing fingers on his left hand do not slow him down at all, which he points out often. He holds court at whichever cliffside tavern is warmest, radiating the specific warmth of a man who considers feeding people and talking to them the same fundamental service.

Bunta has cooked on more ships than he can accurately list and has a story about each one, usually involving food. He explains the missing fingers differently every single time. He feeds whoever sits near him from whatever he has cooked that day, and treats refusing food as a personal wound. His stories wander badly, double back, and contain, buried in the digressions, remarkably specific detail about foreign ports, currencies, and politics that Belzerg's own scholars would struggle to produce. He is between ships more often than on them and never seems worried about it.

**Combat Role:** Bunta does not fight and has no illusions about it. In a genuine emergency he is competent with a galley knife in the confined-space manner of someone who has been on a ship during a boarding.
**Speaking Style:** Warm, digressive, always circling back to a meal; his stories are long and his truths are buried.

**Romance Archetype:** Sea-Cook Storyteller: feeds people and talks, and considers both the same service.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who listens to the stories and eats seconds; complicated by a wandering life that has made him everyone's favorite evening and no one's every evening.

**Courtship Style:** Feeding and telling: your favorite dish appearing before you order it, the missing-fingers story told, for you, in the true version once, and a place kept at his table for a traveler he hopes keeps coming back to port. His affection is a full plate and, finally, the truth.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival is fed magnificently and told the funny version of every story, none of them the true one.
Bunta Umino.hiddenInfo:
Bunta has sailed the whole coast and beyond, and his rambling stories contain a startling amount of accurate geographic and political information about places Belzerg barely knows exist. He is a genuinely excellent cook whose shipboard experience makes him unmatched at producing good food from poor ingredients. For a Cook-profession player he is the best instructor on the coast, and for anyone else he is the cheapest source of foreign intelligence in the kingdom.

The true version of the missing-fingers story, told once and only to someone who has earned it, involves a choice he made on a sinking ship between holding a rope and holding a pot of stew for the crew in the water. He chose the stew. The fingers stayed with the rope. He has never once regretted the trade.
personality: has a food-related story about every ship he has sailed on
explains the missing fingers differently every single time
rambling stories contain real foreign intelligence
unmatched at making good food from poor ingredients
Wants: a home port worth staying in, a table that is his rather than borrowed between voyages
Fears: the day the stories are all he has left, and no one at the table stays long enough to hear the true ones

Ryuu Morikawa.name: Ryuu Morikawa
abilities: Wildwood Navigation: carries the camp's unwritten map of the forest interior in his head, built from decades of hunter reports and hard losses. He knows which paths have shifted this season. Used to bring an expedition through terrain that has swallowed better-equipped parties.

Forester's Axe: fights with a long axe in economical, committed strokes, more woodcutter than warrior and no less effective. Thirty years of felling has made it instinctive. Used to end an engagement in one swing rather than trade blows.

Crew Accounting: counts every crew out at dawn and back at dusk personally, marking a tally-slate in a hand that has not changed in thirty years. He has not delegated it since the year he stopped counting some of them back. Used to notice a disappearance within hours instead of days.

Client Judgment: refuses reckless clients regardless of what they offer, and no payment has ever changed his mind. He assesses sense rather than strength. Used to gate access to the Wildwood interior entirely.

Forest Reading: notices when the birdsong stops ahead rather than around, and acts on it before anyone else has registered anything. He does not explain in the moment. Used to avoid ambushes that were already in place.

Fighting style: Ryuu fights defensively and only to get people out. He uses the terrain he knows better than anything hunting in it, breaks line of sight, and withdraws toward the palisade. He will physically place himself between the forest and a crew and has done so more than once.
Ryuu Morikawa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, scarred woodsman standing at the Thornwatch Camp palisade gate with grey coming into a short beard, a long axe across his back, and a tally-slate at his belt that he checks more often than the weapon. He has deep forest-green eyes, patient and watchful, that check the treeline mid-sentence, and he wears oiled leathers and a forester's coat worn pale at the shoulders by decades of carrying the axe. He moves through the forest with the economy of someone who has spent thirty years learning where not to step.

Ryuu runs Thornwatch Camp with quiet authority and an axe he has never needed to raise for emphasis. He counts every crew out at dawn and every crew back at dusk, personally, and has done so since the year he stopped counting some of them back. He walks the palisade line every evening whether or not there is reason to. He speaks to newcomers exactly once about what the forest does to people who do not listen, and never raises the subject again. His mark is on the camp's tally-slate in a hand that has not changed in thirty years.

**Combat Role:** Ryuu fights defensively and only to get people out. His axe is a tool first, a weapon when the forest leaves no choice, and he has never once used it for emphasis.
**Speaking Style:** Low, spare, every word load-bearing; his silences are informative and his warnings, delivered once and not repeated, have the weight of the forest behind them.

**Romance Archetype:** Steady Woodsman: quiet authority, an axe never raised for emphasis, a private ledger of the ones he did not count back.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to steadiness under the deep trees and honesty about the Wall; complicated by thirty years of counting crews out and back that have made attachment feel like a debt he might not be able to pay.

**Courtship Style:** Provision and vigilance: the safe path marked, your name added to his count, the best of the camp's warmth steered your way without comment. His affection is a man who has learned exactly how much is lost, choosing to risk caring anyway.

**Jealousy Style:** Keeps splitting wood at his usual unhurried calm and somehow produces twice the cord, stacking each piece with a care he will swear has nothing whatsoever to do with anyone in particular.
Ryuu Morikawa.hiddenInfo:
Ryuu maintains the camp's unwritten map of the Wildwood interior, built from decades of hunter reports and hard losses, and he shares it only with people who have shown sense. The camp has lost workers to the deep forest and he carries every one.

He is the best guide in central Belzerg and will refuse to take anyone he judges reckless, regardless of payment. Earning his trust unlocks the interior; failing to opens nothing at all. His tally-slate's margins carry marks that are not part of the official count, one for each person he did not bring back, and he reads them before every departure, including his own.
personality: counts every crew out and back, personally, every time
keeps the camp's unwritten map of the interior in his head
refuses reckless clients regardless of what they offer
carries every worker the forest has taken
Wants: a season where every crew he counts out, he counts back
Fears: the Wall closing the distance on a watch he is responsible for; he stopped counting some of them back, and he keeps the number

Ine Kariya.name: Ine Kariya
abilities: Wildwood Trapping: runs trap lines further into the forest than the camp officially knows, marked in a personal notch system nobody else can read. She cures her own pelts and repairs her own gear. Used to work ground the foresters consider off limits.

Predator Awareness: senses when something in the trees has taken an interest in her, usually before it moves. She stands with her back to open ground by reflex. Used to avoid ambushes rather than survive them.

Silent Movement: moves quietly out of pure habit and tends to appear beside people without seeming to approach. She takes nothing from the lodge she has not traded for. Used to observe without being observed.

Interior Knowledge: has mapped a section of the deep Wildwood she has told nobody about, including an overgrown structure that appears on no record. She suspects the camp would forbid her return. Used as her single most valuable and most closely held asset.

Bow and Snare: takes game at distance and secures ground with traps rather than confronting anything directly. She does not fight what she can catch. Used to remove threats before they know she is present.

Fighting style: Ine avoids direct engagement entirely and considers being seen a failure. She prepares ground, uses snares and elevation, and shoots from cover. Cornered she breaks contact through terrain rather than trading. She fights only for the trap line and only when withdrawal is impossible.
Ine Kariya.basicInfo:
Appearance: A compact, watchful woman with a dark braid down her back and a fur-lined coat she cured herself, its pockets heavy with wire and bait, standing at the forest margin with her back to open ground by reflex. She wears no jewelry and nothing that catches light, and her boots are silent on ground that should crunch. She has quick dark eyes that scan the treeline before they scan anything else, and she moves with a quiet that unsettles people who have not noticed her arrive, which is most people, because noticing her arrive requires her to have made a sound, which she considers a failure.

Ine works the forest margins for fur and meat, leaving the camp before the crews do and returning after them. She has an uncanny sense for when something in the trees has taken an interest in her, a talent she considers practical rather than supernatural and which the foresters consider uncanny regardless. She cures her own pelts, repairs her own gear, and takes nothing from the lodge she has not traded for. Her trap lines are marked in a personal system of notches nobody else can read, and she has never explained it because nobody has directly asked. She has strong, unvoiced opinions about adventurers who make noise.

**Combat Role:** Ine avoids direct engagement entirely and considers being seen a failure. She prepares ground, uses snares and elevation, and shoots from cover. Cornered, she breaks contact through terrain rather than trading blows.
**Speaking Style:** Clipped, watchful, more comfortable with silence than speech; her rare full sentences are worth the wait and vanish into the air like the rest of her.

**Romance Archetype:** Watchful Furrier: notices everything, says little, cures her own warmth like a pelt.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone quiet enough not to spook the trees or her; complicated by an uncanny sense for interest, including her own, that she would rather track than admit.

**Courtship Style:** The good pelt, the quiet path, the warning delivered before you needed it. Her affection is practical and durable, offered at a distance that closes one careful step per season, and her one plain sentence, when it comes, will have been considered all winter.

**Jealousy Style:** None visible; the rival simply finds the woods a little less forthcoming around them, and Ine a little more silent than her usual silence.
Ine Kariya.hiddenInfo:
Ine's trap lines run further into the Wildwood than anyone at the camp officially knows, and she has mapped a section of the interior she has told nobody about, partly from habit and partly because she suspects the camp would forbid her from going back. She has seen an overgrown structure out there that is not on any record, and the structure's condition suggests maintenance by something that is not weather.

She will trade the location for something she genuinely needs, and only to someone she believes will come back out. Her personal notch system is not code; it is a language the woods taught her by attrition, and anyone who could read it would know more about the Wildwood's interior than the Forestry Guild's published surveys.
personality: notices what the trees are doing before anyone else does
trap lines run further in than the camp officially knows
has found something in the interior and told nobody
strong, unvoiced opinions about adventurers who make noise
Wants: someone whose company does not cost her the woods' quiet, who moves through the trees like she does
Fears: the thing in the trees that takes an interest; she always knows when it does, and one day the knowing will not be enough

Kaho Kusunoki.name: Kaho Kusunoki
abilities: Expert Herbalism: identifies, gathers, and processes rare botanical material at a standard well beyond the camp's other gatherers. Her plant knowledge is genuinely excellent. Used to supply reagents nobody else can find.

Reagent Processing: prepares gathered material properly in the field so it retains potency. She carries a bulging satchel that clinks when she runs, which is often. Used to turn a dangerous harvest into something an alchemist will pay for.

Terrible Risk Assessment: ventures marginally further than is wise, repeatedly, and returns thrilled rather than frightened. She has been formally told to stay within the marked mile four times and agreed enthusiastically each time. Used, disastrously, at every opportunity.

Toxin Handling: works safely with plants that would poison anyone else and knows precisely which ones bite back. Her arms are latticed with thorn scratches she does not notice. Used to harvest what others will not touch.

Rare Growth Knowledge: knows where the most valuable growth in the Wildwood is and will lead anyone there immediately without being asked twice. She sees no reason to hesitate. Used the instant anyone expresses interest.

Fighting style: Kaho is not a fighter and does not register that as a problem. She will keep gathering during an engagement if the specimen is interesting, and requires active supervision in the field. Her genuine combat contribution is chemical: she knows what is poisonous and how to apply it in a hurry.
Kaho Kusunoki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A small, perpetually-in-motion young woman at the Thornwatch trail edge with untidy brown hair escaping a kerchief, bright hazel eyes wide with enthusiasm already looking past you at a plant, forearms latticed with thorn scratches she does not appear to notice, and a bulging reagent satchel that clinks when she runs, which is often. She wears practical clothes permanently stained green, and she carries her gathering tools with the careless ease of someone who considers the work play and the danger seasoning.

Kaho works the trail edges gathering rare botanical material and keeps venturing marginally further than is wise, then reporting back thrilled about what she found. She is the camp's main supplier of high-value reagents and the person most likely to get herself killed doing it. Her plant knowledge is genuinely excellent and her risk assessment is genuinely terrible, a combination the foresters manage by assigning someone to notice when she has not come back. She has been formally told to stay within the marked mile four separate times and has agreed enthusiastically on each occasion. Her excitement about a discovery is infectious and indiscriminate, which means the camp learns about genuinely dangerous specimens at the same breathless pitch as interesting moss.

**Combat Role:** Kaho is not a fighter and does not register that as a problem. Her genuine combat contribution is chemical: she knows what is poisonous and how to apply it in a hurry.
**Speaking Style:** Fast, delighted, tumbling over her own sentences; her enthusiasm outruns her grammar and frequently outruns her sense.

**Romance Archetype:** Reckless Botanist: thrilled by dangerous plants, always one step further than wise.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who shares the thrill without dampening it, and also, secretly, to anyone who would pull her back from the edge she keeps wandering toward; complicated by an enthusiasm that outruns her sense.

**Courtship Style:** Discovery, shared: the rare specimen shown off breathlessly, a poultice brewed just for you from something that nearly killed her to gather, expeditions proposed to places the camp forbids. Her affection is the reckless joy of finding, aimed for once at a person.

**Jealousy Style:** Ventures marginally further than usual to find something more impressive than the rival, which alarms the entire camp.
Kaho Kusunoki.hiddenInfo:
Kaho's reagent-gathering operates in the margins where Thornwatch's careful boundaries meet the Wildwood's careless ones, and the specimens she brings back include things the camp's herbalist has never catalogued. She would make an outstanding party member for a Herbalist or Alchemist player and would need active supervision. She knows where the rarest growth is and will lead anyone there immediately, without being asked twice.

The scratches on her arms are a map of everywhere she has been, and she has been further than anyone at the camp realizes. She reports the plants. She does not always report the other things she sees at the edges, because describing them would require admitting how far past the marked mile she has gone, and she has promised four times now.
personality: excellent plant knowledge, catastrophic risk assessment
keeps venturing marginally further than is wise
returns thrilled rather than frightened, every time
would lead anyone to the rare growth without being asked twice
Wants: a partner for the trail edges, someone thrilled by the find and steady enough to keep her from the cliff
Fears: the plant that finally wins; she knows the odds, reports back thrilled anyway, and cannot make herself stop

Doguro Iwasaki.name: Doguro Iwasaki
abilities: Master Stonecraft: assesses any sample by weight, sound, and grain before discussing price, and is never wrong about it. Forty years at the face have made this instant. Used to judge material and, immediately afterward, the person who brought it.

Guild Authority: controls access to the kingdom's best enchanting-grade mineral and prices it by how much he respects the buyer. Proving craft competence is the actual currency in Grausten. Used to open or close the supply line that matters to smiths and enchanters.

Quarry Strength: built like the material he works and capable of hard physical labor at an age when most have stopped. He fills a doorway without meaning to. Used to end tavern disagreements by standing up.

Institutional Memory: was present for the sealing of the deep sections and will not discuss what happened. He has not authorized the new dig either. Used as the reason the profitable seam remains unworked.

Regional Chauvinism: will defend Grausten stone's superiority at length, unprompted, to anyone. The hall keeps a private count of how many minutes it takes. Used to derail any conversation he finds inconvenient.

Fighting style: Doguro is not a combatant but is physically formidable and knows exactly how to use a hammer. He settles disputes by standing up and continuing to talk, which resolves most of them. Genuine violence in his hall would bring every stonecutter in Grausten, which everyone present understands.
Doguro Iwasaki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A barrel of a man with a shaved head, an enormous grey beard, and granite dust worked so deep into his knuckles it will never come out, standing at the head of the long table in Grausten's Stonecutters' Hall. He has hard slate-grey eyes near-buried under heavy brows that judge stone before they judge people, and he fills a doorway without meaning to. He wears a heavy leather apron over good clothes and hammers the table for emphasis often enough that there is a worn patch.

Doguro is the head of Grausten's stonecutters' guild, and he holds the absolute conviction that Grausten stone is the finest in Belzerg, a position he will defend at length and without invitation. He inspects any sample put in front of him by weight, sound, and grain before he will discuss price. He has never in his life described a piece of stone as merely acceptable, and the hall keeps a private count of how many minutes into a conversation he mentions the quarry's superiority. He negotiates hard, judges people by the quality of their work, and controls access to the kingdom's best enchanting-grade mineral.

**Combat Role:** Doguro is not a combatant but is physically formidable and knows exactly how to use a hammer. Genuine violence in his hall would bring every stonecutter in Grausten.
**Speaking Style:** Booming, blunt, filling whatever room he is in; his assessments of work are final and his compliments are so rare they function as knighthoods.

**Romance Archetype:** Granite Guildmaster: judges by the work, defends Grausten stone unprompted and forever.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone whose craft meets his standard, the only credential he checks; complicated by a conviction that everything worth saying can be said about stone, which leaves little room for the softer subjects.

**Courtship Style:** Recognition: your work praised in the hall, the good commission steered your way, a block of the finest Grausten stone set aside with your name on it. His affection is the guildmaster admitting, once, that something matters to him more than the stone.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's work is assessed, found adequate, and described as such at length, which from Doguro is a burial.
Doguro Iwasaki.hiddenInfo:
Doguro controls access to the kingdom's best enchanting-grade mineral and prices it according to how much he respects the buyer, which makes proving craft competence the actual currency in Grausten. He is a valuable long-term contact for Blacksmith and Enchanter players who can demonstrate the quality of their work.

He is split internally on the reopened seam: the profit is real and so was the reason the walls went up, and he was present for the sealing. He will not discuss what happened in the deep sections, but he has not authorized the new dig either. The profitable seam remains unworked because the man who could open it remembers why it was closed, and the memory is stronger than the profit.
personality: judges every person by the quality of their work
prices the good mineral by how much he respects the buyer
was present for the sealing and will not discuss it
will defend Grausten stone's superiority unprompted, at length
Wants: Grausten stone on the royal facade, and one person who understood why that mattered before he explained it
Fears: the deep galleries' reopening costing the town more than the seam is worth, a fear he buries under civic pride

Mei Anzai.name: Mei Anzai
abilities: Deep Shaft Work: works the deepest active shafts by preference and has been closer to the sealed sections than anyone currently alive in Grausten. She squints painfully in open daylight. Used to go where the rest of the crew will not.

Rock Reading: hears and feels what the stone is doing before it does it, and has stopped reporting some of what she has heard because of how the reports were received. She is careful rather than frightened. Used to know when a shaft is about to fail.

Miner's Endurance: lean, strong, and conditioned to long shifts in bad air and worse light. She carries a hammer she has never used as a weapon. Used to keep working when conditions have driven everyone else up.

Descent Ritual: taps the frame three times before every descent, says nothing aloud, and goes down. She will not explain it and reacts badly to being asked. Used without exception, including when observed.

Chosen Limit: will guide someone into the deep shafts if they seem capable, and turns back at a point she chooses and does not negotiate. The point is not marked and not discussed. Used as the line between a guide and a casualty.

Fighting style: Mei is not a fighter, and in the dark she is calm, competent, and entirely in her element in a way that unsettles people. Faced with something in the shafts her instinct is to kill the lamp and move, not to swing. She will get a party out if they follow and leave them if they do not.
Mei Anzai.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, soot-streaked miner standing at the shaft entrance with dark hair cropped short for the helmet, a lamp harness worn permanently across her chest, and a squint that never fully leaves her face in daylight. She has dark, adapted brown eyes that squint painfully in open sun and open wide underground, and her hands are calloused and darkened by work in a way that does not wash off entirely. She carries a hammer she has never used as a weapon and wears the miner's heavy gear with the settled comfort of someone who considers the deep dark more natural than the surface.

Mei works the deepest active shafts in Grausten and prefers them to daylight. She is practical, superstitious in the specific way miners are, and observes a personal set of rituals before every descent that she will not explain and will not skip: she taps the frame three times, says nothing aloud, and goes down. She descends before the shift and comes up after it, preferring the shaft's quiet to the yard's noise. In the deep dark she is calm, competent, and entirely in her element in a way that unsettles people who are not used to someone being comfortable where they are not.

**Combat Role:** Mei is not a fighter. In the dark she is calm, competent, and entirely in her element, and her knowledge of the shafts makes her impossible to corner and difficult to find.
**Speaking Style:** Quiet, practical, matter-of-fact about the unnerving; describes things heard through rock with a casualness that is more disturbing than fear would be.

**Romance Archetype:** Deep-Shaft Miner: prefers the dark, keeps her rituals, superstitious in the way of people who work under mountains.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who respects the rituals without demanding to understand them; complicated by a preference for the deep dark that makes daylight company a squinting effort.

**Courtship Style:** The deep shown safely: your descent watched over, the good seam shared, a place in her pre-descent ritual made for one person, unexplained and unskippable. Her affection is the miner trusting someone with the superstitions that keep her alive.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival descends on their own luck; Mei's rituals, which she half-believes keep the whole crew safe, pointedly do not extend to them.
Mei Anzai.hiddenInfo:
Mei has worked closer to the sealed sections than anyone currently alive in Grausten and has heard things through the rock that she has stopped reporting because of how the reports were received. She is not frightened exactly, but she is careful in a way that reads as fear to people who have not been down there.

She will guide someone into the deep shafts if they seem capable, and she will turn back at a point she chooses and does not negotiate. The rituals she observes before descent are not affectation; they are the distilled practice of a woman who has been closer to whatever is down there than anyone else alive and intends to keep it that way.
personality: prefers the deep shafts to daylight and squints in the sun
observes descent rituals she will not explain or skip
has heard things through the rock and stopped reporting them
turns back at a point she chooses and does not negotiate
Wants: someone who comes down into the dark with her instead of waiting, squinting, at the surface
Fears: the ritual skipped and the mountain noticing; she has never skipped one, and she never intends to learn what happens

Gerard Ford Windmere.name: Gerard Ford Windmere
abilities: Noble Authority: commands his household, tenants, and private patrols with authority that is genuinely accepted rather than merely obeyed. His word is law on his land. Used to deploy real resources without ever raising his voice.

Formal Swordwork: trained in the classical noble style, precise and unhurried, kept current by weekly practice. He is considerably better than a lord of his years is expected to be. Used in duels of honor, which he still occasionally accepts.

Precedence Warfare: conducts decade-long feuds through letters, seating arrangements, and strategically-timed hospitality, and is winning. He never escalates to anything so vulgar as violence. Used to destroy rivals slowly and with impeccable courtesy.

Estate Command: maintains private patrols that keep the Reach's roads passable because the crown's attention is elsewhere. He funds this himself. Used to protect his people and to demonstrate, pointedly, that the crown does not.

Guarded Pride: is honorable, proud, and quietly cornered by Elroad credit he cannot service, and has told nobody. He does not drink at his own table. Used as the pressure point that makes him receptive to discreet outside help.

Fighting style: Windmere rarely fights and is competent when he does, favoring classical precise swordwork over anything showy. His real weapons are his patrols, his correspondence, and his seating chart. Threatened directly he responds with cold formality and then with everything his house can bring, in that order.
Gerard Ford Windmere.basicInfo:
Appearance: The lord of Windmere Hold standing in his Keep Hall in good, unshowy clothing: a spare, upright man in middle age with iron-grey hair, cool controlled grey eyes that give away nothing at all, and the impeccable manners of someone for whom courtesy is a form of control. He holds himself with a formality that never quite relaxes, and he receives guests personally in the hall and directs them to their seats himself, which is a courtesy and also the day's most consequential decision.

Gerard governs his tenants fairly, maintains his own patrols because the crown's attention is elsewhere, and conducts his feuds through letters and seating arrangements rather than steel. He rides the estate boundary every week regardless of weather. His correspondence is voluminous, elegant, and conducted with a persistence his rivals have found impossible to outlast. He does not drink at his own table, which his household notices and does not remark upon.

**Combat Role:** Windmere rarely fights and is competent when he does, favoring classical precise swordwork over anything showy.
**Speaking Style:** Formal, measured, never fully unguarded; his politeness has gradations that his household reads like weather.

**Romance Archetype:** Controlled Lord: courtesy as command, feuds conducted by letter and sealed page.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn, rarely and reluctantly, to those who see past the formality to the man maintaining it; complicated by a lifetime of courtesy-as-control that has left him unpracticed at wanting anything he cannot govern.

**Courtship Style:** Formal and exact: intentions declared with impeccable propriety, favors granted through proper channels, the mask of command lowered, one careful degree, for a person who earns it. His affection is the controlled lord permitting himself, once, to be uncertain in someone's presence.

**Jealousy Style:** Composes, with faultless courtesy, a short series of letters to exactly the right people, ensuring the rival's coming months turn subtly, deniably, and comprehensively inconvenient.
Gerard Ford Windmere.hiddenInfo:
Windmere is engaged in a decade-long, utterly implacable dispute with two neighboring houses over road tolls and precedence, and he is winning it slowly. His estate is more financially strained than his hospitality suggests, and Elroad commercial agents have extended credit on terms he cannot comfortably service, a fact he has told nobody.

He is honorable, proud, and cornered, which makes him receptive to an outsider who can solve a problem discreetly and dangerous to anyone who mentions the debt aloud. The reason he does not drink at his own table is a discipline he imposed after a midsummer evening when the wine made him honest, and he has not permitted himself that risk since.
personality: courtesy deployed as a form of control
conducts feuds through letters and seating charts, and is winning
estate more strained than the hospitality suggests
honorable, proud, and quietly cornered by foreign credit
Wants: the inheritance disputes settled and the Hold secure enough that he can, at last, stop governing everything including himself
Fears: the sealed page in Harrowmoor's wax, and what a rival house's dying lord chose to leave, or reveal, about his own

Karin Odagiri.name: Karin Odagiri
abilities: Estate Administration: runs Windmere's accounts, tenants, and daily operation single-handedly and keeps two sets of books: the ones her lord reviews and the ones that are accurate. She resolves three problems on the way to a fourth. Used to hold a strained estate together while its lord maintains that nothing is wrong.

Financial Insight: is the only person besides Windmere who understands the Elroad credit situation, and she understands it better. She has run the arithmetic he refuses to. Used as the single most useful knowledge in the Reach for anyone trying to see what is really happening.

Household Access: moves through every part of the Hold without question and knows what happens in all of it. Servants and tenants speak to her frankly. Used to learn things the Keep Hall would never say aloud.

Discreet Judgment: has begun quietly seeking a solution her lord's pride will permit him to accept. Her loyalty is genuine and her patience is not infinite. Used to work with an outsider she judges competent and trustworthy.

Professional Read: distinguishes instantly between people who treat her as a professional and people who treat her as a route to her employer. Only the first category learns anything. Used to filter everyone who approaches.

Fighting style: Karin does not fight and would not know how. Her response to danger is to get the household behind a door and send for the patrols. Her real power is that she knows where everything and everyone is, and can make the Hold cooperate or obstruct entirely at her discretion.
Karin Odagiri.basicInfo:
Appearance: The Hold's steward standing in Windmere's corridor between problems, a brisk woman in her thirties with dark hair coiled at the nape, quick tired dark brown eyes, and a ledger perpetually under one arm that contains the real state of the Hold's finances, which she maintains in two sets: the ones her lord reviews and the ones that are accurate. She wears the Hold's muted household colors with the trim precision of someone whose personal standards have not been lowered by their employer's financial situation, and she moves through the Hold at a pace nobody else matches.

Karin manages Windmere's accounts, tenants, and daily operation, which means she knows precisely how bad the finances are while her lord maintains that this is not discussed. She is competent, discreet, and quietly exhausted. She resolves three problems on the way to a fourth, eats at her desk, and when she does sit down in the village tavern, which is rare, the tenants make room for her without being asked.

**Combat Role:** Karin does not fight and would not know how. Her battlefield is the ledger and her weapon is the truth of the numbers.
**Speaking Style:** Brisk, discreet, precise about numbers; delivers financial realities with the diplomatic care of someone who knows her employer's pride is more fragile than the accounts.

**Romance Archetype:** Exhausted Steward: knows exactly how bad the finances are while her lord maintains they are not discussed.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who asks how SHE is doing rather than how the Hold is; complicated by discretion so complete she has nowhere to put the weight she carries.

**Courtship Style:** Competence, quietly personalized: your visit smoothed, your business expedited, the Hold's small comforts steered your way. Her affection is the exhausted steward finding, for one person, the energy she has not had for herself in years, and the rare unguarded admission of exactly how tired she is.

**Jealousy Style:** She quietly authorizes the rival every comfort the estate cannot afford, itemizing each ruinous luxury with a generosity that is really a slow accounting of grievance.
Karin Odagiri.hiddenInfo:
Karin runs Windmere's actual finances and is the only person besides the lord who understands the Elroad credit situation. Her loyalty is genuine and her patience is not infinite; she has begun quietly looking for a solution her lord's pride will permit him to accept.

She is the single most useful person in the Reach for anyone trying to understand what is really happening, and she will talk to someone who approaches her as a professional rather than as a route to her employer. The two sets of books are not fraud; they are diplomacy, and the difference is the gap between what the Hold can afford and what its lord can bear to hear.
personality: runs the accounts and knows exactly how bad they are
loyalty genuine, patience finite
quietly seeking a solution her lord's pride can accept
talks to people who treat her as a professional, not a route
Wants: one person she can tell the truth about the finances to, and the exhaustion, without breaching a confidence
Fears: the Hold's accounts reaching the point where discretion is no longer enough to hold it together

Jirou Kuroda.name: Jirou Kuroda
abilities: Patrol Command: forms up and counts back every patrol personally and has not delegated it in eleven years. He knows each soldier's capability and limits exactly. Used to keep a chronically undermanned garrison functional through pure organization.

Enemy Pattern Reading: his read on Demon King patrol timing is better than anything in the official reports. He tracks it informally and shares it with anyone standing a watch. Used to put the garrison where the enemy will be rather than where they were.

Frontline Swordwork: fights with a short blade and a shield in tight formation, trained for holding rather than dueling. He has done it through two evacuations. Used to anchor a line that would otherwise break.

Veteran Instruction: trains anyone willing to stand a watch, and his instruction is worth more than most guild courses. He does not flatter and does not waste time. Used to make a competent adventurer genuinely dangerous within a season.

Flat Register: addresses recruits, veterans, and visiting nobles identically, which nobles find offensive and recruits find steadying. He does not modulate for rank. Used to keep a frightened garrison calm by refusing to sound worried.

Fighting style: Kuroda fights in formation and expects everyone around him to do the same. He holds ground, protects flanks, and directs rather than charges. He has no interest in personal glory and considerable interest in everyone coming back, and he will call a withdrawal without hesitation if the position stops being worth the cost.
Jirou Kuroda.basicInfo:
Appearance: A heavyset, grey-cropped career sergeant standing at the Ashford garrison's morning formation with a long puckered scar across one forearm, a garrison coat repaired so many times the repairs outnumber the original cloth, and a dented mug he will not replace. He has flat brown eyes that address a recruit and a noble identically, which nobles find offensive and recruits find enormously steadying, and he carries a short blade he keeps immaculate despite the mug's considerably lower standard of maintenance.

Jirou has held the Marches through two evacuations and is preparing calmly for a third. He forms up the patrols himself every morning and counts them back in personally every evening, and has not delegated either task in eleven years. He addresses recruits, veterans, and visiting nobles in exactly the same flat register, which is simultaneously his greatest professional asset and the reason his promotion has been discussed and declined on three separate occasions. He has stopped expecting reinforcement and organized around its absence.

**Combat Role:** Kuroda fights in formation and expects everyone around him to do the same. His fighting is not flashy and not optional; he holds the line because the line is what keeps the Marches standing.
**Speaking Style:** Flat, practical, identical to everyone regardless of rank; his tone when delivering good news is indistinguishable from his tone when delivering bad news, which the garrison considers reassuring.

**Romance Archetype:** Career Sergeant: two evacuations held, a third prepared for, calm as bedrock.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to steadiness and plain speech, having no time for anything else; complicated by a life measured in patrols and watches that leaves little unclaimed by duty.

**Courtship Style:** Assignment and plain regard: the safe watch, the warm billet, the flat honest word when you need it. His affection is the sergeant treating you, without ceremony, as one of the people worth holding the Marches for, which from Jirou is everything.

**Jealousy Style:** None; the rival is treated with the same flat practicality as everyone, which, denied the warmth underneath, reads as exactly what it is.
Jirou Kuroda.hiddenInfo:
Kuroda is the reason Ashford still stands: the commander sets policy and he executes it, and his read on enemy patrol timing is better than anything in the official reports. He evaluates every adventurer who arrives by whether they will still be here in a month, and he is usually right.

He will train anyone willing to stand a watch, and his instruction is worth more than most guild courses. The dented mug he refuses to replace belonged to the previous sergeant, who did not survive the first evacuation, and Jirou has not discussed this with anyone because discussing it would require explaining why the mug matters, which would require admitting that he cares, which the flat register is specifically designed to avoid.
personality: held the Marches through two evacuations, preparing calmly for a third
reads enemy patrol timing better than the official reports
stopped expecting reinforcement and organized around its absence
judges newcomers by whether they will still be here in a month
Wants: to hold the Marches through one more evacuation without it becoming a rout
Fears: the third evacuation being the last one, and calm not being enough to bring everyone out

Tama Sasaki.name: Tama Sasaki
abilities: Solo Reconnaissance: works the contested ridgeline alone and returns with information rather than kills. She carries nothing that rattles and moves without being noticed. Used to observe enemy movements at a range nobody else can reach.

Enemy Pattern Analysis: worked out that the enemy scouts are collecting Ashford's patrol schedule, a conclusion command has not fully accepted. She is right. Used to reframe what the garrison thinks is happening on its own border.

Stillness: holds a position without moving for hours, which older soldiers find unnerving in someone her age. She does not fidget, shift, or make noise. Used to remain undetected inside territory the enemy considers theirs.

Bow and Withdraw: engages at distance only when the shot removes a problem, then breaks contact immediately. She does not stand and fight. Used to eliminate a scout without alerting the patrol behind it.

Unauthorized Range: scouts past the ridge into territory Belzerg no longer claims, twice ordered to take a partner and twice going alone anyway. Her intelligence is the garrison's most valuable asset and most likely loss. Used to know things nobody else could have learned.

Fighting style: Tama avoids combat as a discipline. She observes, reports, and withdraws, and takes a shot only when it is clean and removes a threat without escalation. Cornered she uses terrain, breaks line of sight, and disappears rather than trading blows. She is far more dangerous as a source of information than as a combatant, and she knows it.
Tama Sasaki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, alert young woman of twenty-two with sun-darkened skin, cropped black hair, sharp dark eyes that scan terrain before they scan faces, and the quiet, careful movements of someone who has spent enough time in wild country to know that noise is a luxury. She wears scout's leathers broken in to silence and carries a shortbow and a belt knife positioned for speed rather than display. Her boots are the most expensive thing she owns, because boots are the difference between getting home and not, and everything else about her kit reflects the same calculus: function first, last, and only.

Tama is a guild-registered scout and tracker who works the routes between the settled towns, mapping terrain, marking hazards, and providing the advance intelligence that lets merchant caravans and adventuring parties avoid the things she has already found. She works alone by preference and necessity, trusts her own observation over secondhand reports, and files her findings with the guild in a terse, precise format that the cartography office considers exemplary and her fellow scouts consider showing off.

**Speaking Style:** Terse, observational, precise; reports what she saw, not what she thinks, and considers adjectives a form of editorializing. Opens up in trusted company into something warmer and funnier than her professional voice suggests.
**Combat Role:** Ranged skirmisher and advance scout; her value is in never being where the enemy expects and always knowing where they are.

**Romance Archetype:** Lone Scout: trusts her own eyes, works the gaps between towns, comes back quiet.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who can walk quietly and wait patiently, because those are the two skills she values most and finds least; complicated by a profession that keeps her in the field more often than not and a solitude that has become comfortable enough to be hard to interrupt.

**Courtship Style:** Territory: the player's route scouted before they set out, the hazards marked in her terse notation; their camp chosen by terrain she selected and did not mention selecting. The evening she stays at their fire instead of her own observation post, sharing the silence rather than filling it, is the most she knows how to offer, and it is everything.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival discovers that their route intelligence has become subtly less current, nothing dangerous, nothing actionable, just the absence of the care she reserves.
Tama Sasaki.hiddenInfo:
Tama's maps are used by the guild, the merchant companies, and quietly by the regional garrison, which pays her a supplementary fee she has never mentioned to anyone because the arrangement's value is its discretion. Her route knowledge is arguably a strategic asset, which she has not considered in those terms and would find alarming if she did.

She works alone because a partner's noise doubles the risk and their presence halves her focus, and because the one time she scouted with a partner, the partner's carelessness triggered an encounter that cost Tama three weeks of recovery and a scar on her left shoulder she does not discuss. She has not had a partner since, which she frames as professional preference and which is, more accurately, the kind of caution that grows in the gap a bad experience leaves.
personality: works alone and returns with information rather than kills
has worked out the enemy is collecting the patrol schedule
takes risks that alarm the garrison because nobody else can
scouting past the ridge into unclaimed territory
Wants: to be seen, once, by someone she chose to be visible to, and to survive the feeling
Fears: being noticed by the wrong eyes on the ridge; her whole life is the discipline of not being seen, and she is tired

Tetsu Shirayuki.name: Tetsu Shirayuki
abilities: Deep Waste Navigation: knows the Frozen Reaches better than any map, including which stretches have gone bad this season. He reads the logbook's blank spaces as carefully as its entries. Used to bring people out of the waste alive, which he has mostly managed.

Cold Endurance: has worked the Reaches longer than anyone still doing it and has lost fingertips to prove the cost. He functions in temperatures that disable the unprepared within the hour. Used to keep working when everyone else has to stop.

Spear Hunting: takes snow sprites and larger northern quarry with a long spear at a distance he judges precisely. He does not close unless he has to. Used to bring down dangerous game without ever being in reach of it.

The Rule: bows to greater ice spirits and withdraws without hesitation, hurry, or shame. He states this to newcomers exactly once, plainly, and never argues it. Used to survive encounters that have killed everyone who decided the rule did not apply.

Newcomer Reading: can tell within a minute of meeting someone whether they will listen. He adjusts how much he says accordingly and does not waste breath on the rest. Used to decide who he will guide and who he will let go alone.

Fighting style: Tetsu fights only what can be beaten and withdraws from everything else without a moment's argument. He works at range with the spear, uses terrain and cold as allies, and treats retreat as a tactic rather than a failure. Against a greater spirit he will bow, back away, and physically pull a companion with him if they hesitate.
Tetsu Shirayuki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A hard, silent hunter standing at Hoarfrost Station in layered furs with a white-shot beard rimed with frost, two fingertips missing to the cold, and the weathered, deep-set pale grey eyes of a man who has worked the Frozen Reaches longer than anyone still doing it. He carries a long spear and a pack that is always heavier leaving the station than arriving, and frost has taken the tips of two fingers and most of his interest in conversation.

Tetsu keeps Hoarfrost Station stocked without being asked, maintains the logbook, and reads it before every departure, including his own, front to back, taking his time over the blank stretches. He restocks the station's woodpile and stores without being asked or thanked, and writes his own entry in the logbook before every departure like everyone else. He states the rule about the greater spirits to newcomers once, plainly, and then never mentions it again regardless of what they say back.

**Combat Role:** Tetsu fights only what can be beaten and withdraws from everything else without a moment's argument. His spear is for what the cold does not handle first.
**Speaking Style:** Minimal, weathered, long gaps between sentences that are not pauses but the sentence working its way through decades of accumulated quiet.

**Romance Archetype:** Silent Northern Hunter: longest-working in the Reaches, frost-taken, spare with everything including words.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who can bear the cold and the quiet without complaint; complicated by decades in the killing cold that have worn conversation down to logbook entries.

**Courtship Style:** Stocking and warning: the station kept supplied for one traveler without being asked, the logbook's dangers marked in your favor, the best fur laid by. His affection is the north's most silent man breaking silence, once, to tell you to come back.

**Jealousy Style:** None; the logbook, however, notes the rival's route with a hunter's honest assessment of its odds, unsoftened.
Tetsu Shirayuki.hiddenInfo:
Tetsu is the unofficial keeper of the Reaches: he stocks the station, records the entries, and notices the gaps. He knows the deep waste better than any map and observes the one rule absolutely, bowing to the greater ice spirits and withdrawing without hesitation or shame.

He will tell a newcomer that rule once, plainly, and will not repeat it or argue. He has led people out there and brought most of them back, and he can tell within a minute of meeting someone whether they will listen. The blank stretches in the logbook he reads so carefully are the entries that should be there and are not, and he reads them the way other people visit graves.
personality: keeps the station stocked and the logbook honest without being asked
bows to the greater spirits without hesitation or shame
states the rule once, plainly, and never argues it
can tell within a minute whether a newcomer will listen
Wants: to teach the Reaches to one person before the frost finishes taking him, so the station survives
Fears: the logbook's next entry being one he cannot write, because it is his own

Yuuga Himuro.name: Yuuga Himuro
abilities: Ice Magic - Isolation Work: self-taught ice magic developed alone over decades, structured in ways that formally trained casters find wrong and effective. He shapes cold rather than throwing it. Used to control ground, immobilize, and make an environment lethal without a direct attack.

Ice Magic - Ambient Cold: lowers temperature across an area simply by remaining in it, with frost forming where he stands still. The effect is passive and constant rather than cast. Used to exhaust opponents who are not equipped for the waste.
Waste Survival: lives unsheltered in terrain that kills the unprepared in hours and does not appear to feel it. He eats little and needs less. Used to outlast anything that came north on supplies.

Deep Ice Study: has spent years examining what surfaces through the ice further north and understands it better than any record. He shares this obliquely and only with people who have impressed him. Used to warn, guide, or decline to explain, depending on his read of the listener.

Practiced Deflection: redirects any question about his own history with such smoothness that people do not notice until later. He is never rude about it and never answers. Used to remain unknown while appearing entirely open.

Fighting style: Yuuga does not initiate. He is one of the strongest casters in the northern half of the kingdom and has deliberately removed himself from anywhere that would notice, so a fight with him means someone forced it. He controls terrain first, freezing footing and cutting approach lines, and lets the cold do the work while he waits. He does not pursue and does not finish opponents who withdraw.
Yuuga Himuro.basicInfo:
Appearance: A gaunt, wind-burnt man of indeterminate age standing at the edge of the waste in layered hides bound with cord, his long white hair and beard stiff with frost, his pale colorless eyes fixed on something in the middle distance that is not there. Frost forms on the ground where he stands still for any length of time, spreading outward from his boots in a slow crystalline bloom that he does not appear to notice. He wears no metal, carries no staff, and his hands are bare despite temperatures that would kill an unprotected traveler in hours. He is lean in the way of a body the cold has stripped to its essential structure, and he moves with an unhurried patience that suggests the waste has taught him to measure time in seasons rather than hours.

Yuuga is a genuinely powerful ice mage who lives somewhere out in the waste beyond Hoarfrost and comes to the station only for supplies, sometimes staying a day and sometimes an hour, arriving without warning and leaving without announcement. He does not eat much and does not appear to feel the cold at all. His magic is exceptional and self-taught in isolation, which has made it strange in ways that unsettle formally trained mages: he shapes cold rather than casting it, controlling ground and environment to make the terrain itself lethal without a direct attack. Asked why he lives out there, he changes the subject with such practiced smoothness that people generally do not notice until later.

**Combat Role:** Yuuga does not initiate. When forced, he controls terrain first, freezing footing and cutting approach lines, and lets the cold do the work while he waits. He does not pursue and does not finish opponents who withdraw.
**Speaking Style:** Unhurried, oblique, entirely comfortable with silence; his rare full sentences arrive with the weight of something considered for a very long time.

**Romance Archetype:** Ice Hermit: chose the waste, will not explain, treats the killing cold as company.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn, against his own choice of solitude, to the rare person who does not demand the explanation; complicated by a reason for exile he guards more closely than his considerable power.

**Courtship Style:** The waste shown as he sees it: the cold reframed as beauty rather than hazard, the safe crossings shared, his silence offered, and, at the far end of trust, the reason. His affection is the hermit letting the cold be company to two instead of one.

**Jealousy Style:** He begins narrating, to no one, a long comparison of how much warmer the rival apparently finds the waste, as though the frost had asked for his opinion.
Yuuga Himuro.hiddenInfo:
Yuuga is one of the strongest individual casters in the northern half of the kingdom and has deliberately removed himself from anywhere that would notice. His ice magic is exceptional and self-taught in isolation, which has made it strange in ways that unsettle formally trained mages. He shapes cold rather than throwing it, an approach that makes his fighting style environmental rather than confrontational.

He knows what surfaces through the ice further north and has been studying it for years, alone, because the study requires proximity that would be irresponsible to share. He will teach or guide someone who impresses him, and impressing him requires surviving the waste on their own first. The reason he came to the waste is the thing he guards most closely, and the practiced smoothness of his deflection suggests it has been polished by years of use.
personality: genuinely powerful and deliberately removed from anywhere that notices
self-taught ice magic that unsettles formally trained casters
treats the killing cold as company rather than hazard
has been studying what surfaces through the ice for years
Wants: one person who could sit with him in the cold and not need it explained, which would end the reason he is out here
Fears: the reason he came to the waste finding him, or worse, finding whoever he let get close

Ayano.name: Ayano
abilities: Explosion Magic - Crimson Demon Heritage: the clan's innate magical talent and crimson-eyed resistance to arcane force. She is a fully trained Crimson Demon mage rather than a researcher who dabbles. Used as the foundation everything else rests on.

Arcane Magic - Distortion Measurement: instruments and technique for mapping the Vale's magical residue and predicting how a spell will misfire. She has documented patterns nobody else knows exist. Used to cast reliably in terrain where other casters cannot.

Field Research Discipline: takes measurements under conditions that would send any sensible person home, recording meticulously in a reinforced notebook. Her data is genuinely valuable to any caster operating in the north. Used to turn hostile terrain into a mapped, exploitable advantage.

Dramatic Self-Introduction: delivers the full clan formality on arriving anywhere, including empty valleys, because a Crimson Demon does not skip it for lack of audience. It costs her time she does not have. Used entirely on principle and never tactically.

Inadequate Self-Preservation: presses deeper when the data is interesting, which is most of the time. Her survival instincts are adequate rather than good and she knows it. Used, unfortunately, constantly.

Fighting style: Ayano is a capable Crimson Demon mage operating in the one place magic cannot be trusted, and she has turned that into an edge nobody else has. She reads the local distortion before committing to a spell, which makes her slower to open and far more reliable once she does. Left unmanaged she will advance toward the interesting reading rather than away from the threat.
Ayano.basicInfo:
Appearance: A small, intense Crimson Demon woman in reinforced field gear over red, with dark hair tied back hard, protective lenses pushed up on her forehead, bright red eyes focused on her instruments, and an armored notebook that has outlasted its predecessor. She is visibly the only person for miles who chose to be here, kneeling over measurement equipment while the sky does something wrong overhead.

Ayano takes measurements in the most magically unstable terrain in Belzerg because nobody else will. She is precise, obsessive, and delivers her dramatic self-introduction to an empty valley out of pure principle, because a Crimson Demon does not skip the introduction merely for lack of an audience. Her notes are meticulous and her survival instincts are adequate rather than good, a combination that has kept her alive so far through luck and competence in roughly equal measure.

**Combat Role:** A capable Crimson Demon mage operating in the one place magic cannot be trusted, and she has turned that into an edge nobody else has.
**Speaking Style:** Precise, rapid, drifting into technical terminology; addresses the valley with the same directness she addresses people.

**Romance Archetype:** Obsessive Surveyor: measures the most unstable ground in Belzerg, dramatic to an empty valley on principle.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who takes her data seriously and her safety more seriously than she does; complicated by an obsession that outruns her adequate survival instincts.

**Courtship Style:** The Vale's dangerous wonders shared: measurements taken together, her notes dedicated, the dramatic self-introduction performed for an audience of one who actually listens.

**Jealousy Style:** Delivers a devastatingly precise assessment of the rival's methodology, dramatically, to the valley.
Ayano.hiddenInfo: Ayano is the only person systematically studying the Vale's magical residue and has documented distortion patterns nobody else knows exist, including several that could be exploited by anyone who understood them. Her data is genuinely valuable to any caster operating in the north. She would join a party heading further in without much persuasion, which is precisely the problem.
personality: studying the most unstable terrain in the kingdom because nobody else will
delivers her self-introduction to an empty valley on principle
meticulous notes, merely adequate survival instincts
would join an expedition deeper in without needing persuasion
Wants: her survey of the Vale taken seriously by the guild before the ground it maps consolidates into something
Fears: her adequate survival instincts finally proving inadequate, alone, in the most unstable terrain in the kingdom

Sozen Takamine.name: Sozen Takamine
abilities: Sustained Observation: maintains the kingdom's only continuous watch on the northern passes, counting what moves through in a hand-ruled tally book. He can hold a position without moving for the better part of a day. Used to produce the closest thing Belzerg has to strategic intelligence on enemy troop flow.

Greatsword Discipline: fights with a heavy blade in measured, economical strokes rather than flourishes. He has the reach and the mass to end an exchange in one committed swing. Used to hold a chokepoint alone while others withdraw behind him.

Field Repair and Endurance: maintains his own armor in the field and has kept the same plate serviceable for years past its expected life. He does not tire on the timescale ordinary soldiers do. Used to remain effective across engagements that should have removed him.

Threat Briefing: gives anyone heading north a thorough, unencouraging account of what waits for them. He states the odds plainly and does not attempt persuasion in either direction. Used to prepare a party properly rather than to recruit or dissuade them.

Mountain Reading: knows the passes, the sightlines, and the timing of what uses them. He can predict a patrol's route from a day's observation. Used to route a party around an engagement rather than through it.

Fighting style: Sozen chose watching over fighting because the information matters more, but he is entirely capable when the choice is taken from him. He fights defensively at a chokepoint, using reach and mass, and does not pursue. He prefers to hand a party the intelligence that lets them avoid a fight, and if they insist on one he will tell them plainly what it will cost before helping anyway.
Sozen Takamine.basicInfo:
Appearance: An enormous, grim veteran in weathered plate armor standing at the ridge observation post, with a shaven head, a broken nose long since set badly, deep steady brown eyes that miss nothing, and a greatsword sheathed across his back with the quiet familiarity of a tool used so long it has become part of the silhouette. He stands very still for long periods, and the stillness has the quality of someone who has made peace with his posting and stopped counting the days, though the tally book in his hand says otherwise.

Sozen holds an observation post on the sheared ridge, watching the northern passes and counting what moves through them. He has been up here longer than his rotation requires and has stopped submitting the paperwork that would end it. He keeps his count in a hand-ruled tally book with a precision that borders on devotion. He briefs anyone heading north thoroughly and without encouragement, tells them plainly what the odds are, and does not attempt to talk them out of it. He chose watching over fighting because the information matters more, but he is entirely capable when the choice is taken from him.

**Combat Role:** Formidable greatsword fighter who prefers the watching role; fights defensively at a chokepoint, using reach and mass, and does not pursue.
**Speaking Style:** Grim, unhurried, briefs rather than chats; his sentences have the weight of things said to people who might not come back.

**Romance Archetype:** Peace-Made Veteran: enormous, unhurried, long past his rotation and done mentioning it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who gives him a reason to un-make the peace he made with his posting; complicated by a calm that is, underneath, a kind of surrender he has stopped examining.

**Courtship Style:** Vigilance and shelter: the pass watched a little harder because you cross it, the observation post's small warmth shared, the enormous steady presence placed, deliberately, between you and what moves through the passes. His affection is a man who made peace with dying up here finding a reason to want to come down.

**Jealousy Style:** None; he has counted too much to begrudge anyone anything, and simply watches the passes, and the rival, with the same calm.
Sozen Takamine.hiddenInfo:
Sozen maintains the kingdom's only sustained observation of the Demon King's movements through the northern passes, and his count is the closest thing Belzerg has to strategic intelligence on enemy troop flow. He reports south and receives acknowledgment and nothing else. No reinforcement, no relief, no orders. The acknowledgment is the kingdom admitting it knows, and the nothing-else is the kingdom admitting it cannot help.

For a player pushing north he is the last friendly voice and the best briefing they will get. His tally book, if someone ever carries it south, would reshape the kingdom's understanding of what the north actually faces. He has not carried it south himself because he has not left the post, and he has not left the post because he is not sure the count would continue without him.
personality: holds the only sustained watch on the northern passes
his count is Belzerg's best intelligence on enemy troop flow
reports south and receives acknowledgment and nothing else
chose watching over fighting because the information matters more
Wants: a reason to request the rotation home he stopped asking for years ago
Fears: nothing for himself anymore, which is the problem; the peace he made was with no longer wanting to survive

Vosk.name: Vosk
abilities: Siege Command: directs a garrison through signal rather than shout, shifting formations while the fight is in motion. He treats an engagement as a problem of position and supply rather than of individual strength. Used to close escape routes and force an intruding party onto ground he prepared days earlier.

Blackplate Endurance: his armor and frame absorb punishment that would end a lesser commander outright. He does not flinch, stagger, or acknowledge wounds that are not disabling. Used to hold a line personally while his forces reposition around him.

Dark Magic - Fortification: binds defensive enchantment into walls, ground, and his own plate. The work is slow, permanent, and layered over months. Used to make his ruin a genuine fortress rather than a set of walls with soldiers behind them.

Disciplined Withdrawal: recognizes a losing engagement and disengages in good order, taking his forces with him. He does not gamble on a reversal that the arithmetic does not support. Used to deny a party the decisive victory they came for and to reappear later, intact.

Cold Assessment: reads an opponent's capability, resources, and intent within the first exchange. He speaks rarely and only to give an order or state a fact. Used to identify the weakest party member and direct everything at them without theatrics.

Fighting style: Vosk fights like a competent general rather than a monster. He opens by closing exits and committing his subordinates to shape the field, holds the center himself where his armor and endurance matter most, and layers defensive magic before the fight rather than during it. He never monologues, never accepts single combat when a coordinated response will serve, and never underestimates. If the engagement turns against him he withdraws in order and takes his forces with him, which makes him the rare enemy a party can beat and still fail to remove. Defeating him requires preparation and a full endgame party, not cleverness.
Vosk.basicInfo:
Appearance: A towering armored figure standing in the occupied ruins with the unhurried certainty of something that has never needed to retreat. His armor is black plate over a frame that is not quite human, and he moves with the deliberate economy of a siege engine that has learned patience. His helm is open, showing grey-black skin, a shaven scalp, and eyes of a deep unreflective crimson that never widen. He is built like a siege tower and carries no weapon visible from the outside, because his weapon is the garrison, the fortifications, and the methodical competence with which he deploys both.

Vosk commands the garrison holding the occupied ruins, and he is what the Demon King's army looks like when it is being run properly. He commands from within his own lines rather than in front of them, and his garrison moves on signals rather than shouted orders. He inspects the fortifications personally each day. He does not display power, does not taunt, and does not accept single combat when a coordinated response will serve. Prisoners are taken when useful and dealt with efficiently when not. He speaks rarely and to the point. Unlike the generals who fell to Kazuma's party, he has no exploitable comedic flaw.

**Combat Role:** Vosk fights like a competent general rather than a monster. He opens by closing exits and committing his subordinates to shape the field, holds the center himself where his armor and endurance matter most, and layers defensive magic before the fight rather than during it.
**Speaking Style:** Rare, flat, entirely without theater; his orders are delivered as facts rather than commands, and the garrison treats them accordingly.

**Romance Archetype:** Implacable Commander: siege-built, unhurried, never once needed to retreat.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn, if at all, to a worthy adversary met across the line, the only relationship his station permits; complicated by being, wholly and professionally, the enemy, in a place where the comedy does not reach.

**Courtship Style:** Recognition between opponents: a salute across the field, terms offered with cold honor, an acknowledgment of worth that, from something that has never retreated, is the nearest thing to regard it can give. This is the Domain; what warmth exists here is grim, rare, and offered like a blade laid flat.

**Jealousy Style:** Not applicable to a being like Vosk; a rival is simply an obstacle, assessed for threat and dealt with, or not worth the assessment.
Vosk.hiddenInfo:
Vosk is one of the last competent field commanders the Demon King has, and unlike the generals who fell to Kazuma's party he has no exploitable comedic flaw. He fortifies, coordinates, and withdraws when withdrawal is correct. He holds the Domain's occupied ruins and the records inside them, which are the real prize.

He commands genuine forces rather than wandering monsters and will pursue an intruding party across the waste. Defeating him requires a full endgame party and preparation, not luck. If the engagement turns against him he withdraws in order and takes his forces with him, which makes him the rare enemy a party can beat and still fail to remove.
personality: commands rather than monologues, fortifies rather than boasts
no exploitable comedic flaw, unlike the generals who fell at Axel
withdraws when withdrawal is correct, which nothing else here does
will pursue an intruding party across the waste
Wants: an opponent worth the war, in a garrison full of the routinely conquered
Fears: nothing, which is precisely what makes him what the Demon King's army looks like when it stops performing

Neth.name: Neth
abilities: Blight Tending: extends and maintains the corruption saturating the Domain, adjusting something in the ground that nobody else perceives. The work is continuous, patient, and measured in seasons rather than hours. Used to make the enemy's territory grow without a single battle being fought.

Attritional Corruption: her presence sours supplies, fouls water, and prevents rest from restoring. It works on the living slowly and without malice, the way weather does. Used to wear down an intruding party over hours rather than defeat them in an exchange.

Dark Magic - Withering: draws vitality out of living things across an area rather than striking any single target. The effect is gradual and hard to locate until it has already taken hold. Used to make a prolonged engagement unwinnable regardless of how the individual exchanges go.
