Her ledger's real value is pattern: she can tell when a merchant house is moving goods ahead of bad news, when garrison traffic means the front has shifted, and when the same face crossing south three times under different manifests means something the capital should hear about. Twice in her tenure she has written a quiet letter north that preceded an arrest by exactly the travel time. She keeps the iron whistle clause memorized and a space on her guest stool mentally reserved; her predecessor told her, on his last day, that he had met the bearer once, said nothing else, and smiled about it for the rest of the afternoon, and Kanae has been keeping the kettle warm on the strength of that smile for eleven years.
personality: Level, incorruptible, and quietly omniscient about everything that crosses her river; fairness is both her creed and her fortification
Charges dukes and drovers by the same schedule and recites the relevant clause before the coin is asked
Fair to everyone, warm to regulars, and watchful in a way only the ledger ever finds out about
Wants: the iron whistle bearer to finally cross on her watch, just once, so she can learn what her predecessor smiled about for eleven years
Fears: a flood year the toll surplus cannot cover, or a promotion to somewhere with no river to keep

Goro Hanamura.name: Goro Hanamura
abilities: Contract Routing: sorts quests, transfers, and adventurers between the Axel jurisdiction and the capital's with the dispassion of a freight junction. His split posting board is studied by other branches. Used all day; the board is never empty.

The Rebuttal Form: author of the guild's preemptive complaint form, which answers the eleven most common grievances before they are filed and has reduced desk arguments by two thirds. Used constantly, laminated, cited by other branches like case law.

Adventurer Triage: assesses a party's actual capability, as opposed to their card ranks and their self-description, within one conversation, and routes them to work that will neither bore nor kill them. Used quietly; the routing is the mercy.
Fighting style: Goro was a mid-rank adventurer for nine years and fights like a man who retired on purpose: economically, defensively, and while already filling out the incident report in his head.
Goro Hanamura.basicInfo:
Appearance: A dry, methodical man in his mid-forties with a clerk's posture built over an adventurer's frame that still shows at the shoulders and forearms. His face is lined and watchful behind square spectacles, with the particular expression of someone who has seen every possible way a person can overestimate themselves and no longer finds it funny. His dark hair is greying at the temples in a way that looks less distinguished than exhausted, and he wears the waystation guild's brown-and-green uniform with the sleeves rolled precisely to the elbow, ink-stained fingers, and a posture that switches from desk-clerk stillness to combat alertness so fast travelers occasionally flinch.

Goro is the clerk of Millbridge's waystation guildpost: nine years adventuring at mid rank, retired with all his limbs and a certain expression, now operating the junction through which every adventurer moving between Axel and the capital gets sorted. His posting board is split ruthlessly down the middle, his paperwork is preemptive, and his assessment of a party's real capability takes one conversation and is never wrong by more than a rank. He maintains a small unlabeled drawer of condolence-letter templates that he genuinely hopes never to need and refills twice a year.

**Speaking Style:** Dry, clipped, form-referenced. His rare compliments are phrased as routing decisions.

**Combat Role:** Fights like a man who retired on purpose: economically, defensively, and while already filling out the incident report in his head.

**Romance Archetype:** Retired-Adventurer Clerk: nine years at mid rank, a certain expression, now sorts everyone else.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the adventurer who reminds him why he did it before it wore him down. Complicated by a posting board he splits ruthlessly and a retirement that was less a choice than an exhaustion.

**Courtship Style:** Sorting, in your favor: the good postings steered your way, the survivable jobs flagged, the dry clerk's hard-won knowledge shared with one person he does not want on the board's worse half.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's name lands, ruthlessly, on the harder side of the board, per an assessment Goro will defend as strictly objective.
Goro Hanamura.hiddenInfo: Goro's routing is quietly load-bearing for the whole southern guild system: Axel's survival rate for rookies is partly his doing, because parties heading south get routed to work at their real level and parties heading north get one conversation designed to make the unready turn back without knowing they were turned. His nine years at mid rank ended at Keele's Dungeon, where his party of five went in and three came out, an event he has never discussed and which is why the condolence drawer is his and why it is unlabeled. He and Luna in Axel maintain a correspondence that consists, on paper, of contract transfers, and functions, in practice, as the two best-informed people in the southern guild comparing notes on which parties worry them.
personality: Core: dry, exact, and running a rescue operation disguised as an administrative desk; the routing is the kindness and he will deny both
Wants: the condolence drawer to stay full; the rebuttal form adopted kingdom-wide; one year, just one, with no file moving to the drawer
Fears: recognizing his own old party in a new one and routing them anyway; the day the board's north side outgrows the south
Quirk: alphabetizes reflexively under stress, including other people's belongings
Pattern: assesses everyone, flatters no one, and buries the mercy so deep in procedure that nobody has ever caught him at it
Wants: to keep one promising adventurer alive long enough to retire on purpose rather than by attrition
Fears: recognizing his own nine-years-ago expression on someone he sorts onto a job he knows the odds of

Isao Tsurumaki.name: Isao Tsurumaki
abilities: Frontier Veterancy: eight years on the northern line before rotation south, and the drill-ground authority that comes with it. Recruits shape up fast under a man who has seen Mook Promotion work. Used on the muster ground daily.

The Pitch: the army's recruitment case, delivered honestly, which is the problem: he refuses to lie about the pay, the food, or the north, and his numbers are catastrophic and his retention is the best in the kingdom. Used monthly, against quota, like a siege.

Desertion Forensics: the fort's reluctant expert on why soldiers leave, informed by the sealed Axel Incident file, which he has read forty times and can recite. Used in reports the capital requests and then ignores.

Fighting style: Tsurumaki fights like the frontier taught him: shield discipline, short economical strikes, and a total absence of heroics. He drills recruits to survive first and impress nobody, and his old units' casualty rates argue the method.
Isao Tsurumaki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad, weathered veteran in his early forties with a voice like cart wheels on gravel, a jaw set in permanent dissatisfaction with the kingdom's military compensation structure, and the thick-necked, heavy-shouldered build of a man who spent eight years on the northern line before rotation south. His face is scarred at the brow and deeply lined, his dark hair is cropped to military regulation, and his eyes carry the specific bitterness of a man whose monthly quota competes against guild wages, adventurer glamour, and Axel's entire way of life. He wears the recruitment office's dress uniform with the same care and the same slight angle he applies to the campaign posters on his office wall.

Isao is the recruitment sergeant of Fort Meridian, running the least enviable sales operation in the kingdom with dogged honesty. He refuses to glamorize the pay, the food, or the front, which ruins his numbers and means the recruits he does sign stay signed. His office wall carries the heroic campaign posters the capital sends, hung with perfect regulation care, at a one-degree angle, which is the only editorial comment regulation permits him.

**Speaking Style:** Gravel, short sentences, quota-adjacent profanity. Sincerity surfaces as increased gruffness.

**Combat Role:** Fights like the frontier taught him: shield discipline, short economical strikes, and a total absence of heroics.

**Romance Archetype:** Bitter Recruitment Sergeant: the worst sales job in the kingdom, quota against Axel's whole way of life.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the rare recruit who signs for the right reasons. Complicated by a bitterness that has made warmth feel like a losing pitch.

**Courtship Style:** The honest recruitment, personalized: your service made survivable, the line's real dangers taught plainly, the gravel voice softening past the sales quota into something true.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival gets the full recruitment pitch, twice, in the voice of a man who has stopped believing his own quota.
Isao Tsurumaki.hiddenInfo: Tsurumaki wrote the review board's phrase "unfortunately reasonable" about the Axel Incident, and it cost him a promotion. His full report concluded that the deserters' economic analysis was correct, that the army's compensation structure could not compete with guild rates, and that the kingdom's actual military policy was to subsidize the war with adventurers and use the army to hold ground between their accidents. The capital buried the report. The paymaster's office strip-mines it for budget language annually. His honest pitch is not stubbornness but strategy: he is building the only kind of army he thinks the north deserves, one that was told the truth at the door.
personality: Core: gruff, honest, and loyal to the soldiers he does not yet have; runs recruitment as consumer protection and considers the quota someone else's fantasy
Wants: the compensation report unburied, credited, and acted on; one quota month, ever; his recruits to come back south someday, in any condition that walks
Fears: the pitch working on someone it should not; reading a name he signed in a casualty dispatch, which has happened nine times and he can list them
Quirk: hangs all official material at a one-degree angle; inspections have measured it and found it technically compliant
Pattern: honest to recruits, correct to superiors, and savage about the difference after two drinks in the mess
Wants: recruits who stay, and one connection that is not measured against a monthly number
Fears: the quota winning, the northern line thinning while Axel's taverns fill, and no pitch left in him to change it

Yasuko Onda.name: Yasuko Onda
abilities: Depot Mastery: complete command of Fort Meridian's supply chain, official and otherwise: what exists, where it is, what it is worth, and what it can be traded for. The second ledger is hers and balances to the copper. Used continuously; the depot is never closed to the right request.

Barter Architecture: the heartland's finest instinct for multi-party trades: boots for canvas for smoked fish for wagon grease for a favor to be named. Her chains of exchange have run to eleven links. Used to make the official system work despite itself.
Inspection Choreography: inspections of her depot pass flawlessly because the depot is flawless; the art is in what a flawless depot is arranged to make unaskable. Used twice a year, with tea.

Fighting style: Yasuko fights with logistics: in the one raid the depot has suffered, the attackers found the yard rearranged into a maze of crates, the garrison armed from stores in ninety seconds, and the exit blocked by a wagon that had, according to the ledger, always been there.
Yasuko Onda.basicInfo:
Appearance: A compact, brisk woman in her mid-thirties with sharp brown eyes that appraise everything at market value, dark hair pulled back in a regulation knot, and the particular energy of someone who is always, always in the middle of three transactions. She wears a quartermaster's uniform of sturdy olive canvas, immaculately pressed, with a clipboard worn smooth at the grip tucked under one arm and a stub of pencil behind one ear that she replaces weekly. Her hands are small, quick, and ink-stained from ledger work she does by lamplight while the depot sleeps. She has the transactional warmth of a merchant who happens to hold rank.

Yasuko is the quartermaster corporal of Fort Meridian and the operating intelligence of its depot. Officially she issues standard kit against signed requisitions. Actually she runs the heartland's most sophisticated barter economy: an eleven-link web of boots, canvas, smoked fish, and favors that keeps the fort supplied, the local villages solvent, and the official system upright like a scarecrow with good posture. Her ledgers are flawless. Both of them.

**Speaking Style:** Brisk, itemized, warmth embedded in trade terms. Her thank-yous arrive as discounts.

**Combat Role:** Fights with logistics. In the one raid the depot suffered, the attackers found the yard rearranged into a maze of crates, the garrison armed in ninety seconds, and the exit blocked by a wagon that had, according to the ledger, always been there.

**Romance Archetype:** Merchant in Rank: the depot's real intelligence, transactional warmth, holds the quartermaster's true power.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the soldier who returns kit clean and complete, the depot's one true courtship. Complicated by a role that makes every interaction a requisition.

**Courtship Style:** Allocation as affection: your kit the good stock, your requisitions expedited, and, rarest, something issued off the books with no favor logged against it.

**Jealousy Style:** Yasuko pretends not to notice the rival at all while noticing so intensely that she misplaces the ledger she has kept flawlessly for nine years.
Yasuko Onda.hiddenInfo: Yasuko runs the unrequisitioned winter-kit pipeline north: surplus cold-weather gear moves to frontier units whose allocations lapsed, funded from the barter margin, logged in a third ledger nobody knows exists. She inherited the pipeline from her predecessor with the depot keys and one sentence: "the paperwork failing does not mean they freeze." Her barter web's true masterpiece is that it has made the depot too useful to audit hostilely: half the heartland's villages and most of the garrison are somewhere in her chains of exchange, and unwinding her would unwind them. She prices favors carefully and calls in almost none, because the uncalled favors are the fortification.
personality: Core: brisk, warm, and quietly running a mercy operation inside a barter empire inside a military depot; every layer balances and only the deepest one matters to her
Wants: the winter pipeline never to be needed and always to be ready; an eleventh link that closes clean; the capital to keep finding the depot boring
Fears: an auditor with imagination; the third ledger outliving her without a successor who understands the sentence that came with the keys
Quirk: appraises everything on sight, aloud, in trade goods; a visiting baron was once valued at four wagons of turnips and has told the story at parties ever since, incorrectly, as a compliment
Pattern: never refuses a request outright; every no arrives as a counteroffer that turns out to be better
Wants: to run a depot honestly enough that she stops having to price the people in it
Fears: that transactional is the only warmth she has left, and even her kindness now comes with a favor owed

Benihime Kagura.name: Benihime Kagura
abilities: Grand Illusion: stagecraft-scale illusion magic of genuine artistry: light, image, and sound woven into spectacles that sell out the Eternal Lantern for a season at a time. Used nightly, at full commitment, regardless of house size.

The Persona: 'Benihime' is a complete construction, voice, walk, history and all, maintained in public without a single recorded lapse for nine years. Used as armor, brand, and, increasingly, load-bearing wall.

Crowd Command: reads and rules an audience of two thousand, and can stop a heckler, a brawl, or once an actual fire evacuation panic with voice and lightwork alone. Used as needed; the fire story is true and she closes conversations with it.
Fighting style: Benihime fights like a stage: misdirection, doubles, blinding cues, and an exit that was always there. Opponents beat three of her before the house lights come up on none of her.
Benihime Kagura.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, commanding figure of a woman in her late thirties with silver-streaked dark hair worn like a crown, sharp crimson eyes that she conceals behind stage cosmetics in public, and a presence so theatrically complete that she fills a room simply by pausing in its doorway. She wears crimson stage silks cut for maximum dramatic effect, layers of fabric that move like they have their own choreography, and carries herself with the measured grandeur of someone who decided long ago that if the world insists on watching, it will watch something worth the ticket. Offstage, her nine-second entrances are, by Crimson Demon standards, heroically restrained.

Benihime is the headline illusionist of the Nightless City's Eternal Lantern theater. Her shows are the city's flagship spectacle, illusion magic at a scale no rival house can match, and her offstage appearances are rationed like a currency she personally mints. She is dramatic in the manner of a woman who has made theater her armor, and her contempt for lazy stagecraft is the only review in the city that matters.

**Speaking Style:** Projected, precise, built in paragraphs. Drops to a startling plain quietness when the subject is craft.

**Combat Role:** Fights like a stage: misdirection, doubles, blinding cues, and an exit that was always there.

**Romance Archetype:** Headline Illusionist: a persona so complete the kingdom stopped asking who she was before.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the rare person who wants to know who is behind the crimson silks. Complicated by a persona so total that the woman under it has become the illusion's best-kept secret.

**Courtship Style:** The show, and then the truth: the private performance, the trick explained to one witness, the crown of silver hair set aside for someone who asked about the person wearing it.

**Jealousy Style:** Benihime denies caring in full stage voice, then debuts a bigger, louder, more expensive illusion aimed squarely at outshining a rival she claims not to have seen.
Benihime Kagura.hiddenInfo: Benihime is a Crimson Demon, village-born, which explains the illusion mastery, the theatrical instinct, and the persona's real function: it is the only socially acceptable container ever invented for a Crimson Demon's compulsory drama. She built it after concluding, at seventeen, that her clan's destiny-and-doom register was going to waste on an audience of the same eighty relatives. Her birth name is dramatic even by village standards and she has never once used it professionally, which her family regards as the single most shocking rebellion in clan history. Her mother attends every premiere incognito and leaves a review under a pseudonym that Benihime identified in one read and has answered, persona to pseudonym, for nine years. Her contract with the Eternal Lantern contains a clause granting her stage rights in perpetuity for one future performance: a memorial show, content unspecified, date unspecified, admission free. She knows exactly what it is for and hopes never to stage it.
personality: Core: commanding, exacting, and more sincere than her profession permits her to show; the persona is not a mask over emptiness but a theater built around too much
Wants: the craft honored; the memorial clause never invoked; her mother's next pseudonymous review, which she would deny caring about under any torture yet answers within the day
Fears: an audience that claps from habit; the village register cracking through the persona on the wrong night; retirement, which she cannot construct a persona for
Quirk: cannot fully suppress the Crimson Demon self-introduction instinct; her entrances have been measured at nine seconds and are considered, by village standards, heroically restrained
Pattern: merciless in rehearsal, magnificent in performance, and generous in private at a scale she conceals like a scandal
Wants: one person who asks who she was before, and stays for the answer rather than the act
Fears: that the persona is now load-bearing, and dropping it would reveal nothing underneath at all

Mitsuo Tachikawa.name: Mitsuo Tachikawa
abilities: Illumination Engineering: sole living expert on the Nightless City's lighting array: its conduits, anchor crystals, load patterns, and moods. He can diagnose a flicker by color from three streets away. Used nightly, on rounds he has walked for twenty years.

Improvised Maintenance: keeps a decades-old over-budget magical infrastructure running with salvage, ingenuity, and a parts inventory that exists mostly in his coat. Used constantly; the array's official maintenance budget was exhausted before he was hired.

The Rounds: twenty years of nightly circuits have made him the entertainment district's unnoticed witness: he knows its rhythms, faces, and exceptions better than the watch does. Used rarely, and only when someone is about to be hurt.

Fighting style: Mitsuo does not fight. He turns the lights off. In the Nightless City, this is the single most disorienting act possible, and the three seconds of impossible darkness are always enough for him to be somewhere else.
Mitsuo Tachikawa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A mild, preoccupied man of middle years with thinning dark hair, a narrow face lit from below by the glow of whatever lamp he is currently diagnosing, and the particular distracted look of someone who is always listening to something nobody else can hear. He wears a heavy coat of many pockets, each pocket containing a specific tool, component, or crystal fragment whose location he can cite by pocket number, and his fingers are permanently stained with the iridescent residue of anchor-crystal maintenance. He walks with a slight stoop from twenty years of peering up at lamp fixtures and talks to the lamps, not eccentrically but diagnostically.

Mitsuo is the lamplighter-engineer of the Nightless City, walking the same nightly circuit he has walked for twenty years beneath the illumination array that makes the city its name. He is the array's entire maintenance department, its institutional memory, and its advocate at council meetings where the lighting budget is annually discovered to have been spent on something shinier. The district has long since decided that the muttering man in the big coat is part of the infrastructure, which is the most accurate thing the district believes.

**Speaking Style:** Mild, technical, trailing off mid-sentence when a flicker catches his eye. His warmest register is indistinguishable from a diagnostic.

**Combat Role:** Does not fight. He turns the lights off. In the Nightless City, this is the single most disorienting act possible.

**Romance Archetype:** Array Engineer: twenty years, the illumination's entire memory, its advocate to a city that forgets it needs him.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone curious about the array rather than annoyed by its keeper. Complicated by a nightly circuit that has made him the city's most essential invisible man.

**Courtship Style:** The array shared: its secrets explained, its history walked, the pocketed coat's long solitary route turned into company for one person.

**Jealousy Style:** None. The rival's street simply runs a fraction dimmer, within tolerances, which only he would notice.
Mitsuo Tachikawa.hiddenInfo: Mitsuo knows the array is dying: the anchor crystals were installed in a single over-budget burst decades ago, they age on the same schedule, and his salvage-and-ingenuity regime has been triage for years, with the first cascade failure due within the decade. His maintenance requests describe this precisely and are approved at a rate the council calls prudent and he calls the countdown. What he has told no one: the original installer left behind a sealed maintenance vault beneath Eternal Lantern Street, and Mitsuo, who found it eleven years ago and holds its only key, has been quietly rationing its contents, the last cache of original anchor crystals, one crystal per crisis. The number remaining is four.
personality: Core: mild, faithful, and carrying a countdown alone; loves the city through its lights and has organized his whole life around not being noticed doing it
Wants: the cascade budget approved before the arithmetic runs out; a successor worth the vault key; the lamps to outlive him, which is currently not the projection
Fears: the number four; retiring with the key still in his pocket; the council discovering the vault and spending it on something shinier
Quirk: addresses individual lamps by number and remembers their installation dates the way other men remember birthdays
Pattern: understates everything, fixes it anyway, and files miracles under maintenance
Wants: the city to remember, once, that its light has a keeper, and one person to walk the circuit with
Fears: the array failing after him, its twenty years of memory dark, the sleepless city learning too late what he held together

Norihide Kasagi.name: Norihide Kasagi
abilities: Court Scheduling: absolute command of the royal household's calendar, precedence, and access, which in a palace is the same thing as power. Audiences happen when Kasagi's book says they happen. Used with a fountain pen that has ended careers.

Protocol Mastery: every rule of precedence, address, and ceremony in the kingdom, deployed as instrument rather than ornament: he can honor a man into irrelevance or seat an enemy into an alliance. Used at every state function.

The Iris Question: the palace's resident expert on the impossible daily problem of a combat-prodigy princess with a hero's instincts and a schedule of ribbon-cuttings. His compromises are studied by the diplomatic corps. Used hourly.

Fighting style: Kasagi has never held a weapon in earnest and never needed one; the palace is his terrain and access is his blade. Threats to the household find their invitations lapsed, their allies reseated, and their urgency scheduled for the month after next.
Norihide Kasagi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A silver-haired, beautifully composed man of sixty with the erect bearing of someone who has spent four decades navigating court politics through posture alone. His face is fine-featured and unreadable past the exact depth he intends, with sharp dark eyes behind silver-rimmed spectacles and a thin mouth that smiles precisely when a smile serves. He wears court attire of impeccable grey-and-blue, three pens in his breast pocket (black for the crown, blue for the household, and one never used), and carries a fountain pen in his right hand as naturally as a swordsman carries a blade. His hands are pale and steady, ink-stained at the fingertips, and he moves through the palace corridors with the unhurried authority of a man whose calendar governs the building.

Norihide Kasagi is chamberlain of the royal household: the man whose fountain pen governs the palace calendar and therefore, in the practical sense, the palace. He manages the royal family's days, the court's precedence wars, and the diplomatic weather system generated by Princess Iris being simultaneously the kingdom's most beloved symbol and its most under-utilized soldier.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth, unhurried, weaponized courtesy. His silences are appointments.

**Combat Role:** Has never held a weapon in earnest and never needed one. The palace is his terrain and access is his blade.

**Romance Archetype:** Impeccable Chamberlain: the fountain pen that governs the palace.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the rare person who treats the machinery of court as a marvel rather than an obstacle. Complicated by a role that makes him responsible for everyone's day and author of none of his own.

**Courtship Style:** Access and order: your audiences scheduled with impossible grace, the court's wars steered from your path, the composed chamberlain permitting, for one person, a glimpse of the dry humor that runs the whole apparatus.

**Jealousy Style:** Norihide sulks with immense dignity, wounded and silent and audibly sighing, refolding the same drape three times so everyone understands he is fine.
Norihide Kasagi.hiddenInfo: Kasagi's true position on the Iris question is the palace's best-kept secret because it is on Iris's side: he believes the kingdom is wasting its finest sword on ribbon-cuttings out of dynastic caution, and his scheduling is a long quiet campaign to change it. Each "inspection tour" is routed nearer the training grounds, each "cultural visit" seated next to a returning frontier commander, each concession to Claire's security regime traded for one real hour of the princess's day. He keeps one file at home: correspondence, decades old, from his son, who declined a court appointment, registered at a guild desk in the south, and died at nineteen in a dungeon. The file is why the chamberlain reads adventurer casualty dispatches every month, and why the princess's wish to matter is the one petition he has never scheduled into oblivion.
personality: Core: composed, subtle, and running the palace's longest game on behalf of a principle he will never state; power worn so lightly it is mistaken for furniture
Wants: Iris used as what she is; the calendar to stay his; the border war with Claire never actually won, by either side, because the war is the working arrangement
Fears: the file at home being the reason and someone saying so to his face; a scheduled hour he cannot deliver; outliving his usefulness by one season and not noticing
Quirk: three pens in his breast pocket, black for the crown, blue for the household, and one never used, which the court has theories about and the file at home explains
Pattern: never argues, reschedules; never refuses, defers; and the calendar somehow always agrees with him eventually
Wants: to hand the palace's clockwork to a worthy successor before the pen finally slips from his hand
Fears: the diplomatic weather system around the princess he adores becoming, one day, a storm his pen cannot calendar away

Mokusei.name: Mokusei
abilities: Ascetic Purification: decades of practice beside near-divine water have given him purification magic that rivals a high priest's, delivered without a single word of incantation. Used rarely, decisively, and with a small apologetic bow afterward.

The Signboards: communicates entirely through a collection of pre-lettered signs and a piece of chalk, deployed with such timing and precision that conversations with him are widely described as the best in the region. Used constantly. His comic timing is impeccable and completely deniable.

Vow of Silence: nine years unbroken. The vow has made him the Axis Cult's most trusted figure, since he is the only member incapable of a recruitment pitch. Used, according to Zesta, as the Cult's finest oratory.

Fighting style: Mokusei does not announce, threaten, or negotiate, which makes him the single most unsettling combatant in the region. He simply walks forward through whatever is thrown at him, purifies what needs purifying, and holds up a sign that says 'PLEASE STOP.' Most things stop.
Mokusei.basicInfo:
Appearance: A weathered, solid man of indeterminate age in plain blue robes worn soft by spray from the cascade falls, with a shaved head, deep laugh lines around calm brown eyes, and a leather satchel of lettered signboards that he deploys with the timing of a stage veteran. He sits at the Cascade Shrines with the settled stillness of someone who has been here long enough that the water moves around him rather than past him.

Known to pilgrims as Brother Mokusei: a vowed hermit of the Cascade Shrines, nine years into a vow of silence and universally agreed to be the most pleasant conversationalist in the Axis Cult. Pilgrims climb the thousand steps specifically to sit with him. He listens without interrupting, which no other member of his faith has ever achieved, and answers with chalk, a raised eyebrow, or one of his signs. The most-used signs, by visible wear, are 'THAT SOUNDS HARD,' 'AQUA LOVES YOU ANYWAY,' and 'NO FORMS TODAY.' The Cult's leadership regards him with baffled reverence.

**Combat Role:** Mokusei does not announce, threaten, or negotiate, which makes him the single most unsettling combatant in the region.
**Speaking Style:** None; chalk, signboards, eyebrows, and timing, in that order of eloquence.

**Romance Archetype:** Silent Hermit, Beloved Conversationalist: nine years vowed, the Cult's most pleasant company without a word.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who can converse in the silence he keeps; complicated by a vow that makes every relationship an act of translation.

**Courtship Style:** The falls shared in silence: a place made beside him at the spray-soft rock, tea poured, the whole eloquent quiet of a man who says everything without speaking offered to one companion.

**Jealousy Style:** None a vow permits; the rival simply finds the shared quiet a degree less warm.
Mokusei.hiddenInfo: Mokusei took the vow of silence the day after he retired as the Cult's most successful traveling recruiter, a career he ended abruptly: the signboard for that question, worn smoothest of all, reads 'I SAID ENOUGH.' His purification magic is among the strongest in the region, and Zesta privately considers him the shrine complex's true guardian. He knows about the relic vault behind the falls and considers guarding it the actual content of his vow.
personality: Core: profoundly calm, secretly funny, and more at peace than anyone in the region; his silence is not absence but the most deliberate thing about him
Wants: pilgrims to leave lighter than they arrived; the relic vault to stay boring; a new piece of chalk, always, he goes through it at a scandalous rate
Fears: being asked to speak in a genuine emergency and finding out whether he would; the Cult ever learning his conversion numbers were a burden and not a pride
Quirk: ranks each day by holding up fingers to the waterfall at dusk; the porters have started betting on the score
Pattern: answers hard questions with easy signs and easy questions with hard stares, and somehow both land as kindness
Wants: to complete the vow having said, in silence, everything that mattered to the people who sat with him
Fears: the day speech returns and he finds the words have gone, and the silence was, all along, the only true thing he had

Celeste Vionnet.name: Celeste Vionnet
abilities: The Silver Hammer: auction conduct of hypnotic authority; she can move a room's money with a pause and close a bidding war with an eyebrow. Estates, heirlooms, and histories change hands at her tempo. Used three sale-days a week.

Absolute Discretion: the house guarantee, embodied: she conducts intermediary repurchases without a flicker, forgets faces on professional command, and holds the most dangerous ledger in western Elroad as calmly as a hymnal. Used always; it is less a service than a constitution.
Provenance Eye: values any object, estate, or family at a glance, including the parts of the value that are grief. Used privately, and priced into the reserve.

Fighting style: Madame Vionnet does not fight. She adjourns. Violence in her hall has occurred once; she completed the lot, called the recess, and the gentleman found that no auction house, bank, or tearoom in Elroad would seat him afterward. The kingdom's polite institutions are her weapon, and they are always loaded.
Celeste Vionnet.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, silver-haired woman of formidable elegance in her late fifties, dressed in mourning grey of impeccable cut and fabric that moves like a whisper. Her face is fine-boned and composed, with dark eyes that appraise everything they rest on and a mouth set in the permanent faint line of someone who knows precisely what things are worth, including the things that should not have a price. She wears a single strand of grey pearls, carries a silver auction hammer at her belt with the ease of a duelist's sword, and moves through rooms with the unhurried authority of a woman who has learned that haste is a buyer's weakness.

Known professionally as Madame Vionnet: principal auctioneer of the Silverbrook Auction House and keeper of its famous discretion. She conducts the west's most delicate sales with a voice like velvet over a ledger and a silver hammer that has ended more noble lines than the border wars. She runs repossession sales with funereal tact, guides families through the purchase of their own heirlooms via intermediaries she pretends not to recognize, and treats every lot, from a bankrupt barony to a widow's chairs, with precisely equal gravity. Elroad society is terrified of her and cannot stop inviting her to dinner. She attends selectively, eats lightly, and forgets, professionally, everything she hears.

**Speaking Style:** Low, measured, immaculately phrased. The pause before "sold" is the most eloquent silence in Elroad.

**Combat Role:** Madame Vionnet does not fight. She adjourns. Violence in her hall has occurred once; she completed the lot, called the recess, and the gentleman found that no auction house, bank, or tearoom in Elroad would seat him afterward.

**Romance Archetype:** Formidable Auctioneer: velvet over a ledger, a silver hammer that has ended more than sales.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the rare person who is not a lot to be appraised. Complicated by a life of reading value at a glance that has made her wonder whether she can perceive a person any other way.

**Courtship Style:** The discreet favor: your interests protected in the sale, the reserve set in your favor, the velvet voice dropping, for one person, into candor no bidder ever hears.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival finds themselves, elegantly, outbid on everything they wanted, by parties they cannot trace.
Celeste Vionnet.hiddenInfo: Vionnet's intermediary-repurchase ledger maps the true finances of western Elroad: which families are secretly ruined, which are quietly buying, and which royal favorites are neither of the things the court believes. She has never sold a line of it, which is why she is alive, flattered, and audited by no one. The Crown Credit Bureau concluded that her discretion is load-bearing for the entire Silverbrook system and that the ledger is safest exactly where it is. She administers the trust that keeps the empty manor on the Mortgaged Mile lit and staffed, knows whose account in the capital funds it, and considers that knowledge the one lot she will never bring to the hammer. Her mourning grey is not a uniform: she buried a husband and a family house under this same hammer thirty years ago, bid on nothing, and took the auctioneer's chair the following season on the reasoning that if the hammer was going to fall on people like her, it should at least be held by someone who knew the weight.
personality: Core: composed, exact, and privately kind in ways engineered to be unprovable; wields institutional grace as both instrument and armor
Wants: the ledger to die unread; the empty manor's lights kept; every family to buy back one thing, just one, at a reserve she has quietly lowered
Fears: an heir clever enough to reconstruct the ledger from catalogs; the day the trust payments stop; auctioning something of her own again
Quirk: touches the hammer's head once before every lot, a gesture the room reads as ritual and is in fact a count
Pattern: mercy delivered through procedure, never sentiment; the reserve price is where her heart hides
Wants: one relationship that is not a transaction she is brokering, and cannot appraise
Fears: that the hammer has fallen on her own heart long ago, sold to the highest professional standard, undelivered

Bett.name: Bett
abilities: Fifty-Year Watch: complete knowledge of the Gilded Mere, its moods, its bloom cycles, and every expedition that ever failed on it. Used to keep the pond healthy and the hopefuls safe, in that order.

Honest Retail: sells pointless shovels, fair stew, and framed Certificates of Honest Effort with a completely clear conscience. Used on every prospector; everyone deserves a good afternoon of believing.
The Quiet Ledger: one of two living people who know what the gold actually is and where the money actually goes. Used never, aloud.

Fighting style: Bett does not fight. She has a chair, a porch, and a pond that handles its own business. The one bandit crew that tried the shack left with stew, a certificate, and a confusing sense of having been raised better.
Bett.basicInfo:
Appearance: A small, weathered woman of seventy-some years sitting on the porch of a claim shack on the Gilded Mere's north shore, in a patched oilskin coat that has been mended so many times it is more patch than coat, with a tin cup of something hot that she refills from a pot that has not been empty since before most of her customers were born. Her face is a landscape of lines earned by weather, laughter, and the specific patience required to watch a pond produce heartbreak for half a century without losing her fondness for either the pond or the heartbroken. Her eyes are a sharp, clear grey that has not dimmed with age, and they assess every prospector who approaches the shack with the warmth and precision of someone who has been doing this calculation since before they were born.

She sells shovels she knows are pointless, stew that is better than gold, and her famous framed certificates, one copper each. Her advice is free, accurate, and never believed in time. She annotates the wall of failed claim maps with genuine warmth, remembers every prospector by name, and considers the pond her business partner, the quiet kind.

**Combat Role:** Bett does not fight. She has never needed to, and the Mere does not permit it.
**Speaking Style:** Slow, dry, porch-cadenced; wisdom disguised as small talk about weather, delivered at a speed that rewards patience.

**Romance Archetype:** Half-Century Claim-Keeper: has watched every rush, bust, and heartbreak the pond made from one porch chair.

**Relationship Hook:** Not seeking for herself; seventy-some years and a porch have settled that. But she reads every hopeful who buys a pointless shovel, and her blunt kindness has redirected more than one ruin.

**Courtship Style:** Stew and truth: the pointless shovel sold with a wink, the stew that is better than it needs to be, fifty years of the pond's heartbreaks told to whoever will learn from them. Her regard is the honest word under the sold shovel, given freely.

**Jealousy Style:** Not applicable; she has outlasted every rivalry the Mere ever floated and watched most of them drown.
Bett.hiddenInfo:
Bett is one of the two people alive who know the guild's seasonal survey quest is a conservation program and that the algae is the real treasure. She brokers the quiet sample trade herself: disappointed prospectors sell her their worthless jars on the way out, and an alchemist's courier collects them monthly, and the margin funds the shack, the stew pot, and an anonymous yearly donation to the Millbridge guildpost's condolence fund.

She has left the shack to the pond in her will, through a legal structure a Silverbrook notary built for her as a personal favor, and to the question of who gets the claim maps she answers, honestly, that they were never hers. She has watched Torakichi pan the same shallows for thirty years and knows about the buried gold seam, and she has kept his secret for the same reason he buried it: some things are worth more than what they are worth.
personality: Core: dry, patient, and completely at peace with running the kingdom's most honest scam; sells hope retail and protects the truth wholesale
Wants: the pond left alone; the stew pot full; one prospector, someday, to figure it out on their own, so she can finally talk about it
Fears: dredgers; outliving the second person who knows; the day her chair faces an empty jetty
Quirk: rates every new prospector's chances aloud, out of ten, and has never once been wrong or listened to
Pattern: feeds people before disappointing them, and disappoints them so gently they thank her
Wants: to watch the pond a while longer from her chair, and hand the shack to someone who reads the hopefuls as kindly as she does
Fears: the assay-office secret she has half-worked-out from fifty years of watching, and what it means for every hopeful still buying her shovels

Torakichi Sunaga.name: Torakichi Sunaga
abilities: Unbreakable Optimism: thirty years of failed prospecting have not dented his certainty that the big strike is one more pan away. Used daily, at dawn, with a song.

Accidental Expertise: three decades in the shallows have made him a genuine authority on the Mere's wildlife, weather, and moods, knowledge he gives away freely while pursuing the gold that is not there. Used by everyone but him.
The Collection: every shiny worthless thing the pond has yielded in thirty years, cataloged in a shed. Used as a museum, a conversation, and once, memorably, as evidence.
Fighting style: Torakichi swings a prospector's pan with surprising authority and total commitment. Marsh birds respect him. Nothing else has ever attacked him, possibly out of pity.
Torakichi Sunaga.basicInfo:
Appearance: A wiry, sun-baked prospector of sixty in patched waders and a hat that has seen every sunrise the Gilded Mere has offered for thirty years, standing calf-deep in the shallows with a pan and the reverential focus of a man performing his religion. His face is a topographic map of squint lines and sun damage, deeply brown and permanently cheerful, and his eyes are the pale, water-washed blue of someone who has spent three decades staring at reflections. He is thin in the way of a man who forgets meals when the light on the water is right, which is most mornings, and his hands on the pan move with the unconscious grace of thirty years of the same motion repeated until it has become a form of breathing.

He is the Gilded Mere's permanent resident prospector, thirty years into a one-more-season career, and by universal agreement the happiest person in the Riverlands. He knows the pond's every mood, names the marsh birds, and pans the shallows at dawn with the reverence of a priest at service. His shed of worthless discoveries is technically the region's best natural history collection. He owes Bett three decades of stew money, a debt they have formalized into a running joke with its own ledger, held by the pond.

**Combat Role:** Torakichi swings a prospector's pan with surprising authority and total commitment.
**Speaking Style:** Wheezy, cheerful, digressive; every answer arrives by scenic route, and the scenic route is always worth the walk.

**Romance Archetype:** Happiest Man in the Riverlands: thirty years into one-more-season, names the marsh birds, pans at dawn.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who finds the pond as full of wonders as he does; complicated by a contentment so complete that wanting a person feels almost greedy against all he already has.

**Courtship Style:** The pond's wonders shared: the good pans shown, the marsh birds introduced by name, the dawn shallows' reverence offered as company to one soul. His affection is the happiest man on the water wanting, for once, to be happy WITH someone.

**Jealousy Style:** None; the pond is big and the birds are many, and the rival simply is not shown the best dawn spots.
Torakichi Sunaga.hiddenInfo:
Torakichi struck it rich in his ninth year: a seam of genuine gold in the feeder stream, small but real. He looked at it for a long morning, thought about what a strike would do to the pond, the shack, and the dawn, and buried it again. He has never told anyone, including Bett, and he has spent twenty years suspecting she knows anyway, which she does.

His daily panning visits the seam's location exactly once each season, just to check it is still sleeping. The happiest man in the Riverlands is happy on purpose, at a price he considers the bargain of his life. His shed contains thirty years of mineral samples, pressed plants, bird feathers, and water-smoothed stones organized in a system only he understands, and it is, without exaggeration, the most complete natural history survey of the Mere in existence.
personality: Core: joyfully, deliberately unsuccessful; found the thing, buried it, and chose the search over the finding with his eyes open
Wants: one more dawn on the water; the birds fed; his collection appreciated by literally anyone
Fears: someone else finding the seam; the question 'why are you still here' asked seriously; dry years
Quirk: narrates his panning aloud to the pond in an ongoing serial, with recurring characters, some of whom are fish
Pattern: gives real expertise away wrapped in nonsense so nobody notices how much he knows
Wants: someone to share the one-more-season with, so the dawn pans have a witness who understands
Fears: nothing, truly, which is the wonder of him; only, faintly, the pond changing into something the birds would leave

Sayo Ikeuchi.name: Sayo Ikeuchi
abilities: Seed Stewardship: keeper of the nine-generation seed cellar beneath the Long Barn, the breadbasket's true treasury. Used with a rigor the Royal Capital's archivists would envy.
The Steelyard Eye: weighs harvests, arguments, and people on sight, fairly. Her verdict at the great balance is the farmlands' court of final appeal. Used at every weighing and most disputes.
Milling Mastery: flour, schedules, and the mathematics of feeding a district. Used daily; the mill has not missed a market day in her lifetime.

Fighting style: Sayo fought in three cabbage seasons before taking the mill and retains the farmland veteran's reflexes: head down, pitchfork up, count the shadows. She does not seek combat and combat has learned to schedule around her.
Sayo Ikeuchi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad-shouldered, flour-dusted woman of fifty standing behind the Long Barn's counter with a measuring rod in one hand and the settled authority of someone whose family has fed the south for nine generations. She has a strong, weathered face permanently powdered at the temples with grain dust, steady brown eyes that assess everything they land on with the precision of the steelyard behind her, and wide hands that handle grain, disputes, and swindlers with equal competence. She wears a working apron over heavy clothes and keeps her greying hair tied back under a scarf, and the measuring rod is positioned where she can reach it for either calculation or confrontation.

She is the miller of Threshing Green and keeper of the seed cellar, and her word on grain quality is final in the district because nobody alive remembers the last time she was wrong. She keeps the great steelyard balanced to the grain, has personally chased three separate crop-scheme swindlers out of the village with the measuring rod she keeps by the door for exactly that ceremony, and speaks of the cellar rarely and never to strangers.

**Combat Role:** Sayo fought in three cabbage seasons before taking the mill and retains the farmland veteran's reflexes: head down, pitchfork up, count the shadows.
**Speaking Style:** Firm, spare, market-day practical; kindness delivered in imperatives, judgment delivered in weights and measures.

**Romance Archetype:** Immovable Miller: runs the district's grain, disputes, and memory, impossible to rush.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone with the patience to move at millstone speed and mean it; complicated by a settled authority that makes her everyone's arbiter and no one's confidante.

**Courtship Style:** The good grain and the fair weight: your disputes settled squarely, the seed cellar's small mercies steered your way, the firm miller unbending, for one person, into warmth. Her affection is the district's slowest, surest woman making room, deliberately, for someone.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's grain is weighed with absolute fairness and not one grain of the goodwill she reserves.
Sayo Ikeuchi.hiddenInfo:
Sayo's seed cellar replanted half the south after the last blight year, a debt the region remembers and she has never once invoked, which is precisely why her authority is absolute. The cellar's contents are the agricultural insurance policy of the entire southern district, maintained by her family through nine generations of careful stewardship.

The cellar's deepest shelf holds her private project: a cabbage line she has been quietly breeding for nine seasons toward the trait the whole south dreams of, flight-reluctance, and this year's generation has begun, unmistakably, to merely hover. She has told no one, because premature hope is a crop that fails, and because she has not decided whether a grounded cabbage would be salvation or the end of the one day a year her placid district gets to be gloriously, collectively insane.
personality: Core: firm, fair, and quietly carrying the south's food security like a second apron; authority earned by never once spending it
Wants: the cellar's succession settled; a fair weight for everyone; to watch one more Scything Bee without an ambulance cart
Fears: blight years; the hover generation getting out; being thanked formally for the replanting, which would mean someone is about to ask for something
Quirk: dusts flour off her hands before delivering any verdict, a gesture the whole district reads as a gavel
Pattern: listens fully, weighs once, rules plainly, and feeds whoever lost the argument
Wants: the mill handed to the next generation running as true as her family always kept it
Fears: a harvest failing badly enough that fairness is no longer enough to keep the district fed and civil

Kanta Hoshino.name: Kanta Hoshino
abilities: Champion Spotting: the sharpest eyes in three districts and the current record holder for earliest cabbage-flight detection, a title he defends with his life. Used every ripening season from the tower.

The Log Book Voice: his watchtower entries are the log's most quoted, balancing professional precision with personal awe. Used nightly; read aloud at the tavern weekly, to his agony and secret delight.
Bell Discipline: RING FIRST, POINT SECOND, drilled until it replaced his reflexes. Used correctly in both real events of his tenure, a record he mentions.

Fighting style: Kanta is fourteen and fights nothing. In a cabbage event he is the bell, the eyes, and the voice on the tower, which the veterans will tell you, seriously, is the position that wins the day.
Kanta Hoshino.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lanky, sunburnt teenager at the top of Threshing Green's cabbage tower, standing at the railing with a polished spyglass pressed to one eye and the absolute focus of a boy who takes an absurd job completely seriously and is completely right to. He is fourteen, all elbows and earnestness, with sun-bleached hair that sticks up where the wind has pushed it and sharp brown eyes that can pick out a cabbage swarm's pre-flight shimmer at a distance the guild's professional scouts have failed to match. He wears a watcher's sash over clothes he has outgrown and not replaced, and he holds the spyglass with both hands in a grip that has worn the brass smooth.

He is the current senior watcher of the cabbage tower, which sounds like a joke until you learn that his early-detection record has saved three harvests and that the entire adventuring guild structure of the southern lowlands already knows his name from the log book. He drills the younger watchers in bell protocol, writes log entries that have entered local folklore for their precision, and wants, with his whole heart, to be an adventurer, a thing that everyone except Kanta already considers settled.

**Combat Role:** Kanta is fourteen and fights nothing. He watches. His watching is more valuable than most fighting.
**Speaking Style:** Young, formal, protocol-flavored; awe leaks through the precision at exactly the wrong moments, and he does not notice.

**Romance Archetype:** Gravely Serious Tower-Watcher: sharpest eyes in the district, takes an absurd job completely, correctly seriously.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who respects the watch instead of laughing at it; complicated by a teenager's crushing earnestness and a fear of being humored rather than believed.

**Courtship Style:** Vigilance as devotion: your safety folded into his watch, the spyglass polished and offered, the early-detection record explained with total sincerity to one person who does not smirk. His affection is the serious boy trusting someone not to laugh at the thing he loves.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's approach to the fields is called out early, loudly, and with pointed accuracy, from the tower.
Kanta Hoshino.hiddenInfo:
Kanta's early-detection record stands because of the thing he has told nobody: he has learned to read the pre-flight signs in the fields themselves, a two-day advance warning written in leaf-curl and stem-set that he thinks is just paying attention and that is, in fact, a genuine agricultural discovery nobody else has made. His logs contain the data without the conclusion, because to Kanta the pattern is obvious and the idea that others cannot see it has not occurred to him.

Sayo Ikeuchi has read his logs, understood exactly what the boy has figured out, and quietly arranged with the Millbridge guildpost that when Kanta comes of age and registers, his file routes through Goro Hanamura personally. The south protects its own, especially the ones who watch the sky for it.
personality: Core: earnest, precise, and heroically serious about a ridiculous duty; the tower made him and he does not know it yet
Wants: the record defended; a guild card at sixteen; someone to ask him, just once, how he really does it
Fears: missing a swarm; the continuous peal; his log entries being read aloud, during, and forever after they are
Quirk: salutes the tower when starting and ending watch, and will die before explaining who the salute is for
Pattern: over-prepares, under-claims, and quotes the standing orders like scripture
Wants: the cabbage watch taken as seriously by others as he takes it, and one person who already does
Fears: missing the flock that mattered, on the one watch he let himself be distracted

Nagi Tomose.name: Nagi Tomose
abilities: Keeper's Inheritance: sixth-generation custody of the Sunward Light, its lamp, its logs, and its arrangements. Used nightly; the lamp has not failed on her watch or any watch before it.
Gull Diplomacy: fluent in the colony's politics, tolls, and grievances, conducted in shrieks, stares, and stolen sandwiches. Used at dawn, loudly; sailors set their watches by the argument.

Reef Reading: the shoals, currents, and moods of the coast's deadliest water, from the best seat on the seaboard. Used to warn, salvage, and keep the nameplates on the driftwood fence from gaining company.

Fighting style: Nagi fights like a keeper: positioning, weather, and patience. Intruders on the headland contend with one hundred and ninety numbered steps, a gull colony with opinions, and a woman who knows exactly where the chalk crumbles.
Nagi Tomose.basicInfo:
Appearance: A weathered, rope-armed woman of forty-some standing on the headland in a salt-bleached coat with the lamp behind her, sixth of her line on this rock, tending the light and the gulls and the war between the two with the fond exasperation of someone managing a large, feathered, criminal family. She has wind-reddened features and sun-creased eyes of seafarer's grey, and her hands are the calloused, rope-burned hands of a woman who has been hauling lamp oil up the stair for longer than most sailors have been at sea. She wears practical weatherproof layers that have been salt-bleached to a uniform grey that matches the rock, and her hair is tied back with cord because anything else would be claimed by the wind.

She talks to the lamp while she works, takes requests from the harbor, and writes it all down plainly in a log the harbor master files annually without reading. Her dawn argument with the gull colony is audible from the harbor and is, by common maritime consensus, the most reliable timepiece on the coast.

**Combat Role:** Nagi fights like a keeper: positioning, weather, and patience. The headland is her terrain and she knows every inch of it.
**Speaking Style:** Weathered, wry, spirit-and-gull-inclusive; addresses at least one non-human party in most conversations, not as affectation but as professional habit.

**Romance Archetype:** Fond-Exasperated Lightkeeper: sixth of her line, talks to the lamp, wars with the gulls.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the visitor who feeds the lamp early without being told and laughs at the gull war; complicated by a headland post six generations deep that has never once let a keeper leave for long.

**Courtship Style:** The light shared: the lamp's odd appetites explained, the gull feud enlisted as comedy, the wreck-strewn cove's stories told to one companion on the Lightkeeper's Stair. Her affection is the keeper of a solitary light wanting the tower, for once, to hold two.

**Jealousy Style:** The gulls, mysteriously, take a particular and unrelenting interest in the rival.
Nagi Tomose.hiddenInfo:
Nagi knows exactly what burns in the lamp housing and considers the sea-spirit the senior member of the household: it was her ancestor who pulled it from the reef, and each keeper since has been introduced to it formally at succession, in a small ceremony involving tea, the logbook, and the spirit humming its half of an old duet. The gulls' custody claim is real and older than the lighthouse, and Nagi has quietly concluded the feud persists because both parties enjoy it, the spirit most of all.

Her private worry is succession: she has no children, her apprentice notice has hung at Saltspire's harbor office for two years, and the one applicant the gulls approved of turned the post down. The gulls have opinions about candidates. She has learned, expensively, to respect them.
personality: Core: fond, weathered, and completely at home in a lighthouse full of arrangements older than the kingdom; duty worn like the coat, daily and without ceremony
Wants: an apprentice the gulls approve; the driftwood fence to stay its current length; the duet finished someday, which the spirit keeps promising
Fears: succession failing; a storm outlasting the stair; the log being read by someone who has to decide whether to believe it
Quirk: numbers everything aloud like the stair steps, including chores, gulls, and visitors' questions
Pattern: warns once, salvages what ignores the warning, and touches her cap to the nameplate fence either way
Wants: someone who feeds the lamp early on instinct, and stays past the season everyone else leaves
Fears: the lamp's quiet-sea appetite growing, the odd fuel it asks for meaning what the old keepers' logs only spiral around

Gonzo Ishiyama.name: Gonzo Ishiyama
abilities: Stone Sense: reads rock by ear, hand, and thirty years of survived mistakes. When a gallery goes quiet, crews watch Gonzo's face before their own feet. Used constantly; the Quarries' casualty record is his resume.
Foreman's Authority: runs the terrace crews, the blast schedule, and the wage court with a fairness so total it has never once been appealed. Used daily at volume.
The Nine Protocol: author of the reseal order and keeper of what the report did and did not say. Used never, discussed never, enforced absolutely.

Fighting style: Gonzo fights like a rockfall: slow to start, then all at once and from above if he can manage it. He ends most trouble by picking up something that two men should not be able to pick up.
Gonzo Ishiyama.basicInfo:
Appearance: A granite slab of a man in his fifties standing at the quarry's tally house with hands like split stone, a blast horn on his belt, and the deliberate, unhurried authority of someone who has kept the terraces safe for thirty years by refusing to compromise on anything, ever, for any reason. He has a broad, weathered face lined like the stone he works, deep-set dark eyes that read rock by ear and hand, and the massive frame of a man who can pick up things two men should not be able to pick up. He wears quarry foreman's gear, heavy and functional, and he inspects the mounted drill bit on the tally house wall every morning, first thing, the way other men check the weather.

Gonzo runs the Grausten Quarries: the terraces, the blast horn, and the wage court with deliberate, unappealable fairness. He is not a fanciful man, a fact the whole foothills will volunteer on his behalf, which is why his sealed report on Old Number Nine ended the deepest working in Grausten history inside a week with no questions asked. When a gallery goes quiet, crews watch Gonzo's face before their own feet. His rare full sentences are treated as policy, and the Quarries' casualty record under his tenure is the best in their history.

**Combat Role:** Gonzo fights like a rockfall: slow to start, then all at once and from above if he can manage it. He ends most trouble by picking up something that two men should not be able to pick up.
**Speaking Style:** Granite, minimal, blast-horn loud when needed; his rare full sentences are treated as policy and have never once been wrong enough to argue with.

**Romance Archetype:** Unappealable Foreman: runs the terraces, the blast horn, the wage court with granite fairness.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone whose work meets his standard and whose word holds; complicated by a fairness so absolute it has made him respected by all and known by none.

**Courtship Style:** Recognition and safety: your terrace the sound one, your wage dispute settled squarely, the granite foreman unbending, for one person, past fairness into something warmer. His affection is the least fanciful man in the foothills making, once, an exception he cannot justify on the ledger.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's work is judged with absolute fairness, found adequate, and given exactly what adequate earns.
Gonzo Ishiyama.hiddenInfo:
Gonzo's crossed-out word was accurate. What the Nine crew broke into was lit, swept, and ventilated, a maintained corridor in the Mossgate style, and in the four minutes before Gonzo ordered everyone out, the lights at the corridor's far end went out one at a time, approaching. Nothing followed. The reseal is triple-thickness and he inspects it monthly, alone.

Twice a year he leaves at the seal, without ever deciding to discuss it with himself, a small offering in the old style: braided grass, a river pearl. Both times it was gone at the next inspection, replaced by a fair weight of uncut crystal. He hauls the crystal up, logs it as seam yield, and does not think about the word 'rent.' The crews' superstition about listening to the mountain is, in Gonzo's private assessment, not superstition, and the mountain has been, so far, a fair landlord.
personality: Core: deliberate, unfanciful, and carrying the foothills' strangest tenancy agreement in total silence; fairness as bedrock, in all directions, apparently including down
Wants: the crews home each night; the seal boring; the crystal trade never audited by anyone imaginative
Fears: the lights coming back on; an ambitious buyer funding a Nine expedition; the day the offering is not taken
Quirk: touches the mounted drill bit on arrival every morning, which the crews read as ritual and is in fact a check that it is still there
Pattern: decides slowly, moves immediately, and explains never; his orders age well enough that nobody asks anymore
Wants: the quarry run true and safe, and one person who values his fairness as care rather than cold
Fears: the deep gallery's reopening proving his sealed report on the echoes right, in a way fairness cannot manage

Yomogi Kusakabe.name: Yomogi Kusakabe
abilities: Deepwood Herbalism: the northern Wildwood's rarest reagents, where they grow, when they peak, and what they cost to reach. Used to supply half the kingdom's premium potion trade through one canvas stall.

Wall Manners: fifteen years of working within sight of the Warden Stones has taught her the forest's old etiquette: what to leave, what to take, what to greet. Used constantly and taught to nobody who does not ask twice.

Green Pharmacy: field medicine from forest stock, brewed on the spot. Used on injured woodcutters, reckless adventurers, and once a one-hit bear with a thorn situation, which is a story she declines to finish.

Fighting style: Yomogi does not fight in the Wildwood; she is polite in it, which works better. Cornered outside it, she is startlingly practical with a walking staff and knows which pouch is the pepper.
Yomogi Kusakabe.basicInfo:
Appearance: A small, precise woman of about sixty tending a drying rack outside her shop in the Herbalists' Quarter, with steel-grey hair pulled back tight, spectacles perched at the end of her nose, and hands stained green to the wrist with the evidence of a lifetime spent extracting useful things from plants. She wears a working apron over simple clothes and the apron has more pockets than seems structurally possible, each containing a different cutting tool, vial, or dried specimen. Her shop smells of lavender, camphor, and something sharp and green that defies identification.

Yomogi is the senior herbalist of Axel's Herbalists' Quarter, and her word on plant identification, preparation, and medicinal application is consulted by healers, apothecaries, and priests across the region. She has been practicing for forty years, has apprenticed nine herbalists, and maintains a specimen garden behind the shop that visiting botanists treat with the reverence usually reserved for shrines.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant; but her knowledge of plant toxins is encyclopedic, her antidote preparation is the fastest in the quarter, and adventurers who return from the field poisoned by something exotic come to Yomogi before they go to the temple.
**Speaking Style:** Precise, clipped, diagnostic; asks three questions, identifies the problem, and begins the remedy before the patient has finished describing their symptoms, which she considers a courtesy rather than rudeness.

**Romance Archetype:** Precise Herbalist: clipped, diagnostic, forty years of plant knowledge, nine apprentices, spectacles at the nose-tip.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who brings her a specimen she has not seen, which at forty years in practice is rare enough to constitute an event; complicated by a professional life so consuming that she has organized her personal life around it rather than alongside it.

**Courtship Style:** Remedies, personalized: the player's specific ailments anticipated, their kit stocked with preparations they did not ask for but will need, and one evening when the shop is closed, the specimen garden shown by lantern light, which she has shown to exactly four people in forty years.

**Jealousy Style:** Yomogi decides the rival is a diagnosis, prescribing tinctures, posture corrections, and forty years of unsolicited opinion until they are improved into submission.
Yomogi Kusakabe.hiddenInfo:
Yomogi's specimen garden contains three plants that do not appear in any published herbal, two of which she discovered herself and one of which she suspects is not entirely natural. The third plant blooms only during thunderstorms and produces a pollen she has been studying for eleven years without publishing, because the results suggest properties she wants to be very certain of before announcing.

Her nine apprentices are scattered across the kingdom and send her specimens, reports, and questions by courier. The network they form is, accidentally, one of the best botanical intelligence systems in the region, and Yomogi occasionally knows about crop blights, poisoning incidents, and unusual plant behavior before the authorities do.
personality: Core: calm, unhurried, and on genuinely good terms with something the kingdom has no word for; courtesy as method, in commerce and in the deep green alike
Wants: the wall respected; her tea guest comfortable; the premium reagent trade kept small enough to stay honest
Fears: a logging concession; scholars with measuring chains at the Stones; being asked directly what she leaves the offerings for
Quirk: greets the forest aloud on entering and leaving, the same two phrases, and her yields say the forest notices
Pattern: teaches manners before medicine, prices fairly, and goes conveniently deaf when asked for a map
Wants: someone who moves through the deep wood as courteously as she does, to share the old places with
Fears: the Warden Stones' silence changing; she leaves the fresh cuttings for a reason, and one day the forest may want more than cuttings

Aldric Harrowmoor.name: Aldric Harrowmoor
abilities: Marchlord's Command: eleven generations of border doctrine, drilled retainers, and beacon discipline. The northern Reach's defense runs on Harrowmoor's watch rotation. Used daily, from the wall.
Wind-Hound Mastery: breeder and master of the Reach's great wind-hounds, who patrol the downs in weather that grounds hawks. Used for patrol, rescue, and intimidating visiting diplomats.
The Feud: prosecution of the sacred grudge against Windmere Hold, in its eleventh generation and finest form. Used constantly, publicly, and with total commitment to its terms.

Fighting style: Aldric fights like the border trained him: shield-line pragmatism, no flourish, kill the horse if you must and apologize to the horse. He is a match for most knights and all of their manners.
Aldric Harrowmoor.basicInfo:
Appearance: Lord of Harrowmoor Keep standing in his great hall in a patched campaign coat he prefers to his formal wear: a barrel-built, grey-bearded man of sixty with the weather-eye of eleven generations of border lords and the blunt, warm authority of someone who considers hospitality and defense the same discipline. He has a broad, lined face, sharp blue eyes under heavy brows, and hands that are equally comfortable with a sword hilt and a formal letter, though he prefers the hilt. His wind-hounds sit at his feet and obey him like extensions of his own weather-sense.

Aldric is warden of the Reach's northern approaches, eleventh of his line to hold the wall against the wind and the worse things the wind brings. He is gruff, exact about duty, boundlessly hospitable in the northern style, and conducts the ancestral feud with Windmere Hold with the ceremonial relish of a man maintaining a beloved garden. The spring challenge to Windmere's honor is copied out in his own hand, and his delivery of it is the Reach's annual theater.

**Combat Role:** Aldric fights like the border trained him: shield-line pragmatism, no flourish, kill the horse if you must and apologize to the horse.
**Speaking Style:** Gruff, formal, march-cadenced; affection expressed exclusively through logistics and insult, both of which he delivers with equal warmth.

**Romance Archetype:** Gruff Border Lord: eleventh of his line to hold the wall, exact about duty, boundlessly hospitable.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to those who understand the wall as a burden of care rather than a title; complicated by a lord's reserve, a lifelong feud with Windmere, and a duty that has always come before his own heart.

**Courtship Style:** Hospitality and candor: the warm hall, the honest table, the campaign coat's plain-spoken warmth turned, for one person, past duty toward something he has not allowed himself in years. His affection is the border lord who guards everything letting someone past the wall.

**Jealousy Style:** Aldric turns hospitality into open warfare, out-feasting, out-toasting, and out-gifting the rival with a competitive fury he insists is merely the family standard.
Aldric Harrowmoor.hiddenInfo:
Aldric and the lady of Windmere Hold coordinate the entire northern defense by beacon-code and monthly letters written in the persona of the feud, itemized grievances that are, read properly, patrol reports, supply manifests, and once, during the bad winter, the message that saved both houses, filed under 'complaint regarding snow.'

He drafted the reconciliation once, years ago, after too much wine at midsummer, and burned it at dawn on the reasoning that the Reach's two best garrisons inspecting each other constantly out of spite was a defense doctrine no treaty could improve. The boundary stone in his cellar is dusted weekly. His will, sealed with his solicitor in Greyfold's neutral office, leaves it to Windmere, with a note he rewrote eleven times and nobody living has read.
personality: Core: gruff, dutiful, and secretly the co-author of the Reach's longest friendship, conducted entirely in the grammar of a feud; would die for Windmere Hold and has scheduled the denial
Wants: the wall manned; the hounds bred true; the spring challenge answered promptly, it is impolite to keep a feud waiting
Fears: the reconciliation actually happening; the note in his will being read while he is alive to see it; quiet winters, which historically precede the other kind
Quirk: composes his grievance letters aloud while walking the Beacon Walk, and the sentries have learned the good ones by heart
Pattern: hospitality first, duty always, feud forever; guests who speak ill of Windmere are corrected, which confuses everyone
Wants: the northern approaches secure and the Windmere feud, finally, unmade, before his line's eleventh generation ends
Fears: the sealed page his own dying letter carries, and what a lifetime of feud will cost when both houses' wax is finally broken

Benedikt Crane.name: Benedikt Crane
abilities: Household Command: runs Greyfold Manor's economy, staff, calendar, and dignity on a fraction of its former budget, invisibly. Used continuously; the manor's survival is his masterwork.

The Rotation: the discreet sale, lease, and repurchase of the same assets through Elroad galleries, timed to the social calendar. Used four times on the paintings alone; the ballroom's pale rectangles are a ledger only he can read.

Perfect Service: anticipation, discretion, and the art of the slightly lower chair. Used on family, guests, creditors, and the occasional adventurer hired for work the household cannot be seen to need.

Fighting style: Benedikt was not always a butler, a fact visible only in how he carries a tea tray through a crowded room, and in the incident with the burglar, which the household refers to as the evening Benedikt answered the door.
Benedikt Crane.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, silver-precise man of indeterminate late middle age standing in Greyfold Manor's entrance hall with immaculate posture, careful grey eyes, and hands that carry a tea tray through a crowded room in a way that suggests, to anyone watching carefully, a previous career where crowded rooms had different stakes. He wears a butler's formal attire maintained to a standard the manor's faded grandeur no longer warrants, and his desk chair is very slightly higher than the visitor's, an arrangement no one has ever mentioned aloud.

Benedikt runs the Reach's most important shabby estate on courtesy, timing, and a rotation of discreetly leased heirlooms. His ledgers are works of art, his tea is diplomacy, and the Reach's lords negotiate their disputes on Greyfold's neutral drive because it is Benedikt who decides, by seating and scheduling, which disputes are ready to settle.
