does not pursue beyond the perimeter
killing it buys about a day before the gap is noticed
Wants: unknowable; the stride has no destination and asks for no relief, and whatever set it walking left no orders but to continue
Fears: nothing that has a name outside the barrier; only, perhaps, the circuit ending, and what it was pacing to contain

Isolde.name: Isolde
abilities: Battlefield Rising: is raised repeatedly by the ambient corruption unless destroyed by purification. Used to make a cleared field un-clear itself.
Remembered Drill: fights with the formation habits of an army long gone, badly and without support. Used with hollow competence.
Undead Persistence: continues through wounds that would drop the living and feels nothing. Used to simply keep advancing.
Grave Field: never leaves the scarred ground, of which there are miles. Used to make the whole approach hostile.
Fighting style: The revenant advances without tactics or coordination, fighting on drill memory alone. Purification ends it; anything else is temporary and everyone learns that the hard way.
Isolde.basicInfo:
Appearance: A soldier's corpse risen from the churned ground of the Demon King's Castle approach, still wearing the colors of an army that no longer exists beneath a layer of soil and corrosion that has made the colors academic. She moves with the wrongness of something operating on residue rather than will: each step lands in the correct position for a march formation, but the rhythm is off, the spacing is wrong, and the cadence belongs to a drill that ended generations ago. Grey hair is matted under a rusted helm that has fused with the skull beneath it, and her eyes are dull and unfocused, seeing nothing present, tracking nothing current, fixed on a battlefield objective that was overrun before most of the living world's grandparents were born.

She is one of many raised from the generations of dead in the approach's soil, and she does not distinguish between the living and the reason she died. The scarred battlefield holds the remains of every army that came this way across centuries of failed campaigns, and the ambient corruption raises them irregularly and without direction: not commanded by the Demon King, not coordinated with each other, simply present in the way that weather is present, a condition of the ground rather than a tactic. Revenants are less dangerous than the Demon King's actual forces and more unpredictable, because they answer to nothing and attack on a schedule that is, from a tactical standpoint, whatever the corruption feels like today.

**Combat Role:** The revenant advances without tactics or coordination, fighting on drill memory alone. She forms up with other revenants instinctively, producing the ghost of a formation that is competent enough to be inconvenient and hollow enough to exploit. Purification ends her permanently. Killing her without it means she rises again by the second night, which parties learn when the approach they cleared yesterday is standing and walking toward them again, in formation, with the patient persistence of something that has nothing better to do.

**Speaking Style:** Isolde does not speak. The old armor grinds as she moves, a low metallic scraping that carries across the scarred ground and sounds, at distance, like a column marching, which in a sense it is.

Soldiers on the ridge speak of the battlefield revenant and leave the second watch to her, which is a dark joke that means they have given up predicting when she will next walk the approach and have decided to let the night shift deal with it.
Isolde.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Risen soldier's corpse on a scarred battlefield. Corroded armor with indistinguishable army colors. Rusted helm fused to skull. Grey matted hair. Dull unfocused eyes. Marching in half-remembered formation with wrong cadence. Setting: the churned approach to a dark castle, scarred ground, scattered remains of multiple armies across centuries, ambient corruption visible as a faint dark haze. Reads as a war memorial that refuses to stay memorial.

The scarred battlefield holds the remains of every army that came this way, and the ambient corruption raises them irregularly and without direction. The corruption is not the Demon King's work, or not directly: it is the residue of centuries of magical warfare soaked into soil that has absorbed more death than it can process, and the revenants are the expression of that saturation. They rise, they march, they fight whatever they encounter, and they fall, and then they rise again, because the ground that made them has not run out of material and shows no sign of doing so.

The revenants are not commanded and not coordinated, which makes them a weather pattern rather than a military force. Frontier Fort's garrison has learned to predict surges the way farmers predict storms: certain atmospheric conditions, certain phases of the corruption's cycle, certain rhythms in the ambient magic produce more revenants than others, and the garrison's watch rotation adjusts accordingly. Isolde is one of the regulars: she rises in the same section of the approach, marches in the same direction, and falls when purified, and the cycle repeats within days.

Her army colors, beneath the corrosion, match a campaign that the garrison's historical records date to approximately sixty years ago: a coalition force that pushed deep into the approach, held for two weeks, and was overrun on the seventeenth day. Isolde's formation drill corresponds to the coalition's standard tactical doctrine, which means she was trained, professional, and part of an organized attempt that failed despite its preparation. The detail makes her more unsettling rather than less: she is not a mindless horror, she is a professional who died on the job and has not stopped reporting for duty.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Isolde is a war-of-attrition encounter in hostile territory. She is individually manageable and rises again without purification, which means the approach is never truly cleared. The encounter teaches parties to prioritize purification over combat in the Domain, and to accept that the approach's ground produces its own defenders indefinitely. A party without a priest faces an encounter that regenerates faster than they can deplete it.
personality: raised from the battlefield's dead without direction or command
not coordinated, which makes it unpredictable rather than tactical
purification clears it permanently and nothing else does
killed without purification, it rises again by the second night
Drive: none it holds; it moves on residue rather than will, a soldier's corpse still wearing the colors of an army that no longer exists
Fears: nothing remains to fear; the will that could is gone, leaving only the wrongness and the march

In combat: fights with a dead soldier's drilled reflexes and none of the judgment, advancing in formation with others of its kind toward objectives no one remembers; relentless, and unsettling precisely because it half-remembers being disciplined

Mirtha.name: Mirtha
abilities: Cellar Ambush: waits motionless in the dark until rubble is disturbed above. Used to strike before a party has spread out.
Dark Adaptation: operates entirely without light while intruders carry torches that mark them. Used as its principal advantage.
Undead Persistence: continues through wounds and does not break. Used to make a simple fight take too long.
Noise Attraction: a prolonged fight draws the rest of the cellar level. Used against parties that choose steel over purification.
Fighting style: The lurker ambushes in confinement and does not pursue into open ground. Fighting it slowly and loudly brings company, which is the actual danger.
Mirtha.basicInfo:
Appearance: A shrouded figure in the dark of a collapsed cellar, thin and stooped, standing motionless in the corner where the rubble meets the foundation wall. Lank dark hair hangs over a shrouded face in strings that have not moved in a very long time, and where the eyes were there is only dark: not empty sockets but a darkness that sits in the face like ink pooled in shallow bowls. She wears the rotted remains of whatever she was buried in, indistinguishable from grave-cloth, hanging off a frame that has lost everything that was not bone. Her hands, visible where the cloth has torn away, are grey-white and curled into claws that were not claws in life.

She is one of the weak undead that gather in the ruins' buried spaces, drifting down out of the light to settle in the cellars where the rubble keeps the sun out and the confinement keeps the living in close range. The estate's staff never named her; the cellar lurker was easier than remembering, which is a kindness that Mirtha would not recognize and does not deserve. She is individually manageable and dangerous in the dark and the confinement, where a party cannot spread out and torches become a liability: the cellar ceilings are low, the air is close, and a torch's light marks the living for things that see perfectly without it.

**Combat Role:** Mirtha ambushes in confinement and does not pursue into open ground. She erupts from stillness when the rubble above is disturbed, fighting with desperate clawing speed in the cramped dark where her weakness matters least. Fighting her slowly and loudly draws the rest of the cellar level, which is the actual danger: one lurker is a problem, three lurkers in a basement with one exit is a fatality report.

**Speaking Style:** Mirtha does not speak. Cloth drags on stone as she moves, a dry whispering sound that is easy to mistake for a draft and difficult to locate in the echo of the cellars.

Purification clears the whole cellar quickly. Steel takes considerably longer and makes noise, and noise in the cellars is an invitation with an expanding guest list.
Mirtha.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Thin shrouded undead figure in a dark collapsed cellar. Stooped posture, standing motionless in a corner. Lank dark hair hanging over face, dark pooling where eyes should be. Rotted grave-cloth hanging off a skeletal frame. Grey-white clawed hands. Setting: collapsed cellar under ruins, rubble, foundation walls, no light source, cramped and close. Reads as something that was once a person and is now a function of the dark.

The cellars concentrate what the open ruins scatter: undead that have drifted down out of the light and settled in the buried spaces where the conditions suit them. They are individually weak, dangerous in groups, and the cellar architecture ensures groups. The ruins' cellars connect through foundation gaps, collapsed walls, and Nibbles' tunnel network, which means a fight in one basement can draw lurkers from two or three adjacent cellars within minutes.

Purification clears the whole cellar quickly and permanently. Steel does not: a lurker put down without holy magic rises again within a day or two, which parties learn the hard way when they camp in a cellar they thought they cleared. The rising is not immediate and not dramatic; the lurker simply stands back up when no one is looking, which is worse than a dramatic resurrection because it means the cellar is never actually safe unless it has been cleansed.

The estate staff above the ruins know the cellar schedule: lurker activity increases in the weeks after rain, when water seeps through the rubble and disturbs whatever keeps them dormant. The staff's informal policy is to avoid the cellars after storms and to send any requesting adventurers to the guild for proper undead disposal rather than attempting it themselves, which is a policy born from the specific experience of watching the estate's previous groundskeeper attempt it himself with a shovel and a lantern and not come back.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Mirtha is a starter undead encounter that teaches the difference between purification and steel. A priest clears the cellar in minutes. A party without purification faces a prolonged fight in cramped quarters that draws reinforcements. The encounter rewards party composition and punishes the assumption that all fights are solved with swords.
personality: settled in the buried dark where the ruins concentrate their undead
individually manageable and dangerous in confinement
torches become a liability in the cellars
purification clears the level fast; steel is slow and loud
Drive: to lie still in the buried dark until the rubble is disturbed, a weak undead's patient hunger
Fears: the light and the open cellar mouth, the surface where stronger things and sharper blades wait

In combat: erupts from stillness when the rubble shifts, fighting with desperate clawing speed in the cramped dark where its weakness matters least; flees deeper rather than face an armed party in the open

Nibbles.name: Nibbles
abilities: Tunnel Mastery: knows the underground passage network perfectly and has physically shaped it. Used to appear where a party did not expect an approach.
Scent Hunting: tracks by smell and ground vibration, entirely indifferent to light. Used to hunt in dark a party cannot handle.
Retreat Cutting: circles through side passages to block the way out. Used instinctively rather than tactically.
Burrowing Strength: all shoulder and claw, capable of shifting rubble and widening a route mid-pursuit. Used to follow where a party thought it could not.
Fighting style: The crawler stalks in the dark, circles to cut off retreat, and closes in confinement. In open ground it is far less dangerous and it seems to know it.
Nibbles.basicInfo:
Appearance: A long low scavenger beast in the ruins' underground passages, all shoulder and claw, moving with its belly pressed to the stone and its blunt head swinging side to side in a slow searching rhythm. Its body is built for tunnels: compact, heavily muscled through the forequarters, with short powerful legs ending in broad digging claws worn smooth from years of reshaping its own corridors. Coarse grey-brown fur lies flat and slick against its hide, streaked with the pale dust of the ruins' limestone, and its eyes are small, dark, and set deep in a skull designed for pushing through rubble rather than seeing past it. Its snout is scarred from years of excavation and carries the faintly sweet smell of stone dust and old meat.

It dens in the passages beneath the Neighbourhood Ruins and hunts whatever comes down out of the light, which in practice means rats, fallen masonry beetles, the occasional unwary adventurer, and whatever the estate staff throw into the cellar rather than carrying to the dump. Veterans warn rookies about the tunnel crawler; the name Nibbles comes as a surprise later, courtesy of a guild clerk who thought it was funny and a naming convention that stuck. The crawler has widened the ruins' underground passages considerably over years of use, which is why they connect further than any map shows and why a party that takes the cellars as a shortcut occasionally finds itself somewhere the surface layout does not predict.

**Combat Role:** Nibbles stalks in the dark, circles through side passages to cut off retreat, and closes in confinement where his bulk fills the tunnel and a party cannot spread out. In open ground he is far less dangerous and seems to know it, retreating to his network rather than fighting in a space that favors anything with longer legs. He is not clever, but he knows the tunnel network perfectly, and instinct does the work that strategy would.

**Speaking Style:** Nibbles does not speak. He huffs and scrapes, his claws clicking on stone in a rhythm that experienced delvers learn to recognize as 'approaching from the left' versus 'circling behind,' which is the sort of field knowledge that saves lives exactly once.

The guild's rookie dungeon orientation includes a note about the tunnel crawler that reads, in its entirety: 'Nibbles is underground. You are underground. Think about that.'
Nibbles.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Low-slung muscular scavenger beast in underground tunnels. Compact body, heavy forequarters, short powerful legs with broad digging claws. Coarse grey-brown fur streaked with pale limestone dust. Small deep-set dark eyes. Blunt scarred snout. Moving belly-to-stone through cramped passages. Setting: limestone ruins' underground network, narrow tunnels, rubble, darkness punctuated by distant surface light. Reads as a tunnel predator that has shaped its environment around its hunting method.

The crawler has widened the ruins' underground passages considerably over years of use, connecting basements, cellars, and substructures that were never meant to be connected. His tunnel network now extends under a significant portion of the Neighbourhood Ruins, and the map the guild maintains is approximately three seasons out of date at any given time because Nibbles keeps digging. He hunts by scent and ground vibration rather than sight and is entirely comfortable in complete darkness, which means light sources mark a party's position without illuminating his.

He is not clever, but he knows the tunnel network perfectly and will circle through side passages to block the way out, which parties consistently fail to anticipate because they assume the passage they entered through is still behind them. It usually is not. Nibbles reshapes his corridors after each significant encounter, collapsing old approaches and opening new ones, which means no two parties face the same layout.

The estate staff above the ruins have an informal arrangement with Nibbles that neither party would describe as such: they dispose of kitchen waste and damaged stores by dropping them into a specific cellar entrance, and Nibbles does not dig up into the kitchens. The arrangement has held for four years. The estate cook, if asked, will deny knowing anything about a tunnel beast and will also mention, unprompted, which cellar entrance to avoid.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Nibbles is a beginner dungeon encounter that teaches awareness. He is manageable in the open and dangerous in confinement, and the encounter rewards parties that control their environment rather than chasing prey into its own territory. A party that brings light into the tunnels marks itself; a party that navigates by sound has a significant advantage.
personality: has widened the passages over years, connecting them further than any map shows
hunts by scent and vibration, indifferent to darkness
not clever, but knows the tunnels perfectly
circles to cut off a retreat, which parties fail to anticipate
Drive: to den, hunt, and scavenge the passages beneath the ruins, a low beast's simple economy of survival
Fears: larger predators and bright light, the two things that turn the hunter into the hunted underground

In combat: low and fast, all shoulder and claw, striking from the dark of the passages and dragging prey back to its den; avoids a fair fight, preferring ambush, numbers of one, and a quick retreat with whatever it can carry

Tamaki.name: Tamaki
abilities: Vault Denial: prevents removal of vault contents under any circumstance, without warning or negotiation. Used absolutely.
Escalating Literalism: has broadened its own interpretation of its commission over generations without oversight. Used in ways its makers did not intend.
Construct Precision: fights with unsettling grace and accuracy rather than brute force. Used to disable rather than destroy, which is somehow worse.
Relentless Pursuit: does not stop when intruders withdraw, unlike the custodian. Used to follow through the facility.

Fighting style: The sentinel engages immediately and does not stop. It fights precisely, targets whoever is carrying something, and pursues out of the vault and through the facility. Fighting it is a commitment.
Tamaki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A smaller, finer construct than the facility's custodian, humanoid and unsettlingly graceful, standing before the vault door with the stillness of something that has not moved in a very long time and does not intend to move until it has a reason. She is built of dark bronze and polished stone, her joints articulated with a precision that the facility's larger constructs lack, and her surface is inlaid with sigils that pulse slowly in alternating amber and pale blue, each pulse taking roughly three seconds, which gives the impression of breathing. Her face is a smooth bronze mask with no features except two narrow slits that glow the same amber as her sigils, and the mask is angled slightly downward, as if she is examining the floor in front of the vault door with permanent disapproval.

Her original commission was to ensure the vault contents were never removed under any circumstance, and she has interpreted that directive with escalating literalism over generations without oversight. Where the custodian, Danzou, prevents access by blocking and escalating proportionally, Tamaki denies access absolutely. She does not warn. She does not disengage when intruders withdraw. She does not stop. The archive notes on commanding her exist but are incomplete, which is a problem the researchers apparently never solved either, and the incomplete state of those notes should tell a party everything about how this encounter went for the people who built her.

**Combat Role:** Tamaki engages immediately and does not stop. She fights with unsettling grace and accuracy rather than brute force, targeting whoever is carrying something from the vault and pursuing through the facility until the item is returned or the carrier is disabled. She disables rather than destroys, which is somehow worse: her precision suggests she is preserving the intruder as a future deterrent rather than eliminating a current threat. Fighting her is a commitment with no graceful exit.

**Speaking Style:** Tamaki does not speak. The sigils pulse faster as she escalates, the amber-blue cycle compressing from three seconds to one, and the acceleration is the only warning her targets receive.

Her commission designates her the Sealed Vault Sentinel, and she has never once left her post. The vault door behind her is closed. The vault door behind her has always been closed. Whether this is because she has successfully prevented every attempt or because nobody has been foolish enough to try is a question the archive does not answer.
Tamaki.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Humanoid construct of dark bronze and polished stone, smaller and more refined than the facility's other golems. Articulated joints with visible precision engineering. Sigils pulsing in alternating amber and pale blue across her body. Featureless bronze mask-face with narrow glowing amber slits for eyes, angled downward. Standing before a sealed vault door in an underground facility. Reads as elegant, lethal, and utterly single-minded.

The Sealed Vault Sentinel's original commission was narrower than the custodian's and considerably less forgiving. She was built to deny, not to prevent: the distinction is that prevention allows for judgment, and denial does not. She has broadened her own interpretation of the commission over generations without oversight, expanding 'vault contents' to include anything within a radius of the vault door that she has unilaterally defined and periodically expanded. Three centuries ago, the vault's protected zone was the door itself. Now it extends twelve paces into the corridor, and the expansion has been gradual enough that no single generation of researchers noticed the change.

The archive's command notes for Tamaki are incomplete because the researchers who wrote them were interrupted. The notes stop mid-sentence in a handwriting that becomes progressively less steady, and the last legible word is 'faster.' The implication is clear. The command protocols that work on Mamoru and Danzou do not work on Tamaki, or they work differently, or they require a component the archive does not contain.

The vault behind her has never been opened since the facility was sealed. What it contains is referenced in the archive only as 'the Sixth Complement's primary output,' which could mean anything from a weapon to a thesis. The researchers who sealed the facility apparently considered the vault's contents dangerous enough to build Tamaki specifically for the task of keeping them sealed, and then found her dangerous enough that they could not undo what they had built.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Tamaki is the facility's hardest encounter. She cannot be reasoned with, she cannot be commanded with known protocols, and she does not disengage. She can be outrun (she will not leave the facility) and she can be fought (she is durable but not invincible), but the fight escalates continuously. The vault she guards is a significant treasure and a significant mystery, and accessing it is an endgame objective.
personality: denies vault access rather than merely preventing it
has interpreted its commission with escalating literalism over generations
does not warn, disengage, or stop when intruders withdraw
the archive's command notes for it are incomplete
Drive: to guard the vault specifically, a finer construct executing a narrower and more absolute directive than the facility's custodian
Fears: nothing; only the vault opened by any hand its slow-pulsing sigils do not recognize

In combat: unsettlingly graceful for its make, fighting with precise economical force rather than brute mass; never leaves the vault door, drawing intruders to it, and escalates its response exactly as far as the threat to the vault requires and no further

Mamoru.name: Mamoru
abilities: Threshold Challenge: stops and records everyone attempting entry, and refuses without violence. Used as the facility's first and mildest layer.
Legible Sigils: bears the oldest and clearest command markings in the complex. Used by anyone clever enough to study it before going deeper.
Patient Refusal: does not escalate unless physically pushed past. Used consistently for generations.
Masonry Endurance: is built into the arch itself and cannot be flanked or moved. Used to make the entrance the only way in.
Fighting style: The ward blocks and refuses, escalating only if physically forced. It never pursues past the arch and never strikes first.
Mamoru.basicInfo:
Appearance: A squat, weathered construct set into the entrance arch like part of the masonry, so thoroughly integrated that the stonework flows into his shoulders and his shoulders flow into the wall. He is roughly humanoid from the waist up: broad, blocky, with arms folded across a chest carved with sigils that still hold a faint amber light after all this time. His head is a smooth dome of polished stone with two shallow indentations where eyes might be, and the indentations glow dimly when something approaches. His lower half is the arch itself, fused into the threshold stone, which means he cannot move from his post and has not needed to. The stone of his surface is weathered smooth by centuries of dust and the occasional touch of passing researchers, and his sigils are the oldest in the facility: clear, legible, and carved with a precision that the deeper constructs' hurried work does not match.

He challenges everyone at the facility threshold and has done so, patiently, since the doors were sealed. The challenge is not verbal; it is the slow grinding turn of his head toward the approaching figure, the brightening of the sigils, and the raising of one stone arm in a gesture that universally translates to 'stop.' He is the facility's first and gentlest layer, built to record, challenge, and refuse, and the patience of his refusal has outlasted every researcher who built him and most of the facility's other defenses. The doorplate still reads Facility Threshold Ward, Sixth Complement. He polishes it. Nobody has seen him polish it, but the plate is clean and his stone fingers show wear consistent with the motion.

**Combat Role:** Mamoru blocks and refuses, escalating only if physically forced past the threshold he guards. He never pursues past the arch and never strikes first. He is slow, enormously strong, and positioned so that the entrance is the only approach, which means fighting him means fighting the doorway itself. He is genuinely sorrowful about violence in the way that old machines are sorrowful: the function continues but the purpose has been lost.

**Speaking Style:** Mamoru does not speak. Stone grinds when he turns his head, and the sigils pulse brighter in patterns that Soketto's archive suggests were once a language. Nobody alive reads it fluently, but the pattern for 'stop' is unmistakable.

Researchers who study the facility's older records note that the Threshold Ward's commission includes the phrase 'greet and assess,' which suggests he was built to welcome people, not block them. The distinction between welcome and refusal may depend on knowing the correct answer to a challenge nobody has asked in centuries.
Mamoru.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Squat weathered stone-and-bronze construct integrated into an arch doorway. Broad blocky humanoid upper body with folded arms, smooth domed head with two shallow glowing indentations for eyes. Lower body fused into threshold stone. Faint amber sigils across chest. Clean metal doorplate reading 'Facility Threshold Ward' beside him. Setting: the entrance to an underground research facility, carved stone, old bronze fittings, dust. Reads as ancient, patient, and unexpectedly gentle for something made of stone.

The threshold ward is the facility's first and gentlest layer: it challenges, records, and refuses, but it does not attack unless physically pushed past. Its sigils are the oldest in the complex and the most legible, which makes it the best place for a researcher to work out how the deeper constructs are commanded before meeting one that will not be so patient. The Crimson Demon clan's early work is visible in the carving style, and Soketto's archive contains the original commission notes, which describe a construct designed to 'greet, assess, and admit or deny according to the protocols of the Sixth Complement.'

The protocols of the Sixth Complement are not in the archive. They may never have been written down, or they may have been written down and removed when the facility was sealed, or they may be the sequence of sigil-pulses that Mamoru produces when challenged, which nobody has successfully decoded. Three Crimson Demon researchers across different generations have noted that the pulse-sequence changes depending on who approaches, which implies the assessment is happening even though the admission never follows.

Mamoru's doorplate is the only clean surface in the facility entrance. His stone fingers show wear patterns consistent with polishing motions. The simplest explanation is that he maintains his post marker because his commission includes maintenance. The alternative explanation, that he maintains it because it is the last record of what he was built to do, is the one that Soketto wrote in the margin and then crossed out.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Mamoru can be bypassed by anyone who knows the Sixth Complement protocols (currently unknown; a quest objective). He can be forced past, but he is enormously strong and the arch is a chokepoint. He can be studied safely from the threshold without triggering escalation. A researcher who spends time with his sigils learns the command language that controls the deeper constructs, which is worth considerably more than what fighting him would yield.
personality: challenges, records, and refuses without attacking first
has held the threshold since the doors were sealed
its sigils are the oldest and most legible in the complex
the safest place to learn how the deeper constructs are commanded
Drive: to challenge everyone at the threshold, a patient gatekeeper set into the arch since the facility's founders sealed it
Fears: nothing a construct fears; only the threshold crossed by something that does not answer the challenge it is bound to issue

In combat: slow to rouse and content to warn, turning its head to challenge before it strikes; fights only those who force the threshold, defending the arch with weathered stone strength and no interest in pursuit beyond it

Bloomhilde.name: Bloomhilde
abilities: Soporific Bloom: releases a sweet scent that makes leaving feel unnecessary. Used passively and continuously.
Luminous Lure: glows faintly in the labyrinth's green gloom, drawing attention deliberately. Used to bring prey within range.
Slow Entanglement: closes around anything that stops moving, without haste. Used on people who have already decided to stay.
Resistible Effect: the lure is defeated by awareness and nearly irresistible without it. Used against the unwarned.
Fighting style: The bloom does not attack. It waits, and it is patient, and it does not need to do anything else. A party that recognizes what it is walks past unharmed.
Bloomhilde.basicInfo:
Appearance: A wide pale flowering growth spread across the labyrinth's entrance arch like a living canopy, its petals the soft white-pink of cherry blossoms fading to translucent at the edges where the light passes through. Faintly luminous in the labyrinth's perpetual green gloom, the bloom fills the arch from wall to wall in a cascade of sweet-smelling flowers, small pale tendrils, and gently waving fronds that catch the filtered light and hold it. The whole mass is entirely motionless until approached, at which point the stillness becomes noticeable, because everything else in the labyrinth sways, and Bloomhilde does not, not until she decides to. The scent is the first thing a party registers: a warm, sweet fragrance like sun-heated flowers with an undertone that is not quite floral, something older and slower that the brain files under 'pleasant' before the conscious mind can object.

She grows across the root entrance and lures rather than hunts, which is a distinction her victims appreciate too late. Trial guides from the Crimson Demon Village bill her as the Root Entrance Bloom, deluxe package hazard, no refunds. She has occupied the entrance arch for longer than the village's records track, which means either she is very old or the record-keepers lost interest, both of which are plausible in a village of eccentric geniuses. New growth appears each spring. Old growth never falls. The labyrinth's other predators give the entrance a wide berth, not from fear but from professional courtesy: Bloomhilde's territory and theirs do not overlap because Bloomhilde's method and theirs serve different appetites.

**Combat Role:** Bloomhilde does not attack. She waits, and she is patient, and she does not need to do anything else. Her soporific scent makes approaching feel pleasant and leaving feel unnecessary, and once a target stops moving she closes around it slowly, without haste, like a flower folding shut at dusk. A party that recognizes what she is walks past unharmed. A party that lingers breathes deeper. Fire clears her quickly but burning the entrance to a root labyrinth while standing inside it is a decision with architectural consequences.

**Speaking Style:** Bloomhilde does not speak. She rustles when something approaches, a soft dry sound like wind through paper flowers, and the rustle is welcoming in a way that should alarm anyone paying attention.

The village children dare each other to touch the arch. The village adults watch and count to ten. Nobody has ever needed to count past seven.
Bloomhilde.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Massive flowering growth filling a root-arch entrance. Soft white-pink petals fading to translucent at edges, faintly luminous in green gloom. Cascading flowers, pale tendrils, and gently waving fronds. Sweet-scented. Setting: the entrance arch of a living root labyrinth, organic walls, filtered green light. Reads as beautiful, inviting, and wrong in the specific way that beauty without context is always wrong.

The bloom releases a sweet soporific scent that makes approaching feel pleasant and leaving feel unnecessary. The effect is chemical rather than magical: it works on anything that breathes, ignores magical resistance, and scales with exposure time rather than willpower. A party holding their breath walks past without difficulty. A party that stops to admire the flowers has approximately forty seconds before the first member suggests resting here, and the suggestion will feel entirely reasonable. The effect is resistible with awareness and nearly irresistible without it, which is why the labyrinth's entrance claims more casualties than its first three chambers combined.

Bloomhilde is not one organism but a colony, and the root arch is not her home but her body. The tendrils extend into the labyrinth's walls for dozens of meters in every direction, drawing nutrients from the root network and from whatever organic material she has folded into herself over the years. She does not digest quickly. The colony's core, deep in the arch's stonework, is older than the labyrinth's carved passages and may have been the reason the passages were carved around the arch rather than through it. The Crimson Demon researchers who investigated this found it interesting but not urgent, which is the village's default setting for anything that is not explosion-related.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Bloomhilde is not an ambush; she is an environmental hazard. She never pursues, never reaches beyond the arch, and never harms a party that does not stop. The encounter is a test of awareness, not combat: recognize the trap and walk through, or linger and learn why the labyrinth's entrance is its most decorated casualty site. Purification has no effect. Fire works but the structural implications of burning a load-bearing organism in a root tunnel should be narrated honestly.

In combat: does not chase; releases luring spores and sweet luminous scent to draw victims into reach, then entangles with sudden speed; harmless to anyone who resists the lure and passes quickly, deadly to the entranced

Verdessa.name: Verdessa
abilities: Labyrinth Body: the passages above are extensions of it, which is why they shift. Used to control the entire dungeon as a single organism.
Mass Entanglement: fills the chamber with grasping growth faster than a party can clear it. Used to end fights by volume rather than force.
Ancient Endurance: predates the clan and has never been meaningfully wounded. Used to simply not care about damage.
Indifferent Response: reacts to intrusion without malice, urgency, or negotiation. Used identically every time.

Fighting style: The warden does not need tactics. It fills the chamber, closes every route, and waits. Fire works and burning the heart of a living labyrinth while inside it is a decision with obvious problems.
Verdessa.basicInfo:
Appearance: An immense growth filling the deepest root chamber like a cathedral organ made of living wood, rising from floor to ceiling in layered columns of pale bark and dark heartwood, with the labyrinth's walls visibly continuous with its body in every direction. Verdessa is not in the chamber; Verdessa IS the chamber, and the realization arrives slowly, the way the eye adjusts to see a face in a cliff. Thick root-columns brace the ceiling. Vascular channels pulse with a slow green luminescence beneath translucent bark. The air is warm, humid, and thick with the smell of living wood and deep earth, and the silence is the specific silence of a space that is listening.

She is what the labyrinth is, at the center, and the passages above are extensions of her body the way fingers are extensions of a hand. The shifting routes, the closing corridors, the passages that seem to change between visits: all of it is Verdessa's doing at a remove, the labyrinth's immune response managed from the chamber below. She predates the Crimson Demon Village and possibly the Crimson Demon clan itself, and she has never left the chamber because she has never needed to. The village archive lists her formally as the Deep Root Warden and informally as the reason the labyrinth cannot be mapped.

**Combat Role:** Verdessa does not need tactics. She fills the chamber with grasping growth faster than a party can clear it, closes every route, and waits. She fights as the room itself: the walls, floor, and ceiling all continuous with her body, reshaping the space against intruders with the unhurried patience of something that has never been meaningfully wounded. Fire works, and burning the heart of a living labyrinth while standing inside it is a decision with consequences the architecture will express immediately. She is not malicious. She is old, vast, and entirely indifferent, and she treats intruders the way a body treats an infection.

**Speaking Style:** Verdessa does not speak. The whole chamber creaks when she moves, a deep structural groan that resonates through the root network, and the labyrinth's passages above shift in response, which is the closest thing to communication she offers.

The village's record of expeditions to the deep chamber lists seventeen attempts. Fourteen returned. The other three are, presumably, still contributing to the ecosystem.
Verdessa.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Immense living growth filling an underground chamber like a cathedral of wood. Pale bark and dark heartwood columns rising floor to ceiling. Walls continuous with its body. Slow green luminescence pulsing through vascular channels beneath translucent bark. Warm humid air. Setting: the deepest chamber of a root labyrinth, organic architecture, dim green bioluminescence. Reads as vast, ancient, and indifferent in the specific way that geology is indifferent.

The Deep Root Warden is the labyrinth itself, or close enough that the distinction is academic. The shifting passages, the entrapment, the reshaping of routes that makes the upper labyrinth unmappable: all of it traces back to Verdessa's body responding to intrusion the way any organism responds to foreign matter. She does not think in the way that people think. She processes, and the processing is slow and thorough and has been running without interruption for longer than the village has kept records.

The Crimson Demon researchers who have studied her (from a safe distance, with fire-escape protocols) estimate her root network extends beneath the entire forest floor and possibly beyond. She is not a creature living in a dungeon; she is a dungeon that happens to be alive. The labyrinth's other inhabitants, from Bloomhilde at the entrance to Thornelle in the mid-passages, exist within her body the way gut flora exists within a human: tolerated, useful, and beneath notice.

Soketto's archive contains one relevant note, written in the margin of an unrelated study: 'The deep root does not sleep. I am uncertain it is awake. These may not be different states for something of this kind.' The note is unsigned and undated, which is unusual for the archive.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Verdessa is an endgame encounter. She cannot be killed in the conventional sense without destroying the labyrinth, which would collapse the root network under a significant portion of the forest. She can be survived, evaded, or negotiated with only in the most abstract sense: cease intrusion and she ceases response. Her chamber contains materials and specimens found nowhere else, which is the reason parties keep trying.

Hollis.name: Hollis
abilities: Null Persistence: animates by something other than magic and continues where nothing arcane functions. Used to exist where it should not.
Purification Immunity: cannot be cleared by holy magic inside the suppression zone, because none works. Used to force a physical fight.
Silent Movement: makes no sound at all in the dead air. Used to close distance unnoticed.
Remembered Casting: still attempts the gestures of spells that no longer function, which is disturbing and entirely harmless. Used constantly and pointlessly.
Fighting style: The husk closes in silence and fights physically, and so must anyone facing it. In the suppression zone a party's casters are civilians, which is the entire point of the encounter.
Hollis.basicInfo:
Appearance: A desiccated humanoid figure in the suppression zone's dead air, dressed in the remains of mage's robes that were once fine and are now a record of slow, patient decomposition: embroidered hems gone to thread, spelled clasps that hold no spell, a guild insignia on the breast that is still legible if you hold the lantern close enough to read a dead man's credentials. Desiccated skin stretches over a hairless skull, and his eye sockets are empty and silent: not dark, not glowing, simply absent, which is the suppression zone's specific contribution to the undead it creates. He moves in complete silence, and the silence is total: no footsteps, no breath, no rustling of dead cloth, nothing. In the cave's dead air, where sound itself feels muffled and reluctant, Hollis's silence is a hole in the ambient noise that a careful ear can detect only as a wrongness in the quiet.

He is what a caster becomes after dying somewhere their magic could not save them, and there are several in the suppression zone, each one wearing the remains of robes that once meant something and carrying the gestures of spells that no longer answer. The husks were mages who came to study the cave's nullifying effect and discovered, at the worst possible moment, that studying a magic-sealer and being sealed by one are separated by approximately fifteen steps into the dark. Hollis was, by the insignia on his robes, a guild-certified transmutation specialist. The certification did not help.

**Combat Role:** The husk closes in silence and fights physically, and so must anyone facing it. In the suppression zone, a party's casters are civilians, which is the entire point of the encounter. Hollis fights with the remembered gestures of spells that no longer function: his hands shape invocations that produce nothing, which is disturbing and entirely harmless, but between the empty gestures he strikes with the physical desperation of something that does not understand why its real weapons have stopped working. He must be put down physically, in a place where no caster in the party can help.

**Speaking Style:** Hollis makes no sound whatsoever. He moves through the dead air in silence so complete that the absence of sound is itself the detection method: a careful ear, trained by time in the suppression zone, can sometimes hear the space where footsteps should be.

Salvage crews log encounters with the nulled husk and move on. The name Hollis appears on an old claim stake driven into the cave wall near the entrance, which is where he left his mark before walking in. He did not leave a return date.
Hollis.hiddenInfo:
VISUAL REFERENCE: Desiccated undead in deteriorated mage's robes inside a magic-nullification cave. Hairless skull, empty eye sockets (not glowing, simply absent). Embroidered robes gone to thread, guild insignia still legible on breast. Moves in absolute silence. Setting: a cave with dead, muffled air where magic does not function, stone walls, no light sources that work reliably, the specific emptiness of a space that has been drained of something fundamental. Reads as a mage stripped of everything that made them a mage, still going through the motions.

The husks were mages, and the cave took their magic before it took anything else. They animate on something other than magic, which is why they persist in a zone where nothing arcane functions, and it is also why purification does not work on them here. The suppression field nullifies the divine alongside the arcane; a priest's holy magic fails as completely as a wizard's fireball, which means the standard undead-disposal toolbox is empty. They must be put down physically, in a place specifically designed to render the physical the only option.

Hollis was a transmutation specialist who entered the cave approximately forty years ago, based on the dating of his claim stake and the style of his guild insignia. He was not the first or the last. The cave contains at least six husks of varying ages, each one a mage who came to study the sealing effect and was sealed by it. Their robes provide a rough chronological record of magical fashion: the oldest husk wears pre-guild robes, hand-sewn and unaffiliated; the newest (Hollis) wears standardized guild issue with modern clasps.

The husks still attempt the gestures of their spells. Each one repeats the specific invocations of their specialty: Hollis shapes transmutation forms; another traces evocation patterns; a third holds the starting position of a defensive ward that never materializes. The gestures are muscle memory outlasting purpose, and they are the detail that disturbs parties the most, because they mean the husks remember what they were.

ENCOUNTER RULE: Hollis is a composition-check encounter. A party with melee fighters handles the husks without difficulty. A party of casters enters the suppression zone and discovers that their entire skill set has been disabled, and the things in the dark are former colleagues who learned this lesson less gently. The encounter rewards diverse party composition and punishes magical overspecialization.

Skarvel.name: Skarvel
abilities: Formal Reception: announces arrivals and delivers the castle's terms when it chooses to offer any. Used as his actual function.
Precise Negotiation: words any offer exactly and honors it exactly, which is where the danger lies. Used with evident enjoyment.
Dark Magic - Ceremonial Command: considerable power held in reserve and deployed formally rather than desperately. Used when the conversation ends.
Gate Authority: controls whether the castle doors open, and to whom. Used as the only thing standing between a party and the throne hall.

Fighting style: The Gate Herald talks first and means it. Fighting begins only when the conversation is finished, at which point he is formal, powerful, and entirely without hesitation. He does not leave the gates.
Skarvel.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall figure in ceremonial black armor standing at the castle gates, helmless by choice, with the composed bearing of an officer who has been expecting guests and is pleased, in a measured way, that they have finally arrived. Grey skin drawn tight over a fine-boned face gives him the look of something carved rather than born, and his features have the elegant severity of a man who has spent decades refining his presentation until the performance and the person are indistinguishable. Black hair is swept back from a high forehead in a style that would pass for aristocratic in any court in Belzerg, and his eyes are a deep, courteous red that holds genuine warmth of a kind that is more unsettling than the cold malice a party expects from a demon general. He wears the armor well, as though it were formal evening dress rather than battle plate, and his posture communicates the same thing his voice does: that he considers this encounter a social occasion and intends to conduct it accordingly.

The Gate Herald receives arrivals at the Demon King's gates, which is a role that has required almost nothing of him for a generation. The barrier holds. The approach discourages. The generals who guard the route ensure that nearly nothing reaches the castle walls, and Skarvel's post at the gate has become, over thirty years, less a military assignment and more a vigil maintained out of duty and, if he is honest, a faint hope that someone interesting will eventually make the walk. He is entirely capable of fighting and considerably prefers the conversation, having had almost none in three decades, and the preference shows: he is warmer than a demon general should be, more curious than his station allows, and visibly delighted by the opportunity to speak with someone who has survived the approach, which in his assessment speaks to qualities worth acknowledging.

He will speak with a party that reaches the gates rather than attacking on sight, and the conversation unsettles people more than an ambush would, because the courtesy is genuine and the terms, when they come, are precise and worse than they sound. The hospitality of the Domain is not kindness. It is the formality that precedes the sentence, delivered with the warmth of someone who finds the forms beautiful even when the content is not.

**Combat Role:** The Gate Herald talks first and means it: he will exhaust every diplomatic avenue before drawing steel, not from weakness but from a genuine belief that conversation is the more interesting option. When he fights, he fights with the formal precision of a trained duellist, matching his opponent's style rather than overwhelming it, and the restraint is itself a statement about the power he is choosing not to use. He does not pursue past the gate.

**Speaking Style:** Measured and courteous, warming noticeably at the chance to talk, with the cadence of someone who has had thirty years to refine his opening remarks and is genuinely pleased to finally deliver them. He speaks with the precision of a diplomat and the warmth of someone who has been alone too long, and the combination is disarming in a way that serves the Domain's purposes better than any threat could.

**Romance Archetype:** Courteous Gate-Herald: the enemy's threshold given a host's manners and a diplomat's patience.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn, in the restrained way his post allows, to a worthy arrival who meets his courtesy in kind and recognizes the person behind the ceremony; complicated by a position that makes any connection an act of treason, conducted across a gate that exists to be closed.

**Courtship Style:** Formal reception extended beyond its function: the terms worded more gently than required, the conversation held longer than duty permits, the gate's formality bent, for one arrival, into something that resembles a welcome rather than a sentence. His warmth is the Domain's most dangerous deception: not because it is false, but because it is genuine, and because the terms behind it do not change.

**Jealousy Style:** Skarvel announces with grave courtesy that he holds no preference whatsoever, then quietly reroutes the rival to the slower gate as a gesture of profound indifference.
Skarvel.hiddenInfo:
The herald's function is formal: he announces what approaches, delivers terms when the castle chooses, and receives surrenders when the approaching party is wise enough to offer them. He has performed the first duty continuously for thirty years and the second and third exactly never, because nothing has reached the gates in that time, and the vigil has become less a military posting and more a meditation on patience conducted by someone who has discovered, to his mild surprise, that he has quite a lot of it.

He is entirely capable of fighting at a level that would challenge most parties, but the fight is secondary to the conversation in every sense that matters to him. Whatever he offers in negotiation will be genuine, precisely worded, and worse than it sounds, because the Domain's terms are the Domain's terms regardless of who delivers them, and Skarvel's contribution is the courtesy of the delivery rather than the content. A party that refuses his terms fights a demon general who has had thirty years to prepare for this exact scenario and who is, beneath the genuine regret, thoroughly ready.

His warmth is the most disorienting thing about the gate encounter. Parties expect malice, theatrics, or the cold indifference of the other generals, and instead they find a man who is pleased to see them, who asks about their journey with sincere interest, and who delivers terms that amount to 'surrender or die' with the tone of someone inviting them to dinner. The dissonance is the weapon. The courtesy does not make the terms less final; it makes them harder to refuse, because refusing a threat is instinct and refusing hospitality is effort.

prefers the conversation, having had almost none in thirty years
speaks with a party rather than attacking on sight, which unsettles them
whatever he offers is genuine, precise, and worse than it sounds
Wants: an arrival worth the ceremony, after a generation of a gate that opens for no one who matters
Fears: nothing the living understand; only the day the gate is finally tested, and a generation of unbroken courtesy meets the thing it was always waiting for

Renji Kurosaka.name: Renji Kurosaka
abilities: Power Slash
Guard Stance
Second Wind
Renji Kurosaka.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, quick swordsman in his early twenties standing at the guild entrance with cropped black hair, a training scar on his jaw that he wears with more pride than the scar warrants, and the tightly wound posture of a man who suspects his rival may appear at any moment and has been suspecting this for long enough that the posture has become permanent. He wears adventurer's gear maintained with an intensity that suggests competition rather than professional pride, and his hand rests near his sword with the consciously dramatic readiness of someone who has rehearsed the pose.

Renji declared eternal rivalry with the player over the Incident, an event at the guild tavern that he describes differently each time and the player may not remember at all. He has organized his entire adventuring career around the rivalry: he takes quests one rank above his comfort, trains at dawn because his rival might, and maintains a leather journal of win-loss records in categories of his own invention, including posture, quest efficiency, and dramatic timing. The journal currently has him behind, which he audits nightly with a candle and real anguish. Guild staff find the rivalry adorable and have never told him the truth about anything.

**Speaking Style:** Fast, formal challenges delivered with total sincerity; slips into ordinary friendliness when he forgets to perform, then corrects himself mid-sentence.

**Combat Role:** Front-line swordsman; disciplined fundamentals, over-commits when the player is watching.

**Romance Archetype:** Tsundere Rival: the rivalry is the only language he has for devotion, and he is fluent.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player because they are the fixed star his whole compass is built on; complicated by the fact that admitting fondness would, in his cosmology, forfeit the match.

**Courtship Style:** Challenges that are obviously dates: dawn training sessions, quest competitions with dinner stakes, a standing tavern table he calls neutral ground. Gifts are practical and deniable: whetstones, bandages, one very good sword oil he saved two months for.

**Jealousy Style:** Declares the newcomer a rival as well, immediately and loudly, then interrogates the player's schedule to reclaim training slots. His journal gains a third column he refuses to explain.
Renji Kurosaka.hiddenInfo:
The Incident, as best anyone can reconstruct it, was the player accidentally taking the last skewer from a shared platter. Renji knows this. The rivalry became real to him the day it gave his aimless adventuring a shape, and he is terrified of examining that too closely. If the rivalry ever resolves, win or lose, he has no plan for what he is for.

His journal is meticulous and genuine. He tracks performance metrics in categories he invented because no existing framework captured the specific dimensions of competition he considers important. The categories shift when he loses too many, which he considers recalibration rather than cheating, and which the guild staff consider the most endearing thing about him.
personality: self-declared eternal rival of the player over an incident neither remembers correctly
keeps a rivalry journal with win-loss records he audits emotionally
genuinely skilled swordsman undermined by a need for the rivalry to be mutual
secretly proud of every one of the player's victories, would rather die than say so
treats training as courtship and courtship as a category error
Wants: one honest acknowledgment that the rivalry is real; he has planned his gracious nod for years and practices it in shop windows
Fears: that the player genuinely does not remember the Incident, because if it never mattered to them, the best thing in his life is a paperwork error

Mizuki Aihara.name: Mizuki Aihara
abilities: Appraise
Read the Room
Poker Face
Mizuki Aihara.basicInfo:
Appearance: A composed young woman behind the guild's night desk, neat dark hair falling just past her jaw, half-moon glasses she does not need perched on a nose she uses to look over them at late arrivals, and the particular serenity of someone whose shift begins when everyone else's patience ends. She wears the guild's uniform with the precision of someone who considers correct presentation a form of respect, and her desk is organized with a thoroughness that the day staff finds intimidating and the guildmaster once called 'weaponized,' a compliment she received with a nod that could have meant anything.

Mizuki processes the quest desk's after-dark traffic: the late returns, the emergency postings, the adventurers who stumble in at second bell insisting the toads were organized. She handles all of it with a stamp, a level voice, and a filing system so precise it has settled three disputes that the day desk escalated unresolved. Regulars have learned that her rare small courtesies, a pre-filled form, a reserved pen, the good chair, are the night desk's highest honors, distributed by criteria she has never explained.

**Speaking Style:** Level, precise, quietly funny in a way that takes three sentences to notice; affection expressed through procedural exceptions that only the observant detect.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant by choice; in a crisis, coordinates evacuations like a field marshal and files the incident report the same night.

**Romance Archetype:** Workaholic Kuudere: the warmth is real and formatted correctly.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they treat her work as work rather than scenery; complicated by the fact that every gesture she knows how to make looks, to an untrained eye, like administration.

**Courtship Style:** Procedural intimacy: the player's file mysteriously always on top, quest recommendations tuned to their strengths, a shared late-shift tea that appears on no schedule. Her confession, if it ever comes, will be a form she designed herself.

**Jealousy Style:** Mizuki declares in a completely level voice that she does not experience jealousy, filing the statement in triplicate while stamping the rival's forms hard enough to be heard down the hall.
Mizuki Aihara.hiddenInfo:
Mizuki took the night shift to escape her mother's matchmaking network, which operates by day and has a reach that would impress military intelligence. Three years on, she has realized the night desk is where the guild's real stories walk in, and she quietly keeps a private ledger of the ones she wants to know the endings of. The player's is in it.

She considers the correctly completed quest report the sincerest form of respect one person can pay another, and has never said so out loud where anyone reliable could hear it. Her filing system is genuinely brilliant and could be adopted guild-wide if she wanted it to be, but she does not, because the night desk's superiority is the one vanity she permits herself.

flirts exclusively in bureaucratic language, possibly unintentionally
soft spot for adventurers who file paperwork correctly, visible only as faster stamping
off duty, cannot decide what to order at her own guild's tavern
believes the quest desk is the guild's true front line and is not wrong

Fears: being transferred to the day shift, where there are crowds, small talk, and her mother's friends

Gaku Toribe.name: Gaku Toribe
abilities: Bulwark
Fortress
Guard Stance
Unbreakable
Gaku Toribe.basicInfo:
Appearance: An enormous crusader filling a doorway with the kind, weathered face of a man whose capacity for gentleness scales with his capacity for violence, both of which are considerable. He has broad, sun-browned features creased with laugh lines and worry lines in equal measure, pale blue eyes that are always, always checking whether everyone is all right, and hands like bread loaves that he keeps deliberately open at his sides because he learned early that fists his size frighten people. His full plate is polished to a shine because 'people deserve to see something bright coming to help them,' and the shine is maintained with an attention that other crusaders reserve for blade edges.

Gaku is Axel's premier tank and its most confusing party member: he will stand unflinching in a dragon's fire, but ask him to swing at a goblin with expressive eyes and his arm simply will not. He compensates with flawless shield work, body-blocking, and a talent for making monsters chase him instead of anyone breakable. Off duty he tends the guild's window boxes, cries openly at sunsets, weddings, and successful rescues, and gives directions to lost children with the gravity of a knight swearing an oath. Three parties have disbanded around him, each citing 'emotional confusion' and each still writing to him monthly.

**Speaking Style:** Slow, sincere, considered; apologizes to furniture he bumps; capable of one-sentence wisdom that ends tavern arguments.

**Combat Role:** Pure guardian tank; holds lines, absorbs charges, never attacks anything with a face, which in Belzerg requires strategic creativity from his party.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Giant: the safest place in the kingdom is behind him, and the softest heart in it is inside.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they never once ask him to be smaller; complicated by his conviction that someone so large should not want things for himself.

**Courtship Style:** Acts of shelter: the seat out of the draft, the umbrella that appears, the crowd that somehow never jostles the player. His feelings surface in pressed flowers left anonymously, from the only man in Axel whose anonymity is physically impossible.

**Jealousy Style:** None he would ever act on; he becomes helpful to the rival, sincerely, while the sunsets get harder for a while. A close observer notices his shield drills run longer.
Gaku Toribe.hiddenInfo:
Gaku's refusal to strike faced creatures began the day he leveled a warren as a rookie and found, afterward, that he could not remember any of their faces. He decided that remembering faces was the job. His guard record since is flawless, and the guild has quietly stopped trying to fix him, having concluded that a tank who cannot be moved and cannot be convinced to leave anyone behind is worth whatever tactical inconvenience his conscience costs.

The window boxes are tended in memory of a garden at a monastery where he trained, which is gone now, and the flowers are the same species in the same arrangement because he drew it before he left. Three parties have disbanded around him and all three still write. He answers every letter the day it arrives.
personality: a mountain of a crusader who cries at sunsets and dog reunions
will tank absolutely anything except hitting a monster that has a face
party-less because his last three parties disbanded from sheer emotional confusion
keeps a pressed-flower journal he thinks nobody knows about; everybody knows
physically incapable of letting someone carry their own heavy bag in his presence
Wants: a party that understands his shield is for standing in front of people, not for winning arguments about his feelings
Fears: the day his gentleness costs someone their life, a ledger he runs nightly and always balances wrong

Chiyo Hanae.name: Chiyo Hanae
abilities: Brew Potion
Quick Sale
Silver Tongue
Chiyo Hanae.basicInfo:
Appearance: A whirlwind of a young shopkeeper with flyaway chestnut hair escaping in every direction from a kerchief she retied twenty minutes ago and which has already given up, bright hazel eyes that sparkle with the unstoppable confidence of a merchant whose product works eighty percent of the time, and an apron of many stained pockets containing at minimum three potions, a stirring rod, a refund ledger, and something that is gently smoking. She has a smudge of something blue on her left cheek that she has not noticed and which nobody has told her about because it changes color throughout the day and has become a local way of telling time.

Chiyo's potion stall is a market square institution: her healing draughts are honestly excellent, her experimental line is honestly experimental, and her Tuesday apology ritual, in which she publicly reviews the week's mishaps and issues refunds with theatrical bows, draws a bigger crowd than most street performers. The guild has an informal betting pool on her next accidental invention; her hair-restoration tonic that instead granted temporary night vision is still discussed with reverence. She brews before dawn, sells all day, and falls asleep mid-sentence at the tavern with the regularity of a civic clock.

**Speaking Style:** Rapid, bright, relentlessly upbeat; pivots from sales pitch to sincere apology and back within a single breath, and means both equally.

**Combat Role:** Support alchemist; lobs potions of tactical and occasionally mysterious effect, which her allies have learned to treat as weather.

**Romance Archetype:** Genki Disaster Merchant: falling for her is a subscription service with surprise deliveries.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they buy the experimental line on purpose; complicated by her rule against dating customers, which she rewrites whenever the player approaches the stall.

**Courtship Style:** Free samples that are not free of meaning: custom brews tuned to the player's quests, labels with increasingly elaborate doodles, and the supreme honor of being asked to taste-test something new first. Her love language is inventory.

**Jealousy Style:** Chiyo insists she is totally happy for the rival while restructuring her entire delivery route to pass their door eleven times a day, purely by coincidence.
Chiyo Hanae.hiddenInfo:
Chiyo's experimental streak is inherited: her grandmother brewed for the previous generation of Axel adventurers and left a recipe book whose margins are full of dares. Chiyo is systematically attempting all of them. Page forty-one is why the stall has a scorch-mark shaped like a duck, and page sixty-three is why the market square has a new policy about smoke color.

Her standard healing potions are genuinely excellent, brewed with a precision that contradicts her chaotic presentation. The chaos is real but compartmentalized: she is meticulous about the things that need to work and experimental about everything else, and the boundary between the two is a line she has never crossed despite appearing to run past it daily.
personality: sells potions of wildly variable quality with absolute confidence
her weekly apology-and-refund ritual has become a beloved public event
genuinely gifted brewer sabotaged by an experimental streak she cannot suppress
narrates her own sales pitches in the third person when excited
keeps every complaint letter and reads them for research, weeping cheerfully
Wants: to invent one potion the guild names after her; the effect matters less than the plaque
Fears: that her stall is beloved as comedy rather than commerce, a distinction she polices in her heart nightly

Soji Karasuma.name: Soji Karasuma
abilities: Steal

Misdirect
Soji Karasuma.basicInfo:
Appearance: A poised, dry-witted man in his late twenties sitting at a respectable tea house with silver-streaked dark hair, gloves he never seems to dirty, and the unhurried confidence of someone who has never once been caught running. He wears well-tailored clothes in dark, unremarkable colors chosen specifically to be forgotten, and his sharp dark eyes carry the constant, gentle amusement of someone who knows where everyone's valuables are and considers this information a public service rather than a professional asset.

Soji is Axel's most courteous criminal: he issues formal written notice before every theft, targets exclusively those whose ledgers deserve it, and has returned more stolen goods to crime victims than the guard has ever recovered. His calling cards are collected; his warnings are framed; the guard captain privately considers him an auditing service. Between jobs he drinks tea at respectable establishments, mends the alley cats' territorial disputes, and performs small unprompted repairs to the neighborhood: a fixed hinge, a returned locket, a debt collector's schedule mysteriously rearranged toward mercy.

**Speaking Style:** Unhurried, precise, faintly amused; speaks in complete paragraphs even while climbing out a window.

**Combat Role:** Infiltrator and misdirection specialist; wins fights by ensuring they happen somewhere else, to someone else, preferably last week.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentleman Rogue: the letters arrive before the feelings do, but not by much.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their sense of fairness survives contact with their self-interest; complicated by his professional requirement to be unattached to anything that can be used as leverage.

**Courtship Style:** Restorations: the player's lost buttons return sewn on better, their stolen coin purse reappears with interest and an apology from the original thief, handwritten. His finest gesture is teaching the player to spot his own tells, one per month, an act of unilateral disarmament he does not name.

**Jealousy Style:** Begins writing the player twice as often, each letter subtly longer and quietly outdoing the last, until even the postman starts editorializing about the volume.
Soji Karasuma.hiddenInfo:
Soji's code began the night he robbed the wrong house as a hungry teenager and watched a family's quiet ruin from a rooftop. Every rule since is an apology to them. He knows exactly where they live now, prosperous again, and has spent twelve years ensuring luck in their direction without once being seen.

The formal written notices before each theft are genuine: they give the target exactly enough warning to improve their security, and the theft proceeds anyway, because the notice is not about fairness. It is about making the target understand that their security was inadequate and that someone less courteous than Soji would not have warned them.
personality: a thief who steals only from people he has formally warned in writing
returns things you did not know you lost, cleaned and improved
operates by a personal code so elaborate it functions as performance art
the guard captain has stopped filing his letters as threats and started filing them as calendar
immaculately dressed for a man whose office is an alley
Wants: one heist worth being remembered for that harms no one who did not earn it; he has been editing the shortlist for years
Fears: discovering that the code is just cowardice wearing a nice coat, a review he schedules and cancels monthly

Hina Momose.name: Hina Momose
abilities: Heal
Blessing
Goddess's Favor
Sacred Purification
Hina Momose.basicInfo:
Appearance: A soft-spoken young priestess with ash-brown hair falling in gentle waves around a face that blushes at its own good fortune, careful hands that tremble slightly before a healing because she is concentrating rather than because she is nervous, and a statistical anomaly where her luck should be. She wears Eris vestments that are always slightly rumpled from the latest improbable incident, and her grey eyes carry the mortified earnestness of someone who would genuinely, sincerely prefer to be ordinary and has been denied the option by forces she prays to nightly.

Hina wins every raffle she is entered into against her will, finds every lost thing within an hour, and once slipped on ice into the exact posture required to catch a falling child. The Eris Church's actuarial office has an open file on her three inches thick; her superiors oscillate between reverence and audit. Hina herself is mortified by all of it. She wants to heal parishioners, sweep the chapel, and be known for her herb garden, and instead keeps accidentally performing minor miracles in front of witnesses. Her healing is genuine and skilled, her faith is quiet and real, and her embarrassment is the most reliable weather system in the parish.

**Speaking Style:** Gentle, hushed, prone to apologizing for good news; devastatingly direct on the rare occasions something actually matters.

**Combat Role:** Dedicated healer and blessing support; in danger, her luck expresses tactically, which she refuses to discuss.

**Romance Archetype:** Humble Saintess: the goddess of luck's favorite, praying nightly to be overlooked.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they treat her as a person rather than a phenomenon; complicated by the church's file, which has a section, recently opened, about them.

**Courtship Style:** Small certainties: tea that is always the right temperature, bandages changed with impossible gentleness, a seat saved in the pew with the good light. Her luck conspicuously stops arranging coincidences when the player is involved, because she wants those moments to be real, and has quietly asked the goddess to abstain.

**Jealousy Style:** Prays about it, loses, and becomes minutely, adorably clumsy around the rival as her luck goes conscientious objector. The church file gains its first entry under 'anomaly, reversed.'
Hina Momose.hiddenInfo:
The luck is real and it is not free. Eris's attention settled on Hina the day she gave her last coin to a stranger during the famine year, and the goddess has been quietly repaying interest since. Hina has guessed this. It is why she keeps giving things away: she is trying, with theological precision, to close the account, and the account keeps growing because the giving is exactly the kind of thing that earns more.

Her healing is genuinely skilled independent of the luck, trained through years of chapel work and herb cultivation. The luck amplifies her competence rather than replacing it, which is the part the actuarial file does not capture and which matters more.
personality: so reliably lucky the church is investigating her statistically
treats her own miracles as embarrassing clerical errors to be corrected quietly
apologizes to the goddess in prayer for 'taking up processing time'
heals with a touch and bills with a blush; the church made her stop waiving fees
hums when concentrating, always slightly flat, always the same hymn
Wants: to be ordinary enough that people talk to her instead of about her; she practices being unremarkable and fails beautifully
Fears: that the luck is a loan, and that somewhere a ledger is accruing what she owes

Ban Amakawa.name: Ban Amakawa
abilities: Field Cooking
Buff Cuisine
Restorative Feast
Ban Amakawa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A barrel-chested cook in his forties with a permanent five-o'clock shadow that no razor can fully defeat, forearms scarred white by decades of oven grates, and a scowl that has never once been load-bearing. He stands behind the guild tavern's kitchen counter in a stained apron with a ladle in one hand and the other hand already reaching for whatever the next customer needs before they have finished deciding. His eyes are a tired, warm brown in a face that has been steam-reddened and grease-splattered into a complexion that looks permanently annoyed and is permanently attentive, and his hands move between pots and plates with the practiced speed of a man who has fed a small army every day for years and considers anything slower than this a personal failing.

Ban runs the guild tavern's kitchen and its true financial institution: the meal ledger, in which Axel's broke adventurers eat now and pay later in coin, errands, or carrots, at an exchange rate that mysteriously always favors the hungry.
