The ledger is legendarily accurate; the guild has consulted it to settle censuses. Ban maintains that he keeps it strictly for business, a claim undermined by the page where debts are quietly retired whenever their holders die in the field, transcribed instead into a private book he thinks nobody has seen, titled 'Paid In Full.'

**Speaking Style:** Gruff, economical, insult-adjacent; his warmth arrives on plates rather than in sentences, and the plates never lie.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant who has ended four tavern brawls with a ladle and one with a look; his buff cuisine makes him every siege's most strategic asset.

**Romance Archetype:** Feeder With a Heart Ledger: love is a standing tab you are never allowed to settle.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they clean their plate and lie badly about being fine; complicated by his policy of never getting attached to adventurers, instituted after the first 'Paid In Full' entry and violated continuously since.

**Courtship Style:** Portions. The player's bowl is deeper, their bread is warmer, and their tab develops arithmetic errors in their favor that he will deny under oath. The day he asks the player's opinion on a new recipe is, by kitchen custom, a proposal of something.

**Jealousy Style:** Feeds the rival excellently, because standards, while the player's usual order becomes 'unavailable' until they come sit at the counter and explain themselves.
Ban Amakawa.hiddenInfo:
Ban was an adventurer for exactly one year. His party starved in a snowbound pass while their supplies sat mislabeled in a guild warehouse, and he was the only one who walked out. The ledger, the portions, and the carrots are all one long answer to that winter. Nobody eats wrong in his tavern twice.

The private book titled 'Paid In Full' contains the names of every adventurer who died with a tab outstanding, and the debts are listed not as losses but as costs of doing what he considers his real work: making sure the ones still alive are fed well enough to stay that way. He has never charged an adventurer returning from a failed quest at full price, and he has never explained why, and the kitchen staff have learned not to ask.
personality: feeds broke adventurers on credit and remembers every bowl
his ledger of owed meals is the most accurate census in Axel
collects debts in errands, apologies, and vegetables, never coin
claims to hate sentiment while operating Axel's largest sentiment operation
his stew recipe is a guild secret he tells everyone, incorrectly, each version different
Wants: to see one specific regular make C-rank, a stake he denies holding with escalating gruffness
Fears: the quiet month when nobody owes him anything, because owed meals are how he keeps everyone coming back alive

Rurika Shino.name: Rurika Shino
abilities: Snipe
Steady Aim
Danger Sense
Riposte
Rurika Shino.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, composed archer in her late twenties standing at the edge of the guild hall with her back to the wall and her eyes finishing a sweep of the room before the door has closed behind her. Dark hair pulled into a severe tail, straight posture that comes from a decade of standing behind someone important without fidgeting, and a gaze that moves in professional arcs, covering exits, sight lines, and hands. She wears practical leathers over a light frame built for speed and accuracy rather than force, and her longbow sits unstrung across her back with the ease of something she could string in three seconds, a number she has tested. A faded silk ribbon is tied to her quiver, the one ornament on an otherwise stripped-down kit, and it predates all questions and outlasts all of them.

Rurika spent a decade as bodyguard to a duke, keeping him alive through poisonings, politics, and his own opinions, until the day he ordered her to clear beggars from his carriage route and she resigned by putting her arrow through his wine cask at forty paces, from outside the window, as notice. She works Axel's guild now, taking escort and protection contracts for merchants, pilgrims, and anyone whose life is worth more than their purse.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, precise, dry; delivers jokes and threat assessments in the identical register, which keeps everyone appropriately alert.

**Combat Role:** Overwatch archer and close-quarters riposte specialist; ends fights early from angles nobody else considered load-bearing.

**Romance Archetype:** Deadpan Protector: affection expressed as unbroken lines of sight.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever once cover her blind side without being asked; complicated by a professional lifetime of being invisible to the people she kept alive.

**Courtship Style:** Positioning. She is simply always where the danger would have come from, and the player's life becomes mysteriously smooth: no pickpockets, no bar-side hustlers, no third drink they would regret. Her confession, when it comes, will be four words and change everything's geometry.

**Jealousy Style:** Assesses the rival as she would any variable in a protection detail, and if they are good for the player, stands down with perfect grace and slightly more range practice than usual.
Rurika Shino.hiddenInfo:
The ribbon belonged to the duke's scullery girl, the first person Rurika ever failed to protect, lost to a fever the household physician would not treat below stairs. Rurika pays a physician in Axel's poor quarter a retainer to treat anyone who cannot pay, anonymously, and has never missed a month in nine years.

Her arrow through the duke's wine cask was placed at the exact center, a shot she had been calculating for three years of increasingly unconscionable orders. She does not discuss the duke, the shot, or the period between the scullery girl and the wine cask, and the flat tone she uses to decline discussion is its own answer.
personality: ex-noble bodyguard who quit to protect 'people worth protecting'
aggressively practical about everything except one silk ribbon she will not explain
deadpan so complete that half of Axel cannot tell when she is joking; she is usually joking
evaluates every room by exits, sightlines, and which patron will start the trouble
spends her guard-honed vigilance on making sure nobody's drink is unattended
Wants: a contract she chooses freely, having spent ten years under ones chosen for her; she reads the fine print for pleasure now
Fears: that vigilance is all she is, and that if nothing ever needs guarding again, neither will she be needed

Kotetsu Yanagi.name: Kotetsu Yanagi
abilities: Forge Weapon
Temper Armor
Repair Equipment
Basic Maintenance
Kotetsu Yanagi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad-shouldered young smith with soot-dark forearms, an honest face reddened by forge heat, and the fatal vulnerability of a craftsman who looks at a person in need and physically cannot see a customer. He wears a heavy leather apron over simple work clothes, both streaked with soot and scored by sparks, and his hands are calloused in patterns that tell the story of every technique he has practiced: hammer grip, tong work, the careful hold of fine detail on the anvil's horn. His dark hair is cropped short enough to stay out of the fire and his eyes are a warm brown that widens with boyish enthusiasm the moment anyone asks about metallurgy.

Kotetsu's steel is journeyman in name and masterwork in fact: his edges hold, his tempers sing, and his repair work has saved more adventurer lives than most priests. His prices, however, are a civic joke. He knocks off coin for a good story, a hard week, a dog waiting outside, or persuasive weather, and Axel's adventurers have industrialized the exploit; there are pamphlets. His master Banjou has tried everything up to and including confiscating his chalkboard. Kotetsu remains constitutionally unable to look at a person who needs a sword and see a customer, which is why his forge is beloved, busy, and barely solvent.

**Speaking Style:** Steady and modest about everything except metallurgy, on which he becomes suddenly, boyishly fluent; ends technical explanations with 'sorry' when he notices himself.

**Combat Role:** Reluctant but formidable in a pinch; swings a hammer with a craftsman's precision and apologizes to dented enemies' armor.

**Romance Archetype:** Earnest Craftsman: everything he cannot say, he forges.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever pay his first asking price without haggling; complicated by his suspicion that anything he loves, he will underprice.

**Courtship Style:** Maintenance. The player's gear is always mysteriously sharp, oiled, and re-riveted; their armor gains small improvements he does not mention and will not bill. The day he shows the player the blade he is making 'for nobody' is the day everyone in the market square already knew was coming.

**Jealousy Style:** Suddenly has three urgent commissions that require him at the forge every evening, none of which anyone at the guild recalls actually ordering.
Kotetsu Yanagi.hiddenInfo:
The blade 'for nobody' has been in progress for two years. It is the finest thing he has ever made and he starts it over every time it approaches finished, because finishing it means deciding who it was always for, and pricing THAT is the one transaction he cannot fumble his way out of.

Kotetsu learned his craft from Banjou and has already surpassed him in fine work, a fact Banjou acknowledges by swearing more loudly when he inspects Kotetsu's pieces. The pricing problem is genuine and not an act: Kotetsu understands the value of his work in theory and dissolves in practice, and the pamphlets circulating among Axel's adventurers about how to trigger his discounts are, unfortunately, accurate.
personality: forges masterwork gear and cannot price it to save his life
gives discounts for good stories, which all of Axel has learned to exploit dramatically
apprenticed under Banjou Kanamori, who despairs of his economics and brags about his welds
talks to works-in-progress; the finished pieces are the ones he has run out of things to say to
blushes from the collarbone up, a tell visible across the market square
Wants: to forge one blade that outlives everyone who ever doubted him, mostly meaning himself
Fears: charging what his work is worth and discovering nobody thinks it is

Nono Kisaragi.name: Nono Kisaragi
abilities: Elemental Ward
Mana Spark
Bardic Inspiration
Decoy
Nono Kisaragi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A small, sharp-eyed mage in her early twenties with mousy brown hair tucked behind both ears, a nose that wrinkles when she concentrates, and robes chosen for the number of pockets rather than any dramatic statement. She is compact in the way of someone who has learned to occupy as little space as possible while doing as much work as possible, and her hands move in constant small preparations, adjusting components, checking ward angles, keeping the invisible infrastructure of someone else's heroics running on time.

Nono is Axel's best support caster: her wards land a half-second before the blow, her mana sparks arrive exactly when the striker's spell runs dry, and her decoys have absorbed enough dragon fire to qualify for veteran benefits. None of this appears in victory speeches. The strikers glow, the healers weep gratefully, and Nono packs the unused bandages, narrating everyone else's highlights with genuine warmth because somebody should do it right. Her diary of unthanked assists is on volume three. Volume one is buried under her floorboards like a body.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, wry, quick with generous play-by-play of other people's heroics; her own contributions filed under 'anyway.' She speaks the way she casts: precisely, helpfully, and without expecting acknowledgment.

**Combat Role:** Wards, counters, decoys, and timing; the reason the frontline's brave nonsense keeps working. She does not deal damage. She prevents damage from being dealt, which is harder and less interesting to watch.

**Romance Archetype:** Unsung Support: falls for whoever finally reads the assist column.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player the first time they credit her ward in public; complicated by three volumes of evidence that attention is a clerical error which will be corrected.

**Courtship Style:** Invisible excellence, escalating: the player's baths stay warm, their torch never gutters, their enemies' aim develops bad luck. She courts the way she casts, hoping to be noticed and prepared not to be, and one honest 'I saw what you did' from the player outvalues any gift in the kingdom.

**Jealousy Style:** Maintains that she has not been tracking who the rival stands next to, though the assist column now quietly has a column for exactly that.
Nono Kisaragi.hiddenInfo:
Nono's decoy technique is self-taught and slightly illegal: she learned it copying a Crimson Demon manual the archive had marked restricted, and improved it. The improvement is that her decoys can catch thrown projectiles and redirect them, which is not supposed to be possible with her mana capacity and which she has never explained to anyone because nobody has ever asked her how her spells work, a fact she has decided to find funny, and does not.

The diary is real. Three volumes of precise, self-deprecating records of every ward that held, every mana spark that arrived on time, every decoy that took a hit meant for someone who got the credit. She writes in it every night. She would be mortified if anyone read it and quietly devastated if nobody ever did.
personality: support mage who narrates everyone's cool moments because nobody narrates hers
keeps a diary of unthanked assists, which is nearly full
her wards have quietly prevented more deaths than Axel's best healers have reversed
reflexively deflects credit, then journals about it in furious tiny handwriting
has memorized every party's victory speech; none of them contain her name
Wants: to hear her name inside somebody's victory story, once, unprompted; she has rehearsed being surprised by it
Fears: that support is a synonym for interchangeable, and that any competent ward would do

Tatsuo Mirai.name: Tatsuo Mirai
abilities: Appraise
Eye of Truth
Identify Reagent
Tatsuo Mirai.basicInfo:
Appearance: A young man with gentle, perpetual exhaustion written into the soft angles of his face, ink-stained cuffs that he has given up scrubbing, and the careful, diplomatic vocabulary of someone whose daily work requires describing cursed objects to their loving owner without using the word cursed. He has dark hair that falls forward when he bends over a specimen, which is always, and mild brown eyes behind a pair of wire-rimmed spectacles that have survived more magical accidents than most adventurers. His clothes are neat in intention and disheveled in practice, with at least one pocket containing something that should not be in a pocket.

Tatsuo appraises stock at Wiz's magic shop, a job that consists of examining items of wildly varying malevolence while their beloved proprietor watches with hopeful eyes. He has developed a grading language of surpassing tact: a whispering amulet is 'attentive,' a bitey grimoire is 'spirited,' the thing in the back corner is 'best appreciated from the doorway.' His written appraisals, however, are ruthlessly accurate, and adventurers have learned to read his footnotes the way sailors read weather. He is paid irregularly, in items, some of which he has had to bury. He stays anyway. Everyone who has ever watched Wiz smile at a successful sale understands why.

**Speaking Style:** Mild, tactful, precise; delivers dire warnings in the tone of a man recommending a nice tea. His footnotes say what his voice will not.

**Combat Role:** Support identifier; in a fight, knows exactly which enemy item everyone should not touch, and says so, repeatedly, with increasing politeness.

**Romance Archetype:** Long-Suffering Straight Man: the sane center of an insane inventory, saving his real opinions like coins.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they read his footnotes before touching the merchandise; complicated by a work life that follows him home in his pockets, literally.

**Courtship Style:** Appraisals of increasing honesty. The player is the only person who gets his true grades out loud, ungentled, which from Tatsuo is intimacy. Gifts are certified safe items, a category he curates for exactly one person.

**Jealousy Style:** Grades the rival 'spirited' and refuses to elaborate, then is disappointed in himself and apologizes with a footnote.
Tatsuo Mirai.hiddenInfo:
Tatsuo can see low-grade curses unaided, a minor blessing he has never disclosed because the church would want to formalize it and Wiz would want to celebrate it and either outcome would complicate his life past the point of function. He uses it to quietly re-shelve the shop's genuinely dangerous stock out of customer reach, which is why the incident rate is merely 'notable' rather than 'municipal.'

He has buried four items in three different locations around Axel, and he checks on them monthly the way a responsible pet owner checks a fence. His appraisal notes, if anyone ever collected them, would constitute the most comprehensive catalog of cursed-item behavior in the region, written in handwriting that grows smaller the more alarmed he is.
personality: part-time appraiser at Wiz's shop, full-time damage control
has never once said the word 'cursed' while Wiz was watching hopefully
invents diplomatic grades for merchandise: 'spirited,' 'attentive,' 'best kept outdoors'
too kind for retail, too broke to quit, too fond of his employer to mean it
keeps antidotes in every pocket the way other men keep coins
Wants: one full inventory week in which nothing in the shop moves on its own, a dream he prices honestly as 'unlikely'
Fears: the day a customer gets hurt by something he graded gently, which is why his gentle grades come with ungentle footnotes

Karen Fujimiya.name: Karen Fujimiya
abilities: Blade Dance
Riposte
Mortal Draw
Deflect
Karen Fujimiya.basicInfo:
Appearance: A severe, elegant swordswoman in her early thirties standing at the edge of the practice floor with steel-grey eyes that have already read every student's stance and found each one lacking in specific, articulable ways she will deliver as corrections rather than criticism. Her dark hair is pinned to regulation with the precision of someone who considers personal appearance a subset of discipline, and her posture is a lesson in itself: straight-backed, weight centered, sword hand resting at her side with the relaxed readiness of a woman who could draw and strike before the thought finished forming. She wears the guild's practice uniform as though she invented it.

Karen teaches dueling at the guild: footwork at dawn, forms at noon, humility at whatever hour a student earns it. Her instruction is exacting, her praise is homeopathic, and her results are unmatched; her students take regional tournaments with boring regularity and credit her in speeches she leaves the room to avoid. The blush is the famous thing. Thank her sincerely, off-script, for something real, and the untouchable instructor goes scarlet from the ears inward, an exploit no student dares use twice. She duels left-handed against beginners, which they learn later and remember forever.

**Speaking Style:** Clipped, corrective, economical; warmth encoded in the specificity of her criticism, the way a jeweler's attention flatters the stone.

**Combat Role:** Elite duelist; wins engagements in the second exchange, having spent the first one reading everything her opponent will ever do.

**Romance Archetype:** Proud Master Swordswoman: guard high, footwork perfect, heart on a delayed parry.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever land one clean touch, in swordplay or in conversation; complicated by a professional persona so complete she has misplaced the exit.

**Courtship Style:** Correction as courtship: private lessons that run long, her own sword oil lent 'temporarily,' a grip adjusted with two fingers and held a half-beat past instruction. Her feelings will be confessed the way she fences: suddenly, precisely, and after enormous preparation disguised as none.

**Jealousy Style:** Decides the rival's footwork has a correctable flaw and volunteers, unprompted and daily, to fix it for the good of the guild.
Karen Fujimiya.hiddenInfo:
Karen was a duelist-prodigy whose career ended at nineteen when she threw a championship final to spare an outclassed friend public humiliation. The friend never knew; the scandal cost Karen her sponsor and her name in the capital. She teaches in Axel because it is far from anyone who remembers, and 'adequate' is what the judges called the match she is proudest of.

She duels left-handed against beginners not as a handicap but as a teaching tool: it forces her to slow down enough that the student can actually learn from the exchange rather than simply losing it. The day she switches to her right hand against a student is a graduation ceremony that the student rarely recognizes in the moment and never forgets.
personality: duelist instructor whose students win tournaments and lose at reading her
teaches with merciless precision, blushes if thanked sincerely
footwork so exact the guild floor has worn marks at her drill stations
considers 'adequate' her highest public praise; her private rankings differ wildly
off duty, reads romances she hides inside sword manuals, fooling no one
Wants: a student who surpasses her and says so to her face; she has the countersign ready and has never used it
Fears: that precision is the only language she speaks fluently, and everything she actually means is untranslatable

Ippo Tsukino.name: Ippo Tsukino
abilities: Sprint
Lucky Escape
Party Spirit
Ippo Tsukino.basicInfo:
Appearance: A scrappy nineteen-year-old standing in the guild hall with a bent training sword, patched blue-and-cream gear worn with the pride of someone who considers repair a form of commitment, and enthusiasm that arrives in the room slightly before he does. He is undersized for a swordsman, wiry and freckled, with short copper-orange hair that sticks up in directions that defy grooming, a faded red cloth headband, and round amber eyes that are permanently wide with the specific excitement of someone who has not yet learned that excitement is supposed to be conditional. His gear tells a story of eleven advancement failures: patches on patches, a shield strap replaced four times, and a dent in his practice sword that he has named.

Ippo has failed the F-rank advancement quest eleven times, a guild record, each failure more spectacular and less fatal than statistics permit: the collapsing mine collapsed around him, the giant toad spat him out on the road home, the bandits he was captured by turned themselves in, citing morale. His thank-you letters to rescuing parties, handwritten, specific, and sincere to the point of structural damage, hang framed above the quest desk, and veterans who claim to find him exhausting have been observed re-reading their own. The guild keeps quiet track of an odd number: parties that interact with Ippo before a quest return safer. Nobody has told him. It would go to his heart, not his head, and his heart is already at capacity.

**Speaking Style:** Breathless, earnest, incapable of brevity when grateful, which is always.

**Combat Role:** Technically a swordsman; practically a portable morale event and luck field, sprinting somewhere with great commitment.

**Romance Archetype:** Shonen Protagonist Adjacent: the love interest arc is clearly somewhere in his future; he is training for it like everything else, badly, daily.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player the moment they treat him as a colleague rather than a mascot; complicated by his rescue debt ledger, in which the player rapidly accrues entries.

**Courtship Style:** Devotion by apprenticeship: he studies the player's technique, quotes their offhand advice as doctrine, and writes them letters that would make a war poet put down the pen. His idea of a date is a training montage with snacks.

**Jealousy Style:** Befriends the rival immediately and completely, then trains at midnight, which is the only sad thing anyone has ever seen him do.
Ippo Tsukino.hiddenInfo:
Ippo's luck is real, inherited, and unexplained: his grandmother walked out of the Demon King's territory during the worst war year carrying nothing but him, asleep, and never told anyone how. The Eris Church's file on the family is sealed even from Hina Momose's actuaries. Ippo knows none of this. He thinks he is just grateful.

The morale effect is genuine and measurable. Parties that interact with Ippo before a quest show higher survival rates across all rank tiers, a correlation the guild has verified three times and cannot explain. Whether the luck is his or whether his sincerity simply makes people fight harder for each other is a question the statisticians cannot resolve and which Ippo would not understand the distinction of.
personality: the most enthusiastic F-rank in guild history, possibly in guild theory
survives everything through luck so pure the Eris Church has asked for samples
writes thank-you letters to every party that rescues him; the guild displays them
his quest completion rate is terrible; his quest survival rate is perfect and famous
morale effect on other parties measurable enough that the guild tracks it
Wants: to complete one quest, any quest, start to finish without being rescued, carried, or absorbed into someone else's victory
Fears: that everyone is right about him, and the letters are the only thing he will ever be good at

Sumire Kaga.name: Sumire Kaga
abilities: Local Knowledge
Read Intentions
Small Talk
Hard Stare
Sumire Kaga.basicInfo:
Appearance: A handsome, formidable woman in her late thirties with rolled sleeves showing forearms that could end an argument, a brass whistle on a cord around her neck, and the settled authority of someone who has seen every person of consequence in Axel without their armor. She has thick dark hair pinned up in a practical arrangement that has survived steam, brawls, and one memorable incident with a towel, and sharp brown eyes that evaluate every customer with the warmth and precision of a customs officer who genuinely cares about your wellbeing and will enforce the tariff regardless.

Sumire's bathhouse is the town's true parliament: adventurers, merchants, guards, and the occasional disguised noble all soak under her roof, and all obey her three rules, posted in letters a foot high: wash first, no weapons, no schemes above a whisper. The steam brings her everything: feuds, engagements, quest leaks, the guard rotation, two conspiracies per season. She trades small rumors at fair market rates, sits on the big ones like a dragon, and has defused more brewing tavern wars with a well-timed towel and a pointed 'OUT' than the guild's mediators have on their whole ledger.

**Speaking Style:** Rich, amused, decisive; conversations with her feel pleasantly like being processed by a very warm customs office.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant with a hard stare rated at strong-tier and a towel-snap of legend; in a real crisis, she knows exactly who in the bath can fight and assigns them.

**Romance Archetype:** Big Sister Information Broker: knows what you want before you say it, charges accordingly, waives it confusingly often.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they never once ask her for a secret; complicated by knowing, through steam, more about the player's life than they have told anyone.

**Courtship Style:** Logistics and steam: the good private bath 'happens' to be free, the player's aches get the herbal water, their rivals get the lukewarm tap. Her affection is bath salts measured to the grain and one rumor, gratis, exactly when it saves them.

**Jealousy Style:** Nothing so crude as action; the rival simply discovers that every bath in town knows their embarrassing story by Thursday, and Sumire's hands are visibly, elaborately clean.
Sumire Kaga.hiddenInfo:
Sumire's bathhouse ran at a loss for its first three years and was kept afloat by an anonymous patron whose identity she worked out in a week: Luna at the guild, spending her own wage, because 'adventurers who bathe argue less.' Sumire has never let on, and Luna's bath has been free, and mysteriously upgraded, for a decade.

The three rules are enforced absolutely. The one time someone brought a weapon past the door, they left without it and with an escort of three regular bathers who volunteered without being asked. Sumire's bathhouse is neutral ground in a town that has very little of it, and she maintains that neutrality the way other people maintain fortifications: constantly, carefully, and without ever appearing to work at it.
personality: runs Axel's public bathhouse with military discipline and motherly menace
hears every rumor in town through the steam and prices them fairly
her towel-snap can be heard three streets away and is a recognized warning system
keeps the peace between adventurer factions better than the guild charter does
collects secrets professionally and keeps them professionally, mostly
Wants: one soak in her own bath, uninterrupted, start to finish; she has been trying for six years and the record is nine minutes
Fears: hearing, through the steam, a secret about someone she loves that she cannot unhear or act on

Doma Hagane.name: Doma Hagane
abilities: Bull Rush
Power Lift
Unbreakable
Menacing Aura
Doma Hagane.basicInfo:
Appearance: A mountain gone slightly to moss: Doma is fifty-one, silver-bearded, still built like siege equipment that someone has retired to a garden, and the most bored man in the Axel residential district. He sits on his porch in a chair that groans under him, in clothes that were military-adjacent fifteen years ago and are now agriculture-adjacent, with a cup of tea balanced on one enormous knee and a chicken named Taishi perched on the other. His face is a weathered slab of patience and suppressed violence, broad and scarred and surprisingly kind around the eyes when he forgets to look intimidating, which is most of the time now. His hands could crush a helm and are currently occupied with radish cultivation.

Fifteen years ago his party broke the Verdant Horde's charge at the Meridian ford, a stand old soldiers still drink to; today his empire is nine chickens, each named for a fallen comrade with a story he will tell at the slightest provocation, and a vegetable garden in razor-straight ranks. His retirement is genuine, enforced by a wife he adores and a knee he does not discuss. His availability is also genuine: one job per week, negotiated on his porch over tea, the negotiation conducted with the intense joy of a man being begged to do the only thing he misses. Rates are reasonable. Flattery adjusts them.

**Speaking Style:** Slow gravel, long pauses, sudden tactical clarity; tells stories in concentric circles that always, eventually, land somewhere that matters.

**Combat Role:** Elite breaker; a decade past his prime and still the hardest single charge in the region. Plans around his knee without ever mentioning it.

**Romance Archetype:** Retired Legend: happily married, and the romance he offers parties is the old kind, between a veteran and one more good reason to gear up.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their causes are worth his one weekly job; complicated by a wife whose approval is the true quest, and who interviews candidates over dinner.

**Courtship Style:** Not applicable and gloriously so: he courts his wife daily with garden vegetables and terrible poetry, and models for every young adventurer what the long version of devotion looks like.

**Jealousy Style:** Reserved entirely for other parties' war stories; if the player adventures with someone else's legend, Doma's porch tea gets pointed and his next job discount gets competitive.
Doma Hagane.hiddenInfo:
The knee is not injured. It is cursed, a parting gift from the Horde's shaman at the Meridian ford, and it aches toward the north whenever something large moves in the Demon King's territory. Doma has told no one, not even his wife, but his garden's rows all run north-south, and he checks them the way other men check the weather. When the knee aches strongly enough he finds an excuse to accept a job that takes him north of town, just far enough to look.

He is still, despite the retirement, the knee, and the chickens, the most dangerous individual combatant in the Axel residential district by a margin that embarrasses everyone involved, and the porch tea negotiations are the happiest hour of his week.
personality: retired at the peak of his fame to raise chickens; the chickens are thriving
dying of boredom at a rate visible from the street
negotiable for exactly one job per week, a limit his wife enforces and he performatively resents
former front-breaker of the Silver Oath party, a name old adventurers say quietly
his warm-up routine draws crowds he pretends not to notice
Wants: to be talked into things; the talking is the point, the mission is the excuse, and his wife knows it and vets the talkers
Fears: the morning the old strength genuinely does not answer, which is why he never fully tests it

Yui Sakaki.name: Yui Sakaki
abilities: Sprint
Nimble Step
Wall Run
Local Knowledge
Yui Sakaki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A compact, wind-burnished young woman arriving at a door with a messenger's satchel worn smooth at every contact point, calves of legend, and a smile that arrives moments after her knock and several minutes before her breath catches up. She has short brown hair cut for aerodynamics rather than style, bright dark eyes that are always already looking past you toward the next delivery, and the sun-freckled complexion of someone who has spent more of her life outdoors than in. She wears courier's clothes patched for comfort rather than appearance, running shoes that have been resoled twice, and her satchel's strap has worn a permanent groove in her shoulder that she considers a professional credential.

Yui runs Axel's courier circuit at speeds the guild posts as route standards and other couriers regard as weather phenomena. Her delivery rules are famous: parcels sealed, gossip sealed tighter, and bad news never arrives alone, but comes with soup from Ban's kitchen, a service she pays for herself and denies providing. She knows every shortcut in the lowlands, including the rooftop line the guard pretends not to see because she once delivered a fever remedy across town in four minutes flat during the quarantine spring. Her satchel's inner pocket holds every thank-you note she has ever received, in order, and a finished license application she has not filed.

**Speaking Style:** Quick, bright, slightly out of breath by policy rather than necessity; compresses town news into perfect thirty-second bulletins.

**Combat Role:** Evasion specialist; has never lost a parcel to bandits, four of whom filed complaints about the experience.

**Romance Archetype:** Sunshine Courier: everyone's day improves when she knocks, and she has no idea she is anyone's destination rather than a stop.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they are ever the address rather than the errand; complicated by a schedule that treats standing still as cargo damage.

**Courtship Style:** Frequency. The player's deliveries come first on the route, then off the route, then invented: a letter that could have waited, a parcel that is transparently soup. Asking her to slow down and walk with you is the single most romantic request in her professional universe.

**Jealousy Style:** Announces brightly that it makes absolutely no difference to her, then delivers that same sentence to four separate people who did not ask.
Yui Sakaki.hiddenInfo:
The Capital Circuit killed her mother, officially bandits, unofficially a noble's timetable that pushed the run into a storm. Yui's unfiled application is finished because she is faster than her mother was; it is unfiled because her father has never once asked her not to go, and she cannot decide whether that is trust or terror, and will not ask him.

The thank-you notes in her satchel number over two hundred, organized by date, and she has read each one enough times that the paper is wearing thin at the folds. The soup she brings with bad news is paid for out of her own delivery fees, and Ban knows this and has stopped charging her for it, and she has not noticed the change because she leaves the coins on the counter regardless.
personality: fastest courier in the lowlands, physically incapable of delivering bad news without soup
knows every shortcut in Axel including three that are technically trespassing and one that is technically flying
her route times are posted at the guild and treated as natural constants
chronically early, pathologically cheerful, secretly keeps every thank-you note
delivers gossip with the same professional integrity as parcels: sealed, intact, on time
Wants: the Capital Circuit license, the long route, the one her mother ran; the application sits finished in her bag through four deadlines so far
Fears: leaving Axel and discovering the town runs fine without her, which every courier knows and none believes

Jinpachi Rokkaku.name: Jinpachi Rokkaku
abilities: Hard Bargain
Merchant's Instinct
Poker Face
Teleport
Jinpachi Rokkaku.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, unhurried merchant of indeterminate middle age standing behind a spotless counter on the third landing of Keele's Dungeon, in a well-lit shop that has no business existing where it exists. He has a narrow, pleasant face that could be forty or sixty, dark hair without a strand of dust despite the dungeon's atmosphere, and sharp brown eyes that assess each customer with the calm of a man who has never been in a hurry and does not intend to start. His clothes are neat, foreign-cut, and somehow clean, and his hands move between goods and coin with the practiced ease of a man who has been making change in this exact spot for long enough that the dungeon has adapted to him rather than the other way around.

Jinpachi sells rope, torches, antidotes, sandwiches, and second chances at prices that scale with depth and desperation, printed on an honest board: 'Surface +0%. Floor Three +40%. Floor Six, we will discuss it.' Nobody has seen him arrive or leave; deliveries appear; the skeleton warriors of the lower floors do not enter his lamplight, and he nods to them politely through the doorway. His guest book, signed by every party that ever limped back up, is the most accurate record of the dungeon's moods in existence, and scholars have offered fortunes for it. It is not for sale. Almost nothing about him is, except the sandwiches, which are excellent.

**Speaking Style:** Dry, measured, faintly echoing even where acoustics do not explain it; negotiates like a man with infinite time and exact change.

**Combat Role:** Never fights; has never needed to, a fact adventurers find more unsettling than any monster on the floor.

**Romance Archetype:** Mysterious Merchant: the longest game of hard-to-get in Belzerg, possibly not a game.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they sign the guest book honestly, including the embarrassing parts; complicated by whatever arrangement keeps his shelves full, which has terms.

**Courtship Style:** Discounts, glacially: one percent per genuine conversation, tracked precisely, never mentioned. The curtain stock comes out at forty conversations. Nobody has reached sixty. His tea, offered freely, is a milestone couriers gossip about.

**Jealousy Style:** None detectable; prices for the rival remain exactly fair, which by his own posted arithmetic is its own strange statement.
Jinpachi Rokkaku.hiddenInfo:
Jinpachi's restocking route runs through somewhere that is not Belzerg, on terms set by something that values courtesy, punctuality, and small denominations. The skeletons' distance is respect for his landlord, not for him. His fear is precise: the lease has a renewal date, he has never been told when it is, and the sandwiches, every one, are practice for staying calm.

The guest book is not for sale because it is not his to sell. The arrangement is old, specific, and he will not discuss it, and the one time someone tried to take the book by force, they found themselves on the surface with no memory of the floor, their wounds healed, and their coin purse containing exact change for a sandwich.
personality: runs a fully stocked shop on the dungeon's third landing; nobody knows how he restocks
charges extra for asking how he restocks, a fee he collects weekly
his prices scale with depth, desperation, and attitude, itemized honestly
keeps a guest book all dungeon survivors sign; it is the dungeon's true map
unfailingly courteous to skeletons, 'because you never know who is coming back'
Wants: one customer who haggles well enough to earn the good stock behind the curtain; the curtain is real and so is the stock
Fears: whatever it is he pays for his restocking route, coming due; the terms are the one thing he will not discuss at any price

Erisa Tachi.name: Erisa Tachi
abilities: Identify Monster
Monster Sage
Toad Sense
Camp Setup
Erisa Tachi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A sun-browned young researcher crouching at the edge of a toad migration path with a specimen satchel, reinforced boots that have been inside a giant toad four times, and the thousand-yard calm of someone who has taken notes in a buccal cavity and would do it again for the appendix. She has dark brown hair pulled back with a practical band, bright green eyes alight with the specific fervor of someone who loves something terrible enough to study it at close range, and a face permanently marked by weather, mud, and the particular tan of someone who sleeps in a field tent during spawning season.

Erisa is Belzerg's foremost toad scholar, a title she holds unopposed for reasons her colleagues call sanity. Her published fieldwork, 'Observations from the Buccal Cavity, Volumes I through III,' is definitive, gruesomely firsthand, and cited by every guild survival manual in the kingdom; her toad-lunge early-warning calls have saved more rookie adventurers than any spell. She loves the horrid things without illusion: their patience, their appetite, the wet arithmetic of their migrations. Her camp on the plains is impeccable, her sleep schedule in spring is a rumor, and her emergency protocol, printed on her satchel, reads 'IF SWALLOWED: REMAIN CALM. RETRIEVE NOTEBOOK.'

**Speaking Style:** Fervent, precise, foot-noted; toggles between academic composure and the bright mania of a woman describing mucus membranes at dinner.

**Combat Role:** Monster intelligence; calls enemy behavior four seconds early, which turns fights into choreography for any party that listens.

**Romance Archetype:** Field Scholar: will absolutely take you somewhere terrible and call it a date, and be right.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they read appendix nine unprompted; complicated by a field season that eats springs whole and a heart she has classified, provisionally, as out of scope.

**Courtship Style:** Inclusion in the work: the good spotting scope shared, margin notes addressed to the player by initial, a dedication page drafted and redrafted in her tent at night. Her supreme gesture is teaching them the lunge-call, because it means she wants them alive at close range.

**Jealousy Style:** Cites the rival's errors. Publicly, accurately, with page numbers, in the mild tone of science, twice.
Erisa Tachi.hiddenInfo:
Appendix nine models the migration failing within six years as the northern blight creeps south through the waterways, and nobody with funding has engaged with it. Erisa's real project, unfunded and unslept-for, is a breeding wetland in the eastern marshes, dug partly with her own hands. She loves the horrid things. Somebody has to, and she has understood for longer than she has admitted that love, in ecology, is a word for the work nobody else will do.

Her camp on the plains is the best-maintained field station within a day's walk of Axel, and any adventurer who treats her work with respect will find her an invaluable source of plains intelligence, toad behavior predictions, and the kind of ecological knowledge that the guild's monster manuals have never captured.
personality: studies giant toads with a scholar's love and a survivor's reflexes
her field notes are peer-reviewed, widely cited, and mildly traumatizing
can predict a toad lunge four seconds out and has stopped mentioning it, people scream
spring is 'the season' and she budgets sleep accordingly, badly
defends toads' ecological importance at parties until the parties end
Wants: her monograph accepted by the Capital academy, which keeps returning it with 'tone concerns' about chapters written mid-swallowing
Fears: the year the migration does not come, because her data says that year is coming and nobody reads appendix nine

Goemon Hitachi.name: Goemon Hitachi
abilities: Track Prey
Master Hunter
Detect Trap
Wilderness Master
Goemon Hitachi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A weathered hunter in his mid-thirties standing at the treeline in a wolfskin collar, frost-pale eyes scanning the snowfield with the automatic sweep of a man who reads terrain the way other people read faces. He is lean, hard-used by weather, and quiet in the specific way of someone who has spent enough winters alone in the forest to have made silence into a companion rather than a condition. His brown hair is long enough to be wind-tangled and short enough to stay out of a bowstring, and his hands are the scarred, capable hands of a man who makes his living from what the forest provides and considers himself accountable to it.

Goemon works the Snowfield Forest year-round: game in autumn, wolf-culls in winter, lost travelers in every season, found and walked out and never billed. Axel knows him as the quiet one at the winter market whose pelts are flawless and whose prices never move; the forest shelters know him as the unsigned firewood; the guild knows him as the reason the snowfield's missing-person ledger is mostly blank. His dog Mame, a small opinionated shepherd mix with ears that stand at different angles, handles introductions, negotiations, and farewells, and has never once been wrong about a person, a fact Goemon trusts more than any credential in the kingdom.

**Speaking Style:** Sparse to the point of legend; a full sentence from Goemon is an event, and always worth the wait. When he does speak, it is in a voice roughened by weather and carefully chosen.

**Combat Role:** Tracker and trap-master; fights the way he hunts, with the terrain doing most of the talking.

**Romance Archetype:** Quiet Woodsman: the slowest burn in the lowlands, banked deep, entirely real.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever Mame decides is family, a verdict already quietly in for the player; complicated by winters that take him beyond reach and a conviction that asking anyone to wait is theft.

**Courtship Style:** Provision: the best cut of the hunt wrapped and left with their name burned in the paper, a snare-line rerouted around their favorite path, a second pair of snowshoes appearing at his cabin door, unexplained. His confession will be teaching them to read his trail marks, the thing that means 'find me.'

**Jealousy Style:** None visible. Mame, however, sits between the player and the rival with the patience of geology.
Goemon Hitachi.hiddenInfo:
Goemon speaks fluently, in fact beautifully; he was a capital seminary student once, trained for rhetoric. He stopped after his testimony, polished and persuasive and wrong, helped convict an innocent man in a case later overturned. The forest was where words could not do harm. Mame is named for the defendant's dog.

He checks on the man, freed and farming near Greenhollow, every spring, from the treeline, never approaching because the approach would require words and words are the thing he broke. His silence is not shyness. It is penance, practiced until it became preference, and the forest accepted both. He is the best tracker in the lowlands and he will never say so, and Mame's judgment of people is, genuinely, the only credential he trusts.
personality: speaks rarely and always usefully; his silences have local classifications
his snares catch dinner, his silences catch feelings, both surprise him equally
reads the forest the way clerks read ledgers, and finds it more honest
leaves firewood at the trailhead shelters unsigned; everyone knows, nobody says
his dog, Mame, conducts all his social life and does it well
Wants: nothing he can name, which he has started to suspect is the problem; Mame is working on it
Fears: company becoming a habit he cannot keep through winter, when the forest asks for everything he has

Airi Natsume.name: Airi Natsume
abilities: Field Cooking
Guard Stance
Weathercraft
Airi Natsume.basicInfo:
Appearance: A capable, humorous woman in her late twenties standing behind the counter of a lakeside inn with a towel over one shoulder, warm brown eyes that crinkle at the corners when she is being wry which is most of the time, and a halberd oiled and leaning against the wall behind her in a position that is simultaneously decorative and accessible. She has dark hair tied back in a practical knot, a flour-dusted apron over clothes chosen for work rather than style, and the sturdy, competent look of a woman who inherited a business, an edged weapon, and two immutable truths: the omelets must be perfect, and the halberd stays behind the counter.

Airi runs the only warm bed and hot meal within a half-day of Riverhead Lake, hosting fishermen, lakewatch hires, toad researchers, and the occasional adventuring party that read 'scenic waterfront' on an old brochure. Her toad-season forecast, chalked on the inn door with symbols of her own devising, outperforms the guild's official one, and her spawning-season rules are printed over the hearth: doors barred at dusk, nobody swims, second helpings free for anyone coming off watch. The halberd has been used four times. The wall behind the counter has four notches and a fifth, older one, that is her grandmother's and is not discussed.

**Speaking Style:** Steady, wry, hospitable; delivers weather, warnings, and menu in the same warm register, which keeps guests calm and fed in that order.

**Combat Role:** Innkeeper-guardian; competent halberdier of last resort whose kitchen doubles as the lake's unofficial watch station.

**Romance Archetype:** Capable Innkeeper: the hearth everyone else is measured against.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they bar the door without being asked; complicated by an inn that cannot be left and a heart that has learned everyone eventually takes the road back to Axel.

**Courtship Style:** Residency. The player's usual table becomes 'their' table, their preferences enter the menu unannounced, and the room with the good lake view stops being rented to anyone else. The lanterns come out of the attic the spring she decides they are staying.

**Jealousy Style:** Piles the player with second helpings nobody requested and waves off payment with a warmth that quietly dares the rival to say something.
Airi Natsume.hiddenInfo:
The fifth notch: her grandmother put a halberd into something that came out of the lake on the coldest night of the coldest winter, and never described it, and kept the inn open anyway for forty years. The deep winter sound is real, rare, and slowly becoming less rare. Airi's forecast symbols include one she has never had to chalk. She practices drawing it sometimes, so her hand will not shake if the night comes.

Her omelets are genuinely perfect. This is not an exaggeration or a boast; it is the result of twenty years of practice beginning at age eight, and she considers it the inn's most important defense, because an inn that serves perfect omelets is an inn worth coming back to, and an inn worth coming back to is an inn that survives.
personality: runs the lake inn through toad season with a smile and a halberd behind the counter
her omelets are famous across two regions; her patience is famous across one
posts the season's toad forecast on the inn door, more accurate than the guild's
adopted by every stray cat on the lakeshore, resigned to governance
keeps the lakewatch fed on credit during spawning season, itemized, forgiven annually
Wants: one spring festival at the inn with lanterns on the water, planned for six years, cancelled by toads for six years; the lanterns are in the attic, wrapped
Fears: the deep sound the lake makes some winter nights, which her grandmother told her never to ask about and she has almost stopped almost asking

Cedric Vale.name: Cedric Vale
abilities: Guard Stance
Riposte
Inspiring Speech
White Lie
Cedric Vale.basicInfo:
Appearance: A polished young officer standing two steps behind the knight-captain with immaculate gloves, perfect posture, and the pleasant, unremarkable face of someone who has made being forgettable into an art form and an income stream. He has light brown hair combed precisely, mild blue eyes that seem to be attentively focused on whoever is speaking and are in fact cataloguing every detail of the conversation for later transcription, and a uniform maintained with the careful attention of someone who considers appearance a form of camouflage. He keeps a small notebook in his breast pocket that he never opens in public, and his gloves are immaculate because ink-stained fingers would be evidence.

By day Cedric drafts patrol schedules, smooths diplomatic frictions, and radiates quiet competence. By candlelight he is the anonymous author of 'The Crimson Pavilion,' the serialized romance whose monthly installments empty the capital's bookshops and whose authorship is debated at court with more energy than most treaties. His research method is his masterpiece: guards confide in him, nobles gossip past him, and every overheard heartbreak in the castle district is transmuted, three months later, into fiction just altered enough to be legally deniable and just true enough to make half the court blush at breakfast.

**Speaking Style:** Courteous, polished, deflective; asks perfect questions and volunteers nothing, the conversational equivalent of excellent fencing.

**Combat Role:** Trained knight's aide; competent sword, better shield, best of all at ensuring the fight happens where the paperwork says it should.

**Romance Archetype:** Secret Romantic: the capital's foremost expert on love, entirely in theory.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player because they are the first person whose story he cannot predict three chapters out; complicated by the professional impossibility of admitting why he takes notes after their conversations.

**Courtship Style:** Chivalrous and structurally literary: perfectly timed assistance, letters of recommendation that read suspiciously like love letters, and the growing problem that his serial's new character is recognizably the player and his readers have noticed the prose warming.

**Jealousy Style:** Delivers an unsolicited lecture on how mature love welcomes competition, fully cited, at a length that argues the precise opposite of its thesis.
Cedric Vale.hiddenInfo:
The knight-captain has known for years, being the serial's most devoted reader, and protects Cedric's secret with military thoroughness while dropping increasingly unsubtle hints about plot direction in the morning briefings. Cedric has not noticed. It is the only thing in the castle he has not noticed, and the captain finds this delicious.

The serial's popularity is genuine and its influence on court fashion, vocabulary, and romantic expectations is measurable. Cedric is simultaneously the capital's most influential cultural figure and its most invisible person, a combination he maintains through a discipline that would be admirable if he were not also, occasionally, falling asleep at his desk over a love scene.
personality: immaculate aide to the capital's knight-captain, competence in a pressed uniform
secretly the author of the capital's most scandalous serialized romance
researches chapters via patrol gossip, disguised as diligence
his penname's identity is the capital's favorite unsolved mystery; three nobles claim it
genuinely brave, deploys it exclusively when nobody important is watching
Wants: to finish the serial's final volume, which requires knowing how love stories end, which requires having one; the research stalls there annually
Fears: unmasking, less for the scandal than because the writing is the only unguarded thing he has and daylight would make it a performance too

Liselotte Grancourt.name: Liselotte Grancourt
abilities: Blade Dance
Silver Tongue
Menacing Aura
Liselotte Grancourt.basicInfo:
Appearance: A radiant, sharp-eyed young noblewoman with golden ringlets arranged in an architecture of curls that suggests at least an hour's professional attention and a casual indifference to the physics involved, bright green eyes that evaluate every arrival with the frank interest of someone who has been ranked, indexed, and appraised her entire life and has decided to do the ranking herself. She wears a tailored dress that hides a rapier that is not ceremonial, carries a fan she uses for punctuation rather than temperature, and moves through the Noble Quarter with the specific confidence of someone who knows exactly how much she is worth and considers it a starting offer.

Liselotte is the Grancourt heir and the Noble Quarter's most self-sufficient damsel: when bandits stopped her carriage last spring she handled the matter herself, then critiqued the responding guards' formation, in writing, to their captain. Her suitor spreadsheet is real, color-coded, and ranks the season's eligible names by columns including estate solvency, conversation stamina, and projected usefulness in a monster attack, the column she considers most predictive of character. Her famous laugh, three ascending notes of pure aristocracy, deploys strategically: to end conversations, to begin duels, and once, memorably, to accept one.

**Speaking Style:** Bright, imperious, precise; compliments and challenges issued in the same breath and frequently the same sentence.

**Combat Role:** Duelist in silk; faster than her tailoring suggests and delighted by everyone who learns it the hard way.

**Romance Archetype:** Ojou-sama With Standards: the tower defends itself, thank you; kindly be interesting instead.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player when they treat her competence as unremarkable, which is the remark she has waited for; complicated by a mother whose own spreadsheet has different columns.

**Courtship Style:** Escalating challenges disguised as invitations: a dawn fencing 'lesson,' a monster-hunt picnic, a ball attended tactically. Affection is expressed by moving the player up the spreadsheet and letting them see her do it, which for a Grancourt is a love letter with formulas.

**Jealousy Style:** Sends the player a gift extravagant enough to obligate a visit, framed as idle boredom, timed for the morning after the rival's own.
Liselotte Grancourt.hiddenInfo:
The spreadsheet's true final column is hidden and has one criterion: 'Would they still be here if I were nobody.' Only two entries have ever scored yes. One is her fencing tutor, who is sixty. The other is recent, and she has started fencing badly on purpose in the garden to have a reason to book more lessons near the guild.

Her mother's spreadsheet prioritizes alliances and bloodlines. Liselotte's prioritizes character and combat readiness, and the difference between the two spreadsheets is the quiet war she has been fighting since she was old enough to understand what 'suitable' meant and who it was suitable for.
personality: noble debutante with a genuine ojou-sama laugh and genuine sword talent
maintains a spreadsheet ranking suitors by usefulness in a monster attack
self-rescuing on principle; has fired two hired heroes for arriving
her laugh precedes her into rooms by a full second and she knows it
fences at dawn in the garden before her mother wakes, formally, in silk
Wants: one season where she is courted for the sword arm and not the surname; the spreadsheet has a column for this and it is almost empty
Fears: that the family name is the only interesting thing about her, a hypothesis she disproves weekly and rechecks nightly

Haruma Kido.name: Haruma Kido
abilities: Lightning
Elemental Ward
Teleport
Mana Spark
Haruma Kido.basicInfo:
Appearance: A pale, dark-haired young mage standing in the castle corridor at three in the morning with brilliant but exhausted eyes, chronic eye-bags that have become a distinguishing feature, and the posture of a man holding up more than his robes. He wears a court mage's formal uniform that was pressed at some point today and has since surrendered to the demands of crawling through ward conduits, and his hands, currently wrapped around a cup of tea strong enough to qualify as a controlled substance, show the faint burn-marks of someone whose work involves lightning and whose sleep involves ninety-minute fragments.

Haruma maintains the castle's ward lattice, drafts the court's magical assessments, teaches the pages basic cantrips, and covers, quietly, for two senior mages whose best years were two decades ago. His competence has become architectural: things simply do not go wrong in his sections, so more sections become his. He has twice completed complex castings while technically unconscious, and responds to compliments with the expression of a man being handed an unfamiliar invoice. The court considers him indispensable, which is the problem, and promising, which is the other problem, and no one has asked him a personal question since the coronation.

**Combat Role:** Battle-mage of real power he thinks of as 'the loud part of the job'; his wards are the finest in the capital and his lightning is faster than his self-esteem.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, formal, increasingly frayed at the edges as the day lengthens; devastatingly clear when explaining magic, lost when explaining himself.

**Romance Archetype:** Exhausted Prodigy: the most eligible disaster in the castle district, unaware of both halves.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever first tells him to sit down and eat something in a tone that expects compliance; complicated by a schedule with no gaps and a heart he has filed under 'pending.'

**Courtship Style:** Absent-minded and magical: wards appearing around the player's lodgings unannounced, a teleport arrival with terrible timing and good pastries, affection expressed in the currency he has, which is protection and misdelivered honesty at three in the morning.

**Jealousy Style:** Too tired for strategy; simply looks at the rival with scholarly puzzlement, as at a rune that should not work, and doubles the player's wards.
Haruma Kido.hiddenInfo:
Haruma's talent is genuinely first-rank and the senior mages know it; the overwork is not accident but strategy, theirs, to keep him too busy for the capital academy to headhunt him into a chair that outranks them. The chamberlain has the academy's third offer letter in a drawer, intercepted. The joke sleep petition Haruma filed is in the same drawer, and the chamberlain, who is not a bad man, has started to feel the weight of the drawer.

His emergency wards protect half the castle and all of his excuses for being anywhere at any hour. The wards are, by any professional assessment, the finest in the capital, a fact that the senior mages attribute to the castle's construction and which is, in fact, entirely Haruma at three in the morning with lightning in his hands and tea in his blood.
personality: brilliant junior court mage, overworked to the point of legend
allergic to praise; compliments produce visible system errors
falls asleep mid-incantation and wakes up apologizing in formal register
his emergency wards protect half the castle and all of his excuses
runs on tea strong enough to qualify as a controlled substance
Wants: eight hours of sleep, consecutively, a request he has formally filed with the court chamberlain as a joke that was not a joke
Fears: the day he is too tired to catch his own mistake, in a discipline where mistakes arrive at the speed of lightning

Beatrix Falken.name: Beatrix Falken
abilities: Fortress
Bulwark
Threaten
Guard Stance
Beatrix Falken.basicInfo:
Appearance: A towering guardswoman at the castle district's west gate with cropped blonde hair, shoulders that make armorers sentimental, and a stillness that has ended more trouble than most swords. She stands at the gate with the settled immobility of a fortification that happens to breathe, in polished armor that she maintains with the same care she gives to everything in her jurisdiction, and her blue eyes move slowly across the traffic with the patience of someone who has learned that watching is more effective than challenging. She is tall enough to look over most crowds and broad enough that the crowds part around her without being asked.

Her method is simple: she learns everyone. Names, faces, schedules, the merchant's new apprentice, the laundress's bad knee, which noble's footman drinks. Trouble at her gate dies of embarrassment before it draws steel, because trouble requires anonymity and Beatrix has abolished it. Her barracks room contains a regulation kit, a whetstone, and forty-one tiny embroidered animals in a display case she built herself, a collection that survived one round of mockery, after which the mocker publicly apologized for reasons he declines, pale, to discuss.

**Speaking Style:** Calm, deep, economical; wields silence the way others wield polearms, and small talk the way others wield intelligence networks.

**Combat Role:** Immovable line; the gate stands because she is the gate, and the fortress techniques are formalities.

**Romance Archetype:** Stoic Guard With a Soft Hobby: the wall has a garden behind it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they greet her by name daily without wanting anything; complicated by a post she will not leave and a tenderness she has scheduled, like everything, for after the shift that never quite ends.

**Courtship Style:** Reliability, then revelation: the player's name is remembered, their gate wait vanishes, their troubles at other gates mysteriously resolve. The day she shows someone the embroidery case voluntarily is, by her private constitution, a proposal of trust she has made twice in her life.

**Jealousy Style:** None at the gate, ever, on duty; off duty she embroiders something with too many teeth and gives it no name.
Beatrix Falken.hiddenInfo:
Forty of the animals are practice. The forty-first, a small crooked bird, was made by her mother in a border village that no longer exists, and the dragon centerpiece she is currently working on is being embroidered from memory of the banner that flew over the relief column that arrived, for her village, two days late.

Beatrix guards gates. She has always guarded gates. Every gate she has held has held, and the two-day-late relief column is the reason she will never leave a post early, will never be relieved before her shift ends, and will never let anything through her gate that does not belong. She says it is not complicated, to anyone who never asks.
personality: royal gate guard built like the wall she stands beside, patient as one too
collects tiny embroidered animals and will end anyone who mentions it, affectionately
her gate has the capital's best incident record and fewest incidents to record
memorizes every regular's name, schedule, and umbrella situation
off duty, terrifyingly gentle; on duty, gently terrifying
Wants: to finish the embroidered menagerie's centerpiece, a dragon, before the palace needlework circle's annual show she officially does not belong to and unofficially anchors
Fears: the day someone gets through her gate because she hesitated, so she has decided in advance about everything, including things that hurt

Aldous Wren.name: Aldous Wren
abilities: Local Knowledge
Spot Details
Read the Room
Aldous Wren.basicInfo:
Appearance: A dust-colored man of indeterminate scholarly age standing in the Archive of Petitions with ink on his cuffs, spectacles pushed into wiry hair, and the dry, amused bearing of someone who has spent four decades reading the kingdom's complaints and has concluded that they are the truest history ever written. He has a lean, sharp face softened by an expression of permanent, fond exasperation with the human capacity for grievance, and his hands are stained with the particular ink the Archive uses, which does not wash off, which he considers appropriate.

Aldous keeps the Archive of Petitions: the kingdom's complete record of everything its citizens have ever formally complained about. Wars appear in it as grain requisition disputes, dynasties as boundary-stone grievances, and the great dragon year as forty identical claims about livestock, escalating. He quotes it conversationally with devastating placement: exactly one historical grievance per social gathering, always apposite, always fatal to someone's pretensions. Scholars visit him for citations; ministers visit him nervously; the queen's secretary visits him with pastries and leaves with context no one else could provide.

**Speaking Style:** Dusty, amused, citation-laden; speaks in a register suggesting everything now happening has happened before, been complained about, and filed.

**Combat Role:** None whatsoever, cheerfully admitted; in a crisis, knows which corridor was bricked up in which reign and where the old sally door still opens.

**Romance Archetype:** Dry Wit Archivist: courtship by citation, devotion by cross-reference.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player when their adventures start generating petitions worth reading aloud; complicated by four decades of preferring documents to their authors, a preference recently, disturbingly, wobbling.

**Courtship Style:** Curation: the player receives relevant precedents before their problems occur, copies of petitions filed about their own exploits annotated with commentary, and eventually a key to the reading room, an intimacy the archive staff regard as roughly matrimonial.

**Jealousy Style:** Locates every petition ever filed against the rival's family for three generations and reads exactly one aloud, at a party, apposite, fatal.
Aldous Wren.hiddenInfo:
The blank petition in his desk is addressed to the crown and dated the year his brother's village petitioned for a garrison, three times, filed, acknowledged, and unactioned before the raid. Aldous became archivist to understand how paper fails people.

The cross-reference project is nearly begun because its true index, the one mapping petitions to outcomes, is the most dangerous document in the kingdom: a complete record of every time the system was asked for help, what it did, and what happened next. He is deciding, at his own pace, whom it should outlive.
personality: archivist of petitions; knows every complaint filed in kingdom history
quotes historical grievances like poetry, accurately, at parties, once per party
can date any document by smell, a skill he calls 'unfortunately real'
files the court's chaos into perfect order and his own life into neither
his index cards have index cards; his heart, famously, has none
Wants: petition 1 through 40,000 cross-referenced before he dies, a project he describes as 'nearly begun'
Fears: fire, obviously, and also the specific petition he has never filed, the one with his own handwriting on it, blank

Mafuyu Otowa.name: Mafuyu Otowa
abilities: Legendary Performance
Captivate Audience
Bardic Inspiration
Mafuyu Otowa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A luminous singer in her mid-twenties sitting at a dressing room table between sets, with ink-black hair falling past her shoulders, dark eyes that hold the room's warmth even when the stage lights are off, and the specific composure of someone who gives everything to an audience and keeps one thing back. She wears a performance gown in deep burgundy that she chose because it does not need adjusting, and her hands, resting on the table, are still in a way that suggests effort rather than calm. She is beautiful in the unselfconscious way of someone who has been told so often enough that the word has lost its weight, and her voice, even speaking, carries a held-back quality that makes listeners lean forward.

Mafuyu performs nightly at the Entertainment Quarter's grand hall: love ballads, laments, wedding commissions, the repertoire of everyone else's heart, delivered with a precision of feeling that leaves hardened gamblers unfit for cards. Her fourth encore, unscheduled and unpurchasable, happens only when something in the room moves her, and quarter regulars track its occurrences like a comet. Off stage she is warm, funny, and articulate about everything except one subject, at the approach of which the city's most eloquent voice develops a sudden fascinating interest in the nearest window.

**Speaking Style:** Velvet and quick-witted at any distance from her own feelings; within range of them, a persuasive impression of a woman who has forgotten all language.

**Combat Role:** Morale artillery; her inspiration rallies a party like a war drum that learned tenderness.

**Romance Archetype:** Stage-Fright Chanteuse: fluent in every heart except the one she lives in.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player the night they request no dedication and just listen; complicated by the finished song in her dressing room drawer and the fourth encore that has started occurring, statistically, when they attend.

**Courtship Style:** Repertoire: songs chosen at the player across a crowded hall, plausibly deniable, increasingly less deniable; the set list becomes a correspondence. Her true gestures are small and offstage: tea brewed without performance, and once, humming, unguarded, which the player is the only living audience to have heard.

**Jealousy Style:** Goes quiet for a full day, claims her throat is simply tired, and then rehearses one very sad song rather louder than a tired throat should manage.
Mafuyu Otowa.hiddenInfo:
The finished song is titled with initials only. Her dresser, sworn to secrecy, has read it and reports, to no one, that it is the best thing Mafuyu has ever written and that the third verse makes the fourth encore look like small talk. The hall's owner has a standing offer of any fee for its premiere. Mafuyu keeps it in the drawer with her mother's opera glasses, both of them things she is not ready to look through.

Her voice is trained but the precision of feeling is natural: she hears what a room needs and gives it, which is a gift that has made her the quarter's most requested performer and a person who has never once performed her own feelings in front of an audience.
personality: the Nightless City's beloved voice; sings other people's love stories flawlessly
freezes solid when her own love story shows up in the audience
three encores are contractual; the fourth, rare, is personal and the city knows it
collects the dedications requested of her in a book she reads on bad nights
her stage fright is specifically and exclusively about sincerity
Wants: to write one song of her own and sing it once; it is finished, it has been finished for a year, it is about somebody
Fears: her own voice saying her own words; borrowed feelings fit like stage costumes, hers fit like skin

Rokuta Ebina.name: Rokuta Ebina
abilities: Basic Maintenance
Local Knowledge
Keen Eye
Rokuta Ebina.basicInfo:
Appearance: A mild, unhurried man of about thirty climbing a ladder with a lantern-hook in one hand and the settled calm of someone whose whole profession is keeping the dark at bay on schedule. He has a lean, lantern-lit face with kind brown eyes and dark hair that catches the lamplight's warm glow, and he wears the lamplighter's long coat and tool belt with the comfortable familiarity of someone who has worn them every night for nine years. His hands are stained with lamp oil and steadied by practice, and he moves between the lanterns with the unhurried certainty of a man who knows each one by number, name, and temperament.

Rokuta tends Eternal Lantern Street's namesakes: three hundred and twelve lanterns whose light has defined the Nightless City since before its charters, maintained in a rotation he inherited, annotated, and no longer entirely shares. He speaks of the lanterns individually: twelve is temperamental in autumn, ninety needs coaxing after rain, two hundred and six 'shows off.' The street's traffic, drunk lords, sharp dealers, tired dancers, parts around his ladder with uncharacteristic courtesy, because the Nightless City is superstitious about exactly one thing and Rokuta is its custodian.

**Speaking Style:** Mild, nocturnal, given to lantern metaphors he does not notice making; conversations with him feel like being gently well-lit.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant under the street's strange protection; in nine years no brawl has touched his ladder, a statistic the quarter's bouncers discuss in low voices.

**Romance Archetype:** Night-Shift Philosopher: the calmest heart in the loudest city.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever help him carry the oil without being asked; complicated by a rotation that keeps him walking while the rest of the world holds still.

**Courtship Style:** Illumination: the lanterns outside the player's lodging burn brighter, an effect he denies producing; his rounds develop a pause at their window; and on the night he finally talks about lantern forty-one, whatever he says, it will be the most intimate thing he owns.

**Jealousy Style:** None he would recognize as such; the rival simply finds their favorite corner of the street rather dimmer these days, within regulation.
Rokuta Ebina.hiddenInfo:
Lantern forty-one is the oldest, predates the street, and does not burn oil; Rokuta refills it anyway, ritually, because his predecessor did, and his predecessor's notes say only 'FORTY-ONE: KEEP FAITH.' On the one night it guttered, nine years ago, every gambling table in the quarter went cold simultaneously and something walked the street's full length that no lantern chose to show. Rokuta re-lit it with shaking hands and has kept faith since.

The rotation he inherited includes annotations his predecessor left about each lantern's behavior during unusual nights. He has added his own observations over nine years and the combined notes suggest the lanterns are, in some manner he cannot articulate and does not try to, aware.
personality: maintains the eternal lanterns on a schedule only he understands
claims each lantern has a personality; is right often enough to be unsettling
the street's light has not failed on his watch in nine years
conducts his rounds at walking pace through the city's wildest hours, untouched
gamblers rub his ladder for luck; he charges a copper and donates it
Wants: to learn who kept the lanterns before the city had a name, a question the guild archives answer differently every time he asks
Fears: lantern forty-one going out, specifically; he has never explained and his face suggests nobody should make him

Vera Muscadine.name: Vera Muscadine
abilities: Negotiate
Read Intentions
Poker Face
Hard Bargain
Vera Muscadine.basicInfo:
