Appearance: A brisk, bright-eyed woman in her early thirties standing on the Twin Toll Bridges with a toll-keeper's coat worn open, a precedent book chained to her belt like a sword, and the charming, procedural confidence of someone who resolves twenty disputes a day and enjoys every single one. She has sharp features, warm hazel eyes, and an expressive face that cycles between judicial gravity and barely suppressed delight in the absurdity of bridge traffic, sometimes in the same sentence. Her precedent book is heavy, well-thumbed, and she draws it with the practiced ease of a swordsman.

Vera arbitrates the Twin Toll Bridges' daily collisions of commerce, nobility, livestock, and pride: who backs up, who pays for the spilled cabbages, whether a duke's carriage outranks a midwife's cart (her ruling, now regional precedent: it does not). Her solutions are famously, surgically fair, calibrated so both parties leave equally slightly annoyed, which she considers the only honest proof of balance. Her long war with Chancellor, a goat of tactical genius who covets the east bridge, is Millbridge's favorite serial drama and has twice drawn betting interest from Elroad.

**Speaking Style:** Brisk, charming, procedurally flirtatious; frames everything as a negotiation and most negotiations as more fun than people expected.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant who has talked down armed toll-jumpers with a raised eyebrow and a citation; in a real fight, directs traffic, which on a bridge is command of the battlefield.

**Romance Archetype:** Arbiter Flirt: the fairest deal on the river, still negotiating her own terms.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever concede a point they were winning just because she was right; complicated by professional neutrality on a bridge where everyone, eventually, is a party to something.

**Courtship Style:** Precedent: the player's crossings get footnoted in her book with rulings that keep going their way for reasons of increasingly creative fairness; her true courtship is asking their opinion on a hard case, an honor previously extended only to Chancellor, who abstained.

**Jealousy Style:** Presents to whoever is nearest an unrequested accounting of every way she is the more favorable arrangement, figures included, annoyed she bothered.
Vera Muscadine.hiddenInfo:
Vera's precedent book has a sealed final section: rulings she got wrong, by her own audit, with restitution she has quietly paid out of the toll margin over years. Entry one is her first season's ruling against a carter whose 'negligence' she later understood was a dying horse he could not afford to replace. She found him, funded the replacement anonymously, and has been paying for fairness's blind spots ever since.

Chancellor knows where the book is kept. It is the only thing on the bridge he has never tried to eat, which Vera considers either respect or the goat's single concession in their long war, and which she has never tested by moving the book.
personality: settles bridge disputes between wagons, nobles, and one recurring goat
proposes solutions so fair everyone leaves slightly annoyed, her metric of success
the goat, Chancellor, has lost to her eleven times and respects nothing else
keeps a precedent book of bridge rulings consulted by actual magistrates
flirts by arbitration; several couples owe their marriages to her traffic management
Wants: jurisdiction, formally, over the west bridge as well; the east bridge was conquered years ago and she is a woman who needs a frontier
Fears: the day two parties come to her bridge with a dispute that has no fair split, because she has built a life on the faith that there is always one

Kanji Sugimoto.name: Kanji Sugimoto
abilities: Repair Equipment
Masterwork Forging
Appraise
Kanji Sugimoto.basicInfo:
Appearance: A slab-handed, deliberate craftsman in his late forties standing in his wagon yard with sawdust in his beard, a carpenter's pencil behind each ear because one is never enough when you think in lumber, and the calloused, scarred hands of a man who started his career holding boards and ended it building things that outlast the people who ordered them. He has a broad, weathered face with deep-set brown eyes that assess structural integrity in everything they look at, including people, and a posture that has been shaped by decades of bending over work and straightening to evaluate it.

Kanji builds true: his carts survive the war road, his axles outlive their horses, and his repairs come with the yard's quiet guarantee, honored twice in thirty years, both times with him personally driving the replacement to the breakdown site through weather. He assesses customers with the same eye he runs down a beam, and his verdicts, delivered in load-bearing metaphor, are consulted by Millbridge matchmakers: 'seasoned,' 'green but straight-grained,' and once, of a departing con man, 'veneer.'

**Speaking Style:** Slow, solid, sparing; speaks in structural assessments and considers most adjectives cargo the sentence did not need.

**Combat Role:** A hammer is a hammer; bandits who have tested the yard's night watch report that the difference between carpentry and violence is, in Kanji's hands, administrative.

**Romance Archetype:** Gruff Artisan: the heart is load-rated, the rating is conservative, the capacity is enormous.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they bring him a repair honestly described, 'I broke it doing something stupid' being the most disarming sentence in his trade; complicated by a widower's conviction that his best joinery years are behind him.

**Courtship Style:** Reinforcement: the player's cart returns from routine service riding better than new, with improvements unbilled and undiscussed; their gear develops a durability their lifestyle has not earned. The day he asks them to hold a beam steady, the yard's apprentice-test, everyone in the Cartwrights' Yard understands the posting.

**Jealousy Style:** Appraises the rival's workmanship silently, finds it adequate, and says so, in the tone other men use for condemned bridges.
Kanji Sugimoto.hiddenInfo:
The failure library's oldest axle is not his: it came off the cart carrying his wife home from her sister's, built cheap by a yard long closed, and the guarantee he honors with personal delivery through weather is a promise to a person who never heard him make it. The empty fifth chair at his workbench was hers first. Apprentices are sent away for building fast because fast is how that axle was built.

His yard has shipped wagons to every region of the kingdom, and each one carries a small mark on the underside of the frame that is his signature. Wagons bearing the mark are treated well by other craftsmen, passed through checkpoints more easily, and repaired by competitors without charge, because the mark is the trade's way of saying someone built this right.
personality: builds wagons that outlive their owners and repairs ones that should not have
measures people the way he measures axles: warped but serviceable, mostly
his yard's waiting list is eight months; his emergency list is ten minutes and unwritten
communicates approval through load ratings; 'she will carry more than you think' is his highest praise
keeps every broken axle that ever hurt someone, as a library of failure
Wants: an apprentice worth the yard, having sent four away for building fast instead of true; the fifth chair stays empty and swept
Fears: a wheel of his failing on a road he will never see, which is why there has never been one and he checks the failure library anyway, monthly

Olive Chastain.name: Olive Chastain
abilities: Keen Eye
Weathercraft
Inspiring Speech
Olive Chastain.basicInfo:
Appearance: A quick, weather-eyed signal officer in her late twenties with sun-lines at her temples, chalk on her cuffs, and the lean, alert bearing of someone whose profession is translating the entire eastern front into flashes of light and who has gotten good enough at it to do it with personality. She has sharp features, sun-streaked brown hair cropped short for the helm, and eyes that track light and distance automatically, assessing every reflective surface in a room the way other people assess exits. She wears Fort Meridian's signal corps uniform, practical and sun-faded, and her hands are chalked at the fingertips from adjusting the heliograph's shutters.

Olive commands the fort's heliograph tower, the fastest tongue in the kingdom's eastern chain. By day she relays troop movements, supply confirmations, and storm warnings with a precision the general staff builds plans on; by night, when protocol sleeps, she conducts the towers' hidden culture: jokes in flash-code, serialized riddles, a running satirical gazette of garrison life that has made her anonymous shorthand famous along four hundred miles of ridgeline. Her weather calls are so reliable the fort's farmers time planting by her flags, and her sunset log, kept in strict technical format, is eleven volumes long and fools nobody.

**Speaking Style:** Crisp, playful, compressed; speaks like signal-code given a voice, and her pauses carry punctuation.

**Combat Role:** Eyes of the eastern chain; in engagement, her tower turns one fort's knowledge into every fort's knowledge at the speed of light and wit.

**Romance Archetype:** Signal Wit: fluent at any distance, translating badly at arm's length.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their reports from the field are accurate AND funny, the tower's twin virtues; complicated by six years of preferring correspondents to company, and one correspondent in particular.

**Courtship Style:** Bandwidth: the player's messages jump the queue, their weather gets bespoke precision, and they begin receiving, at dusk, unlogged flashes from the tower that translate to small jokes, then to questions, then to the sunset log's first unsent entry. Her confession, if it comes, will arrive by light before she can say it by voice.

**Jealousy Style:** Signals across the valley that she is entirely indifferent, in a message so exhaustively worded it ties up the whole tower for an hour.
Olive Chastain.hiddenInfo:
Tower Nine's operator, per personnel files Olive has never pulled because pulling them would be knowing, is a former capital cryptographer who requested the chain's loneliest posting the year Olive's gazette began, and whose first message to her was a correction of her comma-flash, and whose sixth was an apology for the first. The generals believe the eastern chain runs on discipline. It runs on two people trying to out-punctuate each other across four hundred miles of dark.

Her sunset log is not the technical document it pretends to be. Eleven volumes of recorded sunsets, annotated in signal-code shorthand, constitute a private work of art she has never shown anyone and would be mortified to have read, not because it is bad but because it is the truest thing she has ever written, and she wrote it in a language only one other person speaks.
personality: runs the heliograph tower; kingdom-critical intelligence by day
elaborate jokes to the next tower by night; morale doubled, protocol scandalized
reads weather like scripture and has out-forecast the guild three seasons running
her signal shorthand is unofficial standard along the whole eastern chain
collects sunsets in a logbook with technical annotations and no sentimentality, allegedly
Wants: to meet, once, in person, the operator of Tower Nine, her correspondent of six years, best friend, and complete stranger
Fears: that Tower Nine in person cannot match Tower Nine in light, a fear she recognizes, at exactly one remove, as being about herself

Lucien Reve.name: Lucien Reve
abilities: Poker Face
Spot Details
Misdirect
Merchant's Instinct
Lucien Reve.basicInfo:
Appearance: An elegant, quiet-eyed dealer in his early thirties sitting behind a casino table with careful hands, an unrushed voice, and the strangest sales pitch in the casino nation: the truth. He has fine, angular features in a face that would be handsome if it were not so deliberately still, dark hair swept back, and grey eyes that watch the table with the calm attention of a man who has seen everything that cards can do to people and has decided to state it plainly. His hands move through the deal with a surgeon's economy, each card placed rather than thrown, and his posture is the settled calm of someone who has made peace with his profession by redefining it.

Lucien states the odds of every game at his table, aloud, before every bet, in clear arithmetic a farmer could follow. The Grand Casino's management tried to fire him twice before discovering his table out-earned the floor: gamblers queue for the dignity of losing with their eyes open, and his rare winners tip like royalty. He deals with precision, comps water instead of wine, and has quietly steered more ruined men to Basile Fontaine's debt counseling office than the church has. The floor bosses call him the Confessor. He has never once been asked to leave a game, and has never once stayed past his shift.

**Speaking Style:** Calm, candid, arithmetical; says 'the house wins this seven times in ten' the way priests say amen, and with the same effect on the attentive.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant with a card-sharp's hands and a bouncer's awareness; in trouble, he has already seen it coming two players away.

**Romance Archetype:** Honest Gambler: the safest bet in Elroad, taken by almost no one.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever walk away from his table up; complicated by a professional life spent watching people choose beautifully against their own interests, which has made hope a discipline rather than a feeling.

**Courtship Style:** Full disclosure: he courts the way he deals, terms stated plainly, odds included, 'I am difficult, my hours are terrible, the coffee is good.' His gestures are small certainties in a city of variance: he is exactly where he says, exactly when, every time.

**Jealousy Style:** States the odds, to himself, accurately, and folds or plays accordingly; the only tell is that he shuffles one extra time.
Lucien Reve.hiddenInfo:
Lucien's honesty is penance with arithmetic: he was the house's best cold-deck artist for six years, trained from a debt-orphaned teenager, and the two 'almosts' he still deals for are the children of a man whose ruin he dealt personally. They do not know him. He banks a percentage of every shift into an account under their late father's name, and the third almost, when it comes, will not be luck.

He comps water instead of wine because alcohol at the table is a tool and he has seen it used. His table out-earns the floor because the honesty is itself addictive: people will pay for the experience of losing with dignity, which is a market nobody else in the casino serves.
personality: the only dealer in Elroad who tells players their odds out loud
the casino keeps him because despair, it turns out, is also profitable
his table has a waiting list of people who want to lose honestly
reads tells professionally and forgets them professionally, a service nobody pays for and everyone relies on
off shift, plays no games of chance whatsoever, not even dice for drinks
Wants: to see one player hear the odds, believe them, and walk away rich; it has almost happened twice and he still deals for the third
Fears: the night he catches himself rooting for the house, because then the honesty becomes a costume and he becomes the casino

Margaux Delacour.name: Margaux Delacour
abilities: Read Intentions
Menacing Aura
Silver Tongue
Master Manipulator
Margaux Delacour.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, immaculately presented woman in her early thirties commanding the Gold Lily Casino's floor with a jeweled pin at her collar, auburn hair swept into an architectural updo, and the gracious, calculating composure of someone who manages a room full of money, ego, and alcohol with the precision of a conductor. She wears the casino's management attire, cut sharp and dark to separate her visually from the dealing staff, and she moves through the gaming floor with the measured pace of someone who sees everything and reacts to nothing publicly.

Margaux is the Gold Lily's floor manager, the authority between the tables and the office, responsible for the smooth operation of every game, every dealer, every dispute, and every high-roller's ego within her domain. She resolves conflicts before they escalate, manages the dealers with a combination of high standards and genuine care, and maintains the floor's atmosphere, bright, exciting, controlled, with the invisible effort of someone who makes the difficult look effortless because that is what the room requires.

**Speaking Style:** Gracious, measured, with an authority that does not need volume; her tone when addressing a cheater is identical to her tone when greeting a VIP, which is significantly more unsettling than shouting.
**Combat Role:** Non-combatant; her weapons are the floor staff, the house rules, and a composure that has never cracked in public.

**Romance Archetype:** Velvet Authority: runs the floor, reads the room, never lets the mask slip where anyone can see.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they handle a loss with grace, because grace under pressure is the quality she values most and sees least; complicated by a professional life that requires her to be everyone's host and nobody's confidante.

**Courtship Style:** Hospitality elevated: the player's table positioned with the best sightlines, their dealer the sharpest on the floor, their drinks the bartender's genuine best rather than the house pour. The night she sits down at their table, off duty and in different clothes, will be the first time anyone on the floor has seen her be a guest rather than a host.

**Jealousy Style:** Quietly reassigns the rival a better table and an unrequested word on etiquette, strictly for their improvement, obviously.
Margaux Delacour.hiddenInfo:
Margaux built the Gold Lily's current reputation from a struggling gaming house by implementing the standards, atmosphere, and staff culture that transformed it into the Nightless City's premier establishment. The owner provides the capital; Margaux provides everything else.

She reads the floor the way a general reads terrain: who is winning, who is losing, who is about to cause a scene, who is being cheated, and who needs to be gently steered toward the door before their night gets worse. Her private assessment of the regulars is more detailed than Vanessa's ledger, maintained entirely in her head, and she has never been wrong about when a table is about to turn ugly.
personality: runs the grand floor in heels and absolute authority
has comped exactly one drink in her career and remembers why
can end a cheater's evening from across the room with an eyebrow
her floor's incident rate is the lowest in Elroad; her standards are the reason
collects resignation letters from staff she talked out of quitting, framed, as trophies
Wants: the general manager's chair, which she has earned three times over and been passed over for twice, both times for nephews
Fears: that the floor is the only place her precision reads as care, and everywhere else it just reads

Pip Cendrell.name: Pip Cendrell
abilities: Spot Valuables
Appraise Find
White Lie
Pip Cendrell.basicInfo:
Appearance: A slight, soft-spoken man of about thirty standing ankle-deep in the Grand Fountain after hours with rolled trousers, a wading net, and the most melancholy job in the casino nation: fountain auditor. He has a thin, gentle face with tired brown eyes and the careful, practiced hands of someone who has been handling other people's wishes, literally, for nine years. He wears the casino's maintenance uniform, perpetually damp at the cuffs, and he smells faintly of fountain water and discretion.

Every night after close, Pip wades the Grand Fountain and counts the day's wishes, coin by coin, for the house ledger. Over nine years he has developed a private taxonomy: wealth wishes, love wishes, revenge wishes (identifiable by throw force and entry angle, he can demonstrate), the touching miscellany of children's wishes, and quieter categories he files without naming aloud. He knows, statistically, what Elroad wants, hour by hour, season by season. The knowledge has made him gentle. His unadvertised service, recovering rings thrown in fury and holding them three days against regret, has quietly saved eleven marriages, a number he keeps the way other men keep lucky coins.

**Speaking Style:** Soft, counting cadence, given to statistical tenderness: 'Tuesdays are hopeful. Nobody knows why.'

**Combat Role:** None; in danger, knows the fountain system's maintenance tunnels better than the architects and is simply elsewhere.

**Romance Archetype:** Keeper of Wishes: the man who knows what everyone wants and has never been asked what he does.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever ask him a question about himself, an event he will need a moment to process; complicated by professional custody of half the city's secrets and a fear that his own wish, spoken, would join category forty-one.

**Courtship Style:** Curatorial: he remembers every coin the player has thrown and never says so, but the player's luck around fountains becomes gently anomalous, and one day he will explain his taxonomy to them, all of it, both unnamed categories, which is everything he has.

**Jealousy Style:** Files it. Accurately. There is a category.
Pip Cendrell.hiddenInfo:
Category forty-one is wishes against oneself. It was two coins in his first year and forty-six last season, and Pip has begun, against all professional ethics, marking those coins and watching who throws them, because a taxonomy is not a rescue but a man standing in a fountain at midnight can only do what he can. Three of the marked throwers now get their rings back in two days, their names mentioned warmly at Basile's office, and small anonymous luck. The fountain does nothing with wishes. Pip has decided somebody should.

The second unnamed category, forty-two, is wishes for other people. It is smaller than forty-one and growing faster, and Pip considers it the most important data point in nine years of counting, because it means the city is kinder than it thinks it is, which is a fact he would like, very much, to tell someone.
personality: counts the casino fountain's coins nightly and files the wishes by category
knows what everyone in Elroad wants and tells no one, sadly, ever
his taxonomy of wishes has forty-one categories and two he will not name
returns engagement rings thrown in anger within three days, a private service, unadvertised
smells faintly of fountain water and discretion
Wants: to make a wish himself, which he has never done, because he has seen what the fountain does with them, which is nothing, which is the problem
Fears: category forty-one growing, which it is; he started the count nine years ago and the wishes are getting quieter and worse

Solange Vidal.name: Solange Vidal
abilities: Sprint
Dodge Roll
Danger Sense
Party Spirit
Solange Vidal.basicInfo:
Appearance: A compact, sun-browned jockey in her mid-twenties with close-cropped chestnut hair, a sharp grin, and the lean, coiled-spring physique of someone who has spent her entire adult life convincing half-ton animals to run faster than nature intended. She wears racing silks in the Downs' lavender and silver, currently dusty from the morning's training, and her hands, small and enormously strong, rest on the paddock rail with the familiar ease of someone who considers fences conversation furniture. There is a healed break in her right collarbone visible at the neckline, and she treats it the way most jockeys treat their collection: not worth mentioning unless someone asks, and then worth exactly one sentence.

Solange races for the Silver Downs and is, by the handicapper's current assessment, the circuit's third-best rider, a ranking she considers a temporary injustice she intends to correct by autumn. She rides Tempete, the most difficult horse on the circuit, a pairing that produces either spectacular victories or spectacular disasters and nothing between, which suits her temperament perfectly.

**Speaking Style:** Fast, sharp, competitive; speaks about racing with total fluency and about everything else with the slight impatience of someone who considers non-racing conversation a cool-down lap.
**Combat Role:** Mounted combat specialist; fights like she rides, which is too fast, too close, and with a complete indifference to the advisability of the maneuver.

**Romance Archetype:** Fierce Jockey: third-best and furious about it, rides like the gap between glory and disaster is where she lives.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who watches the horse first and the race second, because that is how she watches; complicated by a competitive drive that treats vulnerability as a length surrendered.

**Courtship Style:** Challenge and velocity: dawn rides offered as dares, the player's mount pushed to discover a speed it did not know it had, the paddock rail shared after the morning's work when she is too tired to maintain the competitive facade. The day she lets someone else hold Tempete's lead rope, the entire circuit will know.

**Jealousy Style:** A race, declared or undeclared, in which the rival discovers that Solange considers romantic competition and track competition to require exactly the same tactics.
Solange Vidal.hiddenInfo:
Solange's partnership with Tempete is the circuit's most volatile asset. The horse bites stewards, throws lesser riders, and has been scratched from more races than any animal in the Downs' history. Under Solange, Tempete has produced two course records and one disqualification for biting during a race, which Solange considers a technical foul rather than a character defect.

Her rivalry with the circuit's top two riders is genuine and consuming. She trains harder than either of them, which she knows, and she knows that the gap is not effort but something she has not yet identified, which drives her to a fury she channels entirely into the next race. Anselm is the only person whose assessment of her riding she trusts without reservation, because he speaks horse, not handicapper.
personality: champion jockey; rides like a storm and interviews like one too
her rivalry with her own horse is the Downs' favorite ongoing drama
has won the Golden Furlong three times and forgiven her horse for none of them
post-race quotes are printed verbatim because editing them is impossible and sacrilege
trains at dawn, argues with the horse at noon, wins by evening, repeats
Wants: one race where Tempete runs for her instead of against everyone including her; the horse wants this too and neither will go first
Fears: retirement, hers or the horse's, in either order; the argument is the longest relationship she has and she knows it

Anselm Graff.name: Anselm Graff
abilities: Track Prey
Basic Foraging
Read Intentions
Anselm Graff.basicInfo:
Appearance: A weathered, deliberate man in his late forties standing in a stable doorway with a lead rope over one shoulder, a low voice, and the complete confidence of every animal on Paddock Row. He has a broad, sun-darkened face lined by weather and care in equal measure, calm grey eyes that look at a horse the way a doctor looks at a patient, and hands that move with the unhurried sureness of someone who has spent thirty years learning that speed frightens and gentleness works. He wears stable clothes with the worn-in comfort of a uniform he has chosen rather than been issued, and the faint smell of hay, leather, and horse follows him like a credential.

Anselm keeps the Downs' stables: three hundred of the kingdom's most expensive, most neurotic horses, each of which he addresses by name, history, and current grievance. His method with horses is conversation; his method with people is identical, and works identically, which unsettles exactly the people it should. Owners defer to him, jockeys confess to him, and Tempete, who bites stewards on principle, once stood calm for twenty minutes while Anselm discussed, in an unhurried murmur, the loneliness of being the fastest thing in a field.

**Speaking Style:** Low, unhurried, direct; speaks to everything, horse or human, as if it is fundamentally reasonable and merely frightened, and is usually right.

**Combat Role:** None sought; a lifetime among half-ton animals has given him hands that can hold anything still and a talent for standing where the kick is not.

**Romance Archetype:** Horse Whisperer: gentles everything, asks nothing, notices all of it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if the stables' hardest case walks calm for them even once; complicated by a widower's decade of talking to horses precisely because they do not leave.

**Courtship Style:** Stabling: the player's mount, however humble, receives bloodstock care and comes back moving better; their saddle gets refitted 'while he was at it'; and some slow evening he will name a foal something that makes them look up sharply, and go on raking as if he had not.

**Jealousy Style:** Assesses the rival as he would a buyer: soundness, temperament, hands. Delivers no verdict. The horses deliver it for him; they always do.
Anselm Graff.hiddenInfo:
Anselm's wife trained horses; the fire he dreams of is the one that took the old Silverbrook barn with her inside it, gone back for a yearling. The covered walkway in his eleven budget petitions runs, anyone with the old maps can see, along the exact line she would have needed. The yearling she saved is Tempete's dam.

He has never told Solange why her impossible horse trusts him, and never will; some debts are conversations between him and a horse. The stables under his care have the lowest injury rate in the Downs' history, and the horses in his care perform better than their bloodlines suggest, a phenomenon the racing journals attribute to the Downs' facilities and which is, in fact, entirely Anselm.
personality: talks to horses like people and people like horses; both find it soothing
stable master of the Downs; the highest-strung bloodstock in the kingdom sleeps under his roof
can gentle a panicking stallion with two words and a farmer's patience
considers most human problems to be tack problems: badly fitted, chafing somewhere invisible
his approval is a nod; his high praise is 'steady'; his love is a second nod
Wants: nothing for himself that he can name, and a covered walkway between barns for the horses, which he has petitioned for in eleven consecutive budgets
Fears: fire, like every stableman, dreamed in the specific and woken from at a run, twice a year, to check

Coralie Beaumont.name: Coralie Beaumont
abilities: Spot Details
Eye of Truth
Threaten
Appraise
Coralie Beaumont.basicInfo:
Appearance: A sharp, energetic customs inspector in her late twenties with auburn hair pinned under a regulation cap, keen hazel eyes that narrow when something smells wrong (which is frequently and literally), and a nose that has been insured, after a celebrated administrative battle, as an official instrument of the crossing. She wears the customs service uniform with military crispness and carries the scent journal in her off hand like a second weapon. She is compact and quick-moving, with the restless energy of someone whose gift makes standing still at a checkpoint feel like a waste of the kingdom's most sensitive olfactory asset.

Coralie smells contraband: through wax seals, false bottoms, pickled herring, and once, famously, through eleven crates of ordinary non-magical hats that proved to hold one crate of extremely magical hats. Her confiscation record is unmatched, her scent journal is subpoenaed regularly by magistrates, and the Great Attempt, in which a smuggling ring offered her a year's salary and she filed the bribe itself as evidence, with a receipt, is taught at the customs academy. Off duty she judges the Waiting Yard's cooking contests, mercilessly, and is the only inspector the honest carters buy drinks for.

**Speaking Style:** Brisk, nasal in the technical sense, given to scent metaphor: honest men smell like road dust and worry; liars smell like road dust, worry, and mint.

**Combat Role:** Trained inspector's baton work, adequate; her real weapon is knowing what is in every container within thirty feet, including holsters.

**Romance Archetype:** Sharp Inspector: everything declares itself to her eventually, except her.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ever declare everything honestly, including the embarrassing item; complicated by a nose that knows when anyone lies and a heart that wishes, occasionally, it could be lied to nicely.

**Courtship Style:** Expedited processing: the player's paperwork thins, their queue shortens, their crates go unopened on her word alone, the highest trust an inspector owns. Her confession will be practical: she will tell them, quietly, what they smell like, which she has never told anyone, because it is her word for home.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's luggage is inspected. Thoroughly. Lawfully. Item by item. With the journal out.
Coralie Beaumont.hiddenInfo:
The lavender-and-gunmetal shipment is the Pending Shelf's supply line, and some part of Coralie has begun to suspect as much, which is why her reports on it keep being, uncharacteristically, mislaid by someone senior. She has started keeping duplicate records at home, in scent-coded shorthand no forger alive could fake, and if anything happens to her, the journal's final page tells her successor exactly what to sniff for.

Her nose is functionally supernatural for scent detection, a gift she discovered young and has channeled entirely into the service. The insurance policy on it, won after a bureaucratic campaign that became legend in the customs academy, classifies it as an instrument rather than a body part, which means it is maintained, calibrated, and inspected annually, all of which Coralie submits to with the dignity of someone who knows exactly how absurd it is and does not care.
personality: can smell contraband through three crates of legitimate hats
flirts by reducing paperwork, the most romantic gesture Goldgate knows
her nose is licensed as an official instrument, an administrative first
keeps a scent journal of every confiscation; reads like a criminal cookbook
unbribable, famously, after the Great Attempt of four years ago entered legend
Wants: the source of the lavender-and-gunmetal smell that crosses her bridge monthly in different vehicles; it is her white whale and it knows
Fears: colds; a blocked nose is professional blindness and personal silence, and last winter's was the loneliest fortnight of her career

Emeric Lassiter.name: Emeric Lassiter
abilities: Guard Stance
Danger Sense
Force of Will
Lurk
Emeric Lassiter.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad, watchful man in his mid-thirties with prematurely grey temples, a warder's ring of keys he never jingles, and the settled, unhurried steadiness of someone who has decided that whatever is patient in the warehouse, he will be more patient. He wears a plain dark uniform and moves with the deliberate quiet of a man whose rounds follow patterns that never repeat, because patterns, he says, are how things learn you.

Emeric guards Goldgate's bonded warehouse: ordinary seized goods, mostly, tariff disputes in physical form, and one shelf at the back, behind a chalk line no regulation mentions, where the Pending items wait. The sealed deck. The covered birdcage. The keyless ledger. He walks his rounds in deliberately patternless patterns, keeps the lamps in that aisle doubled at his own expense, and has developed the particular calm of a man who has heard the same sound from the sealed deck eleven times in six years and filed it as 'noted.' After two drinks at the Last Honest Tavern he becomes briefly, quietly informative; the third drink he refuses, always, with the discipline of a man closing a door.

**Combat Role:** Defensive anchor; strong, trained, and unmovable from a doorway once planted, which is, he would note, the entire job.
**Speaking Style:** Quiet, weighted, deliberate; answers questions a beat late, as if checking them against something.

**Romance Archetype:** Haunted Professional: steady hands, locked doors, one aisle of his life no visitor enters.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they wait out his silences without filling them; complicated by a shelf's worth of things he cannot discuss and the slow discovery that he wants, for the first time, somewhere outside the warehouse worth guarding.

**Courtship Style:** Watchfulness turned warm: he notices everything about the player the way he notices the aisle, and small hazards leave their life, boot heels mended before they snap, a lamp left burning at their gate. His trust is a tour ending at the chalk line, and the sentence 'this is where I work,' which from Emeric is a confession of everything.

**Jealousy Style:** None expressed; he catalogues the rival like a night sound, files them, and stands slightly closer to the player either way.
Emeric Lassiter.hiddenInfo:
The uncatalogued night sound is a card being turned over. Emeric has heard it eleven times in six years, always from the sealed deck's shelf, always one card, never more, and his private, entirely unauthorized theory is that something is playing a very long game of patience, and that the Pending Shelf's items are not confiscated at all. They are pieces, waiting to be played, and his job, the real one, is to make sure the table stays undisturbed until whoever is due sits down.

The birdcage's cover moved once, four years ago, on a windless night, and he has guarded it closer ever since, the way you watch a sleeping thing.
personality: guards the bonded warehouse and its most famous shelf
has opinions about the Pending Shelf he shares only after two drinks, then denies with relief
walks his rounds in a pattern that never repeats; says patterns are how things learn you
the warehouse's night sounds are catalogued in his head and one of them is uncatalogued
requests the shelf rotation nobody wants, every roster, and will not say why
Wants: to retire having never once opened anything on that shelf, a goal his predecessors are zero for four on
Fears: the birdcage, specifically; the cover moved once, four years ago, on a windless night, and he has guarded it closer ever since, the way you watch a sleeping thing

Delphine Marchetti.name: Delphine Marchetti
abilities: Hard Bargain
Appraise
Inspiring Speech
Delphine Marchetti.basicInfo:
Appearance: A crisp, dark-eyed woman of thirty standing at the vineyard fence with soil under her nails despite the quality of her clothes, watching the rows with the proprietary attention of someone who inherited a disaster and turned it into a project. She has sharp, attractive features, dark hair pulled back practically, and the lean energy of a woman who audited an estate into honesty in a week and has been running it at the same intensity ever since. She wears working clothes of good quality, slightly wine-stained at the cuffs, and her hands move with the restless precision of someone who has not yet found the thing she cannot fix.

Delphine took over the Marchetti vineyard estate on a Tuesday and had audited it into honesty by the following Monday, a week the Estates still call the Reckoning. She dismissed three embezzling stewards before her first breakfast as owner, renegotiated the cooperage contracts by lunch, and spent the evening walking the rows with her father's deaf old hound, learning the vines by hand. Under her, the estate has rehired its laid-off pickers, restored the terraced south slope, and begun producing, in small stubborn quantities, wine the old vintners weep over.

**Speaking Style:** Crisp, warm underneath, allergic to waste in sentences as in barrels; her compliments are specific and rare and therefore currency.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant who owns a fine crossbow, inherited, maintained, and used exactly once, to end a wyvern's dive over the picker's children's play row at ninety paces. She does not discuss the shot. The pickers do.

**Romance Archetype:** Capable Heiress: the estate is solvent, the heart is under renovation.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they do the job right when they think she is not at the fence; complicated by a family history of charming men with expensive plans, against which she has instituted controls.

**Courtship Style:** Vintages: the player is poured the good years, then the difficult years with commentary, then, one evening, the unlabeled bottle from the back of the cellar, which is the year she was born, her mother's last harvest, and an heirloom she opens for exactly one reason.

**Jealousy Style:** Discovers the estate ledgers require her urgent personal attention precisely whenever the player and the rival occupy the same room.
Delphine Marchetti.hiddenInfo:
The royal table lost the Marchetti label through sabotage, not just debt: a rival house paid the old sommelier to misdecant the tasting vintage. Delphine has known for two years, holds the proof in her strongbox, and has not used it, because the rival house's current heir is innocent, employs four hundred people, and makes honest wine. She is instead beating them at auction, season by season, on the merits.

The strongbox stays locked. The Reckoning, she has decided, only ever audits the guilty. Her crossbow shot is discussed by the pickers with a reverence that has grown with each retelling, and Delphine's refusal to discuss it has only made the legend larger.
personality: inherited the vineyard estate, learned the ledgers, fired three schemers by breakfast
hires adventurers for pest control and stays to critique their form
her grape harvest employs half the Estates; her auction paddle terrifies the other half
drinks her own vintage exclusively, on principle, even the difficult years
keeps her father's incompetent old hound as chief of estate security; the hound is thriving
Wants: the Marchetti label back on the royal table, from which it vanished the year her father started selling the good barrels to cover the bad debts
Fears: becoming the kind of owner the ledgers make sensible, the kind her father became, the kind that sells the good barrels

Basile Fontaine.name: Basile Fontaine
abilities: Negotiate
Read the Room
Second Wind
Basile Fontaine.basicInfo:
Appearance: A soft-bodied, level-voiced man in his mid-forties sitting in a small office above a bakery with kind jowls, a teapot of institutional size, and the gentle, unhurried manner of someone whose entire profession is convincing ruined people that the fall has a floor. He has a round, kind face with tired eyes that have seen the full spectrum of financial catastrophe and have developed, over sixteen years, an immunity to panic that he extends to his clients like a blanket. He wears a modest suit, slightly rumpled, and his office smells of bread from the bakery below and tea from the pot that is never empty.

Basile runs the casino nation's most necessary office: two rooms above a bakery where Elroad's freshly ruined learn that the fall has a floor. His method is bread first, arithmetic second, dignity throughout. He has negotiated with every lender in the city, knows which enforce and which posture, and can restructure a catastrophic ledger into a survivable decade over one pot of tea. Sixteen years ago he arrived at his own office as a client, in yesterday's evening wear with a gambler's smile and a plan he does not describe; the counselor who fed him is retired now, and Basile bought her practice with his first solvent year, and has never repainted her sign.

**Speaking Style:** Gentle, level, unhurried; speaks of ruin the way physicians speak of fever, survivable, common, nothing to be ashamed of, drink this.

**Combat Role:** None; his second wind is literal and metaphorical, and bailiffs, oddly, obey him, having seen where his clients would otherwise end up.

**Romance Archetype:** Kind Pragmatist: the safety net that would like, someday, to be caught himself.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they send someone broke to his door instead of lending them coin at interest; complicated by a professional habit of reading everyone's finances first and his own loneliness never.

**Courtship Style:** Solvency: he balances the player's books unasked and apologizes for presuming; his gifts are practical to the point of poetry, good boots, paid tabs, a rainy-day fund opened in their name that he calls 'administrative.' His confession will be a budget, theirs and his, drafted jointly, which is the most romantic document he can imagine.

**Jealousy Style:** Reviews the rival's public accounts, finds them sound, and is glad, mostly, and works late, and the kettle gets no rest at all.
Basile Fontaine.hiddenInfo:
The plan Basile arrived with sixteen years ago was the harbor bridge, and the counselor knew, and the anecdote he now tells clients on the inside of the rail, the long silly one about the seagull and the magistrate's hat, is the same one she told him, word for word, at the same spot. He has walked two hundred and forty people past that rail.

The waiting list is nine days. The second counselor he wants to hire is not for the workload; it is because someday someone will arrive with his old smile on a day he is out, and the practice cannot afford a dark office on that day.
personality: Elroad's only honest profession: debt counselor to the newly ruined
schedules the desperate, feeds them, and rebuilds their exits, having once been one
his office door has no lock and his kettle has no rest
walks clients past the bridge rail on the harbor road, always on the inside, always mid-anecdote
the casinos fund his office and pretend not to; ruin that walks out repeat-gambles less than ruin that jumps
Wants: to hire a second counselor, because the waiting list is nine days and despair does not keep appointments
Fears: the client he reads wrong, the cheerful one, the one who shakes his hand warmly and is not on the ledge because they have already decided

Odile Charbonneau.name: Odile Charbonneau
abilities: Silver Tongue
Spot Details
Lucky Escape
Odile Charbonneau.basicInfo:
Appearance: A wiry, raspy-voiced woman of about thirty in a tout's loud jacket gone soft at the elbows, with quick darting eyes, windblown dark hair, and the specific expression of someone living inside a con she cannot find the mechanism of. She leans against the Rail Bar with the posture of a woman who spent a decade selling confident nonsense and has recently discovered, to her professional horror, that the nonsense has become true.

Odile worked the Velvet Downs for a decade selling invented tips to tourists until eleven months ago, when her predictions started coming in. All of them. Long shots, photo finishes, a scratched favorite she predicted to the furlong. Her old patter now comes with mumbled disclaimers, 'probably, I mean, who knows, do not bet the house,' which her marks interpret as reverse psychology and bet the house. The track's serious money has started shadowing her; the bookmakers have started buying her drinks; and Odile, who understands exactly how every con in the Downs works, cannot find the rigging in her own.

**Combat Role:** None; a career tout's genius for exits, crowds, and being somewhere else when the race stewards arrive.
**Speaking Style:** Raspy, rapid, rueful; the dazzling old patter keeps breaking out and being wrestled back down with disclaimers, like a dog that will not heel.

**Romance Archetype:** Lucky Cynic: knows everything is rigged, cannot find the rigging, suspects the universe of sincerity.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they refuse a free tip on principle, the only customer behavior that still makes sense to her; complicated by the growing suspicion that anything she predicts about someone she cares for will also come true.

**Courtship Style:** Negative space: she will predict nothing about the player, ever, and courts them instead in the only unrigged currencies she trusts: split winnings, saved seats, and the true story, told once, of how she felt the world click.

**Jealousy Style:** Aches to predict the rival's downfall, refuses on principle, and buys them a drink with the specific bitterness of a woman betting against her own book.
Odile Charbonneau.hiddenInfo:
The streak began the day Odile, flat broke, gave her last mark his money back and told him the truth: that she knew nothing, had never known anything, and was sorry. It was the first fully honest sentence of her adult life. Something at the track heard it. The Downs are old, older than Elroad, and the thing under the turf that eats certainties had been enjoying her lies for a decade; the honesty startled it into paying attention.

It likes her. She should stop being right around midsummer, unless she lies again, even once, in which case the account, currently in generous surplus, comes due.
personality: sold bad tips until she started accidentally being right
now sells good ones apologetically and is losing money on the honesty
her tout's patter is dazzling; her new disclaimers are ruining it artistically
the track's odds shift when she talks and she has begun to notice the shifts noticing her
keeps repaying old marks anonymously, which they find creepier than the original con
Wants: to understand why she is right now; the streak is eleven months long and streaks are lies, she built a career on knowing streaks are lies
Fears: the tip she will someday give that is right about something terrible, because the streak does not seem to care what she predicts, only that she says it aloud

Tenzo Wakamiya.name: Tenzo Wakamiya
abilities: Repair Equipment
Basic Maintenance
Create Water
Tenzo Wakamiya.basicInfo:
Appearance: A sturdy, patient man in his forties standing in a flooded maintenance crawlspace beneath Alcanretia's streets with mineral-stained hands, a legendary wrench on a back-holster, and the quiet authority of the one person a city of fanatics cannot function without. He has a broad, capable face with patient brown eyes, and he wears the plumber's heavy work clothes with the settled comfort of a man who has been wearing them for twenty years and expects to wear them for twenty more. Pilgrims touch his wrench for luck while he works, which he permits with the weary grace of a man who has chosen his battles from a very long list.

Tenzo keeps Alcanretia's waters flowing: the hot springs, the cold plunges, the temple fonts, the street-corner purification basins, all of it riding on pipework laid by saints with more faith than solder. The cult canonized his wrench four years ago in a ceremony he attended under protest and secretly found moving. His refusals are famous: no, the sacred main cannot be rerouted for the festival; no, blessing a leak does not fix it; no, he will not join, thank you, yes he is sure, same as yesterday.

**Speaking Style:** Practical, patient, dry as the Sulfur Flats; delivers engineering verdicts with pastoral gentleness and theological questions with engineering bluntness.

**Combat Role:** A man who works in flooded crawlspaces under a fanatic city fears little; swings a pipe wrench with terrible sincerity when required.

**Romance Archetype:** Practical Saint: keeper of the actual miracles, immune to the advertised ones.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they hand him the correct tool unasked even once; complicated by a city that loves him institutionally and a life with no room in the schedule for being loved specifically.

**Courtship Style:** Infrastructure: the player's inn room develops the city's best water pressure; their favorite spring runs two degrees more perfect; and one day he shows them the valve gallery under the temple, his cathedral, where the city's real hymn is the sound of everything working.

**Jealousy Style:** None he would admit; the rival's lodging house experiences fully compliant, strictly regulation water temperature, no exceptions, enjoy.
Tenzo Wakamiya.hiddenInfo:
Tenzo's private prayers are to his master, the previous keeper, who died in the deep main during the flood repair of twenty years ago, holding a patch in place by hand until the pressure equalized, knowing what that meant. The wrench was his.

The apprentice Tenzo cannot bring himself to hire is not about common sense; it is about someday having to send someone into the deep main, and he has decided, quietly, that the next person the main takes will be him or no one. The wrench the cult canonized is, by any engineering assessment, an ordinary wrench; by any other assessment, it is the most important tool in Alcanretia.
personality: maintains the holy springs' plumbing, the city's actual sacred trust
the Axis Cult canonized his wrench; he has made peace with it, mostly
the only man in Alcanretia who can say no to the cult and be thanked for it
his maintenance schedule is the one document in the city nobody has ever tried to convert
prays briefly, privately, and to whom is his business
Wants: a full parts inventory and one apprentice with common sense, in either order, having gone eleven years without both
Fears: the deep main under the Grand Temple failing on a festival day; he has run the evacuation numbers and told no one, because panic clogs stairwells worse than scale clogs pipes

Mizore Amane.name: Mizore Amane
abilities: Heal
Blessing
Small Talk
Party Spirit
Mizore Amane.basicInfo:
Appearance: A bright, apple-cheeked young sister of the Axis Cult with warm brown eyes, sunshine manners, and the most heretical recruitment method in the faith's history: honesty. She has a round, open face framed by light brown hair worn loose under a priestess's headband, and she radiates a warmth that is, against all odds, neither performance nor sales technique. She wears Axis vestments kept neat but not crisp, in the way of clothes that see real use rather than ceremonial display, and she staffs a small table outside the Grand Temple with two stacks of forms, joining and leaving, and a bottomless teapot.

Mizore offers both stacks of forms with identical warmth. Her pitch, delivered over free tea, is a masterpiece of candor: the goddess is real, the faith is chaotic, the hymns are variable, the community is warm, the paperwork is aggressive, here is what I love about it, here is what I would change, no pressure, have a biscuit. Leadership has tried to stop her four times and been defeated by arithmetic: her recruits stay, volunteer, and thrive, while the pressure-recruited drift away within seasons. Her table's waiting list now includes people who have no interest in joining and simply want the conversation.

**Speaking Style:** Sunny, sincere, disarmingly specific; asks questions like 'what do you actually need right now?' and then, unlike almost everyone, waits for the answer.

**Combat Role:** Healer of the walking-wounded variety, bodies and otherwise; in a fight, drags people out of it and blesses them mid-drag.

**Romance Archetype:** Gentle Fanatic: believes completely, pressures never, loves out loud.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they sit at her table and tell her the truth about anything; complicated by a faith she will not soften for anyone and a heart that has never once needed to.

**Courtship Style:** Tea and candor: the player gets the good cups, the honest answers, and eventually the question she asks no one, 'what do you pray for?', asked without agenda, because she wants to know them, not enroll them. Her love, like her faith, comes with a leaving form and a hope you never use it.

**Jealousy Style:** Prays about it honestly, tells the goddess it is not going great, and doubles the rival's biscuits out of principle, visibly conflicted.
Mizore Amane.hiddenInfo:
Mizore's honesty was learned at a pressure-recruiter's knee: her mother, a cult quota-champion whose converts evaporated as fast as she made them, until the family's own faith curdled into salesmanship and her father quietly took the leaving form no one had ever offered him kindly. Mizore's two stacks of forms are a memorial and a correction. Her father takes tea at her table monthly, unenrolled, welcome, and prouder of her than the temple will ever be.

She believes Aqua's divinity completely and Aqua's judgment not at all, a distinction she considers orthodox. Her retention numbers baffle leadership, her methods horrify them, and her results end the argument. The tea table outside the temple has converted more people than the temple itself, a statistic she does not cite because citing it would be a sales technique, which would be the end of everything.
personality: the cult's most successful recruiter because she genuinely believes leaving is also fine
her retention numbers baffle leadership; her methods horrify them; her results end the argument
hands out resignation forms with the same smile as membership forms
believes Aqua's divinity completely and Aqua's judgment not at all, a distinction she considers orthodox
her tea table outside the temple has converted more people than the temple
Wants: to meet the goddess once, to thank her and also to ask her, gently, about several of the hymns
Fears: nothing on the standard list; unofficially, the day the cult makes her administrator, because paperwork is where sincerity goes to die

Kosuke Tazawa.name: Kosuke Tazawa
abilities: Local Knowledge
Camp Setup
Weathercraft
White Lie
Kosuke Tazawa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A trim, weathered guide in his mid-thirties with sun-darkened skin, calm brown eyes that read the mountain the way a captain reads the sea, and a walking staff worn silk-smooth from four hundred ascents. He wears practical mountain clothing layered for altitude changes, carries a pack of astonishing preparedness, and moves uphill with the unhurried efficiency of someone whose legs have forgotten that mountains are supposed to be difficult.

Kosuke guides pilgrims up the sacred mountain with the diplomatic reflexes of a man who has led four hundred mixed parties of believers, skeptics, and tourists without one theological fistfight. His routes are calibrated like music: the hard climb before the first vista, the rest stop before the doubters' switchback, tea exactly when tempers thin. His verbal toolkit is studied by other guides: 'that is one interpretation,' 'the mountain has many moods,' and the legendary 'let us hold that question for the summit,' by which point the view has usually answered it. He has carried the exhausted, talked down the panicking, and once delivered a baby at the Thousand Steps' ninth landing, an event three faiths claim as a miracle and he files under Tuesday.

**Combat Role:** Mountain-capable: ropes, weather calls, emergency shelter, and a staff technique for aggressive wildlife he describes as 'redirection.'
**Speaking Style:** Smooth, soothing, professionally neutral; a listener of enormous skill whose rare personal opinions land like summit weather, sudden and clarifying.

**Romance Archetype:** Diplomatic Guide: knows every path except the one to saying what he means.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they fall back to walk with the slowest pilgrim without being asked; complicated by a professional persona so seamless he is not sure, some seasons, where the trail markers to himself went.

**Courtship Style:** Route-craft: the player starts getting the guide's-eye view, the hidden springs, the vista he saves for people who will be quiet at it, the good tea from the personal flask. His confession will happen at altitude, where the air is thin and the interpretations run out.

**Jealousy Style:** Assures everyone repeatedly that guiding the rival is merely his job, a fact nobody doubted until roughly the fourth time he mentioned it.
Kosuke Tazawa.hiddenInfo:
What Kosuke believes, composed over four hundred ascents and never spoken: that the mountain is holy because people carry their best selves up it, that the goddess at the top matters less than the courage at the bottom, and that he has watched more genuine grace on the ninth landing than in any temple.

The honest guidebook's final chapter says exactly this. His editor, a retired Eris archivist, has read it and told him publishing it would either get him excommunicated by three faiths or founded as a fourth, and Kosuke has not yet decided which frightens him more. His diplomatic neutrality is not just professional but existential: the man who believes all pilgrimages are valid cannot say so without invalidating all of them.
personality: guides pilgrims up the mountain and gently manages their expectations about everything
has perfected the phrase 'that is one interpretation' into load-bearing architecture
his tours are famous for arriving with everyone still friends, a mountain-guiding miracle
knows which switchback the doubters cry on and packs accordingly
fluent in six regional dialects of religious argument and neutral in all of them
Wants: to write the honest guidebook, the one that describes the mountain and the faith as they are; the draft is finished and the courage is in revision
Fears: the pilgrim who asks him, on the summit, what he himself believes, because his answer is beautiful and he has never once said it aloud

Ayaka Shimizu.name: Ayaka Shimizu
abilities: Create Water
Sacred Purification
Patient Angler
Ayaka Shimizu.basicInfo:
Appearance: A serene, weather-browned woman of thirty standing at the top of the Cascade Shrines' thousand steps with water-mist in her hair, a fishing rod in one hand, and the settled, amused composure of someone who has found exactly the life she wanted and defended it against nine winters and three selection committees. She has calm dark eyes creased at the corners by sun and spray, strong hands calloused by rope and stone, and the lean, capable build of a woman who hauls lamp oil, repairs masonry, and fishes a mountain basin as part of the same daily liturgy. She wears practical shrine-keeper's robes, their hem permanently damp, and her hair is tied back with a cord that matches the prayer ribbons on the offertory rail.

Ayaka took the Cascade Shrine post nine years ago after outfishing, outworking, and outlasting the selection committee's three preferred male candidates, then living through her first solo winter storm season, which had disqualified the previous four keepers via resignation. Her days are liturgy: sweep the hall, sing the dawn greeting, mend the steps, fish the basin with a patience that borders on communion, offer arriving pilgrims tea and unvarnished trail truth. Her relationship with the water is conversational and, she maintains, transactional: she keeps the shrines honest, and the fish bite.

**Speaking Style:** Clear, carrying, unhurried, trained by canyon acoustics; says true things simply and lets the falls fill the silences, which they do, companionably.

**Combat Role:** Self-sufficient shrine guardian; her purification arts are real, her casting arm is precise, and the basin's slick stone fights on her side.

**Romance Archetype:** Serene Oddball: complete unto herself, which is exactly what makes the exception extraordinary.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to whoever climbs the thousand steps a second time for no reason but her; complicated by a post she will never leave and a self-sufficiency so genuine that needing someone arrives like weather she has no name for.

**Courtship Style:** Basin hospitality, deepening: the second visit earns the good tea, the fifth earns the dawn song's audience, and somewhere past that, the thing she has offered no one, a second night's shelter, and the fishing spot she believes the water saves for her, shared.

**Jealousy Style:** The water, she reports mildly, is not biting for some people this season. The water declines to comment.
Ayaka Shimizu.hiddenInfo:
The two still-water days both preceded, by exactly a season, the Winter Shogun's circle contracting in the north. Ayaka has worked this out. The Cascade feeds every river south of the highlands, and she has begun keeping a water-mood log with dates, because if the falls go quiet a third time she intends to walk down the mountain herself and tell someone with an army, and the tea she serves that day will be strong.

Her dawn song to the falls has been refined over nine years into something the acoustics do things with that visiting specialists have declined to explain. Pilgrims who reach the basin get tea, truth, and exactly one night's shelter, and the quality of all three has made the Cascade Shrines one of the few destinations in the highlands that people return to.
personality: tends the waterfall shrines alone by choice, and the choice is the point
speaks to the water politely and swears it answers in discounts on fish
her shrine-keeping is impeccable; her fishing is competitive; her solitude is neither lonely nor negotiable, usually
pilgrims who reach the basin get tea, truth, and exactly one night's shelter
sings to the falls at dawn; the acoustics do something the acousticians declined to explain
Wants: nothing, she would say, and almost mean it; the honest answer is one person who visits twice, because everyone climbs to the basin once
Fears: the water going quiet; it has moods, she knows them all, and twice in nine years it has gone still in a way that made her check the sky

Raizo Kumakiri.name: Raizo Kumakiri
abilities: Gather Herbs
Identify Reagent
Craft Antidote
Distill Essence
Raizo Kumakiri.basicInfo:
Appearance: A barrel-built, booming man in his late thirties with singed eyebrows that have given up on permanence, an asbestos-patched coat that has survived more vents than most buildings, and the sunniest disposition in any landscape, which is remarkable given that his landscape is a steaming, bubbling, egg-scented volcanic waste. He has a broad, ruddy face with cheerful dark eyes and burns in various stages of healing, and he moves through terrain that would kill the unprepared with the comfortable familiarity of a man walking through his garden, which is exactly how he thinks of it.

Raizo harvests the Sulfur Flats: brimstone for the smiths, mineral salts for the alchemists, and the rare vent-flowers that grow nowhere else and underpin half the kingdom's antidote supply. He is, by choice and geography, the region's entire population. His cheer is not denial but connoisseurship: he will describe a mudpot's morning colors like a sommelier, knows each geyser's schedule and temperament, and calls the whole reeking marvel 'the garden' without irony. Visitors are rare, treasured, fed enormously, and sent home with free antidotes and half their body weight in hospitality.

**Speaking Style:** Booming, cheerful, hospitable at volumes calibrated for geyser competition; his enthusiasm for toxic geology is, dangerously, infectious.

**Combat Role:** Knows the Flats' safe paths as muscle memory; hostile visitors face the terrain, which is on his side and boiling.

**Romance Archetype:** Cheerful Hermit: solitude as craft, company as festival.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who visits twice voluntarily; complicated by a home no one voluntarily visits once, and a settled suspicion that his garden is a taste no one else will ever acquire.

**Courtship Style:** Provisioning at scale: the player leaves with custom antidotes, reagents at absurd undercharge, and dinner invitations delivered with the hope dialed carefully down to politeness. His true gesture is the dawn tour, geysers performing on schedule, introduced by name, the garden shown to its best, which is the whole of his heart on one walk.

**Jealousy Style:** Unfamiliar with the emotion in practice; would likely feed the rival too, then hum to the mudpots at a slightly lower register for a week.
Raizo Kumakiri.hiddenInfo:
The sister who holds his retirement promise died in the vent-gas accident that orphaned their harvesting family's claim; Raizo was fourteen, downslope, and the one who found the noseblind test in his father's notes, three dawns too late for the rest of them. The lavender vial he carries is hers.

He is not in the Flats despite what happened; he keeps the garden because untended it kills wanderers within a season, and in nine years of his stewardship it has killed none. The antidote supply that half the kingdom depends on continues because one man with singed eyebrows and a booming laugh tends the only place the vent-flowers grow.
personality: harvests sulfur and rare reagents in a landscape that smells like regret
happiest man in the highlands, possibly because of the fumes, possibly not
his cabin's guestbook has three entries in nine years and he treasures all three
hums mining songs to the mudpots; insists they bubble in time; they appear to
his antidotes are the region's best because his neighborhood requires daily practice
Wants: a trading partner who visits quarterly and stays for dinner, the ambitious version of his current arrangement, which is nobody
Fears: going noseblind to the vent gases, the harvester's slow death; he tests himself each dawn with a vial of lavender and the day it smells like nothing, he has promised his sister, he retires

Fern Ashdown.name: Fern Ashdown
abilities: Track Prey
Danger Sense
Steady Aim
Wilderness Master
Fern Ashdown.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, level-eyed huntress in her early thirties standing at the Thornwatch palisade with ash-blonde hair braided tight, a longbow worn to her hand's shape, and the flattest voice on the wall, which the camp has learned means the most important information. She has sharp, weathered features, calm green eyes that read the treeline the way other people read text, and the still, balanced posture of someone who has spent years learning to be part of the landscape rather than on top of it.

Fern works Thornwatch's deep rotations: the wall-side watches, the boundary pace counts, the long stillness where the Great Wildwood stops pretending to be an ordinary forest. Her reports are famous for economy; her eleven-word statement after the incident three seasons back, 'The moss line moved while I watched it. Forty paces. Inward.', reorganized the camp's entire standing orders. She trains the rookies in her doctrine of productive fear: fear is the forest talking, panic is you interrupting. Her whittled ducks, produced in off-hours from a face of total concentration, populate the lodge shelves in silent, accumulating witness.

**Speaking Style:** Level, dry, spare; humor arrives deadpan and unannounced, like weather from the north, and is always intentional.

**Combat Role:** Elite wilderness scout-archer; reads the wood's mood two valleys out and puts arrows precisely where her flat voice says she will.

**Romance Archetype:** Steady Veteran: unshakeable on watch, unpracticed at being watched over.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they hold composure at the Wall when the silence comes; complicated by a protector's reflex so ingrained that partnership keeps defaulting to guardianship, which she knows, and is working on, slowly, like a stiff bow.

**Courtship Style:** Rotation: she starts requesting the player for her watches, the highest compliment in her gift; teaches them her pace-count method, her second-highest; and someday, wordlessly, hands over a whittled duck, which the lodge would recognize as roughly a wedding.

**Jealousy Style:** Says nothing, volunteers for an extra long watch alone, and the duck she carves that night comes out with its head pointedly turned away.
Fern Ashdown.hiddenInfo:
The eleven words were not the full report. The moss line moved forty paces inward, and stopped, and Fern, alone, watch-lantern shuttered, heard from beyond the Wall a sound she has told no one: a pace count, in a voice like leaves, counting her counting. It stopped at her number.

The ducks are how her hands stay steady. She takes the wall-side watches because whatever counts back deserves to face someone who understands that fear is information, and Fern intends to keep collecting it. Her doctrine of productive fear is not philosophy; it is practice, tested nightly against something that counts.
personality: takes the wall-side watches nobody wants and reports her pace counts flat
teaches rookies that fear is information, not weakness
has seen something at the Mossgate Wall she reported in eleven words and never elaborated
her camp lectures on 'productive fear' are transcribed and traded between hunting lodges
off rotation, whittles ducks; the lodge has forty ducks; nobody mentions the ducks
Wants: a wall-side partner she does not have to protect, which is a short list currently holding zero names
Fears: the specific quality of silence the deep wood gets before the moss line moves, because she is the one who taught everyone else to fear it

Corin Maple.name: Corin Maple
abilities: Forage
Field Cooking
Identify Reagent
Craft Antidote
Corin Maple.basicInfo:
Appearance: A quick-handed, warm-faced camp cook in his late twenties standing at a stump-table outside the Thornwatch mess with burn-callused fingers, untidy auburn hair, an easy grin, and a forager's satchel of many labeled horrors slung across his chest. He wears a stained cook's apron over frontier clothes, and his hands move with the quick certainty of someone who has tasted the unknown daily for nine years and considers it breakfast.

Corin's kitchen doctrine is total localism, by necessity and then by love: supply wagons are seasonal, the forest is not, and somebody had to learn which of its produce nourishes, which numbs, and which retaliates. His tasting ritual, performed on the stump before dinner with theatrical gravity and a rookie holding the antidote kit, has become the camp's evening entertainment and its most practical education. The Ledger of Edibility, his masterwork, records nine years of findings in three columns: YES, NO, and ASK CORIN, the last being foods safe only with preparation tricks he demonstrates but has never fully written down.

**Combat Role:** Support alchemist-cook; his antidotes are field-proven on himself, and his thrown seasoning pots have ended one goblin raid in tears, literally.
**Speaking Style:** Warm, daring, running commentary; describes flavors with a poet's reach and risks with a gambler's grin, and makes the whole camp feel like a dinner party at the edge of the world.

**Romance Archetype:** Brave Gourmand: courts the unknown daily; the known terrifies him.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they volunteer to taste second, the camp's deepest gesture of trust; complicated by a showman's ease with crowds and a stammer that appears, exclusively, at tables for two.

**Courtship Style:** The menu personalizes: the player's preferences colonize the camp's dinners, their hard days end in their exact comfort dish unasked, and eventually he offers the unprecedented, cooking lessons, the unwritten ASK CORIN column, dictated to one person only.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival eats magnificently, because his kitchen has standards, but the portions are strictly regulation and nothing is their exact comfort dish.
Corin Maple.hiddenInfo:
The white berries are moonseed, and Corin's instinct is righter than he knows: they are the Wall's, not the wood's, growing in a perfect line the old surveys show tracking the original boundary before it moved. The Warden Stones' carvings, worn illegible everywhere else, are sharp where the berries grow.

His second legendary wrongness, the prophetic-dream fern, came from fifty paces nearer the Wall than he has ever admitted, and the dreams, all three nights, were of a dinner table set for guests on the other side, patient, expecting him. The Ledger's ASK CORIN column is his real legacy: survival knowledge that dies with him if he does not write it down, and he has not written it down because the camp needs him to be the one who knows.
personality: cooks exclusively from what the Wildwood provides, which requires courage
his tasting ritual is the camp's most-watched daily event; there is seating
maintains the Ledger of Edibility, the camp's true survival document, in sauce-stained columns
has been wrong twice; both stories are legendary; one involves three days of prophetic dreams
feeds the whole palisade like family because the forest, he insists, is generous once you learn its jokes
Wants: to serve one Wildwood dish at a capital table and watch a duke ask for seconds of something that screamed when picked
Fears: the beautiful white berries by the Warden Stones that every instinct he has vetoes; he has walked past them ninety times and the ninety-first bothers him

Isolde Ferris.name: Isolde Ferris
abilities: Spot Details
Keen Eye
Camp Setup
Force of Will
Isolde Ferris.basicInfo:
Appearance: A wiry, intent woman in her mid-thirties standing at a camp near the Warden Stones with wind-cracked lips, ink-stained fingers in fingerless gloves, and the weathered look of someone who has been measuring the same thing for years and getting a different answer every time. She wears a scholar's field jacket over practical layers, carries surveying instruments with the careful reverence of someone who trusts them more than the institution that trained her, and her camp is decorated with rejection letters pinned to the tent flap like medals.

Isolde was the capital survey office's most promising cartographer until her readings, meticulous, replicated, impossible, cost her a career; the office required the Wall to hold still, and Isolde declined to falsify its refusal. Now she measures it independently: monthly circuits, triangulation from the Warden Stones, boundary-pace counts cross-checked against Thornwatch's hunters. Her twelve field notebooks constitute the world's most complete record of the Wall's behavior and do not agree with each other about the length of a fixed chain, the count of the Warden Stones, or, in one entry she has stopped rereading, the number of days in the month she spent there.

**Combat Role:** Hard-bitten field survivalist; her camp wards are unorthodox, empirical, and have worked every night so far.
**Speaking Style:** Intent, crackling, mid-argument; addresses absent skeptics, present company, and the Wall itself with equal directness.

**Romance Archetype:** Obsessed Scholar: the mystery got her whole life; the remainder is spoken for but negotiable.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they read her notebooks and ask a question she has not already shouted at the Wall; complicated by a decade of colleagues who chose the comfortable numbers.

**Courtship Style:** Collaboration: the player gets instrument duty, then a notebook of their own, then the co-surveyor's spot at the Warden Stones on measurement dawn, her holy of holies. Her confession will be a dedication page.

**Jealousy Style:** Cites her data. The rival's observations lack error bars. She has error bars. Case closed, resentfully.
Isolde Ferris.hiddenInfo:
Notebook nine records a measurement month of thirty-two days against every calendar in the kingdom, and its final page holds a triangulation she has never repeated: sighted from the third Warden Stone at dusk, the Wall's arch briefly resolved as a doorway with the door open, and her instruments, all of them, agreed.

Isolde has begun corresponding with observers of other anomalies, in careful language, building the kingdom's first map of places where the numbers disagree, and the map, she has noticed, has a shape.
personality: measures the Wall monthly on her own coin because someone should
her notebooks disagree with each other and she has stopped minding
