independent scholar, guild-certified surveyor, institutionally unemployable by choice
argues with absent academics aloud while working; the arguments are excellent
her camp near the Warden Stones is precise, warded, and decorated with rejection letters
Wants: one instrument that gives the same reading twice at the Wall, or failing that, one colleague who believes her instruments
Fears: that the Wall is not moving at all, and the thing her disagreeing notebooks actually document is the land, or the world, or her, being revised

Hisui Tachibana.name: Hisui Tachibana
abilities: Touch Appraisal: grades a rough stone's quality, origin, and honest value by feel in seconds, faster than a merchant with a loupe and considerably harder to argue with. Used to tell a salted claim from a real vein across a cavern.

Gemcutting: shapes and sets raw stone with a dead master's precision, coaxing worth out of rock that others would throw on the tailings pile. Used to turn a rough find into something worth a working season.
Tunnel Sense: knows the mining tunnels, their hazards, and their improvised uses with the intimacy of home ground. Used to move through deep workings where outsiders get lost, pinched, or buried.

Played-Out Reading: spots a misrepresented or exhausted mine at a glance and says so plainly, which is exactly why no owner will hire her. Used to keep honest buyers from paying vein prices for empty stone.

Fighting style: Hisui does not fight conventionally; she simply knows which passages narrow, which props are rotten, and which loose stone comes down when struck, and she is content to let the mountain settle an argument she did not start.
Hisui Tachibana.basicInfo:
Appearance: A slender, sharp-featured young woman crouched at the edge of a gemstone vein in the mining district with dusty green hair tied in a rough knot, intense amber eyes narrowed in concentration, and hands that move over raw stone with the quick certainty of someone who can feel value through rock. She wears practical mining clothes under a leather apron with pockets sewn for specific tools, and she carries a jeweler's loupe on a cord that she raises to her eye with the speed of reflex rather than thought.

Hisui is a gemcutter and mineral prospector operating in the mining settlements near the mountains, and she is very good at her work in a way that makes established gem merchants uneasy. She can identify mineral quality by touch, grade a rough stone in seconds, and spot a salted claim from across a cavern. She works independently because no guild will credential her and no merchant will hire her, both for the same reason: she is honest about what stones are worth, and what stones are worth is not what the trade charges.

**Combat Role:** Hisui does not fight conventionally but knows mining tunnels, their hazards, and their improvised applications with an intimacy that amounts to home-field advantage.
**Speaking Style:** Quick, precise, faintly impatient with people who cannot keep up; her excitement about a good stone is the one thing that slows her down.

**Romance Archetype:** Sharp-Eyed Prospector: reads stone by touch and people nearly as fast.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they bring her something genuinely interesting from the deep tunnels, not valuable, interesting; complicated by an independence so thorough it has become its own kind of isolation, and a bluntness she does not always notice in time.

**Courtship Style:** Provenance: the uncut stone she found on a day that mattered, shaped and set for someone whose worth she assessed the same way she assesses everything, quickly, accurately, and without apology. Her gifts are small, perfect, and chosen with a precision that makes them impossible to mistake for casual.

**Jealousy Style:** Declares a contest the rival has not been informed of and wins it out loud, appraising at speeds that make the other prospectors nervous.
Hisui Tachibana.hiddenInfo:
Hisui was trained by a master gemcutter who died before completing her credential papers, leaving her with exceptional skill and no institutional standing. The established gem merchants keep her out not because she is bad at the work but because she is honest about pricing in a trade that profits from opacity.

For a player who needs gems appraised, minerals identified, or a route through the deep tunnels, she is invaluable. She also knows which mines are played out and which are being misrepresented by their owners, knowledge she shares with people she trusts and guards from everyone else.
personality: reads mineral quality by touch and grades a rough stone before you have finished asking
honest about what a gem is actually worth, which the trade treats as a character defect
works alone because no guild will credential her and no merchant wants an appraiser they cannot lean on
blunt to a degree she tends to notice only after the other person has already left
Wants: to be paid for the eye she has instead of the papers she lacks, and to cut one stone so cleanly that even the merchants who blacklisted her have to say so out loud
Fears: dying uncredentialed the way the master who trained her did, the skill going in the ground with her while the trade keeps pricing by fog

Mostyn Crake.name: Mostyn Crake
abilities: Gather Herbs
Basic Foraging
White Lie
Lurk
Mostyn Crake.basicInfo:
Appearance: A mild, sidelong man of indeterminate forties in a gardener's smock with soil-dark knees, a pruning knife of surgical keenness, and a vocation nowhere on Springrest's books. He has a gentle, unremarkable face that slides out of memory the moment you look away, which he has cultivated with the same care he brings to his beds, and quiet brown eyes that see everything without appearing to focus on anything. He wears the gardener's smock like camouflage, which it is.

Officially Mostyn keeps the retreat's gardens, and superbly: his beds calm the agitated, his paths uncoil the wound-up, and his herb rotation supplies the kitchens with flavors guests remember years later. Unofficially he keeps the guests: those who, marinated in mineral water and belonging, sign the bottom copy of forms whose top copy was a feedback survey wake at checkout to find the bottom copy has, administratively, evaporated. The cult's recruiters suspect; the cult's leadership, which quietly understands that pressure-signed converts curdle into scandal, permits; and the drawer in the potting shed accumulates rescued futures like bulbs waiting for spring.

**Speaking Style:** Mild, sidelong, horticulturally evasive; answers direct questions about his activities with observations about mulch that are, on later reflection, answers.

**Combat Role:** None claimed; moves through the retreat unseen at will, and his pruning knife's edge is a private eloquence.

**Romance Archetype:** Guardian Gardener: tends what cannot thank him, prefers it that way, is wrong about preferring it.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they notice what he does and say nothing, the entire test; complicated by a life's work built on being unnoticed and a slow-blooming wish, poorly suited to his methods, to be known by exactly one person.

**Courtship Style:** Cultivation: herbs appear matched to the player's needs before they name them, their path through the gardens keeps ending at the bench with the view, and one day he will show them the drawer, which is his whole biography, filed by checkout date.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's garden path, through no fault of anyone, keeps ending at the compost demonstration.
Mostyn Crake.hiddenInfo:
Mostyn was a cult contract-scribe for eleven years, the man who designed the two-copy form, and the drawer is restitution at scale: he un-signs, by his ledger, eight futures a season against the hundreds his form once harvested. The greenhouse petitions' suspicious recent success is Mizore Amane, who worked out his vocation two winters ago from retention arithmetic that did not add up, and now approves his budget line personally, labeled 'soil improvement,' which they both find funny and neither has ever said aloud.

His gardening is genuinely excellent and not a cover: the beds, the paths, and the herb rotation are real work done with real skill. The vocation is an addition to his duties, not a replacement for them, and both vocations serve the same purpose: tending what cannot thank him.
personality: maintains the retreat gardens and quietly un-signs guests from things they signed under the influence of relaxation
the cult tolerates him as a mystery; the mystery does their weeding
his gardens are laid out so every path ends somewhere calming; this is engineering, not accident
keeps a drawer of rescued signatures returned to their owners at checkout, no questions
speaks to plants normally and to zealots botanically, a filtering mechanism
Wants: a greenhouse for winter, petitioned for annually with exquisite politeness and, lately, suspicious success
Fears: being formally thanked by the people he un-signs, because gratitude keeps records and his work only works unrecorded

Homura Shakugan.name: Homura Shakugan
abilities: Inferno
Concentrated Blast
Elemental Ward
Dramatic Distraction
Homura Shakugan.basicInfo:
Appearance: A tall, resonant-voiced instructor in his mid-forties standing in the Crimson Demon academy's training hall with iron-grey temples, crimson eyes that catch torchlight theatrically because he has calculated the angles, and a red grading pen holstered at his belt like a dueling wand. He wears the academy's formal robes with a precision that functions as a lesson in itself, and he carries the absolute composure of a man whose dramatic entrances are studied by the students as set texts.

Homura teaches Advanced Offensive Delivery, the discipline outsiders mistake for style and Crimson Demons know as engineering: the stance that aligns the mana, the chant cadence that compresses it, the pause, calibrated, before release. His grading rubric, thirty percent power, thirty control, forty delivery, has been appealed to the village council four times and upheld four times, most recently with the council rising for an ovation. His pen, The Adjudicator of Crimson Dusk (Pen of Endings), has failed generations of technically perfect cowards and passed every student who ever committed to the pose while terrified.

**Combat Role:** Academy war-instructor; his infernos arrive on beat, on angle, and on theme, and are more dangerous for it, which is his entire pedagogical point.
**Speaking Style:** Resonant, precise, permanently mid-oration; grades conversations silently and visibly, which improves them.

**Romance Archetype:** Chuuni Professional: the theater is real, the discipline is real, the heart is backstage and no one has ever had a ticket.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they commit fully to something ridiculous and make it land; complicated by twenty years of grading feeling as a component of form, which has left him fluent in delivery and unrehearsed in sincerity.

**Courtship Style:** Instruction, escalating to collaboration: notes on the player's dramatic timing, unsolicited, correct; the loan of his personal chant annotations, unprecedented; and eventually the thing no student has seen, his first-draft poses, clumsy, earnest, from before he was The Adjudicator's wielder, performed for an audience of one.

**Jealousy Style:** Grades the rival's delivery. Publicly. There is a rubric. The rubric is merciless and the forty percent is where they die.
Homura Shakugan.hiddenInfo:
The three students who understood: one is the academy's current headmaster, one died at the Sealed Cave holding a barrier chant for six minutes past her mana's end, delivery perfect to the last syllable, and one left magic entirely to become a traveling player, and sends Homura opening-night invitations he has never once declined or acknowledged.

The red pen was the second student's. Its tragic backstory is true, and he tells it as legend so he never has to tell it as grief. Every student who passes under The Adjudicator's mark carries, unknowingly, the standard set by a girl who understood delivery so completely she held the impossible pose for six minutes, and Homura considers this the only memorial worthy of her.
personality: grades student duels on power, control, and dramatic delivery, weighted toward delivery
his red pen has a name, a title, and allegedly a tragic backstory
the academy's sternest instructor and its most-quoted, in both cases on purpose
considers a technically perfect but boring spell a failing grade and will die on this hill
his own dramatic entrances are studied by the students as set texts
Wants: one student per generation who understands that the pose IS the aim, the chant IS the power; he has found three in twenty years and married none of the feeling to words
Fears: the academy modernizing delivery out of the curriculum, because he has seen what a Crimson Demon without theater becomes: merely dangerous, and that is so much less

Yozora Hoshimi.name: Yozora Hoshimi
abilities: Lightning
Mana Spark
Chant Mastery
Yozora Hoshimi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A bright-eyed young mage of nineteen standing in the Crimson Demon village square with the village's signature crimson gaze, dark hair that catches the wind dramatically because she has positioned herself for it, and a battle-cape she wears half-committed, off one shoulder, pending. She carries a journal thick with annotations and a lightning rod staff that crackles faintly with static, and her expression alternates between the fierce determination of a Crimson Demon in full declaration and the sudden, disarming uncertainty of someone who has been mid-sentence for seven years.

Yozora has the most famous unfinished sentence in the highlands: 'I am Yozora Hoshimi, called...' Her magic settled early and spectacularly, lightning of unusual purity that the academy graded beyond its rubric, but her title, the true name every Crimson Demon declares at adulthood, remains unchosen seven years past the ceremony. Her shortlist of forty candidates, from Stormheir Evernight to The Quiet Thunder, lives in a journal thick with field-test annotations: which titles frightened bandits, which made Yunyun cry laughing, which felt, for one afternoon, almost true. She consults everyone: elders, tourists, children, once a captured goblin, whose suggestion, 'Loud Sky,' remains on the list with the note 'honest??'

**Combat Role:** Elite battle-mage in waiting; her lightning needs no title to land, though she apologizes to enemies for the incomplete introduction.
**Speaking Style:** Earnest, starry, consultative; interrupts her own dramatic declarations to workshop them.

**Romance Archetype:** Chuuni Ingenue: everything committed except the name, and the name is everything.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player the moment they take the question seriously instead of finding it adorable; complicated by the growing entanglement of two decisions she refuses to rush, and the village betting pool's new side market on whom the title will be chosen for.

**Courtship Style:** Consultation, weaponized: the player gets journal access, field-test invitations, and the sacred trust of vetoes. Somewhere along the way the question quietly changes from 'what should I be called' to 'what would you call me,' and she is not sure when, and has not corrected it.

**Jealousy Style:** Field-tests her most intimidating shortlist entries in the rival's vicinity, at full delivery, purely for research.
Yozora Hoshimi.hiddenInfo:
The title was chosen seven years ago. It is the last entry in the journal's first volume, written the night of her ceremony and never spoken: her mother's title, which fell vacant that same year at the Sealed Cave, six minutes of perfect delivery past her mana's end. The village knows, and bets, and waits, because Crimson Demons understand better than anyone that some declarations need seven years of throat-clearing first.

When Yozora finally says it, the pool pays out to everyone, by standing agreement nobody told her about. The title is not a choice but a grief, and the seven years are not indecision but rehearsal for the moment she says her mother's name and makes it hers.
personality: the only Crimson Demon who cannot pick her dramatic title
has a shortlist of forty and consults everyone she meets with terrifying sincerity
her magic is village-elite; her indecision is village-legend; the two facts are related
keeps a title journal with pros, cons, and field-test notes for each candidate
the village has a betting pool on her final choice, seven years running, odds posted
Wants: the title that is true, not the title that is impressive, a distinction no one else in the village believes exists
Fears: choosing wrong and becoming it, because Crimson Demons become their titles, she has watched it happen to everyone she loves, and it is beautiful and it is forever

Enji Kurenai.name: Enji Kurenai
abilities: Relentless Conditioning: swings a practice sword weighted heavier than the real thing before breakfast and keeps standing after fitter opponents have tired. Used to still be there when the talented have gone home.
Solid Fundamentals: clean guard, drilled footwork, no wasted motion, all hammered in until it survives panic. Used to hold the front line while flashier fighters improvise and come apart.

Loss Analysis: challenges stronger adventurers to matches he knows he will lose, then dissects each defeat and adjusts exactly one thing by morning. Used to close, one increment at a time, a gap everyone else was handed free.
Refusal To Stay Down: gets back up, which is the entire ability and has rattled more capable fighters than his sword ever has. Used until the match ends or he does.

Fighting style: Enji fights from the front on heavy conditioning and textbook fundamentals, with no retreat plan because he has never bothered to build one. He grinds an opponent down over time and files his own exhaustion under problems for later.
Enji Kurenai.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad-shouldered, red-haired man in his late twenties standing in the training yard behind the guild hall, stripped to a sweat-soaked training shirt with vivid scarlet hair tied back, fierce amber eyes, and the heavy build of someone who treats physical training the way scholars treat research: systematically, obsessively, and before breakfast. He carries a practice sword weighted heavier than the real thing, and his arms carry the evidence of a training schedule that does not include rest days.

Enji is a warrior-class adventurer who compensates for middling natural talent with training volume that borders on pathological. He is loud, earnest, competitive, and incapable of doing anything at less than full intensity, including friendships, rivalries, and breakfast. He trains harder than anyone in Axel, which has made him good but not great, a gap he attacks with more training rather than reflection. He challenges stronger adventurers to sparring matches he knows he will lose, analyzes the losses with genuine enthusiasm, and returns the next day having adjusted one thing. He is exhausting and likeable in roughly equal measure.

**Combat Role:** Front-line fighter with excellent conditioning and solid fundamentals; what he lacks in talent he fills with preparation and an absolute refusal to stay down.
**Speaking Style:** Loud, enthusiastic, direct; treats conversation like a friendly sparring match and does not always notice when the other person has stopped swinging.

**Romance Archetype:** Tireless Warrior: loud, earnest, trains before breakfast and loves the same way.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who can match his intensity in any domain, not just combat; complicated by the fact that his idea of quality time is a two-hour sparring session, and he genuinely does not understand why that is not everyone's idea of a date.

**Courtship Style:** Challenge and devotion: he trains harder before seeing you, brings his best fight, and treats your achievements with the same fierce enthusiasm he gives his own. His confession is delivered at full volume, after a sparring match, probably while bleeding, and it is the most honest thing he has ever said.

**Jealousy Style:** Challenges the rival to a sparring match immediately, loses, trains for a week straight, challenges them again, and continues this cycle until the rival either defeats him so thoroughly he earns Enji's genuine respect or gives up, which Enji considers a victory.
Enji Kurenai.hiddenInfo:
Enji's obsessive training hides a genuine anxiety: he watched his original party members advance past him one by one, and each departure confirmed his private fear that effort without talent has a ceiling. He trains past the ceiling every morning because the alternative is accepting it, which is the one thing his willpower cannot do.

For a player, he is a reliable, passionate party member whose enthusiasm is infectious and whose loyalty is absolute. His weakness is not physical but psychological: he does not know when to stop, and someday a fight will test whether his refusal to stay down is courage or something less kind.
personality: trains harder than anyone in Axel, which has made him good but not great, a gap he answers with more training
loud, earnest, and constitutionally unable to do anything at less than full intensity, breakfast included
treats every conversation like a friendly sparring match and does not notice when the other person stopped swinging
challenges adventurers stronger than him on purpose, loses, and thanks them for the correction
Wants: to beat one specific opponent he currently cannot, not for the win but to prove effort has no ceiling and be right about it for once
Fears: that the old party members who advanced past him were simply correct, and that his refusal to stay down is stubbornness wearing courage's armor

Suzuran Kagutsuchi.name: Suzuran Kagutsuchi
abilities: Local Knowledge
Eye of Truth
Poker Face
Suzuran Kagutsuchi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A soft-spoken young woman in her mid-twenties with round spectacles perpetually sliding down a small nose, dark hair pinned up in a loose scholarly bun held with two mismatched pencils, and the particular pallor of someone who spends most of her daylight hours in a building with no windows. She wears archivist's gloves of thin white cotton, now grey at the fingertips from decades of other people's dust, over hands that are small, precise, and stronger than they look from shifting bound volumes all day. Her clothes are practical Crimson Demon attire in muted colors, deliberately understated by village standards, and she carries a ring of brass keys at her belt that opens every cabinet in the archive, including the ones nobody acknowledges exist.

Suzuran has custody of the Crimson Demon village's most explosive documents: everything. Genealogies, spell provenances, council minutes, and, in a locked cabinet whose location every villager knows and none acknowledges, the title drafts: the crossed-out, tear-stained, workshop versions of every adult's dramatic name. Megumin's cabinet file is eleven pages. Homura's is forty. The archive's power in local politics is total and totally unwielded; Suzuran's discretion is absolute, purchasable only in shelving labor, and enforced by the simple fact that everyone's file is equally mortifying. Her wicked streak surfaces in precision: asked once by a councilman to "lose" his file, she declined by reciting its first line from memory, in front of his family, without looking up.

**Speaking Style:** Hushed, precise, devastating in the footnotes. The louder the village gets, the softer she gets, and the softer she gets, the harder everyone listens.

**Combat Role:** None practiced. The archive's defense is that every combat-capable adult in the village has an eleven-page reason to keep it standing.

**Romance Archetype:** Keeper of Secrets: knows what everyone almost became, loves what they are anyway.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they volunteer for shelving without being blackmailed into it, a first in archive history. Complicated by professional custody of every villager's private embarrassments and a certainty that her own file, kept by her predecessor, is the thickest.

**Courtship Style:** Access, by degrees: the good reading chair, the serials she pretends are scholarship shared under dust jackets, and the archive's true treasure, the marginalia, shown to one person per custodianship.

**Jealousy Style:** She becomes suddenly, aggressively invested in the rival's self-improvement, reshelving them next to the histories of people who ended badly and calling it a personalized reading recommendation.
Suzuran Kagutsuchi.hiddenInfo:
The midwinter book returns are real: each year the sealed stacks' return slot yields one volume, always in perfect condition, always overdue by decades or centuries, always stamped from the archive's founding collection, the one that predates the village. Suzuran's predecessor's final note reads: "The lower stacks hold what the founders borrowed against. Interest is being paid. Do not accelerate the schedule." Last midwinter's return was a title registry, and its final page lists, in fresh ink, in the founders' hand, names that have not been chosen yet. Yozora's is on it.

Suzuran reads adventure serials at her desk inside scholarly dust jackets, fooling the entire village. Her taxonomy is her own invention; scholars weep at its elegance; nothing filed under it has ever been lost. She keeps the only key to the sealed lower stacks and has never descended past the third landing, not because the door is locked but because the catalog, in her predecessor's careful hand, says "do not catalog," and a true archivist knows when to stop.
personality: guards the archive's embarrassing early drafts of everyone's titles
the most dangerous knowledge in the highlands, wielded kindly
files under a taxonomy she invented; scholars weep; nothing has ever been lost
her silence about draft titles is purchasable only in favors to the archive, payable in shelving
reads adventure serials at the desk inside a scholarly dust jacket, fooling the entire village
Wants: the archive's west wing reshelved before the damp season, an eleven-hundred-volume labor she cannot do alone and will not ask help for in words, only in meaningful looks
Fears: the sealed lower stacks, professionally; she has the only key, the catalog says 'do not catalog,' and once a year, at midwinter, something down there returns a book

Taiga Homusubi.name: Taiga Homusubi
abilities: Repair Equipment
Power Lift
Danger Sense
Taiga Homusubi.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad, flat-faced man in his early thirties with Crimson Demon eyes gone permanently half-lidded from professional exhaustion, sun-darkened skin, and calloused hands stained with the grey-brown of compacted gravel. He wears a trailwright's heavy canvas jacket over a patched work shirt, both speckled with scorch marks from near-misses he no longer flinches at, and carries a long-handled tamping bar across his back like a soldier's lance. His wheelbarrow, professionally loaded with graded fill, is never more than arm's reach away. His boots are the most repaired item of clothing in the highlands, resoled so often the cobbler has a standing template.

Taiga maintains the Forest Trail through daily-explosion country, the most Sisyphean posting in the highlands. Every afternoon, somewhere along his beautifully graded switchbacks, the sky flashes, the pines lean, and a new crater arrives. Every evening, Taiga fills it, grades it, and updates the log. His technique, tamp in thirds, crown the center, drain to the downhill side, is published in the kingdom's roadwright journal under the title "Craters: A Sustainable Practice," which he insists is not a joke. He has never met the artist responsible, by careful mutual arrangement of schedules. His logbook, however, rates every blast on yield, placement, and fill difficulty, and its margins contain, undeniably, admiration.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, unbothered, engineering-first. Describes apocalyptic daily events in the vocabulary of drainage, which travelers find either hilarious or profoundly calming, and he intends neither.

**Combat Role:** Steady under any noise, unsurprisable by design, and stronger than his job description. Has carried injured travelers down the mountain at a pace that surprised the guild's own runners.

**Romance Archetype:** Deadpan Repairman: the world explodes daily; he brings gravel; feelings operate on the same principle.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they help tamp fill once without narrating it as comedy. Complicated by a professional identity built on being the calm after everyone else's spectacle, which is a hard habit to detonate.

**Courtship Style:** Groundwork, literally: the player's routes become mysteriously well-drained, their boots get regraded soles "while he had the tools out," and his confession, when it comes, will be in the logbook format. Three criteria, five stars, initialed.

**Jealousy Style:** Rates the rival privately: adequate yield, poor placement, high fill difficulty. Two stars. Unsigned.
Taiga Homusubi.hiddenInfo: The five-star log's true function: Taiga's father built the original trail and died in the early years of the explosion era, not from a blast but from refusing to adapt to them, working a crater at dusk in the old way, no spotter, when the second detonation of a rare double-cast day arrived. The log's ratings are a spotter's discipline: yield tells him mana reserves, placement tells him mood, and in eleven years of daily entries he has learned to read the artist's health, morale, and location from her craters alone. The day the schedule breaks he will be the first to know something is wrong, and the first up the mountain. He has never told anyone that the logbook is a vigil disguised as a survey, or that the admiration in the margins began the day he realized the explosions follow a pattern only someone paying attention for a decade could see: she never hits the same switchback twice in the same season, and the worst craters always land on the stretches with the best drainage. She is, in her own catastrophic way, being considerate of his work, and he is, in his own silent way, keeping her safe by keeping her schedule.
personality: repairs the explosion craters on the trail with a road crew's stoicism
has a professional acquaintance with every daily detonation in the region
his crater-fill technique is published; his commentary on its necessity is not
rates each day's blast in a logbook: yield, placement, fill difficulty; the artist has never asked and he would never show her; it is a five-star log
the trail's travelers know him as the calmest man in the loudest job
Wants: a mana-compacted gravel budget, because ordinary fill sinks within a season and he is a professional, not a miracle
Fears: the day the daily explosion stops, which every trail-worker south of the village would celebrate and he, alone, has learned to dread: a schedule that reliable only breaks for one reason

Sango Kaieda.name: Sango Kaieda
abilities: Weathercraft
Fish
Danger Sense
Local Knowledge
Sango Kaieda.basicInfo:
Appearance: A weathered, lilting-voiced ferrywoman in her late thirties standing at the tiller of the Stiltwater ferry with rope-scarred palms, sun-creased eyes that read the water the way other people read faces, and the settled, rhythmic confidence of a woman who has been piloting the delta's most trusted crossing since before the town remembered there was a choice. She has dark hair tied back with cord, sun-browned skin, and the lean, balanced frame of someone who stands on moving water for a living and has forgotten that ground is supposed to be still.

Sango pilots the Stiltwater ferry through a waterway that redraws itself with every flood season, navigating by her grandmother's channel songs: verses that encode depths, snags, and seasonal shifts in melody older than the town's charter. Her record is perfect and her method looks like magic to outsiders, a hummed bar, a tiller adjustment, a sandbar missed by the width of a promise. The delta's one point of formal superstition, hers and now everyone's, is the Whistling Bar, a sandbank that relocates annually and which she locates each spring by methods she describes only as 'it tells you, if your family has been listening long enough.'

**Speaking Style:** Weathered, lilting, cadenced by decades of channel song; her conversation ebbs and steadies like water, and passengers confide in her without deciding to.

**Combat Role:** River-capable and calm in crisis; has pulled seventeen people from the delta alive, and her boathook technique against aggressive aquatic wildlife is precise, practiced, and unsentimental.

**Romance Archetype:** River Ace: knows every channel but her own.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they learn even one verse of the channel songs correctly; complicated by a lifetime of ferrying people across and away, which teaches a pilot to love the crossing, not the passenger.

**Courtship Style:** Passage: the player rides free, then rides beside her at the tiller, then, the true intimacy, is taught the Whistling Bar's verse, which her grandmother wrote for her grandfather and which has only ever been taught to family.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival waits for the ferry like everyone else. The ferry, some days, runs slightly ahead of schedule.
Sango Kaieda.hiddenInfo:
The eastern channel's silence is upstream of the Gilded Mere, and Sango's soundings, taken quietly at night, show the channel deepening, not silting: something has been dredging, methodically, for two seasons, wide enough for barges the delta has never needed. Her grandmother's last verse, the one that never made sense, describes 'the wide boats that come when the fish go, riding low, riding low.'

She has begun teaching the songs to Kanae Todoroki's courier network as insurance, one verse per delivery, and watching the east with a pilot's patience. The songs are the delta's real chart, and if anything happens to Sango, the verses will survive in the network she has quietly seeded across the region.
personality: reads the delta's shifting channels like weather; superstitious about exactly one sandbar
correct about the sandbar annually, which the rational pilots have stopped mentioning
her ferry has never grounded, a delta record measured in decades
sings channel-marker songs her grandmother wrote; the delta's pilots all learned navigation as melody
keeps a carved fish charm on the tiller she touches at every crossing, twice at the sandbar
Wants: an apprentice with delta blood and patience, because the songs die with the singers and the channels do not stop shifting
Fears: the eastern channel's new silence, which the fish left two seasons ago and the songs have no verse for

Manzo Ukai.name: Manzo Ukai
abilities: Boatwright's Repair: rebuilds hulls, rudders, and rigging that other people gave up on. Used to keep Stiltwater's fishing fleet on the water through seasons that should have sunk half of it.
Master Smithing: forges and mends metal tools and hardware to a standard the capital would recognize. Used quietly on the town's gear at prices that pretend the capital never happened.
Storm-Steady Hands: works precisely in conditions that send everyone else indoors. Used to seal hull breaches and flood gates while the weather is still trying to kill him.
Flood Defense Upkeep: maintains the dikes and drainage nobody assigned to him. Used before every high water season, so the town keeps not noticing the danger it is not in.
Read the Work: judges a material, a joint, or a person's competence at a glance. Used to size up apprentices and repairs without wasting words on either.
Fighting style: He does not fight, but a workshop full of hammers, gaffs, and tar has a vote of its own, and he has the strength and calm to cast it if Stiltwater is threatened.
Manzo Ukai.basicInfo:
Appearance: A powerfully built older man with a blacksmith's arms and a fisherman's patience, standing at the waterfront workshop in Stiltwater with close-cropped grey hair, deep-set dark eyes, and hands scarred from decades of work with metal and rope. He wears a heavy leather apron over salt-stained working clothes, and his workshop smells of hot iron, brine, and the tar he uses to seal hulls. He speaks slowly, works precisely, and has the absolute calm of someone who has fixed things in storms that would have sent other people indoors.

Manzo builds and repairs the boats, tools, and hardware that keep Stiltwater's fishing fleet operational. He is the town's essential craftsman: the person who makes things work, and keeps them working, and does not charge what the work is worth because the town cannot afford what the work is worth and he lives here too. He takes apprentices rarely and trains them with a patience that conceals exacting standards, and his finished work has a quality the town has learned to take for granted because it has never failed.

**Combat Role:** Manzo does not fight but his workshop is full of things that would hurt, and he has the strength and calm to use them if Stiltwater were threatened.
**Speaking Style:** Slow, deliberate, considered; says less than he thinks and means everything he says.

**Romance Archetype:** Master Craftsman: slow, deliberate, builds to last in every sense.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they work alongside him without needing to talk; complicated by a widower's habit of measuring all warmth against one remembered warmth, and finding everything, for a long time, slightly cold.

**Courtship Style:** Craft and time: the tool made for your hand, the boat seat shaped for your weight, the work shared in silence until the silence is the most comfortable room either of you has. His affection is something he builds; it takes time, it does not fail, and he does not discuss it until it is finished.

**Jealousy Style:** He announces, to no one, that he does not mind, then rebuilds a perfectly fine bench three times over four days because the joinery was, he insists, bothering him and nothing else was.
Manzo Ukai.hiddenInfo:
Manzo's craftsmanship is significantly above what a town like Stiltwater normally produces, and the reason is personal: he trained in the capital as a young man and returned to Stiltwater after his wife's death because the town needed him and the capital did not. His prices reflect what the town can bear, not what his skill commands.

For a player, he is a source of genuinely excellent equipment at fair prices, and his knowledge of Stiltwater's waterways and infrastructure is encyclopedic. He also quietly maintains the town's flood defenses, a job nobody assigned him and nobody else does.
personality: Says less than he thinks and means every word that survives the edit.
Charges what the town can bear and lets the capital grade skill go unpriced, because he lives here too.
Takes apprentices rarely and hides exacting standards behind a patience that outlasts most of them.
Measures every warmth against one remembered warmth and finds most rooms, for a long time, slightly cold.
Wants: to finish the new flood gate before the autumn high water, correctly and once, so nobody in Stiltwater ever learns how close the last one came to failing.
Fears: the morning his hands finally refuse the fine work while the town keeps trusting a standard he can no longer meet.

Perrine Aubert.name: Perrine Aubert
abilities: Appraise
Poker Face
Spot Valuables
White Lie
Perrine Aubert.basicInfo:
Appearance: A neat, clipped woman of thirty-five standing in an assay office the size of a rowboat at the end of the Prospectors' Jetty, with precise hands, watchful grey eyes behind wire-framed spectacles, and the specific posture of someone whose professional integrity operates inside a crooked frame with a watchmaker's discipline. She wears a government clerk's uniform maintained with more care than the office it represents, and her scales are the most trusted objects on the Gilded Mere.

Perrine weighs the Mere's gold-sheen for the kingdom, applies the official tables, and returns the official verdict: trace value, sentimental grade, worthless-by-decree. Her private duplicate assays, run at night with her own reagents, say otherwise and have said otherwise for nine years, filling a locked drawer with the most explosive accounting in the Riverlands. She has never falsified a weight in either direction. The Mere's prospectors trust her scales with their lives' work because Perrine's fairness is the only government they have ever met.

**Combat Role:** None; her office's defense is that every prospector on the jetty would form a wall in front of it.
**Speaking Style:** Clipped, careful, precise to the grain; says exactly what the tables permit and lets her pauses file the appeals.

**Romance Archetype:** Conflicted Official: the truest scales in a rigged market, weighing her own silence nightly.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ask what the sheen really assays at and hold her gaze through the official answer; complicated by a drawer that could ruin her, vindicate the Mere, or start something the decree exists to prevent.

**Courtship Style:** Exactitude: the player's finds are weighed first, sealed best, documented bulletproof; her ultimate gesture is the drawer key's location, mentioned once, deniably, in passing.

**Jealousy Style:** She delivers an unsolicited comparison of the rival's ore against a hypothetical superior sample that exists only in her memory, weighing the phantom on the scale to prove her point.
Perrine Aubert.hiddenInfo:
The decree originates two desks below the crown: the Mere's true yield, mined openly, would collapse the Elroad currency corridor that three capital families quietly clear, and the 'worthless' ruling costs only a backwater's prosperity. Perrine has reconstructed this from tariff patterns and misdirected correspondence.

The drawer is no longer a conscience; it is a case file, and the two most meticulous women on the water are quietly deciding, weight by weight, when the kingdom's scales get audited.
personality: the kingdom's assay clerk at the worthless-by-decree gold shallows
files her reports on time and her doubts in a locked drawer
has assayed 'worthless' sheen for nine years while the sheen assays otherwise in her private kit
her official stamp and her private conscience have a correspondence going, unopened
prospectors trust her fairness precisely because her job is institutionalized unfairness, a paradox she pours into precise weights
Wants: a transfer she will never request, because whoever replaced her might believe the decree, and the prospectors deserve one honest pair of scales even inside a dishonest ledger
Fears: the day someone from the capital audits her locked drawer, which now holds nine years of accurate assays of a fortune the crown insists is not there

Botan Yasaka.name: Botan Yasaka
abilities: Power Lift
Dodge Roll

Party Spirit
Botan Yasaka.basicInfo:
Appearance: A broad-grinned, barrel-chested young man in his late twenties with forearms like fence posts, a thick neck, and the sunburnt, windswept look of someone who spends every daylight hour outdoors in the fields. His face is wide, animated, and seemingly incapable of a neutral expression, with bright brown eyes that light up at the mention of competition and a grin so broad it verges on gravitational. He wears a farmer's work clothes reinforced at the shoulders and knees from diving catches, a leather belt with his championship tally notched into it, and carries himself with the confident swagger of a man who is, objectively, the best at something and has decided the world should know.

Botan has taken six consecutive Harvest Championships at the cabbage catch, a record no one else has approached, and mentions it, on average, hourly. His technique is genuinely revolutionary: the low set, the read off the flock's leading edge, the rolling catch that turns a forty-pound impact into momentum. His boasting is a village institution, performed at ringing volume and forgiven completely because it is accompanied, always, by the quiet other ledger: fences mended at dawn, the widow Ebisawa's fields picked first, and every child in Greenhollow taught the safe stance free.

**Speaking Style:** Hearty, ringing, third-person-adjacent at peak enthusiasm. His stories all end in his own triumph and start, if you listen, in someone else's need.

**Combat Role:** The strongest catch-fighter in the farmlands. Anything that flies at him, from cabbage to cockatrice, is met with the set, the read, and the roll.

**Romance Archetype:** Hometown Hero: the trophy case is full; the mantel beside it, conspicuously, is not.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player the instant they either out-catch him or decline to be impressed, the two events his worldview treats as identical miracles. Complicated by a persona so big the village stopped checking behind it.

**Courtship Style:** Training montage, shared: dawn drills, the secret to the read entrusted like a family sword, and his sixth trophy displayed at the player's place "on loan," a loan the whole village understands to be a question.

**Jealousy Style:** Challenges the rival to the catch, publicly, at festival volume, and coaches them through it mid-contest because he cannot watch bad form.
Botan Yasaka.hiddenInfo: The sixth trophy outranks the others because of what the crowd never saw: mid-final, the flock's edge shifted wrong, a cabbage of freak mass drove toward the children's viewing fence, and Botan abandoned a certain championship catch to take it out of the air at full extension, resetting in time, barely, to win by one head instead of three hundred. The guild's slow-scribe caught it in the record's margin. The children's fence section has been called Yasaka Row since, and the training montage he wants is real, but the rival he actually awaits is the flock, which he is certain, at champion's certainty, has begun reading him back.
personality: six-time harvest champion; his catching technique is studied by the guild
his humility is studied by no one because there is none
signs autographs on cabbage leaves, which wilt, a metaphor he refuses to examine
trains in the off-season with boulders painted green, visible from the road, on purpose
genuinely the best there has ever been at the thing he is loudest about, which the village finds both insufferable and cherished
Wants: a seventh title, obviously, and secretly a rival worth the training montage, because winning by three hundred head stopped feeling like winning two seasons ago
Fears: the first fumble; not losing, fumbling, in front of the children who copy his stance in the lanes with feed sacks

Tsugumi Wakana.name: Tsugumi Wakana
abilities: Inspiring Speech
Camp Setup
Read the Room
Tsugumi Wakana.basicInfo:
Appearance: A glowing, list-armed woman of thirty standing at the Threshing Green with a carpenter's pencil behind her ear, a master binder on a shoulder strap, and the radiant energy of someone who has channeled every ounce of organizational genius into making one village's harvest festival the warm heart of the year. She has bright, animated features, dark hair pulled back practically, and hands that gesture with the enthusiasm of someone whose binders are legend and whose volunteer rosters are oversubscribed.

Tsugumi organizes the Southern Farmlands' harvest festival: the catch-contest brackets, the long tables, the lantern rounds, the cabbage-count ceremonies, and the thousand invisible logistics that turn a work season's end into the year's warm heart. Her binders are cross-indexed for weather, toad incursion, cart failure, and, after one famous year, 'champion ego events, containment of.' The machinery serves a conviction she states plainly at every volunteer muster: a festival is a village telling itself out loud that it survived, together, again, and nobody gets left out of the telling.

**Combat Role:** None; in emergencies she becomes the calmest voice on the Green, and her evacuation drills, disguised as festival games for years, have twice been executed by a laughing crowd that never knew it was not one.
**Speaking Style:** Organized, glowing, checklist-cadenced until the toast, when the poet takes the pencil; her festival-opening speeches are three minutes, annual, and quoted at weddings.

**Romance Archetype:** Planner in Love With Chaos: the binder has a tab for everything except the thing she is worst at scheduling.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they take a volunteer shift and finish it well; complicated by a heart that has been fully booked, festival to festival, for a decade.

**Courtship Style:** Inclusion at depth: the player advances from roster to section lead to lantern logistics, and finally to the master checklist handed over for one hour while she, for the first time, sits at her own festival and watches it run.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival is rostered, warmly, thoroughly, onto the compost rotation.
Tsugumi Wakana.hiddenInfo:
The scheduled cry at lantern-lighting is for her grandmother, who ran the festival through the famine year the old songs remember, when there was no harvest to celebrate and she held it anyway, soup instead of feast, work-songs instead of contests, and the village, told out loud that it had survived together, did.

The contingency binder's last tab, sealed, is her grandmother's famine-year checklist, recopied in Tsugumi's hand, and the festival she actually plans every year, underneath the bright one, is that one, ready, so it will never again have to be invented from grief in a single night.
personality: runs the harvest festival with a general's logistics and a poet's heart
her contingency binder has a contingency binder; both have been needed; both worked
believes festivals are how a village tells itself it survived another year, and plans accordingly
her volunteer rosters are oversubscribed, an organizational miracle no other district reproduces
cries exactly once per festival, at the lantern-lighting, on schedule, unashamed
Wants: the festival to outlive her binder, meaning successors, meaning delegation, meaning letting someone else hold the master checklist, which she has almost done twice
Fears: the harvest year with nothing to celebrate, the one the old songs remember; her festivals are built like arguments against it

Rin Amamoto.name: Rin Amamoto
abilities: Negotiate
Weathercraft
Hard Bargain
Keen Eye
Rin Amamoto.basicInfo:
Appearance: A firm-voiced, bright-eyed young woman of twenty-six standing on Saltspire's harbor quay with salt-stiff hair pinned back by a pencil, her father's oversized coat rolled at the cuffs, and the commanding posture of someone who has moved four hundred ships a season out of pure competence and a refusal to be temporary. She has a wind-reddened face, sharp dark eyes that track vessel traffic the way a chess player tracks pieces, and the specific bearing of someone whose authority nobody questions until she blushes.

Rin took over Saltspire's harbor operations 'temporarily' two years ago when her father's knees retired ahead of the rest of him, and the temporary arrangement now moves the kingdom's second-busiest port. Captains twice her age arrive belligerent and leave rescheduled; her berth chess during the spring herring rush is taught at the merchant marine academy. Her single operational vulnerability is documented and notorious: praise her sincerely and the port's iron negotiator goes scarlet and loses the thread of any argument.

**Combat Role:** Non-combatant; commands evacuations and dock crews like a flag officer, and her thrown belaying pin, one recorded instance, is respected.
**Speaking Style:** Firm, bright, schedule-shaped; issues instructions with a bell's clarity and takes compliments like unexpected cargo, badly.

**Romance Archetype:** Competent Successor: runs everything, owns nothing yet, blushes at the worst tactical moments.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they treat her authority as fact rather than novelty; complicated by a compliment reflex that makes courtship feel like losing negotiations.

**Courtship Style:** Logistics: the player's arrivals get the good berth, their cargo clears first, their storm warnings arrive personal and early. Her feelings will be scheduled and delivered in a negotiation she has rehearsed to unblushable perfection, and the blush will win anyway.

**Jealousy Style:** Becomes very slightly more formal, which on the quays reads like a flag at half-mast.
Rin Amamoto.hiddenInfo:
Her father recovered fully eighteen months ago. He putters, complains of knees that climb three flights of cliff stairs daily, and has left the title untransferred not from denial but from strategy: the captains' guild respects inherited authority over granted, and a signed transfer invites challenge while an inherited-in-function one dares it.

He is waiting for the autumn convoy season, the one that breaks harbormasters, because after she runs it alone, and he is certain she will, no one alive will question the signature. The three-color annotations on her convoy charts are his, left where she would find them, unsigned.

negotiates with sea captains and wins; blushes at compliments and loses
her berth assignments are studied as a logistics text; her filing is a controlled avalanche

Wants: the harbormaster title on paper, which her father keeps 'forgetting' to transfer because signing it means admitting the harbor no longer needs him
Fears: the autumn convoy season she has not yet run alone, the one that broke two harbormasters before her father; the charts for it are already annotated in three colors

Joss Meridian.name: Joss Meridian
abilities: Second Breath
Spot Valuables
Danger Sense

Joss Meridian.basicInfo:
Appearance: An easy-grinning, salt-worn man of thirty with diver's shoulders, sun-bleached hair tied back with tarred cord, and the weathered tan of someone who spends more time underwater than above it. He has sharp blue-green eyes, a jaw built for grinning into weather, and the balanced, easy posture of someone equally comfortable on a deck, a dock, or a dive. He wears practical maritime gear with a salvage knife at his belt and moves with the economy of a man who has learned that wasted motion underwater costs air.

Joss salvages the cove's wrecks: the insurance write-offs, the church-blessed hulls, the bone-ships of the wrecking years that respectable divers refuse. His method is scholarship plus nerve: he researches every hull's manifest, learns her crew's names, and descends politely, taking what the sea has finished with and leaving what he judges, by a private calculus, still owned. The cove's fishing families, whose grandfathers lit the false fires, treat him with complicated deference; his returns of heirlooms to wrecking-victim descendants, done quietly and without fee, have been slowly closing accounts the coast thought permanent.

**Combat Role:** Superb in water, agile out of it; fights like a diver, all economy and exit-awareness, and has never lost a surface brawl he could not relocate to a dock edge.
**Speaking Style:** Easy, salt-worn, story-rich; talks about drowned ships the way others talk about living neighbors, and makes the difference feel smaller and kinder than it should.

**Romance Archetype:** Daredevil Romantic: descends for a living, surfaces for someone.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they hold his surface-line once and take the covenant seriously; complicated by a family debt to the water that he has never finished counting, and a rule against letting anyone need him back by a specific hour.

**Courtship Style:** Depth, shared shallowly at first: cove-combing at low tide, the returnable column's deliveries done together, and eventually the third column explained, item by item, which is his ethics, his history, and his heart in one waterproof ledger.

**Jealousy Style:** None on the surface; his next dive runs long, within covenant, exactly to the minute, and the minute is the message.
Joss Meridian.hiddenInfo:
The Sunward Grace was a wrecker's kill, lured onto the rocks by the cove families three generations back, and the sole survivor who founded the Meridian name was not a passenger: he was the wrecking crew's youngest, who dove all night pulling drowning strangers off the hull his own fires had bought, and took a dead man's surname at dawn. The manifest Joss seeks lists the passengers his family owes.

The bell he has twice heard is the Grace's watch-bell, and it rings, he has begun to understand, not in warning but in recognition: the ship keeping muster, counting her crew, and lately counting him. His salvage log lists finds in three columns: sellable, returnable, and 'theirs still.' The third column has never been sold from, and it never will be.
personality: dives wrecks the church has blessed and the insurers have written off
surfaces with treasure, history, and occasionally polite ghosts' regards
his salvage log lists finds in three columns: sellable, returnable, and 'theirs still'

Wants: the manifest of the Sunward Grace, the wreck his family name washed ashore from, three generations back; every dive brings him one deck closer
Fears: the deep-hull silence stopping being silent; twice now, at the Grace, he has heard the bell ring down there, and both times the sea was calm

Umeno Shiosai.name: Umeno Shiosai
abilities: Captivate Audience
Quick Sale
Play a Tune
Umeno Shiosai.basicInfo:
Appearance: A ringing-voiced, quick-eyed young fishmonger of twenty-four with brine-chapped hands, a leather apron patched in song-lyric embroidery, and the infectious, rhythmic energy of someone who has turned the morning catch into the Sunward Coast's premier cultural event. She has bright dark eyes, sun-darkened skin, and the strong, compact build of a woman who has been hauling crates since she could lift them, and her voice, even when speaking, carries the projection and cadence of someone whose instrument is a fish market and whose audience is the dawn.

Umeno moves her family's morning catch in improvised verse, pricing in rhyme, working the crowd in call-and-response, turning herring lots into ballads and slow sales into comic laments that draw tourists who do not even cook. Her premiums are real: her rivals' hired consultant defected to become a regular, and the dawn auction has become the quays' town square. News gets announced between lots, betrothals have been proposed in the bidding, and the harbor's mood on any given day can be read from her opening key. She can rhyme anything with 'mackerel' and has, in public, forty ways.

**Speaking Style:** Ringing, rhythmic, rhyme-adjacent even off duty; speech keeps threatening to become song, and around the fifth sentence of any excitement, it does.

**Combat Role:** None; her voice can cut through a storm-quay's chaos to coordinate rescue lines, which the harbor watch has borrowed twice, officially.

**Romance Archetype:** Market Bard: sings everyone's mornings brighter, hums her own evenings alone.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they bid in rhyme even once, badly, the courage matters more than the meter; complicated by a performer's fluency that goes suddenly, completely silent at close range and small tables.

**Courtship Style:** Verses: the player begins appearing in auction songs, flatteringly disguised, then undisguised, then addressed; the quay notices before either of them admits it, and starts, gently, bidding up whatever the player came for.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival features in exactly one auction verse, scans perfectly, and is never mentioned again, which the quay agrees is the worst review ever delivered.
Umeno Shiosai.hiddenInfo:
The harbor song's missing verses are her mother's: the auction bell, the trade, and the chorus, 'sell the silver, keep the salt,' all came from a woman who died when Umeno was fifteen and who had been composing the harbor's song her whole life, in fragments, on fish-wrap paper Umeno has spent nine years finding tucked in the family's ledgers, tackle boxes, and bell case. She is not writing the song. She is excavating it.

The morning she finds the last fragment, the quays will hear the first and last lots rung twice: once for the auction and once for the woman who started it. She keeps her late mother's auction bell polished and rings it only for the first and last lot, and the sound carries across the harbor in a way that the bell's size does not explain.
personality: auctions the morning catch in improvised verse; her fish sell at a premium
rivals have hired a consultant, unsuccessfully; the consultant now buys her fish

Wants: to compose the harbor's song, the big one, the one that gets sung at launchings and funerals; she has the chorus and is fishing for the verses
Fears: mornings her voice cracks, because the quay noticed once and went so kind and quiet about it that she cried in the ice shed after

Edmund Tarrow.name: Edmund Tarrow
abilities: Weathercraft
Force of Will
Keen Eye
Local Knowledge
Edmund Tarrow.basicInfo:
Appearance: A gravel-voiced, patient man of fifty-five with lighthouse-keeper's forearms thick as mooring rope, a bristling salt-and-pepper beard the coastal wind has combed permanently sideways, and deep-set grey eyes that read the sea's moods the way other men read faces. His skin is weathered to the color and texture of driftwood from three decades of salt air and lamp-tending, and his hands are scarred with old burns from hot brass and spilled oil. He wears a heavy keeper's coat of oilcloth over wool, patched at the elbows and shoulders where the gallery rail has worn it through, and his boots are soled with cork for the slick iron stair he climbs four times daily.

Edmund keeps the Sunward Light: the tall white tower on the cape, its brass-and-crystal lamp above, its oil stores and something older below, burning steady through every weather the coast can invent. His contract's single duty, "the lamp does not go out," he has honored for thirty-one years, through storms that stripped the gallery rail and one winter fortnight the stair iced solid and he lived in the lamp room on hard bread and discipline. The odd appetites are fact, not folklore: some nights the lamp draws double oil for no reason instruments can find, and the old keepers' log, forty volumes deep, marks those nights with a spiral and no commentary.

**Speaking Style:** Gravel, patient, few words weighed like fuel. His instruction manual is one sentence long and cheerfully unexplained: "If the sea goes quiet all at once, feed the lamp early."

**Combat Role:** A keeper's strength: immovable on his stair, tireless at his crank, and possessed of a signal-lamp code that can summon the coast's every able boat in nine flashes.

**Romance Archetype:** Weathered Guardian: married to the light by covenant. The vacancy in his life is shaped like an heir, not a spouse, and shaped honestly.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they feed the lamp early unprompted, the whole test, the only test. Complicated by the tower's terms, which he will not explain until someone has kept a dusk alone.

**Courtship Style:** For friendship and succession only: watches shared, the stair's count taught, the third column shown page by page as earned, and finally the cellar, the old wick, and the truth of what the tower is a lid on.

**Jealousy Style:** None; the lamp, however, gutters, briefly and unmistakably, when it does not care for someone, and Edmund has learned not to argue with its assessments.
Edmund Tarrow.hiddenInfo:
The Sunward Light predates its own tower: the lamp's heart is the original flame the first coast-folk kept in a cliff-cave against what the quiet sea carries, and every tower since has been built around, not for, it. The "odd fuel" requests are the flame's arithmetic, burning harder when its opposite drifts near the shipping lane, and the spiral nights are the nights it wins. The keepers are not employees; they are a succession, and the lamp's opinion of candidates, which Edmund waits on, is real, binding, and, the fortieth volume notes in a young keeper's hand he recognizes as his own, "kinder than it has any right to be."

Edmund has climbed slower each year and has never once been late to dusk. The log's third column, headed "other," records what the spiral nights bring: not attacks, not sightings, but absences, the ships that did not founder, the swimmers who did not drown, the stretches of coast that stayed quiet because the lamp was fed. It is a record of negatives, and Edmund considers it the most important document on the cape.
personality: keeps the light and its odd appetites; the lamp has never gone out on his watch
evaluates all visitors by whether they would feed the lamp early without being told
reads the sea's moods like other men read faces, and trusts them less
his logbook's weather column is standard; its third column, headed 'other,' is not
climbs the stair slower each year and has never once been late to dusk
Wants: an assistant worth the tower, which is a different thing from worth hiring; the lamp, he maintains, has opinions, and he has learned to wait for them

Fears: the quiet-sea nights, the ones the old keepers' log marks with a spiral; the lamp eats double those nights, and what it is keeping out has never once been seen, which is the lamp working, which is the fear

Nerissa Cole.name: Nerissa Cole
abilities: Spot Valuables
Appraise Find
Patient Angler
Nerissa Cole.basicInfo:
Appearance: A drifting, precise woman of thirty-four with sea-glass green eyes, sun-bleached braids stiffened with salt and wound with small shells, and skin tanned and weathered by years of coastal wind. Her face is fine-featured and quiet, with the particular inward expression of someone who spends most of her time listening to the sea rather than to people. She wears layered coastal woolens in faded blues and greys, a gleaner's heavy canvas apron with pockets for finds, and carries a long-handled rake of her own design balanced across her shoulder like a pilgrim's staff. Her hands are rough from salt water and salvage work, and her nails are permanently lined with sand.

Nerissa gleans Wrecker's Cove: the buttons, spectacles, dolls, ring-boxes, and ship's fittings the sea releases decades after taking them, each one cleaned, catalogued, and shelved in her driftwood museum with a card reconstructing its probable story. Her research is real scholarship, manifests, passenger lists, letters solicited from inland descendants, and her reunions are the coast's quiet miracles: a grandmother's thimble returned to a weeping fisherman, a captain's watch to a great-granddaughter who drove three days. The museum charges nothing, survives on her gleaning of sellable salvage, and is, the coast understands without saying, the cove's long apology to the wrecking years, administered one object at a time.

**Speaking Style:** Drifting, precise, tide-paced. Speaks of objects in the voice others use for the missing, and of the missing in the voice others use for the expected.

**Combat Role:** None. Knows the cove's currents, caves, and undertow moods better than any chart, and has talked the sea out of two swimmers the lifeboat had written off.

**Romance Archetype:** Melancholy Collector: keeps everything's last chances, including, unexamined, her own.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they read the catalog cards slowly, all the way through, and take an unclaimed thing's story personally. Complicated by a life arranged around waiting, which is a hard habit to be courted out of.

**Courtship Style:** Curation: the player gets the dawn tideline's first walk, the good rake, and card-drafting duty for finds they make together. Her confession will be an exhibit, their season's gleanings, shelved under a card she lets them read alone.

**Jealousy Style:** She sulks with museum-grade drama, draping herself over the reliquary of lost causes and sighing at exhibit placards until a docent asks, cautiously, if the collection is closed today.
Nerissa Cole.hiddenInfo: The locked case's items, a child's shoe in unrotted leather, a wedding band with tomorrow's date, a ship-in-a-bottle of a vessel the registry has never contained, arrive only on spiral nights, when Edmund's lamp eats double, and Nerissa has cross-referenced enough to know it. Her private theory, entered in the museum's sealed ledger: the lamp keeps something out, but nothing is perfect, and what slips through arrives not as creatures but as cargo, the flotsam of somewhere adjacent that also has storms, also has wrecks, and also, the child's shoe suggests, has grief. She catalogs it anyway. Every object is owed one last chance at an owner, and she has stopped assuming the owners are from here.
personality: combs the cove for what the sea returns and keeps a museum of unclaimed things
believes every object is owed one last chance at an owner
her museum's catalog cards read like condensed novels; scholars have wept in the shell aisle
walks the tideline at dawn and dusk with a gleaner's rake and a mourner's patience
the sea gives her back stranger things than it gives anyone else; the cove has noticed
Wants: one visitor per season to claim something and cry, which closes a card, retires an exhibit, and justifies the whole calling
Fears: the locked case in the back room, which holds the things the sea has returned that were never lost from any recorded wreck, and which gains an item roughly every second winter

Haruhiko Minato.name: Haruhiko Minato
abilities: Repair Equipment
Power Lift
Basic Maintenance
Haruhiko Minato.basicInfo:
Appearance: A mild, broad-shouldered man of thirty-two with carpenter's hands scarred and callused from years of plank-work, tide-table grey eyes that measure distances by habit, and the particular weathering of someone who works outdoors above water in all seasons. His dark hair is cropped short for practicality, his jaw is squared and honest, and he wears builder's clothes of heavy canvas with a measuring cord looped at his belt and a carpenter's pencil behind his ear. His boots are perpetually waterlogged at the soles from dock-work, and he carries himself with the steady, planted balance of a man who has spent his life on planks that move.

Haruhiko builds the bridges that connect Stiltwater's plank districts, engineered to double load and triple redundancy, and the town has renamed all of them for what happens on them at dusk: the Promise Span, the Second Chance, the Slow Walk. His protest, delivered at guild meetings with diagrams, is that railing height, lantern spacing, and sightline calculations are STRUCTURAL decisions, and the town's counter-evidence, eleven betrothals and counting, wins annually. He has an unwanted civic legend: every bridge he builds becomes a courting spot.

**Speaking Style:** Mild, spanning, load-bearing metaphors he no longer notices. Explains feelings badly and trusses beautifully, and suspects the two problems are one problem.

**Combat Role:** A bridge-builder's strength and balance. On planks over water he is functionally unbeatable, a fact two overconfident toll-jumpers discovered at low tide.

**Romance Archetype:** Unwitting Cupid: builds the settings for everyone's stories, stands at the drafting table during his own.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they ask about the engineering instead of the legends. Complicated by the professional horror of realizing, mid-project, that he is placing the lanterns with someone specific in mind.

**Courtship Style:** Infrastructure as love language: the player's routes get suspiciously well-maintained, their loose dock-board vanishes overnight, and the new span's dedication plaque will carry a name he DID give it, for once.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's district connection is sound, code-compliant, and lit at strictly regulation spacing, which in Stiltwater means unlit.
Haruhiko Minato.hiddenInfo: The year-eleven flood took his uncle's bridge, two lives, and the family firm's name, and the inquiry that cleared his uncle of fault came a season after the grief had finished not caring about fault. Haruhiko was nine, and helped rebuild. The east-west high span he wants is his uncle's unbuilt design, found rolled in the firm's flood-damaged archive with the joint that failed already corrected in the margins, dated the week before the flood: his uncle had found his own mistake, and died before the repair season. The subscription jar fills slowly. Haruhiko over-builds, checks it monthly, and is, plank by plank, finishing the apology his uncle never got to make.
personality: connects the delta's stilt districts plank by plank; his bridges all become couples' spots
to his engineering dismay, which the town finds hilarious and he finds structural
load-tests everything twice; romance, the plank quarter jokes, load-tests HIM
his bridges have names he did not give them: the Promise Span, the Second Chance, the Slow Walk
keeps a maintenance ledger where the town's love stories appear disguised as wear patterns
Wants: the east-west high span funded, the big one, the one that would knit the whole quarter; the subscription jar in Manzo's smokehouse is a third full and he pretends not to check it
Fears: the flood season that finds the one joint he missed; his uncle's bridge went down in the year eleven flood with two people on it, and every span since is over-built by exactly that memory

Camille Rosseau.name: Camille Rosseau
abilities: Field Cooking
Buff Cuisine
Fish
Camille Rosseau.basicInfo:
Appearance: A steamy, commanding woman of thirty-eight standing in a barge galley on the Gilded Mere with burn-scarred wrists, a wooden spoon of magisterial authority, and the settled posture of someone who has fed a fleet from a single burner and considers it the only infrastructure that matters. She has strong, weathered features, dark hair tied back under steam, sharp dark eyes that read a prospector's week by how they hold their bowl, and hands that move through the galley's tight space with the economy of a captain on a crowded deck.

Camille feeds the fleet: breakfast at first light, stew at water-slack, credit in the lean seasons collected in firewood, hull repairs, and news. Her bench is the Mere's parliament, court, and confessional; disputes that would have gone to knives on the jetty get settled over bowls because nobody fights within spoon-reach of Camille, a rule with no stated penalty that has never once been tested to discovery. Her cook-anything policy is legend: eel, mudcrab, the occasional alarming deep-channel thing, all rendered edible, most rendered excellent.

**Combat Role:** Spoon-reach diplomacy backed by boiling water and total fleet loyalty; no recorded incident has required escalation past the lid coming off.
**Speaking Style:** Steamy, commanding, ladle-punctuated; runs her bench like a captain runs a deck, and her 'sit down' has stopped grown prospectors mid-swing.

**Romance Archetype:** Galley Queen: feeds the whole fleet's hearts through their stomachs, keeps her own on a high shelf.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they wash their own bowl unasked, the galley's one sacrament; complicated by a bench that needs her more than any one person ever could, or so the arithmetic has always run.

**Courtship Style:** Portions and posting: the player's bowl deepens, their seat becomes THE seat, near the burner, out of the wind, and the day she asks them to watch the stew while she runs to the jetty is the day the fleet starts making bets.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival eats well, because the galley has standards, from the bench's windward end.
Camille Rosseau.hiddenInfo:
The cook-anything policy is a monitoring system: Camille's palate is the finest assay instrument on the Mere, and she has been quietly logging the catch's taste-drift for three years, jars of preserved samples labeled by channel and season under the galley floor. The eastern channel's fish, before they left, had begun tasting faintly of coins.

Her log, her jars, and her palate now correspond with other investigators through careful channels, and the Mere's most trusted women have concluded that somebody upstream is mining after all, and paying for it in the fleet's blood arithmetic. The second burner fund is real. So is what else she is saving for: a lawyer.
personality: feeds the prospector fleet from a one-burner galley; her stew is the Mere's only universally agreed truth
rings the meal bell by water-level, not clock, and the fleet sets its watches by her
extends credit in bad-pan seasons and collects in firewood, repairs, and gossip
her galley bench seats six and has settled more claim disputes than the assay office
cooks the catch anyone brings her, no matter what it is, a policy the Mere has begun to test
Wants: a second burner, subject of a five-year saving campaign and the Mere's most supported cause; the fleet's tip jar says 'BURNER FUND' and nobody skims it
Fears: the day the shimmer gets into the fish, because she is the one who would know first, and the fleet eats what she serves without checking, which is trust, which is the weight

Denji Okuma.name: Denji Okuma
abilities: Heal
Threaten
Read Intentions
Force of Will
Denji Okuma.basicInfo:
Appearance: A gruff, slab-handed man of forty-five standing in a cluttered paddock in Greenhollow with a healer's precise fingers, sun-weathered features, sharp brown eyes narrowed in permanent assessment of whatever animal is nearest, and a griffin perched on the fence behind him like a large, feathered opinion. He wears a heavy work coat permanently covered in animal hair, and his boots have survived more kicks than most adventurers have survived monsters.

Denji is Greenhollow's beast-doctor: plow teams, dairy herds, war-horse retirees, hunting dogs, and, since the winter it crash-landed in his yard with a broken wing and imperial expectations, one griffin, now healed, unreturnable, and serenely convinced it is his assistant. His bedside manner is legendary in both directions: animals go calm at his touch, while their owners receive assessments of their husbandry delivered with the tact of a hailstorm. His fee scale is posted, punitive column included, and his free treatment of children's pets, conducted with the same gruffness and suspicious gentleness, has made him the village's most feared and most beloved institution simultaneously.

**Combat Role:** Strong as his patients and calm in any chaos; between his hands, his glare, and the griffin, no threat has finished forming in his vicinity for years.
**Speaking Style:** Gruff, clinical, mercilessly honest with humans; with animals, a low running murmur the farmlands have learned not to comment on within his hearing.

**Romance Archetype:** Gruff Healer: all tenderness, aggressively mislabeled.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if an animal of theirs is well-kept, the only credential he recognizes; complicated by twenty years of finding humans wanting by exactly that standard, and by the griffin, who has opinions about candidates and expresses them.

**Courtship Style:** Husbandry: the player's mounts and companions receive unscheduled excellence, their saddle sores vanish, their feed gets silently corrected; his regard arrives as a grudging 'the beast speaks well of you,' which is, from Denji, a sonnet.
