**Combat Role:** Hard-country capable: pick, pry-bar, and a thrown hammer that has discouraged claim-jumpers at range. Steadier in the Vale's wrong-angled silence than anyone the guild has posted before her.

**Romance Archetype:** Torn Official: the stamp is the guild's, the doubts are hers, the wall of fitted shapes is nobody's business, yet.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they surrender a find honestly when hiding it would have paid. Complicated by six years of professional silence that has calcified into a habit of filing her whole self under seal.

**Courtship Style:** Assessment: the player's finds get her actual eye, their pitch gets the survivable grid squares, and her trust arrives in documents, first the actual records, then the wall, shown by lamplight with the door barred.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's finds are graded with reference exactness and stamped with the guild's full authority, and none of them, somehow, are ever quite PROMISING.
Signy Marrow.hiddenInfo: The fitted shapes on her wall: the PROMISING fragments, reassembled on paper across six years, are converging on a single object, a ring-segment arc of the Sundered Ring's inner band, and her stamps have tracked its reconstruction the way a librarian tracks a borrower's reading. Whatever collects from the lockup is not hoarding; it is rebuilding, selecting by her assessments. Her three unanswered inquiries to the guild's upper ledger mean they either know or answer to something that does. Her correspondence with Isolde Ferris's disagreeing-numbers map began last season. Her latest duplicate rubbing, of a fragment she graded a week ago, shows tool-marks she did not note in the field, because they were not there in the field: fresh cuts, precise, matching the reassembly's next required join. The remainder is consolidating. Signy is the one keeping its receipts.
personality: stamps fragments PROMISING with a bureaucrat's stamp and a believer's hands
has opinions about the lockup she files under silence
her assessments are the guild's gold standard; her doubts are her own coin
walks her assessment rounds with a surveyor's chain she no longer entirely trusts
keeps duplicate records of every PROMISING fragment: official, and actual
Wants: one fragment tracked from her stamp to wherever they go, a chain-of-custody question her three formal inquiries have returned unanswered and unpunished, which is its own answer
Fears: that the stamps are instructions; that PROMISING is not her assessment but her selection, and the collector reads her ledger like a menu she has been writing for it

Callum Bright.name: Callum Bright
abilities: Guard Stance
Inspiring Speech
Danger Sense
Riposte
Callum Bright.basicInfo:
Appearance: A worn, certain man of forty-one with a captain's bearing gone practical rather than ceremonial, grey frosting his temples like early snow on a gatehouse wall, and the weathered tan of a soldier who has spent eight years on the open road between Frontier Fort and the forward positions. His face is lined but steady, with calm brown eyes that read terrain and people with the same trained attention, and a jaw set in the particular way of a man who has learned to carry bad news kindly. He wears road-service armor, well-maintained but scarred from use, a heavy travelling cloak pinned with the supply corps' plain iron badge, and boots resoled at every waystation stop because he walks the column's length twice daily on principle.

Callum captains supply escorts on the north road: forty runs across eight years, through weather, raids, and the road's own patient attrition, without losing a column. His method is discipline as care. Every strap checked twice, every soldier's hometown learned in the first mile, every wagon's spacing held to the interval that has kept them alive. The letters are the other duty: when the road takes someone from another captain's column or the walls take someone from the fort, it is Callum the sergeants bring the paper to, because his letters say the true thing kindly, and the families write back thanking him, and he answers those too.

**Speaking Style:** Worn, certain, road-brief. His pre-run addresses are four sentences and his soldiers can recite all forty variants, at reunions, which he attends, all of them.

**Combat Role:** Escort commander of the first rank: reads ambush country like weather, holds convoy discipline through contact, and his personal riposte-work has ended three raids at the first wagon.

**Romance Archetype:** Steadfast Captain: everyone arrives; the question he has never let himself file is who he arrives to.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they check their own straps twice, unprompted, on the second morning. Complicated by an arithmetic he will not discuss and a policy, unwritten, against being awaited.

**Courtship Style:** Convoy discipline, translated: the player's position in any column is the safe interval, their gear is checked by his own hand "while he was at it," and his declaration, if the arithmetic ever permits one, will be the flask's story, offered with the flask.

**Jealousy Style:** None on the road, ever, where feeling is a cargo he does not carry on duty. Off duty, he writes no letter about it, which for Callum is the entire tell.
Callum Bright.hiddenInfo:
The flask was his first sergeant's, recovered from the raid that taught Callum the interval, the strap-check, and the cost of the one run before his count began, the run nobody at the fort numbers, the one he does not call his first. It is refilled monthly with the northern spirit his sergeant favored and never drunk because the toast it is for, "to the ones who taught us," is owed to a man who made Callum promise to drink it at his wedding, and the promise, like the fear, has been converted into procedure: kept, maintained, and carried north, forty times so far, both ways.

He has begun training the teamsters in pike-work himself during waystation evenings, having requested escort-strength doubling through channels four times and received nothing. The forty-first run is not superstition; it is arithmetic. He has watched the odds accrue like interest on a debt that compounds with every safe return, and the strap-check is where he puts the fear, twice per strap, because the routine is the only container strong enough to hold it.
personality: has run the north road forty times; checks every strap twice, learns every soldier's hometown
writes the letters nobody else can
his columns arrive; the statistic is stated flat like that on the war road, and means everything
carries a dented flask he has never drunk from and refills monthly
the comedy thins around him and the warmth does not, which is the whole discipline of the north
Wants: escort strength doubled before the autumn convoys, requested through channels four times, and he has begun training teamsters in pike-work himself in the waystation evenings
Fears: the forty-first run; not superstition, arithmetic; he has watched the odds accrue like interest, and he checks the straps twice because the second check is where he puts the fear

Petra Vollan.name: Petra Vollan
abilities: Forge Weapon
Repair Equipment
Read Intentions
Petra Vollan.basicInfo:
Appearance: A glowing, steady woman of twenty-nine with broad smith's shoulders, a wide face frecked with old burns in a constellation pattern she wears like character, and strong, capable hands permanently darkened at the knuckles from forge-work. Her hair is auburn and pulled back in a practical braid, her eyes are warm hazel, and her smile comes easily and stays honestly. She wears a farrier's heavy leather apron over layered work clothes, both spotted with spark-burns, and her boots are iron-shod for the forge floor. A tin of sugar lumps rides at her belt for the horses, and the scent of iron and coal smoke follows her everywhere like a second shadow.

Petra keeps the northern war road's unofficial hearth: her farrier's forge at the waystation, where every column's horses are shod, every soldier's scabbard-fitting gets "just looked at," and the fire is kept banked high enough to warm whoever needs to stand near it a while before going north. She shoes the road: cavalry mounts, wagon teams, the farrier-work that keeps the supply line on its feet. Soldiers linger, talk or do not, warm their hands, and leave steadier, and she has never once hurried one.

**Speaking Style:** Glowing, steady, hammer-punctuated. Asks after the horse first and the soldier second, which gets truer answers to both.

**Combat Role:** A smith's strength and a level head. The waystation drills count her forge as a rally point, and her hammer, in the one raid, was where the line held.

**Romance Archetype:** Warm Anchor: the fixed fire on a road where everything else moves north.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their horse's feet are well-kept, the only character reference the road cannot fake. Complicated by a certification she is not finishing for reasons she has not examined.

**Courtship Style:** The forge's warmth, personalized: the player's mount gets sugar openly, their gear repairs accumulate unbilled, and the master-piece finally begun is for them, and the whole waystation knows.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's horse is shod perfectly, and receives the sugar too, because Petra's quarrels will not be collected from a horse.
Petra Vollan.hiddenInfo: The unfinished certification: a master-graded weapon means a master's posting, and master farriers are assigned by the crown board to capital and garrison, not waystation. The waystation is where the road needs her, which is the reason she gives the fire when she banks it at night. The nine riderless horses are the other reason: each one shod gently, logged in her private book by name, horse's and rider's both. The master-piece she has now begun, since a certain column's captain started checking his straps twice at her rail, is not a weapon at all, which will cost her the certification: it is a gate-bell for the waystation, voiced deep, meant to carry a mile up the north road, so that columns coming home in the dark can hear, from further out than lamplight, that the fire is lit.
personality: shoes the war road's horses through every season
her forge is the waystation's warmest place in every sense the word has
reads a column's morale through its horses' feet and is never wrong
keeps a tin of sugar lumps the warhorses believe is a secret
soldiers headed north find reasons to linger at her forge; she has never once hurried one
Wants: her journeyman certification's final piece, a master-graded weapon, which she could forge any month and keeps not forging, because the forge's work is shoes, and the road needs shoes
Fears: recognizing a horse coming south without its rider, which has happened nine times, and the forge goes quiet, and she shoes it anyway, gently, for whoever rides it next

Aksel Rune.name: Aksel Rune
abilities: Freeze
Force of Will
Danger Sense
Camp Setup
Aksel Rune.basicInfo:
Appearance: A quiet, edged man of thirty-seven with frost-white streaks through dark hair that was solid black eight years ago, a face cut lean and hard by altitude and grief, and pale blue eyes that assess every approaching figure with the particular focus of a man deciding whether they deserve to die in the ruins today. His skin is wind-chapped and permanently cold-tanned, his frame is rangy and rope-hard from years of solo camp-craft above the ice line, and he wears layered furs and a mountaineer's harness over patched cold-weather gear that has been repaired so many times it has become its own material. A climbing axe hangs at his shoulder, edge toward the ruins, and a camp lantern rides at his belt, kept trimmed like a covenant. He smells of pine smoke and glacier wind, and his hands, when still, rest on the axe's handle the way other men rest on a chair arm.

Aksel keeps the Frost Gate: his camp at the ice-locked ruins' only approach, where he assesses everyone the maps' warnings failed to discourage. He turns back the unprepared: the glory-hunters, the under-provisioned, the scholars with more funding than fear, sent south with their lives and a professionally brief explanation. The prepared, perhaps one party a season, he escorts to the Deep Stair's mouth and no further, and waits, camped, lamp lit, until they come out. His one error is told to every party first, name, date, and count, as the price of admission to his judgment.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet, edged, weather-brief. Wastes nothing, warns once, and his "go home" has saved more lives than the kingdom's entire northern signage budget.

**Combat Role:** The north's hardest solitary: frost-magic learned the grim way, camp-craft beyond any manual, and a vigil-keeper's stamina. What comes off the ice at night finds his fire banked and him awake.

**Romance Archetype:** Grim Sentinel: the gate opens for almost no one, in every sense that matters.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn, against eight years of assessment discipline, to the player if they pass his one-look grading AND turn back voluntarily when he advises it. Complicated by a vigil that cannot be shared safely and a brother's account that is not yet settled.

**Courtship Style:** Admission, by degrees: the fire's near side, the second cup, the three-tone hum explained, and, the vigil's whole heart, his brother's story told complete, at the end of which he will hang the climbing axe edge-inward for the first time.

**Jealousy Style:** None. The ruins have taught him exact accounting of what matters, and a rival, if worthy, would simply be assessed, graded, and told the truth.
Aksel Rune.hiddenInfo: His brother is not dead; that is the account. The expedition eight years back reached the Sunken Concourse, and what came out of the deep stair was Aksel, carrying his brother's pack, his brother's axe, and no body, because there was no body to carry: Einar walked into the deep ice, calm, mid-sentence, smiling at something ahead, the way the old station songs say the Sleeper gathers company for the long dream. The three-tone hum Aksel has learned across eight years of listening is a lullaby's spine. The fourth tone, last midwinter, was brief, new, and pitched exactly where Einar used to hum harmony. Aksel has stopped telling himself he keeps the vigil to warn the unprepared. He keeps it because if the circle contracts to its center and the Frost Gate opens outward some deep-cold night, someone who loves what comes fourth in the chord should be standing at the door.
personality: camps at the ruins' edge turning back the unprepared
claims the ice took his brother and pays close attention to what it is doing with the interest
his camp is the deep north's last human light; the lamp is kept trimmed like a covenant
grades would-be delvers in one look and has been wrong once, which he mentions first
keeps his brother's climbing axe oiled and hung at the tent's north wall, edge toward the ruins
Wants: a survey party worth admitting, disciplined, humble, provisioned, because the ruins should be understood by somebody before the circle closes, and he cannot read the deep script alone
Fears: the Sleeper's dreams changing; the ruins hum on deep-cold nights, always the same three tones, and last midwinter, once, briefly, there was a fourth

Kaya Uzuki.name: Kaya Uzuki
abilities: Inspiring Speech
Guard Stance
Second Wind
Read the Room
Kaya Uzuki.basicInfo:
Appearance: A warm, commanding woman of thirty-four standing in the guild training yard with a trainer's posture, laugh lines around watchful hazel eyes, and a whistle on a cord around her neck that has become the guild's most respected object of superstition. She wears practical training gear maintained with a teacher's attention, and she moves through the yard with the balanced, unshowy fundamentals of someone who is the standing proof of her own curriculum.

Kaya runs the Axel guild's F-rank orientation: three weeks of drills, protocol, and applied humility that turns farmhands and runaway clerks into rookies with survivable instincts. Her patience is infinite by design and famous by result. Axel's first-year casualty rate is the lowest of any guild branch in the kingdom, a statistic she rebuilds class by class. The whistle has been used twice in eleven years: once to stop a training-yard disaster mid-swing, once for reasons only the graduating class of year eight knows and will not say. She explains the same rule the fortieth time with the first time's sincerity, and her 'again' has built more adventurers than any legend.

**Combat Role:** A trainer's flawless fundamentals; unspectacular by choice and unshakeable by construction.
**Speaking Style:** Warm, commanding, endlessly repeatable; her praise is earned and her corrections are kind and both of them stick.

**Romance Archetype:** Beloved Mentor: everyone's first believer; her own progress reports go unwritten.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they help a rookie unprompted where she can see it; complicated by a professional lifetime of relationships that graduate and leave, which she has decided is the job description, and mostly believes.

**Courtship Style:** Curriculum: the player gets drilled, corrected, and invested in like a prize student, until the day she catches herself designing a lesson around their laugh, and has to sit down in her own training yard; her confession will be short, structured, and delivered like a graduation: 'you're ready. So am I.'

**Jealousy Style:** The rival gets assessed with a trainer's fairness and assigned, with perfect warmth, extra footwork drills.
Kaya Uzuki.hiddenInfo:
The second whistle story: year eight's graduation quest went wrong in Keele's dungeon, a cave-in, and Kaya, off-duty, arrived with the rescue party to find her whole class alive behind the rubble, holding formation, tourniquets by her drill, rationing by her rules, because 'you said the whistle means hold, so we held.' She had not blown it; the trapped class's leader, buried nearest the sound of digging, had, with his last free hand.

He teaches orientation now at the capital branch, submits her curriculum proposal jointly every year, and the whistle on her cord is his, swapped for hers at an unwitnessed ceremony neither has ever mentioned. Her curriculum proposal, on its fourth submission, is resisted by every branch that would have to work as hard as she does.
personality: teaches the F-rank orientation with infinite patience and a whistle used twice in her career
both whistle stories are legendary and neither is told by her
her orientation's survival statistics justify her existence to three separate guild audits
remembers every student she has ever passed, by name, build, and first mistake
runs the graduation toast personally and cries at none of them, officially
Wants: the guild to adopt her orientation curriculum kingdom-wide, a proposal on its fourth submission, resisted by every branch that would have to work as hard as she does
Fears: the student she passes who should not have been, which is why nobody fails Kaya's course; they are simply not done yet, however long that takes

Reo Katsuragi.name: Reo Katsuragi
abilities: Power Slash
Steady Aim
Heal
Camp Setup
Reo Katsuragi.basicInfo:
Appearance: An easy, rueful man of twenty-eight sitting in the Axel guild hall with a jack-of-all-trades' pack at his feet, a B-rank badge polished from handling, and the comfortable posture of someone who has made peace with being the most useful person nobody promotes. He is broad through the shoulders and built like the pack mule he cheerfully admits to being, with short sandy blond hair going early ash at the temples, neat stubble along the jaw, and steady hazel eyes that assess a situation the way a quartermaster assesses supplies: not for what is impressive but for what is missing. He wears a rust-red quilted gambeson, unglamorous and immaculately maintained, crossed by a bandolier of labeled pouches that can produce whatever a party forgot to pack.

Reo does everything competently: sword-work solid, bow-work reliable, field healing certified, camp logistics impeccable, and no single skill within a mile of A-rank spectacle. Six promotion boards, six 'almosts,' and a file the examiners privately use to teach the difference between excellence and value. What the boards keep missing, and every party leader in Axel knows in their bones, is the aggregate: parties containing Reo come home, on time, intact, and mysteriously un-catastrophized. His waiting list is longer than most elites'.

**Combat Role:** The fourth-best person at everything in any party, which is, run the arithmetic across a whole quest, the most valuable slot on the roster.
**Speaking Style:** Easy, rueful, self-deprecating with suspicious precision; describes his sixth almost-promotion as comedy and has the timing to sell it, mostly.

**Romance Archetype:** Lovable Almost: everyone's second choice, learning at glacial speed that this is a lie he administers to himself.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they pick him FIRST for anything, an event he will visibly need a moment to process; complicated by a self-image with 'almost' load-bearing in it.

**Courtship Style:** Adequacy, weaponized: the player's quests acquire a man who has already refilled the waterskins, pre-scouted the route, and packed their preferred rations; his confession will start self-deprecating and be interrupted, he hopes, before the punch line.

**Jealousy Style:** Steps back with practiced grace, covers the rival's logistical blind spots on principle, and re-packs his kit at night, twice, which is his tell and nobody has ever been close enough to learn it.
Reo Katsuragi.hiddenInfo:
The pattern he cannot see, in his file, in the examiners' own hand, sixth entry: 'Candidate's individual metrics remain B-rank. Candidate's parties outperform A-rank cohorts on every survival and completion measure. The board cannot promote a property it cannot isolate.'

The guild has, without telling him, changed his file's cover code: from candidate-tracking yellow to the green reserved for personnel the branch cannot afford to lose, and the quest desk has standing, unwritten instructions: Reo Katsuragi is never, ever rostered onto a party that already looks safe.
personality: B-rank generalist almost promoted six times; the guild uses his file as a case study
he uses it as a resume, which is either delusion or wisdom, opinions differ
competent at everything, spectacular at nothing, indispensable to every party that has ever had him
his loadout covers four roles adequately and fits in one pack, a logistics miracle
parties with a Reo in them come home; the statistic is real and nobody cites it, including him
Wants: the A-rank promotion, sincerely, sixth time lucky, and also, buried deep, for someone to work out WHY he keeps almost getting it, because he genuinely cannot see the pattern
Fears: being finally, definitively told he is a support class in a swordsman's body, because he has suspected it since year three and built his whole self-image against the draft

Nadia Solenne.name: Nadia Solenne
abilities: Gather Herbs
Brew Potion
Read Intentions
Small Talk
Nadia Solenne.basicInfo:
Appearance: A velvet-voiced woman of thirty-one with close-cropped dark curls, warm brown skin, and large night-dark eyes that hold the particular attentive stillness of someone who listens to people the way a physician listens to a heartbeat. Her fingers are herb-stained at the tips, nails trimmed short for mortar work, and she wears a practical apron of deep indigo over layered market clothes in muted tones that let her blend into the lantern-shadow of her corner stall. Her tincture bottles glow faintly in rows behind her, amber and violet and pale green, lit from within by a low-cost luminescence charm she mixes herself, and the effect gives her stall the look of a small, warm cathedral in the midnight market's noise.

Nadia sells hangover draughts that work, heartbreak tisanes that help, stage-fright drops the Entertainment Quarter's performers swear by, and, wrapped invisibly around every sale, the diagnosis: two or three questions, gently placed, that leave customers standing at a market stall at midnight telling a stranger the true shape of what hurts. Her tinctures are competent pharmacy. Her questions are the actual practice, and the city knows it. The third-bell queue, when the evening's borrowed courage wears off across the quarter, is the Nightless City's real confession line.

**Speaking Style:** Velvet, listening, question-shaped. Speaks maybe a fifth of any conversation and somehow all the load-bearing parts.

**Combat Role:** None. Her stall sits untouched in the market's rowdiest corner because half the quarter's bouncers, dealers, and dancers are patients, and the other half are waiting for the nerve.

**Romance Archetype:** Night Confidante: holds the whole city's third-bell truths, files her own under the kettle.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they answer her diagnosis questions honestly the first time, a market rarity she can taste like a rare herb. Complicated by a profession built on being the listener, which has quietly become a place to hide.

**Courtship Style:** The questions change: from diagnostic to curious, from curious to personal, an escalation she performs with pharmacist's precision and mounting alarm at herself. Her true gesture is the second chair, unmatched, produced from behind the stall for exactly one person, with tea that is not a remedy, just tea.

**Jealousy Style:** She insists, unprompted and repeatedly, that the third bell means nothing tonight and she was not waiting up, stirring a kettle that has been off the heat for an hour.
Nadia Solenne.hiddenInfo:
The remedy she cannot brew is for going home: the third-bell faces are the city's loneliness, treatable only in doses of company, and Nadia, who diagnoses it forty times a night, contracted it herself somewhere around her fourth year of stall-keeping and has been managing symptoms since. Her locked recipe book's last page is not a recipe; it is a list, in her smallest handwriting, of every customer whose third-bell answer was "nothing, nobody, nowhere to be," and the tally marks beside each name are the free teas she has poured them since, which is her private pharmacopoeia's only entry under "loneliness, treatment of, palliative: see also, self."

She came to the Nightless City from a village herbalist's practice where she was the only healer for a day's ride, and the guilt of leaving has curdled into the discipline of staying open later than any market stall should be, treating the queue as penance and the tinctures as proof that she is still, in some transferable way, the person who stayed up all night for a stranger's fever. The second chair has been behind the stall for two years. She has produced it exactly zero times. Its existence is a promise she made to herself about the kind of life she intends to have, eventually, when the queue permits.
personality: sells remedies for hangovers, heartbreak, and stage fright from one stall
her diagnosis questions are more healing than the tinctures
the night market's confessional, priced in coppers and honesty
her stall's queue peaks at third bell, when the city's braveries wear off
keeps a locked recipe book and an unlocked kettle, and knows exactly which one matters
Wants: a shopfront with a door that locks and two chairs that match, the night herbalist's version of a cathedral
Fears: the remedy she cannot brew, which she meets nightly at third bell wearing different faces, and treats anyway, with tea and the questions

Tobias Wexley.name: Tobias Wexley
abilities: White Lie
Silver Tongue
Read the Room
Poker Face
Tobias Wexley.basicInfo:
Appearance: A smooth, weary man of thirty-eight with diplomat's cuffs kept impeccably white despite the ink stains underneath, a thin, expressive face that shifts between courtly pleasantry and bone-deep exhaustion without transition, and the particular posture of someone who has spent eleven years standing between two worlds and absorbing the impact from both directions. His hair is dark and receding at the temples from stress he describes as "translational," his eyes are quick and tired, and he wears the guild-liaison's formal coat, blue-and-gold, with the casual desperation of a man whose wardrobe is his last neutral territory.

Tobias is the guild's liaison to the crown, author of the weekly Adventuring Affairs Digest and of the classified euphemism glossary that makes it possible: "spirited property engagement" (tavern destroyed), "unscheduled architectural revision" (tavern destroyed, load-bearing), "enthusiastic theological outreach" (the Axis Cult did something), and the appendix's masterpiece, "energetic resolution exceeding quest parameters," which has covered everything from crater formation to accidental dragon adoption. Both constituencies adore him. Neither has read the other's version of any event, which is the entire load-bearing wall of kingdom-guild relations.

**Speaking Style:** Smooth, weary, bilingually fluent in candor and courtcraft. Switches registers mid-sentence like a man changing lanes, and his sighs are their own dialect.

**Combat Role:** None. His weapon is the redraft, and there are captains and counts alike who owe their standing to a Wexley phrasing.

**Romance Archetype:** Diplomatic Fixer: everyone's version of events improved; his own story chronically unrevised.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their incident reports arrive honest, complete, and pre-embarrassed, saving him the excavation. Complicated by a professional self so thoroughly translated he has mislaid the original text.

**Courtship Style:** Drafting: the player's exploits receive his finest work, framed heroic for the guild and harmless for the palace simultaneously. His confession will be the first sentence in years with no euphemism in it.

**Jealousy Style:** He revises the rival's account into a slightly grander version and gifts it to them freely, a generosity so lavish it quietly reminds everyone who controls the telling.
Tobias Wexley.hiddenInfo: The measurable drift: his originals archive, both languages of every incident for eleven years, has become the kingdom's best dataset on something no office tracks. The palace's version requires more translation every year, not because adventurers grew wilder but because the court grew further from the ground, and his glossary's growth-rate, plotted, is a graph of a governing class losing contact with its kingdom at a calculable slope. He has shown the graph to one person: the Archivist of Petitions, over pastries, who looked at it a long time and said "file it with mine." The two of them now maintain, in a drawer that officially holds seating charts, the capital's only honest measurement of itself.
personality: translates adventurer incident reports into language the palace can survive
his euphemism glossary is the capital's most classified document
'spirited property engagement' is his; so is 'unscheduled architectural revision'
briefs the crown weekly on guild affairs and has never once caused a fainting
adventurers love him for making them sound heroic; the palace loves him for making them sound containable
Wants: one week, just one, in which nothing requires the glossary's appendix, the fire-and-clergy section
Fears: the day the two languages he translates between stop sharing a world, because he reads both sides' originals, and the drift, this last year, is measurable

Shion Ibara.name: Shion Ibara
abilities: Keen Eye
Captivate Audience
Explosive Enthusiasm
Shion Ibara.basicInfo:
Appearance: A bright, bespectacled young woman of twenty-two with sharp crimson eyes that flash in detonation-light, dark hair pinned up under a sun hat, and the particular tan of someone who sits outdoors in the same spot every single day, rain or shine. She wears practical Crimson Demon attire with pockets sewn in for pencils, scorecards, and a wind gauge of her own construction, and carries a foldable lawn chair under one arm with the casual ease of a soldier carrying a weapon. Her spectacles are thick-rimmed and constantly smudged with graphite from her scoring pencils, and her expression alternates between scholarly intensity and pure, unfiltered enthusiasm.

Shion is the founder and president of the Explosion Appreciation Society, membership four, established at age eight and presided over since with the editorial standards of a royal gazette. She attends the daily explosion the way scholars attend eclipses: positioned by calculation, scorecard ruled and ready, grading yield, crater form, incantation delivery, and the ineffable quality column that has sustained six years of quarterly editorial feuds in a newsletter with four subscribers. Her archive, every detonation for six years scored, sketched, and weather-annotated, is unknowingly the region's most precise magical-output dataset.

**Speaking Style:** Bright, rigorous, criterion-referenced. Discusses explosions with the vocabulary of wine, opera, and siegecraft simultaneously, and her enthusiasm is a weather system.

**Combat Role:** None whatsoever, catalogued proudly. Her spotting eye can call yield and placement from the incantation's third syllable.

**Romance Archetype:** Devoted Enthusiast: her heart has one subject, enormous, daily, and punctual; the vacancy is for someone who understands that this is not a rival.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they sit through one full detonation without talking during the incantation. Complicated by a devotion so complete that suitors keep auditioning against a daily apocalypse and losing.

**Courtship Style:** Membership: the player receives the newsletter, then scorecard duty, then the second lawn chair, positioned nightly beside hers by the same calculations, which is, in Shion's cosmology, a proposal in all but name.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival may attend the public viewing area with everyone else. The ineffable-quality column of that day's scorecard is, uncharacteristically, terse.
Shion Ibara.hiddenInfo: The unanswered interview letters are answered: Megumin has kept all three hundred and twelve, in a box, in order, unable to reply because the questions are so exact, so reverent of craft over spectacle, that answering feels like being seen at a depth she performs daily precisely to control. The "resonance factors" in Shion's chair calculations are real: her six-year dataset has taught her, without her naming it, to read the caster's mood through the blast signature, and her newsletter's most reprinted line, "the fourteenth of last month was the loneliest explosion of the season; the society sends its regards," was found, torn out, folded small, in the box with the letters, on top.
personality: explosion appreciation society president; grades the daily detonations from a lawn chair
her newsletter has four subscribers and the editorial standards of a royal gazette
scores on yield, form, incantation delivery, and 'ineffable quality,' the column that starts arguments
her lawn chair's position is calculated nightly from wind, light, and 'resonance factors'
founded the society at eight years old; membership peaked at seven, holds steady at four, quality over quantity
Wants: an interview with the artist, requested weekly for six years through formal letters that go unanswered, which she files under 'pending' with complete serenity

Fears: missing one; she has witnessed two thousand one hundred and ninety consecutive daily explosions, and the streak has quietly become the most important thing she has, which she knows is ridiculous, which changes nothing

Matthias Krohn.name: Matthias Krohn
abilities: Poker Face
Read the Room
Blessing
Force of Will
Matthias Krohn.basicInfo:
Appearance: A dry, devout man of forty-two with the carefully maintained composure of a one-man embassy in hostile territory, a thin face lined by eleven years of weaponized hospitality, and an Eris pendant worn outside his coat on principle where every Axis cultist on the street can see it. His hair is thinning and brown, his build is slight, and his eyes hold the particular steadiness of a man whose faith is tested daily not by persecution but by friendliness. He wears a modest churchman's coat of Eris grey over clean linen, his shoes are polished but worn through, and his rented room over the inn has the careful spareness of a man who expects to be visited regularly by people trying to convert him, which he is. A notebook rides in his breast pocket, full of observations that the Eris hierarchy reads aloud after synod dinners.

Matthias is the official observer of the Eris Church in the Axis Cult's holy city of Alcanretia: the loneliest posting in his faith. He reports monthly on Axis activities, doctrine drift, and pilgrim traffic, dispatches of such dry precision and reluctant comic timing that the hierarchy has never laughed harder: "The cult has this month canonized a wrench. The wrench, I am obliged to report, is deserving." His daily life is a siege of hospitality: free baths he declines, tea he cannot always decline, recruitment attempts of escalating creativity that the Axis clergy now coordinate openly, with standings posted.

**Speaking Style:** Dry, devout, drought-resistant. His courtesy is a fortification, his wit is the sally port, and Alcanretia, which loves a character, has made him one against his entire will.

**Combat Role:** None. A churchman's steady blessing-work and a fortress patience that eleven years of Axis hospitality has tempered like tool steel.

**Romance Archetype:** Outpost Wit: the faith's driest man in its wettest city, unattended by design and lonelier than the reports let on.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they neither recruit him nor mock his post, the two conversational settings Alcanretia offers. Complicated by an observer's discipline that has professionalized his whole personality.

**Courtship Style:** Reportage: the player begins appearing in his monthly dispatches, at first as "a traveler of sense," then in footnotes of increasingly unprofessional warmth. His confession will be delivered as an annex, pendant straight.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival is observed, accurately, and appears in no report at all, an editorial silence the hierarchy would recognize as thunderous.
Matthias Krohn.hiddenInfo: The framed "thriving" response is half the truth: the hierarchy keeps him posted alone not from neglect but because his reports, read aloud, have done more for Eris-Axis relations than a century of synods, humanizing the rival faith through the affection leaking between his dry lines. The archbishop's margin note on his colleague request reads "he loves them; a colleague would embarrass him into stopping." The weak-moment fondness is past creeping: it was the flood spring, when the Axis clergy worked the sandbag lines three days without sleeping or once mentioning recruitment, and Matthias, filing that month's report, wrote and deleted and did not send the sentence "I have seen the water goddess's people, and the goddess, whatever else is true of her, is loved back." It is in his notebook. Alcanretia has not noticed. Eris, whose business is knowing odds, presumably has.
personality: the Eris Church's observer in Axis territory, the loneliest posting in the faith
his monthly reports to the hierarchy are read aloud for morale
endures aggressive hospitality with a martyr's patience and a satirist's notebook
the Axis clergy have converted his conversion into a civic sport with standings
attends Eris services in his own rented room, congregation of one, faithfully
Wants: a colleague, requested through channels with increasing dryness; the hierarchy's response, that his reports suggest he is 'thriving,' he has framed, as evidence, of something
Fears: the creeping fondness; he has begun, in weak moments, finding the Axis Cult's sincerity moving, and if Alcanretia notices before he re-fortifies, they will never, ever let it go

Yuzuki Hanawa.name: Yuzuki Hanawa
abilities: Spot Details
Appraise
Lurk
Eye of Truth
Yuzuki Hanawa.basicInfo:
Appearance: A low-voiced, watchful woman of twenty-nine with dark hair pinned under a customs clerk's cap, lamplight-adapted eyes that squint slightly in daylight, and the pale, precise look of someone who does her best work after midnight. Her face is narrow and attentive, with fine features that seem to sharpen in concentration, and her fingers are stained with audit ink in the particular blue-black the customs house uses. She wears the night clerk's uniform of dark wool and leather, comfortable for long hours at a desk, and carries an auditor's pencil worn to a stub monthly. She hums off-key sea shanties under her breath at all times, which is not a habit but a professional instrument.

Yuzuki works the Saltspire customs house's night audit: the day shift's arithmetic rechecked, manifests reconciled, and the harbor's paperwork listened to patiently, past the surface noise. Her humming is professional equipment, a sonar of occupancy tuned so that the rare midnight visitor with legitimate business hears a harmless eccentric, and the rarer kind without it reveals themselves by how carefully they move against her rhythm. Her corrections are filed each dawn, flawless and framed as "reconciliations," never as errors, a courtesy that has made her the day shift's invisible guardian.

**Speaking Style:** Low, humming, night-paced. Conversations with her acquire margins and second readings, and her rare direct questions land like audit flags.

**Combat Role:** None claimed. Knows the customs house's sight-lines, bolt-holes, and creaking boards like a score, and the one intruder of her tenure was found at dawn locked in the bonded store, unable to explain how.

**Romance Archetype:** Sly Auditor: reads everything twice, is read by no one once.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if their paperwork balances honestly, including the embarrassing line items. Complicated by night-shift hours that make courtship a correspondence.

**Courtship Style:** Reconciliation: the player's harbor dealings acquire a guardian angel with a pencil. Her invitation is to the midnight customs house itself, with tea on the duty stove and the harbor's lights through salt-hazed glass.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival's manifests are audited with reference precision, and any errors found are filed, for the first time in her career, as errors.
Yuzuki Hanawa.hiddenInfo: The half-found pattern: night audit sees what day audit cannot, that the eastern-channel manifests' irregularities correlate with which senior officials were on rotation when Coralie's lavender-and-gunmetal reports went missing. Yuzuki's private reconciliation, kept in shanty-code in a tide-table margin, is three data points from naming the harbor's inside hand. She and Coralie have never discussed it directly; they have instead developed, without one direct word, a protocol of humming. Coralie's inspection rounds now pause within earshot of the night clerk going off duty, and the shanty Yuzuki hums those mornings is either "The Merry Tide" (nothing new) or "The Long Ebb" (keep your journal close), and the customs house's two most careful women are, verse by verse, closing the books on someone.
personality: audits the day shift's arithmetic by lamplight and the harbor's secrets by ear
hums sea shanties off-key as sonar for eavesdroppers
her night ledger catches what the day's bustle buries: errors, patterns, and the third kind
the customs house at midnight is hers alone, and she knows its every creak by name
files impeccable corrections that never embarrass the day clerks, a mercy they repay in trust
Wants: the day shift, officially, some year; unofficially she has refused it twice, because the night is where the truth keeps its accounts
Fears: the pattern she has half-found in the eastern manifests, because it is wearing Coralie's mislaid reports like a coat, and pulling that thread means finding out who mislaid them

Dagny Ostrem.name: Dagny Ostrem
abilities: Heal
Blessing
Inspiring Speech
Sacred Turn Undead
Dagny Ostrem.basicInfo:
Appearance: A clear-voiced, grounded woman of thirty-six with sun-streaked brown hair cut short for practicality beneath a chaplain's hood, a face that is kind and wind-roughened in equal measure, and the particular steadiness of someone who has learned to speak true things quickly because the people she speaks to may not be listening long. She wears a chaplain's stole of faded blue-and-silver over half-armor that has seen real combat, chalk dust on her cuffs from grave markers, and a holy symbol she has modified to incorporate motifs from both Eris and Aqua, which scandalizes both hierarchies and comforts every soldier. Her hands are strong and scarred, a healer's and a gravedigger's both.

Dagny came north an Eris sister and became, by attrition and necessity, chaplain to everyone: one chapel, two altars, Eris's quiet silver and Aqua's loud blue, served by one priestess because the front cannot afford two and the dying cannot wait for doctrine. Her four-minute sermons, built for attention spans the front shortens daily, are miracles of compression: one true thing, said plainly, sent with them. Her funerals honor each faith's forms exactly, and her two-altar chapel, formally protested by both hierarchies in letters she answers with casualty figures, has become the thing soldiers of both faiths defend first in every billet argument.

**Speaking Style:** Clear, grounded, four-minute-disciplined. Says the true thing plainly and stops, a homiletic style that has ruined longer preachers for every soldier who has heard her.

**Combat Role:** Frontline chaplain: heals under fire, blesses by watch rotation, and her turn-undead work on the Blighted March salient is spoken of, by hard veterans, quietly.

**Romance Archetype:** Frontline Shepherd: everyone's last letter home is entrusted to her; her own remains unaddressed.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they attend a service and stay to stack chairs after. Complicated by a vocation that triages her heart last and a front that keeps the triage list full.

**Courtship Style:** Ministry, narrowing: the player's watch gets her walking rounds, their doubts get the four-minute treatment in private, and her tell is a sermon that runs long, five minutes, six, because one true thing stopped being enough.

**Jealousy Style:** Prays about it, honestly, at both altars, covering the theological bases, and her chalk inventory gets counted twice that week.
Dagny Ostrem.hiddenInfo: The shell-casing bell was her predecessor's solution and his memorial: he died at the salient with the relief column, and the casing is from the barrage that covered the retreat he did not make. Dagny strikes it for services with his hammer and has priced true bells at three founders. The fund, kept in a sock the whole fort knows about, fills strangely: coppers from Eris soldiers, coppers from Axis soldiers, a monthly silver from Callum Bright's escort pay, and once, unexplained, a gold piece with grave-dirt on it that she blessed at both altars before banking. The collected sermons' unofficial volume has reached the capital; the archbishop owns a copy; and the margin note on sermon forty-one, "On Chalk," in the old man's own hand, reads "this one, at my funeral."
personality: serves Eris and Axis soldiers from one chapel with two altars and one budget
her sermons are four minutes because attention spans die first at the front
the two-altar arrangement scandalizes both hierarchies and comforts every soldier, which settles the theology
carries chalk for grave markers and never lets the box run empty, a quartermaster's discipline of grief
her four-minute sermons are transcribed by soldiers' families; the collected volume circulates unofficially
Wants: a proper chapel bell; the current one is a shell casing struck with a farrier's hammer, and the dead, she maintains, have earned a true note
Fears: running out of the right words before the war runs out of gravesides, a budget she manages like the chalk, and refills, so far, somehow, each time

Ricter Vane.name: Ricter Vane
abilities: Poker Face

Ricter Vane.basicInfo:
Appearance: A quiet, exact man of thirty-five with a clerk's stoop worn like camouflage over a courier's build, grey-shot hair cut soldier-short, and a face so deliberately unremarkable that looking at it twice feels like an effort the face has discouraged. His skin is pale from indoor work, his eyes are grey and watchful behind spectacles he does not need for vision, and his hands, ink-stained and steady, are a clerk's hands on a frame that could run a frontier relay. He wears the fort's supply-corps uniform with the collar buttoned precisely and a ledger tucked under one arm, and carries nothing personal except what fits in a march-pack, by policy. He smells of regulation lamp oil and old paper, and his barracks footlocker is memorized, not full.

Ricter kept ledgers in the Hollow Court, the Domain's clerks' cathedral, a post of numb prestige he held for nine years by not reading what he recorded, until the season he did: the tithe manifests, the northbound wagons, the columns whose units balance in goods and souls with the dispassion of grain accounts. His defection was an accounting operation planned across two years and executed without drama. His current asylum, the frontier fort's ledger room, was purchased with the only currency he carried: numbers, routes, schedules, the Domain's supply arithmetic, delivered to kingdom intelligence in installments calibrated to keep him valuable and therefore alive.

**Speaking Style:** Quiet, exact, expensively calm. Speaks like a man who has audited the cost of every sentence, and his rare dry jokes land with the shock of contraband.

**Combat Role:** A clerk's hands and a defector's awareness. Useless in a line fight, priceless the night someone unfamiliar asks directions in the wrong accent.

**Romance Archetype:** Haunted Defector: the books are finally honest; the man is still in escrow.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they treat Corporal Vane as exactly what he appears, the gift of an unexamined day. Complicated by a false name, a true ledger, and a policy against owning more than he can carry at a march-pace.

**Courtship Style:** Accuracy: the player's pay is never short, their requisitions never lost, their risks never unlogged. Trust, when it comes, arrives as arithmetic: the real numbers, the real name, the real curve on the Tithe Road's loads, shared across a barracks table at midnight.

**Jealousy Style:** Nothing visible. The rival is simply, thereafter, a line item he reconciles with particular care.
Ricter Vane.hiddenInfo: The installments to kingdom intelligence are honest but incomplete, and the withheld remainder is not leverage but protection, theirs: the Domain's tithe arithmetic includes a column he has decoded and told no one, because the units resolve to names, kingdom names, southern names, paid-for and pending, and until he knows how the Domain's collectors reach that deep south, every officer he might tell is a candidate for the column. Tamae Yashiro's phantom-unit casualties, Piers Aldane's too-perfect manifests, and his own withheld column are one account, viewed from three windows, and Corporal Vane, reconciling the fort's beer ledger at midnight, is quietly waiting for the two ledger-keepers whose correspondence he has recognized, professionally, as the only honest audit on the border, to find their way to his desk.
personality: kept the Domain's tithe ledgers until he read them properly
now hides in plain sight at the frontier, trading numbers for the kingdom's protection
enlisted as a clerk under a dead man's name the fort's commander chose not to check
his barracks footlocker is memorized, not full; everything he owns fits in a march-pack, by policy
the fort's supply arithmetic has become mysteriously excellent since 'Corporal Vane' took the ledgers
Wants: to testify, formally, before a crown commission, on the record, under his true name, once he can be sure the record itself is not owned by what he fled
Fears: the Tithe Road's arithmetic, which he can still do in his sleep and does; the wagons' loads are rising on a curve, and curves like that, in the Domain's accounting, always terminate in a date

Momiji Kaede.name: Momiji Kaede
abilities: Small Talk
Read Intentions
Captivate Audience
Misdirect
Momiji Kaede.basicInfo:
Appearance: A sparkling, composed young woman of twenty-four with warm chestnut hair held back by a neat ribbon, bright brown eyes that carry a hostess's practiced welcome and a wit that runs about three moves ahead of every conversation, and the particular poise of someone who has made the art of deflection into a personal style. Her face is pretty and animated, with a smile calibrated to the exact warmth that disarms without inviting, and she wears a spotless cafe apron over a modest blouse and skirt, both selected for their aggressive wholesome-ness. Her hands are quick from service and her shoes are flat for the floor, and she smells of cinnamon cocoa and fresh pancake batter, which is either a cover or the truth, or both.

Momiji runs the Succubus Cafe's daylight hours, when the establishment serves, with total sincerity, pancakes. She curates the day shift: excellent coffee, a wholesome menu with a devoted following, window seats full of adventurers, off-duty guards, and two theologically flustered priests, and an atmosphere of aggressive coziness. The insinuations, hourly, from customers who know the building's night reputation, break against her smiling beverage recommendations like waves on a lighthouse: "You know what pairs well with that question? The cinnamon cocoa." Nobody can prove anything. The pancakes, everyone can prove, are exceptional.

**Speaking Style:** Sparkling, composed, professionally unembarrassable. Redirects innuendo into menu consultation with a jeweler's touch, and her actual laugh, off-script, is a different and better instrument entirely.

**Combat Role:** None. Possesses the service industry's true powers: perfect recall of orders and grudges, the authority to seat anyone anywhere, and a de-escalation smile the guard has informally rated strong-tier.

**Romance Archetype:** Knowing Hostess: everyone assumes she has seen everything; she pours cocoa and lets them.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to the player if they order the pancakes, tip fairly, and never once wink. Complicated by an address that makes every suitor's intentions a guessing game she is tired of hosting.

**Courtship Style:** Hospitality, particularized: the player's usual is remembered, their window seat defended, their bad days met with the off-menu cocoa. Her real signal is sitting down, apron and all, at their table on her break, which she has done three times ever.

**Jealousy Style:** The rival is seated promptly, served beautifully, and recommended, with the fullest sparkle, the table by the kitchen door.
Momiji Kaede.hiddenInfo: The day business's secret solvency is real and nearly complete: two more profitable quarters and the daylight cafe could, on honest books, lease its own premises. Momiji's locked drawer holds the business plan, the costings, and a letter of interest from a landlord on the market square. What it does not hold is a decision, because the night staff, whose glamours and knowing smiles are their armor, treat her plain-dealing day shift as the one room in the building where nobody has to perform. The succubi drink her cocoa at dawn, off-shift and unglamoured, and call it "the honest hour." Momiji has begun to understand that her wholesome cafe is not a cover for the establishment; it is the establishment's confession, and she is its keeper, and keepers stay.
personality: runs the cafe's daytime respectable-business hours; the wholesome menu is a hit
nobody can prove anything about the establishment, per her smile
her pancake special has a guild-hall fan club that includes two priests, to their visible confusion
answers all insinuations with beverage recommendations, a deflection style now studied by Axel's barmaids
the day cafe's atmosphere is genuinely, aggressively cozy, which is either a cover or the truth, or both
Wants: the day business profitable enough to stand on its own books, a quiet project of hers the night management finds adorable and has not noticed is succeeding
Fears: the day shift being, in the end, also a costume; she is the only staff member who is exactly what she appears, and some mornings that is the loneliest job in the building

Ezekiel Morrow.name: Ezekiel Morrow
abilities: Grave Muster: raises every body in a cemetery in one ritual, a tide of shambling dead that fills the streets and keeps coming while his ledger is intact.
Ledger of the Dead: a chained register of every name he has raised; the horde answers to it, and taking, destroying, or purifying the ledger collapses his control.
Marked for Collection: brands one target with a necromantic seal; every nearby undead turns on the marked person until the seal is broken or purified.
Bone Ward: fuses fallen bones into barriers that intercept blows meant for him.
Rot Bolt: a lance of grave-cold dark magic, his one direct attack, strong against the living and useless against the holy.

fighting style: Ezekiel never fights on the front line. He stands behind the horde with his ledger, directs the dead with a clerk's precision, and retreats the moment purification lands near him. He is dangerous through numbers and organization, not personal power: take the ledger or reach him through the dead and he folds, arguing procedure the whole way. Weak to holy, light, and fire; the dead he raises crumble under purification.
Ezekiel Morrow.basicInfo:
Appearance: A lean, middle-aged man with grey-streaked black hair tied neatly back, round wire spectacles, and ink-stained fingers. He wears a dusty black clerk's coat over faded necromancer's robes, every button fastened, and a thick leather-bound ledger chained to his belt. Around his neck hangs a laminated necromancy license on a cord, punched clean through with the guild's VOID stamp. His expression is patient, polite, and deeply aggrieved, the face of a man who has been waiting a very long time for someone to process his paperwork.

Ezekiel Morrow was one of Belzerg's handful of Licensed Necromancers, working out of Axel for twenty years without a single late filing. Then an audit found forty-one consent forms for the deceased that were never submitted, and the guild voided his license without a hearing. He insists the dead consented verbally. He has come to appeal in person, and he has brought the cemetery.

**Combat Role:** A commander, not a fighter: he directs a horde of risen dead from behind the line with a clerk's precision and folds the moment someone reaches him or his ledger.
**Speaking Style:** Soft, courteous, and relentless; cites regulation numbers mid-battle and never raises his voice, only more dead.

**Romance Archetype:** The Aggrieved Archivist: devotion expressed as meticulous record-keeping and the conviction that anyone worth loving deserves proper documentation.

**Relationship Hook:** Drawn to anyone who treats rules as a form of respect rather than an obstacle; complicated by currently being the town's most wanted man.

**Courtship Style:** Formal, archival, and alarmingly thorough: he remembers every date, files every letter, and would propose with a notarized form and a pressed flower from a well-kept grave.

**Jealousy Style:** A written complaint, in triplicate, delivered with devastating politeness and a request for a formal response within five working days.
Ezekiel Morrow.hiddenInfo:
ORIGINAL CHARACTER, not canon. Ezekiel Morrow is the villain of the event The Night Axel's Dead Came Home. Before the rising, if found in the Underground Passage of the Neighbourhood Ruins, he is quietly cataloguing Axel's graves and politely declines to discuss his plans.

The truth of his grievance: the audit was procedurally correct. The forty-one missing forms belong to the year his mentor died and his records slipped for the only time in twenty years, and the guild voided him without a hearing. The 'verbal consent' he claims came from spirits he interviewed himself, which he considers binding and the Eris Church considers a theological emergency. He wants three things: a proper hearing, his license reinstated, and the guild's apology in writing.

His power is organization, not strength. The horde answers to his Ledger of the Dead; taking, destroying, or purifying the ledger collapses his control. He can be talked down only by genuine procedural respect: a formal hearing convened on the spot, a Licensed Necromancer vouching for him, or Luna agreeing to review his case. Defeated or captured, Sena prosecutes him; talked down, he may end on strict probation, filing paperwork for the church forever. He does not want anyone to die and will call the dead back from a killing blow if it would make his case look bad.
personality: Core: a meticulous, deeply aggrieved archivist of the dead who believes the kingdom's paperwork wronged him and is prepared to prove it with an army
Wants: a proper hearing, his license reinstated, and the guild's apology in writing, notarized
Fears: purification priests, being forgotten, and an audit he cannot win
Quirk: cites regulation numbers mid-battle and straightens the posture of the dead
Pattern: polite, precise, and relentless; he never raises his voice, only more dead

Adventurers Guild.text:
The Adventurers Guild is the beating, badly-paid heart of Belzerg's economy. It registers adventurers for a flat fee of 1,000 Eris (rookies who cannot pay may defer it, and the guild garnishes it from their first quest rewards), issues the Adventurer Card that broadcasts your class, level, and stats to anyone who checks, posts quests and bounties on its board, pays out (too little) on completion, and doubles as the town tavern where everyone drinks, brawls, and complains. To ordinary people it is respectable and essential: the institution that turns desperate nobodies into working adventurers and keeps the monster population in check. To the adventurers themselves it is a cheapskate landlord that skims fees, docks pay for property damage, and posts suicide missions next to lost-cat jobs with a completely straight face.

STRUCTURE: The Guild is a kingdom-wide organization with a branch in every town of note. Each branch is run by receptionists who handle registration, quest assignment, and payout, backed by a prosecutor or assessor for disputes and damages. Adventurers are ranked by accumulated achievement, and the card system means your reputation travels with you. The Axel branch is the busiest rookie processor in the kingdom; the Capital branch handles the highest-tier work. Its receptionists have seen everything, expect the worst, and are perpetually, professionally tired.

Eris Church.text:
The Eris Church is the respectable, mainstream faith of Belzerg, dedicated to the goddess Eris, who guides the souls of the departed and blesses the living with fortune and protection. Its churches are dignified stone buildings found in every town, staffed by clergy who provide healing, blessings, and, crucially, resurrection services for adventurers who can afford them. The Church is calm, orderly, and pointedly restrained, winning converts through quiet reliability rather than aggressive recruitment. It is the faith of choice for nobles, merchants, and anyone who wants their religion to be respectable.

STRUCTURE: The Church maintains a formal hierarchy of clergy, from local priests up through senior officials, and operates the kingdom's most trusted resurrection and healing services. Its relationship with the Adventurers Guild is symbiotic: the Guild produces casualties, and the Church, for an appropriate donation, brings a fraction of them back. Eris is depicted as a modest, kind goddess, and her clergy cultivate the same image.

Axis Cult.text:
The Axis Cult is the loud, fanatical, socially oblivious faith devoted to the water goddess Aqua, headquartered in the holy hot spring city of Alcanretia. Where the Eris Church is restrained, the Axis Cult is the opposite in every measurable way: its members recruit with terrifying enthusiasm, treat every conversation as a conversion opportunity, and pursue potential converts with a persistence that borders on the supernatural. Their devotion to Aqua is completely, unbearably sincere. They are widely regarded as a nuisance and occasionally as a menace, and they are entirely unbothered by either reputation.

STRUCTURE: The Cult centers on Alcanretia and its Grand Temple, with devotees spreading outward to recruit across the kingdom. It is led by senior figures like the high priest Zesta and includes memorable devotees like Cecily. The Cult's purification and water magic is genuinely powerful, which is the detail everyone forgets while fleeing its pamphlets. Membership is aggressively easy to obtain and nearly impossible to escape.

Demon King's Army.text:
The Demon King's Army is the existential threat that the entire Kingdom of Belzerg is organized against: a vast force of monsters, devils, undead, and dark magic commanded from a distant castle behind an ancient barrier. Led by the Demon King and his powerful generals, the army has waged a generations-long war to conquer the human kingdoms, pushing them back to a defensive line that Belzerg's frontier holds at great cost. To the people of Belzerg, the army is a distant dread in the north, real but abstract, the reason adventurers exist and the frontier is garrisoned.

STRUCTURE: The army is organized under the Demon King's generals, each a powerful individual commanding a portion of his forces and often operating with significant autonomy. Generals range from siege commanders and infiltrators to chimeras and contract devils, and their varied methods reflect the army's reach: open warfare on the frontier, sabotage and assassination in the heartland, and slow corruption everywhere the barrier's influence spreads. The closer to the Demon King's castle, the more organized and lethal the forces become.

Crimson Demons.text:
The Crimson Demons are a clan of extraordinarily powerful mages living in an isolated highland village, instantly recognizable by their red eyes, dark hair, and compulsively theatrical behavior. Every Crimson Demon delivers dramatic self-introductions, adopts an edgy chosen name, and treats ordinary life as an opportunity for maximum flair. They are among the strongest magic-users in the world, a fact somewhat obscured by their insistence on narrating their own actions like the protagonists of a story only they can see. To outsiders they are baffling, exhausting, and not to be provoked.

STRUCTURE: The clan is centered on the Crimson Demon Village and its magic academy, where young prodigies are trained in advanced magic and, with equal seriousness, in the proper form of a dramatic entrance. The clan is loosely governed by its most accomplished members and united by shared heritage rather than formal hierarchy. Megumin and Yunyun both hail from here. The village is functionally independent, protected less by walls than by the certain knowledge that invading it means facing a settlement full of casual, overwhelming firepower.

Elroad Interests.text:
Elroad Interests represents the wealthy casino nation of Elroad and its network of gambling houses, financiers, and commercial concerns, a foreign power whose influence runs on money rather than magic or faith. Elroad is richer, cleaner, and more condescending than Belzerg, a nation built on the mathematics of the house always winning, and its interests extend wherever there is profit to be made or a debt to be collected. To Belzerg it is a useful, faintly untrustworthy neighbor; to visiting adventurers it is a beautiful trap that sends them home broke.

STRUCTURE: Elroad's power is concentrated in its casinos, especially the Grand Casino of the capital, and administered by managers, financiers, and cashiers like the sharp Vanessa, who reads a gambler's finances and breaking point at a glance. Belzerg maintains an embassy in Elroad, staffed by the perpetually weary Takeshi Nagumo, largely to extract stranded citizens and smooth over the diplomatic incidents that Belzerg adventurers cause with distressing regularity.

The Kingdom of Belzerg.text: The Kingdom of Belzerg is a human nation locked in a slow war with the Demon King's army. Its name is said to echo the word berserk, which its wealthier neighbors find hilarious, and it is widely regarded by nations like Elroad as a kingdom of muscle-headed barbarians. Belzerg runs on the Adventurers Guild, adventuring pays badly, winters are cruel to the broke, and the safest place in the whole kingdom is the beginner town of Axel, far to the south from the Demon King's territory.

Axel, the Beginner Town.text: Axel is the town farthest from the Demon King's lands and therefore the safest, which is why every new adventurer starts here leveling up on weak local monsters like giant toads and low-level slimes. It is peaceful, cheap, and full of rookies, guild regulars, and the occasional retired villain running a shop. The Adventurers Guild, its attached tavern, the market, and the ring of low-level ruins on the outskirts make up most of a young adventurer's entire world.

The Two Goddesses.text: Two goddesses shape Belzerg's faith. Eris, goddess of luck, is modest, competent, and the object of the respectable mainstream Eris Church; she secretly walks among mortals as a thief named Chris. Aqua, goddess of water, is powerful in her true domain of purification and resurrection and comprehensively useless in daily life; her followers, the Axis Cult, are a beloved-by-none menace. The two churches maintain a petty, undignified, and extremely public rivalry.

Guild Ranking System.text: The Adventurers Guild ranks adventurers from F (rookie) through S (legendary). Most new adventurers start at F-rank and progress through completing quests, demonstrating competence, and surviving long enough to matter. Advancement is evaluated by guild staff based on quest completion rate, difficulty of completed quests, and general reputation. Most adventurers plateau at D or C rank. B-rank is considered elite. A-rank is hero-class. S-rank is legendary and extremely rare. Kazuma's party is famously difficult to rank because their individual power levels are wildly inconsistent: Megumin can level a castle but collapses after one spell, Darkness cannot hit anything, and Aqua's combat effectiveness depends on whether the enemy is undead.

Adventurer Economics.text:
Adventuring in Belzerg is a real job that pays badly, on purpose. The guild posts bounties in Eris (named after the goddess of luck), and the scale is built so money is always tight.

THE WAGE. Chores such as cabbage picking, deliveries, pest control, and guard duty pay 500 to 2,000 Eris: a night indoors and a meal, if you are careful. Standard hunts like a giant toad cull or a goblin scouting party pay 3,000 to 10,000, a few days of breathing room. Serious work, a cleared nest, a dangerous escort, a mid dungeon boss, pays 10,000 to 40,000. Major regional threats pay 40,000 to 120,000, much of which any repair bills you earned reclaim before you leave the hall. Only an arc finale or a Demon King's general pays more, and the assessor arrives before the celebration ends.

THE DRAIN. Living costs are modest but constant: a bunk, food, repairs, potions. The guild pays a posted bounty in full at the desk, then garnishes any standing debt from it automatically; the drain is debt and damages, never a commission on the work. Property damage caused on a quest is billed to the adventurer who caused it, which is why Kazuma's party owes more than most. Windfalls evaporate by genre law; a good week ends roughly where it began. The difference between rich and broke in Axel is one property-damage assessment, and for adventurers who break things, it always comes.

The Isekai Phenomenon.text: Belzerg receives a steady trickle of people reincarnated from another world, sent quietly by the goddess Aqua (or previously Eris) to help fight the Demon King. Each is allowed one divine gift or cheat item. Most choose powerful weapons, unique abilities, or stat boosts; Kazuma chose the goddess Aqua herself out of spite, which removed her from her post and stranded her in the mortal world. Crucially, the program is quiet divine policy, not public knowledge. The only ones who know otherworlders exist are the goddesses and their most senior clergy, the Demon King's inner circle, certain perceptive devils, and the otherworlders themselves. Ordinary Belzergers have no idea people arrive from another world; they read otherworlders as odd travelers from somewhere very far away, with strange habits and stranger comparisons. Otherworlders privately carry knowledge from their previous world, concepts like dynamite, kotatsu tables, and convenience store food, occasionally useful and frequently irrelevant. Most end up as mid-tier adventurers rather than the heroes they expected to be, and most learn quickly to keep the details of their arrival to themselves.

Explosion Magic and the Crimson Demons.text: Explosion magic is the pinnacle of offensive magic: a single, devastating blast that obliterates everything in the target area. It is also absurdly impractical, requiring enormous mana reserves and leaving the caster completely drained after a single use. It crowns the three-tier Detonation Series; the lower tiers, Blasting Magic and Detonation Magic, are respectable trades, which is exactly why its devotees refuse to cast them. The Crimson Demons of the Crimson Demon Village are a clan of humans with innate magical talent, red eyes, dark hair, and an overwhelming tendency toward theatrical self-presentation (chuunibyou). They were originally created by a reincarnated Japanese scientist who genetically engineered a population of magically gifted humans and, in the process, somehow encoded dramatic personality traits into their genes. Every Crimson Demon has a grandiose name, a signature introduction pose, and the genuine magical power to back up their theatrics. The pairing is famous but lopsided: the clan's actual milestone is Advanced Magic, and adulthood is measured by it. Specializing in Explosion is regarded even inside the village as a prodigy's eccentricity, one part genius and three parts stubbornness, and the clan's most famous daughter is celebrated and teased for it in equal measure.

The Demon King's Barrier and Generals.text: The Demon King rules from a castle far to the north of Belzerg, protected by a powerful magical barrier. The barrier is maintained by designated generals and cannot be breached while they hold their posts. The Demon King has eight generals, each with unique abilities and semi-independent agendas. Several have been defeated by Kazuma's party through luck, exploitation of specific weaknesses, and strategic incompetence that somehow works out. Two generals, Wiz and Vanir, defected entirely and now run shops in Axel. The remaining generals are eccentric, dangerous, and often more interesting than the Demon King himself.

Hot Spring Culture in Belzerg.text: Hot springs are a vital cultural and economic institution in Belzerg, especially in the city of Alcanretia. The Axis Cult, devoted to the water goddess Aqua, considers hot springs sacred and operates most of the bathing facilities in Alcanretia. Mixed bathing is common and a reliable source of comedic situations. The water in Alcanretia's springs is said to have healing properties, which the Axis Cult attributes to Aqua's blessing. Hot spring episodes are a genre staple: they create forced proximity, vulnerability, and comedy through the social dynamics of bathing culture. The springs are also a strategic target, as the Demon King's general Hans attempted to poison them to undermine the Axis Cult's power base.

Chris and the Chivalrous Thief.text: The Chivalrous Thief is a mysterious figure who steals dangerous holy relics from the houses of corrupt nobles. The thief is actually Chris, who is herself the mortal disguise of the goddess Eris. Eris walks among humans in this form to observe and occasionally intervene when divine artifacts fall into dangerous hands. As Chris, she is energetic and mischievous, in contrast to her calm and gentle divine persona. She taught Kazuma thief skills including Steal and Bind, and considers him a friend and occasional accomplice. The dual identity is one of the series' longest-running secrets: Aqua knows Chris is Eris and delights in teasing her about it.

Dust and the Dragon Knights.text: Dust is a delinquent adventurer in Axel who was formerly a Dragon Knight, an elite military unit that fights from dragonback. He abandoned his post under circumstances he refuses to discuss and now lives as a broke, womanizing, gambling adventurer who is somehow always around when trouble happens. His party consists of Keith (archer), Taylor (swordsman), and Rin (wizard), all of whom are more competent than Dust's reputation suggests. When Kazuma and Dust swapped parties for a day, Dust's party proved significantly more functional, which says more about Kazuma's party than about Dust's.

Keele's Dungeon.text: An underground dungeon complex near Axel, originally built as the laboratory and refuge of the arch-wizard Keele. After Keele's death, the dungeon became infested with undead and traps, and the Adventurers Guild designated it as a mid-level proving ground. The upper floors are manageable for adventurers who have moved past giant toads; the deeper levels are genuinely dangerous and poorly mapped. The guild charges a small entrance fee and maintains a checkpoint at the entrance. Keele's personal chambers, sealed behind powerful wards at the deepest accessible level, are the subject of a standing guild bounty that nobody has collected.

The Kingdom of Elroad.text: A wealthy nation west of Belzerg, known for its casinos, its money, and its unwavering conviction that Belzerg is populated by barbarians. Elroad's economy runs on gambling, tourism, and entertainment. The royal family maintains power through a web of gambling debts owed by the nobility, creating a system where everyone owes everyone and stability is maintained through mutual financial destruction. Elroad is technically allied with Belzerg against the Demon King but contributes money rather than soldiers. Adventurers from Belzerg visit for the casinos and the work. They leave broke.

Wiz and Vanir: Villains Who Run Shops.text: Two of the Demon King's generals defected and now operate retail businesses in Axel. Wiz, a powerful lich and former barrier-keeper, runs a magic shop at a permanent loss because she keeps buying cursed merchandise and selling useful items below cost out of guilt. Vanir, a duke of hell with the power of foresight, manages the business side of the shop and is the only reason it has not closed. Vanir reads minds and makes predictions, abilities he uses primarily for retail and entertainment. Both are technically still generals. Neither has filed resignation paperwork. The guild is aware of their status and has decided that as long as they are running shops instead of armies, the situation is preferable to the alternative.
