RESEARCH: escorting a scholar to a ruin, specimens for Wiz, testing a suspicious potion. MERCANTILE: a stall to mind, a debt to collect politely, a rival shop to outsell, a Vanir contract to survive. SMALL CRIME: a pickpocket ring, counterfeit charms, a smuggler with a sympathetic story. LARGE CRIME: a noble's missing tax cart, a quartermaster who keeps two ledgers. RIVALRY: a challenge from another party, a duel with rules, a contest the town takes too seriously. PERFORMANCE: the Nightless City needs a stand-in, a wedding needs a bard, a festival needs a mascot. NATURE: a blighted grove, a river that changed course, a forest that keeps its own rules. WEATHER AND SEASON: snow roads, floods, the Winter Shogun's circle, a heatwave emptying the wells. TRAINING: sparring a rookie squad, drilling a village militia, being the practice target. DIPLOMACY: two villages and one bridge, a demi-human envoy, a devil with paperwork. SECRETS: a locked annex, a pending shelf, a held letter, what a general's grudge is really about. COMEDY CONSEQUENCE: the party's own history pinned to the board with fine print. WAR ADJACENT, NORTH ONLY: patrols, holding lines, scouting, reconnaissance for veterans.

Rotation rule: a board never repeats a family, culls and escorts are at most one posting each, toads and cabbage appear only in season and at most once, and investigations, disputes, and social work appear as often as anything with a blade.

Belzerg Price Guide.text:
The Axel guild publishes these rates, and every shopkeeper in the kingdom pretends not to follow them. Prices vary by region and haggling, but always start from here, and the same thing costs the same thing from one scene to the next.

PER-UNIT BOUNTIES (paid at the desk, arithmetic stated): Flying cabbage, 200 Eris each if intact, 50 if bruised, 2,000 for a swarm-leader. Giant toad, 400 per corpse delivered on top of the 6,000 completion pay. Goblin ear, 300. Slime core, 150. Undead cleared, 500 each. Named or rare monsters carry their own posted price.

LIVING COSTS: Stable bunk 100. Guild dormitory bunk 300. Inn room 800 to 1,500 a night. Cheap meal 100 to 300, a proper dinner 500. Tavern round 50 a mug. Public bath 100, an Alcanretia sacred spring 300. Healing potion 1,000, mana potion 1,500, antidote 500. Weapon or armor repair 500 to 3,000. Horse hire 1,000 a day.

GEAR AND ENCHANTED ITEMS by rarity, placed within the band by how strong the item is (its total stat bonus): Common, 200 to 1,500. Uncommon (about 1 to 5 total bonus), 1,500 to 6,000. Rare (about 6 to 11), 6,000 to 30,000. Epic (about 12 to 19), 30,000 to 150,000. Legendary (about 20 and up), 150,000 to 1,000,000, and almost never on a shelf. Mythic and Unique items are not sold; they are found, earned, or stolen. Commissioning an enchantment costs the same band as buying the finished item, plus materials.

PROPERTY DAMAGE (billed only for damage the party actually caused, sized to what broke): a window, door, or market stall 500 to 3,000. A shop interior or a wall 10,000 to 50,000. A whole building 50,000 to 200,000. A landmark or a town-scale disaster 300,000 and up. Fights in the wild cost nothing; monsters do not file claims.

SELLING: shops buy at a third to half of these prices, less from anyone with a Property Damage Record. Wiz pays above market and loses money doing it. Vanir pays exactly what the item is worth to you, which is worse.

Necromancy Licensing in Belzerg.text:
Belzerg licenses a small number of necromancers under crushing regulation, and the guild enforces it. A licensed necromancer carries a laminated card, files a consent form for every deceased person they raise (signed in life, or witnessed by clergy after), submits to monthly audits, and completes a mandatory two-day ethics seminar with the Eris Church. The dead are, in a surprising number of cases, the first to ask to see the card.

Licenses are revoked by guild audit: missing consent forms, raising on consecrated ground without church sign-off, or letting the raised wander unsupervised. A revoked card is punched through with the guild's VOID stamp and must be surrendered, though in practice many former practitioners keep them as a grievance. Unlicensed necromancy is a crime prosecuted by the kingdom, and in Axel that means Sena.

Axel's cemetery on the north edge of town is consecrated ground maintained by the Eris Church, which is why weak undead there are rare and treated as training for rookies. A necromancer strong enough to raise consecrated dead in numbers is a genuine threat to the town, and everyone in the guild knows it.

Learning Drain Touch.text:
Drain Touch is the most useful skill in Axel that nobody advertises: siphon life or mana through a touch, then keep it or hand it to an ally. It began as a lich's technique, but it is NOT undead-only. Any adventurer of any class or race can learn it, because skills in Belzerg are learned by being shown them by someone who has them, or by stubborn practice.

WHO TEACHES IT. Wiz, at Wiz's Magic Shop in Axel, is the known teacher. Ask, and she demonstrates it on your own hand, apologizes, and undercharges. One finished lesson is enough to learn the skill. Other holders can teach it the same way: liches and undead officers of the Demon King's army, reformed undead, dhampirs, Licensed Necromancers, and any adventurer who already learned it.

WITHOUT A TEACHER. Deliberate practice works. Try to draw a trickle of mana through a touch, fail, and try again. The second time it works, the skill is yours.

WHAT IT COSTS. Almost nothing in coin. The price is social: the Eris Church disapproves, Axis priests reach for purification, and using it on a friend without asking is a quick way to lose one. The art grows from Drain Touch itself through Mana Leech, Chill Grasp, and Life Siphon, up to techniques only a lich lord would recognize.

FROM LEVEL 5. Any adventurer from character level 5 can also spend an ability point to unlock the Drain Touch ability directly. Using it is practice: each successful drain counts toward learning the skill itself. Drain Affinity can also be chosen at a level-up trait pick.

Divine Magic and Healing Magic.text:
Belzerg has two great schools of restoration, and they are not rivals so much as neighbors who borrow each other's ladders.

DIVINE MAGIC is faith made practical. It is learned through a church, Eris or Axis or a god of one's own, and it does what only a god can: purifies curses and corruption, blesses allies, turns and destroys undead, wards off devils, and calls the dead back to life. Its healing is broad and holy, and that is exactly the problem for some patients: holy power and the undead do not mix, which is why Wiz faints when a priest gets enthusiastic. That includes a necromancer's own raised dead: a divine heal lands on them as an attack, and no priest has ever accepted 'it was meant kindly' as an excuse.

HEALING MAGIC is medicine with magic in it. No god, no tithe, no paperwork with the church. It is the strongest school for putting a body back together: wounds, poison, disease, broken bone, lost flesh, curses lodged in the body, and the minute after a heart stops. It works on anyone, undead and devils included, and its spells recover quickly, so a healer can keep working long after a priest has run out of miracles. Healers learn from other healers and from clinic work.

Most good parties want both. The priest saves the day; the healer saves the next morning.

Write Your Own.name: Write Your Own
Write Your Own.description: Write the opening instructions the narrator should use to begin your story.

🖋️ Write Your Own.name: 🖋️ Write Your Own
🖋️ Write Your Own.firstQuest: Continue the player's authored backstory, centered on its most immediate hook.
🖋️ Write Your Own.storyStart:
[ You are creating your own character and backstory from scratch. Your history, motivations, and circumstances are yours to define. The world of Belzerg will accommodate whoever you decide to be. ]

The Adventurers Guild in Axel is where nearly everyone's story in this kingdom begins, whatever road brought them here. The hall is warm and noisy, the quest board is crowded with postings, and the receptionist behind the counter has registered every kind of person imaginable without once looking surprised.

Whoever you are, whatever you were before, the guild does not much care. It cares whether you can take a quest and come back alive. That is the whole entrance exam.

Your history is your own to tell, and the world will take it as given.
🖋️ Write Your Own.description:
✍️ MAKE IT YOURS · open-ended
Write your own backstory. Belzerg will continue from wherever you start. End with how you arrived at your starting location.

🚪 Just Arrived.name: 🚪 Just Arrived
🚪 Just Arrived.firstQuest: Enter Axel and do whatever you came here to do.
🚪 Just Arrived.storyStart:
[ You are a traveler arriving at the town gate of Axel, the Town of Beginnings, at midday, with your belongings on your back and your reasons your own. Who you are, where you came from, and what you want from this ridiculous, generous country is entirely yours to decide, starting now. ]

The gate guard waves you through without looking up from an argument about lunch. Inside, Axel is doing what Axel does: adventurers comparing wounds and exaggerations on the guild steps, a market crier promising prices that cannot possibly be sustainable, laundry strung between windows like festival flags, somewhere a distant explosion that absolutely nobody reacts to.

The guild is ahead on the main street if you want work. The market square is to the right if you want trade. The chapel bell is ringing the hour if you want quiet, and the tavern is loud already if you want the opposite.

Nobody here knows you. In a town like this, that is not loneliness. That is an open ledger, first page blank, and the pen is in your hand.
🚪 Just Arrived.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · open-ended
Midday at Axel’s town gate with a bag, a little coin, and no story yet. No goddess, no debt, no destiny, just you and the Town of Beginnings. The simplest way in: walk through the gate and start living.

✨ Reincarnated and Regretting It.name: ✨ Reincarnated and Regretting It
✨ Reincarnated and Regretting It.firstQuest: Register at the Adventurers Guild and survive your first day in Axel.
✨ Reincarnated and Regretting It.storyStart:
[ You are a newly arrived otherworlder, reincarnated into the Kingdom of Belzerg after a death you would rather not describe. A goddess offered you a second life in a fantasy world, you made choices under pressure, and now you are standing on the ground floor of the Adventurers Guild in Axel, the beginner town, with modern knowledge, no local currency, and the growing suspicion that you made a terrible decision. ]

You died. It was not heroic. Then a goddess offered you a second life in a fantasy world and, under pressure, you made some choices you are already questioning. Now you are standing in the Adventurers Guild in Axel, surrounded by people who belong here and know how things work, while you are trying to remember if 'Eris' is the currency or the goddess. Both, apparently.

The guild hall is warm, noisy, and smells like stew and ambition. A receptionist behind the counter is processing registrations with the patience of someone who has done this a thousand times. The quest board by the door is thick with postings. Most of them involve toads.

Your new life starts here. It is already going worse than advertised.
✨ Reincarnated and Regretting It.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You died, met a goddess, chose poorly, and woke up in Axel with nothing but regret and a divine gift of questionable value. The isekai experience, played for comedy.

🪪 Fresh Off the Card.name: 🪪 Fresh Off the Card
🪪 Fresh Off the Card.firstQuest: Take your first quest from the board and make enough to cover tonight's inn.
🪪 Fresh Off the Card.storyStart:
[ You are a brand-new adventurer who registered at the Axel guild today. Your card is freshly issued, your class is entry-level, and your funds are almost gone. You have no party, no reputation, and no idea what you are doing. ]

The ink on your Adventurer Card is barely dry. It displays your name, your class, and a set of statistics that the receptionist glanced at without comment, which you have decided to interpret as encouraging.

The guild hall around you runs on a rhythm you do not know yet. Veterans occupy the good tables and speak in shorthand about quests you have never heard of. A party in the corner is arguing about reward splits. Someone near the bar is loudly recounting a triumph that grows more impressive each time they tell it, and the people listening have clearly heard it before.

The quest board by the door is the whole world right now. Toad extermination. Cabbage harvesting. Goblin subjugation for those with a death wish or a party. The payouts look small until you convert them into meals and inn nights, at which point they look smaller.

You have enough coin for tonight and not tomorrow. Somewhere in that board is your first job, and everyone in this room started exactly where you are standing.
🪪 Fresh Off the Card.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
No divine backstory. You grew up in Belzerg, registered at the guild, and your Adventurer Card is still warm from the press. Time to find out if this career choice was smart.

💥 Crimson Demon Abroad.name: 💥 Crimson Demon Abroad
💥 Crimson Demon Abroad.firstQuest: Register at the Guild with a suitably dramatic introduction and find a worthy target for your magic.
💥 Crimson Demon Abroad.storyStart:
[ You are a Crimson Demon: crimson eyes, dark hair, advanced magic, and a dramatic self-introduction you have been rehearsing since childhood. You have come to Axel to register as an adventurer and show the world what a Crimson Demon can do. ]

You arrived in Axel this morning and have already introduced yourself to three strangers with your full name, title, and signature pose. None of them asked. Two of them walked away. One applauded, which was gratifying until you realized they thought it was a street performance.

The guild hall is smaller than your village's academy cafeteria. The adventurers here are... modest. Their magic is modest. Their ambitions are modest. You are not modest. Your robes billow despite the lack of wind. Your staff hums with barely contained power. The receptionist is watching you with the expression of someone who is already calculating property damage estimates.

This town has no idea what just walked through its gate.
💥 Crimson Demon Abroad.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You are a Crimson Demon who has left the village to make your name. You have red eyes, a dramatic title, and magic that levels buildings. Axel is not ready.

💧 Devoted to the Water Goddess.name: 💧 Devoted to the Water Goddess
💧 Devoted to the Water Goddess.firstQuest: Find work in Axel despite your affiliation, and maybe change one mind.
💧 Devoted to the Water Goddess.storyStart:
[ You are a devout member of the Axis Cult, newly arrived in Axel. Your faith is sincere, your enthusiasm is genuine, and your organization's reputation precedes you everywhere you go. ]

You have come to Axel to spread the word, and you are aware, in the abstract, that this will be difficult. The Axis Cult is beloved by its members and endured by everyone else, and the gap between how you feel about your faith and how strangers react to it is something you have decided to treat as a challenge rather than a verdict.

The guild hall goes fractionally quieter when your affiliation becomes obvious. Someone finds an urgent reason to study the quest board. A priest of the rival church, present at the bar, develops a sudden interest in their drink. You have seen this before, in every town.

But your faith is real. Your purification magic works, your devotion to the water goddess is unshakeable, and when the undead come, the people who cross the street to avoid you today will be very glad you are here. That is a comfort you have learned to carry.

For now, you need work, lodging, and perhaps a single person in this town willing to hear you out.
💧 Devoted to the Water Goddess.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You believe in the water goddess and you are not quiet about it. Your purification magic is real. Your social life is over. The pamphlets are ready.

👑 Noble on the Run.name: 👑 Noble on the Run
👑 Noble on the Run.firstQuest: Establish yourself as an adventurer before your family tracks you down.
👑 Noble on the Run.storyStart:
[ You are a member of a Belzerg noble family who has abandoned your duties to become an adventurer. Your family is looking for you. You chose Axel specifically because it is the last place anyone would expect a noble to go. ]

The guild registration asked for your name and you gave one that is not yours. The receptionist did not blink. In Axel, false names are a courtesy nobody questions.

Your gear is too good for a rookie and you know it. The armor fits better than anything the forge across the square sells. Your manners are a tell: you said 'please' and 'thank you' to the receptionist and she looked at you like you were speaking a foreign language. Nobody in Axel talks like that.

Somewhere back home, a letter you left is being read. An engagement you refused is being renegotiated. A parent you love but cannot obey is dispatching someone to bring you back. You have until they find you to become someone they cannot simply summon home.

The quest board is waiting. Your old life is not.
👑 Noble on the Run.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
Your family wants you married, managing estates, and behaving. You want to hit things with a sword. You chose Axel because nobody important comes here.

🕶️ The Defector.name: 🕶️ The Defector
🕶️ The Defector.firstQuest: Take a beginner quest and maintain your cover. Do not reveal what you can actually do.
🕶️ The Defector.storyStart:
[ You are a former member of the Demon King's army who has defected to Belzerg. Your combat skills and insider knowledge far exceed anything Axel's adventurers possess. You registered under a false name. Nobody knows what you were. ]

The receptionist accepted your registration without suspicion. Your new Adventurer Card has a name that is not yours and a class that undersells you by several threat categories.

You are standing on the guild floor in borrowed civilian clothes, surrounded by adventurers who could not survive a week in the territory you just left, and trying to remember how normal people introduce themselves. The quest board is covered in jobs your old self would have found insulting. Giant toads. Cabbage harvesting. Guard duty.

You are going to have to take one of these and pretend it is difficult. The receptionist glances at you again. She probably does this with everyone. Probably.
🕶️ The Defector.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You served the Demon King's army. You left. Now you are in Axel with a fake name, real skills, and a past that would change everything if anyone found out.

💰 Merchant's Gambit.name: 💰 Merchant's Gambit
💰 Merchant's Gambit.firstQuest: Set up your merchant business. Find buyers, negotiate prices, make rent.
💰 Merchant's Gambit.storyStart:
[ You are a traveling merchant who has arrived in Axel to establish trade. Your guild card reads 'Merchant' and your stats favor negotiation over violence. Your cart is parked outside. Your inventory is your livelihood. ]

The road to Axel was long but profitable in theory: a town full of adventurers who need supplies constantly and have quest income to spend recklessly. Your cart survived the trip, your goods are inventoried, and the market square is spread out in front of you, loud with haggling and opportunity.

The forge needs wholesale materials. The inn needs provisions. The adventurers need equipment they will break within the week and replace at your stall, which is the single most reliable business model in the kingdom. Rookies buy cheap, veterans buy quality, and everyone buys healing potions.

The competition is unusual. One magic shop is run by a woman so softhearted she prices genuinely valuable stock below cost, which is either charity or a slow-motion bankruptcy. Another counter is run by a proprietor who somehow knows what a customer wants before they say it, which makes competing on persuasion a losing proposition. The economics of this town do not follow the usual rules.

Your business instincts are sharp. Your purse is going to need them sharper.
💰 Merchant's Gambit.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You came to Axel with goods to sell and a business plan. The cart survived the road. The plan may not survive the market.

🔨 The Craftsman's Shop.name: 🔨 The Craftsman's Shop
🔨 The Craftsman's Shop.firstQuest: Set up your workshop and find your first customers among Axel's adventurers.
🔨 The Craftsman's Shop.storyStart:
[ You are a skilled craftsman who has come to Axel to set up shop. Your profession is your identity and your income. Adventurers are your customer base: careless, constant, and always breaking something. ]

Axel is, from a craftsman's perspective, an extremely good business decision. The town processes an endless stream of adventurers who damage their equipment with creative regularity and possess just enough quest income to pay for repairs. Demand here is not a hope. It is a certainty.

Your tools are unpacked and your workspace is taking shape. The market square outside carries the noise of commerce: haggling, cart wheels, the ring of the town forge already at work. You will need to establish yourself against tradespeople who have been here for years and know every regular by name.

The trick is reputation. Do good work at a fair price, and word travels through the guild hall faster than any advertisement. Do shoddy work, and it travels faster still. Adventurers are careless with gear and merciless about craftsmen who waste their money.

Your hands know the trade. Now the town has to learn your name.
🔨 The Craftsman's Shop.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You came to Axel to open a shop, not swing a sword. Forge, brew, enchant, or weave. The adventurers need someone who makes things instead of breaking them.

🕯️ Second Chance.name: 🕯️ Second Chance
🕯️ Second Chance.firstQuest: Report your failed quest to the guild, figure out what killed you, and start rebuilding from nothing.
🕯️ Second Chance.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer who died during a quest and was resurrected by a priest in Axel. You woke up in the Eris Church with no equipment, a resurrection bill, and fragmented memories of what killed you. ]

Dying, it turns out, is the easy part. The resurrection was expensive, disorienting, and left you lying on a church pew in borrowed clothes while a patient priest explained that you had been dead for about a day and a half.

Your gear is gone. Your party, if you had one, is not here. Your purse is definitely gone. What remains is your adventurer card, your skills, your guild registration, and a bill from the church that makes property damage look affordable.

The guild hall is across the square. Your name is still on the active roster. Your last quest is listed as 'incomplete.' The receptionist will want a report on what happened. You are still trying to remember.

Most adventurers do not get a second chance. Time to use it.
🕯️ Second Chance.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You died on a quest. A priest brought you back. You owe them money, you lost your gear, and your last memory is something with too many teeth.

🥀 The Lone Survivor.name: 🥀 The Lone Survivor
🥀 The Lone Survivor.firstQuest: File the quest report with the guild and decide whether to continue adventuring alone or find a new party.
🥀 The Lone Survivor.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer whose party was lost during a quest gone wrong. You survived alone and made it back to Axel. The guild requires a debriefing. The tavern is where you are sitting instead. ]

The tavern is loud around you and you are not hearing any of it. Your drink is untouched. Your guild card is on the table, next to a quest report you have not filled out because writing what happened means making it real.

The guild receptionist has been patient. She has seen this before: the adventurer who comes back alone. She will need the report eventually. The details of what happened, the names of who did not return, and the official assessment of what went wrong.

You know what went wrong. You just do not know if you are ready to do this again. But rent is due, your skills are all you have, and the quest board does not care about your feelings.

The first step is filling out the report. The second is deciding what comes next.
🥀 The Lone Survivor.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
Your party did not make it. You did. The guild wants a report. The tavern wants a tab. You want a drink and a reason to go back out there.

😈 The Devil's Deal.name: 😈 The Devil's Deal
😈 The Devil's Deal.firstQuest: Register at the guild (or check in) and begin adventuring before the devil's favor comes due.
😈 The Devil's Deal.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer who made a binding contract with a devil in exchange for power, information, or a favor. The contract was fulfilled exactly as promised. The cost is becoming apparent. ]

The deal was simple. The terms were written clearly. You read them, you understood them, and you signed because the alternative was worse. The devil smiled, the contract glowed, and you received exactly what was promised.

The problem is not what you received. The problem is what you owe. Devil contracts do not deal in coin. They deal in obligations, services, and the kind of favors that make you a useful asset to beings who think in centuries.

You are in Axel now, stronger or more informed than you were before the deal, carrying a mark on your soul that a church priest would notice if they looked closely. The devil will call in the favor eventually. Until then, you are an adventurer with an edge and an expiration date.

Use the time well.
😈 The Devil's Deal.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You made a deal with a devil. The terms were clear. The consequences were not. Now you have power you did not earn and a debt you cannot pay in coin.

🎻 The Bard's Journey.name: 🎻 The Bard's Journey
🎻 The Bard's Journey.firstQuest: Perform at the guild tavern and find a party that needs a bard, or a story worth singing about.
🎻 The Bard's Journey.storyStart:
[ You are a traveling performer who has come to Axel because the town is famous for producing the most entertaining disaster stories in the kingdom. Your instrument is your weapon. Your audience is your income. ]

Axel's reputation preceded it: a beginner town where somehow, impossibly, a party of misfits has defeated multiple Demon King generals through a combination of luck, incompetence, and the occasional genuine miracle. The stories are too good not to collect. The tavern audience is too drunk not to appreciate a good song.

You set up in the guild tavern with your instrument and your charm. The adventurers around you are a goldmine of material: the swordsman who cannot hit anything, the mage who can only cast one spell, the healer who spends more on wine than potions. Every conversation is a potential ballad.

The guild also takes performer registrations. Bards are welcome on quest parties for morale. The pay is terrible. The stories are priceless.
🎻 The Bard's Journey.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You travel, you sing, you collect stories. Axel is full of idiots doing incredible things. The material writes itself.

🐾 The Demi-Human Newcomer.name: 🐾 The Demi-Human Newcomer
🐾 The Demi-Human Newcomer.firstQuest: Register at the guild, find a party that values your unique skills, and figure out the chair situation.
🐾 The Demi-Human Newcomer.storyStart:
[ You are a demi-human arriving in Axel for the first time. Your non-human features (ears, tail, or other traits) draw attention. Belzerg is not hostile to demi-humans but it is not built for them either. ]

The guild registration form had a checkbox for 'non-human features' that you filled in with more detail than the form expected. The receptionist handled it professionally, which was a relief after the gate guard who asked if your tail was a fashion accessory.

Axel is a human town that accepts demi-humans without fully understanding them. The chairs are not designed for tails. The helmets do not accommodate ears. The inn charges standard rates but the beds are the wrong shape. You will adapt. You always do.

The adventurers in the guild hall are mostly human and mostly curious in a friendly way that is only slightly exhausting. Your skills translate. Your enhanced senses are an advantage on quests. Your ears pick up conversations across the room that you were not meant to hear.

Welcome to Axel. You are exotic, which here means interesting, which here means everyone wants to know if the ears are real. They are.
🐾 The Demi-Human Newcomer.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You are not human, and in Belzerg that means extra paperwork, curious stares, and the constant question of whether the inn charges extra for tails.

⛪ The Eris Faithful.name: ⛪ The Eris Faithful
⛪ The Eris Faithful.firstQuest: Settle into the parish and take on your first healing assignment, whether at the church or on a quest party.
⛪ The Eris Faithful.storyStart:
[ You are an Eris Church priest assigned to or visiting the Axel parish. Your divine magic is focused on healing, blessings, and quiet service. The Axis Cult's local chapter tests your patience daily. ]

The Eris Church in Axel is modest, clean, and dignified: a stone building with a simple steeple, a small nave, and the quiet atmosphere of a place where people come for healing, blessings, and the specific comfort of a faith that does not ambush you with pamphlets.

You know your goddess. You serve her faithfully. Your healing magic is reliable, your blessings are genuine, and your patience is tested daily by the Axis Cult chapter across town that insists on recruiting outside your front door.

The guild needs healers on quest parties. Adventurers who come back broken need someone at the church to put them together. The community needs a steady hand. You are that hand, even when the other hand is writing a formal complaint about the pamphlets in your donation box.
⛪ The Eris Faithful.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You serve the goddess of luck and fortune. Your faith is quiet, your healing is reliable, and you are deeply tired of the Axis Cult across town.

🗝️ Woke Up in a Dungeon.name: 🗝️ Woke Up in a Dungeon
🗝️ Woke Up in a Dungeon.firstQuest: Find the dungeon merchant, piece together how you got here, and make it back to the surface alive.
🗝️ Woke Up in a Dungeon.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer who has regained consciousness in the upper floors of Keele's Dungeon with no memory of how you arrived. Your gear is intact. Your adventurer card is in your pocket. The last thing you remember is blurry. ]

The ceiling is stone. The floor is damp. The torch in the wall bracket is guttering, which means someone lit it recently, which means someone was here, which might have been you.

Your gear is intact and your adventurer card confirms your identity, which is reassuring because the rest of your recent memory is a gap you cannot fill. You are in a dungeon. The upper floors, based on the difficulty of what you can hear moving around the corner. Manageable. Probably.

A merchant has set up a supply stall somewhere on this level. You passed a sign that said so. Finding her would mean finding answers, or at least finding someone who saw you arrive.

First: survive the floor. Then: figure out what happened.
🗝️ Woke Up in a Dungeon.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · guided
You do not remember how you got here. The walls are stone. The air is stale. Something is moving in the dark. Your adventurer card is in your pocket. That is a start.

🥾 The Wanderer.name: 🥾 The Wanderer
🥾 The Wanderer.firstQuest: Rest, eat, and take a quest. Decide later whether Axel is a stop or a destination.
🥾 The Wanderer.storyStart:
[ You are a traveling adventurer with no fixed home, arriving in Axel as one more stop on a long road. You carry your possessions with you. You owe nothing to anyone here, and nobody here owes anything to you. ]

You have walked into a lot of towns. This one is smaller than most and friendlier than it needs to be, a beginner town at the safe southern edge of the kingdom where the monsters are weak and the adventurers are young.

The guild hall is warm and loud and smells of stew that has been on the boil since before you arrived. Nobody knows you. Nobody is watching you. There is a particular kind of freedom in that, and a particular kind of loneliness, and you have long since stopped trying to separate the two.

You have coin enough for a few days, skills earned on roads harder than the one that brought you here, and no particular reason to leave quickly. The quest board has work. The tavern has a bed. The town has that settled, unhurried quality that makes travelers stay longer than they planned.

Rest. Eat. Take a quest. Decide later whether Axel is another stop or something else.
🥾 The Wanderer.description:
🏠 AXEL BEGINNINGS · open-ended
You have been walking for a while. No hometown pulling you back, no destination pulling you forward. The road brought you to Axel because roads end somewhere.

🐸 Lakewatch Season.name: 🐸 Lakewatch Season
🐸 Lakewatch Season.firstQuest: Complete your first day of toad watch without losing the logbook, the bell, or your footing.
🐸 Lakewatch Season.storyStart:
[ You are the newly hired lake watch at Riverhead Lake, a half day's walk upstream of Axel. The town council pays a modest retainer for someone to live in the lakeside cabin, count the Giant Toads that wake out of the spring mud, and ring the warning bell if any of them start moving toward the farms. It is the first week of spawning season. The bell rope is frayed. The previous watch left without collecting their final pay. ]

The cabin came with the post: one room, one kettle, one logbook with columns labeled TOADS SIGHTED and TOADS INCOMING. The last entry from your predecessor reads, in increasingly large handwriting, 'they remember me.' There is no entry after that.

The lake this morning is beautiful. Mist on the water, birds in the reeds, and out along the shallows, a line of low green humps that might be rocks. You have counted them three times. The count keeps going up.

The pay is honest, the view is unmatched, and Axel is close enough to visit on rest days. All you have to do is watch the water, keep the log, and never, under any circumstances, fall asleep in the open. It says that part twice.
🐸 Lakewatch Season.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
The town pays someone to count the Giant Toads coming out of the spring mud and ring a bell if they head for the farms. That someone is now you. Nobody explained the second part of the job.

🌱 Farm Country Volunteer.name: 🌱 Farm Country Volunteer
🌱 Farm Country Volunteer.firstQuest: Take a posting from the Greenhollow notice board and earn the village's confidence.
🌱 Farm Country Volunteer.storyStart:
[ You are a newly registered adventurer working village pest-control contracts in the Southern Farmlands, the safest region in the kingdom. Your employer is effectively the whole village of Greenhollow. Your pay is modest, your lodging is a loft above a barn, and your reputation here is entirely front-loaded on whether you damage anything. ]

Greenhollow's village green smells of cut grass and woodsmoke, and the notice board by the well is thick with the kind of work nobody writes into a song: a burrowing pest under the east field, something taking chickens, a fence dispute that has apparently been running for three generations.

The farmers watch you with polite, calculating interest. They have hosted adventurers before. They have also billed adventurers before, and they keep a ledger of both.

It is a soft landing into the profession. The monsters here are the weakest in Belzerg and the consequences of failure are financial rather than fatal. Somewhere north of here is a war, and nobody in this village has thought about it today.

Cabbage season is three weeks out. Everyone keeps mentioning it.
🌱 Farm Country Volunteer.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
You signed on as village pest control in the safest country in Belzerg. It pays badly, the work is honest, and the cabbages are about to become a problem.

🥬 Harvest Champion.name: 🥬 Harvest Champion
🥬 Harvest Champion.firstQuest: Catch enough flying cabbages to make quota before the festival judging begins.
🥬 Harvest Champion.storyStart:
[ You are a seasonal hire at Threshing Green, the great communal harvest floor of the Southern Farmlands, standing atop the Cabbage Watchtower on the opening morning of the autumn migration. In Belzerg, cabbages fly. They ripen, they lift off, and they head south in vast angry flocks, and every village between here and the coast pays catchers by the head. The festival at the end of the week crowns a Harvest Champion. The current champion has held the title for six years and does not intend to share it. ]

From the tower you can see the whole operation: netting crews stretching lines between poles, farmers with padded gloves, a priest blessing a wagon for reasons nobody questioned. The wind smells like soil and faintly, unmistakably, of coleslaw.

Someone below blows a horn. On the northern horizon, a green smudge rises off the fields and turns, with what you would swear is intent, toward the Green.

The quota is two hundred head. The champion catches that before lunch. The cabbages, the veterans say, have had all summer to think about this.
🥬 Harvest Champion.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
Greenhollow's autumn cabbage harvest pays adventurers by the head. The cabbages, this being Belzerg, do not come quietly. You have a net, a tower, and a quota.

🎣 Delta Fisher.name: 🎣 Delta Fisher
🎣 Delta Fisher.firstQuest: Sell your catch, then find out what has silenced the eastern channel.
🎣 Delta Fisher.storyStart:
[ You are a working fisher based in Stiltwater, the stilt-built town in the Riverlands delta. Your livelihood is the water: common catch for the market, rare specimens for the alchemists' agents who come down from Alcanretia. You know the channels. You are registered with the guild but you are a fisher first. ]

Stiltwater creaks gently underfoot, the whole town raised on posts above the slow brown water, walkways swaying as people cross them without noticing. The morning catch is being auctioned under the market awning and the smell is fish, tar, and river.

Your boat is tied at the landing. The ferrymen are arguing about crossing prices, as they do. An alchemist's agent is standing at the back of the auction waiting for something rarer than what is on the table.

You make a decent living at this, better than most adventurers manage, and you have the specific satisfaction of a trade that rewards patience over violence.

The eastern channel has gone quiet this week. No fish, no birds. Two boats went in and have not come back out.
🎣 Delta Fisher.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
You work the delta channels for a living. The fishing is good, the water keeps secrets, and something in the eastern channel has gone very quiet.

✨ Claim on the Shimmer.name: ✨ Claim on the Shimmer
✨ Claim on the Shimmer.firstQuest: Work your claim's first pan of the season and find out why the assay office undervalues the Shimmer.
✨ Claim on the Shimmer.storyStart:
[ You are the new holder of a registered prospecting claim on the Gilded Mere, the wide shining backwater of the Riverlands. You bought the papers, the pan, and the stilted shack off a prospector named Bett, who signed everything with remarkable speed and left on the next barge. The shallows here glow gold at dusk, and every season a few independents pull enough sheen out of the mud to keep the dream alive. The kingdom's assay office rates the Mere as worthless. The kingdom's assay office keeps a permanent clerk here anyway. ]

The shack is sound, mostly. The jetty leans. Your nearest neighbors are a widow who pans at dawn and a pair of brothers who argue so loudly you can navigate by them in fog.

On your first evening, a man in a coat too clean for the Riverlands knocks, introduces himself as a buyer of 'maps, samples, and discretion,' and offers you more for a sketch of your claim than Bett charged for the whole thing.

The water shimmers. The clerk watches. Bett, you notice, did not leave a forwarding address.
✨ Claim on the Shimmer.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
You bought a retiring prospector's claim on the Gilded Mere, shack included. The shallows glitter like a promise. The assay office says the glitter is nothing. Somebody is lying.

⚓ Dockside Arrival.name: ⚓ Dockside Arrival
⚓ Dockside Arrival.firstQuest: Get through customs, convert your coin, and find your first paying work in Belzerg.
⚓ Dockside Arrival.storyStart:
[ You have just disembarked at Saltspire Harbor on Belzerg's southeastern coast, arriving by sea rather than by road. Your money is foreign, your accent is wrong, and your guild card is either freshly issued or from somewhere else entirely. Nobody here knows you. ]

The quays are chaos: cranes swinging cargo, dockhands moving crates at a run, gulls stealing anything set down for more than a moment. The salt wind cuts through everything. Three languages are being argued in within earshot and at least two of the arguments are about the same manifest.

Belzerg proper begins somewhere past the customs house. From the cliff tiers above the harbor you could see the whole kingdom's southeast laid out, if you climbed up and if you had a reason to.

You have a berth's worth of possessions, whatever you carried off the ship, and the particular freedom of a place where nobody has any expectations of you yet.

The customs queue is long. The taverns are close. Both are, in their way, a start.
⚓ Dockside Arrival.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · guided
You came off a ship at Saltspire Harbor with foreign coin, no local contacts, and a very flexible plan.

🔆 Keeper of the Sunward Light.name: 🔆 Keeper of the Sunward Light
🔆 Keeper of the Sunward Light.firstQuest: Learn the lamp routine from the keeper and get through your first night watch on the Sunward Light.
🔆 Keeper of the Sunward Light.storyStart:
[ You are the new assistant keeper of the Sunward Light, the tall white tower that marks the safe channel along the Sunward Coast. The post came with room, board, wages, and a one-page contract containing a single duty written three ways: the lamp does not go out. The keeper who hired you is patient, weathered, and kind, and has a habit of measuring the fuel stores while looking at the sea rather than the fuel. ]

The lamp room smells of oil, salt, and something older underneath, like a church. The mechanism is beautiful, brass and crystal, and the flame burns steady with a faint color you have decided not to have an opinion about yet.

Below the tower, Wrecker's Cove keeps its bones: old hulls on the rocks from the years before the light, when the coast made a different kind of living. Some families in the village still do not climb the Lightkeeper's Stair, out of respect or its opposite.

Your watch begins at dusk. The keeper's last instruction of the day is cheerful and unexplained: 'If the sea goes quiet all at once, feed the lamp early.'
🔆 Keeper of the Sunward Light.description:
🌾 THE GENTLE SOUTH · open-ended
Assistant keeper at the great coastal light. Good pay, long stairs, one rule: the lamp never goes out. The old keeper measures fuel in 'calm nights,' and will not say what a loud night costs.

🎲 Casino Refugee.name: 🎲 Casino Refugee
🎲 Casino Refugee.firstQuest: Find paying work in Elroad to clear your gambling debt and fund the trip home.
🎲 Casino Refugee.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer who traveled to Elroad for the casinos, lost badly, and needs to earn passage home. Your guild card is Belzerg-issued. Your debt is Elroad-documented. The embassy is sympathetic but cannot help financially. ]

The Grand Casino's golden light feels considerably less inviting when your purse is empty and your tab is not. You remember arriving confident. You remember a run of luck that felt like destiny. You remember, with painful clarity, the exact moment you decided to double down.

Elroad is beautiful, expensive, and entirely unsympathetic to foreigners who confused entertainment with investment. The cashier's cage is staffed by a woman who read your finances in a single glance and has been politely, ruthlessly correct about them ever since. The dealers were friendly. The math was not.

The local guild branch accepts Belzerg cards. The quest board pays in local currency at rates that assume competence you will now have to demonstrate. The Belzerg embassy is staffed by one exhausted diplomat who has processed your exact situation dozens of times, can point you toward honest work, and cannot lend you a single coin.

You are broke in a rich country, and the house is still open. The only way out is through.
🎲 Casino Refugee.description:
🎰 ELROAD AND THE NIGHT · guided
You came to the casino nation to gamble. You lost. Now you need to adventure your way out of a foreign country's debt ledger.

🐎 The Long Shot.name: 🐎 The Long Shot
🐎 The Long Shot.firstQuest: Get your horse ready, or at least present, for the opening race of the Velvet Downs season.
🐎 The Long Shot.storyStart:
[ You are the newest owner on Paddock Row at the Velvet Downs, Elroad's storied racetrack, having accepted a racehorse in settlement of money you were owed. On paper this made sense: the horse, Meadowlord's Ransom, has champion bloodlines, a stall at the Downs, and paid-up racing fees for the season. In person, Meadowlord's Ransom is a large, glossy, deeply theatrical animal who runs beautifully for exactly as long as no one is watching, spooks at grass, of which racetracks are famously composed, and screams at his own reflection in the water trough, but only, the groom notes, 'when he thinks it is winning.' ]

Paddock Row is racing's backstage: steam off the morning gallops, trainers arguing in three currencies, touts selling tips they demonstrably do not believe. Your neighbors sized you up in one glance and have been generous ever since, in the way people are generous to the doomed.

The opening card is posted. Entry is paid, forfeit is not refundable, and scratching a horse at the Downs requires a form so humiliating it is framed in the Rail Bar.

The groom, who came with the horse and is the only creature Ransom trusts, gives you the season's honest odds: 'He has one great race in him. He is saving it for something. I would like to know what.'
🐎 The Long Shot.description:
🎰 ELROAD AND THE NIGHT · guided
A debt was settled by handing you a racehorse. The horse is slow, dramatic, and afraid of grass. Racing season opens this week, and everyone at the Downs already knows your name, which is worse than it sounds.

📦 The Pending Shelf.name: 📦 The Pending Shelf
📦 The Pending Shelf.firstQuest: Survive your first week of stamping at Goldgate and learn what belongs, and does not belong, on the Pending Shelf.
📦 The Pending Shelf.storyStart:
[ You are the newest junior clerk in the Customs Hall at Goldgate Crossing, the fortified toll bridge where the Belzerg highway crosses into the casino nation of Elroad. The pay is steady, the stamps are satisfying, and the traffic is a parade of merchants, pilgrims, gamblers going in hopeful and coming out philosophical. Your training covered tariff tables, seizure procedure, and forty minutes of unbroken eye contact from the senior clerk regarding the Pending Shelf, which holds confiscated items awaiting rulings that never arrive. The training on the shelf itself was one sentence: leave it pending. ]

The hall is marble, because Elroad paid for half of it and Elroad does not do modest. Queues braid and unbraid. A woman ahead of you in the tariff line is declaring, with total confidence, eleven crates of 'ordinary non-magical hats.'

The Pending Shelf sits behind the duty desk in its own quiet. A sealed deck of cards. A birdcage, covered. A ledger with a lock and no keyhole. This morning there are two new items, though no clerk remembers logging them in.

Your stamp is inked. The queue is endless. The shelf, the senior clerk says without looking up, counts itself.
📦 The Pending Shelf.description:
🎰 ELROAD AND THE NIGHT · guided
Junior clerk at the great toll crossing into Elroad. Stamp, weigh, wave through. Easy work, except for the shelf of items nobody claims, nobody clears, and nobody dusts. It gained two entries this week.

🏮 Nightless City Drifter.name: 🏮 Nightless City Drifter
🏮 Nightless City Drifter.firstQuest: Find paying work in Nightless City and a place to sleep that is not the street.
🏮 Nightless City Drifter.storyStart:
[ You are an adventurer who has arrived in Nightless City, the perpetually-lit entertainment hub of Belzerg. You are not a rookie but you are broke, and this city is expensive. ]

The golden light of Nightless City does not care what time it is and neither do you, because you lost track somewhere between the gate and the third street performer. The city hums with permanent energy: markets, taverns, gambling halls, and entertainment venues operating around the clock because the magical lighting system has no off switch.

Your guild card works here. What does not work is your coin purse, because it is empty, and pinned inside it is a receipt from a tavern called the Gilt Fool with your signature on a tab for an amount that cannot possibly be correct. The barkeep, a broad woman with the smile of someone who has heard every excuse, is leaning on the counter when you walk in.

'Morning. Or evening. Who cares.' She slides the ledger across. 'You had the imported stuff, tipped the band, and offered to buy the table a round. Twice. The guild board is over there if you need work, and you need work.'

The quest board in Nightless City pays well because the clientele is wealthy and the problems are strange. You are going to need both of those things.
🏮 Nightless City Drifter.description:
🎰 ELROAD AND THE NIGHT · open-ended
You woke up in Nightless City with your guild card, an empty coin purse, and a bar tab you do not remember signing. The city does not sleep, and until you settle that tab, neither can you.

🌙 Night Shift.name: 🌙 Night Shift
🌙 Night Shift.firstQuest: Work a night in the Nightless City and make a payment before your lender's patience thins.
🌙 Night Shift.storyStart:
[ You are a debtor working nights in the Nightless City, the Heartland's city of eternal lanterns, where the entertainment quarter never closes and the ledgers never sleep either. The debt is yours; how you earned it is your business, and everyone here respects that the way they respect all professional privacy, which is to say they have already guessed. Your lender is patient, pleasant, and keeps your paper in a drawer with a lot of other paper. The arrangement is simple: something on account every week, and the pleasantness continues. ]

The Night Market at second bell is the city with its sleeves rolled up: porters hauling crates of lantern oil, cooks feeding the shift change, dealers of every legal thing and several negotiable ones. Work is everywhere for someone willing. Guard a stall, carry a package, walk a nervous jeweler home, stand in a queue for a noble who cannot be seen queueing.

A man from Axel once told you, over dice, that the trick to debt is owing so much they cannot afford to lose you. You have seen where that trick ends. He was buying drinks with borrowed money at the time, and he seemed genuinely happy.

The lanterns hiss. The market breathes money. Dawn is a rumor here, and your payment is due before it.
🌙 Night Shift.description:
🎰 ELROAD AND THE NIGHT · guided
You owe money to serious people, and the city where the lanterns never go out always has work after dark. Every job pays. Every job costs. The trick is reading which is which before dawn.

♨️ Hot Spring Pilgrim.name: ♨️ Hot Spring Pilgrim
♨️ Hot Spring Pilgrim.firstQuest: Find the local guild branch, register or check in, and enjoy the springs without joining the Cult.
♨️ Hot Spring Pilgrim.storyStart:
[ You are a traveler who has arrived in Alcanretia, the hot spring city and holy seat of the Axis Cult. Whether you came for the healing waters, the mountain scenery, or a spiritual calling, you are here now and the Cult is already very interested in you. ]

The mountain road was worth it. Alcanretia is genuinely beautiful: steaming pools nestled between mountain peaks, the sound of falling water everywhere, and architecture that mixes elegant bathhouse design with enthusiastic religious decoration. The springs are real and the healing properties are genuine.

You were approached by a recruiter within thirty seconds of entering the city gates. You have been offered three pamphlets, two blessings, and one free trial membership that you did not request. The recruiters are fast, persistent, and apparently incapable of detecting the word 'no.'

The hot springs are calling. The Axis Cult is calling louder. The local guild branch is around here somewhere, if you can find it between the temples.
♨️ Hot Spring Pilgrim.description:
⛰️ HIGHLANDS AND WILDWOOD · open-ended
You traveled to the holy city of hot springs for the waters, the views, or the faith. The Axis Cult is thrilled to see you. Leaving will be the hard part.

🫖 The Free Retreat.name: 🫖 The Free Retreat
🫖 The Free Retreat.firstQuest: Enjoy the springs and get out of Springrest without joining the Axis Cult.
🫖 The Free Retreat.storyStart:
[ You are a guest at a wellness retreat in Springrest Village, in the mountains below the holy city of Alcanretia. The flyer said FREE: hot springs, cold plunges, healthy meals, guided reflection. The flyer was accurate. What the flyer did not say is that the retreat is run by the Axis Cult, that 'guided reflection' is a recruitment seminar with towels, and that checkout requires a signature on a form whose top copy is a feedback survey and whose bottom copy, faintly, is not. ]

To be fair, the baths are wonderful. The cold spring snaps your mind clear, the mountain air is like new glass, and the food is the best you have eaten in a season. The staff are relentlessly, sincerely kind. That is the trap. Everyone here is having a genuinely lovely time, and about a third of them arrived as skeptics and now lead the morning chants.

A staff member refills your tea and leaves the day's itinerary. Someone has hand-drawn a little blue goddess in the margin, giving you a thumbs up.

The mountain pass down to the highway is open. The paperwork between you and it is not long. It is just never, somehow, finished.
🫖 The Free Retreat.description:
⛰️ HIGHLANDS AND WILDWOOD · guided
You signed up for a free mountain wellness retreat. The waters are real, the meals are generous, and the extremely friendly staff would love just one more signature. You have begun reading the forms.

🌲 Wallwatch.name: 🌲 Wallwatch
🌲 Wallwatch.firstQuest: Stand your first watch at Thornwatch and hear the hunters out about the Wall.
🌲 Wallwatch.storyStart:
[ You are the newest guard at Thornwatch Camp, a palisaded logging operation in the Great Wildwood, the old forest east of Alcanretia. The company pays well because the wood is dense, the monsters are patient, and the camp sits nearer than anyone likes to the Mossgate Wall, a moss-covered line of ancient stonework running through the deep trees that no map explains and no charter mentions. Standing order number one is painted on the palisade gate: no felling within sight of the Wall. ]

The Palisade Yard runs on routine. Saw teams out at dawn, wagons loaded by noon, watch rotations posted on the lodge door. The cook is a retired adventurer who seasons everything like she is still trying to cover the taste of rations. The work songs are good. People look up between verses.

Your first evening, a hunter comes in off the Deep Wood Trail and quietly reports her paces to the foreman: the count from the boundary stake to the moss line. The foreman thanks her and does not write it down. He has stopped writing it down, you learn, because the number has stopped being the same twice.

Watch is four hours, wall side. The trees there grow very straight, very old, and very listened-to.
🌲 Wallwatch.description:
⛰️ HIGHLANDS AND WILDWOOD · open-ended
Guard work at a logging camp deep in the Great Wildwood. Honest pay, good company, one standing order: nobody works within sight of the Mossgate Wall. The hunters say the sightline is shorter than it used to be.

🧙 The Village Prodigy.name: 🧙 The Village Prodigy
🧙 The Village Prodigy.firstQuest: Take a quest from the village board, or find the outsiders who arrived from Axel.
🧙 The Village Prodigy.storyStart:
[ You are a young Crimson Demon mage in the village where you grew up: red eyes, dark hair, genuine magical talent, and a dramatic self-introduction that you have rehearsed a thousand times. You are skilled, powerful, and completely alone because your peers find you either intimidating or exhausting. ]

The village square is busy with Crimson Demons doing Crimson Demon things: dramatic proclamations, explosion practice, unnecessarily theatrical grocery shopping. You are standing at the edge of it, practicing your entrance pose for the thirty-seventh time this week.

Your magic is exceptional. Your academy scores were top of the class. Your self-introduction includes a custom light effect that took six months to perfect. None of this has produced a single lasting friendship, a fact you handle by training harder and practicing louder.

The quest board at the village hall has postings: local monster hunts, academy errands, and a rumor about outsiders visiting from Axel. Outsiders who might actually be impressed by a dramatic self-introduction.
🧙 The Village Prodigy.description:
💥 CRIMSON DEMON COUNTRY · guided
You are the most talented mage of your generation and the loneliest. You have been practicing your dramatic self-introduction for years. Nobody has ever stayed to hear it.

📖 The Explosion Researcher.name: 📖 The Explosion Researcher
📖 The Explosion Researcher.firstQuest: Complete your latest explosion test and decide whether to continue research or take your skills into the field.
📖 The Explosion Researcher.storyStart:
[ You are a Crimson Demon academic at the village's magic academy, researching explosion magic theory. Your work is important, underfunded, and behind schedule. Your test site is a series of craters on the practice range that the village considers scenic. ]

The Explosion Practice Range is yours for the next two hours, which is enough time for exactly one test detonation and forty-five minutes of taking notes in the crater. Your research journals are stacked in your quarters. Your faculty advisor has sent three letters asking about your progress. You have read none of them because reading them would require confronting how little progress you have made.

The theory is sound. The practice is literally explosive. The gap between the two is where your thesis lives, assuming you survive the field testing.

Somewhere beyond the village, adventurers fight monsters with practical magic. You fight the boundaries of magical knowledge with controlled detonations and a notebook that is slightly singed.
📖 The Explosion Researcher.description:
💥 CRIMSON DEMON COUNTRY · guided
You are a Crimson Demon researcher studying explosion magic theory. Your thesis is overdue. Your test site is a crater. Your faculty advisor wants results.

🌳 Trial of the Deep Roots.name: 🌳 Trial of the Deep Roots
🌳 Trial of the Deep Roots.firstQuest: Survive the Trial of Adulthood Experience Package and earn a title you can live with.
🌳 Trial of the Deep Roots.storyStart:
[ You are a paying customer standing at the Root Entrance of the Great Tree Labyrinth, the vast tunnel network beneath the roots of the sacred tree in the Crimson Demon Highlands. The village's youth undergo their Trial of Adulthood here. Some enterprising villagers now offer the Trial of Adulthood Experience Package to outsiders: entry blessing, dramatic title ceremony, commemorative cape, and a guide. You bought the deluxe tier, which includes an eyepatch and a tragic backstory 'consultation.' The waiver you signed was fourteen pages, and every page had illustrations. ]

Your guide is a Crimson Demon teenager with excellent posture who introduced himself for four unbroken minutes and now refers to himself only as the Umbral Cartographer. He has a map. He has assured you the map is 'mostly a metaphor.'

The entrance breathes. That is the only word for it: cool air moving in and out of the root-arch with a slow patience that makes the torches lean. Below, the deluxe package promises, wait 'trials calibrated to your hidden potential,' which the waiver's margin note clarifies as 'monsters.'

The Umbral Cartographer strikes a pose at the threshold and waits. You realize he is holding it until you pose back.
🌳 Trial of the Deep Roots.description:
💥 CRIMSON DEMON COUNTRY · guided
The Crimson Demons sell a Trial of Adulthood Experience Package to tourists: enter the sacred labyrinth, receive a dramatic title, keep the cape. You bought the deluxe option. The labyrinth was not consulted.

🎓 Transfer Student.name: 🎓 Transfer Student
🎓 Transfer Student.firstQuest: Get through your first day at the magic academy and choose the title you will be known by.
🎓 Transfer Student.storyStart:
[ You are the first outsider in years admitted to study at the magic academy of the Crimson Demon Village, home of the kingdom's most powerful and most dramatic mages. Your letter of admission cited 'exceptional promise.' The letter also included a supplies list with three separate cape fittings, a form asking you to declare your Arch-Rival (leave blank if unassigned, one will be provided), and a warm note from the headmaster expressing hope that you would not be discouraged by the entrance examination, which for outsiders is 'mostly ceremonial, with some lightning.' ]

The academy grounds at morning bell are chaos of the highest production value. Students pose on staircases. Two twelve-year-olds duel over who gets to be called the Crimson Void, while a teacher grades their incantation delivery from a folding chair. Everyone has red eyes. Everyone. The effect from the gate is of standing before a theater troupe that could actually level a city.

Your homeroom teacher greets you kindly, hands you a seating chart, and asks, in front of everyone, the only question that matters here: 'And what shall the academy call you?'

Thirty pairs of crimson eyes turn to you with the hushed, ravenous hope that you will get this right.
🎓 Transfer Student.description:
💥 CRIMSON DEMON COUNTRY · open-ended
Admitted to the Crimson Demon village's magic academy as its only outsider student. Your eyes are the wrong color, your name is suspiciously pronounceable, and class participation is mandatory. So are titles.

🏛️ Capital Transfer.name: 🏛️ Capital Transfer
🏛️ Capital Transfer.firstQuest: Check in at the Capital Guild Hall, review the quest board, and take your first capital-level assignment.
🏛️ Capital Transfer.storyStart:
[ You are a mid-level adventurer who has transferred to the Royal Capital's Adventurers Guild branch. The capital is bigger, more dangerous, and more competitive than anywhere you have worked before. ]

The Capital Guild Hall is enormous. Three times the size of any branch you have seen, with multiple quest desks, a ranking evaluation hall, and a tavern wing that serves food you can actually identify. The adventurers here carry themselves differently: better gear, more scars, the quiet confidence of people who have fought things that do not exist in beginner zones.

The chief receptionist processed your transfer with professional efficiency and a glance at your record that lasted exactly one second too long. Then she set a quest sheet on the counter, face-down.

'Welcome to Capital Branch. Your first assignment is a retrieval for House Dustiness. A trade shipment vanished between the Marches and the capital last week. Three senior parties looked at it, asked questions, and handed it back.' She tapped the sheet. 'The pay is excellent. I am told that is not a good sign.'

The tavern wing is already loud. Somewhere in there, somebody knows why three experienced teams walked away from good money. Finding that somebody seems like a reasonable first day.
🏛️ Capital Transfer.description:
👑 THE HEARTLAND · guided
You have been transferred to the Royal Capital's guild branch. The quests are harder, the adventurers are better, and your first assignment involves a noble's missing shipment that three higher-ranked parties already declined.

🎭 The Political Visitor.name: 🎭 The Political Visitor
🎭 The Political Visitor.firstQuest: Navigate your first social obligation at court and decide how much of the political game you are willing to play.
🎭 The Political Visitor.storyStart:
[ You are a minor noble visiting the Royal Capital for political, family, or social obligations. You may be here for a court function, a business deal, a marriage negotiation, or to quietly escape one. The capital's noble quarter is your arena. ]

The Noble Quarter is beautiful in the way that expensive things are beautiful: deliberately, precisely, and with the implicit understanding that someone is paying for it. Walled estates line the streets, each one a statement about the family behind its gates.

Your lodgings are adequate. Your wardrobe is presentable. And on the writing desk, already unsealed because your family has no concept of boundaries, is the invitation to Lord Alexei Dustiness's estate for the betrothal dinner of two families whose land shares a river and whose lawyers share a grudge. You are here because your family holds a minor claim on the water rights and someone with the family name needs to be in the room when the contracts are read. That someone, by process of everyone else being busy, is you.

The dinner is tomorrow evening. Today, the capital's social season offers introductions, alliances, and the adventurers' guild hall, in case the political theater becomes unbearable and you need to hit something honest.
🎭 The Political Visitor.description:
👑 THE HEARTLAND · guided
You have come to the Royal Capital for a family wedding that is actually a land dispute. Your sword is less useful here than your patience, and your patience was already running thin on the coach ride in.

📯 Bridge Courier.name: 📯 Bridge Courier
📯 Bridge Courier.firstQuest: Establish yourself on the Millbridge courier roster and deliver your first sealed commission.
📯 Bridge Courier.storyStart:
[ You are a courier working out of Millbridge, the bridge town at the heart of the Belzerg Heartland, where the north road to the war and the east road to the coast cross the river within sight of each other. The Twin Toll Bridges carry soldiers, grain, nobles, pilgrims, and post, and the couriers' bench outside the Waystation Guildpost is where all of it gets sorted into saddlebags. You have a license, a satchel, and a reputation exactly as good as your last delivery. ]

The work is simple at the bottom of the roster: contracts to the mills, love letters to the garrison, a weekly packet of complaints from the Cartwrights' Yard to the toll office, which the toll office uses to level a table. The pay improves with discretion. The interesting work, the sealed work, goes to couriers the guildpost trusts, and trust in Millbridge is a currency with a ferocious exchange rate.

This morning the bench is crowded and the river is loud with spring. The postmistress calls your name and holds up two commissions: a fat, cheerful bundle of merchant mail going east, and a slim envelope, capital wax, no name on the outside, going north.

She does not say choose carefully. She charges extra for that.
📯 Bridge Courier.description:
👑 THE HEARTLAND · open-ended
Millbridge sits where the kingdom's roads cross its river, and everything that matters passes over its two bridges. You carry letters across them. Some letters are heavier than others.

⛏️ Stonecutter's Apprentice.name: ⛏️ Stonecutter's Apprentice
⛏️ Stonecutter's Apprentice.firstQuest: Prove your craft in Grausten and decide where you stand on the reopened seam.
⛏️ Stonecutter's Apprentice.storyStart:
[ You are a working craftsman in Grausten Quarry Town in the Eastern Foothills, trained in stone and mineral. Your standing here is earned through work rather than a guild card. Grausten supplies the kingdom's masons, smiths, and enchanters, and it has firm opinions about outsiders and about quality. ]

The quarry runs dawn to dusk and the sound of it is the town's heartbeat: hammers, wedges, and the periodic crack of split rock. Dust coats everything including you. From the upper terrace the whole excavation looks like an amphitheater built by something patient.

The stonecutters' hall smells of stove smoke and stone dust, and the walls display sample blocks the way other halls display trophies. Contracts get negotiated loudly. Every village in these hills insists its quarry is the finest in Belzerg and the argument has never been settled.

You have a trade, a bunk, and the respect that comes with competent work. Enchanting-grade mineral moves through here at prices the rest of the kingdom would find offensive.

A new seam has opened toward one of the old walled-off sections. The guild is split about it, and nobody who was here for the sealing will explain.

Master Doguro Iwasaki, the barrel-chested head of the stonecutters' hall and the man who signed your apprenticeship papers, finds you on the upper terrace and jerks his grey beard toward the old walled-off section. If the guild is going to argue about that seam all week, he says, he wants his own eyes on it first, and an apprentice to carry the lantern.
⛏️ Stonecutter's Apprentice.description:
⚒️ THE WORKING EAST · guided
You work stone in Grausten, the quarry town that supplies half the kingdom's smiths. The deep seams are reopening and nobody will say why they were sealed.

🔦 Gallery Number Nine.name: 🔦 Gallery Number Nine
🔦 Gallery Number Nine.firstQuest: Complete the first survey leg of the reopened gallery and log what the echoes are doing.
🔦 Gallery Number Nine.storyStart:
[ You are a licensed surveyor under contract to the Grausten quarry consortium, sent down to map the reopened workings the old masons called Gallery Number Nine. The stone here supplies half the kingdom's smiths, the seam that was reopened this year is the richest in living memory, and the consortium would like a nice clean chart with none of the historical commentary the last survey attempted. The last survey was in your grandmother's time. It was not completed. ]

The Echo Gallery earns its name honestly. Every hammer tap comes back doubled off the terraced dark, which is normal, and then comes back once more, a beat late and slightly softer, which the masons have collectively agreed is also normal. They are friendly, skilled, and superstitious in the practical way of people who work under a mountain: past the ninth marker post, nobody whistles, and after dusk, nobody goes at all.

Your kit is good, your lamp is full, and your contract has a clause you have read four times, in which the consortium disclaims responsibility for 'acoustic phenomena, temporal irregularities in same, and any measurements the surveyor cannot reproduce twice.'

The first marker post is ten paces in. Your tap goes out. Count the answers.

Gonzo Ishiyama, the consortium's terrace master, walks you in as far as the tally line himself, blast horn on his belt and no hurry anywhere in him. He says he will stay within horn's reach of your lamp, which past the ninth marker post is the closest thing to company the gallery allows.
🔦 Gallery Number Nine.description:
⚒️ THE WORKING EAST · guided
The quarry consortium reopened the deep gallery their grandparents sealed, and they are paying a surveyor to map it properly this time. The echoes come back late. Sometimes they come back improved.

🛡️ Garrison Transfer.name: 🛡️ Garrison Transfer
🛡️ Garrison Transfer.firstQuest: Report to the garrison commander and take your first patrol on the Marches.
🛡️ Garrison Transfer.storyStart:
[ You are an experienced adventurer who has transferred to Ashford Garrison on the contested Eastern Marches. This was your choice. The garrison commander has read your file, is unimpressed by it, and will form her own opinion. The war here is not a rumor from the north; it has come over the eastern ridge before. ]

Ashford is half village and half fortress, earthworks thrown up around what used to be an ordinary market town. It has been evacuated twice and rebuilt twice. The people who stayed have the specific hardness of those who expect a third time.

The muster yard is packed dirt and purpose. Soldiers form up for patrol without ceremony. A board on the wall carries both the duty roster and the names of those who did not come back, and nobody has proposed separating the two lists.

The fields east of the wall are worked in daylight and abandoned at dusk. Beyond them is the ridge, and beyond the ridge is territory Belzerg no longer claims in practice, whatever the maps say.

The comedy of the south does not reach this far. Here the job is holding a line with fewer people than the line requires.

Sergeant Jirou Kuroda collects you at the muster yard without a handshake and points you at the line, his repaired coat older than half the roster. Beside him a lean scout named Tama Sasaki looks you over the way she looks over terrain, then nods once, which at Ashford counts as a welcome.
🛡️ Garrison Transfer.description:
⚒️ THE WORKING EAST · guided
You requested a posting to the contested eastern border. The garrison is undermanned, the enemy is organized, and nobody here jokes about the war.

📒 The Quartermaster's Ledger.name: 📒 The Quartermaster's Ledger
📒 The Quartermaster's Ledger.firstQuest: Take over the Ashford supply ledger and decide what to do about the requisitions that do not add up.
📒 The Quartermaster's Ledger.storyStart:
[ You are the new supply clerk at Ashford Garrison, the earthwork fortress holding the kingdom's contested eastern border. The posting is real soldiering by adjacency: you count arrows, salt, boots and beer, and the garrison's fighting strength is exactly as good as your arithmetic. The quartermaster who requested you is sharp, tired, and honest, which is why she needs a second set of eyes. For over a year, sealed requisitions have drawn supplies for two units that no muster roll contains. The seals are genuine. The wagons leave through the Earthwork Gate at month's end and turn north. Her predecessor queried it once, was reassigned to a fort that turned out not to exist either, and has not written since. ]

The ledger room smells of tallow and wet earth. Outside, the garrison drills; the Marches' wind carries the sergeant's cadence over the wall in pieces.

The quartermaster gives you the keys, the cipher, and the courtesy of plain speech: 'Count everything twice. Flag nothing in writing. Whatever those two units are, somebody with a real seal feeds them, and I would like to know whether we are supplying heroes or a hole.'

Month's end is nine days out. The next requisition is already on your desk.

The quartermaster's second set of eyes turns out to come with a third. Sae Kuriyama, the sentry who tallies everything that passes the Earthwork Gate, has been told to match her counts against yours, and she waits by the ledger room door with her tally board and the patience of a fence post.
📒 The Quartermaster's Ledger.description:
⚒️ THE WORKING EAST · guided
Supply clerk at the eastern border garrison. The requisitions are signed, the seals are real, and a tenth of everything goes to units that do not exist. Your predecessor stopped asking. Then he stopped writing.

🕯️ The Windmere Inventory.name: 🕯️ The Windmere Inventory
🕯️ The Windmere Inventory.firstQuest: Begin the estate inventory at Windmere Hold without taking, or appearing to take, a side.
🕯️ The Windmere Inventory.storyStart:
[ You are a hired appraiser at Windmere Hold, the grey-walled seat of one of the Western Reach's old families, brought in from outside the region because everyone inside it is related to somebody. The old lord is three weeks dead. His heirs have gathered like weather. Your commission, signed by the family's lawman, is to inventory the estate: every blade, book, cup and acre, valued fairly, witnessed twice. Until the count is done, the will stays sealed. This arrangement was the old lord's last instruction, and nobody can decide whether it was prudence or a joke at their expense. ]

The Keep Hall is cold in the way of well-built old places, all banners and draft. The steward walks you past generations of portraits, each, he notes, painted 'before things soured' with whichever branch of the family is watching from it.

You are given a room, a ledger, and a boy to carry your scales. You are also given, within the first hour, three separate quiet offers of friendship from three separate cousins, each mentioning, in passing, how easily small things go missing in big houses.

The will sits in the lawman's strongbox. One page of it is sealed separately, in wax the color Harrowmoor Keep uses. In this hall, nobody says that name above a murmur.
🕯️ The Windmere Inventory.description:
🗿 OLD STONES AND COLD PLACES · guided
The old lord of Windmere is dead, the family is circling, and someone neutral has to count the silver. You are the someone. The will has a sealed page, and everyone knows who it concerns.

🗿 Prospecting the Ring.name: 🗿 Prospecting the Ring
🗿 Prospecting the Ring.firstQuest: Stake your salvage pitch on the Rubble Floor and flag your first fragments for the guild assessor.
🗿 Prospecting the Ring.storyStart:
[ You are a licensed relic prospector on the Rubble Floor of the Cracked Vale, the broken country of the Shattered Highlands, under the shadow of the Sundered Ring. Whatever the Ring was, it broke before the kingdom had a name, and the Vale is floored with its pieces. The salvage guild licenses pitches, buys fragments by weight and interest, and stamps the interesting ones PROMISING in a ledger nobody is allowed to copy. Prospectors will tell you, if you buy the drinks, that PROMISING fragments do not stay in the lockup. They are collected. Nobody has met the collector. ]

The work is real: rope, pry-bar, patience, and an eye for the difference between old stone and Stone That Was Something. The Vale is quiet in a way open country should not be. Sound arrives a little worn, as if it walked farther than it did.

On the ridge to the east stands the Standing Silhouette, which every prospector points out to newcomers exactly once and does not discuss after: a tall dark figure-shape against the sky that has, in living memory, always been there, and always been facing the Ring.

Your pitch is marked with painted stakes. The last holder's stakes are still there too, pulled up and stacked. Neatly.
🗿 Prospecting the Ring.description:
🗿 OLD STONES AND COLD PLACES · guided
Licensed salvage in the Shattered Highlands, where something old broke and did not finish falling. The guild pays for fragments and stamps the good ones PROMISING. The good ones are gone by morning.
