❄️ Last Stop Before the Ice.name: ❄️ Last Stop Before the Ice
❄️ Last Stop Before the Ice.firstQuest: Learn Hoarfrost Station's routines and keep the shelter ready for whatever comes off the ice.
❄️ Last Stop Before the Ice.storyStart:
[ You are the new station hand at Hoarfrost Station, the last manned waypoint in the Frozen Reaches, where the northern trails end and the deep ice begins. The station serves everyone the north produces: trappers, ice-road teamsters, mad scholars heading for the ruins, and the occasional adventuring party that read about the Winter Shogun and wants an introduction. Your contract covers firewood, the signal lamp, the shelter room, and clause nine, which states that all agreements at this station are 'subject to seasonal sovereignty' and which the stationmaster initialed on your behalf, saying you would rather not be the one whose handwriting is on it. ]

The shelter room is the station's heart: a long, low, timber hall you are to keep stocked, swept, and above freezing at all hours. The rules are carved over the hearth. Feed any traveler. Ask no debts of the dying. The lamp burns until dawn.

The stationmaster is a broad, calm woman who has wintered here eleven times, which the teamsters mention the way other people mention military rank.

Tonight the wind is straight off the ice, and somewhere far out, rhythmic and unhurried, something that is probably weather knocks twice.
❄️ Last Stop Before the Ice.description:
🗿 OLD STONES AND COLD PLACES · open-ended
Station hand at the last manned post before the deep ice. Board, bunk, and wages nobody argues with. The employment contract mentions the Winter Shogun the way sailors mention the sea: politely, and not twice.

🏰 Frontier Volunteer.name: 🏰 Frontier Volunteer
🏰 Frontier Volunteer.firstQuest: Report to the garrison commander and accept your first frontier assignment.
🏰 Frontier Volunteer.storyStart:
[ You are a mid-level adventurer or soldier who has volunteered for duty at the Frontier Fort, the last permanent settlement before the Demon King's territory. You have combat experience. This assignment requires it. ]

The Frontier Fort is everything the posting described and nothing the recruiter promised. Stone walls blackened by something that was not fire, weapon racks bolted to every corridor, and a garrison roster with more crossed-out names than active ones.

The commander processed your arrival without looking up from a field map pinned under a dagger. 'You can fight. Good. Patrol Three lost their scout yesterday to a Rookie Killer that wandered south of the barrier. I need someone who can track, shoot, or at minimum run faster than the person next to them.' She finally looked up. 'You ship out with Patrol Three at dawn. The route runs six leagues north along the ridgeline. If the fog rolls in, turn back. If something in the fog talks to you, do not answer it.'

The barracks are half-empty. The adventurers who are here eat quietly, check their gear twice, and sleep with their boots on. Nobody has asked your name. They will, if you come back.

In the supply room, quartermaster Seiji Yamabe issues your kit off a ledger balanced on one knee, with a look that says losing any of it would be taken personally. Across the barracks, a wiry soldier named Michiru Tosaka glances up from her half-maintained gear and tells you that you have her old scout's bunk, and that Patrol Three musters before first light.
🏰 Frontier Volunteer.description:
⚔️ THE WAR ROAD · guided
You volunteered for the frontier, where the garrison is short-handed and the posting board lists jobs that would make an Axel adventurer resign on the spot. Your first patrol leaves at dawn.

🛞 Escort to the North.name: 🛞 Escort to the North
🛞 Escort to the North.firstQuest: Report to the wagon master at the Northern Waystation and see the supply column through its next leg north.
🛞 Escort to the North.storyStart:
[ You are an escort guard with a supply column at the Northern Waystation, the fortified rest stop on the long road toward the Demon King's territory. Behind you is the kingdom: guild taverns, festival posters, complaint forms. Ahead is the road that all of it depends on, wagon after wagon of grain, steel, bandages and beer, moving north to the forts. The column pays well for blades and better for steadiness. You signed for both. ]

The waystation grounds are all business: wagons parked in rows, teams watered, a farrier working through a queue of horses with the calm of a man who knows the war cannot start without him. The talk around the cookfires is easy but has edges. People here have made the run before. They laugh at the same jokes, slightly faster, as if getting them done.

The wagon master walks the line at dusk, checking straps that were already checked. Nobody teases her for it. The northbound road out of the gate is wide, well kept, and empty in a way that a good road in good country never is.

Departure is at first light. The last poster on the waystation board is from Axel, advertising a festival. Somebody has written under it, without malice: 'hold one for us.'

Rokuro Tsuchida, the waystation's heavyset caretaker, hands the last of the resupply up onto the lead wagon and then climbs up after it; he is riding north with the column this run, on the reasoning that somebody should know every stone of the road. Petra Vollan, the column's smith, works the end of the farrier's queue beside the gate, checking shoes and straps with burn-freckled hands that miss nothing.
🛞 Escort to the North.description:
⚔️ THE WAR ROAD · guided
You signed on to escort supply wagons up the road to the front. Good pay, honest work, and a road where the jokes get quieter every mile marker. The veterans check the straps twice. You have started doing it too.

🌑 Behind the Lines.name: 🌑 Behind the Lines
🌑 Behind the Lines.firstQuest: Survive your first day in the Blighted March and choose: escape south, or learn why the tithe wagons run north.
🌑 Behind the Lines.storyStart:
[ You are a kingdom scout alone in the Blighted March, the outer province of the Demon King's Domain. Three nights ago your unit covered a retreat that saved the column and scattered the rearguard. You took a blow, lost the ridge line in the dark, and woke half buried in ash-grey soil with your weapon, your waterskin, and no friendly banner within two days' hard travel. The land here is not on fire and never was. It is worse than that: orderly. The roads are maintained. The ruins are occupied. The fields grow something in rows, and the rows are straight. ]

By day you have kept to the folds of the Grey Waste, where the ash drifts deep enough to hide a prone body. Patrols pass in pairs, unhurried. They are not searching for you. That is the part you keep turning over: nothing here behaves as if the war is close. It behaves as if the war is administration.

At dusk you saw wagons on the raised road the locals call the Tithe Road, rolling north under lantern light, escorted, laden, and quiet. No drivers sang. No guards complained. In your experience, that means fear, and money.

Your rations are gone. South is the border, the patrols, and home. North is the answer to a question your kingdom is losing soldiers for want of.
🌑 Behind the Lines.description:
⚔️ THE WAR ROAD · guided
The retreat went wrong and you woke up on the wrong side of the war, in the grey country where the Demon King's writ runs. No rescue is coming. What you do with that is the story.

Beginner's Shortsword.name: Beginner's Shortsword
Beginner's Shortsword.description: A cheap, slightly notched shortsword issued to every rookie who can afford one and pawned by every rookie who cannot. The steel is soft, the edge dulls quickly, and the balance is merely acceptable, but it holds up against slimes, giant toads, and the other weak monsters of the beginner region. It is reassuringly, defiantly ordinary, a weapon with no story to tell and no ambition beyond keeping its owner alive long enough to afford something better. Most adventurers remember theirs fondly. Most also replaced it as fast as they could. [Common]

Worn Shortbow.name: Worn Shortbow
Worn Shortbow.description: A well-used shortbow of plain wood, its finish rubbed away at the grip and its string replaced more times than the owner can count. It lacks power and range, but it is light, reliable, and honest, the kind of weapon that has quietly kept a rookie alive through a hundred giant-toad hunts. It will not impress anyone, and it was never meant to. It is a tool for putting an arrow in something at a modest distance, and it does that job without complaint or flourish. [Common]

Novice Wizard Staff.name: Novice Wizard Staff
Novice Wizard Staff.description: A simple wooden staff topped with a small, cloudy focusing crystal, issued to apprentice mages who have learned just enough magic to be dangerous to themselves. It steadies the flow of mana and helps shape basic spells, doing for a beginner caster what training wheels do for a bicycle. It will never channel anything impressive, but it turns a fumbled incantation into a functional one, which for a novice is the whole battle. Every great mage started with a stick very much like this one. [Common]

Dented Kite Shield.name: Dented Kite Shield
Dented Kite Shield.description: A battered kite-shaped shield of cheap iron, its face dented, scratched, and scorched from hard use and harder luck. The straps are worn but hold, and despite its sorry appearance it still does the one thing a shield must: it puts metal between you and the thing trying to kill you. Rookies favor it because it is affordable and forgiving, and veterans remember carrying one exactly like it before they could afford better. Each dent is a story, most of them embarrassing. [Common]

Adventurer's Leathers.name: Adventurer's Leathers
Adventurer's Leathers.description: A standard set of hardened leather armor, the default kit of every rookie who walks out of the Guild for the first time. It covers the vital areas, allows free movement, and offers genuine if modest protection against the weak monsters of the Axel region. It smells of oil and sweat and the specific optimism of someone who has not yet been swallowed by a toad. Practical, affordable, and entirely unglamorous, it is the armor that turns a hopeful nobody into a working adventurer. [Uncommon]

Guild Adventurer Card.name: Guild Adventurer Card
Guild Adventurer Card.description: The magical identification card issued to every registered adventurer, displaying name, class, level, skills, and core stats in glowing script that updates as the bearer grows. It cannot be faked or altered, which makes it a resume, a passport, and an instrument of public humiliation in equal measure: your actual capability is always one card-check away from being revealed. Guild staff, quest givers, and suspicious shopkeepers all check it. Losing yours is a bureaucratic ordeal. When its bearer dies for good, the card goes dark. [Unique]

Coin Purse (Nearly Empty).name: Coin Purse (Nearly Empty)
Coin Purse (Nearly Empty).description: A worn leather coin purse that has seen better, fuller days. It jingles when shaken, but the sound is thin and hollow, the unmistakable music of an adventurer between paydays. A few small-denomination Eris coins rattle around the bottom, enough for a cheap meal or a single drink but nowhere near enough for the bar tab, the potion restock, or the property-damage settlement looming on the horizon. Every adventurer in Belzerg owns one of these, and every one of them knows the specific dread of that hollow jingle. It is less an item than a state of being. [Common]

Cheap Healing Potion.name: Cheap Healing Potion
Cheap Healing Potion.description: A small vial of thin, cloudy red liquid, the most affordable healing option on any shop shelf. It closes minor wounds, dulls pain, and buys a few crucial moments in a fight, which is often exactly enough. The taste is medicinal bordering on punitive, and the effect is modest, but for a broke rookie standing between a toad and a bad afternoon, a cheap healing potion is the difference between a scare and a resurrection fee. Buy several. You will need them. [Common]

Emergency Rations.name: Emergency Rations
Emergency Rations.description: A compact bundle of dense, nutritionally adequate, aggressively flavorless field food: hardtack, dried meat, and something that claims to be fruit. It will not delight anyone, but it keeps an adventurer moving when there is no time to cook and no tavern for miles. Experienced parties always carry some and always complain about them. The rations last nearly forever, which is either a testament to preservation magic or a warning about what they are made of. Nobody has ever finished a piece and asked for more. [Common]

Crimson Demon Robe.name: Crimson Demon Robe
Crimson Demon Robe.description: The distinctive dark robe of a Crimson Demon mage, cut for dramatic silhouette as much as for magical function. The fabric is treated to resist singeing (a practical necessity when your entire culture practices explosion-adjacent magic) and enchanted to steady the flow of mana. It billows impressively in even the slightest breeze, which is not an accident: a Crimson Demon considers a robe that fails to billow during a dramatic self-introduction to be functionally broken. It is genuinely good mage's armor wrapped around an aesthetic non-negotiable. [Uncommon]

Priest's Vestments.name: Priest's Vestments
Priest's Vestments.description: The modest, dignified robes of a working priest, cut for freedom of movement during long healing rituals and marked with the quiet iconography of the faith. The fabric is blessed in a minor, practical way that steadies divine magic and lends a faint sense of calm to those nearby. They are the working uniform of the clergy who keep Belzerg's adventurers alive, and an Axis Cult version exists that is functionally identical but somehow manages to be louder about it. [Uncommon]

Party-Up Contract.name: Party-Up Contract
Party-Up Contract.description: A standard Guild form that formalizes a party, splitting quest rewards, shared liability, and (crucially) property-damage responsibility among its signatories. It is a dry legal document that has ended more friendships than any betrayal, because nothing tests a bond like arguing over percentages after a job. Signing one is the closest thing Belzerg has to a wedding vow: an optimistic commitment to shared misfortune. Read the liability clause carefully. Kazuma's party famously did not. [Unique]

Eris.name: Eris
Eris.description: The standard currency of Belzerg, named, with characteristic cheek, after the goddess Eris rather than her senior Aqua, a fact the Axis Cult considers a standing insult. Eris coins come in copper, silver, and gold denominations stamped with the goddess's modest profile. They are the lifeblood of the adventuring economy and the constant source of its misery: never quite enough to cover the bar tab, the potion restock, and the property damage all at once. An adventurer's relationship with Eris, the currency and arguably the goddess, is defined by chronic shortage.

Cursed Choker of Binding.name: Cursed Choker of Binding
Cursed Choker of Binding.description: An elegant black choker that Wiz swore was just a fashionable accessory. It tightens slightly when the wearer lies and cannot be removed without a purification spell. Wiz sold three of these last month. She has apologized to all the buyers. One of them is still wearing it because they think the tightening feature is useful for poker. [Common]

Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Staff.name: Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Staff
Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Staff.description: A serviceable magic staff that Vanir personally guarantees is not cursed, haunted, or sentient. The guarantee is technically accurate. The staff works perfectly and channels magic efficiently. The previous owner returned it because it makes a faint humming noise that sounds like quiet laughter when pointed at something expensive. Vanir denies hearing it. [Common]

Axel Guild Membership Badge.name: Axel Guild Membership Badge
Axel Guild Membership Badge.description: A small metal badge issued to registered adventurers of the Axel branch. Proves guild membership and current rank. Required for accepting quests, receiving bounties, and arguing about property damage deductions. Losing this badge costs 5,000 Eris to replace and the receptionist will sigh audibly. [Common]

Emergency Explosion Scroll.name: Emergency Explosion Scroll
Emergency Explosion Scroll.description: A single-use scroll containing a compressed Explosion spell, created by a Crimson Demon who felt that everyone should have access to the joy of explosions. The explosion is approximately one-third the power of a proper casting. The scroll is still enough to level a small building. The Crimson Demon who made it does not understand why the guild restricted sales. [Common]

Wiz's Bargain Healing Potion.name: Wiz's Bargain Healing Potion
Wiz's Bargain Healing Potion.description: A healing potion sold at Wiz's shop at a significant discount because the flavor is indescribable and the bottle occasionally glows in the dark. The healing effect is genuine and reasonably potent. Wiz insists the glow is harmless. Vanir refuses to confirm or deny this. [Common]

Crimson Demon Dramatic Cape.name: Crimson Demon Dramatic Cape
Crimson Demon Dramatic Cape.description: A flowing black-and-red cape designed by Crimson Demon tailors for maximum dramatic effect. It billows in wind that does not exist, catches light at dramatic angles, and makes the wearer look approximately 200 percent more intimidating during self-introductions. Provides no combat benefit whatsoever. Every Crimson Demon owns at least two. [Common]

Debt Collector's Ledger.name: Debt Collector's Ledger
Debt Collector's Ledger.description: A thick, battered accounting book listing outstanding debts owed to various merchants, guild branches, and one very patient landlord. The owner's name is on several pages. Some entries have been crossed out. More have been added. The ledger itself is quest item material: it tells a story of ambition, failure, and compound interest. [Common]

Axis Cult Recruitment Pamphlet.name: Axis Cult Recruitment Pamphlet
Axis Cult Recruitment Pamphlet.description: A brightly colored pamphlet extolling the virtues of Aqua, goddess of water, and inviting the reader to join the Axis Cult. The pamphlet is aggressively cheerful, contains several unverifiable claims about Aqua's divine accomplishments, and folds into a small paper cup that the Cult insists proves Aqua's blessing of water. Discarding this pamphlet in Alcanretia is considered rude. [Common]

Steel Longsword.name: Steel Longsword
Steel Longsword.description: A well-forged steel longsword of standard guild-approved quality. Reliable, balanced, and completely unremarkable. This is what a working adventurer carries when they cannot afford anything better and need something that will not break. The blacksmith who made it put honest work into it and charges honestly for it. [Uncommon]

Reinforced Chain Mail.name: Reinforced Chain Mail
Reinforced Chain Mail.description: Heavy chain mail reinforced at the joints and shoulders for adventurers who expect to get hit often. Reliable protection that trades mobility for durability. Popular with crusaders and anyone who has learned that dodge-based strategies require a level of competence most Axel adventurers do not possess. [Uncommon]

Mage's Focus Crystal.name: Mage's Focus Crystal
Mage's Focus Crystal.description: A polished crystal mounted on a pendant chain, used by mages to stabilize their mana flow during casting. Reduces the chance of spell misfires and slightly amplifies elemental output. Standard equipment for any mage who has moved past the 'pointing and hoping' stage of magical development. [Common]

Wiz's Mystery Box.name: Wiz's Mystery Box
Wiz's Mystery Box.description: A sealed wooden box from Wiz's shop, contents unknown. Wiz genuinely does not remember what she put in it. The box hums faintly when shaken and is warm to the touch. Could contain anything from a useful enchanted tool to a small contained catastrophe. Opening it is a gamble that Vanir considers excellent entertainment value. [Unique]

Dust's Lucky Dice.name: Dust's Lucky Dice
Dust's Lucky Dice.description: A pair of worn bone dice belonging to the adventurer Dust, who swears they are lucky and whose gambling debts suggest a more complicated relationship with the truth. The dice are ordinary in every measurable respect, which has never once dented Dust's faith in them. They have been rolled in every tavern and gambling den from Axel to Elroad, blamed for every loss, and credited for every rare win. Whether they carry any real fortune is a question Dust prefers not to examine too closely, in case the answer is no. [Unique]

Alcanretia Bath Salts.name: Alcanretia Bath Salts
Alcanretia Bath Salts.description: Premium bath salts from Alcanretia's hot springs, blessed by the Axis Cult and sold at a significant markup. They genuinely improve bathing and promote relaxation. The packaging includes an Axis Cult recruitment pamphlet that is structurally integrated into the container so it cannot be removed without destroying the product. [Common]

Crimson Demon Grimoire.name: Crimson Demon Grimoire
Crimson Demon Grimoire.description: A leather-bound spellbook written by a Crimson Demon author who could not resist adding dramatic narration to every spell instruction. The magical content is genuinely useful and well-organized. The commentary is insufferable. Sample margin note: 'At this point, the caster should feel the darkness within awakening. If the darkness does not awaken, try again after lunch.' [Common]

Eris Church Talisman.name: Eris Church Talisman
Eris Church Talisman.description: A small silver coin-shaped talisman blessed by the Eris Church, depicting the goddess of luck. Worn as a pendant or carried in a pocket. The church claims it brings good fortune. Statistically, the evidence is inconclusive, but the placebo effect is well-documented. Reasonably priced and modestly comforting. [Common]

Enchanted Winter Cloak.name: Enchanted Winter Cloak
Enchanted Winter Cloak.description: A heavy wool cloak with a minor warming enchantment, essential for Axel's brutal winters when adventurers cannot afford heating. The enchantment keeps the wearer at a comfortable temperature regardless of weather. Popular, practical, and the subject of at least one guild dispute when two adventurers claimed the same cloak. [Common]

Iron Battleaxe.name: Iron Battleaxe
Iron Battleaxe.description: A solid iron battleaxe forged for power over finesse. Heavy, effective, and the weapon of choice for adventurers who believe subtlety is overrated. The blacksmith who made it charges by weight, which means battleaxes are expensive. [Uncommon]

Silver Rapier.name: Silver Rapier
Silver Rapier.description: A lightweight silver rapier designed for speed and precision. Effective against undead and anyone who stands still long enough to be poked accurately. Popular with thieves and nobles who want to look elegant while stabbing. [Uncommon]

Enchanted Longbow.name: Enchanted Longbow
Enchanted Longbow.description: A longbow with a minor accuracy enchantment that corrects for wind and distance. The enchantment is subtle but the improvement in hit rate is measurable. Archers who use one never go back to mundane bows. [Uncommon]

Wizard's Staff of Focus.name: Wizard's Staff of Focus
Wizard's Staff of Focus.description: A well-crafted staff with a crystalline focus mounted at the tip. Channels and stabilizes mana flow during casting. Reduces spell misfires and slightly amplifies output. An upgrade from a novice staff that every mid-level mage eventually invests in. [Uncommon]

Mithril-Threaded Vest.name: Mithril-Threaded Vest
Mithril-Threaded Vest.description: A cloth vest woven with mithril thread, providing magical protection without the weight of metal armor. Looks like ordinary clothing. Stops a blade. Expensive but worth every coin for mages and thieves who need protection without bulk. [Uncommon]

Crusader's Tower Shield.name: Crusader's Tower Shield
Crusader's Tower Shield.description: An enormous tower shield designed for crusaders who intend to stand in one place and absorb everything the enemy has. Heavy enough to use as a wall. Darkness owns one. She has never successfully hit anything with it, but that is not what it is for. [Rare]

Leather Traveling Boots.name: Leather Traveling Boots
Leather Traveling Boots.description: Well-made boots designed for long-distance travel on Belzerg's roads. Waterproof, comfortable, and built to last. The most practical purchase an adventurer can make and therefore the last thing most adventurers think to buy. [Common]

Ring of Minor Luck.name: Ring of Minor Luck
Ring of Minor Luck.description: A simple silver ring enchanted to tilt probability slightly in the wearer's favor. The effect is small but measurable over time. Gamblers swear by them. Statisticians argue about them. The enchantment wears off after a few months, which is why Wiz sells them at a discount. [Common]

Crimson Demon Eye Contacts.name: Crimson Demon Eye Contacts
Crimson Demon Eye Contacts.description: Magical contacts that make the wearer's eyes glow crimson red, mimicking the Crimson Demon look. Purely cosmetic. Popular with adventurers who want to look more intimidating and with non-Crimson Demons who think the aesthetic is cool. The Crimson Demons find this flattering. [Common]

Adventurer's Compass.name: Adventurer's Compass
Adventurer's Compass.description: A brass compass enchanted to point toward the nearest Adventurers Guild branch, and nothing else. It is a homing beacon for the guild, not a treasure or destination finder: it always knows the way back to a Guild hall and never points to ruins, dungeons, or quest sites. The enchantment occasionally points toward Wiz's shop instead, which Wiz insists is not her fault. [Common]

Elroad Premium Healing Potion.name: Elroad Premium Healing Potion
Elroad Premium Healing Potion.description: A high-quality healing potion imported from Elroad, packaged in a crystal vial with a gold label. Heals more effectively than guild-standard potions and tastes like cherries. Costs five times as much. Elroad's economy runs on this kind of luxury markup. [Uncommon]

Smoke Bomb.name: Smoke Bomb
Smoke Bomb.description: A small clay sphere that produces a thick cloud of smoke when shattered. Standard thief equipment for creating distractions, covering escapes, and making dramatic exits. Kazuma carries several. They work reliably but the smoke smells terrible. [Common]

Antidote Vial.name: Antidote Vial
Antidote Vial.description: A glass vial of universal antidote, effective against most common poisons in Belzerg. Essential for quests involving poison slimes, toxic monsters, or anything Wiz sold that was not supposed to be ingested. Guild-standard issue for quests rated Moderate or above. [Common]

Magic Restoration Pill.name: Magic Restoration Pill
Magic Restoration Pill.description: A compressed mana restoration pill that partially restores the caster's magical energy. Does not taste good. Does not work instantly. Does work eventually. Essential for mages who run out of mana mid-quest and do not have time to wait for natural recovery. [Common]

Vanir's Prediction Card.name: Vanir's Prediction Card
Vanir's Prediction Card.description: A sealed card from Vanir containing a personalized prediction of the buyer's future. The prediction is always accurate. The accuracy is never comforting. Vanir sells them for entertainment value and insists the despair is a feature, not a bug. [Unique]

Giant Toad Jerky.name: Giant Toad Jerky
Giant Toad Jerky.description: Dried and cured giant toad meat, sold as a travel ration by Axel's more pragmatic merchants. The texture is rubbery, the flavor is best described as 'toad,' and it lasts forever because nothing else wants to eat it either. Cheap, filling, and humbling. [Common]

Snow Sprite Core.name: Snow Sprite Core
Snow Sprite Core.description: A crystallized magical core harvested from a Snow Sprite, glowing faintly with cold blue light. Used in enchanting, alchemy, and the manufacture of cooling systems. Valuable enough to justify entering the Snowfield Forest. Fragile enough to make transport stressful. [Uncommon]

Goblin King's Crown.name: Goblin King's Crown
Goblin King's Crown.description: A crude crown assembled from stolen jewelry and hammered tin, worn by the Goblin King of the caves beneath the Neighbourhood Ruins. It has no magical properties but the goblins treat it as a symbol of authority. Whoever holds it can theoretically command the goblins, though 'command' is a strong word for what actually happens. [Unique]

Portable Forge Kit.name: Portable Forge Kit
Portable Forge Kit.description: A compact set of smithing tools designed for field repairs: a small anvil, hammer, tongs, and a collapsible bellows. Not suitable for forging new equipment but sufficient for emergency repairs and basic metalwork. Every working smith carries one on quests. [Common]

Alchemist's Satchel.name: Alchemist's Satchel
Alchemist's Satchel.description: A leather bag with padded compartments for vials, reagents, a small mortar and pestle, and a reference card listing common ingredient interactions. Essential for field alchemy. The compartments are designed to prevent accidental mixing, which has saved many alchemists from self-inflicted explosions. [Common]

Fishing Rod.name: Fishing Rod
Fishing Rod.description: A sturdy fishing rod with a reel, line, and a basic tackle box containing hooks, sinkers, and three types of bait. Standard equipment for anyone who plans to eat something that was not killed with a sword. Works in rivers, lakes, and hot springs (though the Axis Cult discourages fishing in sacred waters). [Common]

Herbalist's Guide.name: Herbalist's Guide
Herbalist's Guide.description: A battered field guide to Belzerg's flora, with pressed samples, identification notes, and warnings about which plants bite. Published by the Adventurers Guild and updated annually. The section on Crimson Demon Village plants includes a warning that the residents may have modified the local ecology 'for fun.' [Common]

Cooking Kit.name: Cooking Kit
Cooking Kit.description: A portable cooking set: a folding pan, a small pot, utensils, a spice kit, and a fire starter. Everything needed to turn monster drops and foraged ingredients into meals that are at minimum edible and at best genuinely restorative. The spice kit makes anything taste acceptable. Almost anything. [Common]

Chunchunmaru.name: Chunchunmaru
Chunchunmaru.description: A perfectly ordinary one-handed sword that its owner insisted on giving a grand, dramatic name in a fit of chuunibyou he has never fully lived down. The name means something impressive to the person who chose it and nothing at all to anyone else, and asking about it is a reliable way to make its owner deeply uncomfortable. The blade itself is decent, well-balanced, and utterly unremarkable, which is the joke: a legendary name attached to a thoroughly average weapon. In the right (or wrong) hands, it fights exactly as well as any other competent sword, no better and no worse, and no amount of dramatic naming will change that. [Unique]

Goddess's Hagoromo.name: Goddess's Hagoromo
Goddess's Hagoromo.description: A flowing feather-light mantle of shimmering blue-white fabric, the celestial garment worn by goddesses. It never tangles, never soils, and moves as if in a breeze that no one else can feel. Worn by a divine being it is simply part of them; worn by a mortal it lends a faint, unmistakable aura of the sacred and a modest blessing of divine favor. The most famous example belongs to a certain water goddess who mainly uses hers to look dramatic while complaining about being broke. Purification and water magic flow more easily for whoever wears it. [Legendary]

Crimson Demon Eyepatch.name: Crimson Demon Eyepatch
Crimson Demon Eyepatch.description: A dark cosmetic eyepatch of the kind favored by Crimson Demons who wish to imply that the eye beneath it houses a sealed and terrible power too dangerous to unleash. It does not, in almost every case, cover any injury or seal any power whatsoever; it is worn purely because it looks impossibly cool and completes the dramatic silhouette. The wearer will insist, if asked, that removing it would be catastrophic. It will not be catastrophic. It will, however, make its owner feel powerful, and in a culture where confidence fuels spellcasting, that feeling is not entirely without value. [Common]

Devil's Half-Mask.name: Devil's Half-Mask
Devil's Half-Mask.description: A theatrical half-mask worn by a mask-devil, split between an expression of mirth and one of menace. It is not merely decoration: the mask is bound to its devil owner's nature, lending the wearer a fragment of the ability to read the surface desires and intentions of those they speak with. In the hands of its true owner it enables dramatic narration, shrewd bargains, and an unsettling omniscience about what customers want before they say it. On a mortal it offers a lesser echo of that insight. It is genuinely useful for negotiation and genuinely alarming to be on the wrong side of. [Rare]

Manatite Crystal.name: Manatite Crystal
Manatite Crystal.description: A raw crystal humming with stored magical energy, the standard reagent for enchanting, high-grade alchemy, and the construction of magical devices. Its glow brightens with its purity, and the finest specimens are worth a small fortune to any enchanter or researcher. Manatite is mined, harvested from certain monsters, and occasionally found in the residue of powerful spells. It is the material foundation of Belzerg's magical economy, the thing that turns raw talent into working enchantments, and a Treasure Hunter or Herbalist who learns to spot a good vein of it will never want for buyers. [Uncommon]

Tome of Explosion.name: Tome of Explosion
Tome of Explosion.description: A weighty grimoire devoted entirely to the single spell of Explosion, its pages dense with the incantations, gestures, and theory required to concentrate a caster's full power into one catastrophic blast. Every sensible magic instructor warns against specializing in it, since a mage who knows only Explosion is helpless the instant they cast it. Every copy of this tome has therefore been studied obsessively by exactly the sort of person who ignores sensible instruction. The theory within is genuine and genuinely powerful. Reading it will not give you the raw mana to survive casting the spell, a limitation its most famous student cheerfully disregards every single day. [Unique]

Arch-wizard's Mantle.name: Arch-wizard's Mantle
Arch-wizard's Mantle.description: The formal mantle of an Arch-wizard, one of the advanced magic classes, woven with mana-conductive thread and marked with the sigils of hard-won mastery. It steadies high-level spellcasting and marks its wearer as a mage of genuine accomplishment, which commands respect in most company and challenges to a duel in the Crimson Demon Village. The mantle is as much a credential as a garment: earning the right to wear one means reaching a tier of power that most adventurers never touch. It billows acceptably, though a Crimson Demon would insist it could billow more. [Uncommon]

Crusader's Full Plate.name: Crusader's Full Plate
Crusader's Full Plate.description: A complete suit of heavy crusader plate, built to let its wearer wade into the thick of battle and draw every enemy blow onto themselves. It is enormously protective and enormously heavy, the armor of a frontline knight whose entire job is to be hit so that no one else is. In the hands of a competent crusader it is an anchor that holds a battle line. In the hands of a certain noblewoman it is worn by someone who draws every enemy attack, cannot hit anything in return, and enjoys the arrangement far more than is comfortable to witness. The plate does not judge. It simply endures, as it was built to. [Uncommon]

Teleport Scroll.name: Teleport Scroll
Teleport Scroll.description: A single-use scroll inscribed with a teleportation spell keyed to a pre-registered location, most often a party's home or the nearest town. Activating it whisks the user (and sometimes their party) instantly out of danger and back to safety, which makes it the single most valuable panic button an adventurer can carry. Clever adventurers use them to escape doomed fights, deliver ambushes, or simply skip a long walk. They are expensive, consumed on use, and have saved more lives than any weapon. Kazuma's party has an almost philosophical appreciation for the strategic retreat, and scrolls like these are why. [Common]

Monster Bait.name: Monster Bait
Monster Bait.description: A pungent lure of blood, offal, and alchemical scent designed to draw monsters toward a chosen spot. Hunters and adventurers use it to control where a fight happens: pulling giant toads onto dry ground, luring a target into an ambush, or clearing a path by drawing a monster away. It works distressingly well, which is the danger, since a misjudged throw summons more than the user bargained for. Every experienced party carries some, and every experienced party has at least one story about the time the bait worked far better than intended. [Common]

Noble's Signet Ring.name: Noble's Signet Ring
Noble's Signet Ring.description: A heavy signet ring bearing a noble house's crest, used to seal letters and, more importantly, to open doors that stay firmly shut to commoners. In the Belzerg Heartland, where noble politics can be as deadly as any monster, such a ring is a key to influence, credit, and the assumption of authority. It carries real social weight and real responsibility, and flashing one you have no right to is a fast way to attract exactly the wrong attention. The Dustiness house crest, among others, commands genuine respect. The ring opens doors; whether you belong on the other side is a separate question. [Common]

Dream Service Voucher.name: Dream Service Voucher
Dream Service Voucher.description: A discreet, unmarked voucher redeemable at a certain establishment that operates quietly beneath Axel's respectable surface, entitling the bearer to one customized pleasant dream. It is passed between adventurers with elaborate casualness and total secrecy, since possessing one is both entirely harmless and mortifying to admit to. The service is genuinely restful and genuinely popular among the lonelier men of Axel, and the vouchers circulate as an informal currency of favors. Redeeming one requires knowing the right person to ask, and asking the wrong person is a social catastrophe. [Common]

Resurrection Certificate.name: Resurrection Certificate
Resurrection Certificate.description: A prepaid certificate from the Eris Church guaranteeing the bearer one resurrection service, provided the body is recovered intact and delivered in time. Cautious (and wealthy) adventurers buy these before dangerous jobs, treating them as the ultimate insurance policy against a permanent death. The certificate is non-transferable, time-limited, and does not cover bodies too destroyed to restore, a fine print that has disappointed many an optimistic estate. Carrying one changes how an adventurer fights: with a resurrection guaranteed, a fatal risk becomes merely an expensive inconvenience. Without one, death on the frontier is exactly as final as it sounds. [Unique]

Winter Shogun's Frost Shard.name: Winter Shogun's Frost Shard
Winter Shogun's Frost Shard.description: A shard of eternal ice left in the wake of the Winter Shogun, the powerful snow spirit that patrols the deep Snowfield Forest. It never melts, radiates a profound cold, and is prized by enchanters and alchemists for frost-aligned work of the highest quality. Obtaining one is genuinely dangerous, since the Shogun does not surrender them willingly and fighting it is famously inadvisable (the wise bow and retreat). A shard is therefore both a valuable reagent and a quiet boast: possessing one implies you survived an encounter that has killed overconfident adventurers, whether through skill, luck, or a very respectful bow. [Uncommon]

Axis Cult Holy Water.name: Axis Cult Holy Water
Axis Cult Holy Water.description: A flask of genuinely blessed water from Alcanretia's sacred springs, consecrated by the Axis Cult and effective against undead in a way that has nothing to do with how annoying the Cult is. Thrown or applied, it sears undead flesh and disrupts dark magic, making it a real strategic asset on the frontier despite its embarrassing provenance. Every flask comes with, at minimum, one recruitment pamphlet the Cult insists on including. Adventurers who sneer at the Axis Cult still buy the holy water, because when the zombies come, theology stops mattering and results start. [Common]

Rope (50 Feet).name: Rope (50 Feet)
Rope (50 Feet).description: Fifty feet of sturdy hemp rope. The single most useful object an adventurer can carry and the one most consistently left behind. It solves climbing, restraint, retrieval, crossing, and at least one problem per expedition that nobody anticipated. Veterans buy it without being asked. Rookies buy it after the first time they needed it and did not have it. [Common]

Torch Bundle.name: Torch Bundle
Torch Bundle.description: A bundle of pitch-soaked torches, each burning for roughly an hour. Unglamorous, cheap, and the difference between exploring a dungeon and groping through one. Fire also has obvious secondary applications that resourceful adventurers discover quickly and guild assessors discourage in writing. [Common]

Bedroll.name: Bedroll
Bedroll.description: A rolled sleeping mat and blanket. Rest on the road restores health and mana meaningfully better with one than without, which every adventurer learns the hard way exactly once during a cold night on the plains. [Common]

Lantern.name: Lantern
Lantern.description: A shuttered oil lantern giving steady, adjustable light that a torch cannot match. The shutter matters: light you can hide is worth considerably more than light you cannot, particularly to anyone who would rather not announce their approach. [Common]

Grappling Hook.name: Grappling Hook
Grappling Hook.description: An iron hook on a length of chain, for climbing walls, crossing gaps, and retrieving things from places that swallow adventurers. Heavy, noisy, and periodically the only thing standing between a party and a very long drop. [Common]

Trail Rations.name: Trail Rations
Trail Rations.description: A week of compact preserved food. Dull, filling, and reliable, and considerably better than foraging in territory where the plants have opinions. Parties argue about them constantly and carry them anyway. [Common]

Mana Potion.name: Mana Potion
Mana Potion.description: A vial of cool blue liquid that restores a meaningful portion of a caster's mana. Expensive relative to healing potions and disproportionately valuable in a long fight, which is why mages hoard them and warriors never understand why. [Common]

Greater Healing Potion.name: Greater Healing Potion
Greater Healing Potion.description: A thick red draught that closes serious wounds and restores roughly half a healthy adult's vitality. Costly enough that most parties carry exactly one and keep a quiet ongoing negotiation about who is holding it. [Uncommon]

Antidote Kit.name: Antidote Kit
Antidote Kit.description: A compact case of purified reagents that neutralizes most common poisons and venoms. Belzerg has a great many things that inject, and this is the difference between an inconvenience and a funeral. [Common]

Warmth Charm.name: Warmth Charm
Warmth Charm.description: A small enchanted charm that keeps its wearer at a comfortable temperature regardless of weather. Modest magic, unglamorous, and worth its weight in gold to anyone traveling north where the cold is a genuine hazard rather than a discomfort. [Common]

Amulet of Clear Thought.name: Amulet of Clear Thought
Amulet of Clear Thought.description: A polished stone amulet that steadies the wearer's focus under pressure, resisting fear, confusion, and the specific mental fog that comes from being shouted at by something enormous. Particularly valued by casters, who lose more fights to panic than to mana exhaustion. [Common]

Merchant's Scales.name: Merchant's Scales
Merchant's Scales.description: A precise folding balance with certified weights, used to verify coin, ore, and reagents. Carrying one signals that you cannot be cheated by weight, which prevents most attempts before they start. Standard adventuring stock, sold in every town of any size, and quietly essential. [Common]

Climbing Kit.name: Climbing Kit
Climbing Kit.description: Pitons, harness, and gloves for serious ascents. Essential in the eastern foothills and the mountain passes, and dead weight everywhere else, which is a decision every party makes wrongly at least once. [Common]

Field Surgeon's Bag.name: Field Surgeon's Bag
Field Surgeon's Bag.description: Bandages, sutures, splints, and a small brutal set of instruments. For parties without a healer, or for the frequent occasions when the healer is the one bleeding. Standard adventuring stock, sold in every town of any size, and quietly essential. [Common]

Signal Whistle.name: Signal Whistle
Signal Whistle.description: A shrill whistle audible at considerable distance, used to call for help, mark position, or coordinate a scattered party. It also carries very well to things that were not being signaled, which is the trade. [Common]

Enchanter's Tools.name: Enchanter's Tools
Enchanter's Tools.description: Fine engraving instruments, focusing lenses, and reagent holders for imbuing work. Required for any serious enchanting, and expensive enough that owning a set is itself a credential. Standard adventuring stock, sold in every town of any size, and quietly essential. [Common]

Crimson Demon Introduction Card.name: Crimson Demon Introduction Card
Crimson Demon Introduction Card.description: A calling card bearing a Crimson Demon's full name, title, and a small illustration of their signature pose. Handed out constantly and unsolicited. Presenting one back to its owner is considered an enormous compliment and will make their entire week. [Common]

Guild Commendation.name: Guild Commendation
Guild Commendation.description: A formal written commendation from an Adventurers Guild branch, recognizing exceptional work. It carries no coin value and considerable social weight, opening doors with guild staff, quartermasters, and the sort of noble who checks credentials before conversation. [Rare]

Iron Shortsword.name: Iron Shortsword
Iron Shortsword.description: Standard guild issue for rookies who have not yet learned that a giant toad will happily swallow both the blade and its owner. [Common]

Tempered Shortsword.name: Tempered Shortsword
Tempered Shortsword.description: Reforged twice after its previous owner insisted both earlier failures were entirely the toad's fault. [Uncommon]

Mithril Shortsword.name: Mithril Shortsword
Mithril Shortsword.description: Light enough to swing all afternoon, which the Axel barkeep notes is precisely the problem with adventurers. [Rare]

Whiskerbane.name: Whiskerbane
Whiskerbane.description: Forged in an Axel back alley and named for the countless giant rats it has parted from their whiskers, this stubby mithril blade has never once faced a foe taller than a fence post and intends to keep that record spotless. Guild veterans swear it hums with pride whenever vermin are near, and sulks visibly the moment it is asked to fight anything genuinely dangerous. [Epic]

Chipped Longsword.name: Chipped Longsword
Chipped Longsword.description: The blade has more gaps in it than a Crimson Demon's explanation of why the village is somehow on fire again. [Common]

Knight's Longsword.name: Knight's Longsword
Knight's Longsword.description: Balanced, dignified, and utterly wasted on whichever party member keeps trying to parry incoming Explosion magic. [Uncommon]

Mithril Longsword.name: Mithril Longsword
Mithril Longsword.description: So finely made that pawning it would clear most of your bar tab, which is exactly why Wiz keeps gently mentioning it. [Rare]

Dawnkeeper.name: Dawnkeeper
Dawnkeeper.description: A knightly longsword said to have held a gate against a horde while its wielder waited for reinforcements who were, as usual, still arguing about dinner. Its polished edge catches the morning light so theatrically that the Eris Church nearly bought it for the altar, then remembered that adventurers cannot be trusted with anything shiny. [Epic]

Chipped Greatsword.name: Chipped Greatsword
Chipped Greatsword.description: Enormous, dull, and heavy enough that lifting it counts as your entire day of physical training. [Common]

Iron Greatsword.name: Iron Greatsword
Iron Greatsword.description: Requires two hands, a wide stance, and a solemn promise never to swing it near the party's fragile archwizard. [Uncommon]

Tempered Greatsword.name: Tempered Greatsword
Tempered Greatsword.description: Cleaves a giant toad in one honest stroke, assuming you connect before the toad remembers it can jump. [Rare]

Mithril Greatsword.name: Mithril Greatsword
Mithril Greatsword.description: Absurdly light for its size, so it merely feels like carrying a heavy door rather than an entire wall. [Rare]

The Mountain's Apology.name: The Mountain's Apology
The Mountain's Apology.description: A slab of enchanted steel so vast that the smith who forged it left behind a note reading simply, sorry. It has flattened ogres, felled a rampaging Destroyer's stray limb, and once served admirably as an emergency bridge across a flooded Axel gutter. Those strong enough to lift it rarely need to swing it twice, and those who cannot lift it make excellent quiet witnesses. [Legendary]

Practice Rapier.name: Practice Rapier
Practice Rapier.description: Tipped with a cork so that dueling lessons end in bruised pride rather than fresh paperwork for the guild. [Common]

Duelist's Iron Rapier.name: Duelist's Iron Rapier
Duelist's Iron Rapier.description: Favored by adventurers who would far rather look elegant while losing than survive while winning. [Uncommon]

Enchanted Rapier.name: Enchanted Rapier
Enchanted Rapier.description: Flickers with a faint shimmer that makes even a clumsy lunge look entirely intentional to onlookers. [Rare]

Countess's Needle.name: Countess's Needle
Countess's Needle.description: This impossibly slender blade once belonged to a minor noblewoman who dueled three suitors, two rivals, and one very confused Axis Cultist all before lunch. It finds the gaps in armor the way Vanir finds the gaps in a merchant's story, and it has never, its previous owners loudly insist, been used for anything so vulgar as an actual fight to the death. [Epic]

Rusty Saber.name: Rusty Saber
Rusty Saber.description: The curve is charming, the rust is not, and the smell is best left undiscussed in polite tavern company. [Common]

Cavalry Saber.name: Cavalry Saber
Cavalry Saber.description: Meant to be swung from horseback, though most Axel adventurers cannot yet afford the horse. [Uncommon]

Officer's Saber.name: Officer's Saber
Officer's Saber.description: Comes with an air of command that fools absolutely no one who has watched you order at the tavern. [Uncommon]

Enchanted Saber.name: Enchanted Saber
Enchanted Saber.description: Its edge whistles faintly on every cut, a sound the Crimson Demons find dramatically insufficient. [Rare]

Frontier Gale.name: Frontier Gale
Frontier Gale.description: Carried by a wandering swordswoman who crossed all of Belzerg chasing rumors and outrunning bar tabs, this curved blade moves so swiftly that opponents report being defeated slightly before the fight had officially begun. It has cut falling rain, sliced a thrown Axis Cult pamphlet cleanly in two, and never once been sheathed with a single speck of blood upon it. [Epic]

Chipped Arming Sword.name: Chipped Arming Sword
Chipped Arming Sword.description: Honest, ordinary, and chipped in a way that strongly suggests its last owner met something extraordinary. [Common]

Iron Broadsword.name: Iron Broadsword
Iron Broadsword.description: Broad, reliable, and heavy enough to double as the thing you use to persuade a stubborn tavern door. [Uncommon]

Knight's Broadsword.name: Knight's Broadsword
Knight's Broadsword.description: Every flourish of the crossguard whispers chivalry, while the nicks along the flat confess to a great deal of panic. [Uncommon]

Tempered Broadsword.name: Tempered Broadsword
Tempered Broadsword.description: Holds a keen edge through an entire dungeon crawl, unlike your party's rapidly fraying patience. [Rare]

Bulwark of Belzerg.name: Bulwark of Belzerg
Bulwark of Belzerg.description: A wide, dependable blade once wielded by a Crusader who guarded Axel's outer road through thirty uneventful winters and counted every one of them a triumph. It is heavier than it looks and steadier than anyone in your party, and it has turned aside blows that would otherwise have turned its wielder into a cautionary tale down at the Guild. [Epic]

Bamboo Practice Blade.name: Bamboo Practice Blade
Bamboo Practice Blade.description: Technically a sword, spiritually a stick, useful mostly for looking terribly serious in the training yard. [Common]

Iron Katana.name: Iron Katana
Iron Katana.description: An eastern import that adventurers buy to seem worldly and then proceed to hold entirely the wrong way. [Uncommon]

Folded Steel Katana.name: Folded Steel Katana
Folded Steel Katana.description: Folded a thousand times by a smith who will absolutely find a way to tell you it was folded a thousand times. [Rare]

Enchanted Katana.name: Enchanted Katana
Enchanted Katana.description: Draws with a soft chime that has quietly ended more conversations than most Crimson Demon monologues. [Rare]

Petalfall.name: Petalfall
Petalfall.description: A single edged masterwork whose draw is said to be so smooth that fallen blossoms part around the blade rather than be cut by it. Its previous keeper claimed to have defeated a hundred foes without once spilling her tea, a story the Adventurers Guild files under unverified but frequently repeated. In the right hands it is pure poetry, and in the wrong hands it is a very expensive way to trip over your own scabbard. [Legendary]

Paired Iron Shortswords.name: Paired Iron Shortswords
Paired Iron Shortswords.description: Two blades for the price of two, wielded by adventurers who confuse owning more swords with possessing more skill. [Common]

Matched Dueling Blades.name: Matched Dueling Blades
Matched Dueling Blades.description: A balanced set for fighting with both hands, and for dropping exactly one of them dramatically at the worst possible moment. [Uncommon]

Enchanted Twin Fangs.name: Enchanted Twin Fangs
Enchanted Twin Fangs.description: Paired blades that glow faintly in unison, mostly so you can locate the one you inevitably flung across the room. [Rare]

The Bickering Twins.name: The Bickering Twins
The Bickering Twins.description: Forged from a single ingot and separated at the quench, these two blades are enchanted to argue with one another in a wielder's grip, each insisting it should be the one to strike first. Masters describe the resulting flurry as unstoppable, while everyone else describes the first week of training as a long series of self inflicted apologies. When their moods align they cut like a storm, and when they do not they still somehow win, purely out of spite. [Epic]

Excalibur's Discount Cousin.name: Excalibur's Discount Cousin
Excalibur's Discount Cousin.description: Wiz swears this budget blade is basically legendary and only marked down because the enchantment occasionally forgets which end is meant to be sharp. It has performed heroically on a good day and sat quietly sulking in its scabbard on a bad one, and no receipt, she reminds you ever so gently, means no refunds. Adventurers keep buying it regardless, drawn less by the steel and more by the shopkeeper's hopeful smile. [Epic]

Blade of the Reluctant Hero.name: Blade of the Reluctant Hero
Blade of the Reluctant Hero.description: Legend holds that this sword chooses a champion of pure heart and unshakable courage, then sighs audibly when it inevitably ends up with someone who simply wanted a weapon that matched their coat. It fights valiantly all the same, carrying its bearer through battles they would very much rather have skipped entirely. [Epic]

Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Blade.name: Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Blade
Vanir's Certified Pre-Owned Blade.description: The merchant devil guarantees this sword has only one previous owner and only one previous curse, both of which he assures you are entirely resolved. Vanir will happily predict exactly how your next fight goes if you buy it, and even more happily decline to explain why the previous owner is not available to serve as a reference. [Common]

The Debtor's Edge.name: The Debtor's Edge
The Debtor's Edge.description: Reforged from a blade Wiz once accepted as collateral on a loan that was, predictably, never repaid, its hilt is still wrapped in the original overdue notice. It cuts cleanly and cheaply, and it seems to hum with the quiet melancholy of a shop forever one bad customer away from ruin. [Epic]

Axis Cult Ceremonial Sword.name: Axis Cult Ceremonial Sword
Axis Cult Ceremonial Sword.description: Blessed by the Axis Cult in a ceremony that was ninety percent shouting the goddess Aqua's praises and ten percent an actual blessing. It is gaudy, loud, and strangely effective against the undead, which is the one accomplishment the cult will never, ever let you forget. [Epic]

Blade of the Coin Goddess.name: Blade of the Coin Goddess
Blade of the Coin Goddess.description: Said to be quietly blessed by Eris herself, this modest silver blade is prized less for its edge and more for the uncanny way its wielder always seems to find a few extra coins after a hard fight. The Eris Church neither confirms nor denies the miracle, and politely requests that you round up your donation regardless. [Epic]

Rusty Skinning Knife.name: Rusty Skinning Knife
Rusty Skinning Knife.description: It has gutted more Giant Toads than most Axel adventurers have survived, and it smells like every one of them. [Common]

Iron Dagger.name: Iron Dagger
Iron Dagger.description: The Guild sells these by the crate to rookies who insist they will fight up close, right up until they see their first Giant Toad. [Common]

Throwing Knife Set.name: Throwing Knife Set
Throwing Knife Set.description: Six balanced blades for the adventurer who wants to look cool retreating, which in Axel is most of them. [Uncommon]

Fine Steel Dirk.name: Fine Steel Dirk
Fine Steel Dirk.description: Balanced well enough that even Dust could pick a pocket with it, assuming he could keep from pawning it first. [Uncommon]

Mithril Stiletto.name: Mithril Stiletto
Mithril Stiletto.description: Thin enough to slip between plate joints and expensive enough that losing it hurts more than any wound it inflicts. [Rare]

Whisper of the Thieves Guild.name: Whisper of the Thieves Guild
Whisper of the Thieves Guild.description: Forged in a back room the Axel Thieves Guild swears does not exist, its blade never catches the light and never squeaks in the sheath. Veteran cutpurses claim it can lift a coin purse on the backswing, which is either a legend or a very specific complaint. Whoever carries it walks a little quieter and trusts their neighbors a little less. [Epic]

Vanir's Backstabbing Special.name: Vanir's Backstabbing Special
Vanir's Backstabbing Special.description: The merchant devil Vanir sells this blade with a signed guarantee that it will find the one weak spot in any enemy, and a much smaller clause noting the same applies to your own alliances. It is unnervingly good at both. Vanir finds your inevitable betrayals delicious, and priced the dagger accordingly. [Epic]

Chris's Borrowed Blade.name: Chris's Borrowed Blade
Chris's Borrowed Blade.description: A slim silver dagger that a cheerful thief in a hood insists she is only lending you, and that she will absolutely want back later. It moves in the hand like it already knows the trick you were about to try. Nobody who has held it can quite remember what her face looked like the next morning. [Legendary]

Sharpened Pitchfork.name: Sharpened Pitchfork
Sharpened Pitchfork.description: A Belzerg farmer's answer to a bad harvest and a worse cabbage-monster season, now repurposed by adventurers too broke for a real spear. [Common]

Iron Spear.name: Iron Spear
Iron Spear.description: The reach weapon of choice for anyone who has learned exactly how far a Giant Toad's tongue can stretch. [Common]

Boar-Hunting Harpoon.name: Boar-Hunting Harpoon
Boar-Hunting Harpoon.description: The barbed head is meant to hold a One-Punch Bear at bay, which works right up until the bear decides otherwise. [Uncommon]

Steel Lance.name: Steel Lance
Steel Lance.description: Long, straight, and heavy enough that swinging it in the Guild hall is a fast way to get your card suspended. [Uncommon]

Mithril War Spear.name: Mithril War Spear
Mithril War Spear.description: Light as a broom and sharp as a tax notice, it lets you keep the monster at a range you can actually run from. [Rare]

Manatite-Tipped Longspear.name: Manatite-Tipped Longspear
Manatite-Tipped Longspear.description: A Crimson Demon smith set a chip of raw manatite in the tip, and the whole shaft hums faintly when danger is near. [Epic]

Toadsticker.name: Toadsticker
Toadsticker.description: Legend around Axel says this spear was carved from the ribs of the last Giant Toad ever to swallow an adventurer whole, and it has held a personal grudge against the species ever since. It punches through slimy hide like the toads owe it money, which spiritually they do. Novices fight over the right to carry it every froglegged spring. [Epic]

Farmhand's Billhook.name: Farmhand's Billhook
Farmhand's Billhook.description: Meant for hacking hedges, it turns out crop-monsters and low-level bandits are trimmed about the same way. [Common]

Iron Halberd.name: Iron Halberd
Iron Halberd.description: Axe on one side, spike on the other, and a hook for the day you finally admit you cannot beat the thing in a fair fight. [Common]

Steel Glaive.name: Steel Glaive
Steel Glaive.description: A single curved blade on a long pole, ideal for adventurers who want the whole tavern to notice them entering. [Uncommon]

Mithril Poleaxe.name: Mithril Poleaxe
Mithril Poleaxe.description: Heavy enough to split a Dullahan's escort in two, yet balanced so cleanly that even a priest could hold the line with it. [Rare]

Guillotine of the Grand Guild.name: Guillotine of the Grand Guild
Guillotine of the Grand Guild.description: This towering halberd once hung above the Adventurers Guild mantle as a warning to anyone who skipped out on their tab. Its blade is so keenly enchanted that quest boards ask you to sign a waiver before touching it. Reception still insists it was purely decorative, right up until they need someone to hold a corridor. [Epic]

Chipped Woodcutter's Axe.name: Chipped Woodcutter's Axe
Chipped Woodcutter's Axe.description: It has felled more firewood than foes, but in a pinch a Belzerg forest goblin splits about like a stubborn log. [Common]

Steel Broadaxe.name: Steel Broadaxe
Steel Broadaxe.description: Wide, mean, and unsubtle, it is the honest adventurer's answer to anything that refuses to negotiate. [Uncommon]

Mithril Greataxe.name: Mithril Greataxe
Mithril Greataxe.description: So light for its size that you can actually lift it twice, which is one more swing than most greataxes allow. [Rare]

Executioner's Enchanted Cleaver.name: Executioner's Enchanted Cleaver
Executioner's Enchanted Cleaver.description: Forged for a headsman who retired early after Aqua kept resurrecting his workload, this broad axe hums with a patient, businesslike enchantment. It cuts cleanly and it cuts once, which the enchantment considers a point of professional pride. Carrying it makes crowds part and small talk end. [Epic]

Beheader of Beldia.name: Beheader of Beldia
Beheader of Beldia.description: This axe supposedly took the head off a certain Dullahan general, which for a Dullahan was less fatal than deeply annoying. The blade still carries a faint headless-knight grudge and swings hardest against anything wearing too much armor and too much confidence. Owners report it whispers directions to the nearest neck. [Legendary]

Blacksmith's Reject Maul.name: Blacksmith's Reject Maul
Blacksmith's Reject Maul.description: The Axel smith could not sell this lopsided hammer, so he calls it beginner-friendly and charges the same as a mug of ale. [Common]

Iron Warhammer.name: Iron Warhammer
Iron Warhammer.description: When your enemy has more armor than brains, this settles the argument with one loud, decisive clang. [Common]

Steel Greathammer.name: Steel Greathammer
Steel Greathammer.description: It does not care where the weak point is, because after a full swing the whole target is the weak point. [Uncommon]

Mithril Sledge.name: Mithril Sledge
Mithril Sledge.description: Light enough to actually raise overhead, which is the exact moment your party remembers to stand well behind you. [Rare]

Enchanted Skullcracker.name: Enchanted Skullcracker
Enchanted Skullcracker.description: A Crimson Demon runesmith etched a shockwave into the head, so it dents armor a full hand's width past where it lands. [Epic]

Aqua's Purification Persuader.name: Aqua's Purification Persuader
Aqua's Purification Persuader.description: A self-proclaimed goddess blessed this greathammer to smite the undead, then immediately used it to bonk a Wiz who owed her drinking money. The blessing genuinely wrecks anything unholy, and also anything that questions her divinity, which she considers the same category. It weeps a little when you set it down, exactly like its patron. [Epic]

Spiked Cudgel.name: Spiked Cudgel
Spiked Cudgel.description: A stick with grievances hammered into it, and honestly the most upgrade many Axel bandits ever manage. [Common]

Knobbly Wooden Club.name: Knobbly Wooden Club
Knobbly Wooden Club.description: Zero maintenance, zero subtlety, and exactly the confidence level of the rookie who picked it over a real weapon. [Common]

Iron Mace.name: Iron Mace
Iron Mace.description: Priests love it because the Eris Church frowns on edges but says nothing about caving a skull in gently. [Common]

Steel Morningstar.name: Steel Morningstar
Steel Morningstar.description: The spikes make it look terrifying, which does most of the fighting before the swinging even starts. [Uncommon]

Mithril Flail.name: Mithril Flail
Mithril Flail.description: A whirling ball of pain that is equally dangerous to your foes and to whichever party member stands too close. [Rare]

Sacred Flail of the Axis Cult.name: Sacred Flail of the Axis Cult
Sacred Flail of the Axis Cult.description: Blessed by an Axis Cult devotee who was far too enthusiastic about hitting people for Lady Aqua, this flail rings like a temple bell with every swing. The zealots insist the sound is a hymn, though most victims describe it as concussive recruitment. It glows warmly whenever someone nearby badmouths the goddess, which in her cult is constantly. [Epic]

Padded Training Gloves.name: Padded Training Gloves
Padded Training Gloves.description: The Guild hands these to brawlers so they can lose a barfight without also losing knuckle skin. [Common]

Cestus Wraps.name: Cestus Wraps
Cestus Wraps.description: Hardened leather straps studded with old nails, favored by adventurers whose weapon budget went entirely to ale. [Common]

Studded Leather Gauntlets.name: Studded Leather Gauntlets
Studded Leather Gauntlets.description: The studs turn a decent punch into a memorable one, and a slap into a genuine apology-forcing event. [Uncommon]

Steel Battle Gauntlets.name: Steel Battle Gauntlets
Steel Battle Gauntlets.description: Plated fists for the adventurer who decided that carrying a weapon was one more thing to drop and lose. [Uncommon]

Mithril War Fists.name: Mithril War Fists
Mithril War Fists.description: So light you forget you are wearing them, right until you gesture during an argument and end the argument. [Rare]

Enchanted Ogre Gauntlets.name: Enchanted Ogre Gauntlets
Enchanted Ogre Gauntlets.description: Reinforced with a shard of ogre bone, each punch lands with a crunch the whole Guild hall can feel through the floor. [Epic]

Megumin's Non-Explosive Backup Fists.name: Megumin's Non-Explosive Backup Fists
Megumin's Non-Explosive Backup Fists.description: A pair of gauntlets a certain Crimson Demon archwizard swears she does not need, since she only ever learned one spell and it flattens everything anyway. They exist for the long, immobile minutes after Explosion when she cannot move and something is still hungry. She calls relying on them a humiliation, and secretly practices punching cushions when nobody is watching. [Epic]

Iron Brass Knuckles.name: Iron Brass Knuckles
Iron Brass Knuckles.description: Small, cheap, and easy to hide up a sleeve, which is exactly how most Axel back-alley debates get resolved. [Common]

Steel Tiger Claws.name: Steel Tiger Claws
Steel Tiger Claws.description: Four blades strapped over the knuckles for the adventurer who felt punching lacked a certain follow-through. [Uncommon]

Mithril Razor Claws.name: Mithril Razor Claws
Mithril Razor Claws.description: Keen enough to shred a Giant Toad's hide and quiet enough to open a locked satchel, though the Guild only endorses the first use. [Rare]

Frostfang Claws.name: Frostfang Claws
Frostfang Claws.description: These pale claws were ground from ice that never melts, taken from a peak where the Winter Shogun's chill still lingers. Every strike leaves a rime of frost, and enemies find their limbs slowing a heartbeat before they realize why. Wiz once appraised them, shivered, and quietly asked whoever found them to please not bring them into the shop again. [Epic]

Hunter's Shortbow.name: Hunter's Shortbow
Hunter's Shortbow.description: Light enough to carry through the woods all day, which is convenient since the giant toads never come to you. [Uncommon]

Fine Yew Shortbow.name: Fine Yew Shortbow
Fine Yew Shortbow.description: Carved by an Axel bowyer who insists the wood was blessed, though he says that about every stick in his shop. [Uncommon]

Ranger's Recurve Bow.name: Ranger's Recurve Bow
Ranger's Recurve Bow.description: Its double curve packs enough snap to drop a target before it finishes monologuing, a rare mercy in this kingdom. [Rare]

Galewind Shortbow.name: Galewind Shortbow
Galewind Shortbow.description: Strung with sinew from a wind-blessed hawk that once nested above Axel's guild hall, this bow lets every arrow ride an obliging breeze. Adventurers swear it never misses in a tailwind, and conveniently forget the times the wind changed its mind. Wiz keeps insisting she only sold it because the enchantment kept blowing her shop door open. [Epic]

Sapling Longbow.name: Sapling Longbow
Sapling Longbow.description: Freshly cut and barely seasoned, it groans with every draw like it would rather still be a tree. [Common]

Ashwood Longbow.name: Ashwood Longbow
Ashwood Longbow.description: A dependable stave that has put more arrows into practice dummies than anything with an actual heartbeat. [Uncommon]

Huntsman's Longbow.name: Huntsman's Longbow
Huntsman's Longbow.description: Favored by the folk who supply the Axel guild with toad meat, assuming they hit the toad and not their own foot. [Uncommon]

Skypiercer Longbow.name: Skypiercer Longbow
Skypiercer Longbow.description: Forged for a border war nobody in Axel remembers, this towering yew stave sends arrows so high they briefly leave the weather behind. Veterans claim a single shot once pinned a fleeing bandit to a distant hillside, though the bandit's family disputes the details. It hums faintly when a storm is coming, which the guild has decided counts as a weather service. [Epic]

Rickety Crossbow.name: Rickety Crossbow
Rickety Crossbow.description: Held together with twine and optimism, it fires true roughly whenever it feels like it. [Common]

Iron Crossbow.name: Iron Crossbow
Iron Crossbow.description: Heavy, slow to load, and utterly indifferent to whether the goblin in front of you was ready. [Uncommon]

Repeating Crossbow.name: Repeating Crossbow
Repeating Crossbow.description: Fires three bolts before jamming, which is two more than most adventurers manage under pressure. [Uncommon]

Steel Arbalest.name: Steel Arbalest
Steel Arbalest.description: Cranking it takes long enough to reconsider your life choices, but the bolt it launches ends the argument. [Rare]

Boltstorm Repeater.name: Boltstorm Repeater
Boltstorm Repeater.description: This clockwork monstrosity was commissioned by a paranoid Axel merchant who feared the Destroyer more than bankruptcy, then repossessed when he achieved both. Its enchanted magazine never seems to run empty, spitting bolts in a continuous hail that makes reloading someone else's problem. Vanir reportedly offered to buy it back twice, which is the closest thing to a product endorsement this town provides. [Epic]

Apprentice's Oak Staff.name: Apprentice's Oak Staff
Apprentice's Oak Staff.description: Sturdy enough to lean on after a failed spell, which is honestly its most reliable function. [Uncommon]

Archmage's Runed Staff.name: Archmage's Runed Staff
Archmage's Runed Staff.description: Every rune along its length hums with channeled mana, and exactly one of them controls a reading light nobody can turn off. [Rare]

Staff of the Stormcaller.name: Staff of the Stormcaller
Staff of the Stormcaller.description: Topped with a crystal said to have been struck by lightning during a Crimson Demon tantrum, this staff answers to those who can shout their incantations loudly enough. It amplifies elemental magic into genuine spectacle, provided the wielder does not faint from mana exhaustion first. The guild files most of its casters under property damage rather than heroics. [Epic]

Willow Practice Wand.name: Willow Practice Wand
Willow Practice Wand.description: Perfect for beginners, since the worst it usually produces is faint smoke and secondhand embarrassment. [Common]

Copper-Tipped Wand.name: Copper-Tipped Wand
Copper-Tipped Wand.description: The copper conducts mana nicely and also your body heat, so it is warm to hold and slightly alarming in a storm. [Uncommon]

Silver Channeling Wand.name: Silver Channeling Wand
Silver Channeling Wand.description: Balanced and precise, favored by mages who prefer their fireballs to land where aimed rather than where fate decides. [Uncommon]

Runed Ivory Wand.name: Runed Ivory Wand
Runed Ivory Wand.description: Carved with focusing runes so intricate that dropping it in a tavern will ruin someone's whole evening of appraisal. [Rare]

Wand of the Four Winds.name: Wand of the Four Winds
Wand of the Four Winds.description: Bound with threads of enchanted silver that shift color with each element it channels, this wand was the masterwork of a mage who then promptly retired to open a bakery. It flows between fire, frost, wind, and stone as easily as changing one's mind, which suits the indecisive adventurer perfectly. Wiz gets misty-eyed whenever it passes through her shop, and refuses to explain why. [Epic]

Apprentice's Spellprimer.name: Apprentice's Spellprimer
Apprentice's Spellprimer.description: Half the pages are diagrams and the other half are warnings the apprentice will ignore anyway. [Uncommon]

Bound Codex of Cantrips.name: Bound Codex of Cantrips
Bound Codex of Cantrips.description: A tidy collection of minor spells, none impressive alone, all mildly useful when the impressive ones run out of mana. [Uncommon]

Archmage's Annotated Tome.name: Archmage's Annotated Tome
Archmage's Annotated Tome.description: The margins are crammed with a previous owner's frantic notes, most of which just say do not. [Rare]

Forbidden Grimoire of the Deep Library.name: Forbidden Grimoire of the Deep Library
Forbidden Grimoire of the Deep Library.description: Chained shut for reasons the Axel guild archivist declined to write down, this tome radiates the quiet menace of knowledge that was filed away on purpose. Its spells work beautifully and its footnotes hint at prices best left unpaid, which is precisely why every ambitious mage wants a look. The book occasionally turns its own pages, and everyone politely pretends not to notice. [Epic]

Cracked Scrying Orb.name: Cracked Scrying Orb
Cracked Scrying Orb.description: The crack distorts every vision slightly, so your prophecies come out roughly as accurate as Vanir's discount tier. [Uncommon]

Amethyst Focus Orb.name: Amethyst Focus Orb
Amethyst Focus Orb.description: Steadies wandering mana into a clean channel, and doubles as a very expensive paperweight during downtime. [Uncommon]

Starlit Mana Crystal.name: Starlit Mana Crystal
Starlit Mana Crystal.description: Flecks of light drift inside it like trapped constellations, which is lovely until you realize how much mana that costs to maintain. [Rare]

Orb of the Endless Well.name: Orb of the Endless Well
Orb of the Endless Well.description: Said to have been drawn from a spring beneath the Crimson Demon Village where mana pools thick as morning fog, this orb feeds a caster's reserves faster than sense can spend them. Wielders report casting spells they did not know they knew, then apologizing to whatever caught fire. Even the clan elders speak of it in the hushed tones usually reserved for gossip about who is dating whom. [Epic]

Acolyte's Wooden Scepter.name: Acolyte's Wooden Scepter
Acolyte's Wooden Scepter.description: Blessed by a junior Eris priest who was mostly sure he did the ritual in the right order. [Common]

Eris Church Prayer Censer.name: Eris Church Prayer Censer
Eris Church Prayer Censer.description: Swings a fragrant smoke that soothes the faithful and, more importantly, covers the smell of adventurer. [Uncommon]

Silver Ceremonial Scepter.name: Silver Ceremonial Scepter
Silver Ceremonial Scepter.description: Dignified enough for a sermon and heavy enough to end one, should an Axis cultist wander in. [Uncommon]

Blessed Censer of the Faithful.name: Blessed Censer of the Faithful
Blessed Censer of the Faithful.description: Its holy smoke mends wounds and lifts spirits, though the Axis Cult insists it just smells expensive. [Rare]

Scepter of Eris's Grace.name: Scepter of Eris's Grace
Scepter of Eris's Grace.description: Crowned with a silver medallion bearing the goddess Eris's serene likeness, this scepter channels divine magic clean enough to make even a lazy priest look devout. It mends grievous wounds and steadies failing hearts, asking only sincere faith and a tithe the church would very much appreciate. Axis cultists refuse to be in the same room with it, which the Eris clergy consider a bonus feature. [Epic]

Crimson Detonation Rod.name: Crimson Detonation Rod
Crimson Detonation Rod.description: Tuned for a single overwhelming blast, after which it and its wielder are equally spent on the floor. [Rare]

Frostbite Focus Wand.name: Frostbite Focus Wand
Frostbite Focus Wand.description: Chills the air around it so thoroughly that mages use it to keep their lunch fresh between fights. [Rare]

Dawnlight Prism Staff.name: Dawnlight Prism Staff
