Searing Palm.description: Wreathe your hand in flame and press it home, branding armor, boiling through rope, or convincing a cornered bandit to reconsider his career. Close range, deeply persuasive.

Fireball.name: Fireball
Fireball.description: Loose a spinning orb of fire that bursts on impact, washing a small cluster of enemies in flame. The staple every Belzerg mage keeps ready, the workhorse spell that pays the tavern tab.

Flame Lash.name: Flame Lash
Flame Lash.description: Draw out a long whip of living fire to crack across a rank of foes, splitting formations and lighting whatever it grazes. Excellent reach, and thoroughly ruins any front line that trained for shields instead of buckets.

Wall of Flame.name: Wall of Flame
Wall of Flame.description: Raise a roaring curtain of fire across a corridor or a road, holding a chokepoint that no sane monster will walk through. Buys the archers time and gives the party something to argue about crossing later.

Blazing Nova.name: Blazing Nova
Blazing Nova.description: Detonate a ring of fire outward from where you stand, hurling back everything that got too close and cooking most of it in the process. The panic button of experienced mages who let the melee get out of hand.

Firestorm.name: Firestorm
Firestorm.description: Call down a churning tempest of flame across a wide stretch of battlefield, turning open ground into a furnace enemies must cross or flee. Marching armies have broken and scattered rather than step into one.

Pyre Ascendant.name: Pyre Ascendant
Pyre Ascendant.description: Wrap a chosen target head to toe in inextinguishable fire that clings and feeds until nothing is left to burn. Water does not help, prayer does not help, and running only spreads it.

Meteor Fall.name: Meteor Fall
Meteor Fall.description: Tear a burning stone from the sky and drop it on a marked point, cratering the earth and immolating everything inside the blast. The kind of spell that ends a siege and starts a very long conversation about property damage.

Sea of Cinders.name: Sea of Cinders
Sea of Cinders.description: Set an entire region alight at once, forests, fields, and fortress walls together, until the horizon glows and the smoke blots out the sun for days. Kingdoms have redrawn their maps around the scar a single casting leaves behind.

Sovereign of the Last Sun.name: Sovereign of the Last Sun
Sovereign of the Last Sun.description: Gather every furnace in the world into one body and let it out, a swelling dome of heat that boils rivers, cracks bedrock, and turns the sky white for miles in every direction. When it fades there is glass where there was ground, silence where there were armies, and one very tired mage explaining to the guild that technically nobody said not to.

Waterjet Flick.name: Waterjet Flick
Waterjet Flick.description: Conjure a thin lash of water to fill a canteen, sting an eye, or knock a cup off a table across the tavern. The first thing an apprentice learns, mostly so they stop asking the goddess to do it for them.

Pressure Lance.name: Pressure Lance
Pressure Lance.description: Fire a narrow, hardened jet of water at a single target, punching bruises through leather and staggering anything smaller than a bear. Cheap, dependable, and it never once threatens to flood the neighborhood.

Binding Current.name: Binding Current
Binding Current.description: Wrap coiling ropes of water around a foe's legs and arms, dragging their footing out from under them. A favorite of adventurers who would rather capture the bounty alive than explain a corpse.

Drowning Grip.name: Drowning Grip
Drowning Grip.description: Form a clinging sphere of water over a target's head that refuses to fall away, choking them until they drop their weapon or their consciousness. Grim, quiet, and unsettlingly effective for something that started as a party trick.

Slipstream Step.name: Slipstream Step
Slipstream Step.description: Ride a low sheet of racing water to cross a room in an instant, leaving a knee-high wave to sweep pursuers off their feet. Half escape, half ambush, and entirely too satisfying to overuse.

Pressure Cutter.name: Pressure Cutter
Pressure Cutter.description: Compress a blade of water thin enough to shear through rope, timber, and the occasional careless goblin at range. The spell that finally taught the party that water can, in fact, do the killing itself.

Whirlpool Snare.name: Whirlpool Snare
Whirlpool Snare.description: Open a spinning basin of water underfoot that drags every nearby enemy inward and holds them thrashing in the churn. Crowd control for the intelligent adventurer, or simply for anyone tired of being surrounded.

Tidal Ram.name: Tidal Ram
Tidal Ram.description: Rear up a curling wall of water and drive it forward, hammering an entire enemy line off their feet and into whatever lies behind them. The point where onlookers stop calling it a support spell and start backing away.

Abyssal Vise.name: Abyssal Vise
Abyssal Vise.description: Wrap a foe in a shell of water and crush inward with the weight of the deep sea, folding armor and buckling bone in a single silent squeeze. Slow to cast, but very little walks away from having the ocean sit on it.

Maelstrom.name: Maelstrom
Maelstrom.description: Tear open a roaring vortex the size of a town square that swallows carts, siege lines, and monsters alike into its grinding heart. Once it is spinning, even the caster is advised to stand well back and look apologetic.

Deluge Front.name: Deluge Front
Deluge Front.description: Summon a wall of driving rain and rising floodwater that races across the battlefield, drowning trenches and sweeping formations away like leaves in a gutter. Whole skirmishes have ended the moment the water reached the enemy's knees.

Leviathan's Wake.name: Leviathan's Wake
Leviathan's Wake.description: Conjure a mountainous surge that rises like something vast turning over in the dark and comes down across an entire valley. Fortress walls, war camps, and forests vanish under it, and the survivors mostly agree never to anger that adventurer again.

The Sunken World.name: The Sunken World
The Sunken World.description: Command the waters of the land to rise all at once, drowning armies, swallowing cities, and turning the horizon into a single grey sea at the caster's word. When the flood finally recedes, the maps are simply redrawn, and no one asks who was responsible.

Idle Breath.name: Idle Breath
Idle Breath.description: Coax a stray current of air to your will, enough to cool a bowl of tea, turn a page, or ruffle a rival mage's carefully arranged hair. Useless in a real fight and every apprentice's favorite party trick regardless.

Cutting Gust.name: Cutting Gust
Cutting Gust.description: Whip a thin edge of air across a single target, parting rope, cloth, or an unlucky finger. Barely a wound, but it teaches the hand that wind can be sharpened.

Buffet.name: Buffet
Buffet.description: Slam a fist of compressed air into a target, staggering them back a pace and spoiling whatever they were about to do. The go-to for interrupting a chanting caster or removing a drunk from your table.

Warding Draft.name: Warding Draft
Warding Draft.description: Raise a curling screen of wind that turns aside arrows, thrown knives, and the occasional hurled tankard. It will not stop a sword, but it has saved more Belzerg adventurers from goblin volleys than anyone cares to admit.

Sky Sickle.name: Sky Sickle
Sky Sickle.description: Loose a crescent of hardened air that flies straight and cuts clean, the wind mage's honest workhorse. Cheap to cast, hard to dodge, and far tidier on the property damage bill than certain explosive alternatives.

Rising Current.name: Rising Current
Rising Current.description: Call a column of air up beneath yourself or an ally, softening a long fall into a gentle landing or launching you onto a rooftop. Adventurers swear by it right up until they misjudge the height.

Zephyr Stride.name: Zephyr Stride
Zephyr Stride.description: Wrap yourself in a running current and take to the air, skimming over walls, moats, and the heads of a startled crowd. Genuine flight, provided you keep the chant going and resist the urge to look down.

Razor Squall.name: Razor Squall
Razor Squall.description: Conjure a whirling flurry of wind blades that shreds everything in a fan before you, cloth and armor and undergrowth alike. The spell that turns a cornered mage into a very poor idea to approach.

Suffocating Vise.name: Suffocating Vise
Suffocating Vise.description: Collapse the air around a single target into a crushing knot of pressure, wringing the breath from their lungs and pinning them where they stand. Quiet, unpleasant, and unnervingly effective on things that assumed being enormous would help.

Roaring Cyclone.name: Roaring Cyclone
Roaring Cyclone.description: Raise a screaming column of wind that tears a formation off its feet and flings weapons, shields, and men in every direction at once. From here the spells stop being subtle and start being reported to the Guild.

Tempest Wall.name: Tempest Wall
Tempest Wall.description: Summon a rolling front of storm winds across the field, flattening tents, banners, and battle lines under a single sustained roar. Whole skirmishes have ended the moment it arrived, mostly because nobody could stay upright long enough to keep fighting.

Heaven's Maelstrom.name: Heaven's Maelstrom
Heaven's Maelstrom.description: Tear the sky open into a churning vortex that hauls siege engines, monsters, and the odd small building up into its throat. The point at which farmers stop watching the battle and start loading the cart.

Sovereign Tempest.name: Sovereign Tempest
Sovereign Tempest.description: Bid the sky itself turn against the land, wrapping a whole province in a hurricane that levels forts, scatters armies, and rearranges the coastline before it finally tires. When the winds fall, the maps have to be drawn again, and the survivors spend years arguing over whether one mage could truly have done such a thing.

Static Spark.name: Static Spark
Static Spark.description: Gather a crackle of charge at your fingertips and snap it into a target, jolting the nerves or lighting dry kindling. Every apprentice uses it to start campfires and to prank whoever fell asleep on watch.

Shock Grasp.name: Shock Grasp
Shock Grasp.description: Load your hand with charge and discharge it on contact, seizing a foe's muscles for a heartbeat. Close enough to be brave, weak enough that veterans call it the coward's slap.

Arc Bolt.name: Arc Bolt
Arc Bolt.description: Loose a thin lance of lightning at a single target for reliable shock damage that ignores most armor. The cheap dependable staple every Belzerg adventurer keeps in their pocket for the third goblin.

Charged Nettles.name: Charged Nettles
Charged Nettles.description: Sow a patch of crackling static across the ground that snaps at anything crossing it, stunning feet and scattering a charge. Cruelly effective against anyone foolish enough to rush a mage.

Chain Lightning.name: Chain Lightning
Chain Lightning.description: Fling a bolt that leaps from foe to foe, forking to a fresh target with each jump and thinning as it travels. The moment a lightning caster stops being cheap and starts being feared.

Voltaic Lance.name: Voltaic Lance
Voltaic Lance.description: Compress a full charge into a rigid spear of light and drive it clean through a single target and whatever unlucky thing stands behind it. Loud, precise, and impolite to the scenery.

Thunderclap.name: Thunderclap
Thunderclap.description: Detonate a burst of charge into a hammer of sound and pressure that knocks a crowd flat and rattles their teeth. Not always lethal, but it ends arguments and the occasional tavern brawl.

Seizing Bolt.name: Seizing Bolt
Seizing Bolt.description: Sink a sustained current into a target and hold it, locking every muscle rigid and pinning the victim helpless where it stands. The signature of duelists who prefer their opponents to watch what comes next.

Rolling Barrage.name: Rolling Barrage
Rolling Barrage.description: Call down a marching line of strikes that walks across the battlefield, each blast throwing dirt and adventurers alike. A serious spell for serious formations, and the reason cavalry learned to fear open ground.

Skyfall Bolt.name: Skyfall Bolt
Skyfall Bolt.description: Reach up, seize the charge of the whole sky, and bring it down as one titanic pillar of lightning that splits the earth where it lands. Cast this in a town and expect a very stern letter from the Guild.

Tempest Crown.name: Tempest Crown
Tempest Crown.description: Wreathe yourself in a living halo of arcs that lashes out at everything nearby and answers each blow with a bolt. For the moment a mage decides the polite phase of the fight is over.

Stormbreaker.name: Stormbreaker
Stormbreaker.description: Summon a black roiling thunderhead over the field and let it hurl bolts of its own choosing, hammering the enemy line long after you have moved on. The kind of weather that gets its own paragraph in the after-action report.

Wrath of the Skyfather.name: Wrath of the Skyfather
Wrath of the Skyfather.description: Pull the full fury of the heavens down upon the land, an unending cascade of lightning and screaming wind that unmakes armies and boils rivers to steam. The sky itself decides the war is finished, and no fortress, no god, and certainly no Guild refund policy has ever argued it back.

L3 Hardpack.name: L3 Hardpack
L3 Hardpack.description: Compress a fistful of loose soil into a stone hard enough to crack a walnut or a foe's knuckle. The first thing an apprentice masters, and the last thing that ever impresses anyone in a Belzerg tavern.

L7 Shale Shard.name: L7 Shale Shard
L7 Shale Shard.description: Peel a flat sliver of rock from the ground and sling it edge first at a single target. Cheap, quiet, and unlikely to bring the guild hall's ceiling down on your head, which is more than certain louder schools can promise.

L10 Stone Spike.name: L10 Stone Spike
L10 Stone Spike.description: Drive a spear of hardened rock up through the ground beneath one enemy, dealing reliable damage and leaving a tidy marker for whoever has to fill the hole in later. The staple every earth mage leans on before attempting anything ambitious.

L15 Clutching Mire.name: L15 Clutching Mire
L15 Clutching Mire.description: Soften the earth around a target's boots into greedy, sucking clay that hardens a breath later, pinning them fast. Adventurers swear by it for holding a fleeing debtor still long enough to talk terms.

L21 Rampart Rise.name: L21 Rampart Rise
L21 Rampart Rise.description: Heave a wall of packed stone out of the bare ground in an instant, tall enough to break a charge or a line of sight. Faster than any mason in Axel and considerably less likely to demand payment up front.

L28 Boulder Fall.name: L28 Boulder Fall
L28 Boulder Fall.description: Tear a wagon-sized slab loose from the bedrock and bring it crashing down onto a target from overhead. Precise it is not, but few things settle a disagreement with an armored ogre quite so thoroughly.

L35 Stone Sepulcher.name: L35 Stone Sepulcher
L35 Stone Sepulcher.description: Wrench the ground upward around a single foe and seal it shut, entombing them in a coffin of living rock. Merciful casters leave an airhole. Practical ones remember to, eventually.

L44 Fault Tremor.name: L44 Fault Tremor
L44 Fault Tremor.description: Split the earth along a running crack that races toward your enemies, staggering everything upright and toppling all but the sturdiest walls. This is the point where earth magic stops being polite and starts rearranging the neighborhood.

L54 Spire Eruption.name: L54 Spire Eruption
L54 Spire Eruption.description: Rupture a wide swath of battlefield into a bristling forest of jagged stone teeth that burst up from below without warning. Whole raiding parties have been undone in the half second it takes to notice the ground has grown fangs.

L66 Grinding Cascade.name: L66 Grinding Cascade
L66 Grinding Cascade.description: Collapse an entire hillside into a roaring river of rock and rubble that buries whatever waits in the valley beneath. Somewhere under all that scree is the problem you were contracted to deal with, now permanently resolved.

L78 The Swallowing.name: L78 The Swallowing
L78 The Swallowing.description: Open a yawning sinkhole under a fortress or a massed army and let the earth simply drink it down, then draw the ground closed overhead as though nothing had ever stood there. Cartographers despise you. Everyone else keeps a respectful distance.

L90 Ruinous Quake.name: L90 Ruinous Quake
L90 Ruinous Quake.description: Seize the bedrock for miles and shake it until a whole city grinds itself to gravel, towers folding and avenues buckling into canyons. The spell that ends a siege by ending the thing being besieged.

L100 World-Sunder.name: L100 World-Sunder
L100 World-Sunder.description: Reach past soil and stone to the sleeping bones of the world and haul them apart, tearing a fault from horizon to horizon until the land itself splits into new and terrible shores. Kingdoms redraw their maps around the scar, and the archmage who dared it, should anyone survive the daring, is remembered less as a person than as a geological event.

Phantom Whisper.name: Phantom Whisper
Phantom Whisper.description: Conjure a single false sound anywhere within earshot, a snapped twig, a dropped coin, a voice calling your name from the wrong alley. The cantrip every apprentice uses to skip a tavern bill before they can hide their own face.

Flicker Shade.name: Flicker Shade
Flicker Shade.description: Throw a wavering patch of not-quite-there across a surface, a shadow where nothing stands or a shimmer that reads as heat. Enough to make a nervous guard look twice, rarely enough to make him look away.

Borrowed Face.name: Borrowed Face
Borrowed Face.description: Drape a shallow disguise over your own features, swapping your hair, your scars, and the cut of your coat for someone forgettable. It holds beautifully until a friend says your real name or someone tries to shake your hand.

Mirror Double.name: Mirror Double
Mirror Double.description: Split off a single silent copy of yourself that walks where you point it, drawing the first sword swing meant for you. It cannot open a door or hold a conversation, so keep it moving before anyone asks it a question.

Sensory Smudge.name: Sensory Smudge
Sensory Smudge.description: Blur one detail in a target's perception, the color of a cloak, the number of coins on a table, the face of the man across the room. Small enough that the victim blames the wine rather than magic.

Veil of the Overlooked.name: Veil of the Overlooked
Veil of the Overlooked.description: Wrap yourself in a haze that slides the eye elsewhere, not true invisibility but a powerful urge in everyone nearby to be looking at literally anything else. Loud noises and direct accusations tend to snap the spell in an instant.

Mirage Curtain.name: Mirage Curtain
Mirage Curtain.description: Raise a broad sheet of false scenery across a road or doorway, an unbroken wall, an empty field, a flooded ford that is bone dry underneath. Cavalry and creditors alike will ride the long way around a bridge that was never out.

Hollow Soldier.name: Hollow Soldier
Hollow Soldier.description: Conjure a convincing armed figure that stands, marches, and swings on command, solid to the eye and ear but empty to the touch. One is a distraction, and the real trick is that nobody counts a line of them closely under fire.

Cloak of Nothing.name: Cloak of Nothing
Cloak of Nothing.description: Erase yourself from sight, sound, and scent entirely, footfalls and breath and all, for as long as your nerve and mana hold. Adventurers swear by it for scouting dungeons, right up until they walk into something they also could not see.

Stolen Countenance.name: Stolen Countenance
Stolen Countenance.description: Assume a total false identity down to the voice, the gait, and the weight of a stranger's hand on your shoulder, holding under scrutiny and touch alike. Whole guild contracts have been fulfilled by the wrong person entirely, and the Axis Church still refuses to discuss the incident.

Phantom Legion.name: Phantom Legion
Phantom Legion.description: Summon an entire battlefield of illusory troops, banners, horns, dust, and the ground-shaking tread of thousands who do not exist. Generals have surrendered fortified towns to armies that would have blown away in a strong wind.

Waking Nightmare.name: Waking Nightmare
Waking Nightmare.description: Seize a mind whole and drown it in a private hallucination, a world tailored to its fears where allies wear the faces of monsters and the floor is never where it looks. The body stands frozen and screaming while everyone around it sees a perfectly quiet room.

The Unwritten World.name: The Unwritten World
The Unwritten World.description: Rewrite what an entire region agrees is real, dropping a false sky, a false season, a war that never began or an enemy that was never there, and holding it until you choose to let go. Kingdoms have marched, mourned, and signed treaties over events that happened only inside your spell, and the truly frightening part is how long it takes anyone to notice.

L3 Green Whisper.name: L3 Green Whisper
L3 Green Whisper.description: Murmur a plant into sudden growth, sprouting a seed, unfurling a bud, or coaxing a half-dead windowsill herb back from the brink. Most apprentices win over every gardener in town long before they win a single fight.

L8 Thornprick.name: L8 Thornprick
L8 Thornprick.description: Flick a handful of hardened thorns at a target, dealing modest piercing damage and a considerable amount of annoyance. Cheap, quiet, and far kinder to the surrounding scenery than most adventurers ever manage.

L14 Snaring Vine.name: L14 Snaring Vine
L14 Snaring Vine.description: Call a vine up from the soil to seize a single target by the leg and hold them fast for a few precious seconds. Seasoned parties keep a druid around purely to stop the fleeing goblins from fleeing.

L20 Beast Soothe.name: L20 Beast Soothe
L20 Beast Soothe.description: Whisper an agitated animal down into calm, cooling the temper of a snarling wolf or a spooked pack horse before it does something expensive. Works splendidly on beasts and almost never on other adventurers.

L26 Bramble Wall.name: L26 Bramble Wall
L26 Bramble Wall.description: Raise a knotted hedge of thorns between you and whatever wants you dead, thick enough to stall a charge and unpleasant enough to discourage a second attempt. It will not stop an Explosion, but honestly, very little does.

L33 Barkhide.name: L33 Barkhide
L33 Barkhide.description: Sheathe an ally in a layer of living bark that turns aside blows which would otherwise leave a lasting mark. It wears off right around the time it starts to itch unbearably.

L42 Verdant Lash.name: L42 Verdant Lash
L42 Verdant Lash.description: Sprout a length of whipping vine from your palm and flog a whole line of enemies, cracking bone and dragging the unlucky off their feet. This is the first nature spell most Belzerg adventurers actually learn to respect.

L52 Blightbloom.name: L52 Blightbloom
L52 Blightbloom.description: Seed a stretch of ground with creeping rot that spreads across a wide area, withering crops, armor straps, and anything careless enough to stand still in it. The local farmers file complaints, but the ogres do stop advancing.

L62 Beastcall.name: L62 Beastcall
L62 Beastcall.description: Summon every creature within earshot to your banner, from field mice to whatever enormous thing was napping under the nearest hill. What answers is rarely the beast you pictured, but it is reliably on your side for the moment.

L72 Grasping Thicket.name: L72 Grasping Thicket
L72 Grasping Thicket.description: Erupt an entire field into a writhing snarl of roots and grabbing branches, seizing an advancing army where it stands. Whole warbands have surrendered rather than spend the afternoon untangling themselves one boot at a time.

L84 Heartwood Awakening.name: L84 Heartwood Awakening
L84 Heartwood Awakening.description: Wake the ancient trees of a forest and set them marching, groaning giants that trample siege lines and shrug off volleys of arrows like a light rain. Enemy generals have learned to check whether a druid is present before choosing the battlefield.

L92 Verdant Cataclysm.name: L92 Verdant Cataclysm
L92 Verdant Cataclysm.description: Command the wilderness to reclaim everything in a single monstrous surge, swallowing roads, walls, and watchtowers beneath a century of growth in the space of one breath. What was a fortified town becomes a rumor and a badly outdated map.

L100 Gaia's Reckoning.name: L100 Gaia's Reckoning
L100 Gaia's Reckoning.description: Rouse the living land across an entire province, forests uprooting to walk, rivers carving new courses, and every root and beast rising at your quiet word. Kingdoms do not go to war with a druid who has come this far, they negotiate, politely, and pray the world decides to lie back down.

Mend Skin.name: Mend Skin
Mend Skin.description: Lay a hand on a scrape, blister, or shallow cut and watch it seal like it never happened. The first blessing every acolyte masters, mostly on their own kitchen knife accidents. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Soothe.name: Soothe
Soothe.description: Ease a fever, quiet a headache, or take the throb out of a twisted ankle for an hour or two. Not glamorous, but it keeps a marching party from turning on each other by nightfall. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Knit Wound.name: Knit Wound
Knit Wound.description: Close a deep gash or a bleeding puncture in seconds, stopping the sort of injury that turns a good day into a funeral. The reliable staple every adventuring priest leans on when the goblins get lucky. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Draw Poison.name: Draw Poison
Draw Poison.description: Pull venom, tainted food, or bad tavern ale out of the blood before it does lasting harm. Belzerg's healers charge extra for this one, since half their clients earn it doing something stupid. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Set Bone.name: Set Bone
Set Bone.description: Fuse a snapped arm or shattered rib back into place, the break mending clean under your palms in the time it takes to scream about it. The patient walks out sore instead of crippled. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Cure Affliction.name: Cure Affliction
Cure Affliction.description: Burn out disease, rot, and lingering sickness, from a plague chill to whatever a slime left festering under the skin. Whole villages have kept a priest fed on the strength of this alone. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Restore Flesh.name: Restore Flesh
Restore Flesh.description: Regrow a lost finger, a torn ear, or a strip of skin scoured away by acid or flame, coaxing the body to remember what it used to be. Slow enough that you will want the patient sitting down. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Break Curse.name: Break Curse
Break Curse.description: Unravel a hex, a petrifying gaze, or a debilitating enchantment woven into a body, peeling the malice off like old bandages. The kind of work that gets a priest hired by nobles who made the wrong enemy. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Purge Corruption.name: Purge Corruption
Purge Corruption.description: Cleanse demonic taint, undeath, and dark magic gnawing at someone from the inside, driving out what the lesser cures cannot touch. A wide, searing light that leaves the afflicted gasping but themselves again. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Renewing Tide.name: Renewing Tide
Renewing Tide.description: Wash a healing wave across an entire battered party at once, closing wounds and steadying failing hearts wherever it passes. When the whole front line is bleeding, this is the difference between a retreat and a rout. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Second Breath (Healing).name: Second Breath (Healing)
Second Breath (Healing).description: Reach into someone whose eyes have already gone dim and drag them back before the soul finishes leaving, provided you are fast and the body is whole. Costly, exhausting, and never as certain as anyone praying for it wants to believe. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Reclaim the Fallen.name: Reclaim the Fallen
Reclaim the Fallen.description: Call a fresh corpse back across the threshold, its wounds sealing and its breath returning as the world grudgingly gives up its claim. The price is steep enough that even seasoned priests weigh whether the dead would thank them for it. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

Deny the Grave.name: Deny the Grave
Deny the Grave.description: Refuse a death the world has already recorded, mending a body long cold and summoning a soul the afterlife had finished welcoming home. Legends carry the names of the few who managed it, and the ruinous toll each one paid to make the ledger lie. Mends anyone, living or undead, with no god required.

L1 Handful of Fireflies.name: L1 Handful of Fireflies
L1 Handful of Fireflies.description: Scatter a dozen motes of soft light into the air to drift wherever you point, bright enough to read by and warm enough to look pretty. The first thing every would-be showman learns, and often the last thing anyone thanks them for.

L3 Purify.name: L3 Purify
L3 Purify.description: Draw every impurity out of a cup, a canteen, or a suspicious barrel of swamp water, leaving it clean enough to drink and cold enough to enjoy. The single most genuinely useful trick on this entire list, which tells you everything you need to know about the rest of it.

L6 Coin Flourish.name: L6 Coin Flourish
L6 Coin Flourish.description: Send a coin walking across your knuckles trailing harmless sparks, or fan a spread of glittering illusory cards from an empty hand. Wins a free drink in nine Belzerg taverns out of ten and a punch in the tenth.

L10 Tavern Dazzle.name: L10 Tavern Dazzle
L10 Tavern Dazzle.description: Flood the room with swirling ribbons of colored light and the phantom smell of festival food that is not actually cooking anywhere. Every patron applauds, and not one of them is a single bit safer than they were a moment ago.

L15 Phantom Fanfare.name: L15 Phantom Fanfare
L15 Phantom Fanfare.description: Summon an unseen brass band that blares your entrance music and showers the street in illusory petals as you arrive. Utterly devastating to your dignity and completely harmless to everything else in the vicinity.

L20 Mirror Double.name: L20 Mirror Double
L20 Mirror Double.description: Split off a shimmering illusory copy of yourself that mirrors your every gesture and expression. Worthless in a duel, priceless when you owe a debt collector money and need to be convincingly seen leaving town in two directions at once.

L28 Cleansing Font.name: L28 Cleansing Font
L28 Cleansing Font.description: Bless a well, a spring, or an entire tavern cellar, purging rot, poison, and disease from the water in one grand theatrical sweep of the arm. Villages have named streets after wandering adventurers for a great deal less than this.

L38 Grand Mirage.name: L38 Grand Mirage
L38 Grand Mirage.description: Conjure an entire phantom crowd, a marching regiment, or a roaring dragon made of pure noise and no teeth, convincing enough to send bandits fleeing before anyone thinks to check. It fools every single soul on the field except the one goblin brave and stupid enough to poke it.

L50 Aurora Spectacle.name: L50 Aurora Spectacle
L50 Aurora Spectacle.description: Paint the whole night sky above a town in rolling curtains of light, perfectly timed to music only you can hear. Festival committees will bid fortunes for it, hardened generals will sneer at it, and it has ended exactly zero battles in recorded history.

L62 Sacred Spring.name: L62 Sacred Spring
L62 Sacred Spring.description: Call up a font of blessed water that closes wounds, sobers the drunk, and washes the exhaustion clean out of an entire weary party at once. Not a fight ender by any measure, but very often the reason the party lives long enough to lose the next one.

L75 Sanctifying Tide.name: L75 Sanctifying Tide
L75 Sanctifying Tide.description: Loose a rolling wave of pure blessed water across the whole field, mending the living where it touches them and searing the undead to hissing steam where it does not. The one afternoon a certain Lich shopkeeper deeply regrets leaving the store, and the entire reason anyone still tolerates a party trickster in the party.

L88 Hallowed Renewal.name: L88 Hallowed Renewal
L88 Hallowed Renewal.description: Purge a cursed lake, a blighted forest, or a plague-struck city district of every last corruption in a single blinding pulse, restoring it to gleaming health while bewildered onlookers openly weep. It burns through a small fortune in mana and undoes in one afternoon what armies of priests could not manage in a year.

L100 Goddess's Encore.name: L100 Goddess's Encore
L100 Goddess's Encore.description: Draw down a true sliver of honest divine power and let it break loose as pure blessed radiance, unmaking curses, banishing the undead wholesale, and calling clean water and morning light across the entire land at once. For one impossible, dazzling moment the useless little showman is exactly the god everyone was accidentally praying to, and the world remembers, briefly, why it once bowed.

Blasting Magic.name: Blasting Magic
Blasting Magic.description: The Detonation Series begins here: a compact, workmanlike lesser explosion that splits boulders, clears stumps, and opens quarry faces. Licensed civil engineers and stonecutter crews certify in it, cast it on schedule, and go home to their families. No collapse afterward, no crater, no drama, which is precisely why the school's devotees refuse to admit it exists. Casting it in front of a Crimson Demon is legal, but rude.

Detonation Magic.name: Detonation Magic
Detonation Magic.description: The middle tier of the Detonation Series: a contained explosion of military grade, strong enough to kill almost any monster outright without leveling the district behind it. Sane battle mages consider it the sensible summit of the school, the point where decisive power and remaining conscious meet. The caster is winded, not helpless. Devotees of Explosion proper regard stopping here the way a pilgrim regards turning back within sight of the shrine.

Divine Presence.name: Divine Presence
Divine Presence.description: Your divinity leaks. Undead recoil and devils go quiet and careful the moment you enter: a genuine goddess-tier aura that works on exactly those two kinds of creature and on absolutely no one else. Guards, merchants, and innkeepers remain unmoved, uncharmed, and unconvinced. Aqua has the same problem. [Rare]

Enemy Detection.name: Enemy Detection
Enemy Detection.description: Sense hostile presence and rough direction before it shows itself. Reliable and undramatic, the best gift a careful person can choose. It does not grade the threat: a toad and a general ping the same. [Rare]

Absurd Luck.name: Absurd Luck
Absurd Luck.description: Once in a while your ridiculous luck stat takes over: the coin lands right, the trap misfires, the one-in-a-thousand escape works. Not skill, and everyone can tell. [Rare]

Redeem Apology Coupon.name: Redeem Apology Coupon
Redeem Apology Coupon.description: Tear out one of heaven's worthless apology coupons and try it. Almost always nothing happens. Occasionally heaven, embarrassed, honors it with a small miracle. [Rare]

Soft Spot Hex.name: Soft Spot Hex
Soft Spot Hex.description: Curse a target with a weak point: choose one damage type (piercing, slashing, bludgeoning, fire, ice, lightning, and so on) and for the rest of the fight the target is vulnerable to it, as if the weakness were in its nature. Arrows find the gap in the armor that was never there before. Purification lifts it. [Uncommon]

Veil Curse.name: Veil Curse
Veil Curse.description: Draw a curse of blindness over a target's eyes. It cannot aim, target anything at range, or read the battlefield, and it fights in close by feel alone, swinging at sounds. Lasts the fight or until purified. [Rare]

Brittle Guard.name: Brittle Guard
Brittle Guard.description: Rot one of a target's resistances: stone skin that shrugged off blades, a hide that ignored fire. For the rest of the fight that resistance simply is not there. Devils consider this the most elegant curse in the curriculum. [Rare]

Tongue-Tied Hex.name: Tongue-Tied Hex
Tongue-Tied Hex.description: Knot a target's tongue so it cannot speak an incantation, a command, or a call for help. Casters that rely on chanting lose their spells for the fight; wordless magic and innate abilities still work. Crimson Demons consider it a war crime. [Rare]

acrobatics.name: acrobatics
acrobatics.description: Agile movement, tumbling, dodging, and balance. From first steps to mastery: keep your feet on uneven ground; tumble past an attack; leap a gap or scale a wall under pressure; dodge a blow that should have landed; the kind of impossible evasion that turns a losing fight around.

athletics.name: athletics
athletics.description: Raw physicality: grappling, climbing, swimming, hauling loot, and fleeing giant toads. From first steps to mastery: basic feats; powerful strikes and hard climbs; exceptional strength; legendary.

intimidation.name: intimidation
intimidation.description: Getting cooperation through presence and threat. From first steps to mastery: unsettle a rookie; make a bandit reconsider; cow a crowd; frighten something that outranks you, which usually backfires.

investigation.name: investigation
investigation.description: Finding clues, connecting them, and being annoyingly right. From first steps to mastery: search a room thoroughly; spot what is out of place; reconstruct what happened here; unravel a scheme from a single loose thread; the deductive streak that solves the case before the guards find the body.

performance.name: performance
performance.description: Music, oratory, and the dramatic chuunibyou self-introduction that Crimson Demons consider mandatory. From first steps to mastery: hold attention; move a crowd; a legendary entrance; a speech so extra it becomes load-bearing to the plot.

persuasion.name: persuasion
persuasion.description: Talking people into things: haggling a fee, calming a mob, sweet-talking the guild clerk. From first steps to mastery: polite requests; real negotiation; change a firm mind; talk a Demon King's general into quitting and opening a shop. It has happened.

survival.name: survival
survival.description: Camping, foraging, tracking, and not freezing to death broke in winter. From first steps to mastery: build a fire; find food and water; track a monster; keep a party alive in the wilds with no money.

swordplay.name: swordplay
swordplay.description: Melee weapon fighting: swords, daggers, and desperate improvisation. From first steps to mastery: hit a stationary giant toad; hold your own against a bandit; actually win a duel; fight like someone who trained instead of complaining. Most Axel rookies never get past the bandit.

archery.name: archery
archery.description: Ranged attacks with bow, crossbow, or well-aimed thrown junk. From first steps to mastery: hit a barn from inside it; hit a moving giant toad; a clean kill shot on a real target; pick off a specific enemy in a crowd; trick shots that make even Crimson Demons grudgingly jealous.

thievery.name: thievery
thievery.description: Stealing, lockpicking, sleight of hand, and the specific Steal skill taught by a certain masked thief. From first steps to mastery: pick a pocket; a locked chest; steal something valuable; Steal activates and grabs a RANDOM item off the target, which is frequently something embarrassing rather than their coin purse, true to the source material. This is a known and humiliating hazard of the skill.

crusading.name: crusading
crusading.description: The crusader's art of taking hits so allies do not. From first steps to mastery: raise a shield; tank a blow meant for someone else; hold a chokepoint alone; absorb punishment that should have killed you. Note: crusaders are famously good at getting hit and famously bad at hitting back.

perception.name: perception
perception.description: Noticing danger, traps, lies, and the price tag before you agree. From first steps to mastery: spot the obvious; notice an ambush; catch a hidden detail; read a room others miss.

deception.name: deception
deception.description: Lying, bluffing, disguises, and pretending the property damage was already there. From first steps to mastery: a small fib; a convincing cover story; fool a suspicious official; a con that holds up under real scrutiny.

streetwise.name: streetwise
streetwise.description: Reading a town: who to owe, who to avoid, where the cheap food and cheaper jobs are. From first steps to mastery: find the guild; find the black market; find out who is lying about a bounty; navigate a strange city cold.

alchemy.name: alchemy
alchemy.description: Brewing potions, poisons, and dubious magic items. From first steps to mastery: a weak healing potion; a reliable one; a genuine enchanted trinket; something Wiz would actually stock. Cursed results are common and hilarious.

smithing.name: smithing
smithing.description: Forging and repairing weapons and armor at the anvil. From first steps to mastery: hammer out a dent or re-edge a blade; forge a serviceable weapon that holds up; quality gear a veteran would carry; a masterwork weapon worth a dramatic name; the kind of arms and armor Wiz would buy at a loss and Vanir would sell at a profit.

commerce.name: commerce
commerce.description: Running a shop, managing debt, and the dark art of not going bankrupt. From first steps to mastery: make change; turn a profit; talk down a creditor; keep a failing magic shop open through sheer denial, as Wiz does daily.

explosion magic.name: explosion magic
explosion magic.description: The single most dramatic and impractical school of magic. Channels enormous arcane force into one catastrophic blast. From first steps to mastery: a blast that levels a small building; erases a fortress; the kind of crater bards write songs about. THE PRICE: Explosion costs more Mana than any other spell, 100 for the basic cast and up to 200 at the top. A caster with Mana to spare stays on their feet, drained; one whose pool it empties collapses and cannot move or cast until they rest. Megumin pours in everything every time, collapses daily, and considers this the only correct way. Nobody else does, including the Crimson Demons, who politely suggest Advanced Magic instead. Formally the school is the Detonation Series: Blasting Magic for quarry work, Detonation Magic for warfare, Explosion for true believers, who acknowledge the lower tiers the way nobles acknowledge cousins in trade.

elemental magic.name: elemental magic
elemental magic.description: Practical offensive and utility spellcasting: fire, ice, wind, water, earth, lightning. From first steps to mastery: light a campfire, chill a drink; a combat-grade bolt; freeze a pond, blind a monster; battlefield-scale weather. The sensible mage's bread and butter, which is why Crimson Demons refuse to learn it. Generalist: every element at solid power, made for hitting weaknesses. Each element's own school (fire, frost, water, wind, lightning, earth magic) hits harder in that one element, and a spell always rolls on the better of the two, so picking one up never makes a caster weaker.

divine magic.name: divine magic
divine magic.description: Faith magic, granted through a god: the church's power. Purification, blessings, turning and destroying undead, warding off devils, and resurrection of the dead, which is its signature and arrives earlier than any other school's. It heals too, in broad holy strokes that lift a whole party at once. From first steps to mastery: bless a drink; turn weak undead; heal and purify a whole party; raise the recently dead; mass purification that annihilates undead and, awkwardly, the scenery. Aqua-tier power at the top; Aqua-tier reliability in daily life. Not: hands-on mending of a body, curing disease, regrowing lost flesh, and healing undead or devil allies are healing magic.

drain touch.name: drain touch
drain touch.description: A lich-taught technique that siphons life force or magic on contact. From first steps to mastery: drain a trickle of mana; sap an enemy's strength; transfer stolen energy to an ally; leave a target drained and staggering. Extremely useful, faintly sinister, and beloved by cheapskates who hate buying mana potions. Open to any class and race, living or undead: Wiz teaches it at her shop in Axel to anyone who asks, and one finished lesson is enough to learn it. Not: shadow and hexes are dark magic; raising the dead is necromancy.

enchanting.name: enchanting
enchanting.description: Imbuing items with magical properties. From first steps to mastery: a minor glow or a blade that stays sharp longer; a reliable elemental effect bound into gear; lasting enchantments that hold through hard use; legendary imbuing that Wiz would buy; layered, permanent enchantments worthy of a hero's signature weapon.

cooking.name: cooking
cooking.description: Battle cooking and restorative meals from field ingredients and monster drops. From first steps to mastery: edible field rations; a hot meal that restores morale; dishes with real restorative and buffing power; cuisine a tavern remembers for years; a feast that turns a broken party into a functional one.

fishing.name: fishing
fishing.description: The peaceful art of catching things from water. From first steps to mastery: land a common food fish; a decent haul worth cooking; rare alchemical specimens that alchemists pay for; the prized catches of Riverhead Lake; whatever it is that lurks in the deep water and was probably never meant to be caught.

herbalism.name: herbalism
herbalism.description: Identifying and gathering botanical materials in the wild. From first steps to mastery: common edible and medicinal plants; useful reagents an alchemist wants; rare, potent specimens; the dangerous plants even Crimson Demons approach carefully; the legendary flora that grows only where something powerful died.

tailoring.name: tailoring
tailoring.description: Crafting and repairing cloth goods and fabric armor. From first steps to mastery: patch a torn cloak so it lasts another quest; a serviceable, well-cut garment; fine fabric armor with real protective value; work worthy of a noble's wardrobe or a Crimson Demon's billowing robes; enchantment-ready masterwork that dresses heroes.

treasure hunting.name: treasure hunting
treasure hunting.description: Finding and appraising valuables in unlikely places. From first steps to mastery: spot the obvious loot; appraise fair market value at a glance; find the hidden cache others walked past; the instinct that leads to genuine fortune; the lost artifacts and sealed vaults that make legends, and enemies.

monster lore.name: monster lore
monster lore.description: Studying monster ecology, weaknesses, and behavior. From first steps to mastery: identify a common monster on sight; know its weaknesses; predict its behavior in a fight; turn a deadly foe into a solved problem for the whole party; the definitive expertise that makes a researcher indispensable and a monster's worst nightmare.

unarmed combat.name: unarmed combat
unarmed combat.description: Fists, feet, and the conviction that weapons are for people with money. From first steps to mastery: throw a punch that lands; win a tavern brawl; disarm an armed opponent barehanded; drop a monster with a single well placed strike; the kind of martial artist who makes swordsmen feel overdressed.

dagger fighting.name: dagger fighting
dagger fighting.description: Close, fast, and dishonest knife work. From first steps to mastery: hold a dagger correctly; win a knife fight; land a blade between armor plates; end a fight before the target knows it started; the quiet expertise every guild rogue pretends not to have.

spear fighting.name: spear fighting
spear fighting.description: Reach, discipline, and the smug advantage of hitting people before they hit you. From first steps to mastery: hold the pointy end forward; keep an enemy at bay; skewer a charging beast; hold a doorway alone; a phalanx of one.

blunt weapons.name: blunt weapons
blunt weapons.description: Maces, hammers, clubs, and the honest argument that armor is just a suggestion. From first steps to mastery: swing without hitting yourself; dent a shield; crack plate armor; end an undead's second career; percussive problem solving at a professional level.

shielding.name: shielding
shielding.description: The noble art of standing there and refusing to die. From first steps to mastery: block a thrown rock; turn aside a sword blow; hold the line against a charge; guard the whole party through a bad turn; become the wall the Demon King's Army complains about.

dual wielding.name: dual wielding
dual wielding.description: Two weapons, twice the confidence, roughly the same number of hands. From first steps to mastery: hold both without dropping one; attack with either; attack with both and mean it; turn a duel into a blur; the flashy technique that works far more often than it should.

frost magic.name: frost magic
frost magic.description: Ice, cold, and the delayed detonation trick a certain Lich shopkeeper perfected. From first steps to mastery: chill a drink or a foe; freeze a target in place; raise a wall of ice; flash freeze then shatter, Wiz's signature; winter on command. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

teleport magic.name: teleport magic
teleport magic.description: Instant travel for people too important to walk. From first steps to mastery: blink across a room; cross a battlefield; teleport the whole party to a place you have been; relocate a bomb shaped problem elsewhere; the escape plan that makes every other escape plan obsolete.

necromancy.name: necromancy
necromancy.description: The paperwork intensive art of employing the dead. From first steps to mastery: sense the undead; animate a corpse; command a small host; bind something that really should stay buried; run a workforce that never unionizes, technically. Your dead stay undead: a priest's heal burns them like any zombie, so patch them up with healing magic or more necromancy.

curse magic.name: curse magic
curse magic.description: Hexes, jinxes, and the petty magic devils adore. From first steps to mastery: sour someone's luck; weaken a foe with a lingering curse; inflict a curse that resists cleansing; a hex worthy of a Mask Devil; misfortune as a precision instrument.

light magic.name: light magic
light magic.description: Holy light, blinding flares, and the Light of Saber a certain lonely Crimson Demon overuses. From first steps to mastery: conjure light; blind an enemy; cut with a blade of light; scour undead from a room; brilliance that leaves afterimages for a week.

dark magic.name: dark magic
dark magic.description: Shadow, dread, and the forbidden shelf of the spellbook. From first steps to mastery: summon concealing darkness; sap an enemy's strength; strike with shadow itself; magic the church files complaints about; mastery of the power nobody admits to studying. Not: siphoning life or mana by touch is drain touch.

support magic.name: support magic
support magic.description: Binds, sleeps, buffs, and the unglamorous spells that actually win fights. From first steps to mastery: a tinder or create water cantrip; bind a weak foe; put an enemy to sleep; buff the whole party at once; the utility caster every party underrates until they leave.

advanced magic.name: advanced magic
advanced magic.description: High arcane theory as a school of its own: raw arcane force, spells woven together into one casting, and the art of unmaking another mage's spell, which no other school teaches. From first steps to mastery: a bolt of pure arcane force; two spells released in one breath; a bolt that curves around cover or splits into several; an enemy's incantation unravelled before it lands; a working the textbooks call impossible. The Crimson Demons' coming-of-age school, and the genius tier Megumin could reach if she diversified, which she will not. It rolls when the arcane craft itself is the feat, and it never adds to another school's roll: a better teleport is teleport magic, a bigger fireball is fire magic.

leadership.name: leadership
leadership.description: Getting a party of disasters to point the same direction. From first steps to mastery: give a clear order; rally nervous allies; hold a group together under fire; make a doomed plan sound survivable; the presence that turns four idiots into a party, briefly.

etiquette.name: etiquette
etiquette.description: Court manners, proper forks, and not starting a war at dinner. From first steps to mastery: bow correctly; survive a noble's tea; navigate a formal ball; insult someone so politely they thank you; move through high society as if born to it, whether or not you were.

insight.name: insight
insight.description: Reading the room, the tell, and the lie. From first steps to mastery: notice someone is nervous; tell a bluff from the truth; read intent before the knife comes out; see through a devil's honeyed contract; know what a person wants before they say a word.

bargaining.name: bargaining
bargaining.description: Haggling, in the sacred tradition of refusing the first price. From first steps to mastery: talk down a market vendor; get a fair deal; win a hard negotiation; out haggle a merchant guild; leave the table with their shirt and their gratitude.

stealth.name: stealth
stealth.description: Moving unseen, which in Axel mostly means not tripping. From first steps to mastery: stay quiet indoors; slip past a bored guard; cross open ground unseen; vanish mid conversation; be somewhere all day and have nobody able to swear you were.

lockpicking.name: lockpicking
lockpicking.description: Locks, traps, and mechanisms that were never meant to open for you. From first steps to mastery: a simple padlock; a chest lock; a warded door; disarm the trap before the lock; open the thing the dungeon designer swore was uncrackable.

riding.name: riding
riding.description: Staying on top of an animal that would rather you did not. From first steps to mastery: sit a calm horse; ride at a trot; control a mount in a fight; ride something with too many legs or too much attitude; horsemanship that makes cavalry officers jealous.

first aid.name: first aid
first aid.description: Bandages, splints, and healing for people without a priest handy. From first steps to mastery: dress a scrape; stop a bleed; set a broken bone in the field; keep a dying ally breathing until real help arrives; the field medicine that quietly saves more parties than magic does.

navigation.name: navigation
navigation.description: Maps, stars, and not leading the party in a circle. From first steps to mastery: read a simple map; hold a heading in the wild; chart an unmarked route; find the way through a labyrinth; never truly lost, even where there are no roads.

mining.name: mining
mining.description: Rock, ore, and the patient violence of digging for a living. From first steps to mastery: swing a pick correctly; follow a vein; extract ore without collapsing the shaft; find the rich seam others missed; read stone like a page, as the Grausten quarrymen do.

carpentry.name: carpentry
carpentry.description: Wood, joints, and building things that do not immediately fall over. From first steps to mastery: drive a nail straight; build a sturdy crate; frame a roof; craft furniture worth selling; joinery so clean it needs no nails at all.

brewing.name: brewing
brewing.description: Ale, spirits, and the beverages that keep Axis Cultists cheerful. From first steps to mastery: not ruin a batch; brew a drinkable ale; craft something people pay for; distill a spirit with a kick; a vintage that starts arguments about which tavern serves it.

farming.name: farming
farming.description: Crops, soil, and the noble struggle against Axel's giant vegetables. From first steps to mastery: plant a straight row; raise a healthy crop; bring in a full harvest; coax cabbages that fight back into the cart, as Axel demands each season; the green thumb that feeds a town.

appraisal.name: appraisal
appraisal.description: Knowing what a thing is worth at a glance, the honest half of a certain cheat skill. From first steps to mastery: price common goods; spot a fake; value an unfamiliar item; appraise a magic item's true properties; name the worth, origin, and hidden flaw before the seller finishes lying.

gambling.name: gambling
gambling.description: Cards, dice, and the mathematics of losing your rent in Elroad. From first steps to mastery: understand the odds; win a friendly hand; read a bluff at the table; walk out of a casino ahead, which is against the rules of nature; the uncanny luck that gets players quietly asked to leave.

fire magic.name: fire magic
fire magic.description: Ignition, fireballs, and the honest adventurer's answer to any problem that can be solved by setting it on fire. From first steps to mastery: light a torch or singe a foe; hurl a fireball into a crowd of goblins; raise a wall of flame to hold a line; immolate a target where it stands; a personal apocalypse of heat, no city walls guaranteed to survive. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

water magic.name: water magic
water magic.description: Currents, crushing pressure, and the drowning grip, mastered by cold calculation rather than divine luck. Nothing at all like a certain useless goddess, the adventurers of Belzerg are told, repeatedly. From first steps to mastery: pin or soak a foe with a jet; seize a target in a drowning grip; raise a churning wall of water; crush a body under abyssal pressure; call down the flood. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

wind magic.name: wind magic
wind magic.description: Air pushed, sharpened, and spun until it stops being a breeze and starts being a problem. From first steps to mastery: shove a target or foul their aim; carve with a blade of wind; ride the air clean off the ground; pin a mob under a screaming cyclone; hand a whole province its own hurricane. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

lightning magic.name: lightning magic
lightning magic.description: Static, arcs, and the crack of a full storm called down on people who probably deserved it. From first steps to mastery: shock a foe or start a fire; chain a bolt between several enemies; paralyze a target where it stands; split the sky with a single killing bolt; command the storm itself. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

earth magic.name: earth magic
earth magic.description: Stone, soil, and the patient art of convincing the ground to do the shoving for you. From first steps to mastery: harden a fistful of earth or sling a pebble; raise a wall of rock from bare ground; entomb a foe in living stone; split a fault line through a city block; crack a continent in two. Specialist school: hits harder in its element than elemental magic, and a spell rolls on whichever of the two the caster is better at, so learning it never costs a thing.

illusion magic.name: illusion magic
illusion magic.description: Phantasms, disguises, and the honest art of lying to five senses at once, the trade of every adventurer too smart to fight fair. From first steps to mastery: fake a sound or a flickering shape; wear a face that is not yours; turn invisible or conjure a soldier who is not there; march a whole army that was never recruited; unmake a mind's grip on what is real.

nature magic.name: nature magic
nature magic.description: Coaxing green things to grow, snare, and occasionally eat people, the patient druidic art of letting the wilderness do your fighting for you. From first steps to mastery: sprout a seed or snag an ankle; snare a target in vines; raise a wall of thorns; turn a beast or a whole grove to your side; wake the wilderness itself.

healing magic.name: healing magic
healing magic.description: Medicine worked with magic, no god required: the strongest and most repeatable school for mending bodies. Closes wounds, cures poison and disease, sets bone, regrows lost flesh, lifts curses from the body, and drags back someone whose heart has just stopped. It works on anyone, living or undead, devils and dhampirs included, which holy magic cannot promise, so it is the only reliable way to patch up Wiz, Vanir, or an undead friend. Its spells recover faster than divine ones, and a good healer earns honest coin running a clinic. From first steps to mastery: close a cut; cure poison and set bone; cure disease and regrow lost flesh; restart a heart that just stopped; undo a death the world had already accepted. Not: purification, blessings, turning undead, and church resurrection are divine magic.

party tricks.name: party tricks
party tricks.description: Spectacular, gloriously useless magic that a certain self-proclaimed goddess mistook for a career. From first steps to mastery: purify a mug or conjure a little light; dazzle a whole tavern into applause; fill a room with illusions nobody asked for; cleanse a poisoned river, Aqua's one honest talent; a miracle so absurd it saves everyone.

Human.name: Human
Human.description: The default species of Belzerg. No special abilities, no dramatic introductions, no inherent magical talent. Just a person with a sword and a dream and probably debt. The most common race in the kingdom and the most likely to die to a giant toad.
Human.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Human. No special racial features. Describe as an ordinary person. No pointed ears, no glowing eyes, no dramatic hair colors unless chosen separately.

Crimson Demon.name: Crimson Demon
Crimson Demon.description: A member of the Crimson Demon clan: genetically engineered mages with red eyes, dark hair, overwhelming magical power, and an irresistible compulsion toward dramatic self-introductions. Every Crimson Demon has a grandiose name, a signature pose, and genuine talent to back up the theatrics. Created by a reincarnated Japanese scientist who thought chuunibyou mages would be funny. He was correct.
Crimson Demon.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Crimson Demon. ALWAYS describe with distinctive crimson-red eyes and dark hair. The character gives dramatic self-introductions with a title and pose. They are genuinely powerful mages who treat theatrics as a cultural obligation.

Demi-Human.name: Demi-Human
Demi-Human.description: Part-animal folk with visible non-human traits: cat ears, fox tails, or other features that range from subtle to dramatic. Uncommon in Belzerg but not rare. Physically capable and perceptive, with senses sharper than humans. Their non-human traits are genuine anatomy, not costumes.
Demi-Human.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Demi-Human. Describe with specific animal features (cat ears, tail, etc.) as permanent anatomy. Enhanced senses surface naturally in perception and combat scenes.

Reformed Undead.name: Reformed Undead
Reformed Undead.description: Someone who died and came back wrong, but in a manageable way. A lich who chose peace, a revenant with unfinished business, or someone Aqua's resurrection spell did not quite complete. Technically dead. Functionally alive. Occasionally unsettling to be around.
Reformed Undead.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Reformed Undead. Describe with subtle signs of being not-quite-alive: slightly too pale, eyes that glow faintly in the dark, cold skin. NPCs occasionally flinch.

Mask Devil.name: Mask Devil
Mask Devil.description: A devil from the underworld, wearing a mask that hides their true nature. Devils in Belzerg are not inherently evil, just inherently dramatic. Vanir is the most famous example: a duke of hell who runs a shop. Devils can read emotions and intentions, which they find delicious. Literally.
Mask Devil.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Mask Devil. ALWAYS describe wearing a distinctive mask. The character reads emotions and feeds on negative feelings, which they find tasty. They are theatrical and enjoy irony.

Half-Demon.name: Half-Demon
Half-Demon.description: Born of a human and demon parent, carrying traits of both worlds. In Belzerg, this means you are slightly too strong, slightly too perceptive, and the Eris Church keeps giving you pamphlets about redemption you did not ask for. Half-demons are uncommon and tend to drift toward adventuring because regular employment involves too many awkward conversations.
Half-Demon.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Half-Demon. Describe with subtle demonic features: slightly pointed ears, unusually sharp canines, eyes that catch light oddly. Strong and resilient.

Otherworlder.name: Otherworlder
Otherworlder.description: Reincarnated from Japan into Belzerg by a goddess, carrying memories of convenience stores, smartphones, and a world that made more sense. You chose (or were forced to choose) a divine gift and woke up in a guild hall. Your modern knowledge is occasionally useful and frequently irrelevant. You miss microwaves.
Otherworlder.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Otherworlder. The character has knowledge of modern Japan that surfaces as culture shock, anachronistic references, and the occasional brilliant idea that only works because nobody here has invented it yet. Treat modern knowledge as a comedic resource.

Cursed Being.name: Cursed Being
Cursed Being.description: Something happened to you that should not have, and the evidence is permanent. A botched spell, a deal with a devil, something Wiz sold you, or a resurrection that left a mark. You function normally except for the one thing that is obviously wrong, which you have learned to work around with varying success.
Cursed Being.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Cursed Being. The character has a visible curse effect: a glowing mark, an unusual physical feature, or a persistent magical anomaly. The curse is part of their identity and occasionally causes problems in social situations.

Adventurer.name: Adventurer
Adventurer.description: The weakest and most common class: a generalist with no specialty. The class you get when you have no aptitude for anything better. Kazuma's class. Surprisingly survivable through sheer versatility, scheming, and refusing to fight fair.
Adventurer.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Adventurer. Jack of all trades, master of none. Win through cleverness, dirty tricks, and exploiting every advantage. No signature ability, just raw adaptability.

Arch-Wizard.name: Arch-Wizard
abilities: Explosion
Arch-Wizard.description: The pinnacle of offensive magic: a mage who has invested everything into raw destructive power. In Belzerg, this usually means Explosion magic, the most devastating and most impractical spell in existence. One cast that drains the tank, a collapse if it drains all of it, and no regrets.
Arch-Wizard.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Arch-Wizard. Massive magical firepower, zero physical capability. The character commits fully to dramatic spell delivery and accepts the consequences. Collapses when a spell takes their last Mana, which Explosion often does.

Crusader.name: Crusader
Crusader.description: A holy knight who specializes in defense: enormous stamina, heavy armor, and the ability to draw every enemy attack in the room. The catch is that Crusaders in Belzerg cannot hit anything. Their accuracy is legendarily terrible. Darkness is the most famous example. She cannot hit a barn from inside it.
Crusader.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Crusader. Tank and defender. Massive defense, zero accuracy. The character draws enemy attacks onto themselves (which they may enjoy, depending on personality). They protect allies by being the biggest target in the room.

Priest.name: Priest
abilities: Heal
Priest.description: A divine caster who heals, purifies, and supports. The useful member of any party. Priests in Belzerg serve either the Eris Church (competent and respectable) or the Axis Cult (enthusiastic and terrifying). Aqua is technically an Arch-Priest and technically the most powerful healer alive. Technically.
Priest.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Priest. Healer and support. Divine magic is their strength: healing, purification, resurrection, and anti-undead abilities. They keep the party alive and functioning.

Thief.name: Thief
abilities: Steal
Thief.description: Stealth, speed, and skills nobody admits are useful until the lock needs picking. Thieves in Belzerg are registered adventurers who learned their skills through the guild, which is how Chris taught Kazuma to Steal. The guild pretends not to notice what the skills are used for outside of quests.
Thief.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Thief. Speed, stealth, and utility. Steal, detect traps, pick locks, and move unseen. Win through positioning and opportunity rather than raw power.

Mage.name: Mage
Mage.description: A versatile magic user who learns multiple schools rather than specializing in one devastating spell. Less dramatic than an Arch-Wizard but far more practical. A Mage can cast all day without collapsing, which Arch-Wizards find deeply unimpressive.
Mage.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Mage. Versatile elemental caster. Multiple spell schools, sustained output, tactical flexibility. The sensible choice, which is why it is less fun.

Swordsman.name: Swordsman
Swordsman.description: A dedicated melee combatant who has invested everything in blade work. Clean technique, reliable damage, and the ability to actually hit things, which Crusaders envy. The backbone of most functional adventurer parties.
Swordsman.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Swordsman. Melee specialist. Strong, accurate, and reliable in combat. Fights with discipline and trained technique.

Archer.name: Archer
abilities: Snipe
Archer.description: A ranged combatant who fights from distance with precision and patience. In a world of explosions and giant toads, the ability to shoot something from far away without getting swallowed is underrated. Keith is an archer. Keith is also underrated.
Archer.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Archer. Ranged precision fighter. Accurate, patient, and effective from a distance that keeps them out of toad-swallowing range.

Knight.name: Knight
Knight.description: A trained warrior from a noble or military background who fights with honor, discipline, and equipment that costs more than most adventurers earn in a year. Knights are respected in Belzerg and slightly resented by commoner adventurers who cannot afford the armor.
Knight.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Knight. Disciplined fighter with strong defense and offense. Trained formally and fights by the book, which is effective against everything except people who cheat.

Berserker.name: Berserker
Berserker.description: A fighter who trades technique for raw aggression. Hit harder, move faster, think less. Berserkers are effective and terrifying and exhausting to be around. The guild keeps a separate damage waiver form specifically for berserker-related incidents.
Berserker.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Berserker. Pure offensive aggression. Massive damage output, low defense, and a fighting style that prioritizes hitting over thinking. Intimidating in combat.

Monk.name: Monk
Monk.description: A martial artist who fights with their body rather than weapons. Disciplined, centered, and capable of impressive physical feats. In Belzerg, monks are rare and slightly confusing to people who expect everyone to carry a sword.
Monk.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Monk. Unarmed combat specialist with exceptional physical control. Fast, precise, and effective without weapons. Centered and disciplined.

Dragon Knight.name: Dragon Knight
Dragon Knight.description: An elite military class trained to ride and fight from dragonback. Prestigious, powerful, and extremely rare. Dust was one before he abandoned his post. The training is brutal, the skills are exceptional, and the class carries a weight of expectation that some people find suffocating enough to walk away from.
Dragon Knight.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Dragon Knight. Elite mounted combatant. Excellent swordsmanship, tactical awareness, and the lingering habits of military training even when dismounted.

Merchant.name: Merchant
Merchant.description: Someone who chose commerce over combat and is somehow making it work as an adventurer. Merchants in Belzerg's guild are registered for the access to trade routes and market information. They fight with money, connections, and the occasional hired sword.
Merchant.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Merchant. Commerce specialist. Appraise, negotiate, and profit. Fights with resources rather than raw power. Knows the value of everything.

Craftsman.name: Craftsman
Craftsman.description: A maker who registered with the guild for material access and the adventure-adjacent lifestyle. Blacksmiths, alchemists, enchanters, and artisans who got tired of the workshop and wanted to source their own materials. Ryohei Tsuchiya the weaver is the most famous Axel example.
Craftsman.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Craftsman. Creation and repair specialist. Forge weapons, brew potions, craft equipment. The party member who fixes what everyone else breaks.

Bard.name: Bard
Bard.description: A performer who turned entertainment into an adventuring career. Bards boost morale, gather information, and fight with the kind of creativity that comes from solving problems with a lute and a smile. In Belzerg, bards perform at taverns between quests and are surprisingly effective at social encounters.
Bard.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Bard. Performance and social specialist. Boost allies, gather information, and solve problems through charm, creativity, and a good song.

Isekai'd by Aqua.name: Isekai'd by Aqua
Isekai'd by Aqua.description: You died, met the goddess Aqua in the afterlife, chose a divine gift (or maybe chose the goddess herself), and woke up in Axel with nothing but the clothes on your back and a vague sense that you made a terrible decision. Aqua probably mocked your death. Welcome to Belzerg.
Isekai'd by Aqua.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Isekai'd by Aqua. The character was reincarnated by Aqua and carries memories of modern Japan. They know what microwaves are. They miss convenience stores. They have opinions about this world's plumbing. Culture shock is a recurring comedy source.

Isekai'd by Eris.name: Isekai'd by Eris
Isekai'd by Eris.description: You died and were kindly processed by Eris, the goddess of luck, who sent you to Belzerg with a gentle smile and a divine gift. Your reincarnation experience was calm, respectful, and well-organized. You arrived prepared. This is unusual.
Isekai'd by Eris.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Isekai'd by Eris. Reincarnated with better preparation than most otherworlders. Eris gave good advice. The character has a quiet respect for the Eris Church and a sense that someone competent is watching out for them.

Born in Belzerg.name: Born in Belzerg
Born in Belzerg.description: You were born here. You grew up here. This is just your world. You do not have culture shock, you do not miss smartphones, and you find otherworlders equal parts fascinating and annoying. You understand the guild system, the economy, and the specific danger of giant toads because you have lived with them your entire life.
Born in Belzerg.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Native to Belzerg. The character understands the world naturally. No culture shock, no modern knowledge. They know the guild system, local customs, and regional geography from personal experience.

Former Noble.name: Former Noble
Former Noble.description: You come from a noble family, which in Belzerg means political connections, a good education, and the specific burden of being expected to marry someone useful. You became an adventurer either out of idealism or to escape the marriage arrangements. Like Darkness.
Former Noble.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Former Noble. The character has noble manners, political knowledge, and the occasional uncomfortable encounter with relatives who want them to come home and be responsible. Money is not the problem; expectations are.

Runaway Soldier.name: Runaway Soldier
Runaway Soldier.description: You served in Belzerg's military or a foreign army and left. Maybe honorably, maybe not. Your combat training is excellent. Your reasons for leaving are your own business. Dust was a Dragon Knight who walked away. You might be something similar.
Runaway Soldier.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Former Military. The character has formal combat training, tactical awareness, and a past they would rather not discuss. Military habits surface under pressure.

Ex-Cult Member.name: Ex-Cult Member
Ex-Cult Member.description: You were in the Axis Cult. You got out. The experience left you with a deep understanding of divine magic, water purification, and the specific psychological damage of being recruited too aggressively. You flinch when someone hands you a pamphlet.
Ex-Cult Member.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Ex-Axis Cult. The character has divine magic training from the Cult and a visceral aversion to recruitment tactics. They know Aqua's scripture by heart and wish they did not.

Wandering Traveler.name: Wandering Traveler
Wandering Traveler.description: You have been walking for a while. No homeland pulling you back, no destination pulling you forward. You ended up in Axel because the road led here and the guild was hiring. Your past is whatever you say it is. Nobody checks.
Wandering Traveler.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Wandering Traveler. The character has no strong ties to any location or faction. They know the roads, the dangers, and the cheapest inns. Freedom is their identity.

Ex-Demon Army.name: Ex-Demon Army
Ex-Demon Army.description: You served the Demon King and left. Wiz and Vanir proved that defection is survivable if you find useful employment. You know how the Demon King's forces operate from the inside: chain of command, patrol routes, and which generals are reasonable. The guild accepted your registration with visible reluctance.
Ex-Demon Army.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Defected from the Demon King's Army. The character has insider knowledge of demon military operations and a complex relationship with both sides of the war. Trust is earned slowly.

Masochist.name: Masochist
Masochist.description: You enjoy pain, danger, and humiliation in ways that concern your party members. Being hit in combat is not a problem; it is a perk. Darkness is the most famous example. Your enthusiasm for being attacked is genuine and deeply uncomfortable for everyone around you.
