Adopts Every Stray.description: Injured birds, lost dogs, one juvenile slime in a bucket: if it is small and sad, it is coming home with you. Your lodgings are a rotating sanctuary and your party has a standing rule about checking your bag for heartbeats before dungeon crawls.
Adopts Every Stray.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Adopts Strays. The character accumulates small creatures compulsively. Current roster varies. The animals adore them and complicate everything.

Rehearses Conversations.name: Rehearses Conversations
Rehearses Conversations.description: You practice important conversations in advance, out loud, doing both voices. The rehearsals are audible through inn walls and never once match the real conversation, which you handle worse than if you had improvised. Your imagined version of everyone is more articulate than they are.
Rehearses Conversations.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Rehearses Conversations. The character pre-performs dialogues audibly and is thrown when reality deviates, which is always. Overheard rehearsals are a recurring embarrassment engine.

Laughs at the Wrong Moment.name: Laughs at the Wrong Moment
Laughs at the Wrong Moment.description: Funerals, ultimatums, dramatic confessions: something in your brain identifies the single worst moment for laughter and pulls the lever. It is not cruelty. It is pressure. Nobody believes that in the moment, including, sometimes, you.
Laughs at the Wrong Moment.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Wrong-Moment Laughter. Tension triggers the character's laughter reflex at maximally inappropriate times. The apologies afterward are sincere and elaborate and do not help.

Chronic Souvenir Buyer.name: Chronic Souvenir Buyer
Chronic Souvenir Buyer.description: Every town, every stall, every festival: you buy the thing. The commemorative thing, the miniature thing, the thing with the town's name misspelled on it. Your pack weighs double and your room is a museum of places you passed through. You can gift-wrap a memory for anyone you meet. Sometimes that is even useful.
Chronic Souvenir Buyer.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Souvenir Buyer. The character compulsively purchases mementos everywhere. Their collection is heavy, worthless, and occasionally, comically, exactly what a situation requires.

Never Forgets a Grudge.name: Never Forgets a Grudge
Never Forgets a Grudge.description: Your forgiveness is warm and total. Your memory is neither. You can recite, with date and weather conditions, every slight since childhood: the merchant who shorted you, the innkeeper who judged you, the goose. Especially the goose. You do nothing with the list. The list simply exists, complete, eternal.
Never Forgets a Grudge.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Grudge Archive. The character remembers every slight in perfect detail while remaining outwardly gracious. The archive surfaces at unexpected moments. The goose incident is never fully explained.

Falls Asleep When Nervous.name: Falls Asleep When Nervous
Falls Asleep When Nervous.description: Your body's response to overwhelming stress is, medically speaking, a nap. Ambushes, confessions, royal audiences: past a certain intensity, your eyelids file for leave. Healers call it fascinating. Your party calls it the worst possible superpower. You call it well-rested, from the floor.
Falls Asleep When Nervous.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Stress Napper. Extreme tension puts the character to sleep, briefly and completely. They wake refreshed into whatever the situation became. Comedy timing is the entire point.

Narrates Their Own Actions.name: Narrates Their Own Actions
Narrates Their Own Actions.description: 'She checks the door. The door is locked. Undeterred, our hero considers the window.' You do this out loud, in third person, constantly. You do not always notice. Stealth missions have opinions about it, and so does everyone within earshot of your inner monologue, which is to say, everyone.
Narrates Their Own Actions.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Self-Narrator. The character narrates their actions in dramatic third person, often unconsciously. The narration is more flattering than the reality it describes, in real time.

Has a Signature Pose.name: Has a Signature Pose
Has a Signature Pose.description: At some point you developed a pose, and now it deploys at any moment of triumph: arms just so, chin angled, an implied wind. You have practiced it. There is a mirror involved. Crimson Demons who witness it nod in solemn professional respect, which is either the best or worst thing about it.
Has a Signature Pose.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Signature Pose. The character strikes a rehearsed victory pose after accomplishments of any size, including minor errands. Crimson Demons approve on sight. The pose is non-negotiable.

Sends Letters Home.name: Sends Letters Home
Sends Letters Home.description: Every week, without fail, a letter home: the adventures dramatized, the injuries minimized, the finances fictionalized. The replies arrive with advice you did not request and news of people you barely remember, and you read every word. Your family's version of your life is now a beloved regional serial. You are not sure who they think you are. He sounds great.
Sends Letters Home.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Letters Home. The character maintains devoted weekly correspondence with family. The letters' version of events diverges heroically from reality. Family replies arrive at comedically relevant moments.

Immune to Embarrassment.name: Immune to Embarrassment
Immune to Embarrassment.description: Somewhere along the way your shame gland simply retired. Public failure, mistaken identity, singing in the square for a bet: nothing lands. You proceed through mortifying circumstances with the serenity of weather. People find this either magnificent or deeply unsettling. Both, usually.
Immune to Embarrassment.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Shameless. The character cannot be embarrassed by any circumstance. Situations that would destroy others do not register. Their composure in absurdity makes everything funnier around them.

Counts Everything.name: Counts Everything
Counts Everything.description: Stairs, steps, coins, crows on a fence: your mind tallies without permission. You know how many boards are in the guild hall floor and how many times the receptionist sighs per hour, on average, seasonally adjusted. Mostly harmless. Occasionally, in a dungeon, when the count is wrong, it is the thing that saves everyone.
Counts Everything.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Compulsive Counter. The character tallies their surroundings automatically and announces totals. The habit is background comedy until a discrepancy matters, when it becomes briefly heroic.

Carpenter.name: Carpenter
Carpenter.description: You build and mend in wood: fences, roofs, cart beds, and the endless structural apologies Axel's adventurers owe their landlords. Steady coin, honest work, and a permanent waiting list, because in this town, something is always recently broken.
Carpenter.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Carpenter. Builds and repairs wooden structures. Assesses buildings on entry out of habit. In Axel, never unemployed.

Brewer.name: Brewer
Brewer.description: You make ale, cider, and the seasonal experiment nobody asks about twice. Brewers hold sacred status in adventurer towns, and your professional opinions about the guild hall's house ale are considered testimony under oath.
Brewer.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Brewer. Brews and evaluates drink. Welcome everywhere, consulted often, and personally offended by bad ale served at good prices.

Farmer.name: Farmer
Farmer.description: You work the land, which in the breadbasket means soil, seasons, and an annual aerial vegetable event that outsiders refuse to believe until they see it. You have harvested under cabbage fire. You know what the sky looks like before they swarm. City adventurers train for combat; you grew up in it.
Farmer.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Farmer. Grows crops, reads weather and seasons, and possesses genuine hard-earned cabbage-harvest combat experience that commands more respect than it should.

Cartographer.name: Cartographer
Cartographer.description: You draw the maps other people bet their lives on, and you take that personally. Roads walked, distances paced, coastlines argued with: your work is beautiful, accurate, and forever fighting the public's conviction that the map is wrong rather than the traveler.
Cartographer.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Cartographer. Surveys and maps terrain. Corrects other people's maps compulsively. Navigation disputes with the character are unwise and frequent anyway.

Miner.name: Miner
Miner.description: You dig, prop, and read stone the way sailors read sky. The foothill quarries pay honest rates for people who know which creak means settle and which means run, and you have been both right and fast enough, so far, every time it counted.
Miner.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Miner. Excavation, ore sense, and underground survival instincts. In caves and dungeons, the character reads the stone and is worth listening to.

Gravekeeper.name: Gravekeeper
Gravekeeper.description: You tend cemeteries: grounds, records, and the residents, who in Belzerg do not always stay filed. It is quiet work, mostly nights, and you have developed the professional calm of someone who knows that most restless dead just want to lodge a complaint. You keep a ledger for that too.
Gravekeeper.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Gravekeeper. Maintains burial grounds and handles minor undead incidents with unflappable procedure. Polite to the deceased on principle. The complaint ledger is real and honored.

Shopkeeper.name: Shopkeeper
Shopkeeper.description: You have run a counter, kept books, and survived inventory day, which makes you calmer under pressure than most veterans. You understand margins, customers, and the exact moment a browsing adventurer becomes a shoplifting problem. Retail is combat with a bell on the door.
Shopkeeper.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Shopkeeper. Commerce, stock-keeping, and customer management. Prices goods on sight, spots theft instantly, and treats haggling as a sparring art.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description: You sing, act, juggle, or declaim, and you can hold a room whether or not the room agreed to be held. Performers ride the road circuit between towns and festivals, and your working knowledge of crowds, exits, and hecklers transfers to adventuring far better than anyone expects.
Performer.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Performer. Stagecraft, crowd work, and improvisation. Can earn a bed in any town with a square. Handles hecklers and monsters with the same fundamental technique.

Scribe.name: Scribe
Scribe.description: You copy, notarize, and draft: contracts, letters, guild forms in triplicate. It sounds dull until somebody needs the fine print read in a hurry, and in Belzerg the fine print is where the danger keeps its spare key. You have saved more lives with a raised eyebrow at clause nine than most healers save with magic.
Scribe.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Scribe. Documentation expertise: reads contracts properly, drafts binding language, and spots the trap clause. Devils who deal in contracts regard the character as a professional peer, warily.

God.name: God
abilities: Divine Presence
God.description: You are an actual god. Not a priest, not blessed, not 'god-touched': the genuine article, with a divine domain, a celestial garment that never soils, and a former job that involved being prayed to. You are in Belzerg anyway, for reasons that are your business (demoted, bored, sent down as a clerical matter, or dragged along by someone spiteful). Nobody here believes a word of it. The hagoromo proves nothing to anyone. Your divine power is real and enormous in exactly one direction, and the direction is rarely 'paying for dinner.'
God.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: God. The character is a genuine, original god of Belzerg's heavens, NEVER Aqua or Eris, who are their own people and canon-locked. Describe an unmistakable divine radiance (skin that catches light, eyes with an inner shine, a hagoromo that moves in a breeze nobody feels) that natives read as 'very attractive, probably a con.' NOBODY BELIEVES HE IS A GOD; this is the running joke and it never fully resolves. His divine power is Aqua-shaped: in his true domain (purification, undead, blessing, the miraculous) he is a one-person apocalypse; at everything practical he is a liability, and his pride writes cheques his rent cannot cash. He KNOWS the reincarnation program exists and may reference the modern world and heavenly bureaucracy freely, but natives still never learn otherworlders are real. Undead and devils genuinely sense what they are and react; the Axis Cult and Aqua herself have strong, undignified feelings about a rival god in town. Play divine hubris warm, not cruel.

Goddess.name: Goddess
abilities: Divine Presence
Goddess.description: You are an actual goddess. Not a priest, not blessed, not 'goddess-touched': the genuine article, with a divine domain, a celestial garment that never soils, and a former job that involved being prayed to. You are in Belzerg anyway, for reasons that are your business (demoted, bored, sent down as a clerical matter, or dragged along by someone spiteful). Nobody here believes a word of it. The hagoromo proves nothing to anyone. Your divine power is real and enormous in exactly one direction, and the direction is rarely 'paying for dinner.'
Goddess.traitNarrativeEffects: RACE: Goddess. The character is a genuine, original goddess of Belzerg's heavens, NEVER Aqua or Eris, who are their own people and canon-locked. Describe an unmistakable divine radiance (skin that catches light, eyes with an inner shine, a hagoromo that moves in a breeze nobody feels) that natives read as 'very attractive, probably a con.' NOBODY BELIEVES SHE IS A GODDESS; this is the running joke and it never fully resolves. Her divine power is Aqua-shaped: in her true domain (purification, undead, blessing, the miraculous) she is a one-person apocalypse; at everything practical she is a liability, and her pride writes cheques her rent cannot cash. She KNOWS the reincarnation program exists and may reference the modern world and heavenly bureaucracy freely, but natives still never learn otherworlders are real. Undead and devils genuinely sense what they are and react; the Axis Cult and Aqua herself have strong, undignified feelings about a rival goddess in town. Play divine hubris warm, not cruel.

Wizard.name: Wizard
abilities: Ember Spark
Wizard.description: The honest middle of the caster ladder: past the Mage who can light a candle, short of the Arch-Wizard who can end a village. You know theory, you can cast most of it, and you have opinions about people who skipped the theory.
Wizard.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Wizard. A competent general caster with real theory and no signature spell yet. Reliable elemental work, decent mana, and the quiet resentment of every Arch-Wizard who got there faster.

Warrior.name: Warrior
abilities: Guard Stance
Warrior.description: The class the guild hands to people who showed up with a sword and no plan. Solid, unglamorous, and the reason parties survive long enough to argue about loot. Every advanced fighter started here and most pretend they did not.
Warrior.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Warrior. Frontline basics: hold ground, take hits, hit back. No flash, no technique names yet, honest competence. Grows into Knight, Berserker, or Sword Master.

Runner.name: Runner
abilities: Sprint
Runner.description: You are fast, and in Belzerg fast is a career. Runners carry messages, scout ahead, and are the first out the door when the toad turns out to be three toads. The guild lists it as a support class. Everyone else lists it as the escape plan.
Runner.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Runner. Speed, endurance, and routes. Scouts, couriers, and retreats. Treated as cowardice by people who have never needed one. Grows into Ranger or Master Thief.

Ninja.name: Ninja
abilities: Lurk
Ninja.description: An advanced class imported from somewhere far to the east that nobody can point to on a map. Smoke, blades, disguise, and a dress code. Belzerg's ninjas are mostly reincarnators with expectations, and a few genuine ones who find the reincarnators embarrassing.
Ninja.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Ninja. Stealth, misdirection, and quick blades, with a little illusion for the smoke and the disguises. Dramatic and effective. Insists on the pose. Other ninjas can tell who read about it and who trained.

Beast Tamer.name: Beast Tamer
abilities: Identify Monster
Beast Tamer.description: You understand monsters better than people, which in this kingdom is a professional advantage and a social diagnosis. Tamers read behavior, calm the calmable, and know exactly which things should never be calmed. The guild pays extra for the second list.
Beast Tamer.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Beast Tamer. Reads monsters, calms and directs the tameable, knows which are not. Companions of the animal kind bond fast. NPCs assume the character is either gentle or unhinged and are usually right both ways.

Alcanretia Bath Attendant.name: Alcanretia Bath Attendant
Alcanretia Bath Attendant.description: You scrubbed the sacred pools, folded the towels, and learned to spot an Axis recruiter's approach by the sound of their sandals. You know water, etiquette, and every way a tourist can be wrong.
Alcanretia Bath Attendant.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Alcanretia Bath Attendant. Grew up in the hot spring city's service economy. Impeccable manners, reflexive water sense, deep and specific knowledge of the Axis Cult's recruitment habits. Never surprised by a pamphlet.

Elroad Casino Dealer.name: Elroad Casino Dealer
Elroad Casino Dealer.description: You dealt cards under chandeliers to adventurers spending combat pay they had not finished earning. You can read a bluff, count a table, and you left Elroad with your dignity and none of your savings.
Elroad Casino Dealer.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Elroad Casino Dealer. Professional at odds, tells, and house math. Distrusts luck and respects it. Elroad's staff remember the character, warmly and with an invoice.

Nightless City Stagehand.name: Nightless City Stagehand
Nightless City Stagehand.description: You hauled scenery and fixed lights in the Heartland's stage district while stars had breakdowns three feet away. You can build a set overnight and defuse a diva before curtain.
Nightless City Stagehand.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Nightless City Stagehand. Backstage instincts: rigging, timing, cues, and crisis management around dramatic people. Reads performers like weather. Unimpressed by drama, good at enabling it.

Wiz's Former Shop Assistant.name: Wiz's Former Shop Assistant
Wiz's Former Shop Assistant.description: You worked the counter at a magic shop run by a lich with no business sense. You priced artifacts, catalogued the cursed ones, and watched the shop lose money on every sale. You left with a good eye and a headache.
Wiz's Former Shop Assistant.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Wiz's Former Shop Assistant. Knows magic items, their real value, and why the shop still cannot turn a profit. Wiz remembers the character fondly and Vanir remembers them as a liability. Handles cursed goods calmly.

Frontier Deserter.name: Frontier Deserter
Frontier Deserter.description: You held a line in the north until you did not. Nobody died because you left, which is the story you tell, and the garrison keeps a different one. You know the roads home better than the roads back.
Frontier Deserter.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Frontier Deserter. Survival craft and quiet movement learned the hard way. Carries northern habits and a guilt that surfaces around soldiers. The Marches remember the name; the south does not care.

Axis Cult Choir Kid.name: Axis Cult Choir Kid
Axis Cult Choir Kid.description: You were raised in an Axis chapel and sang in its choir, which means you know the hymns, the theology, and the exact moment a sermon becomes a sales pitch. You are not a member. You could pass as one in your sleep.
Axis Cult Choir Kid.traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Axis Cult Choir Kid. Fluent in Axis liturgy and tactics without being a believer. Can hum the hymns, quote the pamphlet, and deflect a recruiter with their own doctrine. The Cult considers the character lapsed rather than lost.

Died to a Tractor (Isekai'd).name: Died to a Tractor (Isekai'd)
Died to a Tractor (Isekai'd).description: You died of shock after mistaking a slow-moving tractor for a speeding truck, which is not how the goddess phrased it in the report and is exactly how she phrased it to your face. Welcome to Belzerg. Nobody here has tractors either.
Died to a Tractor (Isekai'd).traitNarrativeEffects: ORIGIN: Died to a Tractor. Reincarnated after the least dignified death on record; the goddess still brings it up. Carries modern-world memories and a sensitivity about vehicles. Culture shock plays as a recurring comedy source.

Cheat Skill: Enemy Detection.name: Cheat Skill: Enemy Detection
abilities: Enemy Detection
Cheat Skill: Enemy Detection.description: You chose the sense that tells you something hostile is nearby before it shows itself. It is genuinely excellent for a coward and it does not distinguish between a Demon King's general and a toad with intentions.
Cheat Skill: Enemy Detection.traitNarrativeEffects: DIVINE GIFT: Enemy Detection. The character senses hostile presence and rough direction before it appears. Reliable, undramatic, and the best gift a careful person can pick. Does not grade threat level; a toad and a general ping the same.

Cheat Skill: Create Water.name: Cheat Skill: Create Water
abilities: Create Water
Cheat Skill: Create Water.description: You chose the ability to make clean water from nothing. The goddess laughed. Then you walked through a desert region, sold water to a garrison, and put out a stable fire, and she stopped laughing. It is still not a weapon.
Cheat Skill: Create Water.traitNarrativeEffects: DIVINE GIFT: Create Water. Conjures clean water at will. Utility beyond expectation, comedy beyond intention, and never a weapon. The Axis Cult regards the gift as proof of something. The character disagrees.

Absurd Luck Stat.name: Absurd Luck Stat
abilities: Absurd Luck
Absurd Luck Stat.description: Your luck is so high the goddess asked if you wanted to become a merchant instead. You said no. The dice, the cards, the coin flips, and the one-in-a-thousand escapes all agree with her. Your combat stats do not.
Absurd Luck Stat.traitNarrativeEffects: DIVINE GIFT: Absurd Luck. A luck stat off the chart and mediocre everything else. Gambling bends, rare drops happen, escapes work at the last second. NPCs who notice suggest a career change. Luck is not skill and the world knows the difference.

Apology Coupon Book.name: Apology Coupon Book
abilities: Redeem Apology Coupon
Apology Coupon Book.description: The goddess botched your paperwork, apologized, and handed you a book of divine apology coupons. They are not redeemable anywhere. Once in a great while, somehow, one is.
Apology Coupon Book.traitNarrativeEffects: DIVINE GIFT: Apology Coupon Book. A booklet of worthless heavenly vouchers. Occasionally, unpredictably, heaven honors one: a small miracle, a lucky break, a door unlocked. The character never knows which coupon will work. Neither does heaven.

Rejected Holy Sword.name: Rejected Holy Sword
Rejected Holy Sword.description: You chose a holy sword. It chose someone else. It came with you anyway, out of what it describes as pity, and it is loud about the difference between wielding it and being worthy of it. It is still a very good sword.
Rejected Holy Sword.traitNarrativeEffects: DIVINE GIFT: Rejected Holy Sword. A genuine holy blade that publicly disapproves of its owner. Excellent steel, constant commentary, refuses to glow on command. Devils and undead still fear it. It is waiting for a better hero and says so.

Owes Wiz Money.name: Owes Wiz Money
Owes Wiz Money.description: You bought something from Wiz on credit, which she should never have extended and did, because she is Wiz. She has not asked for it back. Vanir has. Vanir asks every time.
Owes Wiz Money.traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Owes Wiz Money. Wiz is too kind to collect; Vanir is not. The debt follows the character into every shop scene. Wiz is fond of them regardless, which makes it worse.

Sena's Person of Interest.name: Sena's Person of Interest
Sena's Person of Interest.description: The prosecutor has a file on you. It is not thick yet. Sena greets you by full name in public and asks how your week has been in a tone that means she already knows.
Sena's Person of Interest.traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Sena's Person of Interest. The prosecutor watches the character with professional patience. Not charged with anything, yet. Guild staff are polite and careful. Sena is unfailingly courteous and it is terrifying.

Dust's Drinking Buddy.name: Dust's Drinking Buddy
Dust's Drinking Buddy.description: You have closed the guild tavern with Dust more than once, which means you know his schemes, his tab, and the exact moment each night he becomes a liability. Taylor has a look for you.
Dust's Drinking Buddy.traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Dust's Drinking Buddy. Welcome at the worst table in the guild tavern. Dust treats the character as a co-conspirator; Taylor treats them as a bad influence; the tab is shared whether they like it or not.

Blew Up a Stable Once.name: Blew Up a Stable Once
Blew Up a Stable Once.description: It was one stable. It was mostly empty. The horses were fine. The guild has a form with your name pre-printed on it, and the stablemaster crosses the street.
Blew Up a Stable Once.traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Blew Up a Stable Once. Known for one spectacular property-damage incident. Insurance assessors hover, stablemasters flee, and every explosion in town is briefly assumed to be the character's. Deeply unfair. Slightly earned.

Vanir's Preferred Customer.name: Vanir's Preferred Customer
Vanir's Preferred Customer.description: The mask devil likes you, which he expresses by reading your desires aloud and pricing them accordingly. You get the good stock. You pay for it in coin and in having your inner life narrated.
Vanir's Preferred Customer.traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Vanir's Preferred Customer. Vanir enjoys the character's emotional flavor and gives them first pick and full commentary. Excellent deals, no privacy. Other customers find the arrangement unsettling to watch.

Yunyun's Only Friend (Contested).name: Yunyun's Only Friend (Contested)
Yunyun's Only Friend (Contested).description: Yunyun considers you her friend. She has said so, formally, twice. Whether you agreed is not recorded. Megumin has been informed and has feelings about the ranking.
Yunyun's Only Friend (Contested).traitNarrativeEffects: REPUTATION: Yunyun's Only Friend (Contested). Yunyun treats the character as her confirmed friend and rehearses conversations for them. Megumin contests the title. The Crimson Demon village has heard. It is a lot.

Innkeeper.name: Innkeeper
Innkeeper.description: You keep beds, books, and a bar. You know who is sleeping where, who has not paid, and which adventurer is going to be a problem by the sound of their boots on the stairs.
Innkeeper.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Innkeeper. Runs lodging: rooms, tabs, breakfast, and the delicate art of evicting a berserker. Knows every traveler's business. Innkeepers everywhere extend the character professional courtesy and gossip.

Bath Attendant.name: Bath Attendant
Bath Attendant.description: You maintain baths, sacred or otherwise: water quality, towel supply, and the strict etiquette that keeps a hot spring from becoming a brawl. In Alcanretia this is a holy calling. Elsewhere it is a job with steam.
Bath Attendant.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Bath Attendant. Expert in bathhouse operation, water care, and pool etiquette. Can calm a rowdy bath, spot a fake blessing, and heal sore muscles with hot water and patience.

Casino Dealer.name: Casino Dealer
Casino Dealer.description: You run tables: cards, dice, the wheel. You know the odds cold and you know exactly how much the house is cheating, because you were the house. Your dice are weighted. You call them balanced.
Casino Dealer.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Casino Dealer. Professional gambling operator: odds, tells, table control, and house tricks. Can run a game anywhere. Elroad staff recognize a colleague; honest players should count their coins.

Courier.name: Courier
Courier.description: You carry things fast between places that do not trust each other. Letters, parcels, the occasional item that ticks. You know the roads, the shortcuts, and which checkpoints can be talked past.
Courier.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Courier. Route knowledge, stamina, and a professional silence about what is in the package. Guild couriers vouch for the character. Deliveries are a scene, not a summary.

Stagehand.name: Stagehand
Stagehand.description: You build sets, rig lights, and make dramatic people appear on cue. Belzerg's festivals and the Nightless City run on stagehands. Nobody thanks you. The show happens anyway.
Stagehand.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Stagehand. Rigging, carpentry, timing, and crowd logistics. Can stage a festival, a trap, or an entrance. Performers trust the character absolutely and take them for granted completely.

Bounty Clerk.name: Bounty Clerk
Bounty Clerk.description: You file the postings, verify the kills, and stamp the payouts. You know what every monster is worth, who is lying about the count, and how the guild's fine print actually works.
Bounty Clerk.traitNarrativeEffects: PROFESSION: Bounty Clerk. Guild-side expertise: postings, proof of kill, payout math, and fine print. Receptionists treat the character as staff. Can spot a fraudulent bounty claim across the room.

Steal First, Ask Later.name: Steal First, Ask Later
Steal First, Ask Later.description: Every fight starts with you taking something. Their weapon, their plan, their dignity, occasionally their underwear. Whatever comes off the target is the opening move and you improvise from there.
Steal First, Ask Later.traitNarrativeEffects: COMBAT PHILOSOPHY: Steal First. Opens fights by taking something from the enemy and building on the result. Unpredictable, frequently undignified, effective against opponents who rely on one item.

Lure and Drop.name: Lure and Drop
Lure and Drop.description: You do not fight monsters. You arrange for monsters to fall into holes, walk into ambushes, and eat things they should not. The party thinks it is cowardice. The results think otherwise.
Lure and Drop.traitNarrativeEffects: COMBAT PHILOSOPHY: Lure and Drop. Traps, bait, terrain, and patience. Sets up fights so the enemy loses before it starts. Mocked as cowardly until the giant toad is in the pit.

Buff and Pray.name: Buff and Pray
Buff and Pray.description: Your role in combat is to make everyone else better and then hope. Blessings, wards, a stern word to the goddess. You have never landed a killing blow and you are at peace with that.
Buff and Pray.traitNarrativeEffects: COMBAT PHILOSOPHY: Buff and Pray. Support caster to the bone: buffs, wards, healing, encouragement. Contributes everything and takes no credit. Prays audibly during fights, which unsettles both sides.

Overkill Is Underrated.name: Overkill Is Underrated
Overkill Is Underrated.description: The correct amount of force is more. Subtlety is for people who are not sure. Property damage is a rounding error against a problem that is definitely not getting up again.
Overkill Is Underrated.traitNarrativeEffects: COMBAT PHILOSOPHY: Overkill. Maximum force every time, subtlety never. Reliable results, catastrophic bills. The guild's property damage desk knows the character by name.

Let the Crusader Take It.name: Let the Crusader Take It
Let the Crusader Take It.description: There is a person in heavy armor who enjoys being hit. You have built an entire fighting style around this fact. You stand behind them and do the actual damage while they have the time of their life.
Let the Crusader Take It.traitNarrativeEffects: COMBAT PHILOSOPHY: Let the Crusader Take It. Fights from behind a tank, ranged or precise, letting the frontline absorb aggression. Efficient and slightly shameless. Crusaders adore the character.

The Straight Man.name: The Straight Man
The Straight Man.description: Everyone around you is ridiculous and you are the one who points it out. Your job in every scene is to react with the exact right amount of exhausted disbelief. It is thankless and essential.
The Straight Man.traitNarrativeEffects: SOCIAL PERSONA: The Straight Man. The tsukkomi: reacts to absurdity with sharp, tired commentary that keeps scenes grounded. Reads people fast. Companions rely on the character to notice the obvious thing everyone else missed.

The Weirdo Everyone Tolerates.name: The Weirdo Everyone Tolerates
The Weirdo Everyone Tolerates.description: You are strange in a way people have decided to accept. Your enthusiasms are baffling, your timing is wrong, and somehow the party would be worse without you. Nobody can explain this. They have stopped trying.
The Weirdo Everyone Tolerates.traitNarrativeEffects: SOCIAL PERSONA: The Weirdo. Odd interests, wrong timing, undeniable charm. NPCs sigh and then help. Never quite fits and is never quite excluded. Belongs by sheer persistence.

The Sad-Eyes Negotiator.name: The Sad-Eyes Negotiator
The Sad-Eyes Negotiator.description: You have a face that makes people feel bad for saying no. You use it constantly. Merchants discount, guards relent, receptionists find a form. You feel a little guilty. Not enough to stop.
The Sad-Eyes Negotiator.traitNarrativeEffects: SOCIAL PERSONA: Sad-Eyes Negotiator. Wins concessions through sympathy: the look, the sigh, the quiet disappointment. Works on nearly everyone once. Vanir finds it delicious. Sena finds it suspicious.

The Guild Gossip.name: The Guild Gossip
The Guild Gossip.description: You know everything about everyone in the guild hall and you consider it your duty to share. Who owes whom, who likes whom, who blew up what. Receptionists feed you tips. Adventurers fear your table.
The Guild Gossip.traitNarrativeEffects: SOCIAL PERSONA: The Guild Gossip. A walking rumor mill with excellent sources. Knows the town's business before the town does. Useful for information, dangerous with secrets, beloved by receptionists.

The Tired Adult.name: The Tired Adult
The Tired Adult.description: You are the only person in any given room who has thought about the consequences. You manage the party the way a parent manages a field trip: headcounts, snacks, and a permanent low-grade headache.
The Tired Adult.traitNarrativeEffects: SOCIAL PERSONA: The Tired Adult. The responsible one by default. Organizes, plans, and sighs. Companions defer to the character and ignore them in equal measure. NPCs in authority recognize a kindred spirit.

Explosion Devotee.name: Explosion Devotee
Explosion Devotee.description: You have seen Explosion cast once and nothing else will ever be enough. You attend the daily casting. You have a favorite crater. You will spend everything you earn on staffs you cannot use.
Explosion Devotee.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Explosion Devotee. Obsessed with Explosion magic as spectacle and creed, whether or not the character can cast it. Follows Megumin's schedule, drains funds on gear, defends the discipline in arguments nobody started.

Trusts Aqua.name: Trusts Aqua
Trusts Aqua.description: You believe her. Every time. She says the plan will work and you think, this time, it might. It has never worked. You will believe her again tomorrow.
Trusts Aqua.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Trusts Aqua. Takes the water goddess at her word despite all evidence. Follows her plans, buys her explanations, defends her in public. The party has an intervention scheduled.

Allergic to Paperwork.name: Allergic to Paperwork
Allergic to Paperwork.description: Forms make you physically unwell. You sign without reading, lose receipts on purpose, and have never once filed a property damage report correctly. In a kingdom run on fine print, this is a disability.
Allergic to Paperwork.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Allergic to Paperwork. Cannot or will not handle forms, contracts, or receipts. Signs blind, files wrong, owes fees for lateness. Devils and prosecutors find the character a gift.

Falls for Every Scam.name: Falls for Every Scam
Falls for Every Scam.description: The painted plastic sword. The map to treasure that is definitely real. The deal that is too good and is exactly as bad as it sounds. You have bought all of them. You will buy the next one.
Falls for Every Scam.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Falls for Every Scam. Believes every pitch, buys every fake, trusts every stranger with a deal. Merchants light up when the character enters. Vanir considers it cheating.

Cannot Refuse Darkness.name: Cannot Refuse Darkness
Cannot Refuse Darkness.description: When the crusader asks to take the hit, to stand in the trap, to be the bait, you say yes. You know she enjoys it. You know it is a bad plan. You say yes anyway, every time.
Cannot Refuse Darkness.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Cannot Refuse Darkness. Enables the crusader's worst impulses out of guilt, affection, or exhaustion. Plans bend around her wanting to be hit. The party's tactical ceiling is her happiness.

Snack Priority.name: Snack Priority
Snack Priority.description: In any crisis you will secure food first. Before the escape, before the healing, before the plan. You have been swallowed by a toad while holding a skewer. You kept the skewer.
Snack Priority.traitNarrativeEffects: FATAL FLAW: Snack Priority. Food comes before survival in every decision. Stops mid-battle for provisions, spends quest pay on meals, judges towns by their stalls. Reliably distracted by cooking smells.

Insists on the Full Incantation.name: Insists on the Full Incantation
Insists on the Full Incantation.description: You will not cast, strike, or even open a door without the complete chant, name, and pose. Shortcuts are for people with no respect for the craft.
Insists on the Full Incantation.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Always performs the full incantation and pose, even for trivial actions. Delays everything. Deeply satisfying to watch, exhausting to wait for.

Corrects Aqua's Math.name: Corrects Aqua's Math
Corrects Aqua's Math.description: Whenever the goddess counts, prices, or estimates, you correct her. Out loud. She has never once been right and she has never once forgiven you.
Corrects Aqua's Math.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Reflexively corrects Aqua's arithmetic in front of witnesses. Always right. Never thanked.

Bathes at Every Hot Spring.name: Bathes at Every Hot Spring
Bathes at Every Hot Spring.description: You cannot pass a spring without a soak. Quests are delayed. Parties wait. You emerge relaxed and slightly late for everything.
Bathes at Every Hot Spring.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Detours into every hot spring encountered. Recruiters find the character every time.

Hums the Axis Hymn.name: Hums the Axis Hymn
Hums the Axis Hymn.description: You do not belong to the Cult, but the hymn is catchy and it lives in your head. You hum it under stress. People assume things.
Hums the Axis Hymn.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Hums Axis Cult hymns unconsciously. Recruiters hear it as a sign. The character is not a member and keeps saying so.

Keeps a Debt Ledger.name: Keeps a Debt Ledger
Keeps a Debt Ledger.description: You record every coin owed to you and by you, with interest, dates, and moral commentary. You read from it at inopportune moments.
Keeps a Debt Ledger.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Maintains a meticulous ledger of every debt in the party and quotes it aloud. Nobody asked. Everybody owes.

Mispronounces Names Dramatically.name: Mispronounces Names Dramatically
Mispronounces Names Dramatically.description: You get every name wrong, with confidence and volume. Beldia becomes Bell Deer. Vanir becomes Vanilla. The mask devil has stopped correcting you.
Mispronounces Names Dramatically.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Confidently mangles every name, especially important ones. Villains find it disrespectful. Allies have given up.

Talks to Chomusuke.name: Talks to Chomusuke
Talks to Chomusuke.description: You converse with Megumin's cat as if it were a colleague. You ask its opinion on plans. It has never answered and you have never doubted it agrees.
Talks to Chomusuke.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Holds full conversations with Chomusuke and defers to the cat's judgment. Megumin approves. The cat is unreadable.

Rates Every Tavern.name: Rates Every Tavern
Rates Every Tavern.description: Every inn, bar, and stall gets a score out of ten, delivered unprompted to whoever is nearest. You keep a list. Innkeepers have seen it.
Rates Every Tavern.traitNarrativeEffects: QUIRK: Reviews every establishment aloud on a ten-point scale. Innkeepers are wary. The list is surprisingly accurate.

Alcanretia Bath Yukata.name: Alcanretia Bath Yukata
Alcanretia Bath Yukata.description: A light bathhouse yukata in the Alcanretia style, patterned with waves, worn loose with wooden sandals and the damp hair of someone who just left a sacred spring.
Alcanretia Bath Yukata.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): A light bathhouse yukata in the Alcanretia style, patterned with waves, worn loose with wooden sandals and the damp hair of someone who just left a sacred spring. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Elroad Dealer's Vest.name: Elroad Dealer's Vest
Elroad Dealer's Vest.description: A fitted casino vest with a card-deck pin and rolled sleeves, the uniform of someone who has watched a thousand adventurers lose their combat pay and kept a straight face.
Elroad Dealer's Vest.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): A fitted casino vest with a card-deck pin and rolled sleeves, the uniform of someone who has watched a thousand adventurers lose their combat pay and kept a straight face. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Green Tracksuit.name: Green Tracksuit
Green Tracksuit.description: A green tracksuit from another world, comfortable, unheroic, and worn in Belzerg with total commitment. Natives assume it is a uniform for a profession they have not heard of.
Green Tracksuit.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): A green tracksuit from another world, comfortable, unheroic, and worn in Belzerg with total commitment. Natives assume it is a uniform for a profession they have not heard of. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Hakama and Katana Rig.name: Hakama and Katana Rig
Hakama and Katana Rig.description: A pleated hakama, a fitted top, and a katana worn at the hip in the eastern manner, the outfit of someone who takes swordsmanship, and posing, seriously.
Hakama and Katana Rig.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): A pleated hakama, a fitted top, and a katana worn at the hip in the eastern manner, the outfit of someone who takes swordsmanship, and posing, seriously. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Shop Apron.name: Shop Apron
Shop Apron.description: A sturdy shopkeeper's apron over practical clothes, pockets full of tags and chalk, the look of someone who prices things for a living and has opinions about your haggling.
Shop Apron.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): A sturdy shopkeeper's apron over practical clothes, pockets full of tags and chalk, the look of someone who prices things for a living and has opinions about your haggling. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Cult Pamphleteer Sash.name: Cult Pamphleteer Sash
Cult Pamphleteer Sash.description: Plain traveling clothes cut across by a bright blue Axis Cult sash stuffed with pamphlets, the field dress of a recruiter or someone who lost a bet with one.
Cult Pamphleteer Sash.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Outfit): Plain traveling clothes cut across by a bright blue Axis Cult sash stuffed with pamphlets, the field dress of a recruiter or someone who lost a bet with one. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Alcanretia Hot Spring Street.name: Alcanretia Hot Spring Street
Alcanretia Hot Spring Street.description: A steaming street in the hot spring city, bathhouse lanterns glowing through mist, pilgrims and tourists in yukata, and a recruiter closing in from the left.
Alcanretia Hot Spring Street.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Scene Background): A steaming street in the hot spring city, bathhouse lanterns glowing through mist, pilgrims and tourists in yukata, and a recruiter closing in from the left. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Beldia's Castle Gate.name: Beldia's Castle Gate
Beldia's Castle Gate.description: The black iron gate of a dullahan's castle outside Axel, banners tattered, a shadow horse's hoofprints in the dust, and a fresh explosion crater in the courtyard beyond.
Beldia's Castle Gate.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Scene Background): The black iron gate of a dullahan's castle outside Axel, banners tattered, a shadow horse's hoofprints in the dust, and a fresh explosion crater in the courtyard beyond. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Keele's Dungeon Entrance.name: Keele's Dungeon Entrance
Keele's Dungeon Entrance.description: The mossy stone mouth of Keele's Dungeon, a guild warning sign nailed crooked beside it, torchlight fading into a descent that beginner parties enter loudly and leave quietly.
Keele's Dungeon Entrance.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Scene Background): The mossy stone mouth of Keele's Dungeon, a guild warning sign nailed crooked beside it, torchlight fading into a descent that beginner parties enter loudly and leave quietly. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Guild Rooftop at Dusk.name: Guild Rooftop at Dusk
Guild Rooftop at Dusk.description: The flat tiled roof of the Axel guild hall at dusk, town lights coming on below, laundry lines, and the best seat in the city for watching the daily Explosion from a safe distance.
Guild Rooftop at Dusk.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Scene Background): The flat tiled roof of the Axel guild hall at dusk, town lights coming on below, laundry lines, and the best seat in the city for watching the daily Explosion from a safe distance. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Axel Cemetery.name: Axel Cemetery
Axel Cemetery.description: Axel's quiet cemetery at the town's edge, tidy headstones, a warding lantern on the gravekeeper's post, and the faint chill that means the Axis Cult's undead problem is not entirely solved.
Axel Cemetery.traitNarrativeEffects: APPEARANCE (Scene Background): Axel's quiet cemetery at the town's edge, tidy headstones, a warding lantern on the gravekeeper's post, and the faint chill that means the Axis Cult's undead problem is not entirely solved. Purely visual; no stats or gameplay effect.

Healer.name: Healer
abilities: Mend Skin
Healer.description: The other kind of healer: no church, no god, just trained hands and magic that remembers how a body is supposed to fit together. Healers close wounds faster than any priest, cure what a priest can only pray over, and are the only ones who can patch up an undead friend without setting them on fire. Axel's clinics are busy, the pay is honest, and the patients complain the whole time.
Healer.traitNarrativeEffects: CLASS: Healer. Hands-on restorative magic with no faith required: mends wounds, poison, disease, and broken bones on anyone, undead and devils included. Priests respect the results and are mildly offended by the lack of prayer.

Race.name: Race
Race.description: What species are you? This determines your physical traits, innate abilities, and how NPCs in Belzerg react to you on sight. Crimson Demons have red eyes and dramatic introductions. Otherworlders have modern knowledge and culture shock. Choose what you ARE.

subcategories.name: Peoples of Belzerg
subcategories.description: The mortal peoples who live, work, and adventure across the kingdom.

subcategories.name: Touched by the Beyond
subcategories.description: Those whose nature was altered by death, contract, heritage, or misfortune.

subcategories.name: From Another World
subcategories.description: Reincarnated souls sent by a goddess, carrying memories of a world with convenience stores.

Class.name: Class
Class.description: Your guild-registered adventurer class. This is your core combat identity and determines your starting skills, equipment, and the specific way you contribute to (or undermine) your party. Adventurer is the weakest. Arch-Wizard is the most dramatic. Crusader cannot hit anything.

subcategories.name: Starting Classes
subcategories.description: The entry-level classes anyone can register for at the Guild.

subcategories.name: Advanced Classes
subcategories.description: Prestigious classes with real stat requirements and real reputations.

subcategories.name: Civilian Classes
subcategories.description: Classes that make their living off the battlefield, which is often the smarter play.

Magic Affinity.name: Magic Affinity
Magic Affinity.description: Your elemental alignment. Fire, water, ice, explosion, or none at all. This provides a small skill bonus and subtle ambient effects (fire mages make candles flicker, ice mages keep drinks cold). Choose 'No Magic' if you solve problems with your hands.

subcategories.name: Elemental Affinity
subcategories.description: A natural leaning toward one element, shaping which spells come easily.

subcategories.name: Sacred and Profane
subcategories.description: Magic drawn from the goddesses or from the places they do not look.

subcategories.name: Specialist and Generalist
subcategories.description: The single overwhelming obsession, or an honest lack of talent for any of it.

Origin Story.name: Origin Story
Origin Story.description: How did you end up as an adventurer in Belzerg? Isekai'd by a goddess? Born here? Escaped from the Axis Cult? Your origin shapes your starting knowledge, your relationship with the world, and which NPCs recognize you.

subcategories.name: Reincarnated
subcategories.description: You died somewhere else and a goddess offered you a second try.

subcategories.name: Native Born
subcategories.description: You have always been here, and you know how things actually work.

subcategories.name: Left Something Behind
subcategories.description: You walked away from an organization, and it may not have finished with you.

Divine Gift.name: Divine Gift
Divine Gift.description: What did the goddess give you when you were reincarnated? A legendary weapon? An enhanced body? The goddess herself? Nothing out of spite? If you were born in Belzerg, pick 'Born Here.' This is the cheat item that defines your starting advantage.

subcategories.name: Power and Possessions
subcategories.description: The gifts most reincarnators choose, and most later reconsider.

subcategories.name: Knowledge Gifts
subcategories.description: Subtler advantages that turn out to matter more than a big sword.

subcategories.name: Unusual Choices
subcategories.description: You picked something strange, nothing at all, or were never offered.

Starting Reputation.name: Starting Reputation
traits: Axis Cult Signed You Up Once
Starting Reputation.description: What does the guild already know about you? Are you a nobody? A promising rookie? A troublemaker with a damage record? This determines NPC first impressions and the guild's initial attitude toward you.

subcategories.name: How Belzerg Sees You
traits: Axis Cult Signed You Up Once
subcategories.description: What the Guild and the town already believe about you on day one.

Profession.name: Profession
Profession.description: Your trade skill beyond adventuring. Blacksmith, alchemist, cook, fisher, or pure adventurer. This determines what you can craft, gather, and sell between quests.

subcategories.name: Crafting Trades
subcategories.description: You make things. Adventurers break things. The business model is sound.

subcategories.name: Consumable Trades
subcategories.description: You brew, gather, and prepare what a party consumes on the road.

subcategories.name: Field Trades
subcategories.description: You make your living out in the world rather than behind a counter.

subcategories.name: None
subcategories.description: You kill things for money and hope the loot covers the bar tab.

subcategories.name: Town Trades
subcategories.description: Professions of counters, stages, and paperwork. Civilization has jobs too.

Combat Philosophy.name: Combat Philosophy
Combat Philosophy.description: How do you fight? Explosions only? Dirty tricks? Human shield? Run away? This shapes how combat is narrated and how NPCs evaluate your fighting style. Every approach is valid. Some are just less dignified.

subcategories.name: Approach to Violence
subcategories.description: How you actually fight when the shouting starts.

Social Persona.name: Social Persona
Social Persona.description: How do you interact with people? The reluctant leader who complains but delivers? The lone wolf who bonds slowly? The class clown who deflects with humor? This shapes your party dynamics and NPC relationships.

subcategories.name: Public Face
subcategories.description: How you present yourself before anyone learns better.

Fatal Flaw.name: Fatal Flaw
Fatal Flaw.description: Every KonoSuba character has the one thing that makes them funny. This is yours. Masochist, chuunibyou, chronic debt, hopelessly lazy. Your flaw creates recurring comedy situations and shapes how NPCs react to your behavior.

subcategories.name: The Thing That Ruins You
subcategories.description: Everyone in Belzerg has one. Yours is load-bearing for the comedy.

Quirks.name: Quirks
Quirks.description: Optional comedy traits that create running gags. Pick two. These are the specific, funny details that make your character memorable: terrible cooking, fear of frogs, dramatic entrance compulsion, accidentally intimidating everyone you meet.

subcategories.name: Quirk
subcategories.description: Small habits and compulsions. Pick two; they will come up.

Body Type.name: Body Type
Body Type.description: Your build and physical presence, the first thing the world reads before you say a word. Belzerg judges instantly and updates never. Choose the frame that carries your legend, or at least your luggage.

subcategories.name: Slight and Agile
subcategories.description: Frames built for speed, reach, and getting out of the way.

subcategories.name: Solid and Strong
subcategories.description: Frames built for taking hits, moving weight, or simply being comfortable.

Skin Tone.name: Skin Tone
Skin Tone.description: Your complexion, rendered faithfully in your portrait. Belzerg's sun, spray, forge-heat and library shade have produced every shade there is, and the kingdom has opinions about none of them. Pick what you see in the mirror, or what you would like to.

subcategories.name: Fair to Olive
subcategories.description: Lighter complexions across warm and cool undertones.

subcategories.name: Tan to Deep
subcategories.description: Deeper complexions, plus the unnatural tones that come from curse or blight.

Hair Style.name: Hair Style
Hair Style.description: How you wear your hair, which in Belzerg is a load-bearing personality statement. It is the first thing people describe about you and the last thing to survive an explosion. Choose with the confidence of someone who owns a comb, whether or not you do.

subcategories.name: Short and Practical
subcategories.description: Cuts that stay out of the way of a helmet or a fight.

subcategories.name: Long and Styled
subcategories.description: Longer cuts and deliberate styling, for those with time and vanity to spare.

subcategories.name: Tied and Bound
subcategories.description: Hair gathered, braided, or pinned for work, travel, or ceremony.

subcategories.name: Dramatic and Unusual
subcategories.description: Cuts that make a statement before you do. Crimson Demons approve.

Hair Color.name: Hair Color
Hair Color.description: Your hair color. In Belzerg certain shades carry heavy associations: silver reads as blessed, anything crimson-adjacent reads as about to give a speech. Natural or improbable, wear it like you chose it on purpose.

subcategories.name: Natural Shades
subcategories.description: Colors that occur without magic, dye, or divine intervention.

subcategories.name: Striking Shades
subcategories.description: Rare and unusual colors that draw a second look anywhere in Belzerg.

subcategories.name: Magical and Marked
subcategories.description: Colors that suggest heritage, magic, or something that happened.

Eyes.name: Eyes
Eyes.description: Your eye color, the detail portrait artists charge extra for. Crimson marks a Crimson Demon anywhere in the kingdom and obligates you to a dramatic introduction. Everything else is merely memorable.

subcategories.name: Marked Eyes
subcategories.description: Eyes that signal heritage, magic, or an unusual history.

subcategories.name: Common Colors
subcategories.description: Eye colors seen every day across the kingdom.

subcategories.name: Rare Colors
subcategories.description: Uncommon shades that people remember and comment on.

Facial Features.name: Facial Features
Facial Features.description: Optional finishing touches: the default expression, the memorable mark, the scar with a story you will be asked to tell. Pick up to two. These are what people describe after meeting you, usually inaccurately.

subcategories.name: Expression and Bearing
subcategories.description: The default face you wear when nobody is watching.

subcategories.name: Marks and Scars
subcategories.description: Permanent features with a story attached.

subcategories.name: Worn Details
subcategories.description: Small things added to the face rather than part of it.

Outfit.name: Outfit
Outfit.description: What you wear to work, where work involves monsters. Function, fashion, or an uneasy treaty between the two. The guild has no dress code, which explains a great deal about the guild.

subcategories.name: Adventuring Gear
subcategories.description: Practical kit worn on the job by people who expect to be hit.

subcategories.name: Distinctive
subcategories.description: Outfits that read as a statement before you open your mouth.

subcategories.name: Faith and Order
subcategories.description: Vestments and uniforms of Belzerg's institutions.

subcategories.name: Formal and Fine
subcategories.description: Attire for court, ceremony, and situations where the wrong coat costs you.

subcategories.name: Civilian and Trade
subcategories.description: Clothing for work that happens indoors, or at least off the battlefield.

Scene Background.name: Scene Background
Scene Background.description: The setting your portrait is composed against. Choose where your story imagines itself: a warm tavern, a market in full cry, a crater you are legally responsible for.

subcategories.name: Interior and Institution
subcategories.description: Backgrounds set inside the places that run the kingdom.

subcategories.name: Town and Settlement
subcategories.description: Backgrounds set among the buildings and people of Belzerg.

subcategories.name: Wilderness and Road
subcategories.description: Backgrounds set out in the open country between settlements.

subcategories.name: Dramatic
subcategories.description: Backgrounds chosen for mood rather than geography.

Portrait Style.name: Portrait Style
Portrait Style.description: The art style your portrait is rendered in, from crisp cel shading to soft watercolor. Purely a matter of taste, and the only arena in which Belzerg will not judge you.

subcategories.name: Clean and Graphic
subcategories.description: Crisp linework and flat color, closest to the anime look.

subcategories.name: Painted and Textured
subcategories.description: Softer, richer rendering with visible brush, wash, or pencil.

Portrait Framing.name: Portrait Framing
Portrait Framing.description: How much of you the portrait shows: a tight close-up on your expression, or a full-body shot with stance and attitude. Decide how much of yourself to commit to the record. Three-Quarter View and Half Body match the main cast's portrait framing, so pick one of those to fit in beside Aqua, Darkness, and the rest; the other options are yours to defy convention with.

subcategories.name: Close Framing
subcategories.description: Tighter crops that put the face and expression first.

subcategories.name: Wide Framing
subcategories.description: Wider compositions that show outfit, stance, and attitude.

character.name: character
character.description: A mortal person: human, demi-human, otherworlder, or reincarnated soul. No damage modifiers. Fully subject to social pressure, bribery, and comedy. Standard rules apply.

undead.name: undead
undead.description: Skeletons, zombies, wights, and their kin. Take heavy damage from light and fire, shrug off physical blows, immune to poison and dark. Cannot be reasoned with, bribed, or embarrassed. Prime target for any priest, which is why the Axis Cult is so insufferable about it.

lich.name: lich
lich.description: A powerful undead spellcaster. Extremely dangerous in principle; in Belzerg the most famous one gave up villainy to run a failing magic shop. Vulnerable to light, resistant to physical and dark, immune to poison. Can be reasoned with, unlike lesser undead, and is often lonely.

devil.name: devil
devil.description: Devils from the underworld who operate through contracts, deals, and the consumption of negative emotions. They are intelligent, manipulative, and bound by the terms of their own agreements. Vanir and Maxwell are the most prominent devils in Belzerg. Devils are vulnerable to holy and light magic but resistant to dark and psychic effects. They cannot be poisoned.

dullahan.name: dullahan
dullahan.description: A headless knight of the Demon King's army: heavily armored, carries its own head, immune to fear and social pressure through the simple fact of having no face to read. Resists physical blows. Some are secretly enormous perverts, which is its own kind of vulnerability.

chimera.name: chimera
chimera.description: A growth chimera that modifies its own body by absorbing other creatures and magical artifacts, gaining their traits and abilities. Resistant to elemental damage due to hybrid physiology. No consistent weakness because the body is always changing. Combat should emphasize the chimera adapting mid-fight and the party needing to find the current weak point.

goblin.name: goblin
goblin.description: Small, cunning humanoid creatures that live in organized underground societies. More intelligent than surface dwellers expect: they have kings, military structure, and conduct raids through planned tunnel networks. Individually weak but dangerous in groups. Vulnerable to fire and light magic, which disrupts their dark-adapted vision. Can be negotiated with, bribed, or intimidated, but will fight if their territory is threatened.

humanoid enemy.name: humanoid enemy
humanoid enemy.description: Mortal adversaries: bandits, rogue adventurers, desperate debtors, cranky nobles' hired muscle. No special damage profile. Can be talked down, bribed, intimidated, or scammed. Standard tactics apply.

giant toad.name: giant toad
giant toad.description: The signature nuisance monster of Axel: a huge, dim amphibian that swallows rookie adventurers whole and spits them out covered in slime and shame. Slow, weak to fire and piercing, but embarrassingly effective against overconfident beginners. Cannot be reasoned with; only motivated by hunger.

beginner beast.name: beginner beast
beginner beast.description: Weak local wildlife around Axel: giant crabs, one-hit slimes, oversized bugs. Fodder for leveling. No special profile beyond being convenient XP that occasionally kills a rookie anyway.

demon general.name: demon general
demon general.description: A general of the Demon King's army: a boss-tier threat with a distinct theme and agenda. Individually powerful and often eccentric enough to be talked out of the whole villainy thing. Damage profile varies by general; treat as a serious, dramatic, occasionally negotiable threat.

useless goddess.name: useless goddess
useless goddess.description: A genuine deity operating far below capacity in daily life. Immense power in her actual domain (purification, resurrection, undead-annihilation) and comprehensively useless everywhere else. Immune to conventional death in dramatic ways; a magnet for trouble, debt, and indignity. Cannot be made to take anything seriously until it is far too late.

crimson demon.name: crimson demon
crimson demon.description: A member of the Crimson Demon clan: a powerful, dramatic mage with high intelligence, crimson eyes, and no volume control. Resists arcane damage from long practice. In combat, expect a devastating spell followed immediately by collapse or a monologue. Socially, expect a signature pose.

deadly poison slime.name: deadly poison slime
deadly poison slime.description: A slime variant that dissolves and absorbs organic matter, taking the form of consumed creatures. Immune to poison, resistant to physical attacks that pass through its fluid body, but vulnerable to fire and ice which solidify or evaporate its mass. Can disguise itself as a humanoid using absorbed forms. Intelligent, manipulative, and extremely dangerous at close range.

winter spirit.name: winter spirit
winter spirit.description: Magical ice spirits that manifest in areas of permanent winter. Snow Sprites are the common variety: small, luminous, and valuable for their magical cores. The Winter Shogun is the apex winter spirit: a massive, terrifying entity that demands respect and will kill anyone who shows disrespect for winter. The correct response to the Winter Shogun is to bow deeply and hope it accepts the gesture.

succubus.name: succubus
succubus.description: Dream-weaving demons who operate discreetly among human settlements, trading in customized pleasant dreams rather than violence. Succubi maintain flawless human disguises and survive by being useful, quiet, and commercially valuable to the communities that officially do not know they exist. They avoid combat entirely; their charm abilities are business tools, not weapons. Physically fragile and socially formidable.

one hit bear.name: one hit bear
one hit bear.description: Enormous forest predators whose name is a plain description of what they do to an unprepared adventurer. They are fast, overwhelmingly strong, and appear in territory rated far below their actual threat, which is how they maintain their reputation. Not intelligent and not malicious, simply the reason rookies are told to stay on the road. Vulnerable to coordinated ranged attack; devastating in melee.

flying cabbage.name: flying cabbage
flying cabbage.description: Magical produce that takes flight when ripe and defends itself with unexpected aggression. Individually harmless and collectively a genuine seasonal hazard, flying cabbages are the signature agricultural crisis of the southern farmlands and the subject of an annual guild-sanctioned harvest brawl. They are nutritionally excellent and profoundly undignified to fight.

kobold.name: kobold
kobold.description: Small burrowing humanoids who work in coordinated packs and favor traps, ambushes, and tunnels over open engagement. Individually weak and collectively a real problem for adventurers who assume small means harmless. Kobolds are territorial rather than cruel and will negotiate if approached correctly, which almost nobody attempts.

skeleton warrior.name: skeleton warrior
skeleton warrior.description: Animated bone soldiers raised in numbers by undead commanders, retaining fragments of the training they had in life. They do not tire, do not flee, and do not feel the wounds that would stop a living opponent. Purification and holy magic destroy them outright; blunt force works better than blades against a body with no flesh to cut.

orc.name: orc
orc.description: Large, disciplined humanoid raiders who fight in organized warbands under the Demon King's banner or as independent bandits. Orcs are physically powerful, genuinely tactical, and far more coordinated than the monsters of the southern regions, which makes encountering them a clear signal that a traveler has left safe country.

harpy.name: harpy
harpy.description: Winged humanoid predators that hunt from the air and strike travelers on exposed roads and ridgelines. Their advantage is entirely mobility: they harry, dive, and withdraw, and a party without ranged capability can be worn down without ever landing a blow. Fragile once grounded.

sand worm.name: sand worm
sand worm.description: Enormous burrowing predators that ambush from beneath loose ground, swallowing prey whole in a single strike. They sense vibration rather than sight or sound, which makes stillness the correct response and running the fatal one. A serious threat in open terrain and helpless once fully surfaced.

golem.name: golem
golem.description: Constructed guardians of stone, clay, or metal, animated by embedded magic and bound to a task they will pursue without fatigue, fear, or reconsideration. Golems are immensely durable and slow, and the reliable counter is either disrupting the animating magic or simply outlasting something with no capacity to adapt.

plant monster.name: plant monster
plant monster.description: Ambulatory hostile flora found in deep forest and root-labyrinth terrain: grasping vines, snapping maws, and spore clouds. They are rooted or slow-moving and rely on entrapment rather than pursuit, which makes them dangerous in dense terrain and trivial in the open. Fire is the universal answer and the forest is the reason nobody uses it.

aquatic monster.name: aquatic monster
aquatic monster.description: River and delta predators that ambush from beneath the waterline: eels, giant fish, and worse things that came upstream from deep water. They hold every advantage in their element and lose most of it on land, which shapes every sensible tactic against them. The Riverlands run on knowing which channels they occupy.

dragon.name: dragon
dragon.description: Apex predators of genuine intelligence and overwhelming physical and magical power, rare enough in Belzerg that most adventurers never see one. A dragon is not a quest, it is a regional event. They are proud, articulate, and negotiable, which is almost always the better option than fighting.

companion.name: companion
companion.description: A humanoid adult built to travel with, argue with, and possibly fall for. Companions have full lives, real jobs, and their own opinions about the player's plans. They can join parties, hold grudges, bank favors, and pursue romance through the Realism Gate like anyone else. Standard mortal rules; above-standard screen presence.

familiar.name: familiar
familiar.description: A small bonded magical creature granted by the Divine Familiar gift and tied to that one person. Only that gift creates a familiar: a stray, a pet, or any other ordinary animal is type animal, never this. Familiars have no meaningful combat value and are never targeted as threats; their power is social, comedic, and occasionally, infuriatingly, being right. They communicate only as their own record specifies (posture, expressive silence, judgmental stares), never in speech unless explicitly authored. They are creatures, not people: no romance, no surname or title, one short pet name of its own, described as the animal or entity it is. A familiar stays with its person across scenes unless its person tells it to stay behind or sends it home, and then it waits there. It eats better than they do and is beloved by everyone its person has ever tried to negotiate with.

animal.name: animal
animal.description: An ordinary, non-magical animal: a stray cat, a guard dog, a cart horse, a market pigeon, livestock. It belongs to a place or an owner, not to the player. It appears when a scene has reason to show it, behaves like the animal it is, and stays where it lives when the party moves on. It never joins the party or follows the player between scenes unless the player deliberately adopts, buys, or tames it, and it leaves again the moment the player sends it away or leaves it behind. No speech, no human name, no combat value worth a roll.

health.name: health
health.usageInstructions:
### Health Changes
- Small injuries: -1 to 15% player health
- Medium injuries: -5 to 25% player health
- Massive injuries: -15 to 50% of player health
- Normal Healing potions: +30-40 or ~30% of max health, whichever is greater
- Greater Healing potions: ~50% of max health
- Bandages: +20 or ~15% of max health, whichever is greater
- Waking from unconsciousness: return to between half health and full health, depending on how well your recovery was.
- Being revived from death: return to full health.
### Don't Deduct Health When
- The story mentions treated or untreated wounds
- Story mentions pain from a wound
- When unconscious or carried
- An environment is generally dangerous, but does not explicitly damage the character

Mana.name: Mana
Mana.usageInstructions:
### Mana Costs
- Cantrip / minor effect: 2-5 mana
- Basic spell / ability: 8-15 mana
- Moderate spell / ability: 18-30 mana
- Powerful spell / ability: 35-50 mana
- Ultimate / desperate ability: 55-70 mana
- Cantrips and minor effects cost almost nothing but deal modest damage or provide small utility.
- Basic spells and abilities are your bread and butter: reliable, affordable, and sustainable across a full fight.
- Moderate abilities are your tactical tools: crowd control, area effects, strong heals, or enhanced strikes. Use them to shift a fight in your favor.
- Powerful abilities are your heavy hitters: save them for bosses, emergencies, or moments that need to end decisively.
- Ultimates are dramatic, story-defining moves; they leave you nearly drained and should feel like a last resort or a triumphant finisher.
### Mana Recovery
- Passive recovery: 2 mana per turn in combat.
- Rest recovery: 3× passive rate (6 per turn) when resting, camping, or during downtime.
- Mana potions: +25 to +40 mana.
- Some abilities, Blessings, or equipment may restore mana under specific conditions.
### When To Deduct Mana
- The player explicitly casts a spell or activates a magical ability
- A Blessing effect that clearly draws on magical energy is used
- A combat class ability with a mana cost is activated
### Don't Deduct Mana When
- A passive or always-on effect is running (those are part of your baseline)
- The story mentions magical ambiance, background magic, or the sensation of mana
- A non-magical action is taken (swinging a sword, dodging, persuading, etc.)

### High-Cost and High-Level Casting
- Apex abilities (signature peaks, forbidden techniques): 80-120 mana. These strain even deep pools.
- At high levels the pool grows large, but Belzerg is not a power fantasy: a big pool buys more attempts, not freedom from cost. Set-piece moments should chain enough powerful abilities that the pool visibly drains, and sustained ultimate use exhausts anyone.
- Mana exhaustion is dramatic, not just numeric: casting on an empty pool draws on the body, with visible cost.
- EXPLOSION is the extreme case, priced by tier: Explosion and Concentrated Blast 100 Mana; Crimson Detonation 130; Scarlet Cataclysm, Devastation Pillar, and Worldscar Blast 150; Doomsday Blossom and Heaven Piercing Detonation 180; Crimson God Annihilation 200. The lesser Detonation Series spells use the normal bands. A caster with Mana left over stays standing, drained. A cast that takes the pool to 0, or that the pool cannot cover, takes the rest from the body: the caster collapses, helpless until they rest, instead of paying health. Any caster may pour in the whole pool for a bigger blast and collapse on purpose; Megumin does, every time.

### Casting on Empty and Overcast Rules
- At 0 mana, spells CAN still be cast by burning the body: pay double the mana cost from health instead. Narrate it as visible harm: bleeding from the nose, frost-white fingers, cracking skin. This is a desperate, dramatic option, never routine.
- After any overcast, the caster is Strained for the rest of the scene: casting costs +25%, and concentration checks are harder.
### Concentration and Upkeep
- Maintained effects (barriers, summons, sustained flight, active illusions) reserve 1-3 mana per turn as upkeep while active.
- Taking a solid hit while concentrating risks dropping the effect unless the caster steadies themselves.
### Affinity and Environment
- Casting aligned magic in an aligned place (fire near a volcano, water at Alcanretia's springs, divine magic at a church) runs 20-30% cheaper or noticeably stronger: pick one, not both.
- Opposed environments cost more and feel harder; describe the resistance.
- Ley-rich sites, shrines, and sanctified ground speed recovery. Dungeon zones may make mana unstable: costs fluctuate, and botched casts misfire strangely.
### Extra Recovery Paths
- Meditation, mana-rich meals, hot springs, and shrine rest can add recovery during downtime, but there are no free full refills mid-dungeon; managing the pool between fights IS the gameplay.
### Parity and Fairness
- NPC casters follow the same cost bands and visibly tire; enemy mages running dry is a readable, exploitable state.
- Never double-charge passives: trait effects, cheat-skill passives, and always-on Blessings are already priced into the character.

### Mage Duels and Counterspells
- Countering a spell mid-cast costs roughly HALF the incoming spell's mana and requires perceiving the cast in time. A successful counter shatters the spell visibly; a failed one wastes the mana and leaves the counterer exposed.
- Dispelling an ACTIVE effect costs about its original price: cheaper if the dispeller knows the school, pricier against demon-contract magic.
### Rituals and Group Casting
- Multiple casters can split a large cost, each paying a share plus small coordination overhead. Rituals trade time and vulnerability for effects no single pool could pay: interrupting one mid-channel is the classic counter, and dangerous for everyone in the circle.
### Reading the Pool
- Mana states show: at half pool, casting form tightens; at a quarter, sweat and shortened incantations; empty is unmistakable. Reading an opponent's remaining mana is an insight/arcana check: grant it to trained casters and sharp observers, and narrate the tells so mage fights become resource duels.
### Tempting Sources
- Mana-boosting offers are everywhere: crystal catalysts, demon contracts, reagents of unlisted provenance. They work, and they carry strings. Price them like every temptation: real reward, delayed cost.

Giant Toad Extermination.name: Giant Toad Extermination
Giant Toad Extermination.mainObjective: Kill five giant toads outside the town gate and report to the guild for payment; deliver any corpses you can haul for the per-toad meat bonus.
Giant Toad Extermination.questStatement: The giant toads outside Axel's gate are breeding again. The guild pays 6,000 Eris on completion, plus a bonus of 400 Eris per toad corpse delivered to the depot: the meat is a delicacy, and hauling several hundred pounds of dead toad is entirely your problem.
