This is the quintessential beginner quest: dangerous enough to be real, humiliating enough to be funny, and the pay only looks good until you do the math on the hauling.
Giant Toad Extermination.questDesignBrief: THE beginner quest, the one every Axel adventurer remembers: exterminate the giant toads breeding in the marshes south of town. Luna posts it with a straight face. It is the tutorial made flesh, and it is more humiliating than dangerous. Player paths: hunt the toads directly (and risk the signature indignity of being swallowed whole, which is survivable but deeply unpleasant), lure them onto dry ground where they are slower, use area magic, or coordinate a party sweep. The comedy is foundational KonoSuba: the toads are weak but large enough to swallow an adventurer, and getting eaten (then cut or dissolved out, covered in slime) is the classic rookie rite of passage that happened to Megumin and Aqua both. Payoff: the toads are cleared, the player has their first bounty and their first war story, and they have learned that in Belzerg dignity is the first casualty.

completionCondition.query: The player has killed five giant toads and reported the kills to the guild.

Cabbage Harvest Season.name: Cabbage Harvest Season
Cabbage Harvest Season.mainObjective: Catch as many flying cabbages as possible during the harvest event and deliver them to the guild.
Cabbage Harvest Season.questStatement: It is cabbage season. The cabbages are airborne, aggressive, and worth good coin if caught intact. The guild pays 200 Eris per cabbage delivered intact, 50 per bruised one, and 2,000 for a swarm-leader. Experienced adventurers treat this as a payday; rookies treat it as a nightmare.
Cabbage Harvest Season.questDesignBrief: A seasonal comedy quest unique to Belzerg: the magical cabbages are ripe, which means they have taken flight and are attempting to escape, and the guild has declared open season. Luna posts the harvest as a sanctioned, chaotic brawl. Player paths: chase and catch the flying cabbages by hand (exhausting and undignified), net or trap them, use magic to ground them, or coordinate with farmers and other adventurers for a mass harvest. The comedy is the sheer absurdity of grown adventurers wrestling aggressive airborne produce while farmers watch and tally crop damage. It is a genuine agricultural event treated as a competitive sport. Payoff: the player earns a cabbage bounty proportional to their haul, the farmsteads get their harvest, and everyone involved gets to feel slightly ridiculous. A recurring seasonal fixture that captures Belzerg's cozy, silly heart.

completionCondition.query: The player has caught and delivered at least ten flying cabbages to the guild.

Wiz's Latest Acquisition.name: Wiz's Latest Acquisition
Wiz's Latest Acquisition.mainObjective: Help Wiz deal with her malfunctioning magical artifact before it causes serious damage.
Wiz's Latest Acquisition.questStatement: Wiz bought another magical artifact from a traveling merchant and it is doing something it should not be doing. She is very sorry. She needs help containing or disposing of it before Vanir finds out and lectures her about inventory management again.
Wiz's Latest Acquisition.questDesignBrief: A recurring KonoSuba scenario: Wiz buys cursed or malfunctioning items and needs help dealing with them. The artifact should be genuinely dangerous but also absurd in its malfunction. Wiz apologizes throughout. Vanir commentates if present. The reward is whatever Wiz can afford, which is not much, plus the player's choice of one non-cursed item from her shop.

completionCondition.query: The cursed artifact has been contained, destroyed, or otherwise dealt with.

Vanir's Business Proposition.name: Vanir's Business Proposition
Vanir's Business Proposition.mainObjective: Complete Vanir's business scheme and collect your agreed-upon payment.
Vanir's Business Proposition.questStatement: Vanir has a plan to increase the shop's revenue that requires someone willing to do legwork, accept terms, and trust a devil's definition of 'fair compensation.' The plan is technically legal.
Vanir's Business Proposition.questDesignBrief: Vanir's deals always deliver exactly what was promised, in the most inconvenient way possible. The scheme should be clever, technically fair, and result in the player getting paid but regretting the fine print. Vanir is theatrical and enjoys every moment. The comedy is in the gap between what the player expected and what they technically agreed to.

completionCondition.query: The player has completed the terms of Vanir's business deal and received compensation.

The Prosecutor Returns.name: The Prosecutor Returns
The Prosecutor Returns.mainObjective: Resolve the outstanding property damage claims through payment, community service, or legal argument.
The Prosecutor Returns.questStatement: Prosecutor Sena has arrived at the guild with a stack of property damage claims and a summons for the player. Someone has to pay for what happened last time, and the guild's insurance does not cover 'acts of explosion.'
The Prosecutor Returns.questDesignBrief: A comedic legal quest where the player must deal with the consequences of previous destruction. Sena is professional but exasperated. The player can pay outright (expensive), argue their case (skill-based), do community service (humiliating but free), or find someone else to blame (risky). This should feel like a recurring event that gets funnier each time.

completionCondition.query: The property damage claims have been resolved, whether through payment, negotiation, community service, or legal proceedings.

The Axis Cult Recruitment Drive.name: The Axis Cult Recruitment Drive
The Axis Cult Recruitment Drive.mainObjective: Help the Axis Cult recruit new members in Alcanretia, or find a way to complete the job without actually converting anyone.
The Axis Cult Recruitment Drive.questStatement: The Axis Cult is running a recruitment drive in Alcanretia and has offered surprisingly good pay for anyone willing to help distribute pamphlets and 'share the glory of Aqua.' The catch is that you have to actually do the recruiting, which involves cornering strangers and not taking no for an answer.
The Axis Cult Recruitment Drive.questDesignBrief: A comedy quest where the player must either commit to the absurdity of Axis Cult recruitment or find creative ways to game the system. The Cult's recruitment tactics are aggressive, off-putting, and surprisingly effective. NPCs react with disgust, avoidance, or fascinated horror. Completing the quest honestly makes the player complicit in the Cult's menace; completing it creatively is the comedy path.

completionCondition.query: The player has either recruited new Axis Cult members or found an alternative way to satisfy the Cult's recruitment quota.

Dungeon Delve: Keele's Upper Floors.name: Dungeon Delve: Keele's Upper Floors
Dungeon Delve: Keele's Upper Floors.mainObjective: Clear the upper floors of Keele's Dungeon and return with proof of completion.
Dungeon Delve: Keele's Upper Floors.questStatement: The guild is posting a standard dungeon-delve contract for Keele's Dungeon: clear the upper floors of accumulated undead, map any changes to the layout, and bring back proof of completion. Standard adventurer work, standard adventurer pay.
Dungeon Delve: Keele's Upper Floors.questDesignBrief: A straightforward dungeon crawl with combat, traps, and loot. The upper floors are manageable for mid-level adventurers. The comedy comes from the adventurer graffiti, other parties' failed attempts visible in the environment, and the general indignity of fighting shambling undead for modest pay. Introduce the dungeon as a place with deeper mysteries to draw the player back later.

completionCondition.query: The player has cleared the upper floors of Keele's Dungeon and reported back to the guild.

Yunyun's Challenge.name: Yunyun's Challenge
Yunyun's Challenge.mainObjective: Accept or decline Yunyun's duel challenge. If accepted, defeat or lose to Yunyun in a formal magic duel.
Yunyun's Challenge.questStatement: Yunyun has challenged the player to a formal duel at the town gate, complete with dramatic terms she rehearsed in advance. If the player wins, she will perform any one task. If Yunyun wins, the player must be her friend for a day. She has been waiting at the gate for three hours.
Yunyun's Challenge.questDesignBrief: A comedic character quest. Yunyun is genuinely powerful but so lonely that her stake in the duel is just having someone agree to hang out with her. Win or lose, the real outcome is a bond moment. She will use advanced magic competently and then be heartbroken if the player walks away afterward. Play her loneliness for comedy and warmth, not pathos.

completionCondition.query: The duel with Yunyun has been fought or the challenge has been resolved.

Chris's Secret Errand.name: Chris's Secret Errand
Chris's Secret Errand.mainObjective: Help Chris retrieve the item from the noble's estate without getting caught.
Chris's Secret Errand.questStatement: Chris pulls the player aside and asks for help with a 'personal errand' that involves breaking into a noble's estate to retrieve a 'family heirloom.' She is vague about the details. The heirloom is actually a dangerous holy relic, and Chris is actually the goddess Eris, but the player does not need to know that yet.
Chris's Secret Errand.questDesignBrief: A stealth/heist quest with Chris as the partner. Chris is suspiciously competent for a mid-rank thief. The quest should hint at her true identity without revealing it: she knows the estate layout too well, her skills are sharper than her guild rank suggests, and she cares about the relic for reasons she will not explain. The comedy comes from the heist going wrong in small ways and Chris improvising brilliantly.

completionCondition.query: The item has been retrieved from the noble's estate and delivered to Chris.

Dust's Terrible Plan.name: Dust's Terrible Plan
Dust's Terrible Plan.mainObjective: Help Dust execute his money-making scheme, or salvage the situation when it goes wrong.
Dust's Terrible Plan.questStatement: Dust has a plan to make money fast that involves a gambling den, a borrowed disguise, and at least two lies. He needs a partner. The plan will not work as described. Something better or worse will happen instead.
Dust's Terrible Plan.questDesignBrief: A comedy caper from Dust, the blond gambler whose schemes are always brilliant in conception and catastrophic in execution. He needs the player's help with a plan that is, as always, a terrible idea presented with total confidence: a get-rich-quick scheme, a gambling debt to dodge, or a favor that spirals. Player paths: go along with the plan and improvise when it inevitably collapses, try to talk Dust into something sensible (futile but funny), hijack the plan for the player's own benefit, or bail at the worst possible moment. His party (Taylor, Keith, Rin, Lain) may get dragged in, with Rin's exasperation and Taylor's principled objections providing the counterpoint. The comedy is the whole point: watching a confident plan meet reality. The hook nods to Dust's mysterious past, which Keith carefully never mentions. Payoff: the plan fails in an entertaining way, somebody profits by accident, and the player gains Dust's party as recurring contacts.

completionCondition.query: Dust's scheme has concluded, whether successfully, in disaster, or somewhere in between.

The Crimson Demon Introduction Contest.name: The Crimson Demon Introduction Contest
The Crimson Demon Introduction Contest.mainObjective: Compete in or judge the Crimson Demon Self-Introduction Contest.
The Crimson Demon Introduction Contest.questStatement: The Crimson Demon Village is holding its annual Self-Introduction Contest, where the most dramatic, spectacular, and elaborate self-introduction wins a prize. Arue is documenting the event for her novel. An outsider entering would be unprecedented and either deeply offensive or deeply entertaining.
The Crimson Demon Introduction Contest.questDesignBrief: A pure comedy quest. Every Crimson Demon delivers an absurdly dramatic self-introduction with explosions, light effects, and prepared poses. The player can compete (requiring them to create their own dramatic introduction), judge (requiring them to rate performances), or sabotage (which the Crimson Demons might actually respect). Yunyun enters and nobody watches. Megumin enters and the explosion destroys the stage.

completionCondition.query: The self-introduction contest has been held and a winner determined.

Hot Spring Guardian.name: Hot Spring Guardian
Hot Spring Guardian.mainObjective: Remove the creature from the Alcanretia hot springs.
Hot Spring Guardian.questStatement: The hot springs of Alcanretia are being disturbed by an underwater creature that has taken up residence in the main spring. Bathing has become impossible. The Axis Cult considers this a crisis of faith. Zesta is offering payment and lifetime membership (whether you want it or not) to anyone who removes the creature.
Hot Spring Guardian.questDesignBrief: A combat quest set in a hot spring, with all the comedic potential that implies. The creature is genuinely dangerous but the setting makes fighting it awkward and funny. The Axis Cult 'helps' by praying loudly, which does nothing. Victory is rewarded with coin, a forced induction ceremony, and the lifelong attention of the Axis Cult.

completionCondition.query: The creature has been removed from the hot springs and bathing has resumed.

Dark Presence at the Ruins.name: Dark Presence at the Ruins
Dark Presence at the Ruins.mainObjective: Investigate the dark presence at the beginner ruins and report back.
Dark Presence at the Ruins.questStatement: Arc quest. Reports of an unnatural cold and dark magical pressure emanating from the beginner ruins outside Axel. Several parties have returned early, shaken. The guild is offering a scouting bounty to investigate.
Dark Presence at the Ruins.questDesignBrief: An investigation quest from Luna into a dark presence stirring in the ruins near Axel, where something stronger than the usual weak undead has taken up residence. It starts as a routine clearance and escalates. Player paths: investigate cautiously and identify the threat before engaging, go in swinging, consult Wiz or Vanir (both know undead intimately), or use purification magic. The comedy comes from the contrast between Axel's beginner reputation and the genuine menace lurking in its backyard, and from any attempt to get straight answers out of the town's two ex-general shopkeepers. The hook: the presence may be a scout or remnant of the Demon King's forces testing the region's defenses, or an artifact from Wiz's shop that someone dumped here. Payoff: the threat is neutralized, the ruins are safe for rookie practice again, and the player may surface a clue pointing to a larger scheme.

completionCondition.query: The player has investigated the ruins and reported the dark presence to the guild.

The Dullahan's Ultimatum.name: The Dullahan's Ultimatum
The Dullahan's Ultimatum.mainObjective: Confront Beldia and protect Axel from his death curse.
The Dullahan's Ultimatum.questStatement: Arc quest. The Dullahan general Beldia has entered Axel and issued an ultimatum: surrender the mage who has been using his castle for explosion practice, or he will curse the entire town. The guild is mobilizing every available adventurer.
The Dullahan's Ultimatum.questDesignBrief: A signature early-canon quest: Beldia the Dullahan, a headless Demon King's general carrying his own head, arrives to deliver an ultimatum to Axel and threaten the town. This is the region's first taste of a real general, and the guild rallies its adventurers for a coordinated defense. Player paths: help organize the town's defense, exploit Beldia's known weaknesses (he is undead, so purification and holy magic devastate him, and his cursed sword's paralysis can be countered), volunteer for the front line, or find a clever angle (Beldia has a weakness for teasing and provocation). The comedy is peak KonoSuba: a genuinely menacing general undone by Aqua's overwhelming purification and the town's refusal to take the threat with appropriate dignity. Beneath it, Beldia is a real threat that establishes the stakes of the war. Payoff: Beldia is defeated (canonically by purification magic), Axel proves it is far more dangerous to the Demon King's forces than its beginner reputation suggests, and the player earns their first general-slaying credential.

completionCondition.query: Beldia has been confronted and either defeated or driven away from Axel.

The Walking Fortress.name: The Walking Fortress
The Walking Fortress.mainObjective: Help the guild organize the defense of Axel against the approaching Destroyer.
The Walking Fortress.questStatement: Arc quest. A massive autonomous magical construct, the Destroyer, has been sighted marching toward Axel. It is a walking fortress from a previous era that periodically activates and destroys whatever is in its path. The guild is mobilizing every adventurer for an emergency defense.
The Walking Fortress.questDesignBrief: Setup for the Destroyer fight. The scale of the threat should be genuinely intimidating. The guild mobilizes, Axel's adventurers argue about the plan, and the preparations are chaotic, underfunded, and undercut by the fact that most of Axel's adventurers are not equipped for this. The comedy is in the gap between the threat and the response.

completionCondition.query: The defense preparations against the Destroyer have been organized and the adventurers are ready.

Stop the Destroyer.name: Stop the Destroyer
Stop the Destroyer.mainObjective: Breach the Destroyer, locate its power core, and disable the fortress.
Stop the Destroyer.questStatement: Arc quest. The Destroyer is here. A mobile fortress of ancient magical engineering, marching on Axel with unstoppable momentum. The adventurers must find a way inside, locate its power core, and disable it before it reaches the town.
Stop the Destroyer.questDesignBrief: A high-stakes canon quest: the Destroyer, a colossal Demon King mobile fortress golem, is grinding its way toward Axel, and its arrival would flatten the town. The whole region mobilizes. This is a race against time and a genuine crisis dressed in KonoSuba comedy. Player paths: help evacuate and organize (the responsible route), find and exploit the Destroyer's core weakness, contribute to the massive coordinated attack needed to stop it, or enable the signature solution, a single overwhelming blast of explosion magic aimed at its core, which is the most Megumin possible answer and the canonical one. The comedy: a world-ending threat solved by pointing the village explosion addict at it and letting her do the one thing she lives for. The tension is real; the resolution is triumphant and absurd. Payoff: the Destroyer falls, Axel is saved again, Megumin gets her moment of glory (and immediately collapses), and the region's reputation as a general-killer grows.

completionCondition.query: The Destroyer's power core has been disabled or removed and the fortress has stopped.

The Trial of the Century.name: The Trial of the Century
The Trial of the Century.mainObjective: Survive the legal tribunal and avoid the maximum penalty for property damage.
The Trial of the Century.questStatement: Arc quest. In the aftermath of stopping the Destroyer, the player is arrested for the massive property damage caused during the battle. Prosecutor Sena is handling the case. The player must survive a formal tribunal where their heroism is technically irrelevant to the property damage charges.
The Trial of the Century.questDesignBrief: A legal comedy quest. The player saved the town but destroyed expensive property doing it. Sena is professional and thorough. The defense must argue that the destruction was necessary. The tribunal is formal, the charges are real, and the comedy is in the gap between saving everyone and being prosecuted for how you did it. Allies can testify. Darkness can offer to take the punishment, which is suspicious.

completionCondition.query: The tribunal has delivered its verdict on the property damage charges.

Troubled Waters.name: Troubled Waters
Troubled Waters.mainObjective: Investigate the deteriorating water quality of Alcanretia's hot springs.
Troubled Waters.questStatement: Arc quest. The hot springs of Alcanretia taste wrong. The water's healing properties are fading. The Axis Cult considers this a spiritual emergency. Zesta is offering a bounty for anyone who can identify the cause.
Troubled Waters.questDesignBrief: An Alcanretia quest that starts small and reveals a real threat. Something is wrong with the holy city's blessed hot springs, and high priest Zesta, devoted but eccentric, sends the player to investigate before the Axis Cult panics. Player paths: investigate the source (contamination, a lurking monster, or sabotage), consult the hot spring attendant Mio for local knowledge, use purification or water magic if the player has it, or rally the Cult's own considerable magic. The comedy runs on the Axis Cult treating a plumbing problem as an apocalyptic theological crisis, and on the recruiters who try to sign up the player mid-investigation. Beneath the comedy is a genuine hook: the springs' blessed waters are a real defense against the Demon King's undead, so tampering may be an enemy probe. Payoff: the springs are restored, the Cult is (loudly) grateful, and the player may uncover the first thread of a Demon King's Army scheme against Alcanretia.

completionCondition.query: The cause of the water contamination has been identified.

The Slime General.name: The Slime General
The Slime General.mainObjective: Defeat Hans the deadly poison slime and save Alcanretia's hot springs.
The Slime General.questStatement: Arc quest. The traveling merchant has revealed himself as Hans, a Demon King's general and deadly poison slime. He has been contaminating the springs to destroy the Axis Cult's power base. He is now in his true form: enormous, toxic, and nearly invulnerable to physical attacks. The springs themselves are the battlefield.
The Slime General.questDesignBrief: An Alcanretia arc climax: Hans, a Demon King's general who is a deadly poison slime wearing the disguise of a charming merchant, has come to poison the holy city's blessed springs, a genuine strategic strike against the Cult's anti-undead purification power. Zesta rallies the response. Player paths: see through Hans's human disguise (perception, or catching an inconsistency in his charm), exploit the fact that a slime is vulnerable to the very purification magic the Cult specializes in, protect the springs directly, or coordinate the Axis Cult's considerable water and purification magic against him. The comedy: a sinister infiltration plot running headfirst into the one city whose entire population can purify slimes on reflex, plus the Cult treating the defense as a holy crusade. Beneath it, Hans is a real, lethal threat. Payoff: Hans is exposed and destroyed, the springs and their strategic value are saved, and the Axis Cult is (deafeningly) vindicated in its own importance.

completionCondition.query: Hans has been defeated and the hot springs have been purified.

The General's Grudge.name: The General's Grudge
The General's Grudge.mainObjective: Investigate the Demon King general's presence near the Crimson Demon Village.
The General's Grudge.questStatement: Arc quest. A Demon King's general has been spotted near the Crimson Demon Village. The village elders are concerned but also excited because having a Demon King's general attack your village is extremely dramatic and they have been practicing their battle introductions.
The General's Grudge.questDesignBrief: The setup quest for the Sylvia arc, run by the enthusiastic Yuiyui. A Demon King's general has been spotted near the Crimson Demon Village, and the villagers are simultaneously threatened and thrilled, because being attacked by a general is extremely dramatic and they have been practicing their battle introductions for exactly this. Player paths: investigate the general's identity and purpose through scouting, interrogation of lesser enemies, or consultation with the village elders, who are more excited than useful. The investigation reveals the chimera general Sylvia holds a grudge against the Crimson Demons for their constant, ecosystem-disrupting use of explosion magic. The comedy: the village's considered response to an incoming threat is to practice MORE explosions, which is both the cause of the grudge and, eventually, the solution. Payoff: the player uncovers Sylvia's identity, motive, and the danger she poses, setting up the arc's escalation and the climactic Battle for the Village.

completionCondition.query: The general's identity and purpose have been determined.

The Battle for the Village.name: The Battle for the Village
The Battle for the Village.mainObjective: Unite the Crimson Demons and defeat Sylvia before she destroys the village.
The Battle for the Village.questStatement: Arc quest. Sylvia the chimera general is attacking the Crimson Demon Village in force. She absorbs everything she touches and grows stronger. The entire village must coordinate their magic. Every Crimson Demon gets to deliver their battle introduction, which takes a while.
The Battle for the Village.questDesignBrief: The climax of the Sylvia arc. A village-wide battle where every named Crimson Demon gets a moment. Sylvia absorbs things to grow stronger, which means the Crimson Demons need to overwhelm her before she becomes unkillable. The solution involves coordinated explosion magic from the entire village, which is both the most Crimson Demon thing possible and genuinely spectacular. Everyone delivers their full dramatic introduction before fighting. This takes longer than the actual combat.

completionCondition.query: Sylvia has been defeated and the Crimson Demon Village has been saved.

High Stakes in Elroad.name: High Stakes in Elroad
High Stakes in Elroad.mainObjective: Enter the high-roller tournament and identify who is cheating the Elroad casino.
High Stakes in Elroad.questStatement: The Grand Casino's high-roller tournament is accepting foreign entrants. The buy-in is steep, the odds are rigged, and the prize pool could pay off a year of property damage. Someone is cheating better than the house, and Vanessa wants the player to find out who without causing an international incident.
High Stakes in Elroad.questDesignBrief: A social/investigation quest in a casino setting. The player can gamble, investigate, or both. Kazuma's Steal and luck skills are relevant. The cheater should be someone using magic in a country that prohibits magical gambling interference. Comedy comes from the casino's own rigged games being disrupted by better cheating.

completionCondition.query: The cheater in the casino tournament has been identified and dealt with.

Diplomatic Incident.name: Diplomatic Incident
Diplomatic Incident.mainObjective: Negotiate the release of the arrested Belzerg adventurer from Elroad custody.
Diplomatic Incident.questStatement: A Belzerg adventurer has been arrested in Elroad for property damage at a casino. Takeshi Nagumo needs someone to negotiate their release before it becomes a formal international complaint. The adventurer claims they were provoked. The casino claims otherwise. Both are technically correct.
Diplomatic Incident.questDesignBrief: A diplomacy quest set in Elroad's glittering, mercenary casino nation. A Belzerg adventurer has been arrested for property damage, and both they and the casino are technically telling the truth, which is the entire problem. Takeshi Nagumo is helpful, impeccably mannered, and visibly aging from the stress of representing the kingdom that produced Kazuma's party. Player paths: negotiate the adventurer's release through diplomacy, pay the damages outright (expensive), hunt for a legal loophole in Elroad's byzantine gambling law, gather evidence the casino provoked the incident, or cause a larger distraction that makes the original charge irrelevant. The arrested adventurer is belligerent, ungrateful, and convinced they did nothing wrong. Comedy comes from the gap between Takeshi's weary professionalism and the adventurer's total lack of it. Payoff: the adventurer walks free, Takeshi gets a rare moment of relief, and the player earns a favor from the embassy. A clean resolution avoids a formal international complaint; a messy one creates a new incident for later.

completionCondition.query: The arrested adventurer has been released from Elroad custody.

The Capital's Request.name: The Capital's Request
The Capital's Request.mainObjective: Scout the northern road and report on Demon King's Army activity.
The Capital's Request.questStatement: The Royal Capital guild has received intelligence about Demon King's forces probing the northern defenses. They need a competent party to scout the northern road and report back. The pay is excellent. The danger is real. This is not Axel.
The Capital's Request.questDesignBrief: A step up in stakes: chief receptionist Erika summons the player to the Royal Capital for a sensitive job the frontier branches cannot handle. This is where personal adventuring starts entangling with matters of state. Player paths: the request might involve noble politics, a suspected infiltrator, or a high-tier threat, and the player can approach through investigation, combat, diplomacy, or leveraging capital contacts. Erika is immaculate, exacting, and evaluates the player as sharply as any threat. The comedy is quieter here, drawn from a rough frontier adventurer navigating the capital's polished condescension. The hook connects to the Heartland's real tensions: noble intrigue, corruption, and the Demon King's infiltrators who understand a blow to the capital is worth a dozen frontier skirmishes. Payoff: the player earns standing in the capital, access to higher-tier work, and a thread into the kingdom's larger struggle.

completionCondition.query: The player has scouted the northern road and reported their findings to the Royal Capital guild.

The Nightless City Performer.name: The Nightless City Performer
The Nightless City Performer.mainObjective: Investigate the enchanting performer in Nightless City and determine if magic is involved.
The Nightless City Performer.questStatement: A performer in Nightless City has been enchanting audiences, literally. The guild suspects magical influence in the performances and needs someone to investigate without shutting down the city's biggest attraction. The performer might be a succubus, a mage, or just genuinely talented. The guild needs to know which.
The Nightless City Performer.questDesignBrief: A change-of-pace quest in the perpetually-lit entertainment hub of Nightless City. Luna posts a job that turns out to involve the city's performance scene: a missing performer, a sabotaged show, or a star who needs protection, depending on how it develops. Player paths: investigate through barkeep Jiro's rumor network, go undercover in the entertainment district, use Performance skill to work the scene from the inside, or muscle through the city's shadier elements. The comedy runs on the city's relentless, exhausting cheer and on any player forced to actually perform. Jiro is the key contact, trading information for courtesy and coin. Beneath the glitter is the city's usual undercurrent of debt and vice. Payoff: the show goes on, the player earns a foothold in Nightless City's information economy, and Jiro remembers a favor for future quests.

completionCondition.query: The nature of the performer's enchanting abilities has been determined.

Goblin Subjugation.name: Goblin Subjugation
Goblin Subjugation.mainObjective: Clear the goblin threat from the Neighbourhood Ruins and eliminate or capture their leader.
Goblin Subjugation.questStatement: The guild has received reports of organized goblin raids near the Neighbourhood Ruins. The raids are suspiciously well-coordinated for goblins, suggesting a leader with actual tactics. The guild is offering a bounty per goblin and a bonus for the leader.
Goblin Subjugation.questDesignBrief: A classic early guild quest from Luna: clear the goblin cave whose warren, led by the crowned brute Gruk, has grown bold enough to raid the roads. It looks like a simple extermination and punishes anyone who treats it that way, because Gruk coordinates ambushes with real cunning. Player paths: assault the cave head-on (dangerous solo, manageable as a party), scout and pick off the goblins in stages, lure them into the open away from their terrain advantage, or negotiate/trick Gruk if the player is creative. The comedy is in the rookie assumption that goblins are trivial, undercut hard by the warren's organized defense. The treasury district holds the loot the guild bounty is really after. Payoff: the cave is cleared, the roads are safe, the player claims the hoard, and they learn the KonoSuba lesson that a weak enemy with a plan is more dangerous than a strong enemy without one.

completionCondition.query: The goblin raids have been stopped and the goblin leader has been dealt with.

Winter Sprite Harvest.name: Winter Sprite Harvest
Winter Sprite Harvest.mainObjective: Harvest at least ten Snow Sprite cores from the Snowfield Forest without angering the Winter Shogun.
Winter Sprite Harvest.questStatement: Snow Sprite cores are in demand and the guild is offering premium bounties for harvested cores from the Snowfield Forest. The sprites are fast, fragile, and flee on contact. The Winter Shogun patrols the deeper forest. Do not anger the Winter Shogun.
Winter Sprite Harvest.questDesignBrief: A collection quest with a stealth element. Snow Sprites are fast and flee. The Winter Shogun is the real threat: a massively overpowered boss that the player should NOT fight. Success means catching sprites quietly and bowing respectfully if the Shogun appears. Comedy comes from the gap between the simple objective and the terrifying environment.

completionCondition.query: The player has collected Snow Sprite cores and returned safely from the Snowfield Forest.

Frontier Patrol.name: Frontier Patrol
Frontier Patrol.mainObjective: Complete a patrol circuit along the northern road and report any Demon King's Army activity.
Frontier Patrol.questStatement: The Frontier Fort needs adventurers to run a patrol circuit along the northern road. Demon King's scouts have been spotted and the garrison is too thin to cover every approach. The pay is hazard-rated. The danger is real.
Frontier Patrol.questDesignBrief: A combat/scouting quest at the frontier. This is the serious end of the KonoSuba spectrum: genuine danger, real soldiers, and the Demon King's forces are not funny. The comedy comes from the player's reaction to an environment where the stakes are real and the monsters do not politely wait for you to pose.

completionCondition.query: The patrol has been completed and the findings reported to Reiko Amagai.

Labyrinth Training Exercise.name: Labyrinth Training Exercise
Labyrinth Training Exercise.mainObjective: Participate in the Crimson Demon Village's training exercise in the Great Tree Labyrinth.
Labyrinth Training Exercise.questStatement: The Crimson Demon Village is conducting annual training exercises in the Great Tree Labyrinth. Outside participants are welcome because it makes the exercise more interesting. The Crimson Demons will be performing full dramatic introductions before each combat encounter, which adds significant time to the schedule.
Labyrinth Training Exercise.questDesignBrief: A Crimson Demon quest run by the enthusiastic Yuiyui, framed as a training exercise in the Great Tree Labyrinth that is more dangerous than advertised. The labyrinth's living root passages shift, plant-monsters lurk, and the deeper reaches hold older things. Player paths: navigate the maze by wits, brute force through the plant-monsters, use a Crimson Demon guide's knowledge, or find one of the labyrinth's hidden shortcuts. The comedy is pure Crimson Demon: Yuiyui treats a genuinely lethal maze as a fun team-building outing and insists on dramatic self-introductions at every junction, even to the plants. The real lesson is that the labyrinth predates the clan and deserves respect the villagers rarely show anything. Payoff: the player emerges with improved standing among the Crimson Demons, useful knowledge of the labyrinth for later quests, and possibly a glimpse of whatever older secret sleeps at its heart.

completionCondition.query: The training exercise in the Great Tree Labyrinth has been completed.

The Greenhollow Fence Dispute.name: The Greenhollow Fence Dispute
The Greenhollow Fence Dispute.mainObjective: Settle the Greenhollow fence dispute to both families' satisfaction.
The Greenhollow Fence Dispute.questStatement: Village quest. Two Greenhollow farmers have been feuding over a fence line for three generations and it has finally escalated to sabotage. The village elder wants it settled before someone gets hurt over a hedge. Neither party will accept a ruling from anyone local.
The Greenhollow Fence Dispute.questDesignBrief: A pure social quest with no combat solution. Player paths: arbitrate formally, dig into the actual property records, find the older grievance underneath the fence, trick both parties into agreement, or simply move the fence at night and let them argue about that. The comedy is the sheer disproportion between the stakes and the passion. Both farmers are sympathetic and completely unreasonable. Payoff: the village owes the player a favor, and Greenhollow becomes a friendly base with cheap lodging.

completionCondition.query: The fence dispute has been resolved and both families have accepted the outcome.

Silt and Silence.name: Silt and Silence
Silt and Silence.mainObjective: Discover what has silenced the Stiltwater channel and deal with it.
Silt and Silence.questStatement: Riverlands quest. Stiltwater's ferrymen report that one of the delta's main channels has gone quiet: no fish, no birds, and two boats that went in have not come back. The town needs the channel cleared or at minimum explained before the season's trade is ruined.
Silt and Silence.questDesignBrief: An investigation that becomes a monster hunt in difficult terrain. Player paths: hire a ferryman guide, question the fishers about what changed, approach by boat or wade the shallows, or bait the thing out. Water combat is awkward and should feel it. The culprit is an aquatic ambush predator that has moved in from deeper water. Payoff: the channel reopens, the ferrymen owe the player, and Stiltwater becomes a source of rare reagents.

completionCondition.query: The cause of the silent channel has been found and resolved.

Cargo of Uncertain Provenance.name: Cargo of Uncertain Provenance
Cargo of Uncertain Provenance.mainObjective: Determine what is actually in the Saltspire cargo and who sent it.
Cargo of Uncertain Provenance.questStatement: Coastal quest. A crate at Saltspire Harbor has cleared customs with paperwork that does not match its contents, and the customs house wants it looked into by someone who does not work for them. The shipping agent is cooperative in the way that suggests preparation.
Cargo of Uncertain Provenance.questDesignBrief: An investigation with a smuggling frame. Player paths: inspect the crate directly, trace the paperwork, lean on the shipping agent, follow the intended recipient, or simply buy the crate. The comedy is bureaucratic: everyone involved is technically compliant. Escalate toward either a mundane smuggling ring or something the Demon King's forces sent in by sea, depending on how the player pushes. Payoff: standing with the customs house and a foothold in coastal trade.

completionCondition.query: The true contents and origin of the suspicious cargo have been established.

The Quiet Seam.name: The Quiet Seam
The Quiet Seam.mainObjective: Explore the reopened Grausten seam and determine whether it can be safely worked.
The Quiet Seam.questStatement: Foothills quest. Grausten's miners have opened a seam that runs toward one of the walled-off cave sections, and the stonecutters' guild is split between the profit and the reason those walls went up. They want an outside party to go in first.
The Quiet Seam.questDesignBrief: A dungeon delve with a real moral question attached. Player paths: go in and clear it, investigate why the walls went up, side with the cautious faction, or side with the profitable one. The miners' reticence is grief, not superstition. What is down there should be genuinely dangerous and genuinely explicable. Payoff: access to enchanting-grade mineral at favorable rates, which matters a great deal to an Enchanter or Blacksmith player.

completionCondition.query: The reopened seam has been explored and its safety determined.

A Matter of Precedence.name: A Matter of Precedence
A Matter of Precedence.mainObjective: Get the Windmere dinner through to its end without an open breach between the houses.
A Matter of Precedence.questStatement: Western Reach quest. Windmere Hold is hosting a dinner at which three feuding houses will sit at the same table for the first time in a decade, and the lord needs someone outside the local hierarchy to keep it from becoming an incident. The seating chart is a weapon.
A Matter of Precedence.questDesignBrief: A social set piece with no combat solution and real failure states. Player paths: study the precedence rules in advance, work the retainers for intelligence, defuse each flashpoint as it arises, deliberately provoke one house to unite the others, or fail entertainingly. Comedy from a rough adventurer navigating lethal politeness. Payoff: noble patronage, access to the Reach's political layer, and an invitation the player can spend later.

completionCondition.query: The Windmere dinner has concluded and the outcome between the houses is settled.

Contact at the Ridge.name: Contact at the Ridge
Contact at the Ridge.mainObjective: Intercept the Demon King's scouts working the Ashford ridgeline.
Contact at the Ridge.questStatement: Marches quest. Ashford Garrison's patrols have found fresh evidence of Demon King's scouts working the eastern ridgeline on a schedule, which means the enemy is timing the garrison's responses. The commander wants the scouts taken or turned before that intelligence is delivered.
Contact at the Ridge.questDesignBrief: The player's first taste of real war rather than monster bounties. Player paths: ambush the scouts, track them to their reporting point, feed them false information, or take one alive for interrogation. The enemy here is disciplined and will retreat rather than die pointlessly, which is unlike anything in the south. Tone shifts noticeably: less comedy, more weight. Payoff: Ashford's respect, and hard information about the enemy's eastern intentions.

completionCondition.query: The enemy scouts have been intercepted, killed, captured, or driven off.

What Ine Found.name: What Ine Found
What Ine Found.mainObjective: Reach the unrecorded structure in the deep Wildwood and determine what it is.
What Ine Found.questStatement: Wildwood quest. The trapper Ine has found an overgrown structure deep in the Great Wildwood that appears on no record, and she has told nobody because she suspects the camp would forbid her from returning. She will trade the location to someone she believes will come back out.
What Ine Found.questDesignBrief: An exploration quest gated behind earning an NPC's trust rather than a level check. Player paths: trade Ine something she genuinely needs, prove competence in the forest first, convince Ryuu to authorize it, or simply go without her and get lost. The Wildwood itself is the antagonist: shifting paths, plant monsters, and disorientation. The structure predates any record and should raise more questions than it answers. Payoff: a genuine discovery, Ine's loyalty, and a thread the world can pull on later.

completionCondition.query: The structure in the deep Wildwood has been reached and its nature determined.

The Gaps in the Logbook.name: The Gaps in the Logbook
The Gaps in the Logbook.mainObjective: Discover what has been claiming hunters in the same stretch of the Frozen Reaches.
The Gaps in the Logbook.questStatement: Frozen Reaches quest. Hoarfrost Station's logbook records every hunter's name and intended route, and the blank spaces are the people who did not return. Three entries this season stop at the same stretch of waste. Tetsu wants to know why, and he is too experienced to go alone.
The Gaps in the Logbook.questDesignBrief: A survival-horror-tinged investigation where the cold is a constant mechanical pressure alongside whatever is out there. Player paths: read the logbook carefully and deduce the pattern, hire Tetsu as a guide, seek out the hermit Yuuga's knowledge, or go in prepared and brute-force it. The correct answer may be a greater ice spirit, in which case the resolution is a respectful withdrawal rather than a kill, and the quest should honor that as a full success. Payoff: Tetsu's respect and safe passage through the deep waste.

completionCondition.query: The cause of the disappearances in the Frozen Reaches has been identified and resolved.

Unstable Ground.name: Unstable Ground
Unstable Ground.mainObjective: Escort Ayano to her three measurement sites in the Cracked Vale and get her out alive.
Unstable Ground.questStatement: Highlands quest. The Crimson Demon researcher Ayano has documented magical distortion patterns in the Cracked Vale that nobody else knows exist, and she needs an escort to take measurements at three sites deeper in, through terrain Demon King's forces patrol.
Unstable Ground.questDesignBrief: An escort quest where the terrain actively punishes casters: mana costs fluctuate, spells distort, and a botched cast misfires strangely. Player paths: fight through the patrols, avoid them entirely using Sozen's briefing, split the sites across multiple trips, or cut the expedition short and accept partial data. Ayano's survival instincts are inadequate and she will press deeper if not managed. Payoff: her distortion data, which is a real mechanical advantage for any caster operating in the north.

completionCondition.query: The measurements have been taken and Ayano has returned from the Cracked Vale.

The Records Beneath.name: The Records Beneath
The Records Beneath.mainObjective: Reach the records inside the occupied ruin in the Demon King's Domain and recover them.
The Records Beneath.questStatement: Endgame quest. The occupied ruins in the Demon King's Domain were a human town before the conquest, and its records are still inside, buried under a garrison commanded by Vosk. Sozen believes those records explain how the enemy's territory keeps growing without battles being fought.
The Records Beneath.questDesignBrief: The endgame infiltration. Everything here is lethal: ambient corruption is attritional, supplies sour, rest fails to restore, and the garrison is commanded rather than wandering, meaning it coordinates and pursues. Player paths: full assault on Vosk, infiltration around him, striking Neth first to halt the blight, or a fast smash-and-withdraw. Vosk has no comedic flaw and will not be beaten by cleverness alone at this tier. The comedy is entirely absent here by design. Payoff: the records reveal Neth's role in the corruption's spread, opening the campaign's final strategic objective.

completionCondition.query: The pre-occupation records have been recovered from the Demon King's Domain.

The Golden Survey.name: The Golden Survey
The Golden Survey.mainObjective: Complete the guild's seasonal survey of the Gilded Mere: sample the shallows, log the bloom, and file the report.
The Golden Survey.questStatement: The guild's seasonal survey of the Gilded Mere is posted again: wade the golden shallows, take water samples, log the bloom's spread, and file the report at Millbridge. The pay is modest, the pond is beautiful, and generations of adventurers have taken this quest absolutely certain they will be the ones to find the treasure.
The Golden Survey.questDesignBrief: The classic Gilded Mere experience, and secretly a conservation contract: the survey's real function is keeping industrial dredgers off the pond, which two people in the world know. Player paths: do the survey honestly (pleasant, funny, oddly moving as the pond works its charm), obsess over the gold like everyone before them (Bett sells them a shovel with a clear conscience), or actually investigate the economics, which is the hidden path: sharp players can notice the sample trade, connect Bett's courier, and be quietly offered the truth in exchange for keeping it. Torakichi is a walking tutorial in the pond's real wealth. Payoff: pay, a Certificate of Honest Effort, and, for the perceptive, membership in the kingdom's gentlest conspiracy.

completionCondition.query: The player has completed the survey and filed the report, whether or not they learned the Mere's secret.

The Second Swarm.name: The Second Swarm
The Second Swarm.mainObjective: Help Threshing Green survive a merged double swarm of flying cabbages.
The Second Swarm.questStatement: The watchtower bell is ringing the continuous peal: two cabbage swarms have merged over the northern fields, the event the whole south speaks of like a hundred-year storm. Threshing Green needs every able hand: spotters, netters, harvesters, and someone to keep the church roof from a second historic dent.
The Second Swarm.questDesignBrief: The farmlands' signature disaster at full comic scale. Kanta calls targets from the tower with heroic precision; Sayo runs the ground defense like a veteran commander; the guild bounty pays 200 Eris per intact cabbage (50 bruised) and 2,000 per swarm-leader, which are the size of ponies. Player paths: aerial interception (magic, arrows, improvised ballistae), net-line coordination with the villagers, protecting the vulnerable points (the church roof, the seed barn, Bett's honor-system stall), or the prestige play: taking a swarm-leader intact for the harvest festival. Physical comedy is mandatory: cabbage impacts are cannonball-grade and dignity is the first casualty. Payoff: bounty, festival hero status, and cabbage-based cuisine for a season.

completionCondition.query: The merged swarm has been harvested, dispersed, or survived, and Threshing Green is out of danger.

Keep the Light Fed.name: Keep the Light Fed
Keep the Light Fed.mainObjective: Carry the season's supplies up the Lightkeeper's Stair and negotiate passage with the gull sentries.
Keep the Light Fed.questStatement: Storm season is coming and the Sunward Light needs its supply run: food, lamp-room stores, and the keeper's winter kit, one hundred and ninety steps up a chalk cliff patrolled by a gull colony that levies tolls on all cargo. The keeper pays fair rates and offers one warning: the birds can tell what is in the packages.
Keep the Light Fed.questDesignBrief: A deceptively simple porter job that is actually a diplomacy comedy. The gulls are organized, intelligent, and hold an ancient grievance about custody of something in the lamp room; their tolls are negotiable by the observant (sealed rations pass free, open food is taxed, shiny objects buy escort service). Player paths: brute-force the stairs under aerial harassment, negotiate with the colony (Nagi translates, deadpan), or discover the deeper game: befriending the sentry-captain gull earns the colony's mark, which is worth more on this coast than a guild rank. In the lamp room, players who listen get the humming, the duet, and a glimpse of the lighthouse's real tenant. Payoff: pay, the keeper's friendship, and possibly the gulls' protection along the entire Sunward Coast.

completionCondition.query: The supplies have reached the lamp room before the storms, by whatever arrangement with the gulls.

Old Number Nine.name: Old Number Nine
Old Number Nine.mainObjective: Stand watch at the Number Nine seal during the deep survey and report anything the mountain says.
Old Number Nine.questStatement: Quarry work, posted quietly and paying triple: the foreman wants a reliable party to stand watch at a sealed gallery overnight while the crews run a resonance survey of the deep seams. The posting does not say why the gallery is sealed. The foreman will not either. The triple pay is doing that work instead.
Old Number Nine.questDesignBrief: The foothills' horror-adjacent quest, played for dread and restraint rather than combat. The survey's thumping wakes something's attention behind the Nine seal: lights through hairline cracks, the sound of the corridor being walked, and at the night's turn, a fair-trade offering left at the seal from the other side. Player paths: hold the watch calmly (Gonzo's respect, the full triple pay, and his almost-invisible nod of shared knowledge), panic and break the seal protocol (the lights go out, the mountain goes quiet for a season, and Gonzo's disappointment is worse than any monster), or investigate the exchange economy: perceptive players can identify the offerings as Mossgate-style and connect the two sites' alignment. Payoff: pay, the quarries' trust, and one of the world's deep mysteries touched but correctly left unopened.

completionCondition.query: The night watch at the Number Nine seal has been completed and reported to the foreman.

Offerings at the Wall.name: Offerings at the Wall
Offerings at the Wall.mainObjective: Escort the herbalist's seasonal deep-harvest and observe the courtesies of the old forest.
Offerings at the Wall.questStatement: The herbalist who works the northern deeps is hiring an escort for her seasonal harvest along the Mossgate Wall: three days, good pay, and one non-negotiable condition, posted in her own hand: guests will observe the courtesies. What the courtesies are, she will teach on the road. Whether the party can manage them is, historically, the actual difficulty of this contract.
Offerings at the Wall.questDesignBrief: A wilderness escort quest where the real challenge is manners. The forest's dangers (one-hit bears, the deep paths, weather) are all navigable through Yomogi's etiquette: greetings spoken, offerings left, the arch never passed through, and above all no measuring, mapping, or taking without leaving. Player paths: follow the courtesies faithfully (the forest cooperates eerily; the harvest is spectacular; on the last evening a woman in bark-brown accepts tea at the fire and the player has met something no scholar has), cut corners (the forest's cooperation withdraws by degrees, escalating from lost paths to a one-hit bear encounter that the courtesies would have routed around), or press for answers about the tea guest (Yomogi goes conveniently deaf; persistence costs her trust). Payoff: pay, rare reagents, and standing with the oldest power in the Wildwood.

completionCondition.query: The three-day harvest along the Mossgate Wall has been completed and the party has returned with the herbalist.

The Boundary Stone.name: The Boundary Stone
The Boundary Stone.mainObjective: Convey a sealed crate from Harrowmoor Keep to Windmere Hold under absolute discretion.
The Boundary Stone.questStatement: Lord Harrowmoor requires a party of no particular allegiance to convey a sealed crate to Windmere Hold, deliver it to the lady's steward without ceremony, and return with whatever reply is given. The pay is generous. The instructions are exact. The contents are not the courier's business, and the lord's expression while saying so suggests the contents are very much somebody's business.
The Boundary Stone.questDesignBrief: A Reach-politics comedy of feuding houses who are secretly allies. The crate contains the boundary stone, the feud's eleven-generation casus belli, being returned: Aldric has decided, after a health scare he mentions to nobody, not to leave the reconciliation to his will. Player paths: straightforward delivery (Windmere's lady receives the stone in private, is silent a long moment, and sends back a reply crate containing her house's answering relic and a one-line note that reopens the feud on new, unmistakably warmer terms), snooping (discovering the truth of the beacon-code letters; discretion earns deep trust, gossip poisons the arrangement and both houses' regard), or interference by third parties: an Elroad-funded agent would pay handsomely to see the feud turn real, since the two houses' spite-patrols are the border's true defense. Payoff: pay, the gratitude of the Reach's two great houses, and a front seat at the most tsundere alliance in Belzerg.

completionCondition.query: The sealed crate has been delivered to Windmere Hold and the reply returned to Lord Harrowmoor.

A Discreet Commission.name: A Discreet Commission
A Discreet Commission.mainObjective: Recover the leased painting from the Silverbrook gallery and return it before the midsummer viewing.
A Discreet Commission.questStatement: Greyfold Manor's butler is hiring, with perfect courtesy, for an errand of perfect discretion: a family painting currently residing at a Silverbrook gallery must be returned to the manor before the midsummer viewing, the lease on it having a gap the gallery's schedule does not respect. All documents are in order. The timing is merely, regrettably, impossible through formal channels. The tea while he explains this is excellent.
A Discreet Commission.questDesignBrief: A caper comedy with no crime in it: everything is technically legal and everyone must behave as though nothing is happening. The painting is at Vionnet's auction house pending a showing; the recovery requires either negotiating with the auctioneer (Celeste Vionnet, who knows exactly whose painting it is and what the butler is doing, and will hand it over against a favor to be named with terrifying graciousness), intercepting the gallery's transport schedule through paperwork judo, or a genteel heist through the discretion-guarantee machinery itself. Complication: Rosalind attends the viewing, and the painting must be on the wall, correctly hung, before she enters the ballroom. Player paths reward finesse over force at every step; anything loud fails the spirit of the contract. Payoff: pay, the butler's formidable favor, and a thread: perceptive players glimpse the sixth painting's ownership paper trail.

completionCondition.query: The painting hangs in Greyfold's ballroom before the midsummer viewing begins.

The Shogun's Circle.name: The Shogun's Circle
The Shogun's Circle.mainObjective: Survey one arc of the Winter Shogun's patrol circle and log the season's measurements without an incident.
The Shogun's Circle.questStatement: The Reaches' senior hunter is taking a party into the deep waste to walk one arc of the Winter Shogun's patrol circle and log this season's measurements. The requirements are cold-craft, obedience, and the capacity to bow to something enormous without doing anything else. The pay is good. The interview consists of Ivar looking at each applicant for a long moment. Most do not pass.
The Shogun's Circle.questDesignBrief: The Frozen Reaches' signature quest: an expedition where the enemy is cold, the objective is data, and the climax is an encounter that must not become a fight. Under Ivar's instruction the party learns the deep waste's disciplines, takes the measurements, and, near the arc's end, meets the Winter Shogun itself: the full protocol, the bow, the enormous armored regard, the withdrawal. Player paths: perform the protocol faithfully (the Shogun passes; Ivar's sparse approval; the measurements confirm another year of contraction, which players see him log in silence), break protocol (survivable only by immediate flawless retreat and only barely; Ivar's contempt is permanent), or earn the rare thing: players of exceptional conduct may witness what Ivar has never told anyone, a bow returned. Payoff: pay, deep-waste certification the guild honors kingdom-wide, and the Reaches' longest mystery advanced one measured pace.

completionCondition.query: The patrol-circle arc has been surveyed and the party has returned from the deep waste.

PROMISING.name: PROMISING
PROMISING.mainObjective: Assist the Crimson Demon survey rotation through a full measurement cycle at the Sundered Ring.
PROMISING.questStatement: The Crimson Demon survey rotation at the Sundered Ring is hiring auxiliaries for a full measurement cycle: instrument bearers, arc walkers, and at least one person whose job is to hold the banner. Applicants must sign the clan's standard waiver, which is nine pages, illustrated, and ends with the phrase 'witnessed under an appropriate sky.' The expedition leader's self-introduction alone is worth the trip.
PROMISING.questDesignBrief: Science comedy at the edge of an apocalyptic mystery. Gekirin runs the party through the Ring's survey protocols: mana readings along the Slag Arcs, resonance mapping, dramatic pose calibration for the instruments (this is real; the arrays are keyed to gesture), and the sacred discipline of not casting in the Focus Bowl. Player paths: assist competently (the data confirms the consolidation; players see the readings align on the silhouette and watch Gekirin write PROMISING with shaking, delighted hands), sneak a cast in the Bowl (catastrophic-comedic: amplification beyond reason, a new crater on the Slag Arcs, and expulsion from the expedition with a formal dramatic denunciation), or engage the mystery: players who study the silhouette and the clan's locked-drawer history can piece together what is coming ready, and must decide whether that goes in the guild report. Payoff: pay, clan standing, spectacular data, and a seed of the world's largest pending event.

completionCondition.query: A full measurement cycle at the Sundered Ring has been completed with the survey rotation.

The Pending Shelf.name: The Pending Shelf
The Pending Shelf.mainObjective: Resolve the situation with the ticking item on the bonded warehouse's restricted shelf.
The Pending Shelf.questStatement: Senior Inspector Fosse is hiring outside contractors for a matter the customs service cannot officially have: an item on the bonded warehouse's oldest restricted shelf has begun, after a decade of silence, to tick. The service's legal position is that the shelf does not exist. The inspector's position is that the ticking is getting faster, and that she would like professionals between it and her border, off the record, at excellent rates.
The Pending Shelf.questDesignBrief: A bureaucratic thriller-comedy. The shelf holds the devil-contract courier seizures marked PENDING, and the ticking item is a contract-clock: a bound agreement whose term is expiring, at which point its liability transfers to the holder, which is legally the customs service, which is why legal marked it PENDING and fled. Player paths: research the contract's terms (Jules Marchand can read the instrument; a Silverbrook notary or the capital's scribes can find the loophole), negotiate with the counterparty when it manifests (a mid-rank devil, scrupulously polite, genuinely impressed by good paperwork; Maxwell's name opens dialogue), or resolve it by force (possible, loud, and it converts a contract problem into a devil problem inside a customs house). The elegant ending: transfer the liability to the one party that can hold it harmlessly, or void it on a drafting flaw, delighting devil and inspector alike. Payoff: excellent pay, Fosse's durable favor at the border, and the museum of attempts gains a wing she will not explain.

completionCondition.query: The ticking contract on the restricted shelf has been voided, transferred, or otherwise resolved.

Photo Finish.name: Photo Finish
Photo Finish.mainObjective: Escort the debt payment from the Debtors' Terrace to the credit office through race day.
Photo Finish.questStatement: Lord Ashmont of the Debtors' Terrace requires escorts of exceptional character for the shortest dangerous journey in Elroad: carrying a resident's completed debt payment from the Terrace to the credit office, on race day, through the grandstand, past the Rail Bar, across the most temptation-dense five hundred meters in the known world. The resident making the payment will be walking with you. That is the difficulty.
Photo Finish.questDesignBrief: An escort quest where the peril is temptation. A Terrace resident has, after six years, assembled full payment; the walk to the office passes every mechanism the Downs uses to reclaim exactly such moments: hot tips at the rail, one-last-race odds, the Photo Finish cocktail pricing, and a house that knows to the coin what is in the strongbox. Percival walks along as moral escort, magnificent and rueful. Player paths: shepherd the resident bodily (comedy of interceptions: touts, old friends, a suspiciously convenient long-shot everyone is talking about), engage the house's soft machinery (Colette Marbeau will bury her tips for the day if asked right; the Rail Bar staff can be tipped into slow service), or handle the twist: the final approach passes the credit office's own window display of newly foreclosed keepsakes, the house's last and cruelest play. Payoff: pay, a freed debtor's tearful gratitude, Percival's friendship, and the quiet fury of an institution that lost one, which has consequences worth playing later.

completionCondition.query: The debt payment has been delivered and recorded at the credit office and the resident released.

The Cancellation Backlog.name: The Cancellation Backlog
The Cancellation Backlog.mainObjective: Help the temple's membership administrator clear the trial-cancellation backlog during festival week.
The Cancellation Backlog.questStatement: The Axis Cult Grand Temple's membership administrator is hiring temporary staff, through the guild, at his own expense: festival week has generated a cancellation backlog of historic depth, and the desk requires assistants with strong handwriting, stronger patience, and no susceptibility whatsoever to recruitment. Cultists will attempt to convert you at the desk. That is not a joke. It is item one in the training materials.
The Cancellation Backlog.questDesignBrief: Bureaucratic farce inside the Cult machine. The desk work is real: verifying signatures against the unalterable ink, interviewing claimants who woke up enrolled ('the form was in a bread roll'), and processing appeals while recruiters lodge counter-appeals in real time. Cecily arrives from Axel mid-quest with a batch of her own accidental enrollments, cheerfully unrepentant. Player paths: process honestly and fast (Reiji's profound gratitude, expressed in stamps), investigate signature fraud (one recruiter is amending forms again; catching them cleanly triggers the temple's internal justice, which is Zesta, weeping, disappointed, and terrifying), or the diplomacy route: players who treat departing members kindly generate the exit-goodwill that is Reiji's secret ministry, and he shows them, wordlessly, the desk's true ledger: thank-you letters from the cleanly released. Payoff: pay from Reiji's own purse, a temple contact of rare integrity, and immunity, by administrative miracle, from Axis recruitment for one full year, in writing, stamped.

completionCondition.query: The festival-week cancellation backlog has been cleared at the temple desk.

Slime Drift.name: Slime Drift
Slime Drift.mainObjective: Cull the mineral slime migration before it reaches the Alcanretia spring lines.
Slime Drift.questStatement: The geyser-watcher is calling in the standing bounty: the mudpot slimes are migrating toward the city's spring lines again, drawn by something in the water, and the bathhouse keepers' association pays quietly and well to keep that sentence out of the tourist literature. Requirements: heat tolerance, blunt weapons or strong magic, and the discretion not to ask why the treasurer of the Cascade Shrines' offertory hall is listed as the paymaster.
Slime Drift.questDesignBrief: A monster-cull with a comedy layer and a lore layer. The mineral slimes are weapon-resistant, boiling hot, and drawn to the trace holiness in the spring water; the cull runs across the Boiling Terraces and Mudpot Fields on Danjuro's exact timing charts, with geysers as environmental artillery for players who learn the schedule. Paths: straightforward extermination (hot, dangerous, gloriously undignified; sulfur stink for days, with the dedicated tavern table to prove it), redirect the migration (clever players can use blessed water as lures to walk the slimes back into the deep flats), or follow the money: the paymaster trail leads to Umeko Tatsumi's 'pest control' line item and, for the very persistent, to the sealed sluice gate that Danjuro flags off every map. He will trade the truth of the gate for a sworn promise, and he can tell when a promise is real. Payoff: bounty, the bathhouse association's discreet gratitude, and standing with the flats' keeper.

completionCondition.query: The mineral slime migration has been culled or redirected away from the spring lines.

The Court Census.name: The Court Census
The Court Census.mainObjective: Infiltrate the Hollow Court's perimeter and confirm the date of the seasonal review.
The Court Census.questStatement: Capital guild posting, highest clearance: the army needs the date of the Hollow Court's seasonal review confirmed, because the border probes always follow it by exactly a week and this season's has not happened on schedule. A reconnaissance party is to approach the Court's perimeter, observe the Mustering Bowl, and return with the date. The posting's final line is unusual for guild paperwork: do not be clever. Observe and leave.
The Court Census.questDesignBrief: The endgame reconnaissance quest: no comedy, all weight. The Domain's approach is a masterclass in enemy competence: scheduled patrols, requisition-coded waymarkers, the Tithe Road's terrible punctuality. At the Court's edge, players witness the mustering: legions in silence, the polished dais, and the review's actual delay, which sharp observers can attribute to a figure in a grey stole halting the ceremony over, apparently, a documentation issue. Player paths: clean observation and extraction (the mission as ordered; the date confirmed; the army's respect and the veteran tier unlocked), risk the closer look (glimpsing the Clerks' Cathedral and the annual reader's window, at genuine peril), or the catastrophic option the posting warned against (being clever: engagement anywhere in the Domain brings response times that teach the player exactly why nobody in Axel wants this war). Payoff: elite pay, frontline standing, and the campaign-level intelligence that starts the endgame arc.

completionCondition.query: The review date has been confirmed and the party has returned from the Domain alive.

A Marsh Worth Digging.name: A Marsh Worth Digging
A Marsh Worth Digging.mainObjective: Help Erisa dig and defend her breeding wetland in the eastern marshes before the season turns.
A Marsh Worth Digging.questStatement: A field ecologist named Erisa is building a wetland in the eastern marshes with her own two hands, because the migratory monsters that nest there will die out inside six years and nobody with a budget seems to care. She loves the horrid things, openly, and needs someone to haul channel-stone, fend off whatever wanders in, and not laugh at her while she does it. The pay is whatever her grant does not cover, which is nothing.
A Marsh Worth Digging.questDesignBrief: This is heavy manual labor dressed up as a mercy mission for creatures most adventurers kill on sight, and the indignity is that the player defends the breeding ground of monsters the guild pays a bounty to exterminate. The player can haul stone and dig the channels directly, escort her supply runs out from Axel, hunt the predators picking off the first nestlings, or carry her Appendix Nine to someone who will actually read it and fund the work. Reward is no coin at all, but Erisa becomes a loyal source of zone ecology intel and hands over an experimental preparation she is refreshingly honest about being experimental. The twist is that the wetland works, and next season the plains are louder and stranger for it.

completionCondition.query: The player has helped Erisa advance her eastern-marsh breeding wetland by labor, escort, defense, or securing funding, and has decided whether to keep protecting the species she loves.

Every Head Counts.name: Every Head Counts
Every Head Counts.mainObjective: Escort Sanjuro's cattle drive across the plains without losing stock to the shifted monster zones.
Every Head Counts.questStatement: Sanjuro has ranched these plains for fifteen years and knows exactly where the monster zones begin, which is the trouble: this season they moved, and his usual safe route now runs straight through something with a taste for beef. He needs an escort for the drive, someone who can tell a real threat from a harmless nuisance and will not panic and stampede his herd. He pays fair, deducts for every head lost, and will judge your competence entirely by the cattle.
Every Head Counts.questDesignBrief: A straightforward escort job built on a comedy of priorities, since to Sanjuro the cattle matter more than the adventurers and he will say so to your face. The player must move a slow, dim herd through territory that recently shifted, deciding moment to moment when to fight and when to reroute. They can push through the new zone, take Sanjuro's advice and detour the long way at the cost of a day, scout ahead to remap the shift, or thin the local predators before the drive even starts. Reward is decent day-labor pay minus a per-head deduction for any cow eaten on your watch, plus Sanjuro's genuinely reliable plains intelligence from then on. The twist is that the zone shifted because something larger pushed the usual predators out of their range, and that something is still nearby.

completionCondition.query: The player has escorted Sanjuro's cattle drive to its destination and settled the account, having decided how to handle the shifted monster zone along the route.

Reading the Craters.name: Reading the Craters
Reading the Craters.mainObjective: Find out what Taiga's crater log is telling him about the explosion artist, and check on her if it points to trouble.
Reading the Craters.questStatement: Taiga rates every blast crater on the practice range on a five-star scale, and to a stranger this looks like the hobby of a man with far too much time. It is not. Yield tells him her mana, placement tells him her mood, and eleven years of daily entries have taught him to read the explosion artist's health and whereabouts from her craters alone. Lately the log has been reading wrong, and he cannot leave the overlook long enough to find out why.
Reading the Craters.questDesignBrief: The comedy is a rating log that looks like idle bureaucracy but is secretly a devoted vigil, born from a father who died refusing to adapt to the explosion era. The player is asked to turn one man's anxiety into legwork and confirm the artist is alright. They can study the log with Taiga and track her by the crater trail, ask around the Crimson Demon village about the mage's recent state, stake out the range to catch her mid-cast, or simply climb to the last blast site and see for themselves. Reward is modest coin and Taiga's crater-reading service, which doubles as an early warning for when the range is safe to cross. The twist is that the readings are off either because she is fine but distracted or because she is genuinely not fine, and Taiga needs to know which before he can sleep.

completionCondition.query: The player has investigated the anomaly in Taiga's crater log, learned the true state of the explosion artist, and reported back to Taiga.

The Toll of the Rope Bridge.name: The Toll of the Rope Bridge
The Toll of the Rope Bridge.mainObjective: Make the ravine rope-bridge crossing safe by dealing with the predator working it from above.
The Toll of the Rope Bridge.questStatement: The rope bridge over the ravine on the Crimson Demon road is the finest ambush spot for a hundred miles, and something has claimed it. It waits up where nothing on foot can follow, watches until you are mid-crossing with both hands full of rope, then dives. Travelers have started taking the long way around, merchants are grumbling, and the guild would very much like the crossing back.
The Toll of the Rope Bridge.questDesignBrief: A puzzle-fight against terrain, because the predator, Torimaru, has weaponized altitude and the simple fact that defending yourself on the bridge means letting go of the only thing keeping you out of the ravine. Brute force alone loses, since the crossing itself is the trap. The player can cross as bait while an ally holds the high ground with ranged fire, time the passage around its testing dive and slip over when it commits, fortify or replace the span with something defensible, or lure it down to solid footing where the fight is finally fair. Reward is a small guild bounty, the gratitude of the merchants who use the road, and possibly one enormous feather worth good money to a fletcher. The twist is that Torimaru is clever, has worked this crossing three seasons running, and will not fall for the same trick twice.

completionCondition.query: The player has resolved the threat at the ravine rope-bridge crossing, by killing, driving off, or outmaneuvering the predator, so that travelers can cross safely.

The Map Nibbles Keeps Breaking.name: The Map Nibbles Keeps Breaking
The Map Nibbles Keeps Breaking.mainObjective: Deliver an updated survey of Nibbles' tunnel network, or stop the crawler from expanding it further.
The Map Nibbles Keeps Breaking.questStatement: The guild's map of the Neighbourhood Ruins undercroft is a work of fiction, and the reason is a burrowing thing called Nibbles that has spent years connecting cellars which were never meant to connect. Every season it digs more, and every season a party gets lost in passages that did not exist on the last survey. The guild will pay for an updated map, and pay more if someone can convince Nibbles to stop.
The Map Nibbles Keeps Breaking.questDesignBrief: Ostensibly a cartography contract, actually a delve against a burrower that hunts by scent and ground vibration, so a lit torch buys you nothing and a quiet step buys you everything. The player either charts around the crawler or confronts it head on. They can survey the new tunnels while dodging its patrols, track Nibbles to its main den and drive it off or kill it, collapse the worst of the illegal connections to slow the sprawl, or work out what it eats and redirect its digging away from the traveled sections. Reward is a survey fee scaled to how much of the network you chart, plus hazard pay for handling Nibbles directly. The twist is that the tunnels have started running toward something older that the guild map quietly does not show, and Nibbles has been digging straight for it.

completionCondition.query: The player has either delivered an updated survey of Nibbles' tunnel network or stopped the crawler from expanding it further, and reported the outcome to the guild.

Hold the Lamp Steady.name: Hold the Lamp Steady
Hold the Lamp Steady.mainObjective: Help Yoriko reach and record the upper-floor inscriptions in the Abandoned Castle.
Hold the Lamp Steady.questStatement: Yoriko has spent three months copying the construction marks carved into the Abandoned Castle, and they are quietly insisting the building was never what the official histories say it was.
