She refuses to publish half a truth, so she needs the rest: the inscriptions on the upper floors, where the stairs are unsafe and the light is worse. The work is deeply unglamorous. Mostly you will hold a lamp very still while a scholar mutters at a wall.
Hold the Lamp Steady.questDesignBrief: A slow, atmospheric escort-and-support quest whose comedy is the gap between an ominous discovery and the sheer tedium of documenting it, with the player serving as a human lamp stand and pack mule for genuinely dangerous archaeology. They can clear and shore up a route to the upper floors, guard Yoriko while she works against whatever nests up there, fetch specific inscriptions she cannot safely reach herself, or secure her a defensible workspace so she can stay longer. Reward is poor pay from a scholar with no budget, a copy of her findings once they are complete, and a standing contact who understands the castle better than anyone alive. The twist is that the decoded purpose is unsettling enough that finishing the translation may attract exactly the attention Yoriko has been trying to avoid.

completionCondition.query: The player has helped Yoriko obtain and record the upper-floor inscriptions she needed, and learned what the marks reveal about the castle's original purpose.

Clause Forty.name: Clause Forty
Clause Forty.mainObjective: Find the source of the ringing under Riverhead Lake and decide what to do about it.
Clause Forty.questStatement: Rent a boat from Wallis and clause forty of the contract reads like a joke: management is not responsible for the consequences of answering the deep bell, should you hear it, so row home, do not look down, and tell Wallis. It is not a joke. His grandmother heard a ringing from under the middle of the lake one cold night, put a halberd into whatever came after it, and kept the inn until she died. Lately more customers are asking about a sound from the deep water, and Wallis has stopped smiling when they do.
Clause Forty.questDesignBrief: A creeping dread quest wearing the costume of a liability waiver, set on a lake where the comedy is how hard everyone works to avoid naming the thing beneath it. The player who takes clause forty seriously gets pointed at open water. They can row out and listen for the bell on a cold night, coax the full account from Wallis or cross-reference it with the innkeeper Airi's family story, sound the deep spots the locals refuse to fish, or simply wait for the next customer to hear it and follow their report. Reward is a free boat rental, a fast tow home, and information Wallis has never once volunteered to anyone. The twist is that the deep-winter ringing is real, rare, and slowly becoming less rare, so finding the source means deciding whether to warn the lake or let it keep sleeping.

completionCondition.query: The player has learned the source of the ringing under Riverhead Lake and decided what to do about it.

The Nine Names.name: The Nine Names
The Nine Names.mainObjective: Learn the fate of at least one rider in Petra's private book, or change where the tenth column is riding before it becomes the tenth name.
The Nine Names.questStatement: The waystation farrier, Petra Vollan, keeps a private book no crown inspector will ever see. In it, nine horses are listed by name, and beside each horse a rider who never came back to claim it. She has shod every one gently and fed them out of a budget that officially does not exist, and now a captain rides north checking his saddle straps twice, like a man who has done the arithmetic. She would like someone to find out where the tenth column is going before she has to write a tenth name.
The Nine Names.questDesignBrief: This is a somber logistics-of-grief errand dressed up as horse care, and the comedy is bureaucratic: Petra earned a master's grade and a warm garrison posting, and stays at a freezing waystation because the road needs her and the horses do too. A player can shadow or escort the northbound column and bring the road ahead back to her, trace one named rider through waystation and Northern ledgers to close the book on him, or petition the crown board to resupply the post or reroute the column, a paperwork ordeal with a real payoff. The reward is dreadful pay, a set of expertly reforged shoes or barding at cost, and Petra's private route intelligence once she decides she trusts you. The twist is that one of the nine horses belongs not to a dead man but to a deserter who is very much alive and does not want finding.

completionCondition.query: The player has learned the fate of at least one rider recorded in Petra's private book, or changed the tenth column's course, and decided what to tell her about it.

The Missing Move.name: The Missing Move
The Missing Move.mainObjective: Discover who leaves the chalked chess move on the toll counter each first thaw, and what the missing white king really is.
The Missing Move.questStatement: Noa Kirigaya keeps the toll on the Mountain Pass, and she keeps her predecessor's chess set at the window, though the white king was already gone when she counted the pieces. Four winters running, at first thaw, she has found a single chalked receipt waiting on the counter in the fog, one chess move written in a hand that is neither hers nor her predecessor's. The guild logged the man before her as abandoned-post: an arrival, a merchant, first-thaw fog, no departure, and then no further entries in his ledger. She has stopped pretending the two things are unrelated.
The Missing Move.questDesignBrief: This is the eerie centerpiece of the cluster, a quiet ghost story run on a toll booth's paperwork logic, and it should be played cold and administrative rather than spooky, because the dread is in the continuity, not the fog. A player can stake out the counter through a first-thaw fog and see who or what leaves the receipt, reconstruct the predecessor's last game from the board's frozen position and the four chalked moves that together point to a place, or chase the merchant's manifest through the Millbridge and Northern Waystation ledgers to learn who actually crossed that day. The reward is a modest toll waiver in perpetuity, the predecessor's annotated pass maps, and whatever waits at the end of the game. The twist is that the chalked hand belongs to the merchant, not the vanished tollkeeper, and the game was never a game but a search for the missing king, which is not a piece of carved wood.

completionCondition.query: The player has identified the source of the chalked chess moves and the fate of Noa's predecessor, and decided what to do about the unfinished game.

A Day She Does Not Like.name: A Day She Does Not Like
A Day She Does Not Like.mainObjective: Cross the Mountain Pass with Chiho's guidance, or find out firsthand why she refused to set out today.
A Day She Does Not Like.questStatement: Chiho Amagase is the finest guide on the Mountain Pass and has lost exactly one client in nine years, a record she maintains by refunding anyone who argues and leaving them at the trailhead. Today she does not like the look of the peaks, and she will not explain further than that. You, unfortunately, have somewhere to be, and the sky looks perfectly fine to you, which is precisely what the last person she left behind thought too.
A Day She Does Not Like.questDesignBrief: This is a quest about respecting expertise you cannot personally verify, carried on KonoSuba's deadpan fatalism, and the indignity is that Chiho is almost certainly right while the player almost certainly wants to go anyway. A player can earn her trust by waiting out the bad day and making himself useful at her cabin, which unlocks full guide service and the hermit's general whereabouts, or hire a lesser guide and push through to survive the thing she saw coming the hard way, or study the tells she reads off the peaks and bring her proof the window is actually safe. The reward is safe passage, the locations of the pass caves and shrines, and a pointer toward the hermit Sokudo; push through against her word instead and the reward is a genuine mountain hazard and no refund. The twist is that the one client she lost was family, which is why the refunds are absolute and the arguments never work.

completionCondition.query: The player has crossed the Mountain Pass under Chiho's guidance or learned firsthand why she refused, and secured either her route knowledge or her respect.

The Tea Is More Important.name: The Tea Is More Important
The Tea Is More Important.mainObjective: Find the hermit Sokudo and earn his guidance across the range on his terms, which are not the terms you expect.
The Tea Is More Important.questStatement: Somewhere off the marked paths of the Mountain Pass lives a Monk-class hermit the guides mention and none of them have ever met. Sokudo Ryuzaki is, by any honest measure, one of the most dangerous men in the kingdom, which is exactly why he has arranged his life so that he never has to prove it and can drink tea instead. If you can find his hut, and if you can sit through the tea without insulting it, he knows every cave, shrine, and killing drop on the range.
The Tea Is More Important.questDesignBrief: This is the comedic counterweight to the pass's gloom: a lethal old man whose only test is whether you can behave like a decent guest, and the joke is that players braced for a combat trial get a tea ceremony, where failing the tea is far worse than failing a fight. A player can let Chiho or the shrine markers point him toward Sokudo's general area and then earn the invitation through patience rather than force, or demonstrate restraint in a situation where fighting is the obvious move and which Sokudo will somehow already have watched, or simply arrive bearing something worth his time, a rare leaf, real news off the road, or a genuinely difficult question. The reward is the best route intelligence on the pass, a single lesson worth far more than its brevity suggests, and, of course, tea. The twist is that the test never actually ends, and rudeness on the way out costs everything earned on the way in.

completionCondition.query: The player has located Sokudo, passed his hospitality test rather than a fight, and earned his guidance across the mountain range.

Whether You Should Go Up Today.name: Whether You Should Go Up Today
Whether You Should Go Up Today.mainObjective: Get Genpachi's honest read on the road above, and settle the fate of the party that bought his supplies but ignored his warning.
Whether You Should Go Up Today.questStatement: Genpachi Muraoka has run the same stall for thirty years at the exact spot where travelers first understand that the mountain is serious, and his prices understand it too. He will sell you overpriced supplies with a warm and genuine smile, and he will also tell you, honestly and for free, whether you ought to go up today. A party came through yesterday, bought out half his stock, and ignored the free half of the transaction, and Genpachi has been watching the road above ever since.
Whether You Should Go Up Today.questDesignBrief: This is a somber roadside quest about the cost of advice ignored, wrapped around a haggling joke, where the comedy is Genpachi's genial extortion and the weight is that his free warning was always the valuable half and nobody values a free thing. A player can heed him, resupply properly, and climb prepared to find the party that did not, or investigate why they ignored a thirty-year veteran, which leads back to an Axis recruiter's promise or a contract deadline pushing them uphill, or simply relieve the old man by carrying word back down so he can stop watching the treeline. The reward is a fair reading of the pass condition, a standing discount once he decides you actually listen, and the gratitude of anyone still alive up there. The twist is that the party ignored him because a rival vendor higher up the road undercut his warning as a sales tactic, calling caution a trick to sell more rope.

completionCondition.query: The player has learned the true condition of the road above from Genpachi and acted on the fate of the party that ignored his warning.

The Held Letter.name: The Held Letter
The Held Letter.mainObjective: Decide whether Suzu's sister's final letter should reach the man in the capital, and carry it there if the answer is yes.
The Held Letter.questStatement: In the dead-letter drawer at the Millbridge toll office, Suzu Kanzashi keeps one letter she has never been able to send. Her sister wrote it the week before the river fever took her, addressed to the man who had broken their engagement and left for the capital not knowing she was ill. Suzu is almost certain the letter forgives him, which is exactly why it has sat in that drawer for six years, because delivering it means giving away the last words her sister ever wrote and handing absolution to a man Suzu is not finished blaming.
The Held Letter.questDesignBrief: This is the cluster's quietest and heaviest quest, a courier job that is really about grief and the arithmetic of letting go, with no monster in it and the KonoSuba register carried entirely in the warmth beneath the cynicism, played gently. A player can simply agree to carry the letter to the capital and find the man, the straightforward road with a hard conversation at the end of it, or find out what became of him first, since six years is long enough that he may be dead, married, or ruined, each of which changes what delivery means, or sit with Suzu long enough that she resolves to deliver it herself and needs an escort for the road. The reward is not coin but Suzu's trust and the run of her dead-letter drawer, a surprising trove of undelivered intelligence, plus a favor owed by whoever the letter finally reaches. The twist is that the man has been writing to that same drawer for years, letters Suzu never carried to her sister's grave, and the forgiveness, it turns out, was always meant to run both ways.

completionCondition.query: The player has resolved the fate of the sister's letter, by delivering it, returning it to Suzu, or helping her deliver it herself, and reckoned with what that costs her.

The Engineered Silence.name: The Engineered Silence
The Engineered Silence.mainObjective: Take Rui's final round of threshold measurements deeper into the cave to prove the magic suppression is built, not natural, and decide who to tell.
The Engineered Silence.questStatement: A researcher named Rui has spent three seasons measuring exactly where magic dies at the cave mouth, and the line is too straight, too even, and too consistent to be an accident of geology. Someone engineered this suppression field, tuned it, and has been maintaining it since before the Crimson Demons ever settled here. The village would very much prefer she stop saying that out loud, because the cave is the one place their explosion magic goes quiet, and a door that was built has a builder who might still have the key.
The Engineered Silence.questDesignBrief: The comedy is bureaucratic denial colliding with a genuinely unsettling discovery: the whole village's identity rests on being the strongest mages alive, and here is a soft-spoken woman with a notebook proving somebody figured out how to switch them off on purpose. The player carries or protects Rui's instruments to the deep thresholds where the field is strongest and readings must be taken by hand because no magical tool works. Approaches: escort Rui in person past whatever lurks in the dead zone, retrieve the older survey stones she cannot reach on the upper ledges, or quietly test the field yourself by walking a lit torch to the exact meter where a fire spell would fizzle. The twist is what the measurements imply about a maintenance mechanism still running somewhere below. Reward is lousy: a share of Rui's stipend, meaning almost nothing, plus a hand-copied threshold map and her honest gratitude, which is worth more than the money and still will not buy dinner. Completion hinges on the player learning the field is artificial and choosing whether to bring the finding to the village, bury it, or follow it downward.

completionCondition.query: The player has helped Rui gather the deep threshold measurements, confirmed the suppression field is engineered rather than natural, and decided what to do with the finding.

Put Them Down by Hand.name: Put Them Down by Hand
Put Them Down by Hand.mainObjective: Clear the animated husks from the dead zone using only physical force, since neither holy magic nor fire works inside the suppression field.
Put Them Down by Hand.questStatement: The shambling husks in the cave were mages once, and the cave drained their magic before it took the rest of them. Hollis has worked out the horrible detail: they move on something that is not arcane at all, which is why they keep walking in a place where every spell dies, and why a priest's purification washes over them and does absolutely nothing. In here the entire undead-disposal toolbox is empty, so if you want them stopped, you stop them the old way, with a blunt object and no clever plan.
Put Them Down by Hand.questDesignBrief: The angle is the indignity of losing every shortcut: this is a party's chance to discover that their fireballs and holy chants are decorative props the moment they cross the threshold, and the only spell that matters is a heavy stick swung with feeling. Hollis is grim and practical and will brief the player flatly on why the standard answers fail. Approaches: brute force the husks in a chokepoint where the cave geometry funnels them one at a time, lure them out past the suppression line where magic works again and finish them properly in daylight, or collapse a passage to seal the worst pocket rather than fight it. The twist is realizing that a mage-class party is at its weakest exactly where it expected to be strongest. Reward is grim and modest: salvage rights on whatever the husks were carrying when they died, a small bounty per husk paid by Hollis from a purse that is clearly his own, and the knowledge of precisely where your magic stops working, which may save your life later. Completion is when the husks in the accessible dead zone are physically destroyed and the player understands why nothing arcane touched them.

completionCondition.query: The player has learned that the husks cannot be purified inside the cave and has destroyed the accessible ones by physical means.

The Radius Keeps Growing.name: The Radius Keeps Growing
The Radius Keeps Growing.mainObjective: Map how far the Sealed Vault Sentinel has quietly expanded the zone it will kill inside, and find a way past or around it to the vault door.
The Radius Keeps Growing.questStatement: The golem guarding the sealed vault was built to deny access, and over three unsupervised centuries it has been slowly redefining what access means. Its killing radius used to end at the vault door. Now it reaches most of a corridor, and it has been quietly claiming a little more ground every generation, on nobody's authority but its own. Nobody set it to do this. It simply decided that anything near the vault counts as reaching for the vault, and it has a very generous definition of near.
The Radius Keeps Growing.questDesignBrief: The comedy is corporate scope creep rendered in stone and murder: a construct that has been expanding its own job description for three hundred years with no manager to stop it, and is now technically overstepping a commission written before anyone alive was born. The player needs to establish the actual current boundary without dying to it, which is the whole tension. Approaches: chart the radius empirically by advancing marker stones a step at a time until the Sentinel reacts, then retreating; find the older facility survey Tamaki references that logs where the boundary used to sit and infer how it moved; or bait the golem into committing to one intruder while a second slips along the wall to the door. The twist is that the vault the Sentinel is defending may no longer contain what its commission was written to protect, meaning it has spent centuries expanding a guard over an empty room. Reward is thin: whatever is actually behind the door if the player reaches it, plus a mapped safe-line that makes the corridor traversable, and no thanks from the golem, which does not do thanks. Completion is when the player has determined the Sentinel's current denial radius and either reached the vault door or confirmed why it cannot be reached.

completionCondition.query: The player has mapped the Sealed Vault Sentinel's expanded killing radius and either reached the vault door or established why it is unreachable.

How to Command a Golem.name: How to Command a Golem
How to Command a Golem.mainObjective: Copy the threshold ward's command sigils and cross-reference them with Soketto's original commission notes to learn how the facility's constructs are actually controlled.
How to Command a Golem.questStatement: The threshold ward at the facility's entrance is the gentlest golem in the place: it challenges you, writes you down, and turns you away, but it will not swing unless you shove past it. Its sigils are also the oldest and clearest in the complex, which makes it the one construct a person can study up close without dying. Learn to read what is carved on it, match it against the commission notes in Soketto's archive, and you may work out the command grammar that runs every golem deeper in, before you meet one that skips the challenge and goes straight to the swinging.
How to Command a Golem.questDesignBrief: This is the investigation quest of the cluster: a patient scholarly puzzle wearing the skin of a dungeon crawl, where understanding the syntax of a three-hundred-year-old work order is the actual weapon. Mamoru is careful and a little pedantic and treats the threshold ward as a cooperative colleague rather than a threat. Approaches: transcribe the ward's sigils in place, rubbing by rubbing, without provoking it into the one thing that makes it hostile; recover the original commission notes from Soketto's archive to translate the carving style; or test small commanded gestures on the ward itself, carefully, to confirm which marks mean challenge, record, and refuse. The twist is that the same grammar, once understood, hints at how to instruct or at least confuse the deadlier constructs like the vault Sentinel, turning a language lesson into a survival tool. Reward is a researcher's reward: a working translation key to the facility's command sigils, Mamoru's standing offer of future help, and pay that Mamoru apologizes for because it is a research stipend and everyone knows what those are worth. Completion is when the player has copied the ward's sigils, matched them to the commission notes, and grasped how the constructs are commanded.

completionCondition.query: The player has recorded the threshold ward's sigils, cross-referenced Soketto's commission notes, and learned the basics of how the facility's constructs are commanded.

The Inventory Behind the Falls.name: The Inventory Behind the Falls
The Inventory Behind the Falls.mainObjective: Help Umeko complete her overdue relic count in the vault behind the waterfall and reconcile the one line that no longer matches her ledger.
The Inventory Behind the Falls.questStatement: Umeko inventories the relics stored behind the falls with the same crisp devotion she gives the towels, because in her private theology a clean ledger is worship and Aqua's water is proof enough that purity is holy. She would like a second set of hands for this season's count, partly because the vault path behind the cascade is slick and partly because a line in her ledger has stopped reconciling, and Umeko does not tolerate a line that will not reconcile. Something that should be on a shelf is not on the shelf, and she wrote it down herself.
The Inventory Behind the Falls.questDesignBrief: The comedy is an auditor's soul applied to sacred relics: Umeko treats a discrepancy in a vault of holy artifacts exactly as she would treat a miscounted towel stack, with brisk offense rather than dread, and the horror creeps in around the edges of her professionalism. The player accompanies her behind the falls to physically count relics and find why one entry is off. Approaches: recount the whole vault methodically with Umeko and catch a simple filing error, which she would find both relieving and faintly disappointing; track the missing item as an actual theft and follow who had vault access; or discover the item is not missing so much as changed, no longer matching its own description, which is a far worse kind of unreconciled. The twist is that the relic that will not reconcile may be tied to why the falls behave strangely lately. Reward is characteristically dry: a genuinely useful minor relic Umeko deems surplus, a standing pass behind the falls, and her respect, which she rations more tightly than the towels. Completion is when the player has helped complete the count and resolved, one way or another, the line that would not reconcile.

completionCondition.query: The player has helped Umeko inventory the relic vault behind the falls and determined what happened to the entry that no longer matched her ledger.

The Water Went Still Twice.name: The Water Went Still Twice
The Water Went Still Twice.mainObjective: Investigate Ayaka's water-mood log to confirm whether the falls going still is a warning that the Winter Shogun's territory is about to advance, and carry the finding to someone with an army.
The Water Went Still Twice.questStatement: Twice now the Cascade has gone perfectly, unnaturally still, and both times, exactly one season later, the Winter Shogun's frozen circle contracted southward in the north. Ayaka has been keeping a dated water-mood log because she does not believe in coincidences that keep an appointment. The Cascade feeds every river south of the highlands, so if the falls go quiet a third time, she intends to walk down the mountain and tell someone with soldiers, and she would rather send proof than a feeling.
The Water Went Still Twice.questDesignBrief: The tone here is the somber, investigative end of the cluster: a shrine attendant's quiet dread dressed as diligent record-keeping, where the joke is only that nobody with power will listen to a woman who serves tea and watches waterfalls. The player helps Ayaka turn a hunch into evidence solid enough to move a garrison. Approaches: gather corroborating dates by comparing Ayaka's log against the shrine's older water records and the northern station reports to confirm the pattern is real; stake out the falls to document a stilling event firsthand if one is beginning; or run the finding down the mountain to Fort Meridian or a northern posting and try to make a bored officer take an untitled woman's weather diary seriously. The twist is whether the correlation predicts the next advance in time to matter, or only explains the last one too late. Reward is not gold: a season of strong tea, Ayaka's dawn song sung once for the player alone, and the far larger, unpayable reward of possibly getting the north warned before the ice moves. Completion is when the player has tested the water-still-to-Shogun correlation and gotten the finding into the hands of someone able to act on it.

completionCondition.query: The player has investigated Ayaka's water-mood log, established whether the falls going still predicts the Winter Shogun's advance, and delivered the finding to someone with the authority to respond.

The Labyrinth Has a Pulse.name: The Labyrinth Has a Pulse
The Labyrinth Has a Pulse.mainObjective: Learn why the Great Tree Labyrinth's passages keep rearranging by discovering that the Deep Root Warden is the labyrinth itself, and find a way to move through a maze that is reacting to you.
The Labyrinth Has a Pulse.questStatement: Every map of the Great Tree Labyrinth goes wrong within days, because the corridors close behind you and open somewhere else, and no surveyor has ever explained why. The answer is that there is no maze and no monster in the maze: the labyrinth is a single living thing called Verdessa, and the shifting walls are its body reacting to you the way a body reacts to a splinter. It does not think the way you think. It processes, slowly and thoroughly, and it has been processing intruders longer than the village has kept records.
The Labyrinth Has a Pulse.questDesignBrief: This is the cluster's big engineered-secret reveal played straight and eerie: the dungeon is not a place with a warden, it is the warden, and every party that ever got lost was being handled by an organism too slow and too vast to notice it had guests. The player's task is to understand this well enough to survive it, since fighting the walls is fighting the room. Approaches: move gently and predictably so Verdessa's slow immune response never fully engages, treating passage like not startling a huge sleeping animal; find the deep-body rhythm in how the root-walls shift and time movement to the openings rather than forcing them; or seek out whatever the Crimson Demons left in Verdessa's depths, since the clan clearly knew more about this thing than they admit. The twist is that Verdessa is not hostile so much as immense and indifferent, and the way out is cooperation with a nervous system, not victory over a boss. Reward is strange and non-heroic: safe passage the next time the player must cross, a cutting or seed that responds to Verdessa's rhythm, and the unsettling knowledge of what the labyrinth actually is, which the village would rather not confirm. Completion is when the player has learned that Verdessa and the labyrinth are one organism and worked out how to travel it without triggering its full response.

completionCondition.query: The player has discovered that the Deep Root Warden Verdessa is the labyrinth itself and found a way to move through the shifting passages without provoking its full defensive response.

The Ground That Will Not Keep Them.name: The Ground That Will Not Keep Them
The Ground That Will Not Keep Them.mainObjective: Cross the scarred battlefield below the barrier without being drawn into the endless revolt of the dead who rise, fight, and rise again.
The Ground That Will Not Keep Them.questStatement: Isolde will tell you plainly that the field ahead is not haunted in any way you can fix. It is soil that has swallowed more death than it can hold, and so it gives some back, at random, without malice or command. The revenants rise, they march, they fight whatever moves, and they fall, and by the next watch they are up again. She does not ask you to end it. She asks you to get across, and to understand that killing them changes nothing.
The Ground That Will Not Keep Them.questDesignBrief: The quiet horror here is futility, not menace: this is the one battlefield where victory is meaningless, because the ground itself re-arms the enemy every season. The indignity is that an adventurer's whole toolkit, kill it and loot it, accomplishes precisely nothing. Approaches: time a crossing between risings using Isolde's dated observations of the field's rhythm; move at the hour the revenants are busy fighting each other and slip through the gap; attempt to consecrate or drain a single corridor of soil enough for one safe passage, which Isolde suspects is possible but temporary; or simply carry the wounded and refuse every fight, which is the answer she is really testing for. Reward is safe passage intelligence, a revenant's field-issue token worth a little to collectors, and Isolde's respect, which she gives to nobody who tries to win here. Twist: any player who clears the field and boasts of it is invited back the next season to see the same faces standing.

completionCondition.query: The player has crossed or navigated the self-raising battlefield below the barrier and understood that the revenants cannot be permanently destroyed, choosing a way through rather than a way to win.

Counting Morvath.name: Counting Morvath
Counting Morvath.mainObjective: Time the watcher's circuit and slip past the barrier during the exact window when the distortion blinds his sightline.
Counting Morvath.questStatement: Morvath walks his circuit so that nothing reaches the barrier unseen, and in thirty patrols nothing ever has. The frontier garrison has learned that the alternative to timing him is fighting him, and they would rather not. There is a window, brief and real, where the barrier's distortion swallows his line of sight and he is, for a handful of breaths, blind. Get it wrong and he sees you. See you is the last thing that happens to most.
Counting Morvath.questDesignBrief: This is a stopwatch quest dressed as a death sentence: the whole thing turns on patience and arithmetic, not combat, and the comedy is how much boredom stands between the player and the most dangerous mistake of their life. Approaches: study the garrison's documented circuit timings from cover and commit to the window on faith; observe him personally for a full circuit to confirm the numbers still hold, which costs a day but buys certainty; sabotage or trigger the barrier distortion early to widen the blind window, a risky bet that could also alert him; or, foolishly, try to take him, which the brief exists to discourage. Reward is the single most valuable piece of frontier intelligence, a copy of the circuit ledger, and the garrison quartermaster's gratitude in the form of usable supplies. Twist: the window has been drifting by seconds each season, and the garrison's numbers are one season stale, which the careful player discovers and the reckless one does not.

completionCondition.query: The player has determined the timing of Morvath's circuit and the barrier's blind window and used it to pass the watcher, or has confirmed the documented timing is no longer accurate.

The Paperwork Does Not Mean They Freeze.name: The Paperwork Does Not Mean They Freeze
The Paperwork Does Not Mean They Freeze.mainObjective: Run a load of unrequisitioned winter kit north to a frontier unit whose allocation lapsed, without the delivery showing up in any official ledger.
The Paperwork Does Not Mean They Freeze.questStatement: Yasuko keeps a third ledger that no one is supposed to know exists, and it records where the cold-weather gear actually goes. The crown's paperwork failed a frontier garrison this winter, and failed paperwork, in the capital's understanding, simply means those men are not owed anything. Yasuko understands it differently. She needs the surplus moved north before the hard freeze, quietly, off the books, to soldiers who will otherwise learn what the cold does to men the army has decided not to count.
The Paperwork Does Not Mean They Freeze.questDesignBrief: The restraint here is the point: no monster, no villain, just a quartermaster committing gentle fraud so that strangers do not die of exposure, and the stakes are entirely human. The indignity angle is bureaucratic, the heroism is a smuggling run for blankets. Approaches: haul the load north yourself through the frontier weather, the honest and cold option; move it through Yasuko's barter web of villages so no single leg looks like a shipment; forge or borrow a plausible transfer manifest to give the wagon cover if stopped, leaning on her network of quiet debts; or recruit a returning garrison column to carry it under their own movement orders. Reward is poor pay, a set of genuinely excellent frontier-grade cold gear pulled from the surplus, and standing in Yasuko's web, which opens doors across half the heartland. Twist: one waystation on the route is Petra's forge and one frontier column is the very one whose captain now checks his straps twice, tying the delivery to lives the player may already have touched.

completionCondition.query: The player has moved the unrequisitioned winter kit to the lapsed frontier unit while keeping the delivery off the official ledgers, or has been caught and dealt with the consequences.

The Forged Smile in the Ledger.name: The Forged Smile in the Ledger
The Forged Smile in the Ledger.mainObjective: Trace the phantom-unit requisitions passing through Meridian's books to whoever is balancing them too perfectly to be real.
The Forged Smile in the Ledger.questStatement: Piers can feel a misplaced decimal through a closed cover, and something in Meridian's transfer manifests is setting his teeth on edge. They balance exactly, every time, with none of the friction, spoilage, or human error that real logistics carries. He calls it the accounting equivalent of a forged smile. Somewhere behind these too-perfect books are units that do not exist, supplies that go nowhere, and a hand steady enough to make the lie add up. He wants to know whose.
The Forged Smile in the Ledger.questDesignBrief: This is a paper-trail mystery with a cold current under it: the fraud is quiet, vast, and possibly load-bearing for someone powerful, and the danger is that the answer is not a clerk but a policy. The comedy is dry and forensic, a man moved to dread by numbers that are too tidy. Approaches: audit the manifests alongside Piers and follow the phantom units to their origin office; cross-reference against the casualty ledgers and sealed Ashford records that carry the same signature, building the case from three directions; interview or shadow the courier who physically moves the manifests north; or bait the forger by introducing a deliberate error and watching who corrects it too fast. Reward is dangerous knowledge, a favor from Piers and his rival-correspondent at Ashford, and a sealed copy of the evidence that is worth a great deal to the wrong people. Twist: the phantom requisitions may be funding Yasuko's off-book winter pipeline, or something far darker, and Piers has to decide whether exposing the fraud saves lives or ends them.

completionCondition.query: The player has traced the source of the too-perfect phantom-unit manifests and learned what the fraud is actually funding, deciding what to do with the proof.

The Clearing Keeps Its Own.name: The Clearing Keeps Its Own
The Clearing Keeps Its Own.mainObjective: Enter the Winter Shogun's clearing and leave it again without joining the rimebound garrison that grows by one or two every season.
The Clearing Keeps Its Own.questStatement: Aldric can name most of the rimebound, because he watched them arrive. Every adventurer who did not bow, every hunter who chased a sprite one drift too far, every traveler who ignored the station hands, they are all still here, frozen upright and standing their post. The cold preserves them, the residual magic moves them, and their numbers climb by one or two each winter. The clearing has been gathering its defenders longer than the station's records go back. Aldric would prefer your name not join the list.
The Clearing Keeps Its Own.questDesignBrief: The dread is accumulation: this is a garrison that recruits from the people who came to defeat it, and the horror is quiet arithmetic rather than any single monster. The KonoSuba edge is in the station hands' resigned professionalism, the warnings delivered so flatly because the flatness is the only thing that ever saves anyone. Approaches: bow to the Winter Shogun as Yuki teaches and pass through as a guest rather than a trespasser; move only in daylight and never break the treeline chasing a sprite, the discipline route; retrieve a specific fallen adventurer's effects from among the rimebound for a grieving client without triggering the garrison, a precise extraction under the cold's rules; or attempt to fight, which Aldric will beg you not to do and which simply adds to the count. Reward is survival, the recovered effects and their bounty, and Aldric's warning-marks for the safe corridors, which are worth more than gold in this forest. Twist: one of the rimebound is standing exactly where the player would have to stand to fight, wearing gear identical to the party's own, a mirror the clearing put there on purpose.

completionCondition.query: The player has entered the Winter Shogun's clearing and left it alive without becoming part of the rimebound garrison, having learned why the garrison never stops growing.

The Priestess Who Prays to the Wrong God.name: The Priestess Who Prays to the Wrong God
The Priestess Who Prays to the Wrong God.mainObjective: Expose the Demon King's general Serena before her disguise as a devout priestess turns a community against itself from the inside.
The Priestess Who Prays to the Wrong God.questStatement: Serena does not besiege. She arrives as a kind priestess, earns a village's trust, and then guides it, gently, patiently, into tearing itself apart. It has worked everywhere except against people too stupid to follow her manipulations to their logical conclusion, which she finds genuinely infuriating. She carries a specific, burning hatred for the Axis Cult and its goddess, and she has studied Kazuma's party in detail. Somewhere out there a community is already halfway to believing her. You may be the only one who has noticed the seams.
The Priestess Who Prays to the Wrong God.questDesignBrief: The tension is social rather than martial: the enemy is a rumor with a warm smile, and the danger is that fighting her the obvious way proves her narrative for her. The comedy lives in the paradox that Serena can be undone by sincere idiocy, an Axis devotee too dim to complete the logic she plants, which delights and enrages her in equal measure. Approaches: gather proof of her true nature and present it before the community turns, a race against her timeline; turn her own hatred of the Axis Cult against her by baiting her into overreach in front of witnesses; protect the specific stubborn or foolish holdouts whose refusal to follow her reasoning is the crack in her whole method; or confront her directly, which she is more than equipped to handle and which she would frankly enjoy. Reward is a saved community, a piece of Demon King command intelligence, and a dangerous general's personal, lasting attention. Twist: the community she is working is one the player has helped before, and someone the player trusts is already repeating her lines as their own conclusions.

completionCondition.query: The player has uncovered Serena's infiltration of a community and disrupted her scheme before it turns the community against itself, or has confronted her directly over it.

The Cheat That Chose Conquest.name: The Cheat That Chose Conquest
The Cheat That Chose Conquest.mainObjective: Learn the truth the Demon King's generals guard, that their master arrived in this world exactly as the heroes did, with a divine cheat and a choice.
The Cheat That Chose Conquest.questStatement: His generals know a thing his enemies do not, or do not believe, or have never dared to think through. The Demon King was not born to this world. He was carried into it, as you were carried, as every hero is carried, granted a divine cheat of extraordinary power, given the same blank page every reincarnator receives. He read it, and where others wrote salvation he wrote conquest. Before you can reach him you must first understand him, because the parallel is the whole point, and it is pointed at you.
The Cheat That Chose Conquest.questDesignBrief: This is the first step of a capstone confrontation and it must land as revelation, not combat: the somber weight comes from the mirror, the slow understanding that the ultimate villain is what any arriving hero could become. Play the KonoSuba irony straight-faced, that the world's great evil began with the same cheerful character-creation menu Kazuma once faced, and let the dread build from ordinariness rather than spectacle. Approaches: extract the truth from a captured or wavering general who knows his origin; decode the castle's records and the herald Skarvel's long institutional memory for the account no history dares print; press a defeated infiltrator like Serena, who serves knowing exactly what he is; or piece it together from the too-familiar shape of his strategy, the reasoning of someone who played this game before. Reward is the knowledge itself, which reframes every otherworld hero in the kingdom, and the sober understanding needed to survive step two. Twist: the more the player learns, the clearer it becomes that his cheat and theirs came from the same source, and that someone, somewhere, is still handing these gifts out.

completionCondition.query: The player has learned that the Demon King was himself a reincarnator granted a divine cheat who chose conquest, and grasped what that parallel means for otherworld heroes including themselves.

The Same Blank Page.name: The Same Blank Page
The Same Blank Page.mainObjective: Face the Demon King knowing what he is, and decide what a hero with the same gift and the same choice will do differently.
The Same Blank Page.questStatement: You reached the throne knowing the secret his enemies never learned. He is not surprised that you came. He is faintly, genuinely interested that you understood, because almost no one does, and he has been waiting a long time for someone who arrived the way he arrived to stand where you are standing. He will not gloat. He will simply ask, without menace, what makes you think your page will read any differently than his did. Then he will show you why he wrote what he wrote.
The Same Blank Page.questDesignBrief: The capstone confrontation, and the restraint is everything: this is the somber north star of the whole cluster, so keep the dry KonoSuba wit as a thin dry crust over real weight and let the horror be philosophical before it is physical. The Demon King is a mirror that fights, and the fight only means anything because the player now knows they could have been him. Approaches: defeat his divine cheat by understanding its rules, which the first step's knowledge makes possible where brute force would fail; refuse his framing and answer the question with a choice he did not make, undermining the certainty that armors him; exploit the loneliness under the conquest, the origins unclear even to himself, the reincarnator who chose war and was never sure why; or fight him head on as the culmination of everything the party has become, now that they finally understand the enemy. Reward is the endgame itself, the kingdom's future, and no heroic parade, only the quiet knowledge of what was refused. Twist: whatever the player chooses, the divine source that made him is still open for business, and the throne, once emptied, is a blank page waiting for the next hero to write on.

completionCondition.query: The player has confronted the Demon King with full knowledge of his reincarnator origin and resolved the encounter, choosing how their own gift and choice differ from his.

Tally Marks Against the Cult.name: Tally Marks Against the Cult
Tally Marks Against the Cult.mainObjective: Field-test Rikka's newest batch of refusal cards on live Axis Cult recruiters along the pilgrim road and bring back the results.
Tally Marks Against the Cult.questStatement: Rikka runs the little stall that sells pre-printed cards for politely declining Axis Cult recruiters, and she needs fresh field data. She hands you a stack of untested phrasings, a tally ledger she solemnly calls her research, and a warning that recruiter number three does not take rejection gracefully. Every card that makes a recruiter give up without an argument earns a mark. Your job is to go get told about Aqua for a while and survive it.
Tally Marks Against the Cult.questDesignBrief: The comedy is bureaucratic warfare fought with index cards: the player is a walking A to B test in a holy sales funnel. The indignity is enduring cult pitches on purpose and logging conversion failure rates. Approaches: read cards deadpan and record which lines actually work, ad-lib your own phrasings and let Rikka score them, or lean into a recruiter's pitch far enough to gather intel on the Cult's standing truce with her stall. Twist for the observant player: the recruiters near Springrest are suspiciously gentle, which hints Rikka's truce with Zesta is real. Reward is terrible pay in Springrest scrip, a lifetime supply of refusal cards, and Rikka's genuine respect, which is worth more than the scrip.

completionCondition.query: The player has tested Rikka's refusal cards on actual Axis recruiters, logged which phrasings worked, and returned the tally to her.

The Uncut Route.name: The Uncut Route
The Uncut Route.mainObjective: Verify Hisui's suspicion that a nearby mine is being misrepresented as productive, using her map through the deep tunnels.
The Uncut Route.questStatement: Hisui can appraise a gem in the time it takes a guild merchant to clear his throat, which is exactly why the guild merchants keep her uncredentialed and out of the trade. She has worked out that one of the local mines being talked up as a rich new seam is played out, salted, and about to be sold to some poor buyer at a swindler's price. She will draw you the tunnel route the owner does not know exists. She wants proof, not a fight.
The Uncut Route.questDesignBrief: This is a fraud audit disguised as a dungeon crawl: honest appraisal versus a trade that profits from opacity. The indignity is that the truth is unglamorous rock, and nobody thanks the person who says the treasure is fake. Approaches: sneak the deep-tunnel route Hisui mapped to sample the seam yourself, chat up the mine hands who know it is dead, or confront the owner and watch him bluff. Twist: the salted samples are decent gems, so a greedy player is tempted to just pocket them and say nothing. Reward is fair pay in real coin, a properly appraised gem of the player's choosing at Hisui's honest price, and a standing discount that quietly undercuts the whole cartel.

completionCondition.query: The player has traveled Hisui's tunnel route, determined whether the mine is played out or salted, and decided what to do with the proof.

The Locked Strongbox.name: The Locked Strongbox
The Locked Strongbox.mainObjective: Help Delphine win the coming royal-table auction on the merits, without opening the strongbox that would win it by scandal instead.
The Locked Strongbox.questStatement: Delphine Marchetti lost the royal table years ago to a rival house that bribed a sommelier to ruin her tasting vintage, and she has held the proof in a locked strongbox ever since. She has chosen never to use it, because the rival's current heir is innocent and employs four hundred honest people. Instead she intends to beat them at the next auction fairly, and she needs a discreet pair of hands to make certain nothing goes wrong on the night. The strongbox stays shut. That is the whole job.
The Locked Strongbox.questDesignBrief: The comedy here is restrained and noble: a vengeance thriller where the protagonist has decided vengeance is vulgar and would rather win a wine tasting cleanly. The tension is temptation, because scandal would be so much easier than logistics. Approaches: secure the vintage's flawless transport and decanting so no sabotage repeats, court the auction's fussy judges honestly, or investigate whether the rival house is planning a fresh dirty trick this year. Twist: someone offers to buy or steal the strongbox's contents, testing whether the player respects Delphine's choice. Reward is a case of genuinely excellent Marchetti wine, an introduction to Silverbrook's discreet upper circles, and a favor from a woman who pays her debts in full.

completionCondition.query: The player has helped Delphine contest the auction fairly, kept the strongbox sealed, and the outcome of the tasting has been decided.

Pages the Dead Are Keeping.name: Pages the Dead Are Keeping
Pages the Dead Are Keeping.mainObjective: Recover the catalog reference pages the wandering undead have carried off into the dungeon's upper galleries.
Pages the Dead Are Keeping.questStatement: Yasunori Kubota is an undead scholar bound to a sealed chamber by a commission he cannot abandon: a complete catalog of Keele's Dungeon, eighty percent finished from memory, the last fifth waiting on reference pages that walked off when Keele did. Some of those pages are now bound into the wrappings and nests of the dungeon's lesser undead, who treat old paper as bedding. Yasunori would fetch them himself, but the commission binds him to the chamber and the dead do not respect deadlines. He needs someone with legs and a lantern.
Pages the Dead Are Keeping.questDesignBrief: This opens a four-step chain about finishing a dead man's paperwork, and the joke is that the afterlife has performance reviews. The indignity is looting shamblers for their bedding while a ghost fusses over water damage. Approaches: fight through the upper galleries and collect pages off the fallen, lure or distract the undead to lift pages without a brawl, or bribe the nearby caretaker Jinpachi for a shortcut through the quieter halls. Reward is meager: Yasunori pays in dungeon lore and safe-passage tips, plus a deduction if the pages come back torn. The step ends when the recovered pages are handed over and Yasunori, reading the index numbers, realizes the next batch was wedged into the dungeon's own stonework, and points the player deeper.

completionCondition.query: The player has recovered the reference pages held by the upper-gallery undead, returned them to Yasunori, and learned that the next pages are lodged in the dungeon's masonry.

Wedged in the Walls.name: Wedged in the Walls
Wedged in the Walls.mainObjective: Extract the catalog pages jammed into the dungeon's masonry and trap mechanisms without triggering them.
Wedged in the Walls.questStatement: The index numbers Yasunori recovered point to a second cache: pages folded and forced into the dungeon's own structure, some slid behind loose masonry, several wedged into the guts of Keele's traps as improvised shims. Keele apparently used his own catalog drafts to quiet a rattling mechanism, which Yasunori describes as vandalism against scholarship. Pulling the wrong page could arm a pressure plate or drop a portcullis. The pages must come out clean and intact.
Wedged in the Walls.questDesignBrief: The comedy is a delicate archaeology job where the artifacts are load-bearing, and the ghost cares more about creases than about the player's ankles. Escalates the chain from combat to careful dexterity and problem solving. Approaches: study each trap and disarm it before extraction, use a rogue's touch or the right tool to slip pages free under tension, or accept some property damage and yank them out while dodging the consequence. Twist: one page is not catalog text at all but a note in Keele's hand about a locked private annex, which Yasunori did not know existed. Reward is more dungeon intelligence, a salvaged trap component, and a scolding about paper conservation. The step ends when the pages are freed and the annex note sends the player toward Keele's sealed study.

completionCondition.query: The player has extracted the pages lodged in the dungeon's masonry and traps intact, and discovered Keele's note referencing a sealed private annex.

The Sealed Annex.name: The Sealed Annex
The Sealed Annex.mainObjective: Reach and open Keele's sealed private annex to recover the bundle of reference pages he kept there.
The Sealed Annex.questStatement: Keele's own note names a private annex Yasunori never catalogued, because the commission never granted him access to it. The bulk of the missing pages should be inside, a bound quire the scholar kept close before he left the dungeon for the last time. The annex is sealed by Keele's own design, and the seal was built by a man who filled a dungeon with tests. Getting in is the objective. What Keele kept private is another matter.
The Sealed Annex.questDesignBrief: The chain turns quietly somber here: the annex is where a dead man kept the things he did not want catalogued. The comedy softens into curiosity and a little dread. Approaches: solve Keele's puzzle-seal the way it was meant to be solved, force the annex and deal with whatever guards it, or persuade Keele's lingering ghost, who haunts the dungeon separately, to grant the access he withheld in life. Twist: the quire is inside, but so is evidence of how Keele actually died, which he considers private, and Yasunori must decide whether finishing the catalog means recording it. Reward is the near-complete page set, a personal item from the annex, and the ghost's wary cooperation. The step ends when the quire is in hand and Yasunori sees that one final sheet is still missing, the last thing Keele was holding at the end.

completionCondition.query: The player has opened Keele's sealed annex, recovered the bundled quire of reference pages, and learned that a single final sheet remains unaccounted for.

The Last Sheet.name: The Last Sheet
The Last Sheet.mainObjective: Find the final reference sheet Keele carried to the end and help Yasunori complete the catalog.
The Last Sheet.questStatement: One sheet remains, the last page Keele held before he died somewhere in his own dungeon and stayed as a ghost rather than admit the research was unfinished. The catalog is otherwise complete: cross-referenced, indexed, eighty percent of a life's obsession waiting on a single missing entry. Yasunori has been bound to this commission for longer than he can comfortably count. Bring him the last sheet, and the work is done. Then everyone learns what finishing it actually means.
The Last Sheet.questDesignBrief: The finale pays off the whole chain with KonoSuba's warmth-under-cynicism: a bureaucratic ghost story where turning in the paperwork is the emotional climax. The last sheet rests with Keele's remains, guarded by the truth of his private death. Approaches: recover the sheet from where Keele fell and finish the index yourself, broker peace between Yasunori and Keele's ghost so the two scholars complete it together, or complete the catalog but let Yasunori choose whether to redact how Keele died. Twist: completing the commission releases Yasunori from his binding, which he has wanted and dreaded in equal measure, and the player decides whether to talk him through the moment. Reward is the finished catalog itself, the single most valuable reference to the dungeon in existence, plus whichever bound Yasunori or the freed scholar's gratitude. The step ends with the catalog complete and Yasunori's fate, bound or released, settled by the player's hand.

completionCondition.query: The player has recovered the final reference sheet, the catalog has been completed, and Yasunori's binding to the commission has been resolved.

The Night Axel's Dead Came Home.name: The Night Axel's Dead Came Home
The Night Axel's Dead Came Home.mainObjective: Hold Axel through the night and stop Ezekiel Morrow's risen dead.
The Night Axel's Dead Came Home.questStatement: Arc quest. The Axel Cemetery has emptied. A necromancer whose license the guild revoked has raised every grave and marched the dead into town to appeal his case in person. The guild is calling every adventurer to hold the streets, protect the townsfolk barricaded in the guild hall and the church, and end the night.
The Night Axel's Dead Came Home.questDesignBrief: A town-defense event with real stakes and KonoSuba comedy on top. Ezekiel Morrow directs the horde from the cemetery gate with his Ledger of the Dead. Player paths: hold a barricade and protect civilians; fight through the dead to reach him; take, destroy, or purify the ledger to collapse the horde; or talk him down through procedure (a formal hearing, a Licensed Necromancer vouching, Luna agreeing to review his case). Holy, fire, and purification magic are decisive. The comedy: the dead are Axel's own grumpy ancestors, Aqua purifies whole streets and demands credit, Wiz faints at every wave, and the Eris Church and Axis Cult argue over who is saving whom. Payoff: the town's gratitude, a guild bounty, local fame, and a property damage assessment.

completionCondition.query: DONE WHEN Ezekiel Morrow has been defeated, captured, or talked down AND the risen dead in Axel have been put to rest or dispersed. NOT DONE IF the dead were only held back at a barricade, or if Ezekiel escaped while the dead were still walking.

beldia_attack.beats: Beldia, a Dullahan and Demon King's general in black armor, rides into Axel on a shadow horse carrying his own head. He is furious because someone has been using his castle for daily explosion practice. He demands the explosion mage surrender or he will curse the entire town. He casts a death curse on someone present (targeting whoever drew his attention) that will kill them in a matter of days unless he is defeated. The curse is real and terrifying. The adventurers of Axel must rally to fight him. He fights with honor, announces his attacks, and is ultimately vulnerable to water and purification magic. The scene should be genuinely dramatic until the moment Aqua hits him with purification magic and he realizes he drew the worst possible matchup.
beldia_attack.title: The Dullahan's Ultimatum

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Beldia has been defeated. The curse is lifted. Axel celebrates, property damage bills are calculated, and the guild processes the bounty. The adventurers involved become locally famous, though the details of the fight are already being exaggerated in the retelling.

cabbage_invasion.beats: It is cabbage harvest season. Hundreds of magical cabbages take to the air and fly across the Axel region at speed. The guild has posted bounties per cabbage caught intact. Adventurers are scrambling to catch as many as possible. The cabbages resist capture, dodge, and hit people in the face. This is played as a chaotic, competitive, funny event where everyone is running, diving, and arguing about whose catch is whose. High-level adventurers catch them easily. Rookies get beaten up by vegetables.
cabbage_invasion.title: The Cabbage Swarm

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The cabbage harvest is over. Adventurers compare their catches, argue about totals, and sell their haul to the guild. The local economy briefly stabilizes. Someone got concussed by a cabbage and is being treated at the church.

wiz_item_malfunction.beats: Something Wiz bought from a traveling merchant is malfunctioning in the back of her shop. It could be levitating, emitting strange sounds, attracting vermin, slowly growing, or doing something else that items should not do. Wiz is apologetic and nervous. The player needs to help contain, disable, or destroy it. Vanir, if present, commentates with obvious enjoyment. The item should be genuinely dangerous but the situation should be funny: the curse is absurd, the solution is unconventional, and Wiz keeps apologizing.
wiz_item_malfunction.title: The Thing in the Back Room

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The cursed item has been dealt with. Wiz is deeply grateful and offers the player something from her shop as compensation. Vanir calculates the net loss and announces it with theatrical disappointment.

destroyer_approaches.beats: Reports come in that a massive walking fortress is marching toward Axel. It is visible on the horizon: a towering construct of ancient stone and metal, moving slowly but unstoppably. The guild mobilizes. Adventurers argue about the plan. The town begins to panic. The Destroyer gets closer each turn. The scene should build tension through scale: this thing is enormous, autonomous, and has destroyed settlements before.
destroyer_approaches.title: The Destroyer Approaches

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The preparations are as ready as they will ever be. The Destroyer is close enough now to see individual features on its hull. The time to act is now.

destroyer_battle.beats: The adventurers of Axel assault the Destroyer. The fortress has defensive mechanisms: golems, magical turrets, and structural traps. The adventurers must breach the outer hull, navigate the interior, and reach the power core. The fight should be chaotic, multi-stage, and genuinely dramatic. Multiple parties are involved. The core must be disabled or removed. Whatever method is used will cause massive collateral damage. This is inevitable.
destroyer_battle.title: The Battle of the Destroyer

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The Destroyer's core is out. The fortress collapses. Something nearby has been obliterated by the resulting explosion. The immediate threat is over. The property damage bill is not.

hans_transformation.beats: Hans the traveling merchant drops his disguise in the hot spring district. His human form dissolves into a massive, toxic slime that fills the springs and overflows into the streets. The air becomes poisonous. Civilians flee. The Axis Cult screams. Hans is enormous, amorphous, and dissolves anything organic he touches. Physical weapons pass through him. The scene should be genuinely terrifying for two beats before the comedy of fighting a giant slime in a public bath takes over.
hans_transformation.title: The Merchant's True Form

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Hans is defeated. The springs are contaminated but salvageable. Aqua purifies the water, which is the one thing she is unambiguously excellent at. The Axis Cult declares a holiday. The cleanup costs are someone else's problem.

sylvia_attack.beats: Sylvia attacks the Crimson Demon Village in her true chimera form: massive, shifting, absorbing the terrain as she advances. The village mobilizes. Every Crimson Demon delivers their full dramatic self-introduction before fighting, which takes several turns. The Crimson Demons are individually powerful but Sylvia adapts to counter each attack. The solution requires coordinated village-wide explosion magic. Megumin, if present, insists hers should be the finale. Yunyun helps but nobody acknowledges it until afterward.
sylvia_attack.title: The Chimera's Assault

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Sylvia is defeated by the combined explosion magic of the entire Crimson Demon Village. The crater is impressive. The village considers the crater a tourist attraction. Property damage is extensive but the Crimson Demons consider property damage a form of self-expression.

winter_shogun_encounter.beats: The Winter Shogun appears: a massive, terrifying ice spirit in ancient samurai armor, radiating killing cold. It moves through the forest with deliberate majesty. If the player bows deeply and respectfully, the Shogun acknowledges the gesture and passes. If the player shows any disrespect, fights, or runs without bowing, the Shogun attacks with overwhelming force. The correct response is a deep, sincere bow. Nothing else works.
winter_shogun_encounter.title: The Winter Shogun

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The Winter Shogun has passed. The forest returns to its normal freezing state. The player has learned an important lesson about respect, ice spirits, or both.

goblin_king_negotiation.beats: The Gruk receives the player in his throne chamber. He speaks broken common but with clear intelligence. He offers to stop the surface raids in exchange for a trade agreement: food supplies from Axel in exchange for ore from the cave mines. The goblins are not mindless monsters; they are a small civilization trying to survive. The player must decide whether to negotiate, refuse, or fight. Gruk is surprisingly reasonable if treated with respect.
goblin_king_negotiation.title: An Audience With King Gruk

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The negotiation with the Goblin King has concluded. Whether through diplomacy, combat, or creative problem-solving, the goblin situation has been resolved.

nightless_city_performance.beats: The mysterious performer takes the stage in Nightless City's main hall. The performance is genuinely mesmerizing: music, light, and movement that holds the audience spellbound. The player must determine whether the effect is magical or genuine talent. Investigation during the performance risks disrupting the show and angering the audience. The performer may notice the player's attention and react.
nightless_city_performance.title: The Enchanting Show

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The performance is over. The audience is enraptured or confused depending on what happened. The performer's nature has been revealed or remains mysterious.

frontier_patrol_encounter.beats: During the frontier patrol, the player encounters evidence of Demon King's Army scouts: tracks, discarded equipment, and a campfire still warm. The scouts are ahead on the road. The player must decide whether to follow, report back, or set an ambush. This is real military scouting, not Axel-level adventuring. The Demon King's forces are organized, dangerous, and not funny.
frontier_patrol_encounter.title: Contact on the Northern Road

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The patrol encounter has been resolved. Intelligence has been gathered. The frontier's danger is no longer abstract.

undead_night.beats: Night falls on Axel, weeks after Beldia's defeat, and the Axel Cemetery empties. Ezekiel Morrow, a necromancer whose license the guild revoked after a failed audit, has raised every grave with his Ledger of the Dead and marched them into town to appeal his case in person. This is a real threat: shambling dead flood the streets from the north edge inward, doors are forced, townsfolk barricade themselves in the Guild Tavern Floor and the Eris Church of Axel, and the guild calls every adventurer to the defense. Wounds, fear, and lost ground are real; nobody is safe standing still. The comedy rides on top without undercutting the danger: the dead are Axel's own grumpy ancestors, some of whom stop mid-rampage to complain about their descendants, the price of bread, or the state of their headstones; Aqua purifies whole streets at once and demands credit for each one; Wiz faints at every purification wave; the Eris Church and the Axis Cult argue loudly over who is saving whom. Paths through the night: hold a barricade and protect civilians; push through the dead to find Ezekiel, who directs the horde from the cemetery gate; take, destroy, or purify his Ledger of the Dead to collapse the horde (a thief's or schemer's path); or talk him down through procedure (a formal hearing, a Licensed Necromancer vouching for him, or getting Luna to agree to review his case). Holy, fire, and purification magic are decisive against the dead. A Licensed Necromancer in the party is asked by a dead man to produce their license, and can use it. Ezekiel does not want anyone to die and will pull the dead back from a killing blow if it would hurt his case. The night ends when he is defeated, captured, or talked down and the dead are put to rest.
undead_night.title: The Night Axel's Dead Came Home

onCompleteEffects.instruction: The night is over. The dead are back in the ground, some of them still complaining. Whatever became of Ezekiel Morrow (arrested and prosecuted by Sena, or placed on strict probation filing paperwork for the Eris Church), the Axel Cemetery needs re-consecrating, the guild quietly reviews its audit procedures, and the property damage assessment arrives within the week with a very large number on it. The adventurers who held the town are locally famous, and the story is already being exaggerated in the tavern.

effects.instruction: Wiz greets the player warmly but nervously. Something in the back of the shop is making a sound it should not be making. She apologizes preemptively.
Vanir grins behind his mask, which is never a good sign. He has a proposition, and the terms are very clearly written down.
Prosecutor Sena enters the guild hall with a leather folder and the air of someone who has done this too many times. She asks for the player by name.

effects.text: Answer Sena's summons about the property damage.

conditions.query: The player has encountered or spoken to Yunyun

effects.instruction: The temperature drops. An oppressive magical pressure settles over Axel. A headless knight in black armor rides through the town gate on a horse made of shadow, carrying his own head under one arm. He is looking for whoever has been using his castle for daily explosion practice.
The well-dressed merchant near the hot springs smiles, and the smile is wrong. His skin shifts. Something enormous and toxic begins to unfold from the human shape.

conditions.query: Someone notices the hot springs water tastes wrong or the springs are being contaminated

effects.instruction: The figure at the village perimeter is not a traveler. Her outline shifts, her armor grows from her body, and the Crimson Demons recognize what she is before anyone else does. A Demon King's general has come to the village with a grudge.

An Axis Cult recruiter materializes from the crowd with inhuman speed and a pamphlet already extended. They have been waiting. They open with a question about whether the player has considered the spiritual benefits of water.

conditions.query: Did the player just seriously damage a building or someone else's valuable property on screen, in a town or settlement?

effects.instruction: Luna pulls the player's file and sighs: the repair claims from their recent jobs have come in, itemized, one line for each thing they actually broke. The guild will deduct them from the next payout unless they are settled first.

Chris suddenly changes the subject when the goddess Eris is mentioned. She touches the scar near her mouth and excuses herself with a laugh that is slightly too quick. If Aqua is nearby, Aqua watches Chris leave with an expression that could be smugness or could be something else entirely.

conditions.query: Has the player discussed the goddess Eris with Chris present?
The player has spoken with Chris at least twice and she trusts them enough to ask a favor
The player has spoken to or interacted with Dust

effects.instruction: Luna looks troubled. There have been reports from the beginner ruins. Something is wrong out there.
The guild hall falls silent. The temperature drops. Outside, a shadow passes over Axel that is not a cloud.

effects.text: Rally Axel's defense before Beldia delivers his ultimatum.

effects.instruction: The ground trembles. Somewhere to the south, something enormous is moving. The guild receives an emergency dispatch: a mobile fortress has been sighted heading for Axel.

effects.text: Stop the Destroyer before it reaches Axel.

effects.instruction: The Destroyer is down. Axel is saved. The cheering lasts until Sena arrives with an arrest warrant for the property damage.

effects.text: Attend the trial and answer for the damage.

effects.instruction: The water tastes different. The Axis Cult is in an uproar. Zesta is crying and praying simultaneously, which takes talent.

effects.text: Expose and destroy Hans before he poisons the springs.
Defend the Crimson Demon Village from Sylvia.

effects.instruction: The temperature drops further. The trees creak. Something massive is moving through the deep snow, leaving tracks the size of shields. The Winter Shogun is nearby. Running or bowing deeply are the only correct responses.

The perpetual golden light of Nightless City makes it impossible to tell what time it is. Street performers compete for attention. A vendor offers suspicious meat skewers. The energy is infectious and the wallet is in danger.
Movement in the tunnel ahead. Goblin sentries have spotted the intruder and are organizing a response with alarming efficiency. These are not random monsters; they are soldiers defending their home.

The guild has updated the party's adventurer cards. Level 10 unlocks access to quests rated Moderate and above, which means the guild now trusts you enough to die in more interesting ways. Luna congratulates you with the specific enthusiasm of someone processing paperwork.

The Royal Capital is enormous. The walls are taller than anything in Axel. The streets are wider, the crowds are denser, and the adventurers walking past are visibly higher-level. The guild hall alone is bigger than Axel's entire commercial district. This is the real Belzerg.
The cold stops being weather and becomes presence. Every sound in the clearing dies at once. Something enormous is standing at the far tree line, and it has noticed you.

The warren's noise falls away. On a seat of piled rubble and stolen finery sits a goblin a head taller than the rest, iron crown catching the torchlight. He raises one hand, and his warriors hold. He wants to talk first.

The road north is churned and quiet. Ahead, something in the mud is not mud: boot prints too wide for a human, discarded gear, and a campfire with heat still in the ashes. Whatever made them is not far.

effects.text: Take the toad extermination posting from Luna at the Axel guild.

conditions.query: Has the player seen the Axel quest board or heard about the giant toads?

effects.text: Sign on for the cabbage harvest before the crop takes flight.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about the cabbage harvest or seen a flying cabbage?

effects.text: Ask Wiz about the item that has been causing trouble.

conditions.query: Has the player spoken with Wiz and seen her questionable stock?

effects.text: Hear out Vanir's proposition, carefully.

conditions.query: Has the player spoken with Vanir at his counter?

effects.text: Deal with the Axis Cult's recruitment drive, one way or another.

conditions.query: Has the player been approached by an Axis Cult recruiter?

effects.text: Descend into the upper floors of Keele's Dungeon.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about Keele's Dungeon from the guild or a delver?

effects.text: Accept or deflect Yunyun's challenge.

conditions.query: Has Yunyun challenged the player to a duel?

effects.text: Hear what Chris needs handled quietly.

conditions.query: Has Chris grown confident enough to raise private business with the player?

effects.text: Listen to Dust's plan and decide how far to go along with it.

conditions.query: Has Dust pitched one of his schemes to the player?

effects.text: Enter the Crimson Demon introduction contest.

conditions.query: Has the player witnessed a Crimson Demon self-introduction?

effects.text: Investigate the trouble at the hot springs.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about trouble at Alcanretia's hot springs?

effects.text: Investigate the dark presence at the Neighbourhood Ruins.

conditions.query: Has the player heard something is wrong at the ruins near Axel?

effects.text: Find out what the Walking Fortress is and how much time Axel has.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about a large threat approaching Axel?

effects.text: Investigate what is wrong with Alcanretia's blessed springs.

conditions.query: Has the player heard something is wrong with the blessed water?

effects.text: Identify the general threatening the Crimson Demon Village.

conditions.query: Has the player heard a general was sighted near the Crimson Demon Village?

effects.text: Try your luck, or your judgement, at the Elroad tables.

conditions.query: Has the player entered an Elroad casino or been drawn toward the tables?

effects.text: Get the arrested adventurer out of Elroad custody.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about a Belzerg adventurer arrested in Elroad?

effects.text: Take the sensitive job Erika is holding for someone competent.

conditions.query: Has Erika Shindou assessed the player and offered a sensitive job?

effects.text: Look into the trouble in Nightless City's performance scene.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about trouble in the entertainment district?

effects.text: Clear the goblin cave and deal with Gruk.

conditions.query: Has the player heard about goblins raiding the roads near Axel?

effects.text: Hunt snow sprites in the Snowfield Forest, and heed the rule about the Shogun.
